articleTitle: Delhi bus gangrape: Accused’s DNA matched samples, crucial for water-tight case, say cops
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Greater Noida bus gangrape, Delhi Police FSL fast track court, sleeper bus gangrape case, NHRC notice Delhi UP police, Gautam Buddha Nagar police, Noida passenger safety lapses, bus traffic challans UP Delhi, public transport safety women, Delhi rape, delhi gangrape, delhi moving bus rape, delhi teen raped moving bus, delhi girl raped moving bus
description: Police have said the alleged sexual assault took place as the bus moved towards Delhi.
body_raw: The DNA samples of the two men accused of raping a 17-year-old in a moving bus last month have matched the samples recovered from the bus and the girls clothes, according to the chargesheet filed by the Delhi Police in the case. This makes scientific evidence obtained during the girls medical examination and forensic evidence crucial to the case, as per the investigators. A total of 51 witnesses, including the minors cousin whose house she was going to, her parents and the staff at repair centre that the accused visited before the alleged assault, apart from investigating officers, have been named in the chargesheet, said officers. The Delhi Police filed a 398-page chargesheet in the case on September 18. A city court took cognisance of it on September 24, officials familiar with the proceedings said. Biological samples, including semen and hair strands, were collected during the investigation and sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory FSL for examination. Police had sought an expedited report as they prepared the case for trial. Officers said forensic evidence was the first and one of the key pieces of evidence relied upon by police in building what they described as a watertight case. The girl was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving sleeper bus on August 4 as it travelled nearly 47 km from Greater Noida to Delhis Kashmere Gate in August. On Monday, the Supreme Court took suo motu cognizance of the case, expressed anguish over the matter, and said, One cannot help but draw painful parallels to the 2012 Nirbhaya case, calling into question whether systemic law enforcement mechanisms have made any meaningful progress in the decade since then. Sources also said the minor maintained her statement throughout the investigation, including in her statement recorded under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Her statement corroborated the account she had given to police on the first day of the crime, sources said. The case The incident took place on August 4. The teenager allegedly boarded the bus at Pari Chowk in Greater Noida. According to her statement to the police, the girl had told the bus driver and conductor that she wanted to go to Noida and was told that the bus was headed in that direction. After boarding, she realised that there were no other passengers and attempted to get off but the conductor allegedly pulled her back inside. Police have said the alleged sexual assault took place as the bus moved towards Delhi. The girl was allegedly abandoned in Kashmere Gate after the sexual assault and she approached the local police station. Police said considering the sensitive nature of the complaint, the minors medical examination was carried out and the case registered without jurisdictional delay. Using CCTV footage, they traced the bus to a parking area in Timarpur and arrested the men - bus driver Kuldeep 39 and conductor Sandeep 26, both hailing from Kanpur - within four hours. Red flags found during probe Police investigation traced the route of the bus through Greater Noida, Noida and Delhi and found that the vehicle was allegedly not stopped for a safety or compliance check during the journey. Investigators found that the bus had 11 pending traffic challans - seven of them issued in July - for offences relating to speed-limit devices and permit violations. Police also found that the two men had been hired without police verification. The buss CCTV camera was also found to be non-functional, while heavy curtains covered its windows. Investigators had further examined whether safety mechanisms such as GPS or vehicle-tracking systems and panic buttons were installed and functional at the time of the incident.

articleTitle: After Express report, Goa CEO says cases of 97 voters ‘processed separately’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Goa Chief Electoral Officer, Panaji: After Express investigation into Election Commission and ECs Sukhbir Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, Goa CEO says cases of 97 voters ‘processed separately’.
description: The final electoral roll for Goa after the completion of SIR was published in February with a net deletion of 1.27 lakh voters, representing 10.76 per cent of the state’s electorate.
body_raw: A day after The Indian Express reported on the unprecedented rupture within the Election Commission and the disenfranchisement of potential voters in Goa, the office of the Chief Electoral Officer of Goa on Thursday said that many of the 97 cases that were not included in the final electoral roll published in February this year have been enrolled since, and the remaining cases are being processed. It said the cases were separately processed through house-to-house visits by booth-level officers BLOs for completion of Form 6. The Indian Express on Thursday reported that between February 11 and 17, the office of Goas Chief Electoral Officer wrote eight times to Gyanesh Bharti, the Senior Deputy Election Commissioner in charge of the state, copying Director General of IT Seema Khanna every time, asking for the rollback option that would let the EROs reverse the earlier deletions as the Supreme Court had directed. The requests went unanswered as the deadline for publication of the final electoral roll approached. The provision was not enabled in time, and 97 people were left off the final voters roll in Goa. What the Goa Electoral Officer said A statement from the office of the Chief Electoral Officer, Goa, on Thursday, said, The 97 cases not included in the Final Roll published in February 2026 were separately processed through house-to-house visits by BLOs for completion of Form 6. Many have since been enrolled, while the remaining cases are being processed. It is reiterated that no eligible elector will be left behind. When The Indian Express contacted him, Sanjay Goel, Chief Electoral Officer, Goa, said, We had flagged to the Election Commission in February regarding the list of 97 voters to be included. Subsequently, we went ahead and published the final roll. Immediately after, I wrote to both the DEOs district election officers that all these 97 cases. they should be part of the electoral rolls by filing Form 6 and the BLOs booth-level officers must visit their addresses and get the requisite documentation done. Since then, we have collated data, and many of the names in the list of 97 have been added to the electoral rolls after filing Form 6. And for the remaining cases, we are taking the initiative, and the BLOs will go to their addresses. And once their Form 6 details are filled, they will be added to the roll in a time-bound manner. The final electoral roll for Goa after the completion of Special Intensive Revision SIR was published in February with a net deletion of 1.27 lakh voters, representing 10.76 per cent of the states electorate prior to the commencement of the exercise.

articleTitle: ‘My father married around 20 people’: Sreelakshmi Arackal reveals traumatic childhood
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Evicted Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 contestant Sreelakshmi Arackal about her father.
description: As Sreelakshmi Arackal bid adieu to Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8, certain remarks she made about her father during her time in the house went viral on social media.
body_raw: In a first, Bigg Boss Malayalam saw a mass eviction this past weekend when as many as six contestants were shown the door from the ongoing Season 8 of the reality show. Among those evicted from the Mohanlal-hosted show was social activist Sreelakshmi Arackal. As she bid adieu to the show, certain remarks she made about her family, particularly her father, during her time in the Bigg Boss Malayalam Season 8 house went viral on social media. Opening up about the difficulties she has faced in her life, Sreelakshmi said that the reason she comes across as a man-hater, as many call her, is the intense hatred she holds for her father. He has married around 10 to 20 people, including my mother. I am a child born out of such a relationship. The hatred towards my father is still there in my mind. That is what many people interpret as hatred for men misandry, Sreelakshmi said recently in the Bigg Boss house. Proudly naming her mother as her role model, she added, I was born through a Cesarean section C-section. Even before I turned six months old, my mother began going for daily wage labour. My grandmother wasnt very healthy and was mostly sick. So I did everything myself. Since the 6th or 7th grade, Id go to the ration shop alone and do everything men usually do. My mother was like that too. Shed go for painting and rubber tapping. Growing up watching her made me independent. Poverty was my motivation to study Sreelakshmi noted that for her mother - who thought her life was completely destroyed following childbirth - her brilliance in studies became the only hope. She continued, I was a rank-holder in BSc Physics. When I was born, my mother thought Id be a complete failure. But from first grade, I was always at the top of my class. Thats when my mother gained confidence in me. Poverty was my motivation to study, as there was no other way to succeed. My father is the reason Im standing here today because of the life he gave me. That struggle led me here. Im open about everything because there was no patriarchy in my home. Thats why I can speak freely. I am a basrd. And I salute that man for that, she added. articleTitle: Father in kitchen, girls playing drums: Andhra Pradesh’s textbook bid to end gender stereotypes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The minister said the state government was also working to improve the teacher-taught ratio.
description: “The aim is to avoid gender stereotyping from the first grade itself,’’ said IT and HRD minister N Lokesh Naidu. In the new books, the children will also be introduced to both “good” and “bad” sides of Artificial Intelligence
body_raw: Father working alongside the mother in the kitchen, girls on drums and violins during musical performances, and men and women both standing in line to collect water from a common public tap These are some of the images that can be seen in the new textbooks for classes 1 and 2 in Andhra Pradesh as it attempts to eliminate gender stereotypes from a young age. In the new books, the children will also be introduced to both good and bad sides of Artificial Intelligence. While past textbooks depicted household chores as being performed entirely by women, the new textbooks, introduced recently, changed this approach so that 50 of the household chores shown are performed by men and 50 by women, said an official. The aim is to avoid gender stereotyping from the first grade itself, said Andhra Pradesh IT and HRD minister N Lokesh Naidu. During a chat organised by the Public Affairs Forum of India PAFI in Delhi on Thursday, Lokesh said that the states ongoing reforms in school and higher education have a strong focus on value-based education, gender sensitivity, technology-enabled learning, curriculum reform and industry-linked skilling. Other examples of gender-neutral roles in the textbook are a woman selling vegetables, a man weaving a flower garland alongside a woman at a shop, and a man and a woman working in tandem in an agricultural field. Listing other changes in the school system, Lokesh said primary schools are now implementing No Bag Day on Saturdays, which is reserved for value-based and practical learning. The activities include lessons on managing family budgets and agricultural budgets, field exposure visits and an introduction to AI. Lokesh said students are being introduced to both the positive and negative sides of AI so they can understand the technology and use it effectively in their chosen fields. The Education Department has undertaken two rounds of curriculum improvement for the purpose. The state government is working on a project of gamifying classrooms through technology. Under the proposed approach, after every 45-minute class, students would watch a 60- or 90-second video summarising the lesson, followed by four to five questions. Using clicker technology, students would actively participate in answering the questions, turning the classroom into a more interactive learning environment, he said. From passive to active learners The objective, Lokesh said, is to shift students from being passive learners to active learners. The data would feed into the states Learning Management System LMS, enabling the system to identify individual learning gaps and provide prescriptive homework and targeted learning content, he said. If a student is strong in mathematics but weak in another subject, the system would identify the specific gap and provide additional homework and learning material through the LEAP app, which is accessible to parents and teachers as well. This would allow students to clearly understand the areas where they need improvement, he added. The minister said the state government was also working to improve the teacher-taught ratio. From just 3 schools having one teacher per class in 2024, the number has now increased to 33, he said. The state recently completed a major teacher recruitment drive under which 16,000 teachers were recruited to achieve the objective of one teacher per class, Lokesh told The Indian Express on Friday. He said teacher recruitment is being undertaken every year. At the Delhi event, Lokesh said that besides schools, the state is reviewing university curricula through discussions with academicians. The state is examining what courses, majors and minors, are being offered, whether they remain relevant, and how closely curricula are aligned with market requirements, he added.

articleTitle: What flydubai FZ1073 attacker Hamam al-Hammami’s deleted posts said about women, work and niqab
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Flydubai pilot attack:
description: A LinkedIn profile in the name of Hamam al-Hammami, the Omani co-pilot accused in the flydubai attack, listed his job history. CNN also found deleted posts and videos linked to him.
body_raw: In the days since an attack on a flydubai flight heading for Tel Aviv, attention has turned to the man accused of carrying it out. Hamam al-Hammami, the Omani co-pilot accused of attacking Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, left behind deleted social media posts that give a view into what he wrote about women, religion and mixed-gender workplaces. An analysis of nearly 3,000 now-deleted tweets from 2021 and 2022 showed the Omani pilot was deeply religious and misogynistic, according to CNN. The tweets were studied using an AI-powered search tool and are now part of a wider picture. He was removed from his previous job at Omans national airline last year following concerns about his extremist views, the report said. A LinkedIn profile linked to Al-Hammami has also surfaced which showed him working in Oman Air for seven years. However, there was no mention of flydubai. UAE has also opened an investigation into whether the attack was linked to terrorist activity. What the deleted tweets say In a LinkedIn post from February 2022, he wrote about how hard it was for his mother to find him a wife who would accept his conditions. She had to wear a niqab, a face covering, and stop working after marriage. Families refused, he wrote, until his mother told them My son is a pilot. Then they agreed. Other posts argued against mixed-gender workplaces. A post from January 2022 asked how many religious women had been ruined in such settings, and the posts claimed that these workplaces corrupt women. What else was posted online Two posts went up on the LinkedIn profile on Wednesday, about nine hours after the incident. It is unclear who published them or whether they were scheduled in advance. One source confirmed to CNN that the profile belongs to the pilot. A plane takes off as a flydubai aircraft sits on the tarmac at Dubai International Airport in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. AP Photo The first post was a video of clips filmed in Boeing 737 Max cockpits, including planes of the Israeli airlines El Al and Arkia. It ended with photos of Ayman al-Zawahiri, who led al Qaeda after Osama bin Ladens death, and Humam Khalil Abu-Mulal al-Balawi, who killed nine people in a 2009 suicide bombing and was loyal to al Qaeda. The second post was an AI-generated image of Islams three holiest sites, with a poem about rejecting humiliation and not fearing death. His career and the Oman concern The LinkedIn profile said he worked at Oman Air for seven years and left in February 2025. It said he joined Royal Air Maroc in June 2025 and left in January 2026. An Israeli official said he had worked for flydubai for only eight months. A regional diplomat said he was taken off flight training because of concerns about his radical views and was given another role at the airline. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday the suspect was believed to have gone through Islamist radical indoctrination. What investigators are doing Israeli agencies, including Shin Bet and Mossad, are looking into how an Omani citizen, from a country that does not recognise Israel, came to be part of the crew. The UAE attorney generals investigation covers whether there was any prior planning or direction, state news agency WAM reported. Investigations are ongoing to determine the circumstances of the incident, the motives and any related connections, as well as to examine physical and digital evidence, he added.

articleTitle: Ramayana director Nitesh Tiwari explains why Ranbir Kapoor was cast as Lord Ram
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ramayan (1)
description: Nitesh Tiwari, Namit Malhotra, Arun Govil, Ravie Dubey and Sai Pallavi have shared their perspectives on why they believe Ranbir Kapoor was the right choice for the role of Lord Ram.
body_raw: Ever since the makers of Ramayana announced that Ranbir Kapoor would be playing Lord Ram, the casting choice has drawn mixed reactions. While some fans welcomed the announcement, others resurfaced old videos of statements made by the actor. Now, in a newly released video to celebrate Ranbir Kapoors birthday, filmmaker Nitesh Tiwari, producer Namit Malhotra and actors Arun Govil, Ravie Dubey and Sai Pallavi have shared their perspectives on why they believe Ranbir was the right choice for the role, with the actor also opening up about the responsibility he feels. In the video, Nitesh Tiwari said, In India, we believe that even if we imbibe just 1 of what Shri Ram was, that will make us a great human being. So just imagine, the kind of human he must have been. And thats why, the casting of Shri Ram is next to impossible. We can only attempt. When Namit discussed Ranbirs name, I too thought that he checked all the boxes. Actor Arun Govil, who plays Dashrath in this film and is widely known as the OG Ram from Ramanand Sagars iconic Ramayan, said, Speaking about Ranbir, the way I had imagined Ram would have been-I see certain things in Ranbir. And you dont expect a star to come touch your feet, but he always did that to me on set. If you compare with all the available younger stars of today, Ranbir comes closest to playing Ram. Ranbir Kapoor, meanwhile, spoke about what Lord Rams greatest strength meant to him. The biggest weapon of Shri Ram wasnt his bow and arrow, but his ability to forgive. This is not just another role for me. It is a responsibility. I think everything just comes down to the simplicity and belief of the individual playing Lord Ram, he said. The actor added, There is a well-known principle from our Vedic texts that reads Dharmo Rakshati Rakshitah. Dharma protects those who uphold it. Every day I reminded myself that my job was not to be worthy of this role. My job was to be worthy of the faith that people placed in this role. ALSO READ Mithun Chakraborty won National Award but had no work, danced at parties for food, slept on footpaths Ramayana producer Namit Malhotra also spoke about the decision to cast Ranbir Kapoor. That sincerity and face of Ranbir became for Nitesh and I not a reason to debate, he said. Sai Pallavi recalled seeing a familiar image of Lord Ram in Ranbir when she first met him. I dont know if its quite famous, but there is this picture of a slender Ram and his head is a little tilted and there is a very small, petite Sita. Thats the image I remember from my childhood. Now, suddenly, I could see that Ram that I had seen in my childhood and I was awestruck, she said. Ravie Dubey also shared his perspective, saying, I strongly believed that the simplicity we hear about Lord Ram is the same simplicity I see in Ranbir Kapoors eyes. Ranbir Kapoor initially felt he wasnt fit enough to play Lord Ram Ranbir Kapoors current comments about the role are markedly different from his initial reaction when he was first offered the part. Speaking at a QA during the New York special IMAX trailer screening, Ranbir recalled his reaction when Namit approached him. Coming to play Lord Ram, I remember when Namit offered me this part around four years back, my instant reaction was I am not fit enough, good enough. I felt I wouldnt be able to do full justice. But that fear quickly turned into gratitude because opportunities like this were something I truly needed in my life, he said. The actor added, There was a period when I needed to change my lifestyle. I had just become a father for the first time. The sweet coincidence of playing Lord Ram and becoming a father became a turning point in my life. Ravie Dubey had previously spoken about how playing a character from the Ramayana had changed his own routine. That role changed me. I had to transform myself to do justice to it because the audience can easily tell when you are faking it. I completely altered my routine. In fact, all of us did, including Ranbir Kapoor. He has sacrificed so much for this film. This feels more like a yagya. We all did everything in our power to stay true to these characters in how we behave, react, and even speak, Dubey told Ranveer Allahbadia. Previously, reports had also claimed that Ranbir Kapoor had given up alcohol and non-vegetarian food while preparing for the role of Lord Ram. Ramayana is all set to hit theaters on Diwali this year with the second part scheduled to release next Diwali.

articleTitle: IDFC First Bank scam: Haryana suspends IAS officer Pankaj Agarwal after CBI arrest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pankaj Agarwal Haryana IAS officer
description: IAS officer Pankaj Agarwal is the third IAS officer suspended by the Haryana government as the investigation into the alleged Rs 657 crore IDFC First Bank fraud gathers steam.
body_raw: The Haryana government on Friday suspended senior IAS officer Pankaj Agarwal after he was arrested by the Central Bureau of Investigation CBI in connection with an alleged Rs 657 crore IDFC First Bank fraud. The suspension follows service rules that mandate action against an officer held in custody for more than 48 hours. Agarwal, a 2000-batch officer, was arrested on June 22 and is currently lodged in Ambala jail. Agarwal is the third IAS officer to be suspended as the investigation into the multi-crore scam continues. Earlier, on April 8, the Haryana government suspended Pradeep Kumar 2011 batch and Singh 2012 batch. This week, Singh was arrested by the CBI. The CBI is investigating at least seven IAS officers of the Haryana cadre. An order issued by Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi stated that Agarwals suspension takes effect under Rule 32 of the All India Services Discipline and Appeal Rules, 1969, which provides for the deemed suspension of an officer detained in official custody beyond 48 hours. The order also clarified that he will receive a subsistence allowance as prescribed under the service rules until further orders. Before his suspension, Agarwal was serving as principal secretary of the architecture department. According to the CBI, Agarwal is accused of allegedly misappropriating more than Rs 50 crore from the Haryana School Shiksha Pariyojana Parishad during his tenure as principal secretary, school education department. Investigators have also alleged that he was involved in the embezzlement of nearly Rs 10 crore from the Haryana State Agriculture Marketing Board while serving as principal secretary of the agriculture and farmers welfare department. The CBI took over the investigation into the alleged Rs 657 crore IDFC First Bank fraud on April 8. On the same day, Agarwal was shifted to the architecture department, while several other IAS officers named in the case were assigned less significant roles. Accused of favouring BJP during Rajya Sabha polls Agarwal had previously held several influential positions in the Haryana administration and was regarded as being close to the ruling BJP government. He served as the states chief electoral officer and oversaw the 2024 Haryana Assembly elections. His role as returning officer during the March 16 Rajya Sabha elections attracted controversy, with the Congress accusing him of improperly rejecting votes cast by its MLAs while allowing allegedly invalid votes in favour of the BJP-backed Independent candidate Satish Nandal. Three days after the Rajya Sabha elections, Agarwal was appointed principal secretary of the irrigation and water resources department, adviser to the Haryana Saraswati Heritage Board, and principal secretary of the mines and geology department-despite the corruption probe being underway. Following the Rajya Sabha election, the Congress Legislative Party submitted a memorandum to Haryana Governor Ashim Kumar Ghosh, alleging that Agarwal acted arbitrarily and favoured BJP-supported candidates.

articleTitle: Does RAC guarantee a seat in Indian Railways? What Reservation Against Cancellation means for your train ticket
articleFeaturedImageAlt: An RAC ticket allows passengers to travel with reserved seating accommodation. (Image generated using AI)
description: Does an RAC ticket guarantee a seat on Indian Railways? Know what Reservation Against Cancellation means, whether you can board the train and when an RAC ticket can become confirmed.
body_raw: Indian Railways RAC rules seat guaranteeWhen booking a train ticket, passengers often come across the term RAC and wonder what it means for their journey. Does an RAC ticket allow them to board the train? Will they get a seat, or will they have to wait for a berth to become available?In Indian Railways, RAC stands for Reservation Against Cancellation. Here is how the RAC system works and what passengers can expect when travelling with an RAC ticket. What Reservation Against Cancellation means Speaking to Indianexpress.com, a senior railway official said that RAC is a reservation status used by Indian Railways when confirmed berths in a particular class have already been allotted but limited accommodation is still available for passengers. The official explained that a RAC passenger is permitted to board the train and is provided reserved seating accommodation. In classes with sleeping berths, two RAC passengers may initially be allotted seating on a berth designated for RAC passengers. This means that while the passengers journey is assured, a full sleeping berth is not necessarily assured at that stage, the official stated. Can RAC ticket become confirmed? According to the railway official, an RAC ticket can move to confirmed status if a berth becomes available.For example, if passengers holding confirmed reservations cancel their tickets before chart preparation, the available berths can be allotted to RAC passengers according to the applicable reservation system. So, a passenger whose status was RAC 25 at the time of booking may see it improve to RAC 10, RAC 2 or eventually CNF before the journey. Once the ticket becomes confirmed, the passenger is allotted a full berth, the official said. What happens if the ticket remains RAC after chart preparation? When asked about whether a passenger can travel with RAC ticket after chart preparation, the official replied that the passenger can still travel. If the ticket remains RAC after the final reservation chart is prepared, reserved seating accommodation remains available, but a full berth may have to be shared as per the RAC arrangement, the official added. The official further said that there is also a possibility of getting a full berth during the journey. If a confirmed passenger does not turn up, cancels at a stage permitted under the rules, or a berth otherwise becomes available, the vacant accommodation may be allotted to an RAC passenger by the travelling ticket checking staff as per applicable rules and priority. Why does Indian Railways have RAC system? As per the official, the RAC system helps Indian Railways make better use of available accommodation while giving more passengers certainty about their journey. Instead of keeping passengers entirely on the waiting list, RAC allows a limited number of passengers to travel with seating accommodation while keeping them in line for full berths that may become vacant due to cancellations, the official added.

articleTitle: Radhikka Madan swears by home food, reveals recent lifestyle changes: ‘Very little wheat’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Radhikka Madan
description: The goal is not to eliminate but to find what truly supports one’s health and daily life
body_raw: Sarfira actor Radhikka Madan, 30, opened up about her eating habits, stressing her love for home food. Eat as much as you want. You wont have a problem. I dont have a diet, she said in a conversation with Brut India. She revealed, Ive made some lifestyle changes. Ive stopped consuming sugar, milk, and I consume very little wheat. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Dr Aniket Mule, consultant in internal medicine at KIMS Hospitals, Thane, stressed that cutting back on added sugar is usually a good step, as too much sugar can lead to weight gain, low energy, and long-term metabolic issues. The choice to remove milk and wheat varies from person to person. Some people feel lighter or less bloated without them, especially if they have lactose intolerance or gluten sensitivity. However, for others, these foods provide important nutrients like calcium, protein, and fibre. The decision should depend on how the body responds, not just on trends, said Dr Mule. According to Dr Mule, removing entire food groups without replacing their nutrients can cause deficiencies. For example, cutting milk without adding other sources of calcium, or reducing wheat without including other whole grains, can upset the overall balance. At the same time, many people claim to feel more energetic because they are eating healthier and avoiding processed foods. Instead of following strict rules, focusing on home-cooked meals, regular eating times, and mindful portion sizes helps build lasting habits. When eating becomes simple and balanced, the body adjusts naturally without feeling restricted, said Dr Mule. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Brut India brut.india What to note? Its important to avoid blindly copying someone elses routine. What works for one person may not work for another. A gradual approach is best pay attention to how the body responds, make small adjustments, and ensure meals remain balanced. The goal is not to eliminate but to find what truly supports ones health and daily life, said Dr Mule. articleTitle: Ahead of UP polls, Aradhana Mishra replaces Ajay Rai as state unit chief
articleFeaturedImageAlt: aradhana misra mona
description: The changes are part of the Congress’s restructuring of its organisational strategy in the state months before the Uttar Pradesh elections.
body_raw: Uttar Pradesh Legislature Party leader Aradhana Mishra has been appointed the partys state chief, replacing Ajay Rai. Imran Masood, Congress MP from Saharanpur, has been appointed working president. The changes are part of the Congresss restructuring of its organisational strategy in the state months before the Assembly elections. Aradhana is the MLA from Rampur Khas in Pratapgarh district. She is the daughter of veteran UP Congress leader Pramod Tiwari, who had made a record of sorts by winning Rampur Khas constituency 9 times from 1980 to 2012. In 2014, when he became the MP, Aradhana had won this seat in a bypoll. In the 2017 polls, she won the seat for the second consecutive time, defeating the BJPs Nagesh Pratap Singh by nearly 17,000 votes. The Congress then made her its Legislature Party leader in the state Assembly. Considered to be close to Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi, Aradhana had accompanied her during her visits to the houses of women and other victims of various atrocities in several districts-including Hathras, Unnao, Umbha, Sidharthanagar and Lakhimpur Kheri-in recent years. In the run-up to the 2022 Assembly polls, she had accompanied Priyanka across the state on her women-centred campaign, called Larki hun, lar sakti hun I am a girl, and I can fight. She has a Bachelors degree in Commerce and Masters in Business Administration, and had served as a block pramukh for three terms since 2001. Rai, a Bhumihar leader from eastern UP, was appointed in August 2023. He had replaced Dalit leader Brijlal Khabri ahead of the 2024 elections. Rai contested the last two parliamentary elections against Prime Minister Narendra Modi from Varanasi. In 2024, he succeeded in reducing Modis victory margin. Series of changes In July, the All India Congress Committee AICC had replaced Avinash Pande as the general secretary in charge of Uttar Pradesh with Rajendra Pal Gautam, the national chairman of the partys Scheduled Castes Department and a prominent Dalit leader. Last month, the Congress appointed Kunwar Singh Nishad as chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committees Media and Publicity Department. According to party sources, Nishad, who hails from Mathura, was earlier associated with the BJP, and joined the Congress during Priyanka Gandhi Vadras campaign in Uttar Pradesh in 2022. He had since been serving as a Congress spokesperson in the state. These two appointments came as the Congress seeks to expand its outreach among Dalits and Most Backward Classes MBCs.

articleTitle: Jaishankar hits back at Pakistani journalist at UN: ‘A terrorist country is asking me’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jaishankar,
description: Jaishankar responded sharply after a Pakistani journalist accused India of sponsoring terrorism, as the minister addressed mounting security risks facing ships and seafarers.
body_raw: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar Friday sharply responded to a Pakistani journalist who questioned him about terrorism at the United Nations headquarters in New York. The exchange took place after Jaishankar and Liberian Foreign Minister Sara Beysolow Nyanti addressed reporters on the launch of a new Group of Friends focused on the safety and security of shipping and seafarers. After the ministers remarks, the Pakistani journalist asked Jaishankar, When will your government stop sponsoring terrorism in Pakistan? Jaishankar responded, A terrorist country is asking me that question. Come on. WATCH 81st UNGA Session A terrorist country is asking me that question, says EAM Dr S Jaishankar in response to a Pakistanis attempt at heckling EAM with a terrorism question pic.twitter.comwIfu9OUhfO - ANI ANI September 25, 2026 Indias Permanent Representative to the UN, Harish Parvathaneni, then told the journalist, You have heard your reply. You have heard your response, loud and clear. The exchange came a day after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif was questioned by an Indian journalist as he entered the UN headquarters. The journalist asked Sharif, When will you stop harbouring terrorists? Sharif did not respond. He was also asked later when Pakistan would prosecute Lashkar-e-Taiba chief Hafiz Saeed, according to reports. WATCH New York, US Prime Minister, when will you stop harbouring terrorists? ANI questions Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif as he enters the UN headquarters. Pakistani PM refuses to answer. pic.twitter.comIMANrxWYb5 - ANI ANI September 24, 2026 India, Liberia launch maritime security group The Jaishankar exchange came during a press interaction linked to a new maritime initiative launched by India and Liberia on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly. The two countries announced the establishment of the Group of Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers, bringing together countries concerned about the growing risks faced by commercial vessels and their crews. India, as a major source of seafarers, and Liberia, as the largest shipping registry, have come together to highlight the safety and security of shipping and seafarers, Jaishankar said at the meeting. He said attacks on commercial shipping and seafarers were no longer exceptional occurrences. In the last few months, commercial shipping and marinas have been subjected to repeated attacks in the Gulf, the Red Sea, and its vicinity, Jaishankar said. These actions that disrupt maritime commerce and cost innocent lives are simply indefensible. The group comes amid continuing security risks in key maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman, Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Bab-el-Mandeb and the Black Sea. India has a particular interest in the issue because of the large number of Indian seafarers working aboard Indian-flagged and foreign-flagged vessels. Recent attacks highlight risks to Indian seafarers The maritime security concerns have also had a direct impact on Indian crews. On September 23, one Indian national was killed after the bulk carrier MV Cape Dao came under attack off Oman while heading towards India. The Indian Embassy in Oman said it was coordinating with Omani authorities over the safety of the crew, while Indias Ministry of External Affairs said 19 of the 20 Indian seafarers aboard the vessel had been rescued. The attacks have also disrupted commercial shipping through the region. Reuters reported this week that only two commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on September 21, compared with a pre-conflict average of about 125 large commercial ships a day. Two vessels were also reported struck in the strait, although responsibility for those attacks had not been established. India has separately issued safety advisories for its seafarers operating in conflict-affected waters. The government has said it is maintaining monitoring and emergency-response mechanisms for Indian crews in the Gulf region. The new India-Liberia grouping is intended to bring greater international attention to the safety of commercial shipping and seafarers as maritime routes face growing risks from ongoing conflicts. With inputs from PTI, Reuters

articleTitle: Why are Form 7 applicants facing FIRs? BJP delegation meets DGP, seeks review
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka BJP delegation DGP Saleem Form 7 SIR row
description: A Karnataka BJP delegation claimed that criminal cases were being registered against BJP workers for submitting Form 7 objections and the police were being subjected to political pressure.
body_raw: A Karnataka BJP delegation met Director General and Inspector General of Police DGIGP M A Saleem on Saturday, urging a review of FIRs registered in connection with Form 7 applications during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. The delegation was led by state president B Y Vijayendra, former chief minister B S Yediyurappa and Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R Ashoka. The BJPs intervention comes amid the state chief electoral officer agreeing to initiate legal action against those responsible for allegedly filing bulk Form 7 applications to remove eligible voters. The controversy intensified after fresh instances of mass Form 7 submissions targeting alleged voter deletions surfaced a day after Chief Minister D K Shivakumar cited three FIRs registered over similar complaints. In a memorandum submitted to DGIGP Saleem, the delegation alleged that criminal cases were being registered against BJP workers and political activists for submitting Form 7 objections and claimed that the police machinery was being subjected to political pressure. It urged the police to ensure that criminal proceedings arising from the electoral-roll exercise were based on evidence and due process. The BJP said Form 7 is a statutory mechanism provided by the Election Commission of India for an elector to object to the inclusion of a name or seek deletion of an existing entry from the electoral roll. It argued that the mere submission of multiple Form 7 applications during an electoral-roll revision exercise could not, by itself, constitute a criminal offence. How did Form 7 applications become public? BJP The memorandum cited provisions of the SIR guidelines and the Manual on Electoral Rolls, 2023, and claimed there was no prescribed restriction on the number of Form 7 applications that could be submitted. It also referred to the provision for bulk objectionsForm 7 applications during the revision exercise. The delegation referred to FIRs reportedly registered in Bhalki in Bidar, Belagavi and Narasimharaja in Mysuru under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. It argued that criminal liability should be determined based on the specific role and conduct of each accused, including whether an individual knowingly furnished false information or forged a signature or document. The BJP also raised concerns over the alleged circulation on social media and political forums of Form 7 applications containing applicants names, mobile numbers and signatures. It sought an inquiry into how the documents came into the public domain and identification of those responsible for their disclosure. The delegation urged the DGP-IGP to ensure that the same legal standard was applied to all applicants and complaints arising from the SIR exercise, irrespective of political affiliation, and that genuine violations, if established, were proceeded against in accordance with law.

articleTitle: Sanjay Dutt recalls jail days when cop told him ‘no cigarette’: ‘Sir, yahan bidi toh milegi’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sanjay Dutt
description: Sanjay Dutt recalled his jail days, revealing how a cop tried to unsettle him by denying him cigarettes, only for the actor to quip, 'Sir, yahan bidi toh milegi.'
body_raw: Sanjay Dutts arrest and subsequent imprisonment in connection with illegal possession of arms remains one of the most talked-about controversies of his career. Although the actor was eventually cleared of the terrorism charges, he was convicted under the Arms Act and served multiple prison terms. He has often spoken about that difficult period of his life, and recently recalled how he managed to stay strong despite the circumstances. Speaking to Shekhar Suman on his talk show Shekhar Tonite, Sanjay Dutt said that the authorities tried to break him during his time behind bars, but he refused to let the circumstances affect him. Addressing the audience, Shekhar said, Sanjay Dutt was put in an anda cell, yet he kept his sanity. He then asked the actor, Did you ever feel like ending your life in such situations? Never, Sanjay replied. Shekhar Suman went on to point out that people often fail to acknowledge their mistakes, but said Sanjay Dutt had accepted his own. He then asked the actor, Which was the moment when you felt the weakest? I knew my dad and family went through a lot of things. But I never felt weak, Sanjay said. Shekhar then asked, What are you made of? He listed some of the difficult experiences Sanjay had faced, saying, He lost his mother. He lost his father. He lost his first wife. He went to a rehabilitation centre. He overcame fourth-stage cancer. He went behind bars multiple times. But yet, he is intact. ALSO READ Bhushan Kumar is Bollywoods richest at Rs 36,300 cr wealthier than SRK, Big B combined As the audience cheered, Sanjay Dutt recalled the first time he was handcuffed in front of his father, actor Sunil Dutt. When for the first time the police came and put handcuffs on me, my dad went into shock. With tears in his eyes, he said, What are you doing with my son? I hugged him tight and told him, Why are you letting these handcuffs bother you? Dont be like that. It is just a procedure, please dont be upset. While in reality, it was killing me from the inside. But I had to be strong for him, he recalled. He added, Thats how I moved throughout this trial. It went on for 24 years. When Shekhar Suman asked him where he found the strength to get through the ordeal, Sanjay Dutt responded with a chant of Har Har Mahadev. They thought they could break me Sanjay Dutt also recalled being lodged in cells alongside other criminals and said that his years of privilege never made him feel superior to those around him. You know, for so many years, I am not someone who is egoistic about his stardom. I dont have that in me, he said. The actor credited his parents decision to send him to The Lawrence School, Sanawar, with shaping his outlook on life. So many times, we have sat on the ground on a set and have eaten food. I sat with workers so many times to eat food on set. I dont care about these things, he said. According to Sanjay Dutt, the authorities believed that taking away the comforts associated with his celebrity status would eventually break him. But nothing happened to me. Because I didnt break. They went in shock. Unki phat gayi. They mocked me. One of them came to me and said, You wont get any cigarette here. Now, what will you do? So my reply was, Sir, yahan bidi toh milegi, he recalled. All these changes didnt bother me, so they got tensed that how is he so grounded and unaffected, the actor added. Sanjay Dutts prison terms Sanjay Dutt was first arrested on April 19, 1993, in connection with the 1993 Bombay serial blasts case and faced charges under the Terrorist and Disruptive Activities Prevention Act TADA and the Arms Act over the illegal possession of weapons linked to the case. Sanjay spent around 18 months in jail as an undertrial across different periods before being granted bail by the Supreme Court in October 1995. In 2007, a special TADA court cleared him of terrorism-related charges but convicted him under the Arms Act and sentenced him to six years in prison. In 2013, the Supreme Court upheld his conviction under the Arms Act but reduced his sentence from six years to five. Sanjay Dutt surrendered in May that year to serve the remainder of his sentence and was released from Punes Yerawada Central Jail on February 25, 2016, after receiving remission for good conduct.

articleTitle: Four women, many struggles, one gold: India’s 4x400m relay team wins title
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India's Kiran, Prachi, MR Poovama, and Vithya Ramraj celebrate after winning gold medal in the women's 4x400m relay. (PTI)
description: Kiran Pahal, Prachi Choudhary, M R Poovamma and Vithya Ramraj had contrasting paths to their shared destination: India's only athletics gold at the 2026 Asian Games
body_raw: For Kiran Pahal, running was once an act of defiance. Her father had to fight an entire village in Sonipat to allow his daughter to pursue athletics. For Prachi Choudhary, a farmers daughter from Saharanpur, the dream of a DSP post in the UP Police has been a driving force. Before leaving for Nagoya, she submitted her measurements for the uniform, hoping to turn that ambition into reality. MR Poovamma had to find her way back from a doping ban and depression, with her husband and mother helping her rebuild. Vithya Ramraj, the daughter of an autorickshaw driver, had already broken Indias oldest athletics national record in Nagoya before taking the track for the relay. Four women, from different corners of the country, carrying different expectations. On Tuesday, at Mizuho Park, they won Indias first and only track-and-field gold medal of the Asian Games in Nagoya, reclaiming the womens 4x400m relay title with a time of 329.69. In the last edition in Hangzhou, China had beaten India to gold, but this quartet proved why Indian women remain favourites with a seventh gold in the 4x400m relay at the Asian Games. It was also a victory that capped Indias most successful day of the Games, so far. Neeru Dhanda, who had been hospitalised with an illness 10 days ago, won gold in the womens trap shooting event. India also won its first-ever medal in the mixed 4x100m relay - a bronze Gulveer Singh added a bronze to the two silvers he had already won the womens high jump produced a bronze and, Indian boxers secured significant victories to march into the finals. But the womens 4x400m relay gold shone brightest. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage The rain had soaked the track, but the four Indian women had a gold medal to chase. The route to it was anything but straightforward. Kiran got off to a slow start, handing over the baton in third place. Poovamma took over and set about making up ground. With every stride, she said, the snapshots of her recent struggles flashed in front of her. The dope ban, the depression, the lonely comeback. She thought of her husband, who managed her training programme while continuing to work and cook for her, and her mother, who travelled to Pune to ensure she could train without distractions. When my issues were going on, I was so depressed. I dont know what situation I went through. It was my family and my husband, she said. The veteran, who had won relay gold at the 2014 and 2018 Asian Games, dug into her decade-plus experience and pulled India into the podium position, showing that age - she is 36 - had not slowed her down. Prachi took over with India in front and held the advantage, charging towards a gold medal, and the DSP post. I missed it last time because I won just a silver medal, she said. Before leaving for Nagoya, I submitted my measurements for the uniform. Vithya saw Prachi march towards her, and felt her heart beating fast. She had already broken PT Ushas four-decade-old national record in the 400m hurdles, clocking 54.75 seconds for bronze and won silver in the 4x400 metres mixed relay. Now, she had one more job to finish. She surged into the final lap with the lead, but Bahrains Salwa Eid Nasser was beginning to make her presence felt. Having received the baton in last place, Nasser tore through the field, picking off runners one by one and closing the gap. The pressure mounted. Vithya could see the Bahraini closing in, and the uncertainty began to creep in. I told myself, Its the last race of your season, Vithya. Go for it. Whatever happens, come on, Vithya, you have to fight until the finish line. They all three did good, now its your turn. So I went for it, she said. And she held on. As Nasser closed in, Vithya drove towards the finish line, refusing to yield. The rain continued to fall, the gap continued to narrow, but Vithya had enough left to bring India home in 329.69. Bahrain finished second, China third. For four women whose careers had been shaped by very different struggles, the finish line offered a common reward. Poovamma had returned from the lowest point of her career. Kiran hoped the medal would lighten the burden she carried for her family. Prachi had taken another step towards a long-held dream. And Vithya had found one more moment to fight through the pressure. Four women, four journeys, one relay that brought them together - and brought India back to the top of the Asian Games relay podium.

articleTitle: In Andhra, poll officers told to make videos of voter recertification exercise
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The ECI has also said that anyone whose name is left out during or after SIR, including young and first-time voters, can apply for inclusion through continuous updation.
description: Authorities said this was meant to ensure transparency, with the CEO also directing DEOs to keep their social media handles active and post at least two photos and two videos each day.
body_raw: Andhra Pradesh Chief Electoral Officer Vivek Yadav has asked District Election Officers to post photos and videos of the re-verification of Absentee, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others ASDDO category electors, officials said - a development that comes as election officials embark on an exercise to re-verify the status of the electors not included in the draft electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision process. According to officials, DEOs have been asked to record photos and videos of BLOs testimonials during the door-to-door re-verification exercise, as well as those of young and first-time voters, and voters whose names were deleted from the draft rolls but eventually added after the notice phase. Testimonials relating to claims, objections and the notice phase, videos of Electoral Registration Officers EROs briefing BLOs, and those of DEOs campaigns in colleges for first-time voters are also to be recorded. Authorities said this was meant to ensure transparency, with the CEO also directing DEOs to keep their social media handles active and post at least two photos and two videos each day. The posts must tag the CEO and the ECI, mention the names of polling stations, the Assembly constituency and district, and carry the tagline No eligible voter is left out. The CEO said that from October 8, BLOs will conduct door-to-door visits with lists of electors who were not included in the draft roll for verification. The lists include 44,89,512 electors who were not found at their given addresses during the enumeration phase from June 15 to July 24 this year, as well as another 1,73,071 electors found ineligible during the notice phase. Eligible voters whose names were inadvertently left out will be facilitated to submit Form 6 for inclusion in the electoral rolls. The final roll will be published on October 16. Any voter left out of the final October 16 roll and voters becoming newly eligible to vote can submit Form 6, the office of the chief electoral officer said.

articleTitle: TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh alleges attack on car en route to Mamata rally

body_raw: Trinamool Congress TMC MLA Kunal Ghoshs car was allegedly attacked in West Bengals Hooghly district while he was on his way to attend party chief Mamata Banerjees rally in Serampore. Ghosh claimed that a group of miscreants attacked his vehicle at Shokher Bazar in Uttarpara, damaging its front and rear windscreens and hurling eggs at the car. They attacked with sharp weapons and tried to kill me, Ghosh said, adding that he would return to Kolkata and visit the police headquarters. At around 3.30 pm, Ghosh reached the police headquarters, Bhabani Bhavan, where his car was allegedly stopped at the main gate. He said he had emailed the director general of police regarding the incident. Mamata hits out at BJP Banerjee reacted sharply to the incident. It is not very good sign for democracy. They BJP are trying to stop us at any cost so that we cant hold the rally. We got permission from the high court 15 days ago. Such atrocities on Opposition parties do not happen even in African countries, she said. BJP leader Rahul Sinha denied the allegations, saying it was nothing but their TMCs inner fighting. Local MLA Dipanjan Chakraborty said people of the state had rejected Mamata Banerjee. Peace and development is prevailing in Bengal now. In this situation, Mamata Banerjee is trying to create disturbance.People will not tolerate this. They protested in a democratic manner, he added. articleTitle: 7 die as SUV crashes into parked truck in Gujarat’s Bhavnagar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The police officer said all seven men worked in the shipbreaking yard and commuted daily from Bhavnagar to Alang, a 50-km distance.
description: The incident took place around 9.45 am near Trapaj village at the trijunction of roads leading to Bhavnagar, Talaja and Alang.
body_raw: Seven people died after an SUV travelling from Bhavnagar to Alang in Gujarat crashed into a stationary truck on Tuesday morning. All the victims worked at the Alang shipbreaking yard and were headed there when the accident took place. The incident took place around 9.45 am near Trapaj village at the trijunction of roads leading to Bhavnagar, Talaja and Alang. Manish Nakum, Deputy Superintendent of Police, told The Indian Express that six people died on the spot and one was rushed to a nearby hospital. The survivor succumbed to injuries later, said Inspector PM Desai of Alang police station. The police officer said all seven men worked in the shipbreaking yard and commuted daily from Bhavnagar to Alang, a 50-km distance. The truck driver had parked the vehicle on the service road and had gone to have snacks when the SUV hit the truck from behind, the Inspector added. The front part of the SUV was completely damaged, indicating the intensity of the crash. CCTV videos of the crash show that the impact caused the parked heavy vehicle to move forward. Visuals showed the SUVs windshield shattered and its roof damaged. The doors of the vehicle had to be forced open with iron bars to recover the victims bodies. Inspector Desai said the bodies had been sent for post-mortem and the identities of the victims would be revealed shortly after.

articleTitle: When did India begin latest round of talks with Russia, Ukraine? Jaishankar reveals
articleFeaturedImageAlt: **EDS: THIRD PARTY IMAGE** In this image posted on Oct. 5, 2026, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar along with Institute of Economic Growth (IEG) President NK Singh, left, and former Singapore Foreign Minister George Yeo, right, during the concluding session of the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave (KEC 2026) on ‘India and the World: Adaptive by Design’, in New Delhi. (@DrSJaishankar/X via PTI Photo)
description: Jaishankar said New Delhi started the latest round of conversations with both sides in July this year, after commercial ships came under attack from both sides in the Black Sea.
body_raw: A day after stating that India is in touch with both Ukraine and Russia over the ongoing conflict, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar on Monday spelt out the kind of conversations India was having with the two sides amid evolving dynamics. However, he emphasised that while its not an easy situation, it would be a big positive even if Kyiv and Moscow were to agree on something of a limited nature. The minister said that from the very beginning, India has held that this conflict is unlikely to be resolved on the battlefield. Therefore, it was important to have negotiations between the parties. There were actually negotiations in the early stages of the conflict. Though we have been maintaining for some time that both parties should come to the table, and there were a number of conferences where countries gathered to express their support for peace, but often they would gather in the absence of Russia, he said, in reference to initiatives like the Swiss peace conference. However, he added that New Delhi has always believed that there was no point of having a gathering dealing with the Ukraine conflict where Russia is not there. He said New Delhi started the latest round of conversations with both sides in July this year, after commercial ships came under attack from both sides in the Black Sea. In fact, after losing Indian sailors in such attacks, New Delhi had strongly conveyed its condemnation to both sides and also summoned envoys to register protest. In July, there were attacks on civilian shipping by both Russia and Ukraine. And in the course of those attacks, some Indian sailors were killed, some were injured. We regard these attacks as completely unacceptable, whether it is in the Black Sea, the Red Sea, or the Gulf. So, we protested very strongly to the Russians, to the Ukrainians. I myself took it up with the foreign ministers of both countries. We started getting active initially to secure the maritime shipping and the mariners involved in that, he said. Jaishankar added that those conversations brought out the nature of the cargo which was being shipped. And there was the concern expressed about the grain exports which had come to a halt in the Black Sea. So the conversation developed into whether non-attack on shipping is good, but is there a possibility of facilitating the shipment of grain. it got linked to energy. So, it became a somewhat broader conversation, added the minister. The conversations started with Prime Minister Narendra Modis meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek in August. After that, Jaishankar went to Kyiv to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, which was followed by another discussion between Modi and Putin in New Delhi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. We still keep in touch with both sides. Its not obviously an easy situation. Its not something which anybody can say with a high degree of confidence that something is going to come out. But it seems definitely an effort worth making, he says, adding that resolving concerns about grain, fertiliser and fuel are in Indias as well as the Global Souths interest. We have the interests of the parties themselves that if they can even agree on something of a limited nature, we feel that in the given circumstance thats a big positive, he said. He also spoke about the need to fix the United Nations, not work around it, and how this was going to be an age of flux for the world, with conflicts and tariff volatility making it turbulent, underlining that responding to the challenges emerging out of the choppy waters is the task at hand. Im very confident that we will rise to the challenges, Jaishankar said during an interactive session at the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, where he shared the dais with former foreign minister of Singapore, George Yong Boon Yeo, during the closing session. The minister, however, said that as Indias record shows, we have been able to rise to the challenges, whether it was Covid, or the challenge of a double conflict today. The challenges of energy, food, fertilisers - we need to factor them into our thinking, plan and respond. That in a sense is the task before us. And Im very confident that we will rise to the challenge, he said. Jaishankar also spoke about championing the voice of the Global South. The Global South expects India to articulate on the world stage, he said. On reforms needed for the United Nations and other multilateral institutions, Jaishankar said, The UN is gridlocked, adding that a few countries were resisting its reforms. However, he said that the US is one of Indias principal strategic partners - our largest economic account, our biggest trade account, it is a very major critical defence partner.

articleTitle: ‘Is 140/90 a normal blood pressure reading at age 60?’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: blood pressure
description: Is 140/90 normal blood pressure at age 60? A cardiologist explains what the reading means, why one reading is not enough, how to measure BP accurately at home and when high blood pressure needs urgent attention.
body_raw: A blood pressure reading of 14090 mmHg at age 60 can leave you wondering whether it is something to watch or simply a number that comes with getting older. Does being 60 change what counts as normal blood pressure? One such question was posted on Quora Is 14090 a normal range of blood pressure at the age of 60? We reached out to Dr Aseem Dhall, Director HOD, Cardiac Sciences, ISIC Multispeciality Hospital, to understand what this reading means and when it needs attention. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Is 14090 normal at 60? Not quite. A blood pressure reading of 14090 mmHg is not considered an ideal or normal reading for most adults, including people around 60, the cardiologist clarifies while adding that the reading falls in the high blood pressure range under commonly used guidelines. However, one reading alone does not confirm hypertension, he assures while explaining that blood pressure naturally fluctuates through the day, so repeated readings taken correctly give a better indication of a persons usual blood pressure. Does getting older make 14090 acceptable? Being 60 does not automatically make a reading of 14090 normal. Age can affect the blood pressure target a doctor recommends, but it is only one factor. Different guidelines may use slightly different thresholds and targets, says Dr Dhall. Doctors also consider overall health, medications and other medical conditions. For older adults, treatment may need to be individualised, particularly when there is a risk of dizziness or falls. The important point is to avoid assuming that high blood pressure is simply a normal part of ageing. What if 14090 keeps showing up? This is where repeated readings become important. If someone repeatedly records blood pressure around 14090 at home, it suggests that their blood pressure may be higher than recommended and should not be ignored. Home monitoring can help because readings can be taken in a familiar setting over several days. The person should maintain a record of their readings and share it with their doctor. Based on the pattern and the persons overall health, the doctor can determine whether hypertension is present and whether lifestyle changes, monitoring or medication are appropriate. If you already take blood pressure medication, dont change the dose yourself. Do not start, stop or change blood pressure medicines without medical advice. Before worrying about the number, check that youre measuring it correctly A home reading is useful only if you take it properly. Stress, anxiety, recent exercise, caffeine, smoking and even talking can temporarily push the number up. A single blood pressure reading can temporarily rise because of stress, anxiety, recent exercise, caffeine, smoking or even talking during the measurement. In fact, an incorrect sitting position or a poorly fitting cuff can also affect the result. For an accurate home reading, use a validated upper-arm monitor with the correct cuff size. Avoid exercise, caffeine and smoking for at least 30 minutes beforehand and empty your bladder. Before measuring, sit quietly for about five minutes, keep your feet flat on the floor and support your arm at heart level. Do not talk during the measurement. Take two readings about one minute apart and record both. Doing this at consistent times over several days can give your doctor a clearer picture of your usual blood pressure. What should the target be in your 60s? Once repeated readings confirm consistently high blood pressure, the next question is what level to aim for. No single target suits everyone. For many adults being treated for hypertension, doctors aim for blood pressure below 13080 mmHg when it can be achieved safely, but the target may be adjusted depending on the persons health and tolerance. People with diabetes, kidney disease or heart disease may require closer monitoring and an individualised target. The treating doctor should decide the goal after considering medications, other conditions, age and the persons risk of side effects. When does high BP require urgent attention? A reading of 14090 is different from a severely elevated reading. A blood pressure reading of 180120 mmHg or higher is considered severely elevated. If a repeat measurement remains at this level, seek medical advice promptly. If the high reading is accompanied by chest pain, severe breathlessness, severe headache, confusion, vision changes, difficulty speaking, weakness or numbness, seek emergency medical care immediately. The symptoms matter as much as the number. In such a situation, do not wait for the blood pressure to come down on its own.
