articleTitle: Did AI write France’s breakout novel? What we know about the Thelyson Orelien controversy
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Haitian-Canadian author Thélyson Orélien.
description: An AI detector, an anonymous accuser and a bestselling debut: what we know about the claims against Thélyson Orélien, and why the detectors can't agree.
body_raw: On the same day that 38-year-old Haitian-Canadian author Thlyson Orlien became the toast of French literary society after winning the 2026 Prix du Roman Fnac for his debut novel Ctait ca ou mourir It Was Either That or Die, a social media post accusing him of using artificial intelligence to write it brought the credibility of the prestigious French prize itself into question. Within three days, the controversy widened to include plagiarism allegations about his earlier journalism, and his Canadian publisher suspended promotion of the book. The X account Balance ton Claude, a play on both the French MeToo slogan Balance ton porc and Anthropics AI assistant, had 92 followers when it accused on Monday, September 21. It said it had run passages from the novel through the AI-detection tool Pangram. Pangram has been at the heart of several of this years AI scandals, from Mia Ballards Shy Girl to the Commonwealth Short Story Prize. We tested several passages, at various points in the manuscript, and got almost always the same result 100 AI, the account wrote. It concluded the novel was written almost entirely by artificial intelligence. The post went viral, accumulating more than 4.9 million views and over 1,800 reposts at the time of publication. Orlien has denied the accusation. His French publisher, Grasset, has expressed its absolute confidence in him. His Canadian publisher, Editions du Boral, has taken a more cautious line. The Acadmie Goncourt administers Frances oldest and most prestigious literary prize, the Prix Goncourt, awarded annually to the author of the best and most imaginative prose work of the year. On Friday, it removed Orliens novel from its longlist to preserve the integrity of the Goncourt prize and the academy itself. Who is Thlyson Orlien? Orlien was born in 1988 in Gonaives, Haiti. He studied law in Haiti and left for Canada after the 2010 earthquake. Before leaving, he worked mainly as a poet. In Canada, he continued his studies in economics and political science at the Universit de Montral and worked as a journalist and columnist. He settled in Montreal and moved to Ottawa in 2022. His writing is described as being inhabited by memory, exile, and the question of belonging. What is the novel about? Ctait ca ou mourir is set in Port-au-Prince, the capital of Haiti. It follows Jonas Dorlon, a teacher whose neighbourhood is stormed by heavily armed teenagers. With his house on fire, he realises he faces an impossible choice leave or die. He escapes and crosses 12 countries the Dominican Republic, Brazil, the Darin jungle between Colombia and Panama, Central America and Mexico. He then crosses the US border and eventually settles in Canada. The French edition runs to 272 pages, and translation rights have been sold in around 20 countries. It is the biggest seller in the history of Editions du Boral since the Canadian publisher was founded in 1963. Grasset published it in France on August 19. By mid-September, it had sold nearly 32,000 copies in France. It has won four French prizes the Prix du Roman Fnac the Prix Mduse the Prix Premiere Plume the Prix Roman News Publicisdrugstore It is longlisted for the Goncourt, the Mdicis, the Femina, the Renaudot and the Prix Dcembre. Orliens response Orlien says he began writing the novel in autumn 2017 and completed a first draft in 2019, years before generative AI tools became widely available. I have always loved creation and writing. I cant see why I would feel compelled to use a machine, he told the French newspaper Libration. He argues that the stylistic features critics flagged are rooted in Haitian and Caribbean literary traditions repetition, rhythm, and cascading imagery. He cites Aim Csaire and Jacques Stephen Alexis as influences. He said he was putting together a dossier with his publishers in France and Quebec to prove that he wrote the book himself. I did not expect attacks of this kind. I am not sad, but angry, he said, adding that he had faced racist attacks since his recent arrival in France. By Thursday, speaking to AFP from a literary festival in Manosque, he described a will to silence him. The plagiarism allegations On Wednesday, the controversy widened. La Presse, the Montreal daily, reported that a 2013 column Orlien wrote for the paper was almost entirely a lightly reworked translation of an article the Philippine Star published days earlier. Franceinfo identified another text of his containing a paragraph taken word for word from a 2014 opinion piece by former Colombian minister Rodrigo Botero Montoya. Other alleged examples have since circulated online. The plagiarism allegations concern texts from more than a decade ago, not the novel. On Thursday, Boral suspended all promotional activity for the book, citing Orliens well-being. The book remains on sale. In a statement, the publisher called plagiarism an unacceptable practice. On the AI question, it said it was impossible at this stage to confirm or refute the allegations and urged caution. The Salon du livre de lEstrie in Quebec cancelled his appearance and withdrew his guest-of-honour title the same day. A pattern of accusations Orlien is the latest in a string of authors to face AI allegations this year. The Nigerian author Jerry Falade lost a reported 2 million deal with Minotaur Books after his agents withdrew the manuscript, saying they could no longer verify how he wrote it. Falade denied using AI to write the book, said he had used it only for research, and called the allegations racially motivated. Mia Ballard, a Black American horror author, had Hachette pull her novel Shy Girl after a New York Times investigation. She denied using AI and said an editor she hired for the self-published version used AI tools. H M Wolfe, also a Black American author, faced accusations after a study reported by The Atlantic found that Pangram scored her bestselling novel Daggermouth as 60 AI-generated. She denied it, and her publisher, Simon Schuster, and her fans stood by her. Falade has argued that all three Black authors who landed major deals this year had them cancelled or disrupted over AI suspicions. Many of Orliens defenders see the same pattern in his case. The Commonwealth Short Story Prize drew international headlines when Pangram flagged The Serpent in the Grove by the Trinidadian writer Jamir Nazir as AI-written. Nazir had been named the Caribbean regional winner in May. After reviewing the regional winners drafts, timestamped documents, notes, and outlines, the Commonwealth Foundation cleared him and named him overall winner on July 1. The uproar was such that Granta, the British literary magazine, ended its partnership of more than a decade publishing the prizes winning stories. What the Goncourt says Immeediately after the allegations were levelled, Philippe Claudel, president of the Acadmie Goncourt, said he had at no moment suspected the novel might have been written with AI. Lets not throw opprobrium immediately on an author whose book is currently riding high, he told Franceinfo. I always give the benefit of the doubt to those who are thrown to public opinion like this. Claudel also questioned the timing of the accusation, asking why it was surfacing now. You have an author who is Haitian and Canadian, who is Black, who is francophone, who is foreign, who writes about migrants, he said. He had earlier cautioned that the books place on the second list is not guaranteed either way, since a vote will decide it. But if irrefutable proof emerges by October 6, obviously we would take a decision, he said. In the wake of plagarism allegations, the Goncourt on Friday removed the novel from the longlist. Are AI detectors reliable Pangram, the tool at the centre of the controversy, claims a false positive rate of about one in 24,400 documents, based on its own English-language benchmarks. According to two recent studies, one from the University of Chicago and one from Belgium, it is the most reliable detector on the market, ahead of GPTZero, OriginalityAI and RoBERTa. AI detectors look for statistical patterns, such as low perplexity or burstiness, that correlate with machine-generated text. Some experts say these patterns can also appear in texts that use non-standard forms of English or French. The results so far point in different directions AFP ran the accounts excerpts through its own verification tool, InVID-WeVerify, which judged them very probably written by a human. Seven other detectors AFP tested gave wildly divergent results. One gave 100 AI, two concluded the opposite, and four varied from excerpt to excerpt. Other newsrooms that repeated the Pangram test largely reproduced the accounts findings. La Presse submitted the entire novel and got a score of 94. CBC replicated the 100 result using different excerpts. Franceinfos own excerpts scored 100 AI, and one passage run through GPTZero scored 87. Radio-Canada ran the other Goncourt-listed novels available digitally in Quebec through Pangram, and all came back 100 human. Franceinfo tested Orliens earlier work, published in 2014 and 2015, and Pangram classified it as 100 human. That result has given many pause, though it cuts both ways it suggests the tool is not simply misreading his style.

articleTitle: 1965 war postscript: Inside Lahore-Amritsar ceasefire talks and mind games
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Military Digest 1965 India Pakistan War Ceasefire Talks
description: During the post-1965 ceasefire negotiations in Lahore and Amritsar, cross-border military diplomacy saw unexpected moments—from personal reunions at the airfield to a surprising discourse at the Golden Temple.
body_raw: An interesting postscript to the 1965 India-Pakistan war was the series of joint military meetings held in Lahore and Amritsar, where delegations from both nations discussed the fine print of the ceasefire and coordinated the withdrawal of forces. Held under the auspices of the United Nations and in accordance with the Security Council resolution of November 5, 1965, the talks alternated between the two cities and were coordinated by Brigadier-General Tulio Marambio, the UN Secretary-Generals representative. The Indian delegation was led by Lt Gen Harbaksh Singh, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief of Western Command, accompanied by Lt Col TS Padde GSO-1, Western Command and Captain Amarinder Singh, ADC to the Army Commander. The Pakistani side included Lt Gen Bakhtiar Rana GOC 1 Corps, Lt Col SA Hasan, Lt Col Riaz Azim, and Brigadier Gul Hassan Khan. Initially, the UN representative proposed meeting at a neutral camp midway between Lahore and Amritsar. However, Lt Gen Harbaksh rejected the site as barren and inhospitable, suggesting instead that the Indian team visit Lahore first, followed by the Pakistani delegation visiting Amritsar. When the UN envoy asked whether he had the Indian governments permission to go to Lahore first, Harbaksh replied that he did not need to seek permission and that his decision was final, as he wrote in his book In the Line of Duty-A Soldier Remembers. Diplomatic protocols in Lahore The Indian delegation arrived in Lahore in February 1966 aboard a UN aircraft with General Marambio. Upon arrival, Lt Gen Harbaksh inspected a Pakistan Army guard of honour. At the airfield, a personal connection surfaced the Indian Army Commander recalled seeing his ADC, Captain Amarinder Singh, scion of the Maharaja of Patiala, embracing the young Pakistani Captain commanding the Guard of Honour. Amarinder later explained that the officer was the son of Colonel Majeed, his fathers former Military Secretary, and that the two had played together as children on the Patiala palace grounds. While guiding Lt Gen Harbaksh through Lahore to refresh his pre-partition memories, Pakistani officials attempted psychological one-upmanship. Banners in Urdu were put up across the road advertising rides in a captured Indian vehicle for eight annas. The vehicle was the Jonga jeep of Maj Gen Niranjan Prasad, GOC 15 Infantry Division, which had been captured in a sugarcane field on Lahores outskirts after the officer narrowly escaped an ambush, leaving behind his starred plate, flag, and personal papers. Lt Gen Harbaksh objected to the provocative banners and urged his hosts to turn the car around. When the Pakistani counterpart mentioned making over Rs 10,000 from the rides, Harbaksh denied losing a Jonga jeep and warned that if such trickery continued, he would produce ten Jongas adorned with Pakistani flags for inspection when the Pakistani delegation visited Amritsar. Flowers and spiritual discourses during Amritsar visit When the Pakistani delegation made its reciprocal visit to Amritsar, Lt Gen Harbaksh arranged a tour of the Golden Temple. The visit occurred while Akali leader Sant Fateh Singh was staging a protest inside the shrine premises, preparing for a fast unto death and self-immolation to demand Punjabi Suba a separate Sikh-majority state. Despite the political tension, locals were informed in advance. The reception given to us was tremendous. The shopkeepers of Amritsar were all standing in front of their shops and showered us with flowers. On arrival at Harmandir Sahibs gate, we were received by the whole Prabandhak Committee Shiromani Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee, which had lined up with garlands of flowers, to be presented to every member of the delegation, and the United Nations officers, wrote Lt Gen Harbaksh. Towards the end of the tour, the Pakistani General requested a meeting with Sant Fateh Singh, expecting the leader to make critical remarks about the Indian government. Instead, speaking in Punjabi, Sant Fateh Singh stated that the people of India and Pakistan should not fight each other, offered a discourse on the principles of the Sikh faith, and presented sets of Punjabi religious books to the leaders of the Pakistani and UN delegations.

articleTitle: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
articleFeaturedImageAlt: express investigation election commission gyanesh kumar special intensive revision
description: From keeping them in the dark to adding new voters, deleting names, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi flagged "unauthorised, illegal" moves.
body_raw: The Election Commission of Indias ECI Special Intensive Revision SIR, which began in Bihar in June 2025, an otherwise routine clean-up of the rolls, has struck more than 13 crore names off the draft voter rolls in 30 States and Union Territories. This has put the Election Commission at the centre of intense public debate over its role in deciding who gets to vote - and who doesnt. An investigation by The Indian Express reveals that questions were raised on these very issues within the three-member Election Commission EC itself, time and again through much of this same period. By two of the three Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, no less. The national rollout of the SIR has been under the supervision of all three Commissioners. But Sandhu and Joshi have formally objected, on record, at least 14 times over the last 10 months - four times on a single day - to decisions taken and orders issued, they say, without their knowledge. The stakes couldnt be higher. For, the objections relate to the core of the Election Commissions mandate new voter registration, deletion and restoration of voters in the rolls filing of appeals against orders restoring voters in the SIR process and the custody, and security, of the entire electoral roll itself. All objections related to these were copied to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, too. Some were sent to Deputy Election Commissioners under their watch. In one such written objection, Sandhu complains that the EC acted against the written advice of two Commissioners and claim its action was unauthorised and illegal. Most recently, in a radical departure from the norm, Joshi and Sandhu wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary complaining about changes in work allocation that, in effect, removed a layer of oversight of the IT backbone for the electoral rolls. They made it clear these changes had been done without their knowledge and they struck them down. It was after this, on September 9, that the CEC and the two ECs met, their first full meeting in four months. The Indian Express has seen each of these exchanges, and interviewed a range of officials in New Delhi, Kolkata, Goa and Mumbai, to reconstruct the extent of the disquiet within, unprecedented in scale and significance within the constitutional authority that is entrusted with the free and fair conduct of the nations elections. More so, because all three were handpicked by the NDA government and appointed under the 2023 Act by a selection panel of the Prime Minister, Union Home Minister and the Leader of Opposition. The Opposition member, Congresss Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury, recorded a dissent over the appointment process when Sandhu and Gyanesh Kumar were named Election Commissioners in March 2024. LoP Rahul Gandhi, too, recorded his dissent when Kumar was elevated to CEC and Joshi appointed in February 2025. On September 21, The Indian Express sent a questionnaire to the Commission on the issues flagged by the two Election Commissioners asking what was done to address their concerns. There was no response. Both the ECs were also sent emails on September 21, asking them whether their concerns were addressed. Both the emails also sought responses on whether these issues were flagged during the September 9 meeting. Both emails were followed up by phone calls on Monday and Tuesday. There was no response. 1. Whos a new voter, why was Form-6 changed? In July this year, as first reported by The Indian Express, a form that every adult citizen has to fill to become a voter started asking a question it never did earlier. Linking the application to the SIR, it asked if the new voter or their parents grandparents exist in the electoral roll of last SIR. Applicants could not proceed without answering it. This despite the fact that in May, Joshi had warned on file that Form 6 could not be changed in this manner without the government amending the rules, and Sandhu had agreed. The change was made anyway. After The Indian Express first reported this change in July, Sandhu put on record on August 13 that it was unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately. Until Monday morning, that question was still there. 2. Who should have access to the electoral roll? The Commissions strongest defence against every political allegation on electoral roll rigging has been that the roll preparation is decentralised. Each constituencys voters list is prepared and controlled by its Electoral Registration Officer, a statutory authority on the ground. Usually, the ERO is the Sub-Divisional Magistrate. This list sits on a software, ERONet, and its successor ECINet. Over the past year, the two Commissioners have repeatedly questioned whether EROs access to this list is now being restricted. This was what Joshi red-flagged in May this year - the SIR was gathering pace across states - as gradual centralisation of the electoral roll database and proposed an audit to certify that no one, except the concerned statutory authorities, has credentials to make any change in the voter database. In August, Sandhu reiterated this. He recorded that state-level election officials were reporting they dont have proper and complete access to the ERONet portal, the digital system through which they maintain the electoral roll. He flagged that the Election Commissions Director General of IT Seema Khanna doesnt have any legal authority to restrict proper and complete access and freedom to operate, as given by law, to the statutory authorities. The defence the Election Commission has relied on for decades, the two ECs were saying, is being dismantled from inside its own IT division. 3. West Bengal who authorised the appeals? The SIR was the most deeply contested in West Bengal. There was no evidence of its role in the election outcome. Of the 294 seats that went to polls, in 49, the SIR deletions exceeded the victory margin. But in these, the spoils were almost evenly shared - 26 were won by BJP and 21 by TMC. But the manner in which names were struck off prompted the Supreme Court, in February 2026, to take the last leg of the SIR out of the Commissions hands and get judicial officers to decide on the plight of 60 lakh voters flagged for logical discrepancies. Of these, 27 lakh electors were subsequently deleted by the Commission. The court then ordered tribunals of retired High Court judges to hear appeals against those decisions. Last week, the Commission told the court that there were 38 lakh appeals pending before the tribunals 22.21 lakh filed by deleted voters seeking to be restored. The other 16.10 lakh were filed against voters the judicial officers had included, seeking their deletion. The Commission did not say who filed those. This was the issue flagged by Sandhu - about the Commission appealing against voters whom judicial officers had included. In August, he wrote to Commission officials asking, Who was authorised to file these appeals on behalf of ECI, and by whom? and Who actually filed these appeals on behalf of ECI? He recorded that neither he nor Joshi nor the current Chief Electoral Officer of West Bengal had been informed about the basis or process of filing the appeals. 4. Goa why did the software reject eligible voters? The same centralisation, which Joshi and Sandhu had flagged repeatedly, ended up disenfranchising potential voters in Goa. On January 29, the Supreme Court ordered that voters flagged for logical discrepancies during the SIR be allowed to submit documents and be heard before the final roll was published. A logical discrepancy is a mismatch the software throws up when it tries to link a voter to a parent or relative on an older roll a name that doesnt match, an age gap that doesnt add up. Goas EROs heard these cases. On the documents produced, they found 97 voters eligible for the final roll. The software had no way to record that decision. Between February 11 and 17, the office of Goas Chief Electoral Officer wrote eight times to Gyanesh Bharti, the Senior Deputy Election Commissioner in charge of the state, copying Director General of IT Seema Khanna every time, asking for the rollback option that would let EROs reverse the earlier deletions as the Supreme Court had directed. The requests went unanswered as the deadline for publication of the final electoral roll approached. The provision was not enabled in time. The 97 were left off the final voters roll in Goa. Ninety seven voters is a small number, however this goes far beyond 97 - it is the Election Commission of Indias job to ensure that every valid vote gets counted. Objections within what the law requires The Commission is a constitutional body under Article 324, made up of the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners who are equal in rank. The CEC is first among equals. He does not have the power to decide alone. Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office Act, 2023, all business of the Commission, says Section 18, shall, as far as possible, be transacted unanimously. If the CEC and the Election Commissioners differ in opinion on any matter, the matter shall be decided according to the opinion of the majority. The same section allows the Commission to settle its own procedure and the division of its work, but only by unanimous decision. Indeed, both Commissioners invoked these provisions in their notes to remind the Commissions officers how it is meant to work. On April 16, Sandhu told the Commissions senior officers that many communications go out in the name of the ECI but they do not have the approval of the Commission, and that from then on every communication must have it, as per the provisions of 2023 Act. Eight days later, Joshi told the same officers that several communications are disseminated in the name of the ECI without the requisite approval of the Commission, and that all future communications must have that approval, in accordance with the provisions of Article 324 of the Constitution and the Act.

articleTitle: Farmers’ column: Widowed 19 years ago, 54-year-old Sukhpal now runs Rs 50-lakh worth enterprise
articleFeaturedImageAlt: farmers
description: A resident of Guradi village in Budhlada tehsil, Mansa, Sukhpal has turned dairy farming into more than a means of livelihood.
body_raw: Nineteen years ago, Sukhpal Kaur, at the age of 35, lost her husband. But she still had two young sons and a family to support. Today, at 54, she has a dairy herd valued at more than Rs 70 lakh, an enterprise that generates over Rs 50 lakh annually, adequate savings, and a livelihood that employs two permanent workers. She has enough to live on and hasnt lost her passion to keep building. A resident of Guradi village in Budhlada tehsil, Mansa, Sukhpal has turned dairy farming into more than a means of livelihood. It has become her business, her financial independence and, even at 54, the work that she still wants to do. With an intermediate education, she has also acquired years of practical experience in managing cattle. She understands their feed requirements, monitors their health and nutritional needs, and keeps track of their disease. At present, her herd has around 40 cattle - 26 adult animals and 14 young ones, including Murrah and Neeli Ravi buffaloes, and Punjab and Himachal Jersey cows. For Sukhpal, they are not simply livestock. They are assets that she has built over years of work. Sukhpal said, I sell 150 to 200 litres of milk daily currently, which increases to even 300 litres during some months of the year, supplying households as well as village dairy channels. The rate I get is around Rs 80 to 85 per kg. The dairy generates approximately Rs 50 lakh annually from milk sales. After feed, labour, and other expenses, she says she retains around 50 per cent of the sales value. Two permanent workers assist her with the dairy. She owns around 12 acres of familial land and keeps only about one acre of her land for green fodder, while purchasing most of the remaining fodder. Feed management remains one of the major costs of the enterprise, she says. Yet she considers the dairy profitable and increasingly valuable for another reason. The animals themselves have become a substantial asset. Most of her well-maintained adult cattle could fetch Rs 3 to 4 lakh each if sold today. However, she says she is not looking to cash out. My focus now is on retaining animals and expanding the herd. That marks a change from my earlier years, when livestock sales were an important part of my income. I would sell around six animals a year, earning approximately Rs 12 to 13 lakh from livestock sales, apart from milk income. After she lost her husband, she started her journey with only a couple of cattle, which they had as a couple. Managing a large dairy alongside farming became difficult, so she leased out around 11 acres of her agricultural land, earning around Rs 6 lakh annually from the lease rent. The land could have provided her a relatively secure livelihood. But I chose dairy farming over agriculture I love being among them and taking care of them, she said. She does not describe work as something she needs to escape from after accumulating enough assets. For her, continuing to earn and build is part of remaining independent. One of her sons has been working in Canada for the past seven years, while the other runs a travel business in India. My sons are very supportive, but still I want to work. She says, Their independence has not changed mine. I manage my dairy, maintain my savings and earn my own income. I want to be a giver, not a taker, she says. Sukhpal also says she has never made government financial assistance the basis of her livelihood, has not sought enrollment in monthly-benefit schemes, and has never travelled free on a bus despite the governments scheme of free travelling in public vehicles. Women must not take pride in getting Rs 1,000 per month from the government but should first overcome their own idleness, she says. Sukhpal believes every rural woman should have an income of her own - not necessarily through a job, but by creating self-employment. Even two cows or buffaloes can be the beginning of a dairy that grows into a herd of 10 within a few years where that investment is difficult, even two goats can provide a woman with her own income and lead to a huge expansion in a few years. She believes livestock can also give children fresh milk and milk products, which mitigates several types of malnutrition, while involving them in productive dairy work after studies can keep them away from excessive social media use, idleness, and harmful influences, including drugs. For her, self-employment is ultimately about a woman earning for herself, strengthening her family and giving her children a better direction in life. If you are not working anywhere, create work for yourself. Start small, protect the asset, reinvest, and grow.

articleTitle: ‘Some of them need a job, so they go after us’: Travis Head hits back at former Oz players
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Australia opener Travis Head in action. (Reuters)
description: Opener accuses past greats of "putting a bullet" through current team after Matthew Hayden's scathing assessment of selectors
body_raw: Australia opener Travis Head has launched a strong defence of his team and the national selectors, accusing former players turned critics of putting a bullet through the current side ahead of the first Test against South Africa in Durban on Friday. Heads remarks came a day after Matthew Hayden, the former Australia opener, described the selectors recent picks as the greatest pile of mediocrity that weve seen in a generation of cricket. Haydens criticism, made on a podcast, was aimed at the recall of Nic Maddinson, who is back in the Test squad after nearly 10 years following injuries to Josh Inglis and Cameron Green. Speaking at a press conference on Wednesday, Head did not name any pundit directly but made his feelings clear. I think its unfairly judged a fair bit from a group of past players, pretty much that put the bullet through a lot of players, which I think is unfair, he said. But thats what theyre paid to do. Some of them need a job, so they go after us, and thats totally fine. Head added that the current group was equipped to handle the scrutiny. This group is strong enough to deal with those sorts of things. Thats how it is. Its unfortunate sometimes to have some of that feedback from a generation of players that we have huge respect for, but thats the caper. Hayden had accused the selectors of disrespecting first-class cricket, arguing that batters should average 45 or more before being considered for Test selection. Maddinson, 34, carries a first-class average of 37.11. Head, however, backed the decision to bring in an experienced campaigner. We need mature guys that know what they need to be doing, he said. And I think that revolves back to why weve been so good over a period of time and why Australian cricket was so good back then in that era, because youd bring in the Mike Husseys of the world, who are 30, who are tried and tested and know what they need to do. Former Australia captain Allan Border also weighed in, suggesting that Head, 32, would face his toughest challenge as an opener against the South African attack and might be better suited to batting at number five. Head brushed that aside too. I have laughed at a fair bit of it because if a traditional opening batter had pushed out the same sort of numbers in his first 20 innings, I think hed be pretty safe and not talked about in the way that it has been talked about, he said. Its a lot of headline stuff.

articleTitle: World Teachers’ Day: What global shortages and India’s numbers tell us
articleFeaturedImageAlt: world teacher day 2026
description: UNESCO warns the world needs 44 million teachers by 2030, as India's high pupil-teacher ratios highlight severe global school shortages.
body_raw: World celebrates Teachers Day on October 5, and this year it carries a familiar warning. UNESCO estimates that the world needs 44 million more primary and secondary teachers by 2030 to achieve universal basic education. About 15 million of them are needed in sub-Saharan Africa. In Southern Asia, where India sits, UNESCOs analysis put the gap at 7.8 million. The shortage is not confined to poorer regions. Nations across Europe and North America also find it hard to recruit and retain teachers. Heavy workloads, modest pay and low recognition are among the reasons UNESCO cites. This years observance also marks 60 years of the ILO-UNESCO recommendation on the status of teachers. The issue, then, is not only how many teachers a country has. It is whether its schools can hire, place and retain them. Read World Teachers Day 2026 Why October 5 is observed? India has more students for every teacher than the average across Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development OECD member countries a group of 38 mostly high-income, developed nations at the school level, particularly in primary education. The latest OECD data from its Education in Glance put Indias student-to-teaching-staff ratio at 27 students per teacher in primary education, compared with an OECD average of 14. At the lower-secondary level, Indias ratio is 19 against an OECD average of 13, while at upper secondary it is 21 against an OECD average of 13. The gap is also visible against several major economies. In primary education, the ratio is 21 in the US, 25 in the UK, 15 in Germany and 18 in France, similarly Spain is at 15, much below India. Because OECD data relies on a unified global reporting standard, it allows analysts to directly compare these different education systems on equal terms. Also Read He once saw education as his only way to a job. Now, hes a national award-winning teacher Student-to-Teacher ratio India and other major economies Country Group Primary Education Lower-Secondary Education Upper-Secondary Education India 27 19 21 OECD Average 14 13 13 United Kingdom UK 25 14 14 United States US 21 15 16 France 18 12 13 Germany 15 13 13 Spain 15 11 11 Source OECD Education at Glance This is where a recent SBI Research report on Indian higher education needs to be read separately. The report says Indias pupil-teacher ratio in higher education, covering universities and colleges in regular mode, was 23 in 2023-24 and describes the figure as broadly comparable with international levels. It also points to a wide variation within India Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Goa have a PTR of around 14, while Bihar is at 57, Jharkhand at 48 and Uttar Pradesh at 33. The reports comparison, however, is about higher education and should not be used against the OECD school-level figures above. Government data also show that PTR varies sharply by level and state. What is Indias true school baseline vs the OECD numbers? For school education, the latest UDISE data provide the Indian baseline. In 2024-25, Indias PTR was 20 at the primary level, 17 at upper primary, 15 at secondary and 23 at higher secondary. These figures are not identical to the OECD classification, which separates lower and upper secondary education differently. The OECDs internationally comparable dataset, using its own classification and methodology, records India at 27 in primary, 19 in lower secondary and 21 in upper secondary for 2024. The OECD measure is based on the number of students relative to teaching staff and is reported separately by education level. Its latest table uses 2024 data and covers primary, lower-secondary and upper-secondary education. The OECD also reports that the average student-to-teacher ratio across its member countries fell from 15 to 14 in primary education between 2015 and 2024. Also Read How this Kargil teacher turned abandoned war bunkers into Social Science labs Among major English-speaking education systems, the differences are visible even within the OECD. The US has 21 students per teaching staff member in primary education, 16 at lower secondary and 20 at upper secondary. The UK records 25, 25 and 33, respectively. Australia has 14 at primary level, while data for its secondary levels are not available in the OECD table. Canada records 16 at primary and 13 at upper secondary, with lower-secondary data unavailable. Ireland has 13 at primary and 14 at upper secondary. New Zealand records 16 at primary, 13 at lower secondary and 14 at upper secondary. The school-level picture also helps put SBI Researchs higher-education claim in context. Its report says Indias higher-education teaching workforce grew from about 13.7 lakh in 2013-14 to 17.3 lakh in 2023-24. But the increase in the overall number of teachers has not removed vacancies in centrally funded institutions. Citing parliamentary data, SBI Research says 14,042 of 41,351 sanctioned teaching posts were vacant, or 34per cent. The vacancy rate was 39per cent in IITs, 54per cent in IIITs, 29per cent in NITs and 31per cent in IIMs. Professor-level vacancies were particularly high, at 56.2per cent.

articleTitle: Repo rate hiked by 25 bps to 5.50 pc: Why RBI has hiked interest rates; EMIs set to rise
articleFeaturedImageAlt: sanjay malhotra
description: GDP growth in FY27 hiked 40 bps to 7.1 pc; Inflation forecast up to 5.2 pc
body_raw: The Reserve Bank of India RBI has increased its policy repo rate by 25 basis points bps to 5.50 per cent, marking the first rate hike since February 2023 and signalling a shift towards tighter monetary policy amid rising inflationary pressures, elevated crude oil prices and a challenging global interest-rate environment. The Monetary Policy Committee MPC has changed the policy stance to calibrated tightening from neutral indicating further hike in the interest rates is a likelihood. The MPC has also hiked the growth projection from 6.7 per cent to 7.1 per cent in FY27 in the wake of the higher economic activity in the country. The panel also raised the inflation forecast to 5.2 per cent for FY27 from 5 per cent previously. The decision by the policy panel to hike rates comes after nearly two years of monetary accommodation. The increase is expected to push up borrowing costs across the economy, affecting interest rates on home, personal and vehicle loans, while also providing some support to deposit rates. RBI Monetary Policy Meeting October 2026 LIVE Announcing the monetary policy, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said high frequency indicators show economic activity holding momentum in the second quarter albeit with some moderation when compared to first quarter. The policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or pause, depending on the evolving conditions, Malhotra said. The RBIs move follows growing concerns that inflationary pressures are becoming more broad-based. Retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August, remaining above the central banks medium-term target of 4 per cent for the third consecutive month, although it continues to remain within the RBIs tolerance band of 2-6 per cent. The last rate hike-when it was hiked from 6.25 per cent to 6.50 per cent - occurred in February 2023, making any potential increase the first in over three-and-a-half years. Governor Sanjay Malhotra hinted at policy recalibration due to signs of inflation normalizing, while Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta acknowledged that conditions for a rate hike may arise during the year. Recent CPI data shows headline inflation at 4.82 in August, marking the third consecutive month above the 4 medium-term target, though still within the RBIs 2-6 range. Forecasts project inflation to rise to an average of 5.9 in Q4 2026 before moderating in the following quarters. As inflation risks persist, a more extended rate hike cycle may be on the horizon. Why has the RBI raised rates? The decision comes against a backdrop of rising food and energy prices, weather-related disruptions and higher crude oil prices. Maharashtra has declared drought in about 265 of its 358 talukas, while the possibility of drought has also been flagged in Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan. Reservoir levels across India are around 20 per cent below last years levels, raising concerns about agricultural output and the rabi crop. The possibility of El Nino conditions extending into 2027 remains another key risk to the inflation outlook. Global developments have added to the pressure. Crude oil prices have risen above 100 a barrel amid geopolitical tensions, raising concerns about imported inflation and Indias external balance. The West Asia conflict and the Russia-Ukraine war have also added uncertainty to the global economic outlook. At the same time, global interest rates remain elevated. The US Federal Reserve recently raised its policy rate by 25 bps to 3.75-4 per cent, while US benchmark yields have also risen sharply by 53 bps to 5.31 per cent in a month. The benchmark 10-year bond yield in India has gone up by 25 bps to 7.21 per cent in a month. A narrowing interest-rate differential with the US could increase pressure on Indias financial markets and currency, making the RBIs policy response more important. Foreign investors have been pulling out funds from India in the wake of the rise in yields in the US. What does the rate hike mean for borrowers? The increase in the repo rate is expected to feed into lending rates, particularly for loans linked to external benchmarks. Home, personal and vehicle loan borrowers could see their equated monthly instalments EMIs rise as banks pass on the higher cost of funds. Loans linked to the marginal cost of funds-based lending rate MCLR may also become more expensive. Banks, however, have flexibility in revising MCLR-based rates depending on their funding costs, liquidity conditions and deposit mobilisation. Deposit rates could also rise marginally as banks reassess their funding requirements. The extent of any increase will depend on liquidity and broader funding conditions. Savers and depositors would like to see the deposit rates going up as high retail inflation has cut into their savings. Inflation risks remain broad-based The RBIs decision to hike retail inflation to 5.2 per cent comes as price pressures extend beyond food and perishable commodities. Higher energy prices, food inflation and weather disruptions are adding to the risks. Analysts expect retail inflation to peak at around 6 per cent in the third quarter and average about 5 per cent in FY27. The possibility of sustained inflation above the RBIs target has strengthened expectations that monetary policy may remain tighter for longer. Economists have pointed to the widening gap between consumer and wholesale price inflation, with rising input costs gradually spreading across farming and non-farming sectors. Growth outlook The rate increase comes amid strong economic growth. Indias GDP grew 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of FY27, beating expectations, with consumption, investment and exports supporting momentum. GST collections, automobile sales and bank credit have also remained healthy. While analysts expect FY27 growth at 7.3 per cent, RBI was conservative in its assessment and raised its growth projection to 7.1 per cent from the earlier estimate of 6.7 per cent. However, higher crude prices, elevated global interest rates, geopolitical tensions, trade-policy uncertainty and weather disruptions pose risks to growth in the coming quarters. The 25-bps increase to 5.50 per cent therefore marks an important change in the RBIs policy direction. With inflation becoming broader and global financial conditions remaining tight, the central bank faces the challenge of containing price pressures without significantly weakening domestic growth.

articleTitle: After Janhvi Kapoor’s deepfake controversy, Peddi producer says ‘youth is polluted’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Janhvi Kapoor
description: Peddi producer has condemned the misuse of AI following the Chuttamalle deepfake targeting Janhvi Kapoor, saying the youth have become polluted.
body_raw: Days after deepfake content featuring actor Janhvi Kapoor was widely circulated on the internet, Mythri Movie Makers co-founder Y Ravi Shankar has spoken out against the growing misuse of artificial intelligence AI to generate deepfake content. Janhvi was last seen in Peddi, which was produced by the same production house. It has become really easy to sling mud at each other on social media. On top of that, they are now misusing AI, and no one knows whats real or fake, Ravi Shankar said. The youth have become polluted, be it online or otherwise. It is at a time like this that we need films with divine power that instil a fear of God. It is only beneficial to society. The deepfake that prompted his remarks was an AI-manipulated version of the Chuttamalle song from Jr NTRs Devara Part 1, in which Janhvi Kapoors likeness was digitally altered to create sexually explicit imagery. Jr NTR and Janhvi Kapoor both issued public statements against such videos. It is to be noted that his own film Peddi was also severely criticised for sexualising Janhvis character and normalising assault. Some of the scenes featuring her character were changed after viewers raised objection. Also Read Janhvi Kapoor calls her Chuttamalle AI video with NTR assault Reality of being a woman Talking about Hanuman Ansh, the Neem Karoli Baba biopic whose Telugu release was being announced at the same press event, he said, We are very happy that this film not only conveys a message and shows God and reality, but has also become a commercial superhit. Rs 400 crore for Rs 2 crore is a slap in the face Ravi Shankar announced that Hanuman Ansh will release in Telugu on October 9. Made on a budget of less than Rs 2 crore, the film has already earned Rs 425 crore worldwide at the box office, and is continuing to make money at the ticket counters. It is like a slap in the face to see a film with a Rs 2 crore investment gross Rs 400 crore in collections, he said. We are spending crores of rupees with not much to show for it. But to get Rs 400 crore for Rs 2 crore, thats a real pan-Indian film. He urged producers across the industry to ensure the film reaches every possible audience. Wherever possible, if you have skipped releasing it in any language, please release it in all languages. This film is a massive hit, not just revenue-wise. Its a much-needed film, he said.

articleTitle: Naman Dhir had barely bowled in IPL. Then came his 3/31 on India debut
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Naman Dhir
description: Despite limited IPL bowling under the Impact Player rule, Naman Dhir showed on his T20I debut that he remains a genuine bowling option, taking 3/31 against West Indies in Lucknow.
body_raw: For a player who had bowled just 8.4 overs without a wicket in his IPL career, Naman Dhir could hardly have made a stronger case for his bowling. The Impact Player rule may have reduced his opportunities at Mumbai Indians, but the 26-year-old insisted he was ready. Ive been bowling for a long time. Its not like Ive just started. In IPL, yes, theres an impact player rule, so you see me bowling less. But its not like I havent bowled, Ive bowled a lot and Ive had a great experience here too. Ive got wickets, I hope Ill keep doing well in the future, he said after taking 331 on his T20I debut against West Indies in Lucknow. IPL prepares you for international cricket. Theres a lot of competition there. So I guess if youre playing IPL with a team like Mumbai Indians, then youre prepared for a big level, so you dont feel so much pressure coming here, as I feel right now, he added. His performance also showed that the lack of bowling in the IPL had not left him short of match practice. Dhir said he has continued to bowl regularly in practice and is comfortable handling different workloads. Theres an impact player rule in IPL. Its not like I dont practise I practise there too. Its the same here too. So theres nothing new for me if I get 4 overs, 2 overs, if I get 6 or 7 overs in one-day, theres nothing new for me. Its a normal thing for me. I just have to focus on my plans and try to execute them. Dhirs three wickets came after he watched Axar Patel bowl in the powerplay and felt the slower pace was helping him on the turning pitch. I saw Axar bhai bowling in the powerplay, so he was bowling a little slow. It was turning. And in my mind, I thought if I bowl a little slow with the wicket gripping, I can get them out. So I just stuck to my basic plans and bowled, and I got good results, he said. There was a personal side to the call-up too. Dhir was at the Ranji Trophy camp in the PCA when he got the news, having just come off a good tournament for himself and his team. Obviously, it was a great feeling when I got the call. I was in the Ranji Trophy camp, in PCA, our tournament had just ended, a very good tournament had gone for me, for our team, so it was a surreal feeling. I was with my friends, so right away I called my father, he was emotional I got a little emotional. Obviously, every kid has a dream to play for the country, so if you represent the country, if your name is mentioned in the team, its a big deal, especially, I am from a small town, so especially for me, no one has played from there yet, so its a big deal for me, its a big deal for the area around us. Dhir also made it clear that while his batting may get more attention, he has continued to work hard on his bowling. Even if you havent seen me bowl, but Im bowling as much as Ive come here Ive practised as much as Ive come here, so its not like Im a batting all-rounder or a bowling all-rounder, yes, my batting is a plus point, but at the same time, Im working as hard as Im bowling.

articleTitle: ‘Was doing my duty’: BLO who stopped bulk submission of pre-printed SIR Form 7s in Hyderabad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The first instance of bulk Form 7s in Hyderabad surfaced on October 1, 2026, in Musheerabad constituency.
description: The video of this BLO rejecting the Form 7s went viral when Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee raised the matter on Saturday. “If some are targeting people by filing bulk Form 7s, we will take strict action,” the CEO’s office said.
body_raw: His voice may have gained unlikely attention, with Telangana Congress sharing a now-viral video of him rejecting a bunch of Form 7s allegedly filed by a BJP booth-level agent BLA, but this BLO from Hyderabad chooses not to make much of it, simply saying, I was just doing my duty. He was posted at Booth 173 in the Goshamahal constituency of Telangana Capital when the said Form 7s of the Special Intensive Revision SIR were filed by a BLA in September-end. Its not possible to accept these Form 7s, he is heard saying. Speaking to The Indian Express, the BLO, who works as a Junior Assistant at Osmania Medical College, said, The forms had printed EPIC numbers. There were no names on them. I had no instructions to receive such forms from my superior officers. Hence, I decided not to accept these. The video of this BLO rejecting the Form 7s went viral three days later, when Telangana Pradesh Congress Committee TPCC on Saturday released the video of pre-printed Form 7s of SIR surfacing in Hyderabad. I dont know how that video went viral. I was only stating my point of view, the BLO said. When asked whether he was scared to reject the forms, he said, No, I was not. I was doing my duty. He, however, did not want to be identified as he did not want publicity for an act which was done as part of the BLO duty. TPCC released the video two days after they complained to the Chief Electoral Officer CEO about apprehensions of a larger conspiracy to bulk delete voters as part of the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls 2026. The forms, which the TPCC had accessed, had no names. They were in the last stages of being filed by the BJP BLA, a Congress source alleged. In a press conference on Sunday, BJP state president N Ramchander Rao said his partys BLAs have not submitted bulk Form 7s. The Congress is spreading malicious propaganda against constitutional institutions like the Election Commission, he added. Form 7s are used by electors if they want to delete their own name or to object to any other elector in their constituency. Similar instances The first instance of bulk Form 7s in Hyderabad surfaced on October 1, 2026, in Musheerabad constituency. Pre-printed applications were allegedly filed by a BLA of the Bharatiya Janata Party BJP, seeking deletion of a total 31 electors, who included a Congress BLA and his family members. In another case, a pre-printed Form 7 surfaced in Bahadurpura constituency. This, too, was flagged by the TPCC. In the Goshamahal case, the BLO refused to accept the bulk pre-printed forms, a TPCC leader told The Indian Express. When asked about the complaints, Chief Electoral Officer Sudarshan Reddys office told The Indian Express that an inquiry into the matter is on. If some are targeting people by filing bulk Form 7s, we will take strict action, the CEOs office said. According to TPCC, as per the original plan of BJP BLAs, the forms were to be submitted only after October 1, to inundate the election authorities who are already under the weight of lakhs of pending hearings from the notice phase. The period for filing claims and objections comes to an end on October 7. A TPCC source said, If the CEO does not take action, we will approach the police. This is a matter of protecting peoples right to vote. Telangana BJPs chief spokesperson NV Subhash told The Indian Express that bulk Form 7s are being submitted against Rohingyas who are not citizens of the country. He said, Political parties, including the AIMIM, the Congress and the BRS are supporting enrolment of Rohingyas. There is nothing wrong in filing Form 7s to deny them voting rights. He said AIMIMs Asaduddin Owaisi should personally ensure that the Rohingyas dont get voting rights in India. If he is a true Indian, he should see to it, Subhash said. Earlier in the day, Owaisi, the MP from Hyderabad, said, If false Form 7s are being filed, we appeal to the Election Commission to take action against those responsible for it. If this drama does not stop, remember protests bigger than those at Delhis Jantar Mantar will take place on the roads and streets of Hyderabad.

articleTitle: Taking antibiotics? Your morning milk, coffee or alcohol could interfere with them
articleFeaturedImageAlt: This applies not only to milk, cheese and yogurt but also to calcium-fortified juices, tofu and calcium supplements. The medicine may need to be taken separately from these foods, depending on the antibiotic prescribed. (AI Generated Image)
description: Calcium can bind to antibiotic molecules in the digestive tract and form a compound that the body cannot absorb easily
body_raw: You take an antibiotic on time, with a glass of water, and assume the medicine will simply do its job. But sometimes, what comes with that tablet matters too. The milk in your morning tea, a bowl of curd, your regular cup of coffee or even a glass of wine can interact with certain antibiotics. These interactions can affect how much of the medicine the body absorbs, how it is broken down or how strongly its side effects are felt. This does not mean every antibiotic needs to be taken on an empty stomach or that patients need to change their entire diet. The interaction depends on the specific antibiotic. Knowing which food or drink matters can, however, help the medicine work as intended. Dairy and calcium-rich foods can be a concern with certain antibiotics, particularly tetracyclines such as doxycycline and tetracycline, and fluoroquinolones such as ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin. Calcium can bind to these antibiotic molecules in the digestive tract and form a compound that the body cannot absorb easily. As a result, less of the medicine reaches the bloodstream. This applies not only to milk, cheese and yogurt but also to calcium-fortified juices, tofu and calcium supplements. The medicine may need to be taken separately from these foods, depending on the antibiotic prescribed. Grapefruit and pomelo can interfere with the way certain medicines are processed in the body. With erythromycin and certain other macrolides, grapefruit can affect enzymes involved in drug metabolism, potentially changing antibiotic levels in the blood. This is why patients should check whether their particular antibiotic has a grapefruit or pomelo warning rather than assuming all fruits are safe with every medicine. High-acid foods and juices, including citrus fruits and tomatoes, are also sometimes discussed with penicillins such as penicillin V and ampicillin because acidity can affect the stability of some medicines. However, this interaction is not the same for every penicillin or every formulation, so the specific prescribing instructions should be followed. Some food and drink interactions do not primarily affect absorption. Instead, they can increase the risk of unwanted effects. Linezolid, an oxazolidinone antibiotic, acts as a mild monoamine oxidase inhibitor MAOI. As a result, consuming large amounts of tyramine-rich aged, cured and fermented foods may cause a rise in blood pressure in some patients. Foods of concern can include aged cheese, soy sauce, salami, tap beer and red wine. Ciprofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone, can slow the breakdown of caffeine in the body. Excessive coffee, energy drinks or dark chocolate may therefore lead to stronger caffeine effects, including jitteriness, anxiety, insomnia or heart palpitations. Alcohol needs particular caution with metronidazole and tinidazole. The combination can produce a reaction, which may cause severe nausea, vomiting, flushing, rapid heart rate and intense headaches. Foods such as lentils, beans and whole grains are an important part of a healthy diet but high-fibre meals can affect the timing and absorption of some oral medicines. Fibre can slow stomach emptying and, depending on the antibiotic and formulation, may delay how quickly the medicine enters the bloodstream. The answer is not to stop eating fibre or nutritious foods whenever an antibiotic is prescribed. Instead Check whether the antibiotic should be taken with food or separately from meals. Ask about dairy, calcium, iron and magnesium supplements. Check whether caffeine, alcohol, grapefruit or pomelo need to be avoided. Follow the specific instructions for the antibiotic rather than applying the same food rule to every medicine. There is no single antibiotic diet. The important point is to understand the particular medicine being taken. A small change in timing or an avoidable food interaction can sometimes make the difference between getting the intended benefit from an antibiotic and getting less than expected from the treatment. The author is senior consultant, Internal Medicine, Indraprastha Apollo Hospitals, Delhi

articleTitle: Shai Hope’s unbeaten 162 chases down 352 as India’s bowling leaves questions
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shai Hope played captain's knock, leading his team to a win with an unbeaten 162 vs India during 3rd ODI in New Chandigarh. (Express Photo by Kamleshwar Singh)
description: KL Rahul's century and Rohit Sharma's 92 went in vain as West Indies won by five wickets in the first men's ODI at the New PCA Stadium
body_raw: The New PCA Stadium was decked up for its first mens ODI, expecting local boy Shubman Gill to extend his dream streak. The law of averages was cruelly overdue after West Indies had dismissed him only once in 241 deliveries in two games. Gill deprived his home crowd of a spectacle. Instead, the day belonged to his counterpart Shai Hope, who watched Gill butcher a 406-run chase from behind the stumps three nights ago in Guwahati. Switching positions three times in six days, Hope went back to his sweetest spot at the top. He made his fifth century against India, his highest score at 162 not out, to power a consolation five-wicket win in an emphatic 352-run chase on Saturday. The Indian team management ticked off a few boxes on its batting wish-list, through a sparkling KL Rahul century and Rohit Sharmas 92. The bowling unit left more questions unanswered in a botched defence. Despite a batting order trimmed by injuries, the Windies top order kept Gills bowlers on their toes, matching the asking rate from the start. Indias new-ball struggles eased briefly when Sirajs inswinger castled John Campbell in the fifth over. The search for able back-ups hit a wall again when Hope and Amir Jangoo took apart debutant Anshul Kamboj in his opening spell. Kamboj had been pulled out midway through India As first-class fixture in Pondicherry on Thursday as Prasidh Krishnas replacement. He leaked 41 in five overs. ALSO READ Averages 68.58 at 5, four hundreds, best strike rate after AB KL Rahul is Indias Mr Indispensable Only a run-out, from Virat Kohlis quick reflexes, looked likely to end Jangoos 111-run association with Hope. Kuldeep Yadav skimmed without reward, and Naman Dhir emerged as an unlikely wicket-taker with a contentious caught-behind. Moving up from No. 3 in the previous game, Hope moved smoothly towards his fifth century against India and a second in succession. With few proven hitters in the lower half, an injury to Jewel Andrew and cramps in his legs, Hope slowed down drastically, taking 44 balls without a boundary from 87 to 126. That phase partly dented the chase before the captain waded into the last four overs. Gurnoor Brar and Kamboj traded control for a batch of looseners, and Hope and Gudakesh Motie carted them for eight boundaries in 14 deliveries, which took the chase away. Earlier, a full reveal of the middle order brought India a fourth centurion of the series in KL Rahul, who walked out with the bat for the first time this series. He picked up from where Rohit stopped, after Rohit had braved a sharpened new-ball barrage on length from the West Indies pacers. Jayden Seales and Matthew Forde combined to tempt Gill into an unusual adventure early on. It took only four consistent length deliveries before Gill impatiently missed a charged slap through cover. Seales pounded the deck harder next time, the angle cramping Gill as he nicked behind his hips to the keeper. Virat Kohli was gone the next ball, his fourth golden duck in over 300 outings, when Seales vicious in-ducker found the middle stump. With the pacers lengths rarely overspilling, Rohit measured his release after a watchful spell and pulled impulsively for six over square-leg in the 12th over, though the vision behind his favourite shot has fluctuated this series. He had nearly fallen to the stadium DJs plea for a maximum in the 10th over, miscuing a pull just over mid-wicket. Fifty balls in, Rohit slouched and pumped Alzarri Joseph over the square-leg fence, the same over that produced a reckless heave across the line before a leading edge parried over backward point. The venom of the pacers had dissipated by then, and Rohit switched gears against the left-arm spinners. Vitel Lewis and Gudakesh Motie bled boundaries as Rohit unfurled the sweep, the conventional and the slog, with brutal accuracy. Another abrupt swipe proved fatal, against seamer Keemo Pauls innocuous length ball, and he holed out at deep mid-wicket eight short of a third ton in four innings. Surviving a string of four dropped catches between his 13th and 69th delivery, Ruturaj Gaikwads weary half-century held the fort until Rahul shifted gears at five. With dismissive drives off the seamers at regular intervals, he reached fifty in 41 deliveries. Shepherding the lower order with a calm head, Rahul bought himself vital game time at number five after a patchy England series two months ago. He timed a chilling overdrive towards the close, five sixes in his last 12 deliveries, which reiterated his worth. It still fell short against another keeper-batters riposte. Brief scores India 3517 in 50 overs KL Rahul 129 not out, Rohit Sharma 92 Jayden Seales 362 lost to West Indies 3525 in 48.2 overs Shai Hope 162 not out, Amir Jangoo 67 by five wickets.

articleTitle: Market analyst claims Shah Rukh Khan’s Rs 12,500 crore net worth is 4x his contemporaries
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shah Rukh Khan's net worth is more than four times than that of Salman Khan.
description: Popular market analyst JS Khepar aka Jassi Tech claims Shah Rukh Khan's net worth is more than four times than that of his contemporaries Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar, and Aamir Khan.
body_raw: It may not come as a surprise that Shah Rukh Khan is counted among Indias richest actors. What is perhaps less widely known is the scale of the wealth gap between him and his A-list contemporaries, including Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar and Aamir Khan. Popular market analyst JS Khepar, aka Jassi Tech, recently claimed that Shah Rukhs net worth is more than four times that of each of these actors. Shah Rukh, Salman, Aamirs net worth From the data that I could last decipher, Salmans net worth is around Rs 3,000 crore to Rs 3,200 crore, said JS Khepar in a conversation with Siddharth Kannan, adding that Aamirs net worth is between Rs 1,900 to Rs 2,000 crore. Between both is Akshay Kumar, whose net worth lies between Rs 2,700 crore and Rs 2,800 crore, as per Jassi Tech. However, he dropped the biggest bomb when he revealed Shah Rukhs net worth. Hes the king I dont think his net worth is less than Rs 12,000 crore to Rs 12,500 crore. Thats why he the king, said Khepar on Siddharth Kannans podcast. Hes the badshah emperor in not only films, but also business. Look at KKR Wherever he has investments, theyre all zabardast outstanding, added the analyst. Shah Rukh Khans astronomical net worth includes his Indian Premier League cricket team Kolkata Knight Riders, his sea-facing palatial bungalow Mannat on Bandra Bandstand and a 4BHK sea-facing apartment in Shree Amrit Society on Carter Road in Mumbai, properties in London and Dubai, production house Red Chillies Entertainment, a VFX studio, and salaries from film projects and brand endorsements, among others. Aamir a test player, Akshay a T20 batsman JS Khepar also pointed out the differences between the investing and working styles of Salman Khan, Akshay Kumar, and Aamir Khan. Aamir is a test player, and Akshay is a T20 player. The approach is different in both the games. A T20 player is supposed to bat recklessly. A Test player is all about class. Aamir has that class. Whether his films work or not, he should remain Mr. Perfectionist, said Khepar. Hailing Akshay as a khiladi player even in the way he invests, the analyst said the actor has a presence everywhere. If there was a T5 format, he would have aced it too, he said, adding, And Salman is like a one-day cricketer. Kheper also lauded Akshays incredible fitness, which also allows him to pack in around four films within a year. JS Khepar also revealed that Salmans primary investment is in the real estate of Mumbai. Salman has a Midas touch. He turns mud to gold in real estate, and earns a lot of money there. One should learn that from him. The whole world loves him, including real estate. Theres only money and more money in Mumbais real estate. If not here, then where?, he added. Also Read Neem Karoli Baba film Hanuman Ansh refuses to bow to Drishyam 3, crosses Rs 419 crore mark Salman Khan owns multiple properties in the city, including the palatial Galaxy Apartments on Bandra Bandstand, where he resides with his joint family. Besides other properties on Carter Road and in Worli, Salmans net worth also boasts of a massive 150-acre farmhouse in the suburb of Panvel.

articleTitle: Hours before death, Nana Patekar messaged friend at 2:30 am he was unwell
articleFeaturedImageAlt: nana patekar
description: The veteran actor's friend saw the late-night message only later and reached his Goa home around 4 am to find him sweating and gasping. He was declared dead at 5.20 am. Maharashtra will give him a state funeral in Pune.
body_raw: Actor Nana Patekar messaged a friend around 2.30 am on Thursday to say he was unwell. Less than three hours later, the veteran actor, one of the most distinctive performers in Hindi and Marathi cinema, was declared dead after a cardiac arrest, according to the hospital where he was taken. He was 75. Patekars son, Malhar, confirmed the death to The Indian Express. Yes, the information is true. I am in Pune right now and reaching Goa. I will come up with detailed statement, Malhar said. He added that the funeral would be held in Pune. Patekar will be given a state funeral today, Maharashtra Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar announced, citing his unparalleled contribution to Marathi theatre and to Marathi and Hindi cinema. The decision was taken by the state government headed by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Shelar said. Patekar was at the familys house in Goa. His friend saw the message late, Dr Shekhar Salkar, chief of the oncology department at Manipal Hospital, Goa, told the media. From information that we have received, he Nana messaged his friend that he was not feeling well somewhere around 2.30 am.that he was feeling uncomfortable.but since it was late night time, I think his friend could not get the message properly on time, Salkar said. He friend reached his Patekars house around 4 am when he was sweating and gasping.then his caretaker came here, took the ambulance and went to the residence, which is nearby. When our ER team went there, they started cardiac massage because he was totally unresponsive. By the time, they reached he was unresponsive, they started CPR in the house, shifted him on CPR to the hospital, but by the time it was too late and he was declared dead at 5.20 am, Salkar said. Nana Patekar was brought dead at our hospital at around 4.20 am. We tried our best to give him CPR, he added. Salkar said the hospital did not know whether Patekar had a history of heart trouble. It is a case of cardiac arrest, but the cause we dont know, whether he was a known case of cardiac or he was on any tablets.that we dont have an idea. Because he was brought dead, the hospital registered a medico-legal case. The police came and the body has been shifted to Goa Medical College for post-mortem. After the post-mortem, the body will be handed over to the relatives, Salkar said. Tributes poured in from the film industry, from politicians and from his fans. Fadnavis said, Nana was as great-hearted as he was great on screen. He gave Marathi and Hindi cinema an entire era. From Krantiveer to Natsamrat, there is no parallel to the powerful and accomplished range of his acting. His death is a great loss to the film industry. Fadnavis also recalled Patekars work with farmers and drought-hit communities through the Naam Foundation. Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant wrote, Shocked and deeply saddened to learn about the demise of veteran actor Shri Nana Ppatekar Ji. With his remarkable journey across theatre, Hindi and Marathi cinema, his powerful performances and distinctive artistry left an indelible mark on Indian cinema.My heartfelt condolences to his family, friends, admirers and the entire film fraternity. Actor Riteish Deshmukh wrote, I am shocked beyond words. Feels like a truck has hit me. Deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Nana Patekar ji. An actor par excellence, incomparable to anyone, he carved his place in peoples hearts with his own unique style and brand of acting. There wasnt a role or a character he couldnt perform. He aced it all - a larger-than-life hero, a terrifying villain or be it his poker-faced comedy. He was a hero off screen too, and worked tirelessly through his charity for the good of the people. Patekar started out in theatre and made his film debut with Gaman 1978. He rose to prominence with Parinda 1989, which won him the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor. Krantiveer 1994 won him the National Award for Best Actor, and Agni Sakshi 1996 brought a third, for Best Supporting Actor. His other acclaimed films include Khamoshi The Musical, Ab Tak Chhappan, Apaharan and Raajneeti. He also showed a gift for comedy as the gangster Uday Shetty in Welcome 2007, a role he reprised in Welcome Back 2015. In Marathi cinema, he played a retired stage actor in Natsamrat 2016, one of his most celebrated roles. He also directed, wrote and starred in Prahaar The Final Attack 1991, and received the Padma Shri in 2013. Away from films, Patekar worked with drought-hit farmers through the Naam Foundation, which he set up with actor Makarand Anaspure in 2015. His career spanned nearly five decades.

articleTitle: Accident death insurance rejected over ‘false information’, Andhra man secures Rs 50 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: consumer commission insurance post-mortem report death
description: The Kurnool District Consumer Commission was hearing a complaint filed by the deceased man’s brother and nominee challenging the rejection of his Rs 50 lakh insurance claim following the man’s fatal road accident.
body_raw: An Andhra Pradesh consumer commission has directed a private insurance company to pay Rs 50 lakh to the nominee of a man who died in a road accident, after the insurer rejected the claim citing alleged misrepresentation of facts. The commission also directed the insurer to pay Rs 20,000 as compensation for mental agony and Rs 5,000 towards costs after finding that the insurers own investigator had called the accident genuine. Kurnool District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president Karanam Kishore Kumar and members N Narayana Reddy and S Nazima Kausar were hearing a complaint filed by Yellala Jagadeeshawara Reddy, brother and nominee of Divakar Reddy Yellala, who died in the accident in April 2025. The insurance policy had a sum assured of Rs 50 lakh and was in force when the accident occurred. The rejectionnon-settlement of the claim by the Opposite Party the insurer, without establishing a valid and substantiated ground under the policy terms and conditions, amounts to deficiency in service. The complainant, being the nominee under the policy, is therefore entitled to receive the Sum Assured of Rs 50 lakh. Having regard to the prolonged non-settlement of the legitimate claim and the hardship and mental agony caused to the complainant, he is also entitled compensation, the commission said on October 1. The accident occurred when an unknown vehicle allegedly hit Divakars motorcycle at about 11.30 pm on April 14, 2025, on NH-40 near Ganesh Godown in Govindapalle village, Sirivella. Divakar suffered bleeding head injuries and died on the spot. His post-mortem report recorded Head Injury as the cause of death. Insurer rejects claim The insurance policy commenced on December 19, 2024, and was valid until December 18, 2025. The premium was Rs 4,767, and Jagadeeshawara Reddy was the nominee. The insurance nominee submitted the claim form on May 8, 2025. The insurer later sought additional documents and rejected the claim. In an email dated June 28, 2025, it said scrutiny and verification had revealed misrepresentation of facts to obtain the insurance benefit and that the claim fell outside the policy terms. The insurance company told the commission that the nominee had failed to provide documents despite repeated reminders. It said letters dated May 17, May 19, May 21 and May 25 had sought documents required to process the claim, including the final police report. But the commission found that the insurer had not produced evidence that these communications reached the complainant. No proof that notices reached nominee The commission noted that there were no postal receipts, acknowledgements, tracking reports, courier records, email delivery reports or other documentary evidence establishing that the alleged communications had been dispatched and served. It said that simply mentioning the dates of the communications was not enough to establish that they had been sent to or received by the complainant. The burden was upon the insurance company to establish that the complainant had been called upon to furnish the documents and given a reasonable opportunity to do so, the commission said. It also relied on the insurance companys own field verification report. The investigator found the incident to be genuine and the cause of death consistent with the post-mortem report. The commission said the investigation verified the complainants account of the accident and death. The commission found that the insurer had not identified the particular fact allegedly misrepresented by the deceased. It said the company had not established what declaration was false, when the alleged misrepresentation was made or how it was material to acceptance of the insurance risk. It said the insurance company had not shown that the absence of the final police report extinguished or suspended its liability under the policy. No evidence was produced to show that the report contained any finding adverse to the claim. Holding that the rejection of the claim was not supported by a valid ground under the policy terms, the commission held that it amounted to deficiency in service. The insurer was given 45 days from receipt of the order to comply. If it fails to pay within that period, the Rs 50 lakh sum assured will carry interest at 9 per cent per annum from October 6, 2025, the date of the complaint, until realisation. Takeaway If an insurer rejects a claim citing misrepresentation or missing documents, it should be able to clearly establish the specific violation and show that the claimant was properly asked to provide the required documents.
