articleTitle: Brazil elections: Why a jailed ex-president’s son is leading race, and the Trump factor
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Opposition presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro in Brasilia, Brazil, Oct. 4. (AP Photo/Eraldo Peres)
description: Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence for an attempted 2023 coup in Brazil. How did his son become the frontrunner to lead the country? And what has been Trump’s role in the elections for South America’s biggest country and economy?
body_raw: Brazil voted in the first round of its presidential elections on Sunday October 4, with incumbent President Luiz Incio Lula da Silva and Flvio Bolsonaro receiving 45 and 47 of the vote, respectively. Since neither won over 50 of the vote but still secured the most votes among all candidates, they will go head-to-head in another round of voting on October 25. Bolsonaro is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who won the 2018 elections and rejected the 2022 poll results after losing to Lula. His supporters stormed government offices in the capital, Brasilia, evoking visuals of US President Donald Trumps supporters attacking the US Capitol building in 2021. This is only one of many ways Bolsonaro and Trump are linked, with Trump backing him strongly over the years and expressing solidarity with him over supposed witch hunts for not accepting the results. Today, Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence in relation to the attempted 2023 coup. How did his son become the frontrunner to lead Brazil? And what has been Trumps role in the elections for the continents biggest country and economy? Who is Flvio Bolsonaro? Flvio, 45, is a lawyer by training and Jair Bolsonaros eldest son. A senator from Rio de Janeiro, he bears a striking physical resemblance to his father, which may or may not lend him a political advantage given Bolsonaro Sr.s reputation as a polarising figure. Take the 2022 election, the closest in Brazils history, where Lula received 50.9 of the votes against Bolsonaros 49.1. When Jair first came to power as the leader of Brazils Liberal Party LP, his supporters saw him as a conservative, pro-business politician who would tell it like it is, similar to other populist right-wing leaders globally. Among his key policies was relaxing protections for the Amazon rainforest to encourage commercial activities. He vowed to combat corruption, which was noteworthy since his own political rise was fuelled by mainstream political figures in Brazil getting implicated in major corruption scandals. Bolsonaro is also known to make homophobic and misogynistic statements, telling a woman legislator who accused him of being a rapist I wouldnt rape you because you dont deserve it. He was also criticised for his handling of the Covid-19 pandemic, with Brazil having the second-highest death toll among countries, after the United States. As the Financial Times put it in a profile of the Bolsonaro family, Flvio is the self-styled moderate of the family a vaccinated Bolsonaro, in his own words. In the constant shadow of his father, he treads a difficult line. He all but acknowledges being an inferior substitute. How can you compare Pels son to Pel himself? Flvio asked the FT in an interview earlier this year during which he refused to sit behind his fathers desk in the party HQ. The Bolsonaros have enjoyed voter support among more well-off groups, the more conservative Evangelical Christians, and the countrys southern regions. On the other hand, Lula, 80, is a veteran socialist leader now contesting for a fourth term with supporters such as Catholics, progressives and poorer groups. Flvio has criticised Lula for not being tough enough on crime and drug gangs. Lula was also president when the first BRIC meeting comprising Brazil, Russia, India and China was held in 2009 South Africa was not a member of the grouping then. And what is Trumps role in the Brazilian elections? Since Jair Bolsonaros first term, which partly overlapped with the first Trump administration, Trump has publicly supported him owing to their similar ideology and disdain for critics. He met Flvio earlier this year, calling him a smart young man, who loves his country, Brazil, very much. Within months of his second term, Trump announced 50 tariffs on imports from Brazil in July 2025 for threats to the US. The executive order also noted that Brazilian officials were persecuting Bolsonaro and that this contributes to the deliberate breakdown in the rule of law in Brazil. Trump has earlier warmed up to other strongman leaders globally, with vocal support for those from South America. Another prominent example is Argentinas Javier Milei. This approach is also in line with the US National Security Strategy, released in November 2025. It laid out intentions for the US to be dominant in the Western Hemisphere, and its effects were seen in the military capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in January this year. As The New York Times said of South America in a recent report, Candidates aligned with President Trump on issues like fighting drug gangs and woke ideology have won the last seven elections in the region, with Brazil the biggest remaining prize. This period of rightward political shift comes not too long after a pink tide around 2022. The term was first used around the early 21st century, with the election of Hugo Chavez in Venezuela, followed by a roughly decade-long period that saw many countries reject neo-liberalism in favour of socialism hence pink, rather than Communisms red. Oliver Stuenkel, Visiting Scholar at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace in Washington, wrote back in 2022 for Americas Quarterly that this wave would be more short-lived. His reasons ranged from greater geopolitical instability translating into tougher economic circumstances for governments to their declining interest in maintaining a sense of regional unity and convergence. Todays leftist presidents are less likely to prioritize ties to their neighbors because they are less relevant from an economic point of view. Intraregional trade amounted to over 20 of Latin Americas total exports in 2008, but this share has declined by a third and is set to fall further as commodity exports to China are on the rise, he wrote.

articleTitle: Rs 50,000 per audit, Rs 2.5 lakh in a packet: CBI case against DGCA officer
articleFeaturedImageAlt: DGCA bribery case, DGCA bribe case, CBI DGCA arrest, Sushil Kumar Garg, Sachin Keshav Bhane, DGCA airworthiness certification, Ekvi Air Training Organisation, flight training organisation, DGCA Chennai officer, CBI bribery case, Directorate General of Civil Aviation, Directorate General of Civil Aviation news, Indian express news, DGCA news
description: CBI arrested Sushil Kumar Garg, Deputy Director (Airworthiness), DGCA, and Ekvi Air Training Organisation Private Limited director Sachin Keshav Bhane in connection with an alleged bribery case.
body_raw: A senior officer of the Directorate General of Civil Aviation DGCA allegedly sought Rs 50,000 per audit from the director of a flight training organisation to issue airworthiness certificates for aircraft it operated, without ensuring full compliance with prescribed airworthiness and safety requirements, according to a probe. On Sunday, the Central Bureau of Investigation CBI arrested Sushil Kumar Garg, Deputy Director Airworthiness, DGCA, posted in Chennai, and Ekvi Air Training Organisation Private Limited director Sachin Keshav Bhane in connection with an alleged bribery case. The agency alleged that Garg demanded and accepted a bribe of Rs 2.5 lakh to extend undue favours in the airworthiness certification of aircraft operated by the private firm. According to the First Information Report FIR registered on October 3, Ekvi Air Training Organisation, registered with the Registrar of Companies, Mumbai, and based in Thane, Maharashtra, operates a fleet of seven aircraft, with its training base at Salem Airport in Tamil Nadu. The FIR said Garg conducted an airworthiness audit or inspection of the companys aircraft on July 31. It alleges that he sought a bribe in return for a favourable audit report, without properly inspecting the aircraft and overlooking certain deficiencies observed in the fleet. However, he could not collect the amount on that occasion because he was accompanied by a senior officer. On September 23 and September 26, Garg told the company he would visit its training facility in the first week of October 2026 and collect the payment from its representatives, and that Bhane would be present at Salem during the visit. Later, they negotiated on October 2 and settled at Rs 50,000 per audit. Garg had previously received a mobile phone worth approximately Rs 50,000 from Bhane, the FIR alleged. The FIR alleged that Garg told his wife that day that Bhane had given him a packet containing five bundles of currency notes amounting to Rs 2.5 lakh.

QUESTION 1 The development of optogenetics represents a shift from merely observing brain activity to experimentally establishing causal relationships between neural circuits and behaviour. Discuss. QUESTION 2 How do higher crude oil prices contribute to inflationary pressures in an import-dependent economy like India? Examine the implications for monetary policy and economic growth. QUESTION 1 The development of optogenetics represents a shift from merely observing brain activity to experimentally establishing causal relationships between neural circuits and behaviour. Discuss. Relevance The question is relevant to GS Paper III Science and Technology, particularly biotechnology and advances in neuroscience. It tests the ability to assess how interdisciplinary technologies can transform modern biomedical research. It covers the application of genetic engineering and light-sensitive proteins to study specific neural circuits. NoteThis is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. Introduction -Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel, and Karl Deisseroth were awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for their discoveries in light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. -The technology has altered neuroscience by allowing researchers to stimulate specific neurons with light and study the subsequent behavioral effects, rather than just monitor neural activity. Body You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer From observation to causal investigation -Earlier neuroscience relied heavily on observational and recording techniques to determine relationships between brain activity and behavior. Optogenetics provided a more precise experimental intervention. -Hegemann and Nagel discovered channelrhodopsin-2 ChR2, a light-gated ion channel, while studying the algae Chlamydomonas. -Genes that encode light-sensitive proteins can be introduced into specific types of cells, causing them to respond to specific wavelengths of light. -When light is given to the targeted cells, proteins can modify ion flow, so activating or inhibiting neuronal activity. - Researchers can thus turn specific neurons or circuits on or off and see if a specific behavior changes. This shifts the focus from which neurons are active when a behavior occurs? to does activating or inhibiting these neurons cause the behaviour? Establishing neural circuitbehaviour relationships -Optogenetics has allowed researchers to study the operation of specific brain circuits involved in pain, social behavior, thirst, food consumption, reward, attention, and memory. -For example, Deisseroths research utilized ChR2 to activate specific neurons and control mouse whisker motions. His research also modified neuronal populations connected with alertness and looked into neurons implicated in terror memories. Reactivating the identified neurons could cause fear-related behavior even when the animal was not exposed to the initial threat. Such tests give more compelling evidence of a causal association between certain brain circuits and behavior than observation alone. Conclusion -Optogenetics has transformed neuroscience from a primarily observational field to one capable of precise experimental intervention. By allowing researchers to disrupt specific neural circuits and watch the effects, it provides a powerful technique of establishing causation and may eventually lead to more tailored treatments for neurological and psychiatric illnesses. What approaches were adopted by the Indian vaccine manufacturers to produce COVID-19 vaccines? 2022 QUESTION 2 How do higher crude oil prices contribute to inflationary pressures in an import-dependent economy like India? Examine the implications for monetary policy and economic growth. Relevance The question is relevant to GS Paper III Indian Economy, particularly inflation, monetary policy and external-sector vulnerabilities. It links crude oil prices with the current account, exchange rate, inflation and economic growth. NoteThis is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. Introduction -Higher crude oil prices pose a substantial inflationary risk to India, which relies heavily on imported energy. -An oil-price shock might thus function as a external tax on the Indian economy, influencing pricing, the external sector, and GDP growth. Body You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer How higher crude oil prices fuel inflation? -Higher global crude prices drive up the cost of fuel, diesel, LPG and other petroleum products. The recent increase in fuel costs has resulted in increased inflation in diesel, petrol, and CNG. -Costlier diesel and petrol raise transport costs, including fares and the cost of moving agricultural and industrial goods. According to the Indian Express, transport inflation increased substantially as gasoline prices surged. -Petroleum products play an essential role in industry, agriculture, logistics, and a variety of other industries. As a result, higher energy costs can affect final product prices. -Higher oil import costs increase demand for foreign currency, putting pressure on the rupee. A weakening rupee increases the cost of imported items, contributing to imported inflation. Implications for monetary policy -The RBI is facing a challenging inflation-growth trade-off. If increasing oil prices cause sustained and widespread inflation, monetary tightening may be required to control demand and keep inflation expectations from becoming entrenched. The RBIs rate-hiking process operates by increasing borrowing costs, which cools consumption and investment. -However, monetary policy is constrained in its ability to immediately address a supply-side oil shock. Raising interest rates cannot boost global oil supplies. Excessive tightening may instead impair domestic demand and investment at a time when growth is already hampered by rising input costs. Thus, the RBI must discern between a short oil shock and long-term inflationary impacts. Implications for economic growth -India imports more than 88 of its petroleum requirements persistent price hikes so significantly increase the oil import bill. Higher oil imports may increase the current account deficit and put pressure on the exchange rate. -Higher fuel and travel expenses diminish a households real disposable income and purchasing power. Higher energy costs can put a strain on government budgets, especially where fuel prices are partially sheltered from worldwide fluctuations. The Finance Ministry has warned that continued crude price hikes pose dangers to both the fiscal deficit and the current account balance. Conclusion -For an import-dependent economy, a crude-oil shock affects inflation, the external sector, and growth all at once. The policy issue is not simply to control inflation with higher interest rates, but also to combine calibrated monetary policy with structural reforms that lessen Indias reliance on imported fossil fuels. articleTitle: Iran’s Zimbabwe Embassy uses Balakrishna’s Bhagavanth Kesari clip to troll Trump
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A still from the Nandamuri Balakrishna's Bhagavanth Kesari
description: The Iranian Embassy in Zimbabwe has responded to US President Donald Trump's threats to "annihilate" Iran by posting a clip from Telugu star Nandamuri Balakrishna's action film Bhagavanth Kesari on X, mistakenly labelling it as Bollywood.
body_raw: The Iranian Embassy in Zimbabwe has turned to Telugu cinema to respond to US President Donald Trumps threats against Iran, posting a 58-second clip from Nandamuri Balakrishnas action film Bhagavanth Kesari on X on Wednesday with a pointed message aimed at the American president. Trump talks about annihilating Iran. But he knows Iran is not defenseless. Since we informed, they have recently been watching Bollywood instead of Hollywood, the embassy wrote alongside the clip. The post incorrectly referred to the clip as Bollywood. Bhagavanth Kesari is a Telugu-language film, making it Tollywood, not Bollywood. The distinction was immediately pointed out by Indian social media users, many of whom found the error as entertaining as the trolling itself. What the clip shows The clip chosen by the embassy is from one of the most over-the-top action sequences in Bhagavanth Kesari, directed by Anil Ravipudi. In the scene, Balakrishnas character uses what appears to be a manhole cover as a shield while seated calmly on a chair as dozens of armed men fire at him from the opposite end. After the firing stops, he mounts a gun but does not use it. Instead, he launches large gas cylinders at his attackers, sending them flying. Trump talks about annihilating Iran. But he knows Iran is not defenseless. Since we informed they have recently been watching Bollywood instead of Hollywood. pic.twitter.comv6Le8zkH5X - Iran Embassy in Zimbabwe IRANinZIMBABWE September 23, 2026 Trumps UNGA threats The embassys post came in direct response to Trumps address at the United Nations General Assembly 2026, where he escalated his rhetoric against Iran amid the ongoing conflict in the Gulf, which began nearly seven months ago. Trump reiterated that a major decision had been made on the course of the war and presented what he described as two options for dealing with Iran annihilating the Islamic Republic and doing it quickly versus driving them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations. Also Read NBK111 drops first glimpse on Balakrishnas 65th birthday No more vintage, only new age Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian delivered a forceful address at the same assembly, rejecting Trumps characterisation of Iran as a terrorist state and defending his country as a victim rather than a perpetrator of terrorism. We will never bow our head or bend at the knee, Pezeshkian said. During his speech, Pezeshkian held up images of children killed in the Minab school attack and directly blamed the United States and Israel for providing the weapons used. I come from an Iran where, in truth, they bombed a school. You see these children? These children perished under bombs with weapons used by the US and Israel. They were innocent and had committed no crimes, he said. The US delegation walked out of the hall in protest during Pezeshkians speech. The Bhagavanth Kesari post is not the first time Iran has used Indian cinema to mock the United States on social media. In a previous incident, the Iranian Embassy in Tunisia used an Akshay Kumar meme based on the actors famous fake-crying scene to mock the capture of a US underwater drone by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps IRGC. Lost an underwater drone. Oil is nearing 100. Elections are coming. Hows it going, Trump? the post had read. About Bhagavanth Kesari Bhagavanth Kesari, released in October 2023, is a Telugu action drama directed by Anil Ravipudi and starring Nandamuri Balakrishna in the lead alongside Sreeleela. Produced under Shine Screens and distributed by Dil Raju under Sri Venkateswara Creations, the film collected approximately 120 crore at the worldwide box office. The action sequences, choreographed by Ram-Lakshman, were among the films most talked-about elements.

articleTitle: How Pranavi Urs shrugged off a triple bogey to win golf gold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pranavi Urs won a historic gold in the women's individual golf leaving behind some big names at Asian Games. (Reuters)
description: The Mysore golfer left behind World No 6 Chinese Yin Ruoning, and Singapore's Shannon Xuan Yin Tan, an Order of Merit winner from last year
body_raw: The significance of Pranavi Urss gold medal in womens individual golf-the first-ever for India in the history of the Asian Games-can be gauged by the players she left behind. Chinas Yin Ruoning, who clinched the silver after a playoff against Singapores Shannon Xuan Yin Tan, is ranked world no. 6. Shannon herself was the European Order of Merit winner last year. Six of the top 10 in the world-including five of the top six - hail from Asia. And even though not all of them were in action at the Kasugai Country Club East Course, it shows where the epicentre of the game lies, and makes the achievement of the 294-ranked Indian even more remarkable Four rounds and 72 holes of golf separates the contenders from the pretenders, and where Aditi Ashok had faltered at the 2023 Asian Games in the final round, the 23-year-old from Mysuru made sure to go the whole hog. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage Aditi displayed stellar form in Hangzhou and had a seven-shot lead going into the final round, before a card of 77 undid all the good work and she had to be content with a silver medal, the same colour she, Pranavi and Diksha Dagar combined to achieve on Saturday in the team event. There may have been a chance that Pranavi could have faltered too, especially after a triple-bogey 7 on the third hole wiped off her overnight lead and handed the initiative to Yin. But those were the last shots Pranavi dropped and combined with three subsequent birdies, ensured a level-par round and a win by one with a score of 15-under. That she didnt have a big lead and fought all the way to the end of the round, in a way, made her win even more impressive. In fact, she wasnt even sure at the end that the gold medal was hers. Then her teammates dunked two bottles empty in her head. I just knew it was either a putt to win or to force a playoff, she said after the three-foot putt on the last. All I wanted to do was obviously hole the putt. The self-proclaimed fan of Rory McIlroy and womens World No.1 Nelly Korda had admitted that she had barely slept the previous night and was anxious at the start of her round. After the triple bogey had put her in the chasing pack, Pranavis comeback started with a birdie on the sixth. Another one on the 10th saw her catching Yin and the one on 13, put the Indian ahead again. The Chinese couldnt find a birdie on the back nine. Shannon had six birdies on her card, but two bogeys and a double bogey hurt her chances. Pranavi has been playing on the Ladies European Tour LET for the last couple of years and though she hasnt won yet, she hopes maybe I will get it soon. The magnitude of the achievement was not lost on those running the sport in the country either. Its a fantastic achievement and the way Pranavi stayed calm and composed was really commendable, Champika Sayal, the secretary general of the Womens Golf Association of India, told The Indian Express. She has registered several top-five finishes on the LET and has now proved that she is a world-class player. Blossoming talent India has had a vibrant domestic golf structure for quite some time but, as Sayal said, it was the first time the squad had been put together based solely on world rankings. With the Hero Womens Open at Gurugrams DLF Golf Country Club scheduled later this month, with Pranavi confirmed to be in the field, it would provide a big shot in the arm to the game. Pranavi turned professional as a teenager and won the Womens Pro Tour Order of Merit in 2022. She was part of the team that won the silver medal at the 2023 Asian Games before getting into LET through the Q-School. She had been knocking on the door frequently this season, finishing tied fifth at the Dutch Ladies Open. She has put together other good rounds as well, but is still waiting to get it all together. If she continues to improve, she can even get on the LPGA Tour as well, Sayal hoped. It will inspire upcoming players as well, as Pranavi cut her teeth in the game in the hard conditions of the Mysore Golf Club. The 2028 Los Angeles Olympics is the next obvious target, and there will be a maximum of only two spots available per country. Apart from the mens and womens individual events, there will be a mixed team event as well. The qualification process started in June this year and will go on till June 2028, but the players have to be inside the top 400 in the world rankings to even be in the reckoning. We have four inside the top 400 and five inside 500. The men need to get inside the top 400 first, Sayal remarked. The highest-ranked Indian player currently is Yuvraj Sandhu at 512. He combined with Saptak Talwar 649 and Veer Ahlawat 652 to finish 6th in the team competition. Ahlawat and Talwar finished tied 6th on the individual table.

articleTitle: ‘I was lucky to have him’: Zinedine Zidane on Cristiano Ronaldo
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ronaldo

body_raw: Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo left the national team training camp ahead of their Nations League campaign against Norway, which has created speculation around his retirement. France will face Belgium next, and Frances head coach, Zinedine Zidane, was asked about Ronaldos poor end to his illustrious career. No, I think he should be congratulated on his great career. What he did is exceptional, Zidane said. I was lucky to have him with me and he made me win incredible things, so I take my hat off to Cristiano. I will always have great respect for him, as for all players, but even more so for those with whom I shared so much time, and in particular Cristiano, who made us win so much, said Zidane who coached Ronaldo during his time at Real Madrid. Perhaps the difference is that at a club it never stops it is day to day, it is very all-consuming. I loved doing that, and now I have another side to it and I will try to do it this way, which will be a little different. But in any case, the desire to work well around my team is the same, he added. In a press conference on Wednesday, Portugal Head coach George Jesus said that he was not planning to start Ronaldo in Portugals game against Denmark in the Nations League on Thursday, adding that there is no feud between the pair. After the said press conference, Ronaldo put out a post on Instagram saying that he would be leaving the Portugal camp which was preparing for the upcoming Nations League matches. After the national team press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp. In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave the national team, to which I always devoted myself. Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my teammates good luck, without exception, Ronaldo posted on Instagram.

articleTitle: Tamil Nadu bypolls are an early test for Vijay’s young government
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay
description: Both constituencies in the state are reserved seats, won in April by AIADMK candidates who subsequently resigned, joined Vijay’s TVK, and are now seeking election again under their new party’s symbol
body_raw: Five months after Tamil Nadu voters elected a new government, some of them returned to polling booths on Tuesday to answer a narrower question Whether the political movement that brought C Joseph Vijay to power has endured through its first months of governing. Voting was brisk by late morning in the two Assembly by-elections in Tamil Nadu. At 11 am, Madurantakam recorded 35.55 per cent turnout and Dharapuram 37.28 per cent. Both constituencies are reserved seats and were won in April by AIADMK candidates who resigned to join Vijays Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam TVK, and are now seeking re-election with this party. In neighbouring Puducherry, meanwhile, Thattanchavady was voting in a separate by-election necessitated by Chief Minister N Rangasamys decision to vacate the constituency after winning two seats in April. Turnout there was 19.2 per cent by 9 am, slightly above the 18.32 per cent recorded during the same first two hours in the April Assembly election. ALSO READ Vijays river of obscenity barb to slam DMK, Udhayanidhis reels counter The Tamil Nadu contests carry a different political weight. TVK won 108 seats in April but fell short of an outright majority and formed the government with support from smaller parties. Since then, defections from the AIADMK have altered the political landscape. Madurantakams Maragatham Kumaravel and Dharapurams P Sathyabama were among the AIADMK legislators who resigned and moved to TVK. Voters are now being asked, in effect, whether their representatives moved alone. That question explains the unusual intensity of the campaign. Vijay spent four days personally campaigning in the two constituencies - two days of public rallies and two of roadshows - a substantial commitment for two by-elections from a Chief Minister whose own appearances during the April statewide campaign had been comparatively limited. For TVK, winning both seats would validate not only its candidates but the continuing movement of politicians and local organisations towards the ruling party. Losing one would give the AIADMK and DMK an opening to argue that the post-April political realignment has limits. CHECK THE LIVE UPDATES ON THE BYELECTIONS HERE. The first hours of voting offered few reliable clues. Madurantakam began sluggishly, reaching 15.99 per cent turnout around 9.30 am, before the pace accelerated. When reporters asked Kumaravel about the initially lower turnout compared with the general election, she offered a distinctly local explanation Tuesday, she said, was a day when many women visited temples. They would pray for a TVK victory and then come to vote, she said. People have the same enthusiasm as during the general election, Kumaravel said. They are coming to vote with smiling faces. The gender question has occupied TVKs calculations throughout the campaign. Women outnumber men among registered voters in both constituencies Madurantakam has 108,797 women and 104,926 men among its 213,788 voters, while Dharapuram has 116,013 women and 107,285 men among 223,306 electors. Earlier, Kumaravel said voters retained confidence in Vijay and argued that the four-month-old government needed more time to demonstrate change. Polling hitches Polling itself encountered some interruptions. In Madurantakam, electronic voting machines EVMs developed technical problems at two polling stations. At booth 26 in Sithandi, the control unit had to be replaced twice. At booth 55 in L Endathur, the ballot unit was changed after polling agents objected to a visible mark on the name of a candidate. In Dharapuram, voting at a booth in Kottapulipalayam was interrupted by an EVM malfunction, while another machine problem delayed polling at Kundadam-Manurpalayam. There were political disputes as well. At Kolinjivadi, agents objected to a polling official whom they accused of acting in favour of TVK, leading to an interruption in voting. At Veerachimangalam, AIADMK members stopped a vehicle carrying TVK functionaries from outside the constituency, alleging that they had come to distribute tokens to households. DMK and AIADMK members then argued with TVK workers. The allegations come after a campaign in which opposition parties repeatedly accused the ruling party of using money and government machinery to influence voters. TVK has denied accusations of cash distribution. Sathyabama, the TVK candidate in Dharapuram, also entered polling day dealing with a video circulating on social media that purported to show her discussing election expenditure and other matters. After voting at a school in Madukkampalayam, she said the video had been fabricated and that those responsible for releasing it had been identified. The people are clear, she said, insisting that the video would not affect the result. For the AIADMK, the identity of the TVK candidates has been central to the election. Both were elected on AIADMK tickets only months ago. Edappadi K Palaniswami has accused them of betraying the voters who elected them, while AIADMK workers have repeatedly used the word traitor during the campaign. The DMK has made much the same event into a broader democratic argument. Former CM M K Stalin described the by-elections as having been imposed on voters because elected representatives resigned and returned to seek their votes under another party. The DMK has its own stake in Tuesdays numbers. It is contesting without most of the alliance that accompanied it into the April election. Even without winning, an improvement on its previous performance would allow the party to point to the size of its independent vote after its loss of power. The Left parties, despite supporting the TVK government from outside, are contesting against it CPIMs Suganthi is in the race in Madurantakam and CPIs P Lakshmanan in Dharapuram. Naam Tamilar Katchi is also contesting both seats, making the elections five-cornered. In Puducherry, the political geometry is different. Eleven candidates are contesting in Thattanchavady, but the principal contest is among the ruling AINRC-led NDA, Congress and the DMK. Rangasamys AINRC has fielded Ashok Anand, while Congress candidate E Vinayagam has TVKs support. The DMK has fielded K Sethuselvam. For Rangasamy, the election provides an early measure of support for his four-month-old NDA government. For Vijay, the Puducherry contest places TVK in the less exposed position of supporting an ally rather than defending its own government and two defectors. The distinction is important. A general election asks voters who should govern. A by-election held five months later may be asking what they make of what has happened since. In Madurantakam and Dharapuram, even that question has an unusually literal form. Voters elected two candidates in April. The candidates changed parties. On Tuesday, the voters get to decide whether they have changed with them. Polling continues until 6 pm. Counting will take place on October 9.

articleTitle: UPSC Ethics Simplified | Civic Virtue on Indian roads: What does it say about us?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Ethics Simplified | Civic Virtue on Indian roads: What does it say about us?
description: Roads are not merely physical infrastructure. They are also spaces where citizens practise, or fail to practise, values such as self-restraint, justice, responsibility and respect for others. Our ethicist, Nanditesh Nilay, explores what our conduct on the road tells us about civic virtue.
body_raw: UPSC Ethics Simplified, a special series under UPSC Essentials by The Indian Express, explores ethical concepts relevant to the Civil Services Examination. In todays article, we examine what our conduct on the road reveals about civic virtue and ask a larger question What happens when citizens fail to exercise self-restraint, responsibility and respect for others in public spaces? Our ethicist examines the issue through the lenses of civic virtue, good citizenship, self-restraint and moral duty. What happens when a person is involved in an accident on the road? If someone is hit, intentionally or unintentionally, an immediate ethical response should be to stop, check on the person and take responsibility for ones actions. The recent Gurugram case involving a woman biker raises questions about these basic civic responsibilities. The Indian Express reported that a woman biker was allegedly chased and rammed by a car on Golf Course Road. Video footage showed the car following the biker before colliding with her motorcycle. The police later added sections relating to attempt to murder, stalking and insulting the modesty of a woman to the FIR. The incident is therefore not only about road safety. It also provides an opportunity to examine a larger ethical question What do our everyday actions on public roads tell us about our civic virtues? What are civic virtues? A virtue is a set of traits, habits and qualities that enable individuals to fulfil their responsibilities effectively. Civic virtues are qualities that help individuals act as responsible members of a political community. They include concern for the common good, participation in public life, respect for institutions, opposition to corruption and responsibility towards fellow citizens. The importance and formation of civic virtues have been central questions in political philosophy from ancient times. Roads provide a simple but powerful setting in which these virtues are tested. Patience, self-restraint, respect, responsibility and concern for another persons safety are not abstract ethical concepts when we are behind the wheel. They directly influence the safety and dignity of other citizens. Aristotle Good person and good citizen Aristotle drew a subtle distinction between a good person and a good citizen. The virtues of a good person are universal or absolute in character, while the virtues of a good citizen are also related to the constitution and the responsibilities of living in a political community. Aristotle further connected the two through virtue of character. Qualities such as courage, temperance, justice and practical wisdom are cultivated through habituation in a well-ordered community and expressed through civic engagement. This idea of habituation is particularly relevant to civic life. Ethical conduct is not developed merely by knowing what is right. It is strengthened by repeatedly practising the right behaviour. For instance, stopping after an accident, helping an injured person, controlling anger during a traffic dispute or respecting another persons right of way may appear to be small acts. But repeated acts of self-restraint and responsibility help build civic character. Thus, the question is not merely whether a person knows the rules. It is whether the person has developed the character to follow them, especially when emotions run high. W.D. Ross Duties that guide moral action British moral philosopher W.D. Ross rejected the idea that all moral decisions can be reduced to one supreme principle. He proposed the idea of prima facie duties. These are genuine moral duties that normally carry weight, although in a particular situation one duty may have to take precedence over another. Ross identified duties such as fidelity, reparation, gratitude, justice, beneficence, self-improvement and non-maleficence. The idea is important because real-life ethical situations often involve competing considerations. Determining which duty should take precedence requires moral judgement and practical wisdom. It cannot always be reduced to a mechanical formula or an algorithm. Self-restraint and self-improvement Rosss idea of self-improvement also has a direct connection with civic virtue. Self-improvement is not limited to acquiring knowledge or professional skills. It includes cultivating ones virtues, character and capacity for self-control. A person must understand ones own intentions and limitations well enough to fulfil promises, avoid causing harm and prevent personal desires from overriding ones duties. This is where self-restraint becomes important. On a road, anger, impatience, ego or the desire to assert ones power can quickly affect another persons safety. A mature ethical response requires an individual to recognise these emotions and exercise control over them. The principle of non-maleficence, or the duty to avoid causing harm, becomes particularly relevant. If an action can seriously harm another citizen, the individuals responsibility cannot end with saying that the harm was unintended. Ethical conduct also requires us to consider the foreseeable consequences of our actions and our responsibility towards others. When civic virtue is missing The Gurugram incident brings these questions into sharp focus. The woman biker questioned why the driver did not stop to help her if the collision had been unintentional. The police investigation later examined video footage and escalated the charges. The ethical lesson goes beyond one individual or one incident. When self-restraint, justice, responsibility and concern for others are absent from civic conduct, public spaces can become places where power, aggression or privilege determine who feels safe. This is why civic virtue matters in both personal and professional life. A society cannot depend only on laws and punishment. Laws provide an external framework for behaviour, but civic virtues help create the internal willingness to act responsibly even when no one is watching. Development is more than roads and highways India often views roads, highways and other infrastructure as visible symbols of development. They are important indicators of economic progress and connectivity. But development cannot be measured only by the quality or length of our highways. A developed society also requires citizens who can share public spaces with discipline, empathy, responsibility and respect for others. If physical infrastructure advances while civic virtues remain weak, development remains incomplete. The road, therefore, becomes more than a means of transportation. It becomes a test of citizenship. The fundamental question is not only How good are our roads? It is also How good are we as citizens while using them? Compassion and civic life The Dalai Lamas emphasis on cultivating a compassionate mindset provides another dimension to this discussion. When our thoughts are dominated by excessive preoccupation with the self, emotions such as fear, anger, jealousy and mistrust can become stronger. Concern for the well-being of others, on the other hand, can make our minds clearer and our conduct more peaceful. This idea has relevance for civic life. A road is shared by strangers. We may never know the person driving beside us, walking across the road or riding a motorcycle ahead of us. Yet our actions can directly affect their safety. Civic virtue begins with recognising that the stranger on the road is also a citizen with equal dignity and rights. What should an ethics aspirant remember? The Gurugram case can be used to connect several concepts in UPSC Ethics GS Paper IV Civic virtue Responsibility towards the common good and fellow citizens. Self-restraint Controlling anger, ego and impulses. Non-maleficence Avoiding actions that cause harm to others. Justice Respecting the equal rights and dignity of other citizens. Self-improvement Cultivating ethical character and emotional control. Compassion Recognising and responding to the vulnerability of others. For a future civil servant, these values matter not only in extraordinary situations but also in everyday public life. Roads can testify to a countrys physical development. But the way citizens behave on those roads can testify to its civic character. Post-Read Questions 1. A good citizen is not merely one who obeys the law, but one who possesses civic virtues. Discuss with reference to Aristotle and contemporary public life. 2. How can self-restraint, non-maleficence and compassion contribute to safer and more ethical public spaces? The writer is the author of Being Good, Aaiye, Insaan Banaen, Kyon and Ethikos Stories Searching Happiness. He teaches courses on and offers training in ethics, values and behaviour. He has been the expertconsultant to SAARC countries, UPSC, Central Bureau of Investigation CBI,National Judicial Academy, ATI, RAKNPA, Haryana Institute of Public Administration, ISA MountAbu, National Centre for Good Governance,Competition Commission of India CCI, etc. He has PhD in two disciplines and has been a Doctoral Fellow in Gandhian Studies from ICSSR. His second PhD is from IIT Delhi on Ethical Decision Making among Indian Bureaucrats. He writes for the UPSC Ethics Simplified concepts and caselets weekly. articleTitle: Railway constable saves passenger from falling between train and tracks in Gujarat
articleFeaturedImageAlt: RPF constable
description: The 61-year-old passenger was travelling from Rajkot to Dwarka.
body_raw: At 1.50 am on Friday, Amit Dahiya, a constable with the Railway Protection Force RPF, was on night duty at Jamnagar railway station in Gujarat, keeping an eye out for suspicious activity as the Rajkot-Okha train was halted at Platform No 1. As the Passenger train started to depart the station, slowly gaining momentum, an elderly man slipped and fell while trying to board the train. A scream from another person on the platform drew the attention of Dahiya. He turned to his right and, within a split second, sprinted towards the man, slipping into the space between the moving train and the platform. Without losing a second, he safely pulled the passenger, Batuk Das, out from between the platform and the moving train, and he was rescued without sustaining any injuries. A statement from Sunil Kumar Meena, Senior Divisional Commercial Manager of Rajkot Division, said, The 61-year-old passenger, Batuk Das, was travelling from Rajkot to Dwarka. At Jamnagar Railway Station, he got down from the train to fetch water. After taking water, when he attempted to board the moving train again, he lost his balance and fell between the moving train and the platform. Meena further said, The RPF Constables promptness, courage and presence of mind helped save the passengers life. Following the incident, Assistant Sub-Inspector Mukesh Kumar, along with his staff, immediately reached the spot. After ensuring the passengers well-being, he was safely seated back in the same train, which was then allowed to proceed on its onward journey towards Okha. Dahiya was commended for his prompt action.

articleTitle: What are IRDAI’s proposed insurance reforms, why have they hit insurance stocks?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Insurance shares got pummeled on the stock market on Thursday and Friday. (Magnific/file)
description: The reforms are aimed at improving consumer protection, reducing mis-selling and countering dark patterns. While this is good news for households, it will eat into the profit margins of the companies distributing these policies.
body_raw: On Wednesday, Indias insurance regulator issued a consultation paper on reforming various aspects of insurance - including its distribution, structure, expenses and commissions. Over Thursday and Friday, however, insurance companies saw their shares getting pummeled on the stock market. PB Fintech, the parent company of Policybazaar, fared the worst it fell 36 on Thursday and followed it up with another 3 fall on Friday. TurtleMint, another insurance distribution platform, slumped 20 on both Thursday and Friday. Max Financial Services, which lost 10 on Thursday, gained 3 on Friday. HDFC Life and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance are down 4-5 since Wednesdays close. Many banks have also ended lower. But why have the proposed reforms by Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India IRDAI led to insurance distributors facing so much heat from investors? The reform road In its paper, titled Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution, IRDAI proposed a host of reforms aimed at improving consumer protection, reducing mis-selling of products, and countering dark patterns in the industry. While this is good news for households and other buyers of insurance policies, it will eat into the profit margins of the companies distributing these policies. Consider life insurance, where IRDAI wants the commission in the first year to be a maximum of 20 of premium for distributors and 25 for agents. This would be less than half the commissions charged currently, with the regulator in 2023 having scrapped such commission caps. The regulator has called for comments by October 25 on its proposed reforms. Limits on commissions especially hurt online insurance aggregators like Policybazaar and TurtleMint, which have high customer acquisition costs compared to others who depend on a network of agents, such as Life Insurance Corporation of India. Online aggregators depend heavily on upfront commissions. Commissions and expenses What the proposals address are the rapid rise in money earned through commissions, with IRDAIs paper pointing out that sales are led by commissions, instead of pricing and quality. Citing the example of general insurance, IRDAI said that while premiums from brokers in 2024-25 was 37 higher from 2022-23, commissions were up a huge 173. Then there is life insurance premiums from corporate agents rose 28 over the two years, but commissions surged 125. What this means is that a distributors income has grown 4-5 times faster than premiums. In efficient markets, consumers compare products on suitability, price and quality. In the countrys insurance sector, heavy dependence on commission-led distribution and lack of transparency on pricing and quality has clogged these competition signals. High distribution payouts have weakened the competition outcomes away from better value to customers, the paper said. Another proposal refers to the reduction in the Expense of Management, or EoM, to 12.5 and 20 of life and general insurers gross direct premium income, respectively, over a five-year period, with limits also set for 2028-29. EoM is the cost an insurance company charges against the premiums it gets. This includes administrative and distribution costs, including commissions paid to agents. EoMs can rise as insurers bid to secure top distributors. According to CareEdge Ratings, the EoM of 20 of Indias 22 life insurers and 28 of 31 general insurers is currently higher than the proposed limits for 2028-29. Indias insurance problem The proposed reforms come at a crucial time, with the Foreign Direct Investment FDI limit for the insurance sector having been raised to 100 in December last year. The same was notified earlier this year in May. This was done with an eye on raising insurance penetration in the country despite being the worlds 10th largest insurance market, insurance penetration was just 3.7 in 2024-25. Insurance penetration is the total insurance premium collected both life and non-life divided by the GDP. According to CareEdge Ratings, the proposed commission caps do little to fix the problem of persistency, or the lack of continued payment of insurance policy premiums. .writing a new policy still pays a distributor several times more than retaining an existing one. A structure that ties remuneration to persistency outcomes would do more, whether by deferring part of the first-year commission, vesting it against 13th- and 25th-month persistency, clawing it back on early lapse, or flattening the first-year to renewal gradient more sharply, the agency said in a report. There is also the problem of online aggregators being the best performers in terms of persistency but getting hit hard with the commission caps. As IRDAIs own report showed, 71 of policies sold online are active for five years the figure is a smaller 43 when it comes to sales made by corporate agents like banks. Some also believe the commission caps may disincentivise insurers from selling lower-ticket, lower-margin policies, which drive penetration in non-tier-1 cities and lower-income groups. Lower-ticket policies naturally have lower payouts, and with these steps, the payouts will reduce further. We as an industry would love to expand to smaller geographies so that everyone can own insurance, but the payment structure should also support that, an executive from a general insurance company said. Krishnamoorthy Rao, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Generali Central Insurance, pointed out that the framework should also recognise the structural cost differences faced by smaller insurers, so that distribution remains competitive, sustainable, and inclusive. Impact on banks Banks are an important distribution channel given the cross-selling opportunities and the lenders deep distribution networks. And commission caps are expected to hurt banks with multiple tie-ups and heavy incentive-led payouts compared to those who have single partnerships, brokerage JM Financial noted. According to it, the average income from insurance distribution for banks across its coverage has risen to 5.1 of profit before tax in 2025-26 from 3.5 in 2022-23. Insurance distribution is a high-margin and capital-light annuity that leverages an existing customer franchise, branch network and technology stack, and a lower commission cap therefore transmits to operating profit, said Ishank Gupta, an analyst at Choice Institutional Equities. Banks with insurance subsidiaries, such as HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, State Bank of India, and Kotak Mahindra Bank will be relatively insulated from the changes as they retain a portion of the commission savings due to higher insurer margins, Gupta added.
