As it is often said, The way you do one thing is the way you do everything. That holds true in the case of Deepika as a mother. She is completely present. Absolutely immersed. Extremely attentive, sensitive, caring, and beautifully gentle. He also spoke about how motherhood had changed Deepikas priorities. Everything in Deepikas life now revolves around Dua. Everything else comes secondary, sometimes even her own health. Deepika and Ranveer began dating while working together on Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela and got married in November 2018 in an intimate ceremony in Lake Como, Italy. They welcomed their first child, daughter Dua, in September 2024, and have now become parents for the second time with the arrival of their baby girl.

articleTitle: From ITIs to AI: Why India needs to rethink skill development
articleFeaturedImageAlt: NITI Aayog, India, skilling, vocational education
description: NITI Aayog's report calls for reimagining India’s skilling architecture to address the gap between labour market needs and workforce skills. What does India’s skilling journey reveal about this mismatch, and how can the country strengthen its skilling system to keep pace with changing demands of job markets? See infographics for quick key insights.
body_raw: - Ritwika Patgiri Students from Class 9 onwards can choose Kaushal Tracks for specialised vocational training based on local and national job demand, proposed a NITI Aayogs report. The report also calls for universities to offer courses that focus on high-growth areas, such as green industries and electric vehicles, and help workers reskill for changing job markets. These recommendations made in Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat2047 point to a challenge facing India a large section of young people are not making a direct transition from education to employment or skill development. It underscores the urgent need for a shift from generic degrees to applied, industry-aligned specialisations. But what does skilling mean in the context of a changing labour market? Is it simply about acquiring a set of skills or does it involve upskilling, reskilling and adaptation to new technologies and occupations? What does Indias skilling journey reveal about the gap between labour market needs and workforce skills? First, a brief overview of the NITI Aayogs report? Why NITI Aayog calls for reimagining skills The report says that more than 7.67 crore people have undergone skill-based training since 2014-15, adding that the Union Budget for 2025-26 allocated Rs 34,000 crore towards skilling-related expenditure across multiple central ministries. Despite this, outcomes remain uneven, says the report. Based on data from the 78th round of the National Sample Survey, the report maps workforce and learners into five segments, together representing approximately 60 crore citizens i schooling, ii tertiary education, iii formal and informal work, iv not in education, employment, and training NEET youth, and v women. The report underlines the significance of establishing stronger links between education, skills and actual employment, as only 8.25 per cent of graduates are employed in roles aligned with their qualifications. Skill training can happen through both institutions, like Industrial Training Institutes ITIs and on-the-job training. However, close to only 8 of the Indian firms provide on-the-job training, according to the NITI Aayogs report. The cost of providing on-the-job training for firms is often higher and they prefer trained individuals. This makes the role of skill institutions important. Therefore, the report proposed to incorporate vocational education and employability skills from schools to universities, with a stronger focus on applied, industry-aligned specialisations, along with greater use of apprenticeships and work-integrated degree and diploma programmes. The report also called for greater focus on sectors expected to generate demand, including green industries and electric vehicles, while providing reskilling for workers in declining occupations. Investing in human capital These recommendations hint at a broader shift towards viewing education and skill development as an investment in human capital. India has the largest youth population in the world, about 65 of its people under the age of 35, representing the potential of the demographic dividend. According to the human capital investment theory, economist Gary Becker argued that the various ways to invest in human capital include schooling and on-the-job training. He argued that earnings increase with age at a decreasing rate, and this increase is positively associated with the level of skills. Unemployment rates, in turn, are negatively associated with the level of skill. Similarly, Theodore Schultz argued that investment in education and training of young people yields returns over a longer period of time. In India, skill development has been perceived as a way to enhance employability and minimise the gap between labour market needs and workforce skills. For instance, according to data from Employment and Unemployment Surveys of National Sample Survey Office NSSO and the Periodic Labour Force Survey PLFS, formal training increased from 1.6 in 2011-12 to 4.1 in 2023-24, non-formal hereditary training from 1.8 to 11.6, non-formal self-learning from 1.8 to 11.6, and non-formal on-the-job training increased from 1.7 to 9.3. However, close to 65 of people aged 15-59 remain without any form of training.This points to a significant skill deficit in India and a gap between skill workers possess and those required by the labour market. A 2022 study by the National Skill Development Corporation NSDC estimated a significant deficit of 29 million between the demand and supply of skilled workers in India, particularly in sectors like IT, BFSI, healthcare, semiconductor manufacturing, and green jobs. This has been attributed to the failure of the countrys education sector as well as the performance of the numerous ITIs. Indias skilling push Skilling can be defined as a process through which individuals gain a particular skill or set of skills. However, the nature of skills required in the labour market keeps evolving with technological advancements and changing occupational demands. Upskilling refers to acquiring relevant advanced skills within a field or occupation to keep pace with changing technologies, roles, and responsibilities. Reskilling, on the other hand, involves learning new skills for different areas or roles. Economist Amit Basole notes that in India, the definition of skill is entangled with notions of dignified work. First, jobs that require mental skills are often considered more prestigious than those that prioritise manual skills. Second, the nature of caste hierarchies has influenced the allocation and social valuation of occupations and skills based on them. Finally, certain skill-based institutions are considered more prestigious than others, reflected, for instance, in the distinctions between IITs and ITIs. The 11th Five-Year Plan 2007-2012 marked a shift in policy focus on skill development. The National Skills Policy was introduced in 2009, followed by the launch of the National Skill Development Mission by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship MSDE in 2015, which targeted training 400 million individuals by the end of 2022. During this time, vocational training institutes grew exponentially and a number of schemes were introduced, including the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana, and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme. Despite this, the country spends only around 3 of its educational budget on vocational education. The number of ITIs, established in 1950 under the Craftsmen Training Scheme, increased from 9776 in 2014 to 13888 in 2026. The number of National Skill Training Institutes, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendras, and Jan Shikshan Sansthans also increased. However, Basole notes that the character of the expansion changed because new ITIs were mostly private in nature, compared with the initial years till the 1980s when the government played a dominant role in their administration and expansion. More importantly, the expansion has not necessarily translated into comparable improvements in the quality and market-relevance of training. Why many ITIs seats are vacant It has also been found that students entering ITIs are more likely to have completed Class 10 and come largely from OBC, SC, and ST communities. Basole cautions against interpreting this pattern as a sign of inclusivity. Students from marginalised backgrounds face barriers in accessing educational opportunities and are more likely to drop out after Class 10 and 12. While relatively better-off students are more likely to pursue degree programmes or other forms of better or higher education, the caste-representation in ITIs is more likely a fallback option rather than an aspirational choice. The challenge is compounded by the large number of vacant seats in ITIs. According to NITI Aayogs 2023 Transforming Industrial Training Institutes report, in 2021, more than 50 seats in Andhra Pradesh and 58 in Assam stayed vacant, while only 47 of seats were occupied in Delhi. The reason for the large number of vacant seats has been attributed to a range of factors. The trade mix offered by ITIs remains heavily concentrated in manufacturing and technical occupations. For instance, the trade of electrician is offered by almost all ITIs, followed by the trade of fitter. Yet, around 65 of electrician seats and nearly 72 of fitter seats across ITIs are unoccupied, according to NITI Aayog. Notably, Indias growth story is largely driven by service, and ITIs have not been able to expand training relevant to service sectors, including financial services and information technology. Similarly, relevant trades such as AI, automation, and green technologies have not received much emphasis. As of 2022, only 0.09 of all the ITI students were placed, according to the NITI Aayog report. This represents a very dismal picture. Moreover, the gendered nature of trades offered by ITIs and a very distinct gendered pattern in the type of trades men and women apply for constitute other factors behind the vacant seats at ITIs. In addition, the shortage of instructors at ITIs is yet another constraint. What India can do to strengthen its skilling system So, what can be the way out for India to enhance its skill development? The evidence points towards several areas for reform. For instance, studies reveal that ITIs located near industrial belts are more likely to create employment. Trade mix and curricula need to evolve in keeping with the changing requirements of relevant industries and service-sector jobs, as well as emerging areas like AI and green skills. The gendered nature of ITIs also requires a transformation. This requires a more structural change where changing gendered roles and perceptions can lead to changes in gendered occupational trades. Other structural changes include greater spending on both general and vocational education. There has also been a rapid decline in the duration of skill development courses. As more people are completing their degrees and earning their certificates, these training programmes sometimes as short as 10 days have not resulted in acquiring gainful skills. Finally, international experiences can provide useful insights. For instance, Germany introduces an early vocational education model at the upper secondary level. Post read questions 1. What explains the persistent mismatch between the skills acquired by Indias workforce and those demanded by its labour market? Suggest measures to bridge this gap. 2. The expansion of Indias vocational training infrastructure has not necessarily translated into better employment outcomes. Discuss with reference to Industrial Training Institutes ITIs. 3. How can India move from a degree-centric education system towards an education model that integrates vocational training, apprenticeships and work-based learning? 4. How can India make its vocational education system more responsive to the growth of the services sector and emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, automation, electric vehicles and green technologies? 5. Gender and caste continue to shape participation and outcomes in Indias vocational education system. Discuss the structural factors responsible and suggest measures for making skill development more inclusive. articleTitle: Three years later, in West Asia, a peace still out of reach
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Three years later, a peace still out of reach
description: No lasting settlement is possible without Israel's participation, or without Hamas giving up arms in Gaza
body_raw: The horrific terror attack on Israel by Hamas three years ago, in which almost 1,200 were killed and 251 taken hostage, set in motion a war that continues to ripple far beyond Gaza. The devastation that followed has left Israel isolated internationally, with several Western nations formally recognising the State of Palestine. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahus decision to conduct joint military operations with the US against Iran, perceived to be weakened by internal turmoil and the decimation of its proxies, has plunged West Asia into further chaos. No lasting settlement in Gaza is possible without Israels participation, or without Hamas giving up arms - peace still doesnt look within reach. The situation in Gaza, where more than 70,000 people have been killed in the last three years, continues to be enormously disturbing. The humanitarian crisis remains acute, with shortages of supplies, displacement and military strikes by the Israel Defence Forces IDF despite the ceasefire that began almost a year ago. The much-touted peace plan of US President Donald Trump has made little progress. Only two weeks ago, the Board of Peace announced a 2.45 billion recovery plan for the Strip - a fraction of the 71.4 billion that the UN estimates will be required for recovery and reconstruction over the next decade. Hamass disarmament remains an issue locked in an impasse Israel says reconstruction cannot proceed without disarmament, while Hamas, which prolongs the stalemate and the suffering of Gazans, resists disarmament without a full Israeli withdrawal first. The first phase of the Trump plan envisaged Israel retaining control of 53 per cent of Gaza since then, however, IDF forces have expanded their presence to two-thirds of the Strip. The power to enforce meaningful progress lies ultimately with the White House, but the US President seems consumed by the political fallout of the war with Iran. At the same time, the once-unbreakable US-Israel alliance is fraying Public support for Israel in America has fallen to historic lows, and the bipartisan consensus around military aid shows signs of weakening. Within Israel, the Gaza war has exposed deep divisions over the governments conduct - especially in light of revelations that Netanyahu ignored warnings from Egypt and the UAE about an impending Hamas attack - and the countrys entanglement in regional conflicts, including in Lebanon and Syria. In 20 days, Israel will hold an election, giving citizens their first chance since the terror attack to pronounce a verdict on Netanyahu. The coalition that emerges after October 27 will help shape not only the future of Gaza, but also Israels trajectory. It will indicate whether three years of militarism can give way to a path that leads away from war.

articleTitle: India fined 20% of match fees, West Indies 10% as slow over rate in 3rd ODI draws ICC ire
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Indies' Shai Hope, left, and India's captain Shubman Gill after West Indies' won the third and final One Day International (ODI) cricket match of a series between India and West Indies, in Mullanpur, Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. (PTI Photo)
description: The match went on for over nine hours and the length of the game was pointed out by notably by former India head coach Ravi Shastri from the commentary box and by former wicketkeeper-batter Dinesh Karthik on social media.
body_raw: India and West Indies were both fined by the International Cricket Council on Monday for maintaining a slow over-rates during the third ODI in New Chandigarh. The match went on for over nine hours and the length of the game was pointed out by notably by former India head coach Ravi Shastri from the commentary box and by former wicketkeeper-batter Dinesh Karthik on social media. While India have been fined 20 per cent of their match fee, the West Indies were docked 10 per cent of their earnings after being ruled four and two overs short of their required over-rates respectively, once time allowances were taken into consideration. Match referee Prakash Bhatt imposed the sanctions after the match on Saturday. Both captains pleaded guilty to the offences and accepted the proposed sanctions, meaning there was no need for formal hearings, the ICC said in a statement. The charges were levelled by on-field umpires Jayaraman Madanagopal and Sam Nogajski, third umpire Sharfuddoula Ibne Shahid and fourth umpire Virender Sharma. While India finished with a 2-1 win in the series, the West Indies recorded a famous win in the match itself, rewriting the record for their highest succesfull run chase in ODIs. Captain Shai Hope led the way with an unbeaten 162 as West Indies chased down 352. It was the first time since December 2019 that India had lost an ODI match at home against the West Indies. Earlier, India captain Shubman Gill fell after scoring just one run in his domestic home ground, after having scored centuries in the previous two matches. Virat Kohli was out for a golden duck after that, ending his streak of big scores as well. Rohit Sharma then scored a 92 and that was followed by KL Rahuls unbeaten 162 pushed India to a total of 351 The two sides will now turn their attention to the five-match T20I series, which begins on Tuesday in Lucknow.

articleTitle: Punjabi LGBTQ influencer and makeup artist Mad Sandhu shot dead in Amritsar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Punjabi social media influencer and makeup artist Madhu Sudan
description: Police say they have some solid leads and will soon crack the case
body_raw: Punjabi social media influencer and makeup artist Madhu Sudan, popularly known as Mad Sandhu, was shot dead by unidentified persons in Amritsar on Saturday, with police saying they have some leads and the accused will be nabbed soon. The incident took place at Loharka Road at around 6 pm, while Sandhu, the son of a retired Punjab Police inspector, was waiting outside a car wash centre for his vehicle. Two unidentified assailants reached there on a motorcycle and opened fire at Sandhu before fleeing the spot, Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Sirivennela said. Around two to three rounds were fired, with an eyewitness claiming that Sandhu was shot at close range. A purported video of the incident showed Sandhu lying in a pool of blood. He was rushed to a private hospital where he succumbed to his injuries, police said. Based on a statement from the family, police registered an FIR and initiated the preliminary investigation. The motive of the attack was yet to be ascertained, a senior police officer said, adding they were working on multiple angles. Deputy Commissioner of Police DCP, Investigation, Amritsar Commissionerate, Prabhjot Singh Virk said, The investigation is currently in its initial stages. We have leads and will solve the case very soon. We have recorded the familys statement. Sandhu used to speak about make-up artistry and gender issues on podcasts and had built a strong digital presence, accumulating around 2.4 lakh followers on Instagram. The make-up artist was also the founder of Mane Lane Unisex Salon in Amritsar and actively operated beauty academies offering courses ranging from self-makeup to professional bridal artistry. Sandhu, who often faced homophobic trolling on his gay identity, would hit back, saying God has made me the way I am, and would remind his audience that if coming from a Jat Sikh family and living in a city like Amritsar, he could achieve success in life, then they too could. His follower base was highly polarised. While admirers supported his creativity, self-expression, and professional artistry by leaving encouraging comments on his tutorials and on his gender-fluid fashion choices, the posts also frequently attracted aggressive online harassment, homophobic trolling, and derogatory commentary questioning his credibility as an educator. A few months ago, an audio-video clip went viral featuring a confrontation between Sandhu and a Nihang Singh, with the latter objecting to the influencers social media activities, cross-dressing choices, and older video reels, warning him to refrain from content deemed harmful to Punjabi culture and youth. Although Sandhu issued a public clarification stating he had changed his content style and stopped repeating past mistakes, he maintained that old clips were being recirculated intentionally to manufacture unnecessary controversy. Congress leader Raj Kumar Verka slammed the AAP government over Sandhus murder, saying the law and order has completely collapsed in Punjab. The AAP government has failed to protect the life of the common man.There is an atmosphere of fear. Meanwhile, Bhagwant Manns government puts up massive hoardings proclaiming a magnificent government and an honest government. It is astonishing that neither Arvind Kejriwal nor Bhagwant Mann said a word about this, he said. Amritsar MP Gurjeet Singh Aujla said Sandhu had been receiving threats for a long time and had openly mentioned these threats on social media as well. Despite this, the government and police failed to take the matter as seriously as they should have, he said, adding that if the threats had been taken seriously in time and necessary security measures had been put in place, perhaps an innocent life could have been saved. Aujla demanded the early arrest of the accused and a thorough investigation into the case.

articleTitle: ‘Further custody necessary’: ED gets Vatika promoters’ custody for 3 more days
articleFeaturedImageAlt: vatika
description: The Bhallas, arrested on September 28, were produced before Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (PMLA) Narender Sura after their initial four-day remand expired.
body_raw: A special Prevention of Money Laundering Act PMLA court in Gurugram on Friday extended the Enforcement Directorates ED custody of Vatika Limited chairman-cum-managing director Anil Bhalla and promoter Gautam Bhalla by three days in an alleged Rs 154-crore money laundering case linked to plot transactions in Gurugram. The Bhallas, arrested on September 28, were produced before Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge PMLA Narender Sura after their initial four-day remand expired. Seeking seven more days of custody on behalf of the ED, special public prosecutors Simon Benjamin and Atul Agarwal, along with Assistant Director Dilip Singh Shaktawat Investigating Officer, submitted that although statements of several individuals, including the accused, were recorded during the four-day custody, interrogation could not be concluded due to paucity of time and bulky record. The ED argued that custody was essential to confront the promoters with documentary evidence and with 10 other individuals acquainted with the case who have been summoned for recording statements. It said further custody was required to unearth and trace the proceeds of crime and verify the involvement of other persons in the alleged transactions. Opposing the plea, the defence argued that ED had sufficient time to complete its interrogation and alleged that notices issued on October 1 summoning witnesses were intended just to get the ED custody extended. The defence also submitted that the accused had not been confronted with any of the individuals whose statements had been recorded during the four-day remand. Instead, they were questioned about extracts of statements and contractual agreements already in the EDs possession, it was alleged. Maintaining that the investigation is entirely grounded in documentary evidence, including public documents, the defence urged the court to decline any extension. Partly allowing the EDs application, Judge Sura said that further custody of the accused was needed for the probe. After perusing the record produced before this court, the nature of investigation conducted till date, and the fact that for the purpose of thorough investigation, some other persons have been summoned for making statements under Section 50 of the Act, which may be required to be put to the accused for clarification of the facts, further custody is necessary, the court said. The court directed that both accused be produced before it on October 5 at 4 pm. The EDs probe, initiated in March on the basis of Delhi Police Economic Offences Wing FIRs, concerns allegations arising from plot transactions involving residential plots of Vatika India Next in Sectors 82 to 85 and Vatika India Next-2 in Sector 88A. The agency has alleged that land contracted for plots collected for between 2010 and 2012 was not substantially delivered and that some plots were redeveloped and sold to third parties. It has valued the allegedly undelivered plots at Rs 140.73 crore. The second allegation concerns a 2024 agreement with Scaler Ventures for 165 plots in Vatika India Next-2, where 14 plots were allegedly sold to third parties without consent. The agency has pegged the total alleged proceeds of crime in the case at around Rs 154.36 crore.

articleTitle: 60-year-old man out on morning walk killed in elephant attack in Bengaluru
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru elephant attack, elephant attack Bengaluru, Bengaluru elephant attack today, Mysore Road elephant attack, man killed by elephant Bengaluru, Bengaluru elephant news, Doddabele elephant attack, Bannerghatta elephant, Bengaluru forest officials, elephant sighting Bengaluru, Kumbalagodu elephant attack, Nagaraju elephant attack, Bengaluru news, Indian Express news
description: Bengaluru forest department officials have launched an operation to locate and capture the elephant.
body_raw: A morning walk turned fatal for a 60-year-old man after he was attacked and killed by a wild elephant close to Mysore Road in West Bengaluru early Monday. Nagaraju, a resident of Anchepalya near Mysore Road, was attacked around 5.30 am near Doddabele village. He was walking with his daughter, who was a short distance behind him when the incident occurred. According to the police, Nagaraju had left home for his routine morning walk when the elephant appeared on the stretch. There were other walkers who were on the same stretch, and when they saw the elephant, they ran away. Nagaraju did not get a chance to escape and was attacked by the elephant, an officer said. The police said he suffered multiple rib fractures in the attack. The elephant left the area soon after the attack. Passers-by rushed Nagaraju to Raja Rajeshwari Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival. The police have registered a case and are awaiting the post-mortem report. Officials of the Kaggalipura forest range under the Bengaluru Urban Division have launched an operation to locate and capture the elephant. Forest officials suspect the animal may have strayed from the Bannerghatta Wildlife Sanctuary. According to local residents, elephants were frequently sighted in the area until three or four years ago, but such sightings had become less common. Elephants are known to move between the Bannerghatta and B M Kaval forest areas, sometimes venturing towards the Vrishabhavathi River in search of water. A resident said the area was once part of the BM Kaval forest and a known elephant habitat, but much of the forest has since been cleared for real estate development. Historically, this was an elephant habitat which has been encroached upon by people, the resident added.

articleTitle: The Gandhi students think they know — and the challenge of teaching them
articleFeaturedImageAlt: gandhi jayanti
description: Before the formal syllabus, students often have already met him through an “unofficial curriculum”: Inherited polemics, decontextualised quotations and photographs, and increasingly derisive memes, reels, forwards and videos carrying ready-made verdicts
body_raw: By Praveen Dhanda In the 1930s and 1940s, Gandhi entered Indraprastha College, Delhis oldest womens college, not through a syllabus but through movements. During the Civil Disobedience Movement, students marched, picketed liquor and foreign-cloth shops, and held a bonfire of foreign cloth on the premises. During Quit India, the involvement intensified. Students jumped the college walls to join processions, assisted Aruna Asaf Ali in putting up anti-British posters, and several were jailed. The college magazine of 1944, Pradeep, recorded the Charkha Association, supported by charkhas purchased from Students Union funds and donated by professors. A 1937 handwritten college magazine in the college archives offers another glimpse of how Gandhi then figured in the student imagination. Beneath a pen-and-ink portrait, a student named Indra Vati penned a poem Gandhi, urging her fellow students to follow our great and gallant hero. Nearly nine decades later, Gandhi arrives in my political thought classes at the same college, having already been taught elsewhere. Before the formal syllabus, students often have already met him through an unofficial curriculum Inherited polemics, decontextualised quotations and photographs, and increasingly derisive memes, reels, forwards and videos carrying ready-made verdicts. This unofficial curriculum lands well against a familiar, flattened moral portrait inherited from school, making the supposedly hidden or scandalous Gandhi feel like a revelation. The pattern is wider than the classroom. The pedagogical difficulty is not criticism itself, but postponing the verdict long enough for understanding to begin. With Gandhi, more than with most thinkers, students often arrive with premature certainty. A student who says, I know little about a thinker gives the teacher considerable room. A student who has seen three reels, corroborated by another video, and thinks the case is closed presents a different challenge. The pre-judgment can extend to the teacher too. An attempt to explain an aspect is quickly read through the pro-or-anti binary. True, the students of the 1930s and 1940s also had an unofficial curriculum of Gandhi, but it had a practical grammar around it. The two unofficial curricula are not simply positive and negative versions they differ in how knowledge of Gandhi is produced and acquired. In the earlier mode, khadi was worn, spinning done, picketing undertaken, processions joined - or at least these were live possibilities in the world around. In significant measure, it asked students what Gandhi required of them. The contemporary one readily asks what judgment they should pass on him The self moves outside the frame, while Gandhi becomes the object to be judged. The concepts remain in the formal syllabus, without much of the world of practice. The result is that Gandhi naturally looks artificial. Against this backdrop, a mischievously framed meme or reel finds fertile ground. It favours the visible over the conceptual, the incident over the context, the striking over the slow, and the person over the idea. As one is more a spectator than a participant, the direction of scrutiny also shifts from self-examination what does this demand of me? to other-examination what does this reveal about him?. In this low-friction form of knowing, a fragment can be seen, judged and repeated with little resistance, and repetition itself passes for corroboration. This facilitates premature certainty. So we get a peculiar contemporary split. The formal curriculum gives the student Gandhis thought without much of its practice the unofficial curriculum gives her Gandhi the person without much of his thought. Gandhi is especially vulnerable to this split, because he made life itself a site of philosophical and political practice. Perhaps nowhere is this split more visible than in the attention given to Gandhis experiments with brahmacharya. For many, this is among the most vivid things they know about him. One class was revealing. Students invoked a familiar photograph of Gandhi with young women, including his grandniece Manu, and presented it through the visible facts of age, gender and bodily proximity, within an already sexualised frame. Detached from its conceptual world, the episode is easily reduced, as in many online memes, to something like Old man, young woman, bed. Once described that way, the verdict is almost built into the description. When the photograph is placed back within the conceptual world that such a description leaves out Manus own account of Gandhi as her mother Gandhis attempt to think through motherhood and naritva, which Ashis Nandy reads as a challenge to conventional masculinity brahmacharya as self-mastery tied to swaraj and self-purification and the surrounding communal bloodshed of Noakhali, the frame shifts. This did not settle all ethical questions. But many questions receded, others grew more nuanced, and the impulse to deliver a verdict gave way, at least for a while, to self-reflection. The writer teaches at Indraprastha College, Delhi University. Views are personal

articleTitle: How Rashami Desai lost 4.5 kg in 25 days: ‘Nobody is ready to believe’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rashami Desai
description: Walking is one of the simplest and most sustainable forms of physical activity, but is it enough?
body_raw: Actor Rashami Desai once candidly spoke about her weight loss journey, sharing that travelling and walking helped her find peace of mind and lose weight. Now, my fitness mantra is set. Previously, I was a blindfolded horse who only wanted to work. I put on a lot of weight in the middle. I lost around 4.5 kgs within 25 days. I went on a trip, leaving everything. Work is important, but you really need peace of mind. I didnt lose as much from workouts as I lost from walking. And nobody is ready to believe because I was travelling for 1.5 months. Along with travelling, I walked so much, and I was eating healthy. Thats when I understood that health doesnt mean only going to the gym and lifting weights. It can be something you enjoy and lose weight as well as mentally feel great, she told the Care World TV in 2020. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. When Rashami Desai opened up about losing weight with the help of walking and bolster-based exercises, it highlighted an important fitness lesson weight loss does not always require high-intensity workouts or hours in the gym. Low-impact movement, when performed consistently and combined with appropriate nutrition, can also contribute meaningfully to a fitness transformation, said consultant dietitian Garima Goyal. Walking is one of the simplest and most sustainable forms of physical activity. Goyal shared how regular brisk walking increases daily energy expenditure, supports cardiovascular health, improves insulin sensitivity, and can contribute to fat loss when accompanied by an appropriate calorie deficit. It is also relatively low-impact, making it accessible to people who may find intense workouts difficult because of their fitness level or joint concerns, said Goyal. However, walking and exercise alone do not guarantee weight loss. As pointed out by Desai, overall calorie balance, adequate protein intake, portion control, sleep, and consistency all play important roles. Ideally, walking and mobility-based workouts should eventually be complemented with some form of progressive resistance training to help preserve and build lean muscle mass during weight loss, stressed Goyal. Starting with accessible activities such as walking and gradually progressing your exercise routine can often be more sustainable than jumping into an extreme fitness programme, said Goyal. articleTitle: The joy of making: How two Pune spaces are helping adults rediscover creativity and community
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pune art and craft classes
description: Two art and craft spaces in Pune are attempting to answer that question by creating places where adults can learn, experiment and, perhaps, find a community along the way.
body_raw: Written by Kalyani Lad For many adults, leisure is squeezed between work, family responsibilities and the demands of everyday life. But what happens when the desire to learn something new remains, while the time, confidence and community to pursue it seem increasingly harder to find? Two art and craft spaces in Pune are attempting to answer that question by creating places where adults can learn, experiment and, perhaps, find a community along the way. One such studio, inaugurated in August, is barely a few weeks old, but its idea has been nearly two decades in the making. Its founder, Aditi Deo, an artist and teacher who has worked with children and adults, says the idea emerged from a gap she saw in the city the lack of spaces where adults could simply learn and experiment without feeling they had to be experts. There are hardly any activities like these for adults. You tend to attach importance to an activity based on how it benefits your overall well-being. It is not just about learning the activity through the activity, you get a sense of well-being, says Deo. The studio offers regular classes in watercolour, pen-and-ink and pencil sketching, while gradually expanding into yarn crafts, crochet, knitting, embroidery and other creative workshops. A ukulele club has also begun, with a zine-making workshop planned. For Deo, however, the studio is about more than acquiring a skill. It is about creating a space for adults who may suddenly find themselves with more time, but fewer opportunities to connect with others. We are now at an age where there is a lot of time, but there is nothing to do, and no place to go, she says. The classes are therefore kept flexible. Participants can move between batches, attend individual sessions and access recordings, allowing them to fit learning around unpredictable schedules rather than the other way around. The approach also takes into account the multiple responsibilities many women continue to juggle. Yet time may not be the biggest barrier. For many adults, it is the hesitation to begin. Deo believes people often assume they need to possess a certain talent before taking up art. She argues that creativity need not be pursued for a certificate, career or even perfection. If you remove the expectation that I want to be a good artist, you will be good from day one. Good in art is very subjective, she says. While paid classes help sustain the studio, Deo also hopes to keep parts of the space accessible to those who simply want to sit, create or spend time in an environment that encourages creativity. In a city where adult life can easily become defined by work and obligation, the studio is attempting something simple creating space for curiosity. A screen-free sanctuary In Kharadi, another small space filled with yarn, fabric and conversations is bringing together people looking to learn traditional crafts while spending time away from screens. Rhoda Stanley, 62, started The Craft Room in July 2025. It was not originally conceived as a business. After spending years abroad and returning to India in 2020 during the pandemic, Stanley noticed how people were increasingly isolated, indoors and glued to screens. The space had initially been intended for her sons clinic. When he began practising elsewhere, Stanley decided against renting it out and instead asked herself what she could give back to society. The answer came through something she had always known craft. A social work graduate from Mumbai and a lifelong maker, Stanley works with crochet, knitting, embroidery and quilting. Over time, she says, she noticed a break in the transmission of these skills between generations. People would always say, I have seen my grandmother do it. Their mothers didnt, they dont, and so their children wont, she says. What began as hobby classes has grown into a space where participants can learn crafts while also meeting others. In its first year, more than 100 participants, from 10-year-olds to working professionals, mothers of children with special needs and expectant mothers, have attended the classes. Aishwarya Raj Katawat, who attended one of Stanleys classes, says the space helped her reconnect with a part of herself she had put aside. During my pregnancy, when I was five months along, discovering the studio felt like a godsend gift. It gave me a way to reconnect with the creative side of myself that I had put aside. I had always thought of embroidery as something girls were simply expected to learn. But here, I discovered that it could be a form of artistic expression, a way to mend, create and tell a story, she says. Stanleys courses are structured, with five sessions for crochet and embroidery and six for quilting. They include material kits, lessons on the history of the crafts and informal conversations over tea. For Stanley, the process is as important as the finished product. The classes, she says, teach patience, perseverance and a sense of ownership. Growing old is not a block, she says. God has prepared for every stage of life something. I am in a stage where I can give, and people are willing to receive. At a time when many activities are increasingly mediated through screens and designed for instant consumption, these spaces are bringing people back to something slower the simple act of making something by hand. Kalyani Lad is an intern with The Indian Express

articleTitle: Rajasthan smuggler began new life in Madhya Pradesh as furniture trader. Then police closed in
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajasthan smuggler began new life in MP as furniture trader. Then police closed in
description: After he was named a wanted drug smuggler, Vishna Ram stayed at different locations in Rajasthan, including rented accommodation in Jodhpur and houses of relatives.
body_raw: A wanted drug smuggler from Barmer, who has been evading arrest for nearly two years, was arrested by the Anti-Narcotics Task Force ANTF from Mandsaur in Madhya Pradesh. The accused, identified as 32-year-old Vishna Ram, son of Madaram, a resident of Kudla in Barmer, was carrying a reward of Rs 1 lakh. Police said he had changed his identity and had been running a furniture business in Madhya Pradesh to avoid arrest. According to police, Vishna Ram had been involved in criminal activities for around 12 years and has over 18 cases including those under the NDPS Act, attempt to murder, assault, Arms Act, theft and fraud, registered against him in different police stations of Rajasthan. ANTF Inspector General Vikas Kumar said, Vishna Ram had studied up to Class 12 and initially worked as a driver. He later came into contact with drug smugglers while working as a labourer. His grandfather was addicted to poppy husk, and Vishna Ram initially began procuring small quantities for him. He subsequently came into contact with smugglers in Neemuch and entered the drug trade himself. Over the years, he allegedly established links with smugglers in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and Haryana and supplied drugs in the Marwar region. Police said he eventually became a key link in the trafficking network operating between Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, police said. After he was named a wanted drug smuggler, Vishna Ram stayed at different locations in Rajasthan, including rented accommodation in Jodhpur and houses of relatives. With repeated police raids making it difficult for him to remain in the state, he eventually shifted to Madhya Pradesh, which he believed would be a safer place to hide. There, he started a furniture business and began living like an ordinary businessman to conceal his past. However, the ANTF continued tracking him. The breakthrough Police officials said the breakthrough came after information was received that Vishna Ram was running a furniture business in Madhya Pradesh and had called artisans from Jodhpur to work. The ANTF team began monitoring the movement of the artisans and followed the trail to Umaria village under the Pipliy Mandi police station area of Mandsaur district. When the team reached the location, Vishna Ram was allegedly partying with his friends and some of the artisans at the house of his smuggler associates uncle. The premises were surrounded and Vishna Ram was arrested.

articleTitle: Second Saraighat Bridge in Assam: New rail-cum-road link across Brahmaputra to boost Northeast connectivity
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Proposed second Saraighat Bridge in Assam (Image: Northeast Frontier Railway)
description: Second Saraighat Bridge Assam: The Second Saraighat Rail-Cum-Road Bridge project in Assam will add a new link across the Brahmaputra, while doubling the Agthori-Kamakhya railway section to boost rail capacity and strengthen Northeast connectivity.
body_raw: Second Saraighat Bridge in Assam The Ministry of Railways is set to begin the construction of Second Saraighat Rail-Cum-Road Bridge Project in Assam, along with doubling of the railway track between Agthori and Kamakhya stations. The projects are aimed at further strengthening rail and road connectivity across the Brahmaputra. It will also increase transportation capacity for Guwahati and enhance connectivity of the Northeastern region. The project falls under the administrative jurisdiction of Northeast Frontier Railway NFR zone. According to Kapinjal Kishore Sharma, Chief Public Relations Officer CPRO of Northeast Frontier Railway, the project is an important addition to Assams transportation infrastructure and will strengthen the movement of both passengers and goods across the region. Doubling of Agthori-Kamakhya railway line The railway-doubling project between Agthori and Kamakhya stations covers 7.20 km. It was sanctioned by the Ministry of Railways in 2024, following which detailed planning and tendering work was taken up. According to Sharma, Larsen Toubro LT has been entrusted with executing the project. Given the location of the new bridge in a highly developed urban environment, the project has involved considerable challenges relating to land acquisition, removal of encroachments and shifting of existing utilities, he said. According to NFR, a substantial part of these challenges has already been addressed with the support of the state government and local administration. Meanwhile, engineering work has also progressed, with geotechnical investigations completed and major engineering, design and construction drawing activities underway. New double-decker bridge over Brahmaputra A major part of the project is the 1.3-km-long Double-Decker Rail-Cum-Road Bridge over the River Brahmaputra. The new bridge will have Two railway lines on the lower deck A three-lane road carriageway on the upper deck A footpath along the road deck This will increase capacity compared with the existing Saraighat Bridge, which currently carries one railway line and a two-lane road. The main bridge will be constructed on well foundations and will have a welded Open Web Girder superstructure with a 125-metre span. The bridge will also be connected to approach viaducts on both sides. The viaduct will extend for around 600 metres on the Agthori side and 200 metres on the Kamakhya side. The viaducts will be supported on pile foundations with composite girder superstructures for both railway and road components, with four road spans on each side forming part of the integrated double-decker arrangement. The project will also interface with the road approaches being developed by NHAI, providing connectivity towards Jalukbari on one side and the Agthori-side road network on the other, the CPRO said in a statement. Construction of Second Saraighat Bridge NFR said the project is being planned with a focus on modern construction technology, digital engineering, quality and safety. Digital monitoring and bridge instrumentation systems will be incorporated to help monitor the structure and its performance. The construction methodology is being tailored to the challenging conditions of the Brahmaputra River with particular focus on foundation construction, structural erection, quality assurance, construction safety and long-term durability, the railway official said. Significance of Second Saraighat Bridge The Second Saraighat Bridge is expected to add more capacity to an important transportation corridor connecting the two banks of the Brahmaputra. Sharma said that the additional railway capacity will facilitate smoother movement of passenger and freight traffic, while the three-lane road component will strengthen connectivity between the northern and southern banks of the city and support its future transportation requirements. By bringing together rail, road and associated approach infrastructure as a single integrated corridor, the project will enhance multimodal connectivity across the Brahmaputra. The project is being closely supported and monitored by the concerned authorities, including the Railway Board, reflecting its importance for connectivity and capacity enhancement in the Northeastern region. Its integration with the NHAI road approaches will further strengthen the multimodal connectivity of the corridor, he added.

articleTitle: Alcohol shop charges Rs 75 extra for beer bottle, Himachal man wins Rs 12,500 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: consumer court beer case
description: The commission observed that selling any packaged commodity or excisable product above its printed MRP constitutes a flagrant violation of laws.
body_raw: A consumer commission in Himachal Pradesh has directed a liquor shop and its salesman to refund Rs 75 and pay 12,500 to a customer after he was allegedly charged Rs 230 for a beer bottle carrying a maximum retail price MRP of Rs 155. President Hemanshu Mishra and members Arti Sood and Narayan Thakur observed that selling any packaged commodity or excisable product above its printed MRP constitutes a flagrant violation of the Legal Metrology Act, Consumer Protection Act, and state excise regulations. Charging above the MRP amounts to an unfair trade practice under Section 247 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, as well as a severe deficiency in service. The refusal to issue a receipt further demonstrates an intent to conceal illegal trade practices, the order read. Illegal trade practices According to the complaint, the complainant visited a liquor shop in Kangra on April 27, 2026, and purchased a bottle of beer. It was stated that the bottle carried an MRP of Rs 155, but the salesman charged him Rs 230, resulting in an overcharge of Rs 75. When the customer objected, the salesman allegedly told him that he was charging the amount on the instructions of the shop owner. The salesman also allegedly refused to issue a purchase receipt. Alleging gross deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, the complainant moved consumer commission seeking a refund and compensation. The liquor shop and its salesman did not appear before the commission after being served with notices and were proceeded against ex-parte. The commission noted that the complainants evidence therefore remained unrebutted and unchallenged. The opposite parties, despite valid service of notice, chose not to contest the complaint and opted to remain ex-parte. Consequently, the evidence adduced by the complainant remains entirely unrebutted, unchallenged, and uncontroverted. There is no legal or factual reason to disbelieve the cogent, trustworthy, and convincing evidence adduced by the complainant, it said. The commission found that the complainant had established that he was charged Rs 230 for a product bearing an MRP of Rs 155. It also noted that refusal to issue a receipt further showed an intent to conceal illegal trade practices. The commission thus allowed the complaint and directed the opposite parties to jointly and severally refund Rs 75 and awarded Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 7,500 litigation costs. Taking note of what it described as the gravity of the illegal overcharging and the alleged defiance of excise norms by a licensed liquor vend, the commission directed that a copy of its order be sent to the Additional Commissioner, Excise and Taxation Department, Dharamshala, for strict departmental and penal action as per rules. Takeaway Sellers cannot charge consumers more than the printed MRP. Overcharging above the MRP can amount to an unfair trade practice and deficiency in service, attracting refund, compensation and litigation costs. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Himachal Pradesh helpline 18001808087 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Slept on mats, couldn’t afford rent; Hrithik Roshan’s Rs 2,500 cr wealth rebuilt family fortune
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hrithik Roshan
description: Hrithik Roshan is now worth Rs 2,500 crore, but once saw dad Rakesh lose everything and mortgage his house and cars to launch him.
body_raw: Hrithik Roshan is now among Indias wealthiest actors, with an estimated net worth of Rs 2,500 crore, according to the Hurun India Rich List 2026. The actor ranks fourth among Indian actors on the list, behind Shah Rukh Khan, Amitabh Bachchan and Salman Khan. His wealth also includes his business interests, including his HRX brand. The figure stands in contrast to the financial uncertainty Hrithik witnessed while growing up, particularly during some of the most difficult phases of his father Rakesh Roshans career. Hrithik saw Rakesh Roshan lose everything after Koyla Rakesh Roshans 1997 film Koyla, starring Shah Rukh Khan and Madhuri Dixit, was unsuccessful at the box office and left the filmmaker facing serious financial difficulties. In an old interview with Zee ETC Bollywood, Hrithik recalled seeing his father break down over the losses. There was a time, I think after one of his films, I think after Koyla, when there were some problems at home. He had lost all his money. Whatever he had earned, everything that he had earned, so there were problems coming from all sides. I saw him one morning, and whatever he had made, he said, I have lost everything. So that was the first time, actually, that I saw tears in his eyes. Rakesh Roshan could not afford the familys rent The Koyla setback was part of a longer period of financial struggle for the Roshan family. In a 2006 interview with Simi Garewal, Hrithik recalled that there was a time when his father could not afford their rent. His mother, Pinky Roshan, took Hrithik and his sister to her parents home while Rakesh stayed with his mother. Until the time my dad could earn enough money to buy another house. And then we shifted into another house which was barely just walls and floors. We slept on mattresses, these mats and slowly got the furniture in, Hrithik said. Rakesh later recalled his own struggles as an actor and the uncertainty of providing for his family. As an actor, I was not that successful but I kept trying. I never moved ahead in my career despite some of my movies doing well. So I started producing films and then moved to direction. Now, when I look back, I feel happy. Back then, I had no idea how I would get the money to run my house. I had two children, a wife and a family to look after. But somehow we always managed, he said. ALSO READ Inside Imtiaz Alis daughter Ida Ali and Krish Agrawals intimate engagement Just us, ours Rakesh mortgaged house and cars to launch Hrithik When Rakesh decided to launch his son as a leading actor with Kaho Naa. Pyaar Hai, he took another major financial risk. The film went around Rs 3 crore over budget, and Rakesh mortgaged his house and cars to fund it. Hrithik did not initially know about the financial risk his father was taking. I said I am mortgaging the house, maybe if I require, I will take money, otherwise I will try to manage. But it so happened that I managed it with the funds I had. Had the film not done well, then I would have to shift somewhere else or. but I took that chance, Rakesh had told Mid-Day. Hrithik only learned the extent of what his father had risked later. In The Roshans, he recalled how his mother told him that the family home and cars had been mortgaged. Thats the night I found out, my mom told me, that the house was mortgaged, the cars were mortgaged. I realised how much was at stake, Hrithik said. Kaho Naa. Pyaar Hai changed everything Released in 2000, Kaho Naa. Pyaar Hai became a major success and launched Hrithik as a leading Bollywood star. The film, directed and produced by Rakesh Roshan, also starred Ameesha Patel. For Rakesh, the gamble paid off. For Hrithik, it marked the beginning of a career that would eventually take his estimated wealth to Rs 2,500 crore. articleTitle: Uruguay announce star-studded squad for India match in Kolkata

description: The Uruguay match is a part of a high-profile series of international friendlies which India will play in September-October, which also includes clashes with 5-time world champions Brazil and Panama in October 3 and September 25 respectively.
body_raw: Uruguay coach Diego Forlan on Saturday announced a star-studded squad for the October 6th friendly vs India in Kolkata with Real Madrids Federico Valverde and former Liverpool striker Darwin Nunez headlining. The match is a part of a high-profile series of international friendlies which India will play in September-October, which also includes clashes with 5-time world champions Brazil and Panama in October 3 and September 25 respectively. The announcement comes at the beginning of a new chapter for Uruguay following Marcelo Bielsas departure, with legendary former striker Diego Forlan taking charge of the senior national team and the Under-20 side, said All India Football Federation AIFF in a statement. Now, as Uruguays head coach, Forlan faces a new challenge as he prepares his side for the upcoming clash against India. With established stars such as Valverde, Nunez, Araujo and Gimenez featuring alongside a new generation of talent, Uruguays September-October window promises to offer an early glimpse into Forlans vision for the next chapter of La Celeste, the statement added. Valverde is among several marquee names in the Uruguay squad, which also includes Rodrigo Bentancur, Lucas Torreira, Giorgian de Arrascaeta, Facundo Pellistri, Maximiliano Araujo and Brian Rodriguez. The defence boasts plenty of international experience, with Ronald Araujo, Jose Maria Gimenez, Nahitan Nandez, Guillermo Varela, Mathias Olivera and Sebastian Caceres named in the squad. Santiago Mele, Cristopher Fiermarin and Ignacio de Arruabarrena are the three goalkeeping options, while the attack features Nunez, along with Miguel Merentiel, Rodrigo Aguirre, Federico Vinas, Martin Satriano and Alvaro Rodriguez. The match in Kolkata will also mark Forlans first assignment at the helm of Uruguay, with the former World Cup star taking charge of the national side as coach. articleTitle: CBI arrests DGCA official, firm director in bribery case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: CBI arrests DGCA official, firm director in bribery case
description: The agency has alleged that Garg demanded and accepted a bribe of Rs 2.5 lakh for extending undue favours in the airworthiness certification of the aircraft operated by the private firm.
body_raw: THE CBI has arrested Directorate General of Civil Aviation DGCA Deputy Director Airworthiness Sushil Kumar Garg, posted in Chennai, and Director of Ekvi Air Training Organisation Pvt Ltd Sushil Kumar Garg in connection with an alleged bribery case. The agency has alleged that Garg demanded and accepted a bribe of Rs 2.5 lakh for extending undue favours in the airworthiness certification of the aircraft operated by the private firm. According to sources, the payment was linked to regulatory clearances concerning the airworthiness of aircraft operated by Ekvi Air Training Organisation Pvt. Ltd. Airworthiness certification is a key regulatory process intended to ensure that aircraft meet prescribed safety and operational standards. Besides Garg and Bhane, the CBI has also named the company and other unknown persons in the case, officials said. Further investigation is underway to ascertain the role of other individuals in the case and to examine whether the purported exchange of money was part of a wider arrangement involving aviation-related approvals, the agency said. The CBI had received inputs about the alleged bribe demand, following which an FIR was registered and a raid was conducted, sources said. According to officials, Garg accepted the Rs 2.5 lakh bribe, after which he and Bhane were arrested. The agency will move court seeking transit remand of the accused officer to bring him to the national capital for questioning, they said.

articleTitle: Late-night drive, masked men and 999 call: How a woman farmer may have foiled UK terror plot
articleFeaturedImageAlt: uk-terror-plot
description: Half past one in the morning. An empty lane. Three abandoned vans. And then, masked men breaking from the shadows. One farmer's 999 call may have stopped an attack on RAF Fairford before it began.
body_raw: It was 1.30am on a country lane in Gloucestershire, and a farmer driving home from a party found her route blocked. Three white vans sat abandoned across the road, with nobody in sight. As she turned the car around, men in balaclavas broke from the scene and scattered, some into the fields, others through the trees towards RAF Fairford, an air base a few hundred metres away that the US uses to strike Iranian missile sites. She did not stop. She drove off, called 999, and warned her neighbours on WhatsApp to lock their doors. Less than 25 minutes later, five men were sitting handcuffed in the road, surrounded by counter-terror police. By 8am, police had declared a major incident, 85 homes had been evacuated, and army bomb disposal teams were examining the vans behind a 400-metre cordon. By Sunday evening the story had reached the top of government. Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being kept updated, US President Donald Trump was commenting on the arrests, and counter-terrorism police were asking whether Iran was behind a suspected attack on a base that sits at the centre of the war. I am quite lucky The farmers account Speaking to The Telegraph, the farmer, who has not been named for her own safety, said she has since thought about what could have happened had the men tried to stop her car. She told the paper it was pretty incredible to have had a brush with potential terrorists face to face. She said the vans looked wrong from the first moment, and that the air base had been under a credible terror threat before that night. The UK and U.S. have a local farmer to thank for alerting police to a potential terrorist attack.She was driving home from a party, when she spotted what appeared to be 3 abandoned white vans.They were blocking a country road.She turned her car around in confusion. pic.twitter.comRjCEICtIYJ- Mario Nawfal MarioNawfal September 27, 2026 One van carried the name FUEL 2YOU in red lettering with a Sheffield phone number. The Telegraph reported that the number was one digit short and did not connect when reporters called it, and that the company name returns no results on Google or Companies House. The real fuel delivery firm, Fuel2U, has said its name was used without its knowledge or permission and that it is helping the authorities. What have police said? Five men were arrested first under explosives law and then on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, under section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2000. That allows police to hold them for up to 14 days without charge. Vicki Evans, the senior national co-ordinator for Counter Terrorism Policing, said the inquiry is at an early stage with five men in custody. She said police are working closely with partners to understand what happened. Police have not released the mens nationalities or set out their lines of inquiry. A source familiar with the investigation told Reuters that an Iran-linked motive is seen as the most likely, while a Russian sabotage plot and an Islamist plot are also being examined. Did the US know about the plot? Trump told reporters the men were looking to do big damage and that the US had them under view for a long time, calling the arrests an amazing job. That account is not matched by Whitehall. Sources told The Telegraph the arrests were not a planned operation and were not intelligence-led. Gloucestershire Police said it only learned the men were in the village of Whelford because of the farmers 999 call. MAJOR BREAKING President Trump CONFIRMS a group of terrorist were ARRESTED in the UK after they tried blowing up RAF Fairford Base - home to both US and UK troopsThey were looking to do big damage to our fort.we had them under view for a long time. AND WE GOT EM. .- USA Report UsaReport07 September 28, 2026 Why is RAF Fairford a target? RAF Fairford is a forward operating base for US forces in Europe. The UK government has allowed US bombers there to carry out strikes on Iranian missile sites that have been hitting ships in the Strait of Hormuz. In July, Irans Revolutionary Guards warned Britain not to let US bombers fly from Fairford, saying any base used to launch attacks would be a legitimate target. Britain replied that its armed forces were ready to protect the country. Local councillor Tristan Wilkinson told Reuters there was a specific threat from Iranians against the base about six weeks ago, and that surveillance in the area was increased at the time. The real thing what experts say about the vans Former Army bomb disposal officer Lucy Lewis told The Telegraph the scene had the hallmarks of a large attack. Its the real thing, she said, pointing to black barrels seen beside the vans and saying such loads are often fertiliser-based. Dr Antonio Giustozzi of the Royal United Services Institute said the set-up looked like a multi-vehicle suicide attack, with one vehicle used to break through each ring of security. He said the attackers would have been unlikely to reach US jets given the bases defences. What has changed on the ground? Armed police blocked the base on Sunday morning and large machinery stopped access. Locals said security had been raised in recent days, with heavy vehicles placed across the gates and civilian staff sent home on Friday. Reuters witnesses said security was also stepped up at other bases used by the US, with armoured vehicles and soldiers at the gates of RAF Lakenheath and RAF Mildenhall in eastern England. A US Air Force spokesperson declined to discuss specific protection measures but said US and UK-based units remain vigilant. How did politicians react? Burnham said on X that the incident would be deeply concerning for local residents and thanked the police and armed forces. Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said the public deserves to be told the truth about the suspects identities. A 400-metre cordon remained around the vans on Sunday evening, and residents of the evacuated homes, many of whom were moved to a leisure centre in Cirencester, were waiting to return. Gloucestershire Police thanked them for their patience. Police have yet to say who the men are or what the vans carried. The five remain in custody.

articleTitle: CBSE private candidate exam form 2027: Registration date for Class 10, 12 likely this month
articleFeaturedImageAlt: CBSE Class 10, 12 Board Exams 2027
description: The eligibility categories for 2027 will be confirmed only in the new notification. Based on CBSE's previous notification, private-candidate applications included students falling into categories such as Essential Repeat, Compartment and Improvement of Performance.
body_raw: CBSE Private Candidate Form 2027 for Class 10 and 12 The Central Board of Secondary Education CBSE has not yet announced the date for submission of examination forms by private candidates who wish to appear for the Class 10 and Class 12 board examinations in 2027. Last year, the forms were released in September. The CBSEs examination circular page, updated on September 18, 2026, currently lists the September 10 notification regarding the prior intimation for submission of the List of Candidates LOC for the Class 10 and 12 examinations for the 2026-27 session. However, a notification for submission of examination forms by private candidates for the 2027 examinations has not been released yet. For the 2026 Board examinations, CBSE opened the private-candidate application process in September 2025. The Board issued the notifications for Class 10 and Class 12 private candidates on September 8, 2025, and the application process began on September 9. For Class 10, the notification covered candidates who had been declared Essential Repeat, candidates placed in the compartment category, candidates who had been declared failessential repeat in specified previous years, and candidates seeking improvement in one or more subjects. CBSE also issued a separate notification for Class 12 private candidates for the 2025-26 examination cycle. The Board stated that applications and fees would be accepted only online and that applications submitted after the prescribed deadline would not be accepted. The notification for the 2027 examinations will mention the eligibility criteria, application dates, examination fee, late-fee window, subjects available and instructions for selecting the examination city. Students should particularly check their eligibility before applying. In the previous cycle, CBSE required candidates from earlier examination years to enter details such as their roll number and year of passing. The Board also cautioned that incorrect information could result in rejection of the application. The examination centre is allotted according to the city selected by the candidate in the online application. CBSE had advised candidates to choose the city carefully as it would not be changed after allotment.

articleTitle: Iconic CID trio reunites for new crime series Paapanasham, but there’s a major catch
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Dayanand Shetty, Shivaji Satam, Aditya Srivastava
description: CID actors Shivaji Satam, Aditya Srivastava, Dayanand Shetty, Ansha Sayed and others have reunited for a new crime-based show.
body_raw: CID, featuring Dayanand Shetty, Shivaji Satam and Aditya Srivastava in pivotal roles, is one of the nations most-loved crime shows. The team ruled the audiences hearts for more than two decades, and now, several members of the popular cast are reuniting for a new crime-based show, Paapanasham. He shared a video featuring the entire cast, who introduced Paapanasham and revealed a few details about the series. The video opens with Shivaji Satam saying, The day you all have been waiting for, has finally ended We have commenced the shoot of our new show in Mangalore, Udipi.
