Its thus become the sixth highest grossing Bollywood film of 2026 globally, eyeing the next target of Rs 293 crore, set by Priyadarshans horror comedy Bhooth Bangla, starring Akshay Kumar.

articleTitle: The tussle for top posts in India’s CAPFs: IPS officers or force veterans?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Five forces are at the centre of the dispute — Central Reserved Police Force (CRPF), Border Security Force (BSF), Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) and Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB). (File)
description: At the heart of the dispute are promotion bottlenecks, the meaning of Organised Group A Service status, and a new law enacted by Parliament this year.
body_raw: An unusual controversy in the Supreme Court over the listing of contempt petitions has brought back into focus a much older institutional battle. Who should occupy senior command positions in the Central Armed Police Forces CAPFs - officers who have spent their careers in these forces, or IPS officers brought in on deputation? At the heart of the dispute are promotion bottlenecks, the meaning of Organised Group A Service status, and a new law enacted by Parliament this year. What happened in the Supreme Court? A bench of Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and A S Chandurkar was hearing contempt petitions alleging non-compliance with the Supreme Courts May 23, 2025 judgment on career progression of CAPF cadre officers and IPS deputation. The case was scheduled for September 29, when the Ministry of Home Affairs MHA was supposed to explain why, despite the courts direction to progressively reduce IPS deputation, 46 IPS officers had subsequently been brought into the forces. Although the case appeared in the cause list, by the time it came up for hearing, it had been struck off. The bench ordered it to be listed the following day and sought an explanation from the Registry. But on September 30, the contempt cases were placed before a specially constituted bench of Justices Manoj Misra and Bhuyan instead of the regular bench of Justices Bhuyan and Chandurkar. The Registry said the Centre had earlier requested the Chief Justice of India to have the contempt cases heard along with a separate petition challenging the new CAPF law since the governments defence in the two overlapped. Lawyers for CAPF officers objected, arguing that alleged violation of the 2025 judgment was distinct from the subsequent challenge to the Act. But the courtroom dispute is only the latest development in a battle running for over a decade. What is the dispute? Five forces are at the centre of it - Central Reserve Police Force CRPF, Border Security Force BSF, Central Industrial Security Force CISF, Indo-Tibetan Border Police ITBP and Sashastra Seema Bal SSB. Each has its own cadre of Group A executive officers, generally recruited as Assistant Commandants, who can rise through the hierarchy to senior command positions. However, senior positions have traditionally also been filled through deputation, particularly by IPS officers. Before the 2026 law, recruitment rules provided for 20 of DIG and 50 of IG posts to be filled through deputation. CAPF cadre officers contend that this creates a structural bottleneck. As the number of posts narrows higher up the hierarchy, setting aside senior posts for deputation further reduces promotional opportunities for officers who have spent their careers within the forces. This was one reason behind their long battle for Non-Functional Financial Upgradation NFFU, which allows an officer who cannot be promoted for want of vacancies to nevertheless receive the financial benefits of a higher grade. The Delhi High Court ruled in favour of CAPF officers in 2015. The Supreme Court upheld the decision in 2019, following which the Union Cabinet granted Organised Group A Service OGAS status and NFFU benefits to Group A executive cadre officers of the CAPFs. Why did the problem continue? CAPF officers say NFFU has only partially addressed stagnation because it has been implemented through existing Recruitment Rules. These require an officer to spend a prescribed number of years in each rank before becoming eligible for the next grade. Thus, even when NFFU gives an officer the pay of a higher rank without an actual promotion, the clock for his next financial upgradation may not start until he is actually promoted. For instance, an officer who gets 2IC-level pay after five years as Deputy Commandant may remain stuck there financially if he is not actually promoted as 2IC - the prescribed service for the next grade does not begin. CAPF officers say this perpetuates the very stagnation NFFU was intended to overcome, and have sought Service Rules that provide for progression based on overall qualifying service rather than actual vacancy-based promotions. The matter returned to the Supreme Court in 2025. In its May 23 judgment, the court held that CAPFs had to be treated as OGAS not merely for NFFU but for other cadre-related purposes as well. It ordered a cadre review and review of existing service and recruitment rules after hearing representatives of the CAPF cadres. Most significantly, it directed that posts earmarked for deputation up to the Senior Administrative Grade DIG and IG be progressively reduced, within an outer limit of two years. The Centres review petition was dismissed in October 2025. Why does the MHA want IPS deputation to continue? The MHA argued before the Supreme Court that the CAPFs, given their operational role, could not be treated on a par with ordinary civilian Group A services, and that IPS officers provided an institutional link between the Centre and state police establishments when the forces were deployed in states. IPS officers who intervened in the litigation also defended the deputation system. The Supreme Court did not order an end to IPS deputation. It instead sought to balance the governments stated operational requirement against the stagnation faced by cadre officers, directing a progressive reduction of deputation posts up to SAG. CAPF officers argue that personnel who have spent decades commanding units and serving in conflict areas should not find the upper reaches of their own organisations partly closed to them. There is also a paradox the Centre has itself struggled to fill posts reserved for IPS officers because states have been reluctant to release them on central deputation. What is the new CAPF Act? While the court battle continued, the government brought the Central Armed Police Forces General Administration Bill in Parliament. Introduced in Rajya Sabha on March 25, it was passed by both Houses in early April and has since become law. The Act creates an umbrella framework for Group A officers of the five CAPFs and empowers the Central government to frame rules governing recruitment, promotion, deputation and service conditions. Crucially, this rule-making power operates notwithstanding an inconsistent judgment, decree or order of a court, while rules framed under the Act prevail over inconsistent rules or government orders. The legislation also protects a sizeable deputation component at senior levels 50 of IG posts and at least 67 of Additional DG posts are to be filled through deputation, while all Special DG and DG posts are to be filled through deputation. The government argued that the law was necessary to create a uniform framework for the five forces and that IPS deputation remained necessary for operational requirements and Centre-state coordination. Opposition MPs, however, argued that the legislation was effectively seeking to overcome the Supreme Courts 2025 judgment and perpetuate the disadvantage faced by CAPF cadre officers. They sought its referral to a Select Committee and eventually walked out during its passage in both Houses. CAPF officers have separately challenged the new law in the Supreme Court. There are therefore now two overlapping proceedings - the contempt petitions over whether the government complied with the 2025 judgment, and a challenge to the 2026 law that subsequently changed the statutory framework - to be decided by the same bench.

articleTitle: 4 gold, 1 silver medal won by Indians at the International Astronomy and Astrophysics Olympiad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India won four gold, one silver medal at the International astronomy, astrophysics olympiad
description: With four gold medals, India finished third jointly with Vietnam in the medals tally, behind Iran and South Korea, which won five gold medals each.
body_raw: The Indian team won four gold and one silver medal at the 19th International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics IOAA, held in Hanoi, Vietnam, between September 25 and October 5. All five Indian participants won medals, with Pranjal Dixit from Hyderabad, Sumant Gupta from Delhi, Akshat Srivastava from Gurugram and Arnav Sehrawat from Faridabad winning gold medals. Harshil Amitkumar Patel from Vadodara won a silver. With four gold medals, India finished third jointly with Vietnam in the medal tally, behind Iran and South Korea, which won five gold medals each. The competition saw participation from 307 students representing 64 countries, making it the largest IOAA so far in terms of both participating countries and students. Read Indian team bags 2 gold, 4 silver medals at International Mathematics Olympiads in China As per the information shared by the Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education HBCSE, which trains selected students from India for different science Olympiads, since Indian participation started in Astronomy Olympiads in 1999, 49 of students have won gold, 35 silver and 13 bronze medals so far. In the last five years, all students have won either gold 64 or silver 36 medals. With the IOAA, all the senior level Olympiads Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Astronomy of this year are now concluded. Every Indian student has won either a gold 16 students or a silver medal 8 students this year, for the first time since participation in International Olympiads started in 1989. Also Read Indian team wins 5 gold at International Physics Olympiad 2026 As a result, the IOAA performance also marked a significant milestone for Indias participation in international science Olympiads. For the first time since India began participating in the International Olympiads in 1999, every Indian student across the five senior-level Olympiads - Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Astronomy - has won either a gold or silver medal this year. Of the 24 Indian students, 16 won gold and eight won silver. At the IOAA, the competition comprised theory, observation and data analysis, accounting for 50, 25 and 25 per cent respectively. Also Read India bags four gold medals at International Chemistry Olympiad 2026, JEE Advanced topper Kabeer Chhillar among winners The Indian team was accompanied by Prof Bhaswati Mookerjea of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research TIFR, Mumbai, and Prof Sanved Kolekar of the Indian Institute of Astrophysics, Bengaluru. Prof Aniket Sule of HBCSE-TIFR attended as the current president of IOAA.

articleTitle: J&K collected Rs 114 crore from job aspirants in 3 years, Assembly told
articleFeaturedImageAlt: J&K collected Rs 114 crore from job aspirants in 3 years, but vacancies dipped
description: According to the figures shared by the government in the Assembly, the number of posts advertised by the Public Service Commission in the UT has declined from 2,586 in 2023-24 to 1,400 in 2024-25 and just 357 in the last financial year.
body_raw: Jammu and Kashmirs two government recruitment agencies have collected Rs 114 crore as application fee from aspirants of different examinations over the last three years. The information was shared by the government in the JK Assembly during the ongoing autumn session. The figures shared by the government also reveal a sharp decline in the number of posts advertised by the two recruitment agencies since the Omar Abdullah regime took power in October 2024. The number of posts advertised by the Public Service Commission declined from 2,586 in 2023-24 to 1,400 in 2024-25 and just 357 in the last financial year. The posts advertised by the SSB have also shown a sharp decline. In 2023-24, the agency had advertised 4,228 posts, which rose to 5,044 posts in 2024-25. However, the number has come down to just 1,731 in 2025-26. Responding to a question, the government said that over the last three years - 2023-24, 2024-25 and 2025-26 - the Jammu and Kashmir Public Service Commission JKPSC and the Jammu and Kashmir Service Selection Board JKSSB have collected Rs 114 crore from the candidates applying for various jobs. The Public Service Commission recruits candidates for the gazetted posts while the Service Selection Board does it for non-gazetted posts. The government informed the House that the Service Selection Board has collected around Rs 89.50 crore from aspiring candidates as application fee for 11,003 non-gazetted posts advertised by the recruitment agency. It further said that the Public Service Commission has advertised 4,961 posts over the last three years and collected Rs 24.43 crore from the aspiring candidates. Agencies have become money-minting machines Government examination agencies have become money-minting machines, extracting money from unemployed youth instead of helping them, said Peoples Democratic Party PDP legislator Waheed Para, who had asked the question in the House. Papers are sold, exams are withheld and nearly 90 of recruitment has remained stalled for two years. The irony is that the recruitment agency itself doesnt even have a permanent chief, he said. While the two recruitment agencies withdrew many posts, the Public Service Commission is yet to refund its candidates. The SSB, on the other hand, has refunded an amount of Rs 1.36 crore to the applicants. JKPSC, with the assistance of NIC National Informatics Centre, is devising an online mechanism for refund of fees on account of withdrawal of posts or multiple payments, the government has said. The mechanism is likely to be operational shortly, it added. Giving the details, the government has said that the SSB has advertised 4,961 posts - 2,586 in 2023-24, 1,400 in 2024-25, and 357 in 2025-26. While the recruitment agency has received 2,76,065 applications for these posts, only 1,85,808 candidates appeared in the exams. Similarly, the SSB has advertised 11,003 non-gazetted posts over the last three years - 4,228 in 2023-24, 5,044 in 2024-25, and 1,731 in 2025-26. The recruitment agency has received 18,36,056 applications for over 11,000 posts. Only half of the candidates - 9,38,777 - appeared in the recruitment exams.

articleTitle: 350 hours for Rashmika Mandanna, 500 for Shakira: The making of two showstopping looks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rashmika Mandanna
description: Rashmika Mandanna’s Anamika Khanna gown took 350 hours, while Shakira’s Gaurav Gupta look with 'banarasi skirt' took over 500. Here’s why these 850-plus hours of Indian couture are turning heads.
body_raw: One black gown took 350 hours. Another stage look took about 500 hours. Put Rashmika Mandanna and Shakiras latest fashion moments together, and you get more than 850 hours of Indian fashions finest handiwork. If you have been scrolling through Instagrams fashion algorithm over the past 24 hours, you might have noticed fans going gaga over this particular Indian fashion moment. Well, there is a reason for it. Rashmika Mandanna has been teasing fans for around a week, sharing glimpses of her preparations for Vogue World 2026 in Milan as well as her various magazine cover looks. The excitement is understandable this is her first appearance at the global fashion spectacle, which took place at Milans Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II on September 22. For the occasion, Rashmika went all black in a dramatic Anamika Khanna gown that took 350 hours to make. The dress comes from the designers Moonlit Palace couture collection, which was presented in Hyderabad in July. The gown looks fairly simple from a distance but get closer and there is quite a lot going on. There is black lace, a sharply boned corset, embroidered appliqu, sheer sections and an elongated asymmetric silhouette. Then comes the silver detailing around the waist, which breaks up all that black and gives the gown an almost armour-like feel. The metal work was hand-finished, and 350 hours went into the lace embroidery, sculpted corsetry, metal detailing and surface embellishment. The trailing hem also gives the fitted silhouette some movement, especially when the different black textures catch the light. For accessories, the actor went with Swarovski jewellery - for which she is also the brand ambassador- , a Gucci bag and Aquazzura heels. Styled by Priyanka Kapadia, Rashmika wore two statement rings - the Una Angelic cocktail ring with an XXL cushion-cut crystal and the Vienna cocktail ring with mixed-cut crystals - along with Vienna ear cuffs. What is inside Rashmikas Gucci bag? In Vogues Whats In My Bag? feature, Rashmika gave a glimpse to her fans of what she was actually carrying around Milan perfume, her phone, a powder puff - give to her by makeup artist Tanvi Chemburkar - because it was super hot in Milan, and a small Ganpati idol. In Rahsmikas words Perfume goes wherever I go, my lips dry very fast and its super hot in Miland right now As per Ganpati idol, its keeps her company and in good vibes and the phones is well, she needs her team by her side. Besides Rashmika many other known faces also attended the event, including Jennifer Lopez, Cardi B, Vittoria Ceretti, Alicia Keys, and Dakota Johnson. There was also an unexpected star - humanoid robots. View this post on Instagram A post shared by VOGUE India vogueindia Shakiras Banarasi moment While Rashmika brought black lace and corsetry to Milan, Shakira brought Gaurav Gupta couture to Madrid. For her Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour residency, the singer wore a custom Gupta creation featuring a sculpted gold Lunar Wolf breastplate and a handwoven silk brocade skirt from Banaras. The outfit took more than 500 hours to create and involved a team of more than 10 artisans. And this was not made just to sit pretty in photographs. The outfit was designed with Shakiras high-energy stage performances in mind, combining the rigid, sculptural breastplate with a softer, more fluid skirt. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Gaurav Gupta gauravguptaofficial The wolf motif is, of course, the detail you notice first. The sculpted brass piece sits like armour across her torso, while the Banarasi skirt brings in a completely different texture and movement. This is not Shakiras first Gaurav Gupta moment either. In February 2025, when she kicked off her world tour in Rio de Janeiro, she wore another custom Gupta creation, the Lunar Blue Wolf Gown, featuring a sculpted metallic wolf breastplate. That outfit reportedly took more than 600 hours to create. Around the same tour, Shakira also wore a fiery red custom Anamika Khanna ensemble featuring intricate threadwork, beads and Swarovski crystals.

articleTitle: Zero sugar, zero gluten, zero lactose – what fuelled Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s return
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bhuvneshwar Kumar putting in the hard yards with his physio Ramneesh Vohra. (Instagram & Special Arrangement)
description: Veteran seamer last played for India four years ago but always had the drive for excellence, which prompted him to make big sacrifices to regain swing, which had been his hallmark in his heyday
body_raw: I want to be like that again. Will it be possible? A few months had passed in calm silence. Bhuvneshwar Kumar and his physio Ramneesh Vohra had not let their association be disrupted by the snub that struck him 12 days after Indias 2022 T20 World Cup semi-final exit. He was taken off the national radar after a New Zealand tour. His 37 T20I wickets in 2022 remain the most by an Indian man in a calendar year. We met regularly but never had a word about it for almost 2-3 months, Ramneesh, a BCCI-qualified physiotherapist, tells The Indian Express from his clinic in Noida. We never discussed what went wrong. Bhuvneshwars stillness was perplexing, even for Ramneesh. His thoughts finally came out in the open one morning. I want to be like that again, Bhuvneshwar told Ramneesh. He pointed to a mobile screen that replayed the booming in-swingers that rattled Pakistans Nasir Jamshed and Mohammad Hafeez on his T20I and ODI debuts in December 2012 on a loop. That was 10 years earlier. The confidence had undeniably taken a hit. Could he bend the ball to his will again? Will it be possible? he asked Ramneesh. Bhuvneshwar wasnt searching for swing to wear the India blues again. He just wanted to enjoy and give his best no matter where he played. The chat was all about that, Ramneesh recalls. The hard yards put in, alongside Bhuvneshwars personal trainer Surya Yadav, helped the veteran seamer complete a circle on Tuesday. At 36, he found himself back in the T20I squad for Indias New Zealand tour, the country where he played his last international game in November 22. The platform was laid by two victorious IPL seasons with Royal Challengers Bengaluru RCB. Nerve-less control in the Powerplay and at the death yielded him 45 wickets at a sub-9 economy, the best among all pacers in the league over that period. Ramneesh first crossed paths with Bhuvneshwar during the COVID lockdown at a Noida academy in 2020. Suryas technical inputs came in about four years later. He never wanted to increase pace. He only wanted to regain his swing. We first put in work to help regain that swinging capacity. The technical aspects were handled by Surya. I would handle his joints, which had to be opened up first. Only then could he proceed to strengthening, do functional activities and later enter game-pattern activities. His priority was to get his foot landing at the crease like in 2012, when his contact was on his toe and not the entire back foot, says Ramneesh. The transformation was in full flight during RCBs triumphant Playoffs run in May. Two near-140 kph deliveries froze Shubman Gill and Sai Sudharsan, Bhuvneshwar getting them with his rejuvenated bouncer and nip-backer. Earlier, he used to be a bowler, like many others. Now, he can run a marathon if he wants, Ramneesh says proudly. Hard yards The sacrifices were big but not impossible for Bhuvneshwar, who, according to Ramneesh, has had no fun activities or parties outside cricket. Zero sugar, zero gluten and zero lactose for the last six years. He has shed fat from his visceral organs. Thats the main thing. He weighed 80 kg earlier, with 22-25 percent body fat. Now at 75 kg and 16 percent body fat, Bhuvneshwar has improved his muscle mass. Thats the beauty when you develop a bond with an athlete, Ramneesh adds. The two have transcended the player-doctor relationship to brothers and neighbours in the same society of the city. We strictly keep our work off social media and often train at my home or his, he says. Ashish Winston Zaidi raves about Bhuvneshwars comeback. Zaidi, a former Uttar Pradesh seamer, retired in 2006, a year before Bhuvneshwars debut. The two later caught up regularly during the UPT20 league. In 2009, Zaidis straight talk was Bhuvneshwars greatest counsel, a day before he dismissed Sachin Tendulkar for his only duck in the Ranji Trophy and burst to fame before the IPL. Maine bola usse Tendulkar jaan thodi ley lega I told him Tendulkar wasnt going to kill him. He was a nervous teenager then but a very mature cricketer now, recounts Zaidi. He made a mistake somewhere trying to increase pace. Moving back to swing, and line and length have helped his comeback. His bowling amazed me this season. Nowadays, a lot of boys are bowling quick but have no swing. If you look at the batting tracks today, if you dont have swing or movement, you are in trouble, the former cricketer says. Ramneesh recalls only one instance of Bhuvneshwar expressing disappointment over his exit from the national team in late 2022, when Bhuvi sir arrived as the chief guest on his revamped clinics inauguration. Someone asked him why he got the keeper up to the stumps during that Adelaide T20 World Cup semifinal against England. He said that it wasnt his call and the decision didnt go well. He always used to say, I dont want to think about it or its consequences. I am not doing anything to get somewhere. But he got himself somewhere on Tuesday. Back in an India shirt, with the avenues opening up further as they enter a 50-over World Cup year. 37 Bhuvneshwars T20I wickets in 2022 are still the most for an Indian man in a calendar year. 45 Bhuvneshwar is the highest wicket-taker in the IPL since 2025. 105 T20I matches Bhuvneshwar would have missed by the start of the New Zealand tour, the most for an Indian between two appearances. 363 Bhuvneshwar is the highest wicket-taker among Indian pacers in all T20s

articleTitle: A for Alert, B for Bunker: How Maharashtra’s school kids are learning disaster ABCs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The chart was developed by Palghar District Disaster Management Officer Vivekanand Kadam to make disaster preparedness familiar to children through simple words, repetition and visual learning.
description: It began as an alphabet a disaster management officer made for his toddler. Now it's in government classrooms across Maharashtra, teaching children words like evacuation and tsunami warning.
body_raw: For children in several government schools in Maharashtra, the alphabet no longer stops at Apple, Ball and Cat. A colourful classroom chart begins with A for Alert, B for Bunker and C for Cyclone, and introduces terms such as evacuation, mitigation, search and rescue, and tsunami early warning systems. The chart was developed by Palghar District Disaster Management Officer Vivekanand Kadam to make disaster preparedness familiar to children through simple words, repetition and visual learning. The idea took shape in 2024, when Kadam began thinking about the impact of climate change and disasters over the next two to three decades. He first made the alphabet for his toddler, Vedansh, and later expanded it into a school learning tool. It was formally launched on July 26, 2025, Kargil Vijay Diwas. Kadam, who studied disaster management as part of his policy and management education, said he consulted a United Nations climate dictionary while selecting the terms. What the alphabet teaches Each letter pairs a term with a short explanation. Some cover natural hazards F for Flood, L for Landslide, G for Glacier Melting and Z for Seismic Zone, which explains that regions differ in their vulnerability to earthquakes. E for Environmental Degradation links damage to forests, soil and water to higher disaster risk. Others introduce the people and systems that respond to emergencies N for National Disaster Response Force, O for Operation Centre, P for Public Address System, Q for Quick Response Team and V for Very High Frequency, the radio band used by emergency teams. U stands for United Nations Office, and W for World Meteorological Organization. The chart also covers the ideas behind preparedness, such as D for Disaster Management Cycle, H for Hazard, M for Mitigation and R for Risk Reduction. K for Know Your Strengths asks children to understand their abilities and limits so they can act safely and seek help. Some letters are more specific. I is for Isolation Ward, J for Jumping Net, a safety net used in rescues from heights, X for Xylene, which introduces chemical hazards, and Y for Yachting Accident, on water safety while boating. The alphabet is not part of the formal syllabus. It is used as a supplementary resource, with teachers explaining the terms in Marathi. Other districts have taken it up. Parbhani District Disaster Management Officer Pawan Khandke said the charts had been distributed in 50 Zilla Parishad primary schools. Children are given homework and assignments based on the alphabet, and those who do well are recognised, he said.

articleTitle: Was Cathy born evil? Netflix’s East of Eden rewrites Steinbeck’s most notorious villain
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A still from East of Eden. (Source: Netflix)
description: Netflix’s East of Eden, starring Florence Pugh as Cathy Ames, gives John Steinbeck’s infamous ‘psychic monster’ a traumatic past, reigniting a decades-old debate over whether she was born evil or made monstrous.
body_raw: Are monsters created, or is one born evil? In East of Eden, future Nobel laureate John Steinbeck backs innate evil through Cathy Ames, one of the most ruthless femme fatales ever written. Now, a woman screenwriter has challenged his take on that chicken-and-egg ouroboros in Netflixs seven-episode adaptation of the American classic. Steinbecks Cathy is a serpent-tongued Eve who leads men astray, leaving only death and regret in her wake. Zoe Kazan-granddaughter of Elia Kazan, who directed the 1955 adaptation starring James Dean-tells the story from the villains perspective. To the delight and dismay of Steinbecks readers, Kazan gives Cathy, played by Florence Pugh, a villain-origin story. Here is what you should know about how Steinbeck wrote Cathy, what the series changes, the split verdict on the adaptation, and the novel itself. Steinbecks Cathy I believe there are monsters born in the world to human parents. From the outset, Steinbeck describes Cathy as something inherently evil, calling her a psychic monster with a malformed soul. He says Cathy learns early to use sex as power. In Steinbecks telling, she gets two older boys punished for assaulting her.As a teenager, she seduces her Latin teacher, who kills himself. She sets fire to the family home with her parents inside, empties her fathers safe and fakes her own death. She sleeps with her husbands brother on her wedding night, tries to end her pregnancy, takes over a brothel by poisoning its owner, and turns it into a house of sadomasochism and blackmail. With such a litany of crimes, she is portrayed as a soulless monster, a seductress, with Steinbeck reaching for Satanic descriptors to describe her her feet are small and stubby, with fat insteps almost like little hoofs, and on one occasion, her tongue flickers like a serpent. What the series changes In the Netflix adaptation, Cathy commits nearly all the same crimes, but Kazan tries to rationalise it as a traumatic response of a child violated. The aforementioned carriage-house frame-up is replaced with a scene in which an older boy lures Cathy with candy when she is but a child. In her teens, her lovesick teacher becomes a predator, and her timid father is portrayed as a tyrant who whips her and treats her as his property. In Kazans telling, Cathy is a woman exposed to the worlds cruelty at a young age, and rather than be exploited, she decides to manipulate the world and be cruel in turn. Her ambition to be free from the restrictions of society and family spurs her to escape all kinds of bonds, often through murder. She takes over a brothel through underhanded means, and uses it to gather blackmail. This is a perverted rebellion against the ambition of her contemporaries, motherhood and marriage, which in the mid-20th century would make her villainous even without the murders. Pugh told Radio Times that despite the empathetic treatment granted to a woman who in the original text is an irredeemable psychopath, Cathy is not given absolution she does not get away scot-free. For better or worse Many commentators have argued that the changes defang Cathy and reduce her to a traumatised victim, when she actually is an unrepentant perpetrator. It also robs the story of its originality by allowing a female villain with criminal tendencies who isnt driven by a moment of desperation or a last resort. As the influential critic Louis Owens, who wrote in John Steinbecks Re-Vision of America, says, Cathy is evil thats simply the way it is. Many of Steinbecks detractors believe the changes to be an improvement, as they prevent Cathy from staying a one-dimensional character, the archetypal personification of the original sin that cost Adam Paradise, or even Lilith, who refuses to bend. The change allows the character to be more than an unflattering caricature of his ex-wife Gwen, with whom he had an acrimonious split, with allegations of infidelity thrown on either side. Besides the novels central idea, timshel, the Hebrew word Steinbeck translates as thou mayest, gives the male characters the luxury of choosing their own path, but denies the same to Cathy, who is sentenced to be a monster from birth to death. Sarah Appleton Aguiar also argues in a 2005 essay that Cathys malevolent nature tends to present itself only when she is feeling cornered or trapped. Does Steinbeck hint at abuse Bibliophiles who have already watched the adaptation point out that Steinbeck himself writes that Cathy learned very young that sexuality is the most disturbing impulse humans have. In chapter 17, the narrator doubts himself, admitting that without knowing what Cathy wanted, it is easy to call her bad and hard to say why. In the letters to his editor later published as Journal of a Novel, Steinbeck went further To that extent I am a monster like Cathy. And when a correspondent told him that Cathy only became believable at the end of the book, he replied that this was when, through fear, she became like us. What is East of Eden? Published in 1952, East of Eden is a 600-page American saga, which Steinbeck wrote for his two sons. Reception was mixed, with some calling Steinbeck moralistic, melodramatic, and misogynistic, but it quickly became a bestseller within two months. The book has never gone out of print, and it saw another burst of popularity in 2003, when Oprah Winfrey chose it to relaunch her book club. The Trask story retells the biblical tale of the rival brothers Cain and Abel twice first through Adam and his violent half-brother, Charles, then through Cathys twins, gentle Aron and moody Cal. Villain or antihero, Cathy remains its most argued-over character. Whatever ones view of good versus evil, or nature versus nurture, a book that still sparks this much debate almost a lifetime after publication has earned its place among American classics.

articleTitle: Average 73% decline in wildlife population sizes between 1970 and 2022: WWF report
articleFeaturedImageAlt: wildlife population, wildlife population sizes, wildlife population sizes decline, wildlife sizes decline, wildlife, Wildlife Protection, wildlife conservation, World Wide Fund for Nature, Indian express news, current affairs
description: There has beena 73% decline in the average population sizes of monitored vertebrates — mammals, fish, birds and amphibians — over 52 years between 1970 and 2022, according to the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) biennial Living Planet Report, 2026.
body_raw: The average size of monitored vertebrate - mammals, fish, birds and amphibians - populations declined 73 over 52 years between 1970 and 2022, according to the World Wide Fund for Nature WWF biennial Living Planet Report, 2026. As part of the Living Planet Index LPI, average changes in the size of wild populations of vertebrate species are measured over time, tracking variations in relative abundance rather than absolute numbers. This means that the size of these populations fell by, on average, 73 during the assessment period, and it does not reflect the number of individual animals lost, nor the number of populations lost. Habitat loss and degradation, overexploitation of resources, climate change, impact of invasive species, pollution and disease are some of the dominant drivers of changes across ecosystems and wildlife populations, the Living Planet Report stated. The way the world produces and consumes food is the single largest driver of biodiversity loss. The food and agriculture system is the leading cause of habitat destruction, overharvesting, and a major source of greenhouse gas emissions. Even as the report noted the declining trends in wild populations, it also noted that nature can recover if society follows a clear pathway to trigger positive tipping points in the energy, food and finance systems that drive biodiversity loss. The Living Planet Report 2026 is both a stark reminder of the scale of the biodiversity crisis and a message of hope. While the Living Planet Index continues to highlight significant declines in monitored wildlife populations, the report also shows that these declines are not inevitable, said Ravi Singh, Secretary General and CEO, WWF-India. Species recoveries, including those of tigers in India and globally, demonstrate what sustained conservation action, collaboration and long-term commitment can achieve, he added. The LPI, produced by the Zoological Society of London, includes 35,803 population trends of 5,790 vertebrate species from 1970 to 2022. The strongest declines, 85, were seen in freshwater ecosystems, followed by terrestrial ecosystems, at 69 and marine ecosystems at 59. Although the overall trend is negative due to the magnitude of the declining trends, half of the populations included in the LPI are stable or increasing, WWF said. The report highlights recoveries in populations of green turtles, bluefin tuna, tigers and southern African elephants, which, it said, demonstrate that targeted conservation interventions can deliver proven results. The report noted rise in global wild tiger numbers between 2010 and 2025 - from 3,200 to around 5,700 individuals.

articleTitle: Ronit Roy, 60, stuns fans with six-pack abs and a high-intensity chest workout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ronit Roy’s high-intensity workouts prove that age-related muscle loss can be challenged through discipline and resistance training.
description: Ronit Roy showcases intense workouts at 60, proving that age is no barrier to fitness.
body_raw: Actor Ronit Roy has long been a familiar face in Indian cinema and television, but his current fitness levels are prompting a fresh wave of attention. At 60, an age when many people begin to scale back physically, he is doing the opposite lean, strong, and visibly muscular, with a physique that challenges long-held assumptions about ageing. His journey reflects not just discipline but a deliberate approach to strength training and overall health. In an Instagram video posted in September last year, Roy shared a behind-the-scenes look at a high-intensity chest workout. The clip captures him performing dumbbell bench presses with 40-pound 18 kg weights, maintaining controlled form under the supervision of a spotter. He is also seen pushing his limits, lifting heavy weights while attempting to perform squats at the squat rack in the gym. These arent casual or occasional exercises - they are structured, high-resistance training aimed at building and preserving muscle mass over time. Even more striking is his physical condition. The video highlights a level of leanness and core definition, including a clearly visible six-pack, that is rarely associated with men in their sixties. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. So, for someone in their 50s or 60s, how can heavy resistance training like the kind shown in Ronit Roys workout be incorporated safely? Sadhna Singh, senior fitness and lifestyle consultant at HereNow Official, tells indianexpress.com, A structured and progressive approach is critical. Individuals in this age group should prioritise mobility, joint stability, and proper movement mechanics before introducing heavy loads. Starting with moderate resistance and gradually increasing intensity allows the musculoskeletal system to adapt without undue strain. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Ronit Bose Roy ronitboseroy According to the expert, supervision, at least initially, can help ensure correct form and reduce injury risk. Equally important is listening to the body and allowing adequate rest between sessions, as recovery capacity naturally declines with age. Role of recovery time, protein intake, and metabolic conditioning in maintaining muscle mass Singh states that recovery becomes a central pillar of fitness as one ages, since muscle repair and hormonal responses are slower compared to younger years. Adequate protein intake supports muscle protein synthesis and helps counter age-related muscle loss. Metabolic conditioning, including a mix of strength training and cardiovascular work, improves insulin sensitivity and fat metabolism. Together, these elements create a sustainable framework for preserving lean muscle while maintaining overall metabolic health, notes Singh. Realistic fitness benchmarks older adults should aim for The focus should shift from aesthetics to functional strength and resilience. Benchmarks such as maintaining muscle mass, improving grip strength, sustaining balance, and preserving bone density are far more meaningful indicators of health. Consistent strength training, weight-bearing exercises, and activities that challenge coordination have been shown to support not only physical independence but also cognitive function. The goal is to remain strong, mobile, and metabolically healthy rather than chasing visual outcomes alone, concludes Singh. articleTitle: Can Singapore turn doomscrollers become doomreaders?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Singapore, Singapore doomreaders, Singapore doomscrollers, doomscrollers, Singapore, Singapore government, editorial, Indian express, opinion news, current affairs
description: A new initiative by Singapore’s government to encourage people to read books rather than doomscroll raises the question. It’s a “gamification” strategy, allowing people to earn money by recording daily reading sessions of 15 minutes or more on a government website
body_raw: Theres a sense in which the cultivation of a habit can be a journey from reason to unreason, dilettante to fanatic. Take reading, for instance. Making a conscious decision to read a book for so many minutes each day, at a fixed time, and having the discipline to maintain it, is one thing Structured, rational, methodical. Its everywhere today, displayed in reading lists, challenges, aesthetic photographs and dating-app bios. In the habits fullest manifestation, however, theres always a tinge of madness, a willingness to sacrifice sight, sleep and society for the printed drug. For many, the unwelcome cure is the drudgery of adult life. How easy is it to make the leap from one to the other? A new initiative by Singapores government to encourage people to read books rather than doomscroll raises the question. Its a gamification strategy, allowing people to earn money by recording daily reading sessions of 15 minutes or more on a government website. The amounts on offer are small. But behavioural scientists and psychologists argue that a reward mechanism may nudge people with some interest in reading over the line. For them, the question is whether the habit will stick once the reward is taken away. Theres reason to be optimistic. History shows that it is possible for movements and campaigns to create a reading public. The work of the Chartist press in 19th-century Britain to inculcate the habit among the working class is one example. If Singapores policy enjoys similar success in the face of the rising tide of brainrot, it may encourage efforts elsewhere. The real test will be - can doomscrollers become doomreaders?

articleTitle: Inside Ananya Panday’s Greece vacation: ‘Most beautiful five days’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ananya Panday takes a trip to Greece
description: Explore the world famous pink sands of Elafonissi Beach, photograph the striking turquoise waters at Balos Lagoon, or enjoy wild watersports at beautiful Paleokastritsa Beach.
body_raw: Ananya Pandays latest European rendezvous has set the bar pretty high for a summer getaway.While theChaand Mera Dil actor shared snapshots from her trip to Greece on Instagram, exploring tranquil waters on speedboat rides and stealing quieter moments on the beachfront, we turned to TripAdvisors top recommendations and found some must-visit attractions to add to our Greece travel bucket list.Come take a look Acropolis This ancient citadel, built in the fifth century B.C., towers over the city and is home to some of the most impressive ancient ruins, buildings, and artefacts. One of them is the Parthenon, which features the majestic ruins of an ancient Greek building known for its dignified white marble columns and perfect sense of proportion. The countrys most famous temple, it was dedicated to the goddess Athena and is considered the peak of Greek art. Elafonissi Beach Located on Cretes southwest coast, this remote beach is best known for its pink sand. The crystal-clear waters make this a popular summer vacation spot, attracting sunbathers and watersport enthusiasts alike. Plaka One of the oldest neighbourhoods in Athens, youll see Roman columns, medieval churches, and ancient landmarks like the Choragic Monument of Lysicrates-along with shops selling jewellery, clothes, ceramics, and souvenirs. Sidewalk restaurants and family-run taverns serving authentic Greek food are an added bonus. Balos Lagoon This lagoon is one of the most photographed spots on the island of Crete, with stunning turquoise waters and a panoramic landscape. Visit early in the morning to experience the lagoon at its calmest and most tranquil state. TripAdvisor suggests taking the ferry from Kissamos Port for a relaxing, convenient way to reach Belos. Paleokastritsa Beach Surrounded by lush greenery and rocky cliffs, Paleokastritsa Beach is known for its crystal-clear waters, white sandy beaches, and stunning natural beauty. The beach is also great for a variety of water sports, making it popular amongst adrenaline seekers and thrill chasers. Tours of the bay take you to the enchanting Nausicaas Cave, the famous Blue Caves, and secluded beaches accessible only by boat. The Monastery of Theotokou, overlooking the bay, is just a short distance from the beach and is considered one of the islands most important monasteries. Meteora Meteora makes for ajaw-dropping landscape in centralGreece,where six historic Eastern Orthodox monasteries sit atop massive, 400-meter-tall sandstone pillars. Meaning suspended in the air, this UNESCO World Heritage site sits near the towns of Kalabaka and Kastraki and is about 3.5 hours by train or car from Athens.

articleTitle: Man weighing 144 kg loses over 60 kilos: What transformation may mean for his health
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Niraj Jha
description: The journey brought changes that went well beyond his physical transformation
body_raw: How does it feel to be over 60 kgs lighter? Sometimes the end is just life making room for a different beginning. At 144 kg, I knew something had to change. What followed was a journey that transformed far more than my body. I lost 60 kilos, but somewhere along the way, I also discovered a version of myself I did not know existed, expressed Niraj Jha in a post on Instagram. Looking back, what once felt like the end was actually where everything began. 144 kg to 79 kg. 60 kilos lighter. And still evolving, the man added. A mans transformation from 144 kg to 79 kg has drawn attention online, with his journey documenting a weight reduction of more than 60 kg and, in his words, a change that went far beyond his physical appearance. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. From a health perspective, consultant dietitian Garima Goyal said that a reduction of this magnitude represents a major change in body weight. At a higher starting weight, losing excess body fat can potentially improve several obesity-related health risks, including metabolic health, blood pressure, physical mobility and cardiovascular risk. However, the health impact of any transformation depends on factors such as the individuals medical history, body composition and how the weight was lost, Goyal told indianexpress.com. One of the most important considerations in a major weight-loss journey is preserving lean muscle while reducing fat mass. A very large reduction on the weighing scale should not be viewed simply as a race to reach a smaller number. Adequate protein, resistance training and sufficient nutrition can help support muscle preservation, while physical activity can improve strength and functional capacity, said Goyal. Long-term weight management also has an important psychological dimension. When someone has lived at a higher body weight for years, the changes may extend into everyday experiences walking becomes easier, movement becomes more comfortable, clothes fit differently and activities that once felt exhausting may become more manageable, said Goyal. At the same time, a transformation reel cannot show the complete journey. It doesnt reveal the persons exact diet, medical history, training programme, setbacks, or whether the weight loss was entirely intentional. That context matters, particularly when a large amount of weight has been lost, mentioned Goyal. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Niraj Jha fitwithnbj And reaching 79 kg does not necessarily mark the end of the process. Maintaining weight loss requires a sustainable approach to nutrition, physical activity, sleep, behaviour and ongoing health monitoring. The goal ultimately needs to be more than simply maintaining a number on the scale, said Goyal. Weight loss can be one chapter of a much larger change in health, confidence and daily life, added Goyal. articleTitle: Taapsee Pannu on secret wedding: ‘My husband, his family didn’t sign up for this scrutiny’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mathias Boe and Taapsee Pannu got married in a secret wedding ceremony.
description: Taapsee Pannu has not released her official wedding photos or videos, as she does not want to subject her husband, Mathias Boe, to public scrutiny.
body_raw: Its been almost three years since Taapsee Pannu tied the knot with Danish badminton player Mathias Boe. However, not only did she keep it a hush-hush affair, shes also not released the official wedding pictures or the wedding video yet. The actor recently explained the rationale behind sticking to that stand all this while. Sharing why she didnt announce her wedding, Taapsee Pannu said, Why should I have a public announcement? Ive always kept my personal and professional lives apart. Not that I want to hide them, am scared or embarrassed of them. But Ive refrained from making announcements. I think its personal, and Id want to keep it like that. It feels very weird to put out a press note or a deck of photos and videos. Taapsee added that whoever knew both of them personally, and has been a part of their journey, was there at the wedding. They all have the pictures and videos. All of them were given the edited videos of all the ceremonies 24 hours after the event. They were requested not to post them, and they were all sensible enough to respect that, said Taapsee. She also claimed that shes more than happy to show the pictures and videos to those whom she knows personally, but werent present for the wedding. Taapsee Pannu on leaked wedding video There was only one video that leaked from the wedding festivities of Taapsee Pannu in Udaipur. That was very embarrassing. But that happens with people whore not invited by you, but by your family. Your family wants them to be there, but you maybe dont know them enough. Some of them didnt understand the basic brief given to them, she lamented. However, Taapsee said she didnt mince words to either her family or the guest who leaked the video. I wanted to be respectful enough to not take away their phones. Thats very childish. I would want to believe that those people will value it when Im cordially telling them that even if you click pictures, please dont post them. Almost everybody was clicking videos, added Taapsee, clarifying that the guest who leaked the video wasnt from the film industry. Knowing the kind of a private person I am, they dare not post pictures, said the actor, laughing. Taapsee on her husbands private life Taapsee Pannu said her decision to keep her wedding photos and videos private was also driven by her desire to shield Mathias from the kind of public scrutiny she routinely faces. When you see a picture or a video, its not just about me. Its about a lot of other people, including my husband, whos not the kind of public figure I am. Hes a sports star, but people are not that crazy about the personal life of the person, especially in this part of the world and the kind of a sport hes in. So, hes open to the kind of scrutiny Im used to, explained Taapsee. She also argued that the scrutiny would not be limited to her husband, but also their guests. If I put out a picture, our guests will also be scrutinized. Whether its good or bad comes later. They didnt sign up for it. I signed up for it, so I cant make them go through that kind of scrutiny, the actor added. Taapsee on her love story with Mathias Taapsee Pannu quipped that she never cried during her vidaai, as her husband Mathias Boe spends more time with her in India than he does in his native Denmark. Whose vidaai really happened? Considering Mathais spends more time in India with me, his family should realise it was his vidaai. I had to do it just for the sake of the ceremony. My friends just cried out of happiness that I finally got married. Id lost hope otherwise. I was laughing, even during the pheras, recalled the actor. Ive held him close to me all these years because I dont think I can do better. I think this is the best decision Ive made in my life. Weve been together for 13 years because of an extreme sense of security. Most importantly, theres immense respect. Love comes after that. A relationship wont last if theres no respect. Respect the person if you want to keep the relationship going, and love will follow, added Taapsee.

description: After torrential rains wrecked havoc in parts of Uttar Pradesh killing at least 46 people, the India Meteorological Department has forecast light rain over the area on Monday.
body_raw: The India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorm and lightning over Uttarakhand and light showers over parts of Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, northeastern states, Gujarat, Goa, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Kerala. Light rain over Uttar Pradesh After torrential rains wrecked havoc in parts of Uttar Pradesh killing at least 46 people, the India Meteorological Department has forecast light rain over the area on Monday. The weather department has predicted strong surface winds and generally cloudy sky with one or two spells of rain or thundershowers. The depression over southeast Uttar Pradesh had weakened into a well-marked low pressure area over its northern parts. While 1,021 houses were damaged in three days, Sitapur recorded the highest number of rain and storm-related deaths at seven, followed by Lakhimpur Kheri, Bahraich and Balrampur with five each. Ayodhya and Gorakhpur reported four deaths each, according to the Relief Commissioners office. Between September 25 and the morning of September 27, the state received 66.5 mm of rainfall against the normal 7.6 mm for the period, the Relief Commissioner said. As many as 56 of the states 75 districts recorded excessive rainfall, with Farrukhabad recording 7,385 per cent above normal, followed by Kannauj 5,664 per cent, Shahjahanpur 4,408 per cent, Hamirpur 4,240 per cent and Mahoba 4,100 per cent. Heavy rain was also reported in Kanpur, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Gorakhpur, Bareilly and several other parts of the state, accompanied by strong winds reaching 30-40 kmph. Properties were damaged most extensively in Hardie, where 272 houses were affected, followed by Sitapur 108, Chandauli 75, Auraiya 60, Gonda 54, Hamirpur 51, Shahjahanpur 47 and Bahraich 44. While rescue operation is ongoing in full swing in the affected areas, the Sonik toll plaza on the Ganga Expressway in Unnao was inundated on Sunday. The Ganga Expressway project manager, R S Mishra was quoted as saying by PTI the expressway remained fully operational and traffic movement was normal despite the unusually heavy rainfall. He said there was no waterlogging anywhere on the expressway except at one ramp in Unnao, where drainage had been affected partly due to the relatively low height of a high-tension power line near the ramp. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav shared a video of the waterlogging incident on X and slammed the Uttar Pradesh government suggesting that it be renamed the Ganga Express Waterway. BSP supremo and former Uttar Pradesh chief minister Mayawati on Sunday urged all state governments to provide full assistance at every level to people affected by heavy rains and other natural calamities. In a post on X, Mayawati said, In such difficult natural circumstances, all concerned state governments should provide complete help to the affected people at every level. The state government should not limit itself to formalities but should make efforts to provide proper help to the affected people on the ground and provide immediate relief. Flooding in Bastar Chhattisgarhs Bastar witnessed severe flooding triggered by the cyclonic storm Arnab prompting the rescue of over thousands people and airlifting of 16 citizens on the north bank of the Indravati river near Dongaghat village, the rainfall intensity is likely to reduce significantly on Monday. Light to moderate rainfall is likely in parts of Chhattisgarh and maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to remain around 33C and 25C respectively. In respite, the water level continued to recede and authorities are constantly monitoring the situation, while health personnel remain deployed at the relief camps. On Sunday, the Indravati river had reportedly crossed its danger mark of 8.3 metres by a wide margin, reaching a peak level of 12.39 metres leading to severe waterlogging in low-lying areas. The water level has gradually started receding since, providing some relief to the administration and residents. Several villages in Bastar region across the seven districts have got cut off due to the rains, said a government official from Jagdalpur. As many as 1,215 people have so far been rescued from flooded and inaccessible areas by the district administration, State Disaster Response Force SDRF and disaster management teams. Snowfall and rain likely in Himachal Pradesh In Himachal Pradeshs Kinnaur district, the IMD has forecast snowfall in higher reaches of Himachal Pradesh for Monday and rains in middle and lower hills as well as the plains of the state. Precipitation will continue across the state till September 29 after which weather will remain clear till October 3. National Highway 05 was blocked for vehicular movement after shooting stones and mudflow following heavy rain. According to the district police, continuous rainfall triggered shooting stones and mudflow along the Chaura-Samdo stretch of the highway, leading to the closure of the road. The highway had earlier also been blocked near Tapri due to mudflow, leaving several vehicles stranded and causing inconvenience to commuters. Teams from the district administration, police and the Public Works Department PWD have been deployed at the affected sites to restore traffic movement. Machinery has been deployed at the site to clear the accumulated muck and remove vehicles stuck on the road near Tapri, said officials. With inputs from PTI, Express News Service

articleTitle: Rajasthan HC cites Gandhi, denies bail to 5 in Kanhaiya Lal case: ‘Terrorism a weapon of the weak’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajasthan High Court, Kanhaiya Lal case, Rajasthan High Court denies bail in Kanhaiya Lal case, Terrorism, Kanhaiya Lal Teli murder case, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Denying them bail Saturday, the court says that the paradigm of bail shifts entirely when the crime in question ‘is not aimed at an individual, but at the very soul of the nation’.
body_raw: The Rajasthan High Court on Saturday denied bail to five accused in Udaipurs Kanhaiya Lal Teli murder case, invoking Mahatma Gandhis words that terrorism and deception are weapons not of the strong, but of the weak. A Bench of Chief Justice Sanjay Agrawal and Justice Sameer Jain denied bail applications of Wasim Ali, 34, Muslim Khan, 43, Mohsin Khan, 27, Mohammad Mohsin, 34, and Asif Hussain, 25, saying that we find that the gravity of the offence, the specific roles attributed to the appellants in the larger criminal conspiracy, and the heinous nature of the terrorist act disentitle the accused-appellants to the benefits of bail. On June 28, 2022, two people - Mohammed Riyaz Attari and Ghouse Mohammad - had allegedly posed as customers and hacked to death Kanhaiya Lal Teli at his shop in Udaipur over a post shared by him on social media in support of Nupur Sharma, a BJP spokesperson who was suspended for her objectionable remarks about the Prophet during a live television debate. The Bench also quoted a poem by Ramdhari Singh Dinkar on tolerance and, in prefatory remarks, said The seat of a judge is surrounded by an invisible, yet crushing weight, the weight to protect the rights of the citizens and people of this country which are enshrined under the Constitution of India. The paradigm of bail shifts entirely when the crime in question is not aimed at an individual, but at the very soul of the nation, the Bench said, adding Terrorism is not merely an assault on a physical body it is a calculated, theatrical assault on the psychological sovereignty of the country. Its ultimate objective is not just to commit an offence, but the assassination of peace. It seeks to replace the Rule of Law with the Rule of Fear. The NIA had filed a charge sheet, and the trial court framed charges against the five accused in 2024. They have been in judicial custody since their arrest in the days and weeks following the murder. They had filed bail applications before a Special Court, which had rejected their pleas in October and November 2024. Representing the accused, Syed Saadat Ali and others primarily contended that there is no cogent evidence on record to demonstrate that the accused were present in or around the vicinity of the deceaseds shop during the relevant period leading up to the incident, specifically between June 10 and June 28, 2022. Next, they said that there is no evidence on record to suggest that the accused had sent any message, voice note, or text on any WhatsApp group that could be construed as hurting the religious faith of any community or promoting enmity. They also relied on bail granted to two other accused, Farhad Mohammed and Mohammed Javed, by the trial court and by the High Court on the exact same set of charges as framed against the present accused-appellants. They also said that the accused have been in custody for over four and a half years and that the trial will take its own considerable time. although the charge-sheet was filed on 22.08.2022 and charges were framed in early 2024, the trial is far from conclusion. Senior counsel Raja Thakare, appearing on behalf of the National Investigation Agency, said that the five accused played an active, indispensable, and integral role in the commission of the alleged crime. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, Thakare and others said that the court is not required to conduct a mini-trial or weigh the evidence meticulously at the bail stage. The Court must look at the material provided by the investigative agency at its face value, and if it discloses reasonable grounds for believing the accusation to be prima facie true, bail must be rejected. The high court said that the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act places a statutory embargo on the grant of bail if the court, on a perusal of the charge-sheet, is of the opinion that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accusation against such person is prima facie true. It said that the NIA has completed a detailed and comprehensive investigation, filed the charge-sheet, and the trial court has already framed charges against the accused This establishes that upon a prima facie evaluation, there exists sufficient material to proceed against the appellants, and therefore, the foundational test laid down by the Honble Supreme Court. is squarely met at this stage. The high court, however, clarified that its observations are solely for the purpose of deciding the present bail and that the trial court shall proceed with the trial uninfluenced by the observations made hereinabove.

articleTitle: UPSC Essentials daily subject quiz : International Relations MCQs (Week 181) — Check out answers with explanations
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Essentials daily subject quiz : International Relations
description: Solve and practice questions from International Relations for UPSC Prelims 2027. Attempt questions on the Permanent Mission of India to the UN, Monroe Doctrine, and more.
body_raw: UPSC Essentialsbrings to you its initiative of subject-wise quizzes. These quizzes are designed to help you revise some of the most important topics from the static part of the syllabus. Attempt todays subject quiz onInternational Relationsto check your progress. As we mark the 3rd anniversary of the UPSC Essentials magazine, we thank our readers for being part of this journey. QUESTION 1 With reference to the Permanent Mission of India to the UN, consider the following statements 1. The Permanent Mission of India to the United Nations is based in New York. 2. The Permanent Mission of India to the UN is headed by the Minister of External Affairs. Which of the statements given above isare correct? a 1 only b 2 only c Both 1 and 2 d Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance The question is relevant to understanding Indias representation and participation in the United Nations system. It covers the role of permanent missions, diplomatic representation and multilateral institutions. Explanation - The Permanent Mission of India in Geneva has three separate wings namely, the Permanent Mission of India to the United Nations and Other International Organizations in Geneva, the Permanent Mission of India to the Conference on Disarmament in Geneva and the Permanent Mission of India to the World Trade OrganizationWTO in Geneva. Hence, statement 1 is not correct. - The Consulate General of India in Geneva is housed in the Permanent Mission of India to the UN in Geneva. It is headed by Indias Permanent Representative to the United Nations, not the Minister of External Affairs. Hence, statement 2 is not correct. Therefore, option d is the correct answer. Source pmindiaun.gov.in QUESTION 2 Consider the following statements 1. Adding new permanent seats would require changing the UN Charter itself. 2. It requires a two-thirds vote in the General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of all member states, including agreement from every existing permanent member. Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements? a Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct and Statement 2 is the correct explanation for Statement 1. b Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct and Statement 2 is not the correct explanation for Statement 1. c Statement 1 is correct but Statement 2 is incorrect. d Statement 1 is incorrect but Statement 2 is correct. Relevance The question is relevant to understanding the structure, composition and reform of the United Nations Security Council. It helps in understanding the ongoing debate over UNSC reform and expansion of permanent and non-permanent representation. Explanation - The Security Council currently has 15 seats. Five belong to permanent members holding veto power China, France, Russia, the UK and the US while the other ten are filled by countries elected for two-year terms. - Adding new permanent seats would require changing the UN Charter itself, which needs a two-thirds vote in the General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of all member states, including agreement from every existing permanent member. Hence, statements 1 and 2 are correct. - Even with Russias backing, the push to reform the council has made little real progress. Views among the other permanent members are divided, and China, one of Russias closest partners, continues to firmly resist India joining their ranks. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. QUESTION 3 Consider the following It is the worlds largest island, with a population of less than 57,000 - making it one of the least densely populated areas globally. It is an autonomous, self-governing country. It is located between North America, Europe, and the Arctic Ocean. It is home to the US-Pituffik Space Base, which is crucial for ballistic missile early warning and Arctic defence. The island also has vast reserves of rare earth minerals. The above-mentioned statement refers to a Iceland b Greenland c Faroe Islands d Svalbard Relevance The question is relevant to understanding the geopolitical significance of the Arctic region and its growing strategic importance. It covers strategic locations, natural resources, defence infrastructure and great-power interests in global politics. Explanation - Greenland, the worlds largest island, covers an area of around 2.16 million sq km, with approximately 81 covered by a massive permanent ice sheet. Its population - less than 57,000 - makes it one of the least densely populated areas globally, and nearly half of it lives in the capital city of Nuuk. Roughly, 88 of the population is Inuit or of mixed Inuit Danish heritage. - Greenland is an autonomous, self-governing country, within the Kingdom of Denmark. Copenhagen, however, retains the responsibility of foreign policy, national defence, security, and monetary policy. - Located between North America, Europe, and the Arctic Ocean, Greenland has immense strategic significance as it dominates sea lanes and air routes. In fact, it controls the access between the Arctic and Atlantic Oceans, which covers the Greenland-Iceland-United Kingdom gap a vital choke point. - It is home to the US-Pituffik Space Base formerly the Thule Air Base, which is crucial for ballistic missile early warning and Arctic defence. The island also has vast reserves of rare earth minerals. With the melting ice caps, accessibility to its untapped resources has increased. Therefore, option b is the correct answer. QUESTION 4 The Monroe Doctrine refers to a A US policy declaring that the Western Hemisphere should be closed to further European colonisation and interference b A European agreement to divide the newly independent states of Latin America among Britain, France and Spain c A US policy committing Washington to avoid all political and military involvement in the affairs of Latin American countries d A doctrine establishing the principle that European powers could intervene in the Americas whenever regional governments faced internal political instability Relevance The question is relevant to the study of major doctrines and approaches in the foreign policies of great powers. It helps understand power projection, strategic interests and regional influence in international relations. Explanation - The United States National Security Strategy NSS-2025 explicitly prioritised the Western Hemisphere with a mandate to restore American pre-eminence over the region, which was tantamount to the revival of the Monroe Doctrine of 1823. - The Monroe Doctrine refers to a US policy declaring that the Western Hemisphere should be closed to further European colonisation and interference. - James Monroes annual message to the United States Congress outlined two core principles that together became known as the Monroe Doctrine. The first, the non-colonisation clause, sought to prevent European powers from pursuing future colonial expansion in the Americas. The second was the principle of non-interference, which warned European powers against imposing their political systems on the Americas or threatening the integrity of newly independent states. In return, the president pledged that the United States would refrain from involvement in European affairs. Therefore, option a is the correct answer. QUESTION 5 Hurricane Polo has intensified into a Category 5, becoming one of the most powerful hurricanes to form in the region of a The Caribbean Sea b The Gulf of Mexico c The North Atlantic Ocean d Mexicos southwestern Pacific coast Relevance The question is relevant to understanding the geographical dimensions of regional security and disaster management. It connects natural hazards with regional preparedness, resilience and international cooperation. Explanation - Hurricane Polo has intensified into a Category 5 storm off Mexicos southwestern Pacific coast, becoming one of the most powerful hurricanes to form in the region in recent decades. - The US National Hurricane Center NHC said that Polo was nearly stationary about 325 km south of Zihuatanejo, Mexico, with maximum sustained winds of 270 kmph and a minimum central pressure of 905 millibars. The storm was expected to turn sharply northwest before moving west-northwest over the following days. Therefore, option d is the correct answer.
