articleTitle: Special Intensive Revision (SIR): Why is it important? Why ECI is doing it now and what you need to do
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Special intensive revision in West Bengal
description: SIR Form Online Fill up, Download, Submission Guide: SIR, or Special Intensive Revision, is a large-scale verification exercise that the ECI undertakes when it believes the routine annual “Summary Revision” is not enough to clean the voter rolls.
body_raw: As the Election Commission of India ECI rolls out its Special Intensive Revision SIR across multiple states, the term SIR has been trending across India. and along with it a lot of questions and confusion. The exercise first began in Bihar ahead of the Assembly elections and has now expanded to 13 states and Union Territories in the country. For many, this has raised a simple but urgent question What is SIR and why does every voter suddenly have to fill out a new form? What is SIR? SIR, or Special Intensive Revision, is a large-scale verification exercise that the ECI undertakes when it believes the routine annual Summary Revision is not enough to clean the voter rolls. It involves house-to-house enumeration, pre-filled forms, online submissions, and fresh verification of old voter data. Article 324 of the Indian Constitution grants ECI plenary powers to supervise and update electoral rolls. Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, also allows the Commission to order an intensive revision whenever it finds inaccuracies in the existing rolls. Why is SIR being conducted now? The Election Commission has reasoned that the usual yearly revisions can no longer fix what it calls legacy data issues - errors built up as India has not had a nationwide house-to-house revision since 2002-2004. In those two decades, voter rolls across states have accumulated Dead or shifted voters who were never deleted Duplicate registrations of the same person in multiple locations Statistical distortions where elector numbers rise faster than projected population With major state elections due in 2026, the ECI wants a voter list that is legally defensible, transparent and free of inflated numbers. What information does the SIR form ask for? The SIR form has four key sections 1. Pre-filled details to be verified When the Booth Level Officer BLO visits, they bring a pre-printed form carrying Your name EPIC, or Electors Photo Identity Card, number Address Part and serial number Assembly constituency Existing photograph Voters must check spelling, address accuracy and if the photograph is clear. The ECI is replacing old or unusable images during SIR. 2. Legacy linkage - the new and crucial addition This is the biggest addition in the 2025 SIR. Voters are now required to trace their name or a parentrelatives name to the voter list from the last intensive revision that occurred more than two decades ago. The commission has created an all-India database of these old rolls, available on its website voters.eci.gov.in. To check the legacy linkage, citizens will need to enter Name of self or relative as it appeared in the old roll Relationship father, mother, spouse Old EPIC number if available Assembly constituency, district and state from where they were registered 3. Updated personal information Citizens must provide Date of birth Mobile number Parents or spouses names Their EPIC numbers Aadhaar optional, but often requested for deduplication 4. Mandatory declarations Every voter must confirm that They are an Indian citizen Their name is not registered elsewhere All information provided is accurate What should citizens do right now? 1. Complete the enumeration before December 11. Earlier the deadline for the SIR enumeration was December 4. Later, it was extended to December 11. BLOs will make up to three visits. If they have visited Verify the pre-filled data Provide the legacy linkage details Sign the form Note the date of submission If the BLO assigned to your area hasnt visited Go to voters.eci.gov.in Link your mobile number using Form 8, if required Fill the Enumeration Form online Submit it via Aadhaar-based e-Sign optional Use Know Your Polling Station to call your BLO and request a visit 2. Check if your form has been uploaded Log on to the portal and check your EPIC status. 3. Check the Draft Roll on December 9 On December 9 Visit the CEO website or your polling station Confirm that your name appears in the draft roll If your name is missing from the draft voters roll, file Form 6 between December 9, 2025, and January 8, 2026. 4. Check the final roll on February 7 If your name is deleted, you can appeal within 15 days, first to the District Magistrate and then to the Chief Electoral Officer if needed. Why SIR is important SIR is not a routine paperwork exercise. The ECI is revamping the voter list after two decades of accumulated errors. If you skip the form, fail to verify your data or miss the deadlines, your name may not appear in the draft or final rolls. This means you may be unable to vote in upcoming elections. It becomes essential for voters to verify early, submit the form, and check the draft roll.

articleTitle: Baft-e-Hawa: Janhvi Kapoor turns heads in a 460-count Bengal muslin sari in Paris
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Janhvi Kapoor in a Baft-e-Hawa muslin sari with an ornate embellished blouse in Paris
description: Janhvi Kapoor wore a 460-count Bengal muslin sari by Pankaj S Heritage to the Business of Fashion gala in Paris. Here’s what Baft-e-Hawa means and why the historic textile is so prized.
body_raw: Janhvi Kapoor took Bengal heritage to the Business of Fashion gala in Paris, wearing an ensemble by Pankaj S Heritage. Styled by cousin sister Rhea Kapoor, Janhvi wore a 460-count Bengal muslin in Khud - Rang, or unbleached, known for its exceptionally light, airy quality. Also referred to as Baft-e-Hawa, Shabnami or Chandani, the fabric represents one of the finest traditions of Indian handwoven textiles. The sari was paired with an ornate blouse featuring polkis, garnets and emeralds, along with saraafa tassels, kiran and resham fringing. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Talking about the look, Sneha Yadav, fashion consultant, brand image strategist, NIFT alumna, says that the design involves the tension between the simple muslin fabric and the bold blouse design. The sari possesses a near effortless feel whereas the decorated sleeves bring in formwork, workmanship and theatricality. This opposition prevents the ensemble from appearing too conventional or unduly flashy, she adds. What exactly is Baft-e-Hawa The name Baft-e-Hawa means woven air, a description that captures the fabrics extraordinary lightness. It wasnt a poetic exaggeration. It was a literal description of how the cloth felt in your hand. This was the finest Dhaka muslin we are talking about, spun exclusively from Phuti Karpas, a delicate cotton shrub that grew only along the silty banks of the Meghna River basin, in modern-day Bangladesh, says Nabanita Ghosh, Co-founder Director, Abritee. Making this fabric required extraordinary skill and precision. According to Ghosh, the spinning happened at the most unlikely hours.Young women with exceptional eyesight worked on boats during the humid hours of dawn and dusk, when the dew and humidity kept the micro-thin threads from snapping. The skill lay in their eyes, their fingertips and their timing, she says. The beauty lies not just in the fineness of the weave, but also in the expertise required to create it and the softness and fluidity that it brought to the garment. A khud-rang, or unbleached, cloth like this leaves the weaver nowhere a slight irregularity to hide, says Ghosh. There is no dye or finishing to cover an uneven thread, so every bit of its quality comes from the hands that made it. A count like 460 sounds technical, but what it really represents is patience. What legend says The most famous story about this cloth dates to the reign of Mughal Emperor Aurangzeb. Dhaka was then a Mughal hub, and its finest muslin, malmal khas, was made for the imperial court. The emperor is said to have scolded his daughter, Princess Zeb-un-Nissa, for appearing to wear nothing at all. Her reply was that she was wearing seven layers of it, says Ghosh. The story, however, has been retold and modified over generations. What gets lost in the retelling is that Baft-e-Hawa was never about transparency. It was about control, Ghosh says. Anyone can make a thin fabric. Making one that is fine, even, and still strong enough to be worn is what made it a global benchmark. The older names associated with the fabric describe it best. Shabnami, meaning dew, and Chandani, meaning moonlight, were given by people who handled this cloth and described exactly what they felt. Why the styling works With a fabric as delicate and visually distinctive as Baft-E-Hawa, adding too much ornamentation can easily overwhelm it. In Janhvis look, the relatively simple sari keeps the fabric visible, while the elaborate sleeves add structure and drama. When that delicacy is paired with a silhouette and intricate detailing, the result is a dialogue between softness and structure. That balance is what gives Janhvis look its character and makes the textile feel very relevant in a contemporary fashion context, she says. According to Yadav, this contrast helps bring a historical Indian textile into a contemporary fashion context. The sari stays closely linked with craft work, yet the styling imparts a contemporary, sculptural nature, proving that history may be read in a manner that feels present without needing to mask or recreate its roots, she says. Janhvis Paris appearance brings attention to the extraordinary craftsmanship behind one of Indias most delicate textile traditions - and shows how a historic fabric can be styled without losing its identity. A quirky touch to her Paris trip A few days back, while flying to Paris, Janhvi added a quirky touch to her fashion sense. articleTitle: Woman’s Rs 20 lakh caught between two banks’ ‘ping-pong’, gets refund, payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Himachal Pradesh Consumer Commission, deficiency in service, wrongly transferred money to closed account, bank transfer to closed loan account reversal, Consumer Protection Act 2019 45 days reply rule, refund of wrong bank transfer, National Consumer Helpline 1915, bank ping pong blame game consumer case, principle of non-traverse consumer court, Hemanshu Mishra consumer commission order, private bank transfer error refund rules
description: A woman mistakenly transferred Rs 20 lakh to her husband’s already-closed loan account and was caught between the two banks' blame game for over two months.
body_raw: A Himachal Pradesh Consumer Commission has held two banks guilty of deficiency in service after a womans Rs 20 lakh remained blocked in an administrative loop for over two months after she mistakenly transferred it to her husbands already closed loan account, involving two banks blaming each other over who should reverse the transaction. Calling it a ping-pong blame game, the commission directed the banks to refund the amount and pay Rs 30,000 payout to the woman. President Hemanshu Mishra, members Arti Sood and Narayan Thakur observed that the institutional apathy of both banks subjected the woman and her family to avoidable financial distress, severe mental agony, and forced litigation. The ping-pong blame game trapped the consumer in an administrative loop. Holding funds in a closed loan account despite clear, immediate written notices from both the remitter and the account holder constitutes a gross operational default and a clear deficiency in service, the September 11 order said. The order added that instead of executing a prompt reversal, standard protocol when funds were credited to a defunct or closed account, the bank engaged in bureaucratic delay, issuing automated responses before ultimately advising the wife to approach the remitting bank. 20 lakh transferred to a closed account The wife initiated a transaction of Rs. 20 lakh from her savings account held with a private bank, intending to transfer funds to her husband, and due to a clerical error, the funds were mistakenly directed to her husbands closed personal loan account maintained with another private bank. The loan account was fully settled and closed before the transaction date. Realising the error, the wife immediately notified her husbands bank on April 2, requesting reversal. The bank advised her on April 5 to approach her home branch from which the transaction was initiated. She then routed her complaint through her home branch on April 14. Subsequently, her bank put the blame back on the husbands bank, stating that reversal depends on the beneficiary bank. Caught in a cycle of blame-shifting between both banks, her funds remained blocked, forcing her husband to take an alternative loan by pledging shares on April 24 to manage liquidity. Alleging deficiency in service on the part of both the banks, she filed the present complaint, seeking refund along with compensation and litigation costs. Upon notice, both the banks appeared before the commission, but failed to file their reply within 45 days from the date of service. Hence, their right to reply was struck off and not legally recorded. Complaint allowed The commission observed that the documents adduced by the woman remain entirely unrebutted, unchallenged, and unimpeached, leaving no cogent reason to disbelieve the reliable and convincing evidence presented on record. The commission directed the two banks to pay Rs. 12,500 to the woman along with interest and also directed the husbands bank to pay Rs. 7,500 to her along with interest. It further added that both the banks jointly and severally pay Rs. 10,000 to the woman for litigation expenses. Takeaway The ruling highlights that if the banks fail to file their written versions within 45 days of notice, as mandated under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the principle of non-traverse would apply, and the complainants avermentswould stand legally admitted. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Himachal Pradesh 1800-180-8087 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: ‘Peace and closure’: Mirabai Chanu on a medal that took four Asian Games cycles
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mirabai
description: A coach's remark in a Manipur gym set the target. Chanu and Vijay Sharma needed years, a changed plan for the Commonwealth Games and a Paris miss to reach it
body_raw: When Mirabai Chanu first walked into a gym in Manipur to try weightlifting, a coach looked her up and down and made a casual remark that would stay with her for over a decade You could win a medal at the Asian Games. She surpassed that remark in nearly every way but the one it named. Chanu, who can lift three times her bodyweight, won medals at the World Championships, the Commonwealth Games and, in 2021, a historic silver at the Tokyo Olympics. That consistency, chiselled over years of work and protected through countless injuries, had one gap the Asian Games. Something always kept happening during or around the Asian Games. It reached a point where I would constantly wonder why this was happening, says Chanu. Her longtime coach Vijay Sharma, sitting next to her, chimes in I wont call it a psychological barrier. You can say that it happened by chance. We have discussed this many times. We realised if we attributed it to bad luck, we wouldnt be able to do anything about it. So they did something about it. It started with how they approached the Commonwealth Games. Training loads were kept with Chanus past injuries in mind, and the duo chose not to chase a Commonwealth Games record. A gold with minimal effort was the call. It left her fresh to push at the Asian Games, for the one medal that would complete her. Weightlifting asks for unflinching trust between coach and athlete. Even at these Asian Games, Chanu did not know what weights she was supposed to lift, or where she stood on the medal table. It was Vijays split-second permutations and combinations that ensured a silver arrived while keeping her limits in mind. Vijay was there in Sydney in 2000 when Karnam Malleswari won a bronze medal. Malleswaris gripe since has been that if her Russian coach had trusted her, a better medal could have been Indias. When youre in the arena, you need to make decisions in a fraction of a second. Whatever decisions we take are for the best of the players, says Vijay. He did not allow that breakdown of trust, which he saw with Indias first Olympic weightlifting medal, when he started training Chanu. That trust is essential. In life, whether with a life partner, in business, or in coaching, without trust, there is no bonding, and without bonding, there are no results. The trust that she has in me, even after she has won medals at the World and Olympic level, she still asks me what sets to pick up, says Vijay. I didnt even know that I didnt need a third lift in Japan, admitted Chanu. Sir told me that the silver medal was assured and that we wouldnt need to risk another lift. Once the medal was assured, Chanu could finally feel the weight lift off. It was a collective sense of wrong, felt by both her and Vijay, that was corrected in Nagoya. The fourth-place finish at the Paris Olympics had rankled deeply for both of them, more than two years on, until Nagoya came along. Winning this medal after so many years, across four Asian Games cycles, feels like a dream come true for both me and Vijay sir. It helps cover up the pain of missing out on the medal in Paris. Every time we looked at photos or videos from Paris, it reminded us of what we missed. This medal brings us peace and closure, said Chanu. Their next challenge is the LA Olympics, and a jump to the 53 kg category. Chanu admits that a higher weight class feels more comfortable. Now with the weight increase, itll give some relief from injuries, so we can focus even more on performance and everything else. Whenever I win a medal, I immediately look ahead to the next competition what I need to do, what changes to make. I learn from every medal and championship, and thats where I get my motivation, says Chanu.

articleTitle: Indian official attends SCO event in Pakistan: 5 broad takeaways
articleFeaturedImageAlt: SCO, Pakistan
description: This was the first visit to Pakistan by an Indian official delegation since Operation Sindoor last year. Why did the visit happen, and what is next?
body_raw: India sent a senior official to Pakistan this week for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation SCO national coordinators meeting, the first visit by an Indian official delegation since Operation Sindoor last year. The SCO Council of National Coordinators meets under a rotational annual chair. Pakistan assumed the presidency after the Bishkek summit on August 31-September 1, so the meeting took place in Islamabad. For India, as an SCO member, attending was an obligation. Despite the state of bilateral ties, Delhi sent Alok Dimri, a 1998-batch Indian Foreign Service officer. Dimri is an Additional Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs and a former ambassador to Kyrgyzstan. He has also served as joint secretary in charge of G20 and BRICS, and has been posted in China, Mongolia and New York. It was also the first such visit since External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar travelled to Pakistan for the SCO heads of government meeting in October 2024. Amid the freeze in bilateral ties, the visit has five key takeaways. 1. Diplomatic tightrope for India First, India is in a diplomatic tough spot. The US has been seen to side with Pakistan just as Delhi tries to portray Pakistan as a state sponsor of terrorism. China, Pakistans all-weather friend, helped it during Operation Sindoor with weapons and live satellite intelligence. In this unfavourable environment, Delhi has had to engage with Pakistan and China in multilateral formats. PM Modi met Chinese President Xi Jinping at the SCO summit in Tianjin, and Xi visited India for the BRICS summit in September. Engaging with Pakistan at the SCO is a calculated, pragmatic move, since it is better to have situational awareness of how Islamabad plans to conduct its activities under the SCO umbrella. India will watch the tone and direction of Pakistans SCO-related activities. India hosted a G20 tourism working group meeting in Kashmir in May 2023, and Indian officials will watch whether Pakistan hosts meetings in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. They will also watch for maps showing Indias territories as part of Pakistan or China in SCO documents, banners, posters and other printed or digital material. An Indian official familiar with the strategy explained the rationale If you are not part of the table, you are on the menu. So, it is important for us to be in the room. 2. PM Modis potential visit to Pakistan Second, Pakistan is certain to invite PM Modi to the SCO leaders summit in Pakistan next year. The dates are yet to be announced, and whether the PM attends will be a political call. India boycotted the SAARC summit in Pakistan and Modi has not travelled there since 2015, so this is a bridge to be crossed at an opportune time. The SCO meetings will help assess the possibility of a visit. 3. Trump factor Third, the Russia-Ukraine and US-Iran wars have consumed global attention, with no end in sight. Trumps unpredictable behaviour and support for Pakistan Army chief Asim Munir have emboldened Rawalpindi over the past year and a half. India must be careful about the ramifications of any future conflict with Pakistan as long as Trump is in office, until January 2029. Limited diplomatic engagement, apart from military-level contact, leaves a door ajar for communication. 4. India responding to Pakistans claims Fourth, Delhi will not take provocative statements from Pakistan lying down, as its muscular rhetoric at the SCO foreign ministers meeting in Goa and at the UN General Assembly this year has shown. Any Pakistani statement on Kashmir or terrorism will draw a strong Indian response. 5. The China challenge Fifth, the challenge from China is far more consequential for Delhi than Pakistan. The border standoff since May 2020 is the bigger threat. Keeping both fronts calm is a strategic objective for India, and multilateral contacts often help defuse tension.

articleTitle: New video shows chaos on flydubai flight after Indian pilot foils attack
articleFeaturedImageAlt: New video shows flydubai
description: New video shows passengers and crew crowded at the cockpit door of flydubai Flight 1073, calling for a doctor and a pilot, after an apparent attempt to crash the plane.
body_raw: New footage broadcast on Israeli television on Thursday showed the confusion on flydubai Flight 1073 after passengers and crew stopped an apparent attempt to crash the plane, which was flying from Dubai to Tel Aviv. It showed several people crowding around the cockpit door. The clip was shown by Channel 12 news on Thursday and was filmed from a seat near the cockpit. In it, people shout in English and Hebrew, call for a doctor and tell others to sit down. It then shows Captain Smit Machchhar, who is from India, lying on the floor with blood on him, and the Omani co-pilot with his hands tied behind his back. Machchhar had opened the cockpit door while hurt, which helped passengers get in and take control. The co-pilot was moved from Saudi Arabia to the UAE on Thursday, and the UAE is checking whether the attack had any link to terrorism. What the video shows The clip starts in the cabin. It is not clear when the camera was switched on. One person can be heard saying he the accused Omani pilot tried to crash the plane. Others are heard yelling take him out. Another person is heard yelling sit down. View this post on Instagram A post shared by CNN cnn A cabin crew member calls out for one of the additional pilots onboard. Crew members work quickly to open a first aid kit. The clip comes as the pilot suspected of the attack has been moved to the UAE, where the investigation continues. The plane had gone into a dive after the attack. Yaniv Hayoun, a plumber who helped enter the cockpit, steadied it. A second pair of flydubai pilots, who were on the flight, then took over and landed it, according to The Times of Israel. After a break in the recording, people can be heard asking again and again for a doctor. Dr Shota Musaev, a dentist from Israel, goes to the front of the plane to give treatment, though the video does not show who he is helping. A man asks in Hebrew if there is another pilot on board, and someone says yes. Indian pilot Smit Machchhar has been hailed as a hero for saving passengers after he was stabbed by his colleague in an alleged attempt to crash a flydubai plane on Wednesday. Reutersmade changes using AI The footage then moves to Machchhar on the floor outside the cockpit. He says the co-pilot hit me so many times. He adds that he can move his hurt hand but can no longer close it into a fist. Close by, the attacker is surrounded by crew members, and his uniform is also covered in blood. Scenes after the landing in Saudi Arabia The video picks up again after the emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Medics treat Machchhar on a raised platform outside the aircraft door. People still inside the plane ask where the police are and say the co-pilot must stay on board. The co-pilot is seen on his knees with his hands tied behind his back. One flydubai steward calls him a terrorist in English and says police are needed. Another person says he cannot go anywhere. A passenger says he has been like that for one hour and 40 minutes or more. The clip ends with Machchhar telling the medics about his hand. Asaf Rajuan, one of the Israeli passengers who helped hold the co-pilot, says he took a blow to the head. A voice off camera says someone will laugh about it one day. Investigation moves to the UAE The co-pilot was handed from Saudi custody to the UAE on Thursday. The UAE said it is looking into whether the incident was linked to any terror activity, or to planning or direction by others, The Times of Israel reports. David Mencer, a spokesman for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, told Fox News that Israel can now join the UAEs team and learn what the co-pilots aims were and who was behind him. Hayoun said the co-pilot shouted in English that he wanted to be killed after he was tied up. Hayoun took this to mean the man had failed in his plan and chose to die. This is his own view, not a finding from the investigation. Musaev said the Israelis first used headphone wire to tie the man up so that he could not start to go wild. Netanyahu told Fox News that the co-pilot underwent Islamist radical indoctrination, but gave no more detail. He also said it is too early to say if Iran had a role, and that he expects clearer findings soon. Netanyahu met survivors of the flight on Thursday. A passenger on board a flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv captured the moment it landed safely in Saudi Arabia after an ordeal of what Israeli officials said was an attempt to crash the plane pic.twitter.comE9QMuqGM23- Reuters Reuters October 2, 2026 Smit Machchhar is from Mumbai. The Times of Israel says that by opening the cockpit door he helped save all of the roughly 180 people on the plane. Other outlets, including The Guardian, put the number of passengers at 174. A teacher from Gurukul School of Art paints a portrait honoring Smit Machchhar,, an Indian pilot with FlyDubai, in Mumbai, India. Photo AP Prime Minister Narendra Modi has called him a hero. Indias embassy in the UAE said on Thursday that he is in good health and recovering well, and Indias foreign ministry said he has been moved to Abu Dhabi for more medical care. The new video gives the first look at his condition soon after the attack. He is seen talking to the medics about his injured hand, and the footage shows the crew and passengers around him.

articleTitle: iPhone 18 Pro Max review: Apple finally lets the Pro be a tool
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The iPhone 18 Pro Max is designed to put professional-grade camera controls and creator workflows in the palm of your hand. (Image: Nandagopal Rajan/The Indian Express)
description: The iPhone 18 Pro Max is not a phone for everyone. With manual camera controls, desktop-class performance and longer battery life, Apple is positioning its Pro Max as a professional creator tool.
body_raw: For those who cared to listen, there was a big message at the Apple iPhone launch event, and no, it was not the advent of the first iOS foldable, the iPhone Duo. Apple drew a clear line between its consumer and Pro devices. The message itself was not new, but it had always been subtle before. This time Apple did not even launch a regular iPhone at the event. With the iPhone 18 Pro Max, Cupertino made it clear that this phone is for those who want a professional workflow in their hand. But let us not think of the Pro series as a phone for niches, not when millions across the world are donning the creator hat and making content for online platforms. This is Apple taking the battle to the camera companies and others who thought this segment could be theirs. The iPhone 18 Pro Max presents itself as a single device that can handle the entire creator workflow at a fraction of the price of a professional setup. At Rs 1,79,900, the iPhone 18 Pro Max can handle the entire creator workflow for less than half the price of a camera setup that delivers the same output. Let me explain why. There are three factors that push the iPhone 18 Pro Max to the level of a standalone professional-grade device. View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Indian Express indianexpress Changes in the camera The iPhone 18 Pro Max packs significant camera changes which, interestingly, are not of much use to regular users. To use a simple analogy, if you shoot in Auto or Programme mode on a DSLR, these changes wont affect you. Apple is targeting those who shoot in manual mode. You now get a variable aperture, adjustable shutter speed and a live histogram to take your photos and videos to the next level. The variable aperture on the 48MP Fusion camera has physical blades that let in more light when you are shooting in dark conditions. The aperture now has an auto mode and four f-stops ranging from f to f This versatility clearly adds character to some shots, especially with a light source in the frame. I loved how the bulbs in my shots had a star effect that changed with the aperture setting. However, this feature is available only on the main lens. I was personally more interested in shutter speed, as this is my go-to mode when shooting with cameras muting the light a bit to bring more focus on the subject. I could shoot silhouettes like I did on the DSLR, without third-party iOS apps. And you can use all these features while shooting video too. The live histogram and adjustable white balance make a huge difference when you are shooting in bright Noida sun. Yes, phone cameras usually adjust to this quickly. But that does not work for professionals who want exactly what they had envisaged to show up in the frame. This is the control I got with the new camera features, and that too while shooting 4K at 120fps. The camera also drives the only design change in the phone a slightly thicker camera bump. Desktop-class processor For years now, iPhone processors have been ahead of the competition. In the initial years you could at least compare what that meant. Over the past couple of years, it has become difficult to compare even between generations of the iPhone. The A19 Pro on the iPhone 17 Pro Max was already blazing fast, and it is now tough to tell how much faster the A20 Pro is. What really matters is how this translates into a smoother workflow. Shoot a video in 4K at 120 or 60fps, make edits and colour corrections, render a new stitched output, and you will not get stuck at any point. Nor will the phone heat up at any stage, including while shooting high-frame-rate 4K video. This is the processor and the redesigned vapour chamber working in tandem. Most of us associate vapour chambers with gaming, but they make even more sense for professional workflows. A 1-minute 4K 60 fps video was processed and exported in a couple of seconds without any lag. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Nandu79 nandagopalrajan The processor also powers a supercharged Siri, which now understands what the user is doing or reading. You can ask it what it sees on the screen at any moment, or what is visible through the camera. For creators, that means getting context on a script, information about the location the camera is seeing, or tips on improving a frame, all without leaving the screen. Siri leverages the processor and Apples Gemini partnership to finally become relevant in an AI world. Queries get quick responses that are mostly accurate, and there is a chance its use will now go beyond Apple users voice-dialling someone. More battery life Apple packed a larger 5391mAh battery into the iPhone 18 Pro Max, meaning battery life is actually better despite the more powerful processor. This may be the first iPhone that can last 24 hours of proper usage without hours of browsing and consuming content, shooting a few minutes of video and editing the same, as well as regular chats and other app usage without you reaching for the charger. That is significant, especially for professional users. I could also use a third-party 60W GaN charger to get the battery to 50 in around 15 minutes. Whats missing? The iPhone 18 Pro Max is a well-rounded phone. But if you were expecting a phone that would show the world you have upgraded from the 17 Pro Max in just a year, you only have the new colour options to pick from. There is no significant design change or feature you can flaunt. This is clearly another signal. It is almost like saying this segment does not really care about design antics as long as the product makes practical sense. Since Apple is going after the professional user, it could have introduced accessories that turn this into a proper professional rig. You can buy those from other companies today, but an Apple rig would add more power to this phone. Who should buy? If youre a regular smartphone user, dont upgrade to this the regular iPhone or iPhone Air will do just fine. If you already have a Pro device, only upgrade if youre on an iPhone 15 Pro or older which had a significantly different camera. Otherwise, hold for another cycle. Unless you shoot in manual mode, the day-to-day experience wont feel very different. But if you are a creator or power user who will benefit from the better camera and processor, you can upgrade this year like every other year. This phone will give you an edge and more efficiency. I felt the iPhone Duo stole the thunder from the iPhone 18 Pro Max, arguably the most powerful phone on the planet. But this phone is grounded in its strengths and in the confidence that it is better than the rest. It knows it is playing for a professional crowd, one that will not be too impressed by the looks of the Duo.

articleTitle: Diego Forlan on Indian football: ‘Talented young players, need stronger academies & league’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uruguay coach Diego Forlan in action. (AP)
description: The 2010 FIFA World Cup Golden Ball winner said that playing international friendlies against stronger opposition like Brazil and Uruguay would benefit the Blue Tigers in the long run.
body_raw: After Brazil coach Carlo Ancelotti caused quite a stir last month when he said India did not have a footballing culture, Uruguay coach Diego Forlan said that while the main sport in the country was cricket, India still had a lot of young talented football players. Your main sport is cricket, so its different. Football has been here for many years, of course, but its not the main sport. But you have a lot of young talented players, Forlan said, speaking on the eve of the India vs Uruguay match. The 2010 FIFA World Cup Golden Ball winner said that playing international friendlies against stronger opposition like Brazil and Uruguay would benefit the Blue Tigers in the long run. I think this kind of game, playing against Brazil, Uruguay, and also having a strong league, would improve the development of young players. In the near future, India could be playing important and crucial games, he said. ALSO READ India vs Uruguay Can the Blue Tigers build on Brazil lessons? You need to build from the roots - academies, young players, kids to start playing a lot. If you build more academies, the league gets stronger and stronger, you will achieve getting more players and getting better players, thats for sure, added Forlan. Before the Uruguay fixture, India have played Panama against whom they drew 1-1 and then taken on Brazil, where they showed some spark in the beginning before getting trounced 4-0. Uruguay, meanwhile, landed in Kolkata on September 30 and have been taking time to acclimatise to the Indian conditions. We know its not going to be easy. Playing here, the weather is humid. You also need to adapt. Thats why all these days that we came here were good for us to adapt. The weather is different from Japan and Korea, so we know its going to be a difficult game, Forlan said. Before talking on India, Uruguay had toured Japan and Korea, losing to the former 1-3 and defeating the latter 4-1.

articleTitle: Varalaxmi Sarathkumar on choosing not to have children: ‘A good parenting decision’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Varalaxmi Sarathkumar
description: Varalaxmi Sarathkumar’s views on family and parenthood raise an important question about personal choice
body_raw: Varalaxmi Sarathkumar, 41, who married Mumbai-based businessman and gallerist Nicholai Sachdev in 2024, opened up about not having children and why its a good parenting decision in itself. I personally said I am not interested in having children.it is not that I cant have.I dont want to have children.there is a very clear choice that I dont want. My husband also doesnt want to, the Vikram Vedha actor told video jockey Bharanee Suresh on Behindwoods TV. She continued, We already have a daughter from his previous marriage. I will always look at her like that. We already have two puppies, whom I look at as my children. I dont want to have it is my personal choice, and we both have that thinking. Not having children is a decision because of responsibilities galore. If you are not ready for it, dont have.and I think thats a very good parenting decision in itself. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. How does choosing not to have children make a case for responsible parenting? As a psychotherapist, Delnna Rrajesh, a relationship breakthrough coach, said that it opens a conversation we need to have without turning it into a debate between parents and people who are child-free by choice. For generations, particularly for women, parenthood has often been treated less as a decision and more as the inevitable next stage of adulthood education, career, marriage, children. The question was frequently when rather than whether. But bringing another human being into the world is perhaps one of the few decisions that deserves more conscious examination, not less. A child needs much more than parents who can financially provide. Parenting requires time, emotional availability, patience, consistency, lifestyle adjustments and the willingness to repeatedly place another persons developmental needs alongside ones own. It changes careers, relationships, finances, sleep, freedom, identity and everyday priorities, reflected Delnna. This does not make parenthood a burden. For people who genuinely desire it, raising a child can be one of lifes most meaningful experiences. But something can be deeply meaningful and still not be the right life choice for everyone. That distinction matters, Delnna told indianexpress.com. There is also an important psychological difference between I dont want children and I would be a bad parent. A person does not need to construct a deficit, trauma or justification around their decision for it to become legitimate. Not wanting parenthood can itself be sufficient information about the life they consciously wish to build, emphasised Delnna. Equally, choosing children should not happen merely because everyone eventually does, because parents want grandchildren, because friends are having babies, because a marriage has reached a certain number of years, or because a woman fears she may later regret not becoming a mother. A child should not be brought into the world primarily to resolve social pressure. Because wanting a baby and wanting to parent are not the same thing. Babies grow into toddlers who test boundaries, children who need enormous consistency and teenagers who require patience, emotional regulation and increasing autonomy. Parenting is not the photograph of the newborn. It is the thousands of ordinary days that follow. Conscious parenting therefore begins, paradoxically, before conception. Parenthood is a profound form of nurturing, but it is not the only expression of a meaningful or caring life, emphasised Delnna. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Bharanee Suresh vjbharane Nor should we swing to the opposite extreme and portray choosing children as less evolved than remaining child-free. There is no psychologically superior choice. There is only a more or less conscious one. Some people deeply want parenthood. Some deeply do not. Some remain uncertain. Some discover the desire later. Some experience infertility or circumstances in which the choice is taken from them entirely. Each deserves sensitivity rather than assumption, said Delnna. Perhaps the real shift society needs is from asking adults, particularly women, When are you having children? to recognising that this is an intensely personal decision that does not require public explanation. The most responsible parenting decision is not automatically to have children. Nor is it automatically not to. It is to understand the magnitude of raising another human being and make that decision as consciously as possible. articleTitle: Porn videos surface in Spotify search results, highlighting gaps in content moderation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Spotify down
description: As per Spotify’s platform rules, users should “avoid” uploading content that contains sexually explicit material.
body_raw: A Spotify user who searched for the rapper M.I.A came across a pornographic video on the platform, among other suggested results. The sexually explicit material appeared in the Video tab of the search section, according to a screenshot posted by the user on Reddit. After sifting through dozens of search results on Spotify, The Verge reported that it found other pornographic videos that had been uploaded on the platform. The accounts posting such videos are likely to be podcast accounts that have been publishing erotic audio for years. Some of them reportedly had a long string of alphanumeric characters as their username. As per Spotifys platform rules, users should avoid uploading content that contains sexually explicit material, including but not limited to pornography or visual depictions of genitalia or nudity presented for the purpose of sexual gratification as well as content advocating or glorifying sexual themes related to rape, incest, or beastiality. Users can also report sexually explicit material but not directly on the platform. The process of reporting such content involves copying the URL of the content and visiting a separate webpage designed for flagging possible violations on Spotify. The examples of pornographic videos found by The Verge have been removed due to violation of our policies, a Spotify spokesperson was quoted as saying.

articleTitle: Police issue notices to MPSC protesters, coaching classes; Commissioner calls protest ‘illegal’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: MPSC paper leak, MPSC protests, MPSC protests intensify, MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar, Pune news, Pune, Maharashtra news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Protest enters Day 6, AAP's Sanjay Singh joins protesters
body_raw: Terming the ongoing protest in Pune over the MPSC paper leak illegal, Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar said that police issued over 70 notices to protesters, coaching classes, and Telegram channels in connection with the protest. The notices were issued two to three days ago, he added. The protest is illegal, there is no permission to do it. It is causing inconvenience to the general commuters and the leaders are coming and giving provocative speeches inciting students. This is not proper and not within the legal framework. So please withdraw from the agitation is what we have said in the notices, Kumar told The Indian Express. On the future course of action of the police and whether the protesters had been given any time period to withdraw the protest, Kumar said, Time period, not really. But we are keeping a close watch on the developments and we have been exercising extreme tact and patience so as to not let a conflict situation happen. We are hoping that the agitating students realise that they are doing something illegal and in contravention of rules and regulations. But well intervene appropriately as and when required. Leaders including Rohit Pawar, who has been leading the protest, had not been issued any notice, the commissioner added. He said that no FIRs had been filed, other than an FIR filed by a journalist who was allegedly attacked by a person at the protest. The protest demanding resignation of Maharashtra Public Service Commission MPSC chairperson Vivek Bhimanwar continued for its sixth day on Tuesday. Students gathered at the SM Joshi bridge in large numbers at night as various political leaders addressed them. Earlier in the day, the protesters carried out a symbolic last rites ceremony targeting the MPSC Chairman. Aam Aadmi Party MP Sanjay Singh joined the protesters on Tuesday. I have been told that along with MPSC, papers of talati, drugs inspector, health recruitment, PMC, BMC, teacher recruitment, MMRDA, and MH-CET, all papers have been leaked. And the paper leak that got the whole country on the ground, NEET paper was also leaked. This is a paper leak government, Sanjay Singh alleged. He added, When I asked why is Vivek Bhimanwar MPSC chairperson not resigning, I was told that Bhimanwar and Devendra Fadnavis jodi is like Jai and Veeru. There is a lot of love between them. And he is not ready to take his resignation. Beware of the poision of Hindu-Muslim that they try to fill in your brain during elections. And remember, those who could not be of God Ram referring to the Ram Mandir donation theft, they can never be yours either, said Singh. The protesters are occupying the area near SM Joshi bridge. Two other protest spots have also emerged at Lal Bahadur Shastri Road, and Alka Talkies chowk, with all groups having different demands. Protesters have been demanding the resignation of the MPSC chairperson over the leak of the Drug Inspector examination held in March this year.

articleTitle: Nobel Medicine Prize 2026: How three scientists discovered a way to control brain cells with light
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel are shown on the screen as they are awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (AP/PTI)
description: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries that laid the foundation of optogenetics — a technique that lets scientists switch specific cells on and off using light.
body_raw: The Nobel Prize in Physiology and Medicine for 2026 was jointly awarded to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their discovery of an algae protein that react to light and its use as a switch to study the functions of nerve cells. Their explorations led to the creation of a new field of study called optogenetic, which may finally help scientists understand how the brain forms memories, feelings and behaviours. We were able to precisely pace the heart and look at the effects that different heart rates have on brain states. Communication across the body, from the body to the brain, but with the precision of a gain of function in a peripheral organ allowing us to see the effects on brain and behavioural state . this ability to execute a precision intervention in one organ and read out the effects in complex behaviours - this is something that people have wanted for a long time to be able to do, said Deisseroth. In simple terms, they found a way to control cells with light. Imagine that the brain is a vast electrical network containing billions of tiny cells called neurons. These neurons communicate by sending electrical signals, allowing us to move, see, remember, feel pain and experience emotions. Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel helped scientists develop a remarkable way of controlling these electrical signals using light. Their research led to the discovery and development of light-sensitive proteins, called opsins, that can be placed in specific cells. When light is shone on those cells, the proteins act like tiny switches, turning the cells activity on or off. This technology is known as optogenetics - essentially, using light to control genetically modified cells. What is optogenetics? It is basically a field of research that uses light to manipulate the activity of neurons or other types of cells and study the resulting effects. This is done by expressing the light-sensitive protein in the targeted cells. Within the brain, it has contributed towards identifying neural circuits responsible for sense of pain, social behaviours, thirst, food consumption, reward and attention or the understanding of how memories are created. How did the discipline evolve? Interestingly, the field rests on a theory proposed by Francis Crick, the molecular biologist who was behind the discovery of and was awarded the Nobel prize for the double helix structure of DNA. He envisioned activating individual nerve cells in a brain to investigate the mechanisms that underlie human consciousness. With nerve signals being extremely rapid, he realised it would only be possible if scientists were somehow able to manipulate the nerve cells with light. He himself admitted that the idea sounded far-fetched. But it was made possible by the work of Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel on the alga Chlamydomonas. These are famous for their ability to quickly swim towards a light. Hegemann found that it reacted extremely quickly, within half a millisecond after the light reached a tiny orange dot called eyespot that the alga used to detect light. To compare, it takes 10 milliseconds for the human eye to react to light. Hegemann wondered how could the response to light be more than twenty times faster in Chlamydomonas? He hypothesised that a single protein complex both captured light and acted on it in the alga as opposed to the multi-step process in the human eye. Yet, finding this protein was a challenge because when the proteins in the algal eyespot were removed from their natural setting, they became unstable and easily damaged. This is when he discovered that Japanese researchers had mapped the DNA of Chlamydomonas, among which were the codes for two genes that had similarities to light-capturing proteins. Enter Nagel. He used egg cells of frogs to express the two proteins and confirm that Hegemanns hypothesis was actually correct. The alga detected and reacted to light using the protein channelrhodopsin-2 ChR-2. They then introduced the cells in different types of cells and found that they all became light sensitive. Karl Deisseroth found that ChR-2 could control the activity of specific nerve cells in the manner proposed by Francis Crick. He used it to control rat nerve cells in a petri dish and later in the rats. With Deisseroths lab at the forefront, researchers soon found more proteins that can turn nerve cells on and off, and which are activated by different wavelengths of light. How does it help to study the brain? Imagine the brain to be a building with lots and lots of rooms - now there was no way for us to know what happens if the light is switched on in just one room. Optogenetics has given us an extremely powerful way to switch on and off the neurons and see what happens. It has allowed us to manipulate nerve cells and study its effects with unprecedented level of precision. It has completely changed the scale at which discoveries are happening in neurosciences, said Vidita Vaidya, senior professor at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research. While optogenetics is still largely used in the laboratories to see which set of neurons regulate what type of behaviour in animals - it helps us look into the black box, she says - it is still ways away from therapies to help those with spinal cord paralysis. Dr Sanjeev Kumar Mahto, professor at IIT BHU, said it has allowed scientists to see the functions of the brain and enhance the understanding of what causes certain conditions. Deisseroths research group introduced the gene for ChR-2 in 2006 and successfully used a light to activate neurons to control movements of the mouse whiskers.The same year he used the technique to wake sleeping mice by manipulating a recently discovered type of nerve cell that was suspected to control wakefulness. His team also studied the brains of mice as they experienced fear, and noted which nerve cells appeared to form the memory. When they later reactivated these nerve cells, the mice showed signs of fear, despite not being in danger at the time. What kind of therapies are being developed based on this field? There are ongoing clinical trials on restoring vision in people who have become blind due to retinitis pigmentosa, a disease that destroys the eyes rods and cones. Using special glasses emitting light, the person was able to discern and grasp objects on a table. There are also hopes that optogenetics could improve cochlea implants. Currently, these implants stimulate the auditory nerve using electricity.

articleTitle: King Charles warns Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor not to use royal funds in battle against police
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor legal challenge
description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor receives an annual stipend from King Charles’ private funds, although the amount has not been disclosed.
body_raw: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor has reportedly been warned not to use money provided to him by King Charles from the monarchs private funds to finance his legal challenge against Thames Valley police in England. This comes in the backdrop of the former Duke of York seeking to quash search warrants that led to his arrest earlier this year for his alleged role in sharing sensitive information with Jeffrey Epstein. The Guardian report, which cited palace sources, comes just days ahead of a private high court hearing on Thursday over his legal claim. Mountbatten-Windsor receives an annual stipend from King Charles private funds, although the amount has not been disclosed. However, it has been made clear that the money should not be used to fund the judicial review, the report said. The report further said that Mountbatten-Windsors legal defence was a matter for him and his lawyers, while Buckingham Palace had no role in deciding the strategy or actions being taken in the case. Andrew Mountbatten-Windsors arrest and charges The legal challenge relates to searches carried out by Thames Valley police following Mountbatten-Windsors arrest on February 19 on suspicion of misconduct in public office. The former duke was arrested on his 66th birthday over allegations that he had shared sensitive information with Jeffrey Epstein while serving as the UKs trade envoy. Police searched his residence on the Sandringham estate and his former home, Royal Lodge, after warrants were issued by a judge at the Old Bailey. The searches ended on February 24, according to Thames Valley police. Mountbatten-Windsor was interviewed under caution and later released under investigation. The arrest came as scrutiny continued over allegations concerning his links with Epstein and the handling of information during his time as a trade envoy. The former duke, who now lives on King Charles private Sandringham estate in Norfolk, was previously granted permission to challenge whether Thames Valley police acted lawfully in obtaining and executing the search warrants. What is expected in the Thursday hearing The Guardian cited a judicial spokesperson who confirmed on Monday that a hearing in the legal claim would take place at 2 pm on Thursday before Justice Hilliard at the High Court. The hearing will concern an attempt by Thames Valley police to restrict access to court documents and will begin in private. It remains unclear whether Mountbatten-Windsor will attend the hearing. The king had maintained that the legal process should proceed independently. Following Mountbatten-Windsors arrest, Charles issued a written statement saying the law must take its course. Thames Valley police said its investigation into alleged misconduct in public office remained ongoing and confirmed that it was involved in legal proceedings concerning warrants previously obtained from the central criminal court. As these legal proceedings are currently ongoing, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further, the Guardian report quoted a police spokesperson as saying.

articleTitle: Hanuman Ansh box office: Neem Karoli Baba film earns just Rs 20 lakh less than The Vvaan on 9th Tuesday
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hanuman Ansh box office collection day 61: Neem Karoli Baba biopic earns just Rs 20 lakh less than Sidharth Malhotra's The Vvaan: Force of the Forrest.
description: Hanuman Ansh box office collection day 61: The Neem Karoli Baba biopic slipped down below the daily mark of Rs 1 crore after 41 days, only to bounce back to that figure on its ninth Tuesday.
body_raw: Hanuman Ansh box office collection day 61Vishal Chaturvedis devotional film Hanuman Ansh, which features Shobhinaw Satyaa as revered spiritual guru Neem Karoli Baba, continues to hold its own in front of new releases even in its ninth week at the domestic box office. While its daily earnings pale in comparison to Ajay Devgn-starrer crime thriller Drishyam 3, its on the verge of surpassing those of the holdover release - Sidharth Malhotra-starrer action adventure fantasy film The Vvaan Force of the Forrest. After over 60 days, Hanuman Ansh has earned Rs 385.62 crore gross and Rs 326.48 crore net in India, and Rs 425.52 crore worldwide. Hanuman Ansh box office collection - Week 9 On its ninth Tuesday day 61, Hanuman Ansh took advantage of the discounted ticket prices to get back into the Rs 1 crore range. It garnered exactly Rs 1 crore from 1570 screens, a 33.33 growth from its ninth Monday day 60 collection of Rs 75 lakh from 1475 screens. That was, in fact, the first time in 41 days of its historic box office run that the films daily earnings went below the Rs 1 crore mark. Ever since Day 18, Hanuman Ansh has been consistently earning more than Rs 1 crore every day, all the way till day 59. It finally fell below that threshold on its ninth Monday, owing to massive competition from Abhishek Pathaks Drishyam 3, which amassed Rs 21 crore from over 16,000 shows on its first Monday, as per Sacnilk. However, despite the competition, Hanuman Ansh has managed to secure around 1500 screens even in its ninth week. Its ninth weekend is testimony to its enduring appeal, since the film collected Rs 3 crore on Sunday day 59, Rs 2.10 crore on Saturday day 58, and Rs 2.25 crore on Friday day 57, which was a holiday on the occasion of October 2, celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti. The impact of Hanuman Ansh is not limited to only the box office, but also the cultural ethos of Indian society. Nainital District Magistrate Lalit Mohan told The Indian Express earlier this week that partly owing to the film, daily visitors have increased by 10,000 over this past long weekend at Kainchi Dham, the spiritual site associated with Neem Karoli Baba in Uttarakhand, prompting the district management to devise an alternate route to avoid congestion. Made on a modest budget of Rs 2 crore, Hanuman Ansh has now earned almost 213 times at the worldwide box office. It initially opened at just Rs 25 lakh on August 7 and collected Rs 1.10 crore in its opening week at the domestic box office. However, following the upsurge in week 3, the weekly collections kept multiplying. After over two months at the domestic box office, with no streaming premiere in sight, Hanuman Ansh is just a couple of crores away from surpassing the domestic box office collection of Sunny Deol and Varun Dhawan-starrer period war drama Border 2 Rs 329.70 crore to become the second highest grossing Indian film this year, after Ranveer Singh-starrer spy thriller Dhurandhar 2 The Revenge Rs 1108.90 crore. Hanuman Ansh was released internationally by Hombale Films over a month after its domestic release on September 11. Since then, its collected Rs 39.90 crore at the overseas box office in less than a month. Its dubbed Telugu version is slated to release in cinemas this Friday on October 9, which may further complement its unprecedented box office run. Vvaan box office collection day 12 Meanwhile, the holdover release from a couple of weeks ago September 25, Deepak Kumar Mishras The Vvaan Force of the Forrest has also been impacted by the Drishyam 3 wave. It collected Rs 1.20 crore from 1990 screens on its second Tuesday day 12, benefitting from discounted ticket prices, to register a 26.30 growth from its second Monday day 11 earnings of Rs 95 lakh. Thats also the first instance when Vvaan went below the daily earnings mark of Rs 1 crore so far. Over its second weekend, it earned Rs 3.25 crore on Sunday day 10, Rs 2 crore on Saturday day 9, and Rs 3.25 crore on Friday day 8 at the domestic box office. Its opening weeks cumulative earnings stand at Rs 53.60 crore in India. Also Read Fahadh Faasil says wont get half of Rs 300 cr as Bethlehem Kudumba Unit earns Rs 326 cr Thus, the total box office collection of Vvaan now adds up to Rs 76.30 crore net and Rs 64.25 crore gross in India. It has collected Rs 7.20 crore internationally, which makes its worldwide gross earnings go up to Rs 83.50 crore. Given the current trajectory, Vvaan needs to pick up pace if it aspires to cross the coveted Rs 100 crore mark in India, or even globally.

articleTitle: Homes evacuated near UK military base after 5 men with ‘explosives’ arrested; bomb squad called in
articleFeaturedImageAlt: uk air base, us
description: RAF Fairford major incident investigation is being led by UK counter-terrorism police after several men were arrested over suspected explosives offences.
body_raw: The UKs counter-terrorism police are leading the investigation into a major incident at RAF Fairford air base, used by the United States in southwest England. The police have arrested 5 men on suspicion of explosives offences, and the bomb disposal squad was called in to examine several vehicles, reports stated on Sunday. Gloucestershire police said that nearby residents of a number of properties in Whelford, western England, had been evacuated from their homes and taken to a nearby leisure centre, adding that the situation at the air base has been contained, AP reported. After the agencies declared a major incident at the RAF Fairford base, a bomb squad was dispatched to Whelford village with extra security measures, including the fortification of entrances to the base. Road blocks were also seen in the area over the weekend. BREAKING UK police find EXPLOSIVES less than 1 mile from airbase used for attacks on Iran Several men have been arrested over suspected explosives offences in Gloucestershire, triggering the evacuation of homes in the village of Whelford. Army bomb-disposal specialists. - Mario Nawfal MarioNawfal September 27, 2026 The British government said Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being updated about the incident. We are grateful to the emergency services, who have acted quickly to detain several suspects and put measures in place to keep the community safe. It would be inappropriate to comment further whilst investigations are ongoing, a government spokesperson said. I would like to thank all those emergency and specialist teams who have acted so swiftly regarding the incident in Gloucestershire. We can be reassured that this is being dealt with, and it is exactly why our emergency response teams and Armed Forces are on standby 24 - Wes Streeting wesstreeting September 27, 2026 Notably, the UK administration had allowed the US to use RAF Fairford base to attack Iranian missile sites that were hitting ships in the Strait of Hormuz. Irans Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps IRGC had threatened in July that any base being used to strike the Islamic Republic will be a legitimate target. Describing the area where the arrests took place, a Reuters report stated that nearly 30 emergency vehicles, including ambulances, fire engines, and police cars were parked in the Fairford village near the air base, while a helicopter flew above. Defence Minister Wes Streeting, in a post on X, thanked emergency and specialist teams deployed to the scene. We can be reassured that this is being dealt with, Streeting added. articleTitle: The Paradise box office day 2: Nani-starrer witnesses 57 percent drop, earns Rs 98.5 cr

description: The Paradise box office collection day 2: Nani-starrer The Paradise has collected Rs 98.50 crore in two days.
body_raw: The Paradise box office collection day 2 Nani-starrer The Paradise had a strong start at the box office but the film has experienced a severe drop in its collections on the second day. After bringing in nearly Rs 76 crore worldwide on opening day, the film could only manage to earn roughly Rs 22 crore worldwide on the second day. The overall worldwide gross collection of the film currently stands at Rs 98.5 crore. The fall on the second day is of over 57 percent in net domestic collections. The Paradise earned Rs 14.9 crore net in India on the second day across 7,000 shows. The overseas market added Rs 4 crore, taking the total overseas gross to Rs 26 crore, according to industry tracker Sacnilk. How Day 2 compares to his previous films Dasara, Nanis previous collaboration with director Srikanth Odela, collected Rs 9.75 crore net on Day 2 across 5,329 shows, bringing its two-day India net to Rs 32.95 crore and worldwide gross to Rs 48.99 crore. The Paradises second-day collection is higher than Dasaras second day, and its worldwide collection so far is twice as Dasara. ALSO READ Dorothy movie review Karthik Subbarajs film will make everyone uncomfortable Saripodhaa Sanivaaram collected worldwide gross of Rs 28.16 crore in two days, while Hi Nanna, the emotional family drama that became one of Nanis most beloved recent films, collected worldwide gross of Rs 16.33 crore in two days. The Paradise has done better than all these films but given the mediocre reception it has received so far, it seems unlikely that the film will be able to sustain any momentum past the first week. Nani acknowledges The Paradises flaws On Friday, Nani took to X and thanked the audience for their support. He also acknowledged the flaws in the film and shared, I have seen all your reactions and responses. Ive received all your love and equally enjoyed your hilarious trolls. Im heartwarmed by the way audience have owned the film, and also learnt from the flaws that critics and reviewers have pointed out. Thank you for everything is all I can say. We have made The Paradise with a lot of blood and sweat to give you a unique experience, and its all yours to celebrate or judge.
