With his performance in the grand finale, Ritesh impressed the judges he even left special guests - Jackie Shroff, Tamannaah Bhatia, and Sidharth Malhotra quite amazed. Indias Best Dancer Season 5 started on Sony Television in June. Talking about the latest season and its theme, India Wala Dance, judge Jaaved Jaaferi had exclusively told SCREEN in June, Dance on reality shows was looking the same everywhere there are a handful of choreographers, and it was quite visible that they all are doing the same things. It was only smart to realize to change and go back to the time when we enjoyed dancing and not be so technical about it. On this show, we are technical, but its also about connecting with the audience. In the 70s, 80s, and 90s, what we did right was that Shammi Kapoor Sahab, Mithun Da, Jeetendra Sahab, and later on SRK and Aamir connected through dance. So we tried to create the same feel with this show.

articleTitle: ‘Better to die with self-respect’: Ex-Rajasthan minister walks out of Congress
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vishvendra Singh
description: Sacked after Sachin Pilot’s 2020 rebellion and re-inducted as minister, Singh is from the erstwhile royal family of Bharatpur and an influential Jat leader from the region.
body_raw: Vishvendra Singh - a former Cabinet Minister in the Ashok Gehlot government - announced his resignation from the Congress on Friday, two days after levelling allegations against state unit president Govind Singh Dotasra and accusing the partys Bharatpur and Deeg units of sidelining actual party workers in local polls. Sharing a statement on social media on Friday morning, Singh said it was better to die with self-respect than suffocation. Just a day earlier, following Singhs attack, Dotasra had dismissed as propaganda the alleged differences within the party, saying, There is no discord among us. This is the BJPs toolkit. The BJP spreads propaganda and tries to show that there are differences within the Congress. I have always taken decisions in life by listening to the voice of my beloved Giriraj Maharaj and my conscience. Today, the baseless statements made by some small-time so-called leaders have angered my workers. My conscience is also saddened and distressed. If the party for which I sacrificed my life has rewarded my loyalty, honesty, and dedication in this way, I am deeply shaken, Singh wrote. Earlier, Congress district presidents for Bharatpur and Deeg had reportedly sent a report against Singh to the party high command. In a post on September 30, the former minister alleged the two distributed tickets to their favourites while sidelining genuine party workers and said the voters responded to this in the election. Who is responsible for the ruin of Congress in Bharatpur-Deeg? Singh had said, alleging that the voters were now ready to hold the district presidents and Dotasra accountable. Singh said Bharatpur was the Chief Ministers home district and the Congress should have been stronger there, and alleged that the local leadership had damaged the party. In a separate post, he had also targeted Dotasra, saying that he misused his power in the previous Congress government to benefit his family members, saying, Such corrupt leaders should resign with immediate effect, or the Congress party high command should take strict action against them and expel them from the party. The BJP has levelled similar allegations over the years and the Congress and Dotasra have refuted them on multiple occasions. Singh said Friday that I have always lived my life with dignity, respect, and self-respect. I have never compromised on my principles and ideals. My workers are angry because of the current tradition of chaploosi flattery. If calling a spade a spade and not supporting falsehood is a sin, then I will do it every time. I neither do wrong nor tolerate wrong. He said that his public life is for the people and I live for them and will die for them. Every drop of my blood has been, and will continue to be, shed for my workers, my voters, the people of my constituency, and the state. My public life is an open book. It is spotless, I have never allowed any stain to be put on my reputation, nor will I ever allow it to be put on my reputation. Within the Congress, his sudden broadside against Dotasra had given rise to the speculation that he may be on his way to join the BJP. Three-term MP-MLA Singh hails from the erstwhile royal family of Bharatpur and is the son of its last ruler Brijendra Singh, who died in 1995. An influential Jat leader from the region, he has earlier been a BJP MP. He was first elected as a Lok Sabha MP from Bharatpur on a Janata Dal ticket in 1989. Then in 1993, he was elected as an MLA from Nadbai Assembly seat on a Congress ticket. In 1999, he was in the BJP and was elected to the Lok Sabha from Bharatpur, and then again in 2004. In 2013 and 2018, he was elected as an MLA from Deeg Kumher Assembly seat on a Congress ticket. Beyond politics, he has been in the news for internal rifts within his family too. 2020 rebellion Six years ago, Singh had made headlines as one of the key architects of then Deputy Chief Minister Sachin Pilot-led rebellion against the Ashok Gehlot government in 2020. The Special Operations Group had lodged two different FIRs based on the complaints by then government Chief Whip Mahesh Joshi. Both were lodged under IPC sections 124A sedition and 120B punishment for criminal conspiracy. The first FIR was regarding the purported conversation between Vishvendra Singh and Union Jal Shakti Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat following the rebellion and audio leaks, Vishvendra Singh was removed as Tourism Minister and was suspended from primary membership of the Congress party. The complaint, without naming either, had claimed that a conversation was played on social media and television channels, where two persons are heard talking, and transcribes their conversation. In the said conversation, the persons are planning a conspiracy to topple a democratically elected and legally established government, through exchange of money and by spreading unrest. This comes under sedition. Hence, please lodge a case against the conspirators as per rules, and take action, the complaint by Joshi had said he had also submitted the audio clip of the conversation. With Pilot camp eventually returning to Jaipur, Vishvendra Singh was again handed the Tourism department, along with Civil Aviation, in a cabinet expansion in November 2021. Following his reinduction, he had apparently grown closer to Gehlot than to Pilot.

articleTitle: Great Nicobar project: Supreme Court dismisses Centre’s objection to maintainability of PILs in Calcutta High Court
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Great Nicobar project: SC dismisses Centre’s objection to PILs’ maintainability in HC
description: A Chief Justice of India Surya Kant-led three-judge bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, asked the HC to make an endeavour to decide the matter on the dates (November 25-26) fixed.
body_raw: The Supreme Court on Monday declined to entertain the Centres objections regarding the maintainability of a PIL filed before the Calcutta High Court against the clearance for the ambitious Great Nicobar project. A Chief Justice of India Surya Kant-led three-judge bench, also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, asked the HC to make an endeavour to decide the matter on the dates November 25-26 fixed. The National Green Tribunal NGT had in February this year cleared the way for the governments Rs 81,000-crore Great Nicobar mega infrastructure project, noting its strategic importance and observing that there were adequate safeguards in the projects environmental clearance. This was challenged before the HC on the ground that it violates the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers Act, 2006. Before the HC, the Centre raised objections to its maintainability, but they were rejected. Following this, the Centre approached the Supreme Court. Appearing for the Centre, Attorney General R Venkataramani told the SC, .this is such an important matter on which somebody comes and files a petition years later, and then three different petitions try to challenge it in three different ways. Then they say the tribals are affected, and they are not before the court. Now they have got impleaded. Therefore, this petition should not be there before the High Court at all. This question of maintainability goes to the root of the matter. He urged the bench to allow him to make submissions on the point of maintainability. Do not close the door on maintainability because something very important turns on that. I just want to keep the door open, he said. Appearing for respondent original petitioner before HC Meena Gupta, Senior Advocate S Muralidhar said the Centres counsel had himself urged the HC to list it for final hearing. He contended that the PIL was maintainable as it involved the issue of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups. Justice Bagchi said the preservation of culture is a constitutionally protected fundamental right. He added that the Great Andamanese had by now become integrated with the mainstream population, adding, Do they become integrated completely with the mainstream, or do we keep them with their unique identity and the identity of their culture? The court ultimately left it to the HC, noting that other similar matters were also pending there.

articleTitle: Katrina Kaif on how motherhood changed her: ‘Looking my best is now about feeling my best’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Katrina Kaif
description: Katrina Kaif spoke about self-care, switching off from work and the lifestyle habits that help her feel healthy from within.
body_raw: Katrina Kaif is not just an actor now - she is a successful entrepreneur and a new mom. In a recent interview, Katrina spoke about her brand, how motherhood and pregnancy changed her, and also what makes her feel most like yourself, away from a film set, a red carpet or a brand meeting. Katrina on finding balance away from work Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter India, the actor spoke about what helps her feel grounded when she is away from films, red carpets and brand commitments. For Katrina, spending time with family and friends is an important part of maintaining that balance. Having downtime with your family and friends always helps you find your centre. For me, I have to discipline myself to switch off sometimes. Its ingrained in me to constantly be working and creating something, whether with films or with Kay Beauty, so learning to have moments where you disconnect is important to recharge and reset, she said. Katrina further stressed the importance of creating moments of quiet in an increasingly digital world. In todays fast-paced world where there is limitless information and entertainment available through digital mediums, creating moments of stillness and quiet for the mind to be calm is important, she added. Katrina Kaif on how motherhood changed her routine Katrina also revealed that her skin became more sensitive after pregnancy, prompting her to become more careful about the products she used. Post-pregnancy, my skin became even more sensitive, so it was a really tricky time because I had to understand what products were working for me. I found myself looking for products that felt soothing, calming and restorative, she said. Katrinas Kay Beauty has grown into a major name in the industry in the last seven years after its launch. The brand now has nearly three million customers and crossed Rs 380 crore in GMV Gross Merchandise Value in FY2026, according to Nykaas latest annual reporting. Katrina Kaif says her definition of beauty has changed Reflecting on how her beauty standards have changed since she began her modelling and acting career, Katrina said she no longer sees looking her best as simply being about appearance. Its changed a lot. When I started out early through my modelling and acting career, there were a lot of stereotypes about what the beauty standards were. Now for me, looking my best is really about feeling my best, and that comes from taking care of myself as a whole, she said. The actor also listed several lifestyle habits that she believes make a difference to how she feels and how her skin behaves. A healthy diet, keeping the inflammation in your body under control, staying active, meditation, a phone-free daily hour of your morning and getting natural light first thing in the morning. It all makes a huge difference to how I feel, and ultimately how my skin behaves. I think when you feel healthy, that confidence naturally reflects on the outside. articleTitle: Who is Petal Gahlot? Indian diplomat hits back at Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif at UN
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India-Pakistan
description: Indian diplomat Petal Gahlot delivered New Delhi's Right of Reply at the UN for the second year running, tearing into Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif over terrorism, Kashmir and Trump's "intervention" claim.
body_raw: Petal Gahlot, First Secretary at Indias Permanent Mission to the United Nations in New York, has delivered Indias Right of Reply to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif at the UN General Assembly for the second consecutive year. Her latest response followed Sharifs remarks on Jammu and Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty. Sharif warned that any attempt by India to stop, impede or divert Pakistans share of the Indus waters would be treated as an act of war. Gahlot rejected Pakistans references to Jammu and Kashmir, criticised what she described as the Pakistani militarys dominance of the countrys political system and warned that continued cross-border terrorism would have consequences. Who is Petal Gahlot? Gahlot is a career Indian Foreign Service officer and currently serves as First Secretary at Indias Permanent Mission to the United Nations in New York. The missions April 2026 staff list identifies her as a First Secretary. She joined the mission in July 2023. Before that, she served as an Under Secretary in the Ministry of External Affairs Europe West Division from June 2020 to July 2023. Gahlot also served as an adviser in the Office of the President of the UN General Assembly during September 2024-September 2025. The UNs PGA79 handover report lists her as an SDAdviser from India. Exercising its right to reply, Indian diplomat Petal Gahlot said that terrorism continues to be at the core of Pakistans foreign policy. PTIFile Photo She studied Political Science, Sociology and French Literature at St Xaviers College, Mumbai, where she was part of the colleges Indian Music Group, Malhar. She later completed a masters in Political Science at Lady Shri Ram College for Women in Delhi and a masters in Language Interpretation and Translation at the Middlebury Institute of International Studies at Monterey. What did Gahlot say to Pakistan this time? Gahlot exercised Indias Right of Reply after Sharifs UNGA address. Responding to Sharifs references to Jammu and Kashmir, she said, This is an integral and inalienable part of my country and will always remain so. She then turned to Pakistans political system, describing it as a regime of the army, by the army, and for the army. Their puppets may come and go, but let us have no illusion about who calls the shots, she said. Gahlot also referred to what she described as a security cordon around Pakistans capital and criticised Sharifs remarks on democracy and human rights. WATCH New York First Secretary in Indias Permanent Mission to the UN, Petal Gahlot says, References were made to the Indian Union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. This is an integral and inalienable part of my country and will always remain so. But if we must talk about. pic.twitter.comsHVeKYPrVc- ANI ANI September 26, 2026 Why did she mention Pakistans 27th Amendment? Gahlot referred to Pakistans 27th Constitutional Amendment while questioning the militarys role in the countrys political system. The amendment, approved in November 2025, expanded the powers of army chief Asim Munir, who was elevated to the post of Chief of Defence Forces. Under the changes, he retains his rank after completing his term and receives legal immunity for life. Gahlot cited the provision as part of her argument about the militarys continuing influence over Pakistans political system. She also invoked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, pointing to the fact that Osama bin Laden was found living in Abbottabad, near Pakistans premier military academy. What did she say about Kashmir? Gahlot rejected Sharifs references to Jammu and Kashmir and reiterated Indias position that the territory is an integral and inalienable part of the country. She then turned attention to Pakistan-administered Jammu and Kashmir. If we must talk about Kashmir, let us turn our attention to the Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir. Ask the people of Rawalkot about the wanton killings, the brutal violence and the denial of basic rights that they have long experienced, she said. The remarks were Gahlots characterisation of the situation in Pakistan-administered Kashmir. WATCH New York First Secretary in Indias Permanent Mission to the UN, Petal Gahlot says, At the heart of the issue is the long-standing practice of cross-border terrorism by Pakistan. We demonstrated last year that terrorists will have nowhere to run and nowhere to hide.. pic.twitter.comAW75mY3ulj- ANI ANI September 26, 2026 What did Gahlot say about terrorism? Gahlot described cross-border terrorism as central to Indias dispute with Pakistan. At the heart of the issue is the long-standing practice of cross-border terrorism by Pakistan, she said. We demonstrated last year that terrorists will have nowhere to run and nowhere to hide. Our right to defend ourselves against terrorism will be exercised and continued. Terrorism by Pakistan will have consequences, she added. She invoked Operation Sindoor, Indias May 2025 military operation following the Pahalgam terror attack, which New Delhi said targeted terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-administered Kashmir. Gahlot also criticised Sharifs remarks on religious tolerance, pointing to what she described as Pakistans treatment of minorities and its blasphemy laws. She concluded by accusing Pakistan of repeatedly making what she described as false claims at the UN. Reiterating falsehoods year after year does not make them true, she said. What did Gahlot say to Sharif at the UN in 2025? Gahlot had delivered Indias Right of Reply after Sharifs UNGA address in September 2025 as well. Sharif had described Operation Sindoor as unprovoked aggression by India and credited then-US President Donald Trump with helping prevent a wider conflict. India rejected that account. Gahlot called Sharifs speech absurd theatrics and accused him of glorifying terrorism. No degree of drama and no level of lies can conceal the facts, she told the General Assembly. She also accused Pakistan of shielding The Resistance Front from responsibility for the Pahalgam attack and referred to Pakistans history involving Osama bin Laden. Those were assertions made by Gahlot as part of Indias Right of Reply. Gahlot also said Pakistans armed forces had pleaded for a cessation of fighting after Indian strikes hit Pakistani airbases during Operation Sindoor. She rejected third-party mediation and reiterated Indias position that outstanding issues between India and Pakistan should be addressed bilaterally. And in a direct message to Sharif, she said that if Pakistan was genuinely seeking peace, it should immediately shut down all terrorist camps and hand over to us the terrorists wanted in India. Gahlots latest intervention therefore marks the second consecutive year in which she has delivered Indias direct response to Sharifs UN General Assembly address. With inputs from PTI

articleTitle: Canadian vlogger’s post prompts footpath repair in Bengaluru’s Indiranagar
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bengaluru footpath viral video Canadian vlogger
description: While Caleb Friesen's video garnered more than 2.1 million views, the Lokayukta took up a case suo motu and directed its police officers to visit the place.
body_raw: A day after a Canadian vloggers video on the poor condition of a footpath in Bengalurus busy Indiranagar went viral and the Lokayukta took cognisance of it, the civic authorities swung into action to repair the footpath on Sarturday. Vlogger Caleb Friesen posted a video on Friday highlighting that the damaged footpath on 12th Main Road inconvenienced pedestrians. Such footpaths would be totally unacceptable in any other country, he added. On Instagram, he posted, Indiranagar shouldnt be like this. The footpaths should be walkable, safe, pedestrian-friendly, impressive, and a reflection of all the innovation that happens in the city. Instead, theyre a mess. 12th Main in Indiranagar features rubble to rival a conflict zone, holes so big they look extraterrestrial, slabs that seem like they could give way at any moment, and trees that double as dustbins. Why are the footpaths at the centre of Indias tech ecosystem so pathetic? Why doesnt Bengaluru seem to care about its reputation both locally in India and internationally? I dont have answers to these questions. All I know is what I see, and what I experience as a pedestrian any time Im in the city. I think its high time for a footpath upgrade in Bengaluru. Something bigger and more comprehensive than the city has ever seen in all its centuries of existence. Something that Bengaluru can be proud of. Something that sets an example for the rest of the country. I do wonder if the city will rise to this challenge, or continue to be a national and international pedestrian infrastructure embarrassment the way that it is currently. Lets see. While the video garnered more than 2.1 million views, the Lokayukta took up a case suo motu and directed its police officers to visit the place. The officials found that construction debris had been lying there for three days. Lokayukta warning for engineers Later, the Lokayukta issued directions for the chief engineer of Bengaluru Central City Corporation and other engineers concerned. The officials informed the Lokayukta that they initiated action on Saturday evening, but not against the person who put construction debris on the footpath obstructing the road. The Lokayukta was not satisfied with the response and stated, This clearly shows that, despite this matter being taken very seriously by this authority and the case regarding waste disposal in the city in different zones is being monitored intensively for the last more than 2 years, the concerned officials of the Bengaluru Central City Corporation, are showing such apathy. Therefore, all the engineers are hereby cautioned and instructed to ensure that no such incident occurs or recurs again. This shall be treated as a final warning before initiating any action against them personally for their dereliction and resultant maladministration. The Lokayukta also directed its police team to carry out random inspections of the area under the Bengaluru Central City Corporation and report any such lapses before September 9. Voting not paying taxes not enough Vlogger Caleb Friesen later posted another video on Instagram and said, So glad to see the rapid response from GBA Like so many in the comments, I too wish that the city authorities were more proactive instead of reactive fixing things before anyone needs to complain. That said, I commend their effort and the ongoing work theyre doing to fix up the problematic spots. Also I have said this before and will continue to say it my skin colournationality plays a role insofar as it acts as masala, helping my content to go viral. But anyone can create their own personal masala as a creator Baadal Nanjundaswamy dressed up as an astronaut to highlight moon crater-like potholes. Residents of Cox Town organised a pothole pooja to raise awareness. Anyone can complain creatively to get things done - very few people do though. They believe that if they pay taxes and vote, thats enough. It isnt. If you want positive change to happen, you need to, 1. Make it known that youre not satisfied with the status quo in a respectful, peaceful way, and 2. Do whatever is within your power to make a positive change. Virendra Suryawanshi placed many calls before and while this video went live, and has been working alongside GBA. Arun Pai mobilises volunteers to beautify spaces and discourage further neglect and degradation. Please think about how you the reader of this comment can contribute to positive change. India isnt going to improve on its own.

articleTitle: Oracle layoffs 2026: Company cuts 546 cloud workers jobs in US as AI spending rises
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Oracle layoff, oracle AI,
description: Oracle's Cloud Infrastructure revenue jumped 121%, but hundreds of workers were cut as the company shifts billions towards cloud and AI infrastructure.
body_raw: Oracle has terminated 546 employees in its America Cloud Infrastructure organisation, Business Insider reported, citing a document. The latest developments also show how jobs are being cut inside a business despite it seeing double revenue, even as the company dramatically increases spending on cloud and Artificial Intelligence infrastructure. The 546 workers represented about 7.6 per cent of the 7,185 employees listed in the document. Software developers, programme managers, infrastructure engineers and data-centre support workers were among those affected. Oracle has not disclosed the total number of employees affected by its latest round of layoffs. Developers, managers among those affected The document, obtained by Business Insider, lists the job titles and ages of employees affected in Oracles America Cloud Infrastructure organisation. Business Insider said the document included employees eligible for severance benefits but could not determine whether it represented everyone laid off from the organisation. Oracle did not respond to the publications request for comment. Software Developer III was the single job title with the largest number of layoffs, with 57 positions listed. Across all levels, software developers accounted for about 17 per cent of the roles cut, Business Insiders analysis found. Programme manager IV and principal core infrastructure engineer were also among the most affected roles. Management roles were also heavily represented. Business Insider counted 128 positions containing the word manager, or about 23 per cent of the listed cuts. Programme manager positions alone accounted for 61 terminations. Oracles data-centre support services division, which handles maintenance and technical support, had 41 employees included in the document. They included the divisions vice president and two senior directors. The report also found that a majority of the employees listed were over 40, while about 16 per cent were aged 60 or older. Oracle said the information was provided to comply with federal age-discrimination laws. The age distribution, by itself, does not establish that age was a factor in the layoffs. Oracles cloud business is growing rapidly The layoffs are notable because they come inside one of Oracles fastest-growing businesses. Oracle reported 7.4 billion in Cloud Infrastructure revenue in its first quarter of fiscal 2027, up 121 per cent from a year earlier. Total cloud revenue rose 62 per cent to 11.6 billion. That means the latest cuts are not simply happening in a shrinking cloud operation. They are taking place as Oracle expands its infrastructure business rapidly and invests heavily in the capacity required to serve cloud and AI customers. Spending is moving sharply towards infrastructure Oracles capital spending has risen dramatically alongside that growth. The company reported 28.5 billion in capital expenditure for the quarter ended August 31, compared with 8.5 billion in the same quarter a year earlier. Oracle has maintained its fiscal 2027 capital expenditure forecast at 90 billion-95 billion. The spending includes servers, networking equipment and data-centre-related assets. Oracle has been expanding its infrastructure capacity as demand for cloud and AI services grows. Oracles restructuring plan In its latest regulatory filing, Oracle said its 2026 restructuring plan was designed to improve operational efficiency and included the adoption and integration of artificial intelligence technologies across certain functions and other operational activities. The company also said some savings from the restructuring were being offset by investments in resources and geographies supporting its cloud offerings, including its second-generation cloud infrastructure. That provides evidence of an AI-related restructuring strategy. It does not, however, establish that AI directly replaced the 546 workers listed in the Business Insider document. CFO I really, really dont like doing more with less The latest layoffs came a day before new Oracle Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson addressed employees at her first companywide meeting. Maxson said the companys approach was not simply to ask employees to do more work with fewer resources. I dont mean doing more with less, which is a phrase that I really, really dont like. According to Business Insider, which reviewed a recording of the meeting, Maxson said Oracle wanted employees to simplify processes that did not help customers and make clearer choices about where resources would have the greatest impact. The roughly hour-long town hall did not directly address the layoffs. Executives instead focused on growth, customer demand and opportunities created by artificial intelligence. Oracle co-CEO Mike Sicilia told employees, Id ask you to keep asking a very simple question How does the work that Im doing help deliver a better outcome for a customer? Sicilia also acknowledged the changes taking place inside and outside the company, saying that how employees work together and support customers and one another would matter. What about Oracles India workforce? The latest US figures are relevant to India because Oracle has a substantial workforce in the country, including product engineering, development and support operations. But Oracle has not disclosed how many Indian employees were affected by the latest round. Indian employees and their families have also shared accounts of the layoffs on social media. The Indian Express, citing PTI, earlier reported on a LinkedIn post by Pooja Sahu, whose husband Sourabh was among those affected after 12 years at Oracle. She described him working through holidays, birthdays and family occasions and said he had even logged in from a hospital while she underwent surgery. Other Oracle employees in India have also turned to LinkedIn seeking referrals and new opportunities.

articleTitle: What does the Centre’s new mining law say and why are states opposing it?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A coal mine in Jharkhand. (Wikimedia Commons)
description: The Odisha Assembly has seen Opposition protests for days over the Centre's mining law that limits states' powers to tax mines.
body_raw: For four days now, the Odisha Assembly has seen disruptions over the amended mines law, passed by Parliament in August, that seeks to set a uniform national tax framework for major minerals and limit state powers to levy taxes on mining lands. On Friday, the Opposition BJD and Congress MLAs, sporting black scarves, raised slogans in the House demanding the repeal of the Mines and Minerals Development and Regulation Act, alleging that it snatches the rights of mineral-rich states. What does the law say? Why has it triggered a storm in states, such as Odisha, whose economies are deeply intertwined with mining? We explain What does the new mining law say? In August, Parliament passed the Mines and Minerals Development and Regulation Amendment Act, 2026. The amendments seek to restrict states from imposing specified levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing land. The law will also extinguish unpaid or unrecovered dues arising from such levies imposed before it comes into force, with some estimates putting the value of such outstanding dues across the mining sector at around Rs 2 lakh crore. According to the government, the amendments were needed because excessive state-level levies could raise the cost of key minerals, feeding into inflation and infrastructure costs. So whats the controversy? These amendments override the key financial aspects of a landmark 2024 Supreme Court ruling ruling that opened the door for states to raise additional revenue from mining. The ruling, on July 25, 2024, upheld states exclusive power to tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands. The ruling also waived interest and penalties on tax demands for the period before July 25, 2024, and allowed the payment of such dues to be staggered over 12 years from April 1, 2026. The judgment overruled a 1989 ruling, India Cement Ltd v. State of Tamil Nadu, which had held that royalty was a tax and that states lacked the legislative competence to tax mineral rights, as the subject fell under the Union List. Tamil Nadu and Jharkhand have already imposed such levies , called mineral-bearing land MBL taxes. In Jharkhand, the MBL tax on iron ore was initially set at Rs 100 per tonne and later raised to Rs 400 per tonne. Tamil Nadu has imposed an MBL tax of Rs 160 per tonne on limestone. Karnataka, too, has proposed a similar tax on non-auctioned iron ore mines. The new law would, therefore, lead to a significant revenue shortfall for states. Indeed, the passage of the Act drew sharp opposition from states. Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren has said it could significantly dent the states prospective revenue, while Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan has raised concerns over their implications for Indias federal structure. How much could states lose? The dependence on mineral revenues is particularly significant for mineral-rich states. According to a Comptroller and Auditor General of India report on state finances, states own non-tax revenue stood at Rs 3.3 lakh crore in 2024-25, of which 41 - or Rs 1.36 lakh crore - came from receipts related to mineral and petroleum. While these minerals and petroleum receipts accounted for a mere 3.4 of all states revenue receipts, for mineral-rich states, the proportion was much larger 23 for Odisha, 13 for Jharkhand, and 5 for Chhattisgarh. Jharkhand CM Soren had said mining revenue accounted for approximately 84.9 of the states own non-tax revenue in 2024-25. Soren claimed the Mineral Bearing Land Cess, which the state has been imposing on mining companies, was expected to generate approximately Rs 11,000 crore annually. Meanwhile in Odisha, the BJD alleges that the new law could cost the state Rs 12,000 crore in annual losses and Rs 1 lakh crore in arrears. Prabhat Ranjan, Senior Director at Nexdigm, a global consulting and advisory firm specialising in tax, regulatory, risk, governance, and business advisory, had said the amendments would, in effect, serve as a cost-containment and investment-certainty measure for mining companies, but concerns over potential revenue loss for states cannot be brushed aside. Why the government is backing the law In August, a senior official at the Mines Ministry said that there are around 14 levies in the mineral sector and these levies will continue to be there. All we are saying is all these levies together should not be beyond a certain percentage, a senior ministry official said, adding that this percentage will only be decided after consultation with all the states. B K Bhatia, mining industry expert and former Director General of the Federation of Indian Mineral Industries FIMI, had told The Indian Express in August that the amendments would help prevent states from imposing multiple and excessive levies on mining companies. According to him, while the amendments will help the mining industry by providing greater certainty over the fiscal burden, they are unlikely to result in any material revenue loss for states, as most of these levies have been legally contested for decades, resulting in large amounts of pending dues.

articleTitle: Retired Delhi High Court judge, family lost Rs 3.2 crore in real estate scam
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ML Varma
description: After years of delays, bounced cheques and assurances, retired Delhi High Court judge M L Varma has now approached the police. An FIR has been filed on his complaint
body_raw: Sixteen years ago, Justice M L Varma was going through his morning ritual of reading the newspaper when his eyes fell on an advertisement in a corner. The advertisement carried striking pictures of an upcoming project in Noida Sector 15, said the 84-year-old, who retired in 1991 from the Delhi High Court. It promised a high rental commercial unit. The pictures were so attractive and appealing, it looked like it was absolutely out of the world. They showed a metro station nearby, a very good sector, he added. Interested, he quickly dialled the contact number mentioned in the advertisement. He also nudged a relative to book another unit in the same project. The papers were signed at his office in Delhis Neeti Bagh, and he and his brother-in-law, Naveen Sawhney, paid Rs 3 crore. It is now 2026 and not a single brick has been laid, he said. We have been cheated out of the money. Thirteen, fourteen, fifteen years, and not a brick has been laid there, Justice Varma said. Last month, he filed a complaint at the Hauz Khas police station in Delhi against Aims Sanya Developers Private Limited, and its directors Roop Kishore Madan, Sanjay Thukral and other unknown persons. Police lodged the FIR on September 18 against unknown persons under sections of criminal conspiracy and criminal intent. A senior police officer said the investigation is underway and no arrests have been made till now. There was no response to emails sent to the builder seeking comment. The phone number registered for this project on the RERA website was not reachable. Five years of assurances and delays Varma initially had no plans to take the legal route, hoping instead that the builders would honour their commitments. It seemed like a good investment to make, to be able to earn some money later., said Varma. who enrolled as a lawyer in 1964 and is quasi-retired - he still practises and does arbitrations. The location was good and they had shown such a good picture, the brochure had made it very attractive. It would also have fetched rent, so that would have been a source of income. According to the complaint, the commercial project was to be completed within 36 months, with a grace period of six months, and was to yield high returns on investment for the investors and purchasers. As per the assurances and public advertisements, the construction of the commercial project was to commence in September 2010 and conclude by March 2014, the complaint stated, alleging that the complainants have been cheated of over Rs 3,22,34,640. After the deadline passed, Varma said he made multiple trips to the builders office in Defence Colony. He would be made to wait for hours, he said, while the builder did not show up. A few years ago, they eventually entered into a Memorandum of Understanding MoU. If there was a delay, he was supposed to give assured returns based on what the property would have fetched if it had been rented. He did not. Eventually, some years ago, we entered into an MoU. He gave advance cheques, but the cheques would bounce. That went on for five years, Varma claimed, adding that the accused paid the monthly assured returns intermittently. Eventually, when the builder stopped picking up calls in October 2025, the family decided to approach the police. He the builder induced and tricked us into buying a property which he had no intention, from day zero, of building, claimed Varmas son Satvik, a senior advocate in the Delhi High Court. Property not even demarcated Satvik said he could have understood the delay if construction had at least begun. If he had dug up the land, there could have been reasons such as a National Green Tribunal order or a ban on construction. But. the property is not even demarcated. We dont even know if it has a name now. Earlier, it was called Landmark Towers, then they changed it to Tempean Towers, he said. Varma and his wife, Nita, had persuaded Naveen to invest in the project. Naveen died two years ago after suffering from cancer for a year and a half. We could have used those resources. My father always felt that because of his mistake, my uncle lost his money as well. There was guilt and a moral dilemma, said Satvik. Varma still has the brochure of the property, which runs into multiple pages and contains elaborate maps. He asked in disbelief What could be more dishonest than this? If it can happen to someone who has been a part of the legal system for over 50 years, then what is likely to be the plight of the common man about whose misery one reads every day, who is deprived of their life savings?

articleTitle: India vs Uruguay: Can the Blue Tigers build on lessons from Brazil match?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India's players pose for a group photo before the international friendly soccer match against Brazil in Kolkata, India, Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026. (AP Photo/Bikas Das)
description: India will look to build on the lessons from their Brazil clash when they take on two-time world champions Uruguay in Kolkata, with Khalid Jamil’s side facing another stern South American test.
body_raw: A few fans were loitering around the Salt Lake Stadium ticket counters on Monday, a day ahead of Indias match against Uruguay. The scene was markedly different from before the Brazil match, when the same counters had been largely empty. The much-anticipated Brazil game also failed to sell out, with swathes of empty seats visible during the match. With ticket sales for the Uruguay match also struggling, the All India Football Federation appeared to have taken note. A couple of days before the match, the federation announced that tickets for some blocks had been slashed by 90, with seats that once cost Rs 1,999 coming down to Rs 199. In addition, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that people who had bought tickets for the Lionel Messi GOAT Tour last December but were deprived of seeing their star because of the events organisational chaos would receive free tickets for the India-Uruguay international. Kolkata giants Mohun Bagan, East Bengal as well as Mohammedan FC also announced complimentary tickets for their members and supporters. Since these measures were taken, a lot of stands showed as sold out in the matchs official ticketing app. The Uruguay match was always going to be a harder sell than Brazil. The South American team does not have a so-called superstar in its squad who commands the same recognition among casual Indian football fans. One big name who could perhaps have helped ticket sales was Real Madrid captain Federico Valverde, but he was ruled out ahead of the tour due to injury. That left Uruguay with names such as Darwin Nunez and Ronald Araujo, world-class players in their own right, but not quite as familiar to Indian fans. Their coach, Diego Forln, though, is a much more familiar name to Indians, having played for Mumbai City in the Indian Super League. The 2010 FIFA World Cup Golden Ball winner took over this Uruguay side after their disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign, where they failed to win a single match and were eliminated in the group stage under Marcelo Bielsa. Since then, they have lost to Japan but thrashed South Korea 4-1, with Nunez bagging a brace. Next up is 138th-ranked India, a relatively straightforward match on paper. Forlan, however, did not agree. Theres never an easy game in football. We will try to do our best and enjoy our game tomorrow, he said at the pre-match press conference on Monday. He also had praise for the Blue Tigers, lauding them for their performance against Brazil. You could see some combinations, some long balls, some good players. If you give them time and space, they can damage you, and they can play well. So, you have to respect everybody, he said. While Uruguay are not as unfamiliar an opponent as Brazil, with the two sides having met twice, their last meeting came way back in 2001 and was not an official FIFA friendly. Uruguay remain two-time World Cup winners and the 20th-ranked team in the world. The heady days of Luis Suarez, Forlan and Edinson Cavani may be behind them, but this side in transition still has enough quality to hurt any opposition. Former Liverpool striker Nunez is in good form, while former Barcelona defender Araujo and former Arsenal midfielder Lucas Torreira remain more than capable of holding their own in defence and midfield, respectively. India, meanwhile, want to take lessons from the Brazil game forward and use them against Uruguay. Not conceding an early goal is important. We have to go with the flow, but we are going to play against a good team. One mistake can cost us really badly, so we have to be very careful and not take this match lightly at all. They are a good team, attacking-wise and defensively. They have experienced players and their coach is also one of the best. We have to be careful in all aspects, coach Khalid Jamil said.

articleTitle: Hanuman Ansh team performs aarti at Neem Karoli Baba’s Kainchi Dham, film earns Rs 424 cr
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shobhinaw Satyaa visits Kainchi Dham after the success of Hanuman Ansh.
description: As Hanuman Ansh earned over Rs 424 crore at the worldwide box office, its team including lead actor Shobhinaw Satyaa, visited Kainchi Dham, the spiritual site associated with Neem Karoli Baba.
body_raw: The team of Vishal Chaturvedis blockbuster devotional film Hanuman Ansh has paid a visit to Kainchi Dham in Uttarakhand in order to offer their prayers to Neem Karoli Baba, the revered spiritual guru whose life their film is based on. However, their visit comes a day after the director urged devotees to exercise caution and avoid visiting the site amid reports of overcrowding over the long weekend. Vishal was not a part of the group visiting the holy site. Hanuman Ansh team visits Kainchi Dham The team of Hanuman Ansh - led by actor Shobhinaw Satyaa, who plays Neem Karoli Baba in the biopic - participated in the aarti and paid their respects to the spiritual gurus shrine at Kainchi Dham. Satyaa expressed his gratitude for the visit and also thanked the audience for making their film a super-duper hit, as per ANI. We are missing the rest of the team, especially our director Vishal Chaturvedi. It is because of his hard work that the film got made and reached this level of success. But he has a lot of responsibility at the moment and because of that, he couldnt make it, he told Uttarakhand News. ALSO READ Salman Khan hosts BJP youth leader at Mumbai home Touched by your warmth, simplicity The team of Hanuman Ansh managed to make it to Kainchi Dham despite the swelling crowds reported in the past few days. So much so that Vishal Chaturvedi had to take to his Instagram handle on Sunday to urge devotees to check the situation before heading there. Kainchi Dham is overcrowded, and people have said that this is because of the influence of Hanuman Ansh. If that is the case, and if that is not the case, even then, people should visit there only after knowing the present conditions, he said. It is my humble request that if there is overcrowding, please consider visiting other places. Dont become part of a situation where women and children feel suffocated or get stuck in traffic jams, added the director. He also suggested that in case of overcrowding, the devotees could consider visiting other sites associated with Neem Karoli Baba, like Neem Karoli village and Vrindavan in the neighbouring state of Uttar Pradesh. Over the long weekend, which started with Gandhi Jayanti this past Friday on October 2, more than 35,000 devotees visited Kainchi Dham every day, as opposed to the 25,000 the administration is used to handling. The Nainital administration is now even considering opening an alternate route to ease the pressure, as reported by The Indian Express. Both the pilgrims and the locals use the same road to Kainchi, which also goes up to Mukteshwar, causing a traffic jam for hours, said Nainital District Magistrate Lalit Mohan. He attributed the rush to both the end of the monsoon season - enabling safer travel to the hills - and the release of Hanuman Ansh, which has amassed over Rs 420 crore at the worldwide box office so far. Hanuman Ansh box office collection After 60 days at the domestic box office, Hanuman Ansh has now earned Rs 384.44 crore gross and Rs 325.48 crore net at the domestic box office. Its just Rs 4 crore away from surpassing the domestic box office collection of Anurag Singhs period war drama Border 2, starring Sunny Deol and Varun Dhawan, post which itd become the second highest grossing Indian film of 2026 after Aditya Dhars spy thriller Dhurandhar 2 The Revenge, starring Ranveer Singh. Ever since its overseas release by Hombale Films on September 11, Hanuman Ansh has collected Rs 39.80 crore at the international box office. The films worldwide collection currently stands at Rs 424 crore. On October 9, Hanuman Anshs dubbed Telugu version will also release in cinemas across India, which is likely to increase the films box office collections. Made on a budget of less than Rs 2 crore, the film has already earned over 212 times globally.

articleTitle: Heart attack symptoms when you’re alone: What to do in the first few minutes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: heart attack
description: If you suspect a heart attack while alone, don't wait for symptoms to worsen. A cardiologist shares the immediate steps to take—and the mistakes to avoid.
body_raw: A suspected heart attack is an emergency, and being alone at home can make the situation more frightening. But the first few minutes are important, and trying to figure out the cause of your symptoms yourself can waste valuable time. Do not wait for the symptoms to become severe. Call emergency medical services immediately, says Dr Parin Sangoi, Consultant Interventional Cardiologist, Wockhardt Hospitals, Mumbai Central. Here is what to do if you are alone and think you could be having a heart attack. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. 1. Call emergency services first Do not wait to see whether the discomfort goes away on its own. Heart attack symptoms can include pressure or heaviness in the chest, but breathlessness, cold sweating, nausea, dizziness or discomfort in the arm, shoulder, back, neck or jaw can also be warning signs, Dr Sangoi says. If you experience symptoms that could indicate a heart attack, call your local emergency medical service immediately. The sooner the blocked artery is treated, the more heart muscle can potentially be saved, he adds. 2. Sit down and rest Once you have called for help, sit down somewhere safe and avoid unnecessary movement. Dr Sangoi recommends keeping your phone with you and, if possible, unlocking the door so emergency responders can enter quickly. Do not drive yourself to the hospital. While waiting for medical help, sit down and rest rather than trying to get yourself there, he says. 3. Dont let medication delay the emergency call If you have medication prescribed for angina, such as nitroglycerin, take it only according to the instructions already given to you by your doctor. Call for help first. Medication should never delay the emergency call, says Dr Sangoi. The aim is not to try to manage a possible heart attack on your own, but to get professional medical care as quickly as possible. 4. What about aspirin? Aspirin can be useful in a suspected heart attack, but it is not suitable for everyone, Dr Sangoi explains. If an emergency operator or doctor advises you to take aspirin, follow their instructions provided you do not have a known aspirin allergy or another contraindication. Getting medical care quickly is the priority, rather than trying to manage the episode at home, he adds. 5. Dont assume its acidity or anxiety One of the biggest mistakes is waiting because you think the discomfort is caused by gas, acidity or anxiety. The most dangerous mistake is assuming that the discomfort is acidity, gas or anxiety and waiting for it to pass, says Dr Sangoi. Heart attack symptoms can vary from person to person, and it isnt possible to reliably distinguish the cause at home. 6. Avoid these common mistakes If you are alone and experiencing possible heart attack symptoms, Dr Sangoi advises against Driving yourself to the hospital Walking around or exercising Taking several medicines on your own Using home remedies to settle the symptoms Spending time searching online to determine whether it is really a heart attack Waiting for symptoms to become severe before seeking help You cannot reliably make that distinction at home, Dr Sangoi says. 7. If you become unresponsive If you become unresponsive and stop breathing normally, CPR and an automated external defibrillator, if available, may be needed, says Dr Sangoi. articleTitle: Plague scare in Russia, tourism season in Goa, and a screening demand from opposition leader
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The tourism season in the coastal state officially commenced last week with the arrival of the first charter flight from Russia’s Yekaterinburg, carrying 162 passengers to Goa.
description: In Goa, which sees a significant number of Russian tourists, the development has sparked concerns.
body_raw: With the death of a 28-year-old laboratory worker in Russias Irkutsk region in Siberia sparking public health concerns about pneumonic plague during Goas tourist season, the states Opposition Leader has called for health screening of all tourists arriving in the coastal state from Russia. This comes as Goas tourist season kicks off, with the first batch of international tourists arriving last week. A woman working at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East died of plague last week. While 200 people who came into contact with her have now been quarantined, Russian authorities claim the worker died on October 2 of pneumonia of an as-yet-unestablished origin, and that there is no risk of an epidemic breaking out. In Goa, which sees a significant number of Russian tourists, the development has sparked concerns. On Wednesday, Congress leader Yuri Alemao, the Leader of Opposition in the Goa Assembly, said the government must immediately introduce precautionary health screening for tourists from Russia. The remarks come a day after the World Health Organization WHO sought more information on the death from Russia, saying that timely, complete and transparent information sharing under the International Health Regulations is essential to clarify conflicting reports and enable an accurate assessment of potential public health risks. I demand surveillance for passengers arriving from Russia, in coordination with Central health authorities. Tourism is vital to Goa, but public health and the safety of Goans must come first. Prevention is always better than crisis management, said Alemao in a post on X. Alemao said the government cannot afford complacency regarding concerns after the death of the laboratory worker in Russia. With regular charter flights now bringing tourists from Russia to Goa, I demand the government immediately introduce precautionary health screening, he said. For his part, Kedar Naik, the Goa governments director of tourism, said the department is yet to receive any advisory from the WHO or any other health organisation regarding the issue. As of now, the tourist season is going well. We are welcoming all the tourists to Goa. There is no concern since we have not received any advisory from the WHO or any other organisation. If the health regulators issue any advisory in this regard, we will look into it and accordingly initiate corrective measures, Naik said. The tourism season in the coastal state officially commenced last week with the arrival of the first charter flight from Russias Yekaterinburg, carrying 162 passengers to Goa. Another charter with 285 passengers from Moscow arrived on October 4. After the arrival of the first charter flight from Russia on September 30, Tourism Minister Rohan Khaunte said the tourism departments approach is to strengthen the traditional source markets such as Russia and the UK, while simultaneously widening Goas international footprint. As connectivity grows, we also want international travellers to discover more of Goa.our heritage, culture, wellness, nature, cuisine, spirituality and the diverse experiences that lie beyond our beaches. Our focus is on building Goa as a better-connected, responsible and year-round global destination, Khaunte had said.

articleTitle: A late surge at Nagoya and a long way to Los Angeles
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A late surge at Nagoya & a long way to Los Angeles
description: India must aspire to increase the gold medal count. China’s is 169, more than double the number won by Asian Games host Japan
body_raw: A shadow of despair hung over the early phase of Indias Asian Games campaign with the gold haul stuck at four for what seemed like ages. But within a week, thanks to a late surge and a few spectacular medals, the national anthem was played 21 times. The total gold count fell from 28 in Hangzhou, and so did the total medal tally, from 107 to 85. However, India finished fourth, the same position as the previous Asiad. The standout performance came from the archery contingent, which humbled the mighty Koreans enroute to multiple gold medals. While compound archery was expected to make a mark, the mixed team winning gold and booking a quota for the LA Olympics was a shot in the arm. A truly world-class performance came from Kumkum Mohod, just 17, who ended the Korean dominance by winning gold in individual recurve - the first-ever Indian male or female to do so at the Asian Games. The womens hockey team won the title after 44 years by beating China in the final. This after reports of infighting and a string of poor results had brought down the team morale. The turnaround after coach Sjoerd Marijne returned to the helm was commendable. The boxers with three gold medals and wrestlers with a haul of two, too, contributed to Indias late climb after athletes from both sports failed to finish atop the podium in the last edition. The comeback story from boxing belonged to Parveen Hooda - stripped of her 2023 bronze medal for an anti-doping whereabouts failure, she bounced back to win gold. On the penultimate day, golfer Pranavi Urs, little known outside the ranks of those who regularly follow the sport, added a surprise continental title. But while India has defied the catastrophic forecasts, there is still a long way to go to catch up with the global superpowers. India must aspire to increase the gold medal count. Chinas is 169, more than double the number won by host Japan. Some of the performances by Indian athletes give them little or no chance at the Olympics two years from now. India didnt win a single gold medal at the 2024 Paris Olympics despite the government pumping in money for training. A repeat show two years from now at Los Angeles will be disappointing.

articleTitle: Review under new rules: 2 Gujarat cadre IAS officers ordered to retire early
articleFeaturedImageAlt: gujarat government, Gujarat cadre IAS officers, Gujarat cadre IAS officers retirement age, Gujarat cadre IAS officers retirement, Ahmedabad news, Gujarat news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Department of Personnel and Training of the Central government has taken the decision after the last 15 years’ service of the two officers was reviewed under the provisions of the new All India Services Pension Rules by a committee headed by the Chief Secretary
body_raw: In a significant development, two IAS officers of Gujarat cadre have been ordered to be prematurely retired from services after reviewing their services in the last 15 years, top sources in the Gujarat government said on Thursday. The two officers have been identified as Gaurav Dahiya and K Rajesh. Rajesh is under suspension since July 2022 whereas Dahiya was posted as Additional Development Commissioner in the state government. A top official in the General Administration Department GAD of the Gujarat government confirmed the development while stating that the Department of Personnel and Training of the Central government has taken the decision after the last 15 years service of the two officers was reviewed under the provisions of the new All India Services Pension Rules by a committee headed by the Chief Secretary. Under the new All Indian Services Pension rules, the performance of an officer is being reviewed after 15-20 years. And a complete review is being taken of the service from the perspective of integrity and morality. The two officers had a lot of issues in this regard and have been ordered to be prematurely retired from October 1, 2026 after their performance was reviewed by a committee headed by the Chief Secretary, a top officer of the GAD said, on the condition of anonymity. Rajesh, a 2011-batch IAS officer of Gujarat cadre, was suspended in July 2022 after the Central Bureau of Investigation CBI booked him for allegedly taking bribes for approving arms licenses, allotting government land and regularising encroachment on government land, among other charges. The charges were related to his tenure as Collector of Surendranagar district. Subsequently, he was also booked by the Enforcement Directorate ED. He was later released on bail. Dahiya, a 2010-batch IAS officer of Gujarat cadre, was suspended in 2019 after facing charges of bigamy, fraud, and criminal intimidation. He was subsequently reinstated in the service.

articleTitle: Sanjay Dutt says his ‘can’t feel peace in India’ remark a ‘scripted conversation’, Shekhar Suman comments
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sanjay Dutt offers a clarification for his India remarks on Shekhar Tonite.
description: Sanjay Dutt offered an explanation for his remarks on Shekhar Tonite, where he confessed that he "doesn't feel peace in India anymore". The actor claimed it was part of a scripted conversation in the form of a satire.
body_raw: Actor Sanjay Dutt ended up inviting the ire of the internet and certain sections of society after his remarks this past weekend on Shekhar Sumans satire show Shekhar Tonite on YouTube. The actor, after confessing he doesnt feel peace in India anymore, went on to deliver a monologue commenting on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and US President Donald Trump in his signature style of iconic character Munna Bhai from Rajkumar Hiranis seminal social comedy franchise. However, Dutt has now offered an explanation. Dutt lives with his family, wife Maanyata Dutt and two children, in Dubai. Sanjay Dutt offers clarification on India remark I want to clarify that it has never been my intention to hurt the feelings of any individual, community, or institution, to insult them, or to disrespect them, wrote Dutt on his X handle on Sunday. He claimed he made those remarks in context of a scripted conversation intended to engage in lighthearted and humorous dialogue. He further explained that his tone was akin to the humour and satire used in the Munna Bhai franchise, particularly the second part, Lage Raho Munna Bhai 2006, which used Gandhigiri, a modern take on Mahatma Gandhi to comment on the current state of society. He claimed that the intention was to convey a message of love, unity, and goodwill. He reiterated that unfortunately, his words were interpreted out of that context. He wrote on X, I would like to clarify that it was never my intention to hurt, offend, or disrespect the sentiments of any individual, community, or institution. My remarks were made in the context of a scripted conversation intended to be light-hearted and humorous. The spirit behind them was similar to the humour and satire seen in films like Munna Bhai, particularly the concept of Gandhigiri, which was intended to convey a message of love, warmth, togetherness, and goodwill. Unfortunately, my words were interpreted outside of that intended context Shekhar Suman defends Sanjay Dutt Hours after Sanjay Dutts clarification, the shows host Shekhar Suman also came out in his defence. Sanjay Dutt has huge respect for our country and fellow countrymen, and what he said was completely innocuous and in a very positive way. He should not be penalised and maligned for what he never said or meant. I know him for years he is a good man who loves his country and has utmost regard for it, Shekhar told NDTV in an interview. What did Sanjay Dutt say on Shekhar Tonite? Before he was asked to deliver a monologue as Indias Prime Minister in the final segment of Shekhar Tonite, Dutt confessed he doesnt feel peace in the country anymore. The people of this country are so lovely. There should be peace here. I cant feel that peace in our country anymore. We Indians are large-hearted people and we are hospitable. We have given so much, and we should always remain that way. I pray to Shiva ji that those days come back soon, he said. Later, he delivered a monologue as Indias PM in the Munna Bhai style. During that performance, he underlined the criticism towards PM Modi that he takes too many foreign trips instead of spending more time with his countrymen. Aap log ekdum tension nahi lene ka. Apun is khushi ko celebrate karne videsh nahi jaane wala hai. Apun idharich rahega, aap sab logon ke beech. Nahi to PM aur janta mein connection kaise banega You people dont have to worry at all. I am not going abroad to celebrate this happiness. I will stay right here, among all of you. Otherwise, how will there be a connection between the PM and the people?, he said. He also indirectly claimed that PM Modi focuses too much on optics and getting his pictures clicked everywhere. Apun ko desh ke liye bahut kuch karne ka mauka mila hai PM banke, toh apun ek aur kaam karega. Jahaan jahaan uska photo laga hai na, apun usko ekdum kam kar dega. Desh ko desh ka photo dikhna chahiye. I have got the opportunity to do a lot for the country as a PM, so I will do one more thing. Wherever the PMs photograph has been put up, I will cut that down. The country should see a picture of the country, added Dutt. He also proposed replacing PM Modis pictures with those of Gandhi, since the Father of Indias non-violent philosophy is what every contemporary leader should be subscribing to in order to make the world a better place. He didnt spare Trump either, referring to him as mamu and offered him a jadoo ki jhappi. Dekho Trump mamu, zyada tante nahi paalne ka. Duniya mein missile waise hi bahut ho gaya hai. Ab thoda pyaar bhi export karne ka. Kahin missile bhejne ka mann kare to pehle guldasta bhejne ka. Kisi ko dhamki dene ka mann kare na to use phone karke ghar bulane ka aur chai peete-peete baat suljhane ka. Trump, dont create so much trouble. There are already enough missiles in the world. Now export a little love too. If you feel like sending a missile somewhere, send a bouquet first. If you feel like threatening someone, call them home and resolve the matter over a cup of tea, said the actor. Lage Raho Munna Bhai revolved around Dutts gangster character who reads up excessively on Gandhi, in order to impress his love interest and radio jockey Vidya Balan, that he ends up hallucinating Gandhi everywhere. That leads to him treading on the non-violence path of Gandhi, offering bouquets instead of threats to his friend-turned-nemesis Lucky Boman Irani. Also Read - So we dont end up in jail Kapil Sharma on why he watches younger comics Produced by Vidhu Vinod Chopra, and co-written by Hirani and Abhijat Joshi, Lage Raho Munna Bhai earned over Rs 120 crore at the worldwide box office. Its the sequel to Hiranis 2003 gangster comedy Munna Bhai MBBS, and also stars Arshad Warsi, Dia Mirza, Saurabh Shukla, Kulbhushan Kharbanda, and Jimmy Shergill among others.

articleTitle: Claude comes to Google Workspace: Here’s how to edit Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Claude for Google Workspace
description: With the new feature, users can easily access Claude by opening a sidebar next to their Google file.
body_raw: Anthropic on Tuesday, October 6, announced an expansion of its Claude AI-powered services into Google Workspace, enabling users to work with the AI chatbot on Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides. It also lets users create and edit Google files directly from their Claude chat window. Claude for Google Workspace has been released in public beta for all paid Claude plans. What is Claude for Google Workspace? With the new feature, users can access Claude by opening a sidebar next to their Google file. This eliminates the need for users to constantly switch between apps or browser tabs when they are working. Once Claude is accessed, it can read the Google Doc, Sheet, or Slide that is open, see which text, cells, or slides have been selected, and make changes directly in the file. Google Docs In Docs, Claude can fix a sentence or restyle a heading in place without changing the formatting. It can also propose edits to larger docs as suggestion cards in the sidebar. Claude can also be used to generate executive summaries and create tables. Google Sheets In Sheets, Claude can write formulas, build pivot tables, and native Sheets charts, and add new tabs. Users can also attach source files and, for instance, ask for a Q3 budget vs. actuals report with a tab for each team and a summary chart. Google Slides In Slides, Claude can build new slides matching the rest of the decks layouts and themes, so they match the rest of the deck. It can also flag elements that overlap or run off the slide, or text thats hard to read. There are two modes under which Claude works with Google files. In the default Ask before edits mode, each change appears as an approval card with a summary and Claude waits for the users approval to make the edit. In Accept all edits mode, Claude works through the task and applies changes without stopping. How to access Google files within Claude When a user signs into their Claude account, the sidebar will have the same models, connectors, and skills they use in Claude. This is helpful for those who, for instance, save a quarterly business review QBR deck as a skill by pulling data from Salesforce and recent call notes from Google Drive. Their team can then build the next deck following the same format and steps. Users also now have in-chat access to Google files. To use this feature, Paste a Google file link or ask for a Google doc, sheet, or deck. On supported setups it will open in a pane beside the users conversation. Claudes access matches a users existing Google sharing permissions, as per Anthropic. How to use Claude for Google Workspace If you are a Claude subscriber and want the AI assistant to work better with your Google files, follow these steps -Install Claude for Google Workspace from the Google Workspace Marketplace, -Open a file and go to Extensions Claude Open Claude. -Admins can deploy it to their domain or selected groups from the Google Admin console. -To edit Google files from Claude, turn on the Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides connectors. -On Team and Enterprise plans, an owner or primary owner needs to enable the connectors first.

articleTitle: Orissa High Court upholds divorce over wife’s cruelty but hikes her alimony to Rs 25 lakh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Orissa High court divorce cruelty alimony rs 25 lakh wife
description: The family court granted the husband’s divorce plea in 2022 on grounds of cruelty by the wife and directed him to pay her Rs 16 lakh as permanent alimony.
body_raw: The Orissa High Court recently confirmed a couples divorce on the ground of cruelty by the wife but increased her permanent alimony from Rs 16 lakh to Rs 25 lakh. The court noted that the couple stopped living together within months of their marriage. It also held that once cruelty by the wife was established, the husbands decision to live separately could not be said to be without reasonable cause. Chief Justice Harish Tandon and Justice Chittaranjan Dash were hearing the appeal filed by the wife challenging the family courts order of May 2022. The family court had allowed the husbands plea to end the marriage and ordered him to pay Rs 16 lakh as permanent alimony. Once the course of matrimonial cruelty established against the appellant wife is taken into account, it cannot be said that the respondent husbands withdrawal from her society was without reasonable cause, the October 1 order read. Started living separately within few months The woman claimed to have married in July 2017 with her estranged husband. It was added that their marriage did not continue for long and the couple have been living separately since February 2017. The husband filed for divorce in 2020, citing cruelty. The wife opposed the plea and later filed an application seeking to resume the marriage. The family court eventually granted the husband a divorce, rejected the wifes plea to resume the marriage and ordered him to pay Rs 16 lakh as permanent alimony. Aggrieved, she filed an appeal before the Orissa High Court challenging the family courts May 2022 order. Arguments The wife, through senior advocate A Mohanty, submitted that the finding of cruelty based on the allegation that the woman was accustomed to a lavish lifestyle could not by itself constitute matrimonial cruelty. He further argued that the serious allegations made by the wife regarding demand of money, physical and mental harassment and other matrimonial misconduct had not been properly appreciated. On the contrary, the man, through advocate A K Sarangi, submitted that the matrimonial relationship had become irretrievably strained within a short period of the marriage. He added that the couple had been living separately since February 2017 and repeated efforts at reconciliation had failed. He also supported the amount awarded towards permanent alimony, based on the income and financial circumstances of the husband. Not on talking terms The high court noted that the marriage had lasted only a few months before the couple stopped living together. It also noted that the wife had admitted that although they had lived together as husband and wife until February 2017, they were not even on talking terms afterwards. The court clarified that differences in financial background, standard of living or lifestyle cannot by themselves amount to matrimonial cruelty. The relevance of these circumstances is only in understanding the actual matrimonial dynamics between the parties, it added. The court upheld the divorce, noting the long period of separation, lack of communication, repeated but unsuccessful efforts at reconciliation, serious allegations exchanged by the couple and the overall course of their relationship. It held that these circumstances amounted to mental cruelty. On alimony, the court considered the husbands income, expenses and liabilities, the wifes professional qualifications and previous employment, as well as her current unemployment. It said the amount needed a reasonable enhancement and increased the total permanent alimony to Rs 25 lakh.

articleTitle: Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami defends SIR, addresses ‘purification’ ritual: ‘Was not against any caste’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uttarakhand CM defends SIR, addresses 'purification' ritual: 'Was not against any caste'
description: The Congress, meanwhile, has continued to attack the state government over both the SIR and the Haldwani incident. It said the party would hold a 'Dalit-Adivasi Self-Respect Meeting' on Tuesday in New Delhi to discuss the ritual and 'continuing violations of laws protecting SCs and STs'.
body_raw: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Sunday defended the Election Commissions Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls, saying its final decisions had been taken unanimously. Addressing the media, Dhami said questions could be raised about the Election Commission, but insisted that they should be based on records and facts. Everyone has the right to raise questions. But questions and allegations should be accompanied by facts. They should be based on the entire institutional record and should be based on truth, he said. He also addressed the purification row, rejecting the Congresss claim that the ritual in Haldwani in August was directed against party president Mallikarjun Kharge or Dalits. The havan that was performed as purification was not against any person, nor was it against any caste, he said. On the SIR issue, Dhami referred to The Indian Express report that said the two Election Commissioners had recorded at least 14 objections on administrative and procedural matters related to the process. He said the Election Commissions official position was that the final orders relating to SIR had been taken unanimously. The conclusion should be drawn only after looking at both these facts together, he said. He also cited the Election Commissions press conference on Saturday, saying that the original SIR order issued on June 24, 2025, as well as subsequent schedules for states and Union Territories, had received the unanimous approval of the commission. Presenting any internal comment or objection directly as a difference of opinion in the final decision of the Commission would not be appropriate, Dhami said. He said the purpose of SIR was not to deprive eligible voters of their rights but to clean and update electoral rolls. He also pointed to measures announced by the Election Commission for voters whose records are unmapped or contain logical discrepancies. Congress attempting to manufacture narrative He accused the Congress of habitually fabricating a narrative to create confusion, only to be exposed soon after. Dhami said the Congress has once again attempted to manufacture a narrative against the Election Commission to mislead the people. On the alleged purification ritual held at Haldwanis Ramlila Maidan on August 11, Dhami said, Tell me before or after the havan, was there any press release, video, statement by anyone, or anything published in a newspaper saying that this ritual was being performed against a person or against a caste? If you have any evidence, bring it to us and we will take action. He said Uttarakhand had a tradition of people from different castes and communities participating together in religious and cultural events. The Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee, meanwhile, has continued to attack the state government over both the SIR process and the Haldwani incident. On September 25, the party held a protest march to the Election Office at the Secretariat and submitted a memorandum addressed to the President, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners. The Congress alleged that the SIR process had raised serious irregularities and procedural discrepancies and said objections had been filed against large numbers of voters. It specifically sought the publication of Assembly-wise and booth-wise details of all Form-7 applications and demanded an investigation into people who had filed unusually large numbers of such applications.
