articleTitle: Between Trump’s US and Xi’s China, the trap India must avoid
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Xi trump
description: A seat at the global high table means protecting our interests, and shaping the future. India must deepen bilateral relationships and thereby forge a value-aligned global community
body_raw: Confronted by global upheavals and cognisant of vulnerabilities, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President have met twice in 2026. The US-China rapprochement will increasingly shape geopolitics, geoeconomics and techno-capitalism. This evolving G2 framework may even restore a semblance of global order. Washington has paused its containment strategy, while Beijing recognises its limitations in dictating geopolitical outcomes. Both understand their shared interest in curbing global disruptions and the costs of economic decoupling. As Chinas report The Great Global Transformation and the Path to US-China Coexistence asserted, China has weathered Americas offensive phase, forced a strategic stalemate and emerged as a near-peer, imposing an inevitable peace. Living between two hegemons carving out rival global blocs poses structural questions for India and the Global South. After all, the Thucydides Trap Xi invoked is about established powers confronting rising ones, and great powers colluding to constrain third powers. Can we independently shape the emerging world order or influence the G2? If we cannot, will the G2 transcend self-interest to privilege systemic stability and a fairer world? This means objectively assessing where we are, and where we should be. A section of the strategic establishment has long championed anchoring Indias future to Washington. This was predicated on the assumption that America would depend on India to contain China. However, the Trump administrations insistence that Asian states shoulder their own defence suggests its acceptance of a Chinese sphere of influence for a temporary modus vivendi. Moreover, the White Houses 2025 National Security Doctrine implies Indias diminished strategic salience, rendering the Philippines and the Squad more valuable than India and the Quad. Washington is also seemingly drawing a Lakshman rekha by circumscribing New Delhis aspirations in the Indian Ocean Region and US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau asserting that India wont be allowed to grow like China. Despite Prime Minister Narendra Modis efforts to court the Republican Partys radical faction, the BJP government has kowtowed to Trumpian diktats, belying its decolonisation and strategic-autonomy rhetoric. It has acquiesced to Washington imposing punishing tariffs and stirring dangerous subcontinental dynamics while attacking our energy sovereignty and shipping. Instead of confronting these, the BJP government has committed to purchasing American goods worth 500 billion, is restructuring Indias AIdigital infrastructure around a US-led stack, and has ignored curbs on Indian immigration. These raise uncomfortable questions - does Washington view India as a sovereign equal, or merely a junior partner serving its interests? Most critically, does this enjoy bipartisan support in Washington? On the other hand, China has violated Indias territorial integrity, weaponised our dependencies the trade deficit has reached 100 billion, strived to forge a unipolar Asia, stymied Indias membership bids for the UNSC and Nuclear Suppliers Group, and empowered Pakistan. These factors have compelled India to strengthen Indo-Pacific partnerships as geopolitical insurance. Faced with converging and competing Sino-American imperatives, India risks drifting into the Thucydides Trap. Unfortunately, the BJP government has mired India in asymmetric relationships and a performative foreign policy that prioritises optics over tangible national interest gains. This is compounded by the BJPs intellectual and strategic inertia, manifested in clumsy navigation of global finance, trade and supply-chain disruptions, failure to foster a business-friendly environment and spark innovation in advanced industries and strategic sectors, and subordination of foreign policy to petty politics and hollowing out of institutions. All these are locking India into semi-peripheral status and constraining us at this historic geopolitical inflection. A seat at the global high table means protecting our interests, and shaping the future. India must deepen bilateral relationships and thereby forge a value-aligned global community. Furthermore, only by recalibrating economic, industrial, and investment policy as instruments of statecraft can we reassert our strategic autonomy. This demands a multi-pronged approach Building a durable industrial base, depoliticising and enhancing governance capabilities, cohesive federal leadership and substantively enhancing the quality of life for all peoples, forging an Indian Dream that hopefully outpaces the American myth. These necessitate mature leadership, a clear strategic vision, institutional coherence and deft global engagement rather than the BJPs ideological, performative and reactionary internationalism. Only then can we reclaim our space in the world, and chart a credible course toward great-power status. Khurshid is former external affairs minister and Deshpande is director, Samruddha Bharat Foundation

articleTitle: Odds back Can Xue, pattern a woman: All about 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nobel Prize in Literature 2026: Composite portrait of three women writers on a dark background: a woman with grey hair in a topknot and dark-rimmed glasses resting her chin on her hand; an older woman with curly grey hair, a pink beaded necklace and a headset microphone; and a woman with shoulder-length dark hair, glasses and a maroon scarf over a white top.
description: Nobel Prize in Literature 2026 will be announced on October 8 at 4.30 pm IST. Can Xue leads the odds; Rushdie at 25/1. Prize money, process and more.
body_raw: Will it be Can Xue, the Chinese writer known for her experimental fiction, perennial favourite Haruki Murakami, or a writer of Indian or South Asian descent? The question, which has occupied literary circles for months, will be answered on October 8, when the Swedish Academy announces the 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature. When and where to watch The Swedish Academy will announce the prize on Thursday, October 8, at 4.30 pm IST 1 pm in Stockholm at the earliest. The announcement will be streamed live on the Nobel Prizes official website and social media channels. Who are the frontrunners According to the British betting site Ladbrokes, Can Xue is the favourite at 101, followed by Haruki Murakami Japan at 141, Gerald Murnane Australia and Thomas Pynchon US at 161, and Cristina Rivera Garza Mexico, Enrique Vila-Matas Spain, Lidia Jorge Portugal, Ludmila Ulitskaya Russia, Margaret Atwood Canada and Michel Houellebecq France at 20 Bookmakers have no inside information, but they are not always wrong. Last years winner, Lszlo Krasznahorkai, fluctuated between 61 and 101 across various betting markets. Who is Can Xue? Deng Xiaohua, who goes by the pen name Can Xue, has appeared on bookmakers lists for years. She was tied with Lszlo Krasznahorkai, who won the 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature, at 101 on Ladbrokes. The 73-year-old author is known for experimental fiction, including dreamlike, stream-of-consciousness prose that defies conventional plot. Her writing has been likened to Franz Kafka and Jorge Luis Borges. Her best-known books in English areThe Last Lover, which won the US Best Translated Book Award in 2015 Love in the New Millennium, which was longlisted for the International Booker in 2019 and I Live in the Slums,which was longlisted in 2021. Is this her year? Since 2018, the prize has alternated between women and men, ending with Krasznahorkai. If that pattern holds, which the Academy is under no obligation to keep, the 2026 winner would be a woman. Patterns over the last decade Over the past decade four of the 10 laureates were women six wrote in a language other than English six were European one was from Asia South Koreas Han Kang, in 2024 none from South Asia Is there an Indian or South Asian contender? This year, the best-placed writers of South Asian origin are Salman Rushdie, 251 One of the worlds most famous writers, Rushdie was the target of a fatwa issued by Irans Ayatollah Khomeini in 1989 over his book, The Satanic Verses. Thirty-three years later, in August 2022, he was stabbed during a speaking engagement in New York. He won the 1981 Booker for Midnights Children, and is credited with bringing magic realism into Indian writing in English. His latest book is The Eleventh Hour 2025, and a documentary on the attack, which left him blind in one eye, was released this year. Michael Ondaatje, 251 With the same odds as Rushdie, Ondaatje was born in Colombo in 1943 and shared the 1992 Booker for The English Patient. He is known for lyrical, fragmented narratives that blend poetry with history. His latest book is a poetry anthology, The Distance of a Shout 2026. Ananda Devi, 401 A Mauritian writer of Indian descent who writes in French. Devi is known for her unsparing portraits of women confined within tradition and her depiction of fractured identities. She won the 2024 Neustadt Prize her latest book is Chronicle of a Lost Kingdom 2026. Amitav Ghosh, 501 Of late, the Kolkata-born author is known for his writings on climate change. He is the author of the Ibis trilogy, beginning with Sea of Poppies, and The Great Derangement. His latest book is Ghost-Eye 2026. Has an Indian ever won? Only once. Rabindranath Tagore won in 1913 and was the first Asian laureate. Two other winners have Indian links Rudyard Kipling, born in Bombay, won in 1907, and V S Naipaul, a Trinidad-born British writer of Indian descent, won in 2001. Does a Booker help? While the Nobel Prize honours a writers whole body of work, the Booker rewards a single novel written in English, and the International Booker rewards a single book translated into English. Even so, the two lists overlap. Five authors-V S Naipaul, Nadine Gordimer, William Golding, J M Coetzee, and Kazuo Ishiguro - who won the Booker Prize, and four who won the International Booker Prize-Alice Munro, Lszlo Krasznahorkai, Han Kang, and Olga Tokarczuk- have won the Nobel Prize. Abdulrazak Gurnah, the 2021 laureate, was shortlisted for the Booker in 1994 for Paradise. Interestingly, Rushdies Midnights Children won the prize in 1981. It was later named the Booker of Bookers in 1993 and the Best of the Booker in 2008 Ondaatjes The English Patient shared the 1992 prize and won the Golden Man Booker in 2018. A Booker is not a guarantee. For instance, Doris Lessing was shortlisted several times without winning, and won the Nobel in 2007. The favourite, Can Xue, was longlisted for the International Booker in 2019 and 2021, while Amitav Ghosh was shortlisted in 2008 for Sea of Poppies. How is the winner chosen? Each September, the Academy invites qualified people to nominate. They include members of the Swedish Academy and similar academies professors of literature and linguistics former laureates heads of national writers organisations Writers cannot nominate themselves. In April, the Nobel Committee picks 1520 preliminary candidates, then narrows them to five in May. The Academys 18 members vote, and whoever gets more than half the votes wins. Will we ever know who was nominated? The Academy publishes no longlist or shortlist, and it doesnt tell nominees they are under consideration. Nomination records are sealed for 50 years, so this years nominations will only open in 2076. Several Indians have been nominated, according to the Nobel archive, including philosopher Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, repeatedly from 1933 to 1962 Sri Aurobindo, in 1943 Bengali novelist Tarashankar Bandyopadhyay, from 1971 to 1973 R K Narayan, from 1974 How much does the winner get? This year, the winner will receive SEK 12 million, about 12 crore, up from SEK 11 million in 2025. The prize will be presented in Stockholm on December 10.

articleTitle: India, Switzerland to strengthen ties in defence, nuclear energy sectors
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India, Switzerland to strengthen ties in defence, nuclear energy sectors
description: After the bilateral meeting with the visiting Swiss President, PM Modi said, “Today, we identified new possibilities for cooperation in military exchanges and defence production. We also reached a consensus on further deepening our collaboration in the field of nuclear energy.”
body_raw: India and Switzerland signed pacts on mobility that will ease granting longer-duration visas and the exchange of young professionals and agreed to strengthen cooperation in defence and nuclear energy sectors, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Swiss President Guy Parmelin on Monday. After the bilateral meeting with the visiting Swiss President, PM Modi said, Today, we identified new possibilities for cooperation in military exchanges and defence production. We also reached a consensus on further deepening our collaboration in the field of nuclear energy. On people-to-people ties, he said that the Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement and the Young Professionals Agreement signed today will open up numerous new opportunities in Switzerland for Indian students, researchers, professionals, and the youth. According to Ministry of External Affairs, the MoU aims to develop migration and mobility cooperation under equal treatment principles, and to prevent and combat irregular migrationhuman exploitationtrafficking in accordance with national laws. It provides for multiple-entry visas for up to 5 years, including stays of up to 6 months on each visit, and renewable 1-year student permits, it said. On the agreement for exchange of young professionals, MEA said that the pact incorporates an exchange of 300 persons annually per country, which may increase to 500, and a timeline of 30 to 90 days for verification of nationalityresidency status, among other provisions. Lauding Swiss President Parmelin, Modi said, I appreciate his commitment to India-Switzerland relations. Last October, with his personal support, we operationalised a historic Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the European Free Trade Association EFTA countries. This is Indias first FTA with any economic bloc in Europe. It is also an ambitious blueprint for investment, innovation, jobs, and shared prosperity. Through this, we aim to realise the goals of attracting 100 billion in investment and creating one million direct jobs in India over the next 15 years. Swiss President Parmelin said, Trade was a key aspect, as my visit marks the first anniversary of the entry into force of the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement between India and the European Free Trade Association. This partnership benefits both sides India gains access to capital, technology transfers, and easier access to markets for high-value-added goods. Switzerland, for its part, benefits from trade with a massive partner experiencing sustained growth-at a time when global trade has become more vulnerable and unpredictable. He said, I am accompanied by a large delegation of high-ranking business leaders, underscoring our commitment to capitalising on the opportunities offered by this trade and economic partnership agreement. To further boost investment, Switzerland hopes to conclude an investment protection agreement soon. In this context, achieving results in discussions on intellectual property protection is equally important, the Swiss President said. In October last year, the Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement TEPA between India and the European Free Trade Association EFTA States of Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, came into force. Modi said, We have taken several important decisions to expand market access for Indian exports to Switzerland and further facilitate investment between the two countries. This will increase Indias exports of agriculture, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and engineering goods to Switzerland. At the same time, we will attract new Swiss investment in key sectors like biotech, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing, and sustainability, he said. Through these initiatives, we will jointly develop trusted supply chains and reliable solutions for the entire world, he added. Modi said, The ropeway in Varanasi, the Jewar Airport in Noida, and railways and tunnelling projects in hilly areas are shining examples of our infrastructure cooperation. An agreement was also inked for collaboration on transport and infrastructure. We invite Swiss infrastructure companies to invest in India on a large scale, and to participate in capacity building, design, and manufacturing, Modi said. The PM said new joint research projects in priority areas such as health, clean energy, and space will be launched soon. He said India-EFTA Prosperity Summit on Wednesday will be an important platform to translate the promise of our trade and investment partnership into concrete outcomes, he said. PM Modi also extended his best wishes to Switzerland for hosting the next edition of the AI Summit next year.

articleTitle: As reservoirs shrink, this Maharashtra district moves to guard remaining water
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Beed reservoir levels water crisis
description: Officials from the revenue department, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board, and the police will check water theft from reservoir backwaters in Beed three times a day.
body_raw: As water levels in reservoirs in Maharashtras Beed have sunk to 16.38 per cent and groundwater levels are falling sharply, the district administration has ordered inspections of waterbodies and stepped up action to protect drinking water sources. Speaking to The Indian Express, District Collector Vivek Johnson said dedicated teams comprising officials from the revenue department, Maharashtra State Electricity Board MSEB, and the police have been formed to check water theft from reservoir backwaters and monitor the situation. The inspections will be conducted three times a day. There are 164 reservoirs across the district, including small, medium, and large projects. We have been facing water theft from certain locations in the backwaters of reservoirs. To check these thefts, we have ordered joint inspections, Johnson said. According to Johnson, the officials have been checking illegal water theft for the last three months. However, it was found that some farmers were reconnecting pump connections even after action was taken against them. As part of the intensified action, the administration has started dismantling electricity distribution points at select locations from where water is being stolen. These transformers are being removed and stored in the MSEB godown, while transformers supplying power to regular connections will remain operational, the collector said. Johnson also directed talathis and gram sevaks to maintain a strict vigil over water theft from small and medium water supply projects. At larger reservoirs, including Majalgaon and Manjara, dedicated teams have been deployed to monitor illegal water lifting, he said. 37 rainfall deficit in Beed The intensified monitoring comes at a time when Beed is facing a significant rain shortfall and declining water availability. Data from the district information office shows that against the expected average rainfall of 566.1 mm till September 30, the district received only 356.6 mm, or about 63 per cent. The rainfall deficit has also translated into a sharp decline in groundwater levels. The average water level recorded in observation wells has fallen to 7.36 metres, which is 4.55 metres deeper than the average level recorded in September over the past five years. A decline in groundwater levels was recorded in all 126 wells surveyed, with Georai tehsil recording the steepest fall of 6.64 metres. Reservoir storage also remains low. Of the 164 projects in the district, usable water storage is at 16.38 per cent. The Majalgaon project has 28.53 per cent storage, while medium projects have 12.49 per cent and minor projects only 5.49 per cent. As many as 32 projects have completely dried up. Currently, the average capacity of all 164 large, medium, and small reservoirs is roughly 16 per cent. Apart from these, there are several minor sources such as open wells, borewells, jackwells and small lakes. Their water availability in the coming months depends on the groundwater table, Johnson said. The administration is therefore already relying on tankers to meet drinking water requirements. As many as 150 tankers are currently supplying water twice a day across the district, Johnson said. 40of water sources acquired As of September 29, wells or borewells had been requisitioned in 28 villages and at 32 other locations. We have acquired 40 per cent of water sources, he said. The pressure on drinking water supplies is particularly evident in Parli Vaijnath, where the municipal council has begun planning for the coming months. We have a population of roughly 1.2 lakh. Considering the current reservoir capacity and evaporation rate, we have planned to supply water once every eight to 10 days to ensure water availability till June 2027. The implementation will start on October 8, Trimbak Kamble, Chief Officer of the Parli Vaijnath Municipal Council, told The Indian Express. Livestock and fodder stock also affected The water shortage is also affecting livestock. Available fodder stocks are expected to last for an average of only 37 days. The situation is particularly critical in Patoda, where stocks are estimated to last 21 days, and Ashti, where they are expected to last 27 days. Parli has the highest availability, with fodder stocks estimated to last around 70 days. The impact of the rainfall deficit has also been felt during the Kharif season. Sowing was completed on 7,87,218 hectares, or 97.31 per cent of the expected 8,08,946 hectares. Soybean sowing exceeded the target at 137.90 per cent, while cotton sowing stood at 78.36 per cent. Preliminary assessments have indicated crop damage of more than 75 per cent across all 11 talukas, with the affected area estimated at around 5.14 lakh hectares. Amid the water and agricultural stress, the district has also received funds for irrigation-related works. A total of Rs 2,341.33 lakh has been sanctioned for three projects in Ashti, Beed, and Georai under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana 2.0. The projects are expected to cover 10,642 hectares. For the administration, however, the immediate challenge remains protecting the limited water available in reservoirs and groundwater sources. We are now making a drought management plan for all villages in the district and mapping their primary and secondary water sources. Around 40 sources are currently being regularly monitored, Johnson said.

articleTitle: Inside Visakhapatnam spying case: Pakistani women operatives lured, blackmailed naval personnel, probe finds
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Inside Visakhapatnam spying case: Pakistani women operatives lured, blackmailed naval personnel, probe finds
description: 2 arrested, 16 under scanner as investigators piece together how Pak-based operatives used social media and WhatsApp to orchestrate honey-trap.
body_raw: Investigators probing allegations of spying in Visakhapatnam claim to have pieced together how intelligence operatives from Pakistan trapped and then blackmailed civilians and navy personnel to gather information about the movement of vessels and submarines. According to investigators, around six months ago, a woman operative allegedly posed as a shipping firm employee and struck up a conversation with Annam Sai Varaprasad, 28, a civilian hired on a contract basis to drive naval officers vehicles at the Visakhapatnam naval base. The woman messaged him on his social media accounts, investigators said, adding that though he was initially suspicious, he allegedly continued the conversation. She told him she was from a neighbouring state. At first, the conversation focused on his personal life where he lived and why he was not married. Then, investigators said, she asked about his work, his salary, and the kind of vehicles he drove. Eventually, the woman allegedly shared sexually explicit content with Varaprasad and promised to visit Visakhapatnam soon to meet him. As the conversation progressed, she allegedly managed to extract information about the officials he drove. From then on, he was threatened that he would be reported to his employers and arrested. Investigators said what followed was blackmail to provide information about the locations of various naval assets, the deployment of officials, etc. The platform for their communication shifted from social media to WhatsApp. However, Varaprasad had basic security clearance and lacked access to observe and report on classified assets, naval ships docking, and submarines arriving or leaving, investigators said. The Andhra Pradesh Polices Counter Intelligence Cell and naval officials monitored him for over a month before his arrest on October 6. Officials are also examining his phone to check if he received payments through cryptocurrency, investigators said. According to investigators, Varaprasad allegedly shared details of a trainee sailor, Pradeep Mukharjee, 31, whom he previously met at the Visakhapatnam base. He too was allegedly trapped by a Pakistan-based intelligence operative, who posed as a medical professional. Threatened with arrest and legal complications after they allegedly exchanged sexually explicit messages, he too shared information about the Vizag and Coimbatore facilities, where he was attending a training course, investigators said. He was allegedly forced to share OTPs to activate WhatsApp accounts of Pakistani operatives, and was threatened with dire consequences on a voice call if he stopped cooperating, investigators said. These WhatsApp numbers were then used to lure and trap at least 16 others, using a similar modus operandi. They targeted employees posted in Kerala, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Goa, Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Chhattisgarh and Bihar, investigators said, and information sought included movement of naval ships and submarines arriving and leaving. Andhra Pradesh Counter-Intelligence Cell officials said that after it was established that Varaprasad and Mukherjea allegedly shared information and helped operatives trap others, they registered a case against them on September 2 and put them under surveillance. On October 1, simultaneous raids at the homes and residences of 18 persons, including 13 naval personnel, were conducted in an operation named Operation Firewall 2026, and 12 teams supported by officials of the anti-terrorist squads of several states, navy intelligence officers, and local police seized phones, electronic devices, and documents. Authorities are investigating the 16 people to determine their level of involvement and have arrested Varaprasad from Visakhapatnam and Mukherjea from Coimbatore.

articleTitle: Telangana CEO orders action against Form 7 misuse to delete eligible voters
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Telangana: BLOs are conducting door-to-door distribution of Enumeration Forms for the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. (Express File Photo)
description: A Telangana poll official has warned of action against those misusing Form-7 to seek deletion of voters from electoral rolls.
body_raw: The Chief Electoral Officer of Telangana, C Sudarshan Reddy, has issued an order to the Commissioner of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, the District Education Officer, Hyderabad, and all collectors and DEOs of districts across the state, asking them to take appropriate action against individuals who submitted Form 7s to falsely delete eligible voters from the electoral rolls during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The CEOs memo, issued on Monday, reads, It has come to the notice of this office that there have been instances of filing bulk applications in Form 7 before the EROs electoral registration officers and it is also alleged that such forms are not genuine. The memo added that officials, including collectors, DEOs and EROs, should take action against the applicants, who have made knowingly false statement or declaration in writing in form 6, 6A, 7 and 8 as per the provisions of section 31 of the Representation of People Act 1950. The memo further states that such action shall be preceded by an inquiry under Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The CEOs instructions come against the backdrop of the Telangana Pradesh Congress Committees TPCC electoral office filing a complaint with the Commissioner of Police, Hyderabad, seeking FIRs over alleged Form 7 misuse. The first alleged instance of bulk Form 7s in Hyderabad surfaced on October 1, 2026, in Musheerabad constituency. Pre-printed applications were allegedly filed by a booth-level agent BLA of the BJP, seeking the deletion of 31 electors, including a Congress BLA and his family members, the Congress claimed. In another case, a pre-printed Form 7 surfaced in Bahadurpura constituency. This, too, was flagged by the TPCC. The third instance brought to the notice of the commissioner was from Goshamahal assembly constituencys booth number 173. In the Goshamahal case, the BLO booth-level officer refused to accept the bulk pre-printed forms, a TPCC leader claimed. The Congress is in power in the state. Speaking to The Indian Express, a BLO who refused to take in pre-printed Form 7s said, I was only doing my duty. I brought it to the notice of the ERO. What is Section 31 Section 31 of Representation of People Act -1950 refers to making false declarations. It reads, If any person makes in connection with-a the preparation, revision or correction of an electoral roll, or b the inclusion or exclusion of any entry in or from an electoral roll,a statement or declaration in writing which is false and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both. Rule 20 of the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 pertains to inquiry into claims and objections. As per the rule, The registration officer shall hold a summary inquiry into every claim or objection in respect of which notice has been given under Rule 19 and shall record his decision thereon. The rule further states, At the hearing, the claimant or, as the case may be, the objector and the person objected to and any other person who, in the opinion of the registration officer, is likely to be of assistance to him, shall be entitled to appear and be heard. The registration officer may in his discretion-require any claimant, objector or person objected to, to appear in person before him b require that the evidence tendered by any person shall be given on oath and administer an oath for the purpose.

articleTitle: Parth Pawar-linked firm’s Rs 300 crore land deal: Why ‘more professional’ probe now?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Parth Pawar land deal: Why High Court queries led to a 'more professional' probe
description: Parth Pawar owns 99% of the firm that bought the Pune land, yet only his 1% partner has been charged. Investigators say there's no evidence against Pawar. But the High Court has some hard questions, starting with whether he gained from the deal.
body_raw: After the Bombay High Court repeatedly asked why Rajya Sabha MP and NCP leader Parth Pawar, son of Deputy Chief Minister Sunetra Pawar, has not been named an accused in the Pune land deal case despite holding a 99 per cent stake in the firm, Maharashtra Director General of Police DGP Sadanand Date has ordered a more professional and detailed investigation. The investigating officer found no evidence of Pawars complicity, and earlier this year a state-appointed committee led by IAS officer Vikas Kharage found no material evidence of direct wrongdoing or criminal liability by him. So why a more professional and detailed investigation now? The Rs 300 crore deal The FIR was registered at Khadak police station and later transferred to the Pune Economic Offences Wing EOW. It is alleged that 40 acres of Mahar Watan land in Mundhwa, near Koregaon Park, leased to the Botanical Survey of India, was illegally sold to Amadea Enterprises LLP in May 2025 without mandatory state approval. The land, reportedly worth around Rs 1,800 crore, was allegedly bought for Rs 300 crore, with a stamp duty waiver of Rs 21 crore. Pawar holds 99 per cent of Amadea and co-accused Digvijay Patil 1 per cent. Chargesheets of January 30 and April 2 named Patil and businessperson Sheetal Tejwani, who allegedly held power of attorney for 272 watandars. The DGP stated it was unambiguously clear that Tejwani conspired with Digvijay Patil and cheated the government by illegally executing a sale deed and underselling the land. What the HC asked On December 10, 2025, hearing Tejwanis bail plea, the court asked if police were protecting Pawar. On September 7, Justice Madhav J Jamdar noted submissions questioning whether Pawar had not been named because he was very highly influential, and sought affidavits from the DGP and the investigating officer IO. On October 1, granting anticipatory bail to suspended Pune City tehsildar Suryakant Yewale, Justice Jamdar questioned the state over serious allegations against Amadea. The states lawyer argued that Amadea was an LLP, not a firm under the Indian Partnership Act, and that Patil had taken decisions based on his independent existence in it. Your stand is that the person who is having 99 shareholding is not responsible and the one who is accused is the person having 1 shareholding, Justice Jamdar said. Is the person who is having 99 share, Mr Parth Pawar, not a beneficiary of this transaction? What the EOW found In his affidavit, the IO, Assistant Police Inspector Dattatraya Mahadeo Waghmare, said bank records, revenue filings and interrogations yielded no evidence for establishing financial complicity of Parth Pawar, and no call records, communications, meetings or instructions linking him to the co-accused. Pawar did not sign or witness the sale deed and gave no authorisation, resolution or power of attorney to Patil or anyone else to buy the land, the IO said. No money passed between Amadea and Tejwani, and no financial trail led to Pawar. Tejwani told investigators she negotiated solely and exclusively with Patil. Under the Limited Liability Partnership Act, 2008, the IO added, Pawar could not be made an accused by holding him vicariously liable. Emphasis on detailed, professional probe However, state DGP Sadanand Date submitted an affidavit after personally perusing case documents and interacting with the Pune CP and the IO. I say that on detailed scrutiny of investigation papers, I found that on certain points, indeed, there is definitely need for more professional and detailed investigation, DGP Date stated, adding that instructions have been issued to the Pune Commissioner of Police CP to ensure comprehensive investigation against each of the named accused and other suspects. Citing sensitivity of the matter and concerns expressed regarding the investigation, the DGP ordered Pune CP to review probe progress weekly and submit a report after six weeks. The DGP office will monitor the probe in a periodical manner and make all necessary efforts to ensure that all available leads are vigorously pursued by Pune CP and the IO.

articleTitle: Tariffs, sanctions becoming policy instruments, sometimes weaponised: P K Mishra
articleFeaturedImageAlt: P K Mishra, Tariffs, sanctions, policy instruments, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, Kautilya Economic Conclave, Trump Tariffs, trump tariff impositions, India-US ties, trade war, us trade war, donald trump, reciprocal tariffs, Trump India trade deal, India US tariff cuts, Trump India tariffs announcement, India US trade agreement, Modi Trump trade talks, India US economic relations, India lowers tariffs for US, US India trade negotiations, Trump Modi tariff deal, India US import export policy, Trump on India tariffs, US India business ties, trade war India US, India trade policy changes, India US tariff reduction, Indian express news, current affairs
description: He said the future will belong to those who can be “steady without being closed, careful without being fearful, and ambitious without being naïve”, and India intends to be such a country.
body_raw: The Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, P K Mishra, on Saturday said tariffs, export controls and other restrictions are increasingly being used not only for conventional commercial objectives but also for strategic purposes, and these instruments of economic policy are sometimes even weaponised. He said the future will belong to those who can be steady without being closed, careful without being fearful, and ambitious without being naive, and India intends to be such a country. Speaking at a session on A World Priced for Risk during the 5th Kautilya Economic Conclave, Mishra said, We are increasingly confronted, not merely with risk, but also with uncertainty. The events of this decade have brought this distinction into sharp focus. We have seen a pandemic disrupting production and mobility across the world, wars disrupting energy and food markets. Shipping routes and geographical chokepoints become sources of economic vulnerability. Export restrictions, sanctions and tariffs become instruments of economic policy, even sometimes they are weaponised. Critical minerals, technologies and even financial infrastructure require a new strategic significance. Discussing risks associated with energy availability, Mishra said, For decades the principal question for an energy importing country or energy importing economy was often price of energy. Today, there is another question - will the energy be available or can it reach us? A disruption in a major shipping route can affect the price of crude oil thousands of kilometres away. Geography has, therefore, become an economic variable.The economic logic of globalisation was built around specialisation - produce where costs are lowest and move the goods efficiently across borders. The logic remains relevant and even powerful, but the experience of the pandemic, geopolitical conflict and more recent disruptions have highlighted another consideration the cost of interruption. A supply chain that is efficient in normal times may be fragile if the single-node supplier or geography becomes unavailable, he said. We are seeing similar development in critical minerals. Lithium, cobalt, rare earths and other minerals are essential to batteries, electronics, renewable energy and advanced manufacturing, but their extraction, processing and refining are highly concentrated geographically. Geography, we thought technology has made it irrelevant, but it has returned to the centre of the table, and it is not only oil, the minerals of energy transition are held in very few hands. For nearly all of them, a single country does most of the refining. So, the clean energy future, which was meant to free us from oil dependence, risks creating new ones, Mishra said. The result is a world in which economic policy and geographical considerations are becoming more closely intertwined. The question before policymakers is therefore not whether globalisation has ended. It has not. The question is how we preserve the gains from openness, while making economies less vulnerable to concentrated and unpredicted shocks. On Indias response to global supply chain shocks in the wake of disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, Mishra said, India is a major energy importer and any prolonged disruption to an important maritime route can affect the economy adversely. Indias response has combined several layers of protection. We have maintained substantial stocks, increased domestic production and ensured that alternative supply routes and suppliers are available. For example, the number of countries from which we import crude oil has increased from 27 to 43, which is very large, he said. He said India has also responded through greater diversification of our external economic relationships. An open economy will always depend on other economies. The objective is not to eliminate that dependence, but to avoid excessive concentration. Indias recent trade policy illustrates this approach. India now has a broader network of trade agreements, including agreements with the UAE, Australia, AIFTA ASEANIndia Free Trade Area and more recently, the United Kingdom, Oman, New Zealand and the European Union. There is one more form of resilience that is perhaps less visible, and that is macroeconomic resilience, he said. I believe the world that is coming will belong to those who can be steady without being closed, careful without being fearful and ambitious without being naive. India intends to be such a country. I hope that together we can help build such a world.

articleTitle: ‘Painful parallel to Nirbhaya case’: Supreme Court takes note of Delhi rapes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court takes cognisance of recent rape cases in Delhi. Directs registration of suo motu case.
description: The Supreme Court also said public spaces cannot be allowed to become "zones of high risk" because of inadequate lighting or poor surveillance.
body_raw: The Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognisance of deeply disturbing news reports of recent rape cases in Delhi-National Capital Region NCR, saying they starkly underline a systemic failure on the part of law enforcement and civil administrative authorities to guarantee basic public safety. Taking note of the alleged rape of a minor in August on a sleeper bus, which travelled nearly 47 km from Greater Noida to Old Delhis Kashmere Gate, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said, One cannot help but draw painful parallels to the 2012 Nirbhaya case, calling into question whether systemic law enforcement mechanisms have made any meaningful progress in the decade since then.The top court referred to the gangrape and assault of a 23-year-old physiotherapy intern in a moving bus in South Delhi on December 16, 2012, which triggered one of the largest spontaneous public protests in India. The woman later died in a hospital in Singapore. The alleged gangrape of a 17year-old at Astha Kunj Park in Southeast Delhi by three men posing as policemen on September 21, and another gangrape-murder case from Northwest Delhi earlier this month were among the other incidents that court flagged during the hearing. The court said the incidents have raised serious concerns regarding the safety and security of public spaces in and around the city and issued a series of directions for examining the broader institutional failures that may have led to the crimes. It also asked the Delhi High Court to assign the mentioned cases to a designated fast-track special court, and to ensure that the trials are concluded expeditiously, preferably within a year. As an interim measure, the top court asked Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar to constitute dedicated police teams for each police district, headed by an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police, to conduct an immediate survey and inspection of vulnerable pockets.drawing up a districtwise vulnerability map and sharing it across adjoining police stations.appropriate patrolling and security arrangements at all identified public parks and vulnerable areas at all times a besides an immediate lighting and CCTV audit, in all public parks and vulnerable zones to eliminate blind spots. The interim measures have to be undertaken within four weeks, said the bench. Referring to the South Delhi park gangrape case, the Supreme Court said, it has also brought to light pre-existing complaints of recurrent sexual harassment faced by students of Lady Shri Ram College for Women, situated in the immediate vicinity of Aastha Kunj Park. Regrettably, these prior grievances failed to serve as a wake-up call for the police or the local administration to rectify institutional security lapses through enhanced patrolling and vigilance before yet another victim fell prey to unscrupulous perpetrators, said the bench. The court said that the right to live with dignity, free from the fear of violence, is an intrinsic facet of the fundamental guarantee of life and personal liberty enshrined under Article 21 of the Constitution. Public spaces, including parks, roads, buses, metro stations, subways, foot bridges, etc. cannot be permitted to become zones of high risk due to grossly inadequate illumination, poor surveillance, lax patrolling, or other preventable administrative deficiencies. Even as statements made by public authorities and elected representatives expressing concern over these incidents are understandable, expressions of concern, devoid of accountability, fall short of answering the larger institutional question, said the court. Expressing solidarity is not the solution to this social evil. What is required is a measurable response, with responsibility and accountability fixed upon the authorities entrusted with prevention of crime, maintenance of public order and protection of vulnerable persons, said the court. The court emphasised that public spaces suffering from inadequate illumination, deficient surveillance, or a lack of visible police patrolling and prompt interventional response mechanisms inevitably expose every citizen to heightened security risks. Where basic measures of public safety remain compromised, no individual, irrespective of age, gender, or sexual identity, can navigate public spaces with a sense of security. The primary obligation of the State and its instrumentalities is to maintain public spaces that are safe, accessible, and secure for all, while remaining particularly attentive to the heightened risks faced by children, women and other sexual minorities, it said. The bench made it clear that the scope of the.suo moto proceedings is not directed at assessing individual criminal culpability, but rather at examining the broader institutional failures that transcend any single case. The primary objective of the present proceedings is to evaluate whether effective systemic, preventive, and monitoring frameworks are currently in place to ensure safety in public spaces across Delhi-NCR, it said. It sought a comprehensive status report from authorities concerned on the measures presently undertaken to ensure adequate safety and security arrangements in public places, including parks, roads, public transport facilities, markets, educational institutions and other areas frequented by women and children, the manner in which the National Database on Sexual Offenders NDSO is presently being utilised by the Delhi Police. and the manner in which the Ministry of Home Affairs is utilising the Investigation Tracking System for Sexual Offences ITSSO, which was stated to have been launched as an online analytical tool for monitoring and tracking time-bound investigation in sexual-offence cases. The court said that the reports submitted shall not be confined to a description of the schemes or infrastructure existing merely on paper but clearly set out.whether it is presently operational the geographical area and population covered the officer or authority responsible for its implementation the volume of complaints, calls, cases or interventions handled during the preceding three years and the average response time, wherever measurable.

articleTitle: Anthropic warns government attitudes may hurt customer ties, IPO prospectus shows
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Anthropic has warned of potential business risks linked to government policies and growing concerns over artificial intelligence.
description: Anthropic has warned that US government actions and views about its AI technology could hurt its business, affecting revenue, customers and partners.
body_raw: Anthropic warned that government attitudes toward the company and its technology could have broader implications for its business, including its relationships with commercial customers and partners, according to the IPO prospectus seen by Reuters. Companies routinely warn that policy changes could affect their business, particularly government contractors. For example, SpaceX said in its IPO filing that maintaining strong relationships with US government agencies is critical to its business and warned that any deterioration in those relationships could materially harm its ability to retain existing business and win new opportunities. Anthropics disclosure appears broader, suggesting that government perceptions of the company and its conduct could extend beyond its direct dealings to affect customers, partners, other commercial relationships - and even civilization. The filing warns that advanced AI could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, an extraordinary warning by a company planning an IPO that could be valued at 2 trillion for the firms capacity to profit from the same technology. The company said revenue from government agency contracts accounts for less than 1 of its annual revenue. The company has become a magnet for concern about the risks carried by the rapid advancement, intense global competition and limited oversight of AI technologies. The broad question of AI safety has come into the public eye recently with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodeis call for the industry to slow its development, following repeated accounts of hacking activity by so-called rogue autonomous AI agents. Amodei met US President Donald Trump last Sunday for dinner as calls for greater regulation of AI have grown. Trump has largely rejected those calls, though the Federal Trade Commission is conducting an industrywide probe of AI firms including Anthropic, Reuters reported on Wednesday. In the prospectus, Anthropic cited several interactions with the US government over the past year as examples of actions that could hurt its business. The filing said that in February the president ordered federal agencies to stop using the companys models and that the US Department of Defense designated Anthropic a supply-chain risk to national security. The company may experience material revenue losses or business disruptions attributable to these events, Anthropic said. Anthropic also said that in June the US Department of Commerce imposed worldwide export restrictions on its Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models, prompting the company to disable the models for all customers to ensure compliance. While the Commerce Department later lifted those restrictions and Anthropic redeployed the models, the company warned that similar actions could occur in the future. Such measures could result in significant reputational harm, including adverse media coverage, public scrutiny, and negative perceptions among existing and prospective customers, partners, employees, and investors, regardless of the ultimate outcome. The company added that selling to government agencies carries additional risks, including changes in the governments view of Anthropic or its technology.

articleTitle: Swades’ Gayatri Oberoi quit films; married to 59th richest Indian with Rs 48,100 cr worth
articleFeaturedImageAlt: shah rukh khan swades co star
description: Shah Rukh Khan's Swades co-star Gayatri Oberoi quit films after the success of the film. Her husband, Vikas Oberoi, is now the 59th richest individual in India.
body_raw: The latest Hurun India Rich List 2026 declared the net worth of some of the wealthiest individuals in India. Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan is the richest Indian actor with a net worth of Rs 10,000 crore but a former co-star of the actor actually has a bigger net worth than him. Gayatri Oberoi ne Joshi, who worked alongside Shah Rukh in Swades, is married to real estate entrepreneur Vikas Oberoi, and as per this years list, Vikas net worth is listed at Rs 48,100 crore, and he is the 59th richest individual in India. Vikas was on the same list last year as well and back then, his wealth was listed at Rs 42,960 crore. At the time, he was the 58th richest individual in India. Gayatri and Vikas 9-storey Juhu home spread across 75,000 sq ft Gayatri and Vikas reside in a nine-floor bungalow that is spread across 75,000 sq ft in the Juhu neighbourhood of Mumbai. The couples home was designed by Italian architect and designer Piero Lissoni. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Architectural Digest India archdigestindia In an earlier chat with Architectural Digest India, Gayatri opened up about her home. The two basement levels are for parking and fitness. There is a separate floor for the gym, spa and a 12-seater cinema. The four floors above that - from ground to the third - are all for entertaining. The area starting from the fourth floor is their private living area. The rooftop has an infinity pool with a view of the Arabian Sea. Gayatri shared that her husband wanted their home to run like a boutique hotel but she hated that analogy. Vikas always said the house should run like a boutique hotel-and initially, I hated that comparison. Its a home, not a hotel But in function, it truly does run that efficiently, she told the publication. The residence also houses art by Ravinder Reddy, MF Husain and Manjit Bawa. Vikas knew Gayatri was the the one Gayatri started her career in the entertainment industry in the late 1990s as a VJ for Channel V. The next year, she participated in Femina Miss India International and went on to represent India at Miss International 2000. Gayatris big break came in 2004 when she landed the lead role opposite Shah Rukh Khan in Ashutosh Gowarikers Swades. In 2005, she married Vikas. While not much is known about their love story, Vikas spoke a bit about her in a chat with Economic Times back in 2014. I had known Gayatri for a long time before we got married. We were just friends, more like acquaintances. Luckily, we kept bumping into each other and I strongly felt she was the one I wanted to spend the rest of my life with, he said. Why Gayatri quit films after Swades success After tying the knot, Gayatri quit films and in a chat with Bollywood Hungama in 2019, she elaborated on that decision. She said that after the success of Swades, she was very selective about the kind of roles she took on. She recalled winning several debut awards for the film as well, but it was right around that time that she met Vikas. I met my husband, Vikas Oberoi, and I was very satisfied with where my career had taken me. And when I met Vikas, I realised that this was something that I wanted more than doing movies and being in Bollywood. Thats why, it was quite easy to give up that thought. I could have continued to work yet be married. But I consciously made that decision because if I am committing to something, I want to give my hundred percent to it. And I always wanted to commit my hundred percent to my marriage, to my family and to my children, she said. Gayatri said that she felt that she had been lucky and had a great opportunity but she wanted to move on to something that was also a part of her dream life, having a wonderful family. I met my husband whos like my soul mate in every way. I guess life sometimes has other plans and better plans, she said. Gayatri and Vikas are parents to two sons - Vihaan and Yuvaan.

articleTitle: Ex-MP Kuldeep Bishnoi’s ‘Sneh Milan’ without BJP flags sets Haryana abuzz
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kuldeep Bishnoi outreach programm
description: While Kuldeep Bishnoi has maintained that he continues to be with the BJP, the events have nevertheless been seen as a show of strength.
body_raw: For the past three months, former MP Kuldeep Bishnoi, younger son of three-time former Haryana chief minister Bhajan Lal, has been on an intensive public outreach across Haryana-but without BJP flags, banners, or other party symbols. Since launching the campaign from Sirsa on July 21, Bishnoi has held gatherings in parts of Panipat, Kurukshetra, Jind, Kaithal, and Dadri districts, drawing political attention and triggering speculation about his next move, particularly after he was not nominated to Rajya Sabha a few months ago. While Bishnoi has maintained that he continues to be with the BJP, the events have nevertheless been seen as a show of strength. Bishnois gatherings have been named Sneh Milan. The manner in which these programmes are being held across districts, with old political associates and supporters seen alongside him, has raised questions about their political significance. There are no party flags on the stage, no formal political rally format, and no indication of any major political announcement. A close associate said he was reaching out to old contacts and supporters separately from the BJPs formal programmes. Old political relationships associated with the Bhajan Lal family, former associates and people from various social groups are being seen at these gatherings. It would not be appropriate at present to view these programmes as a sign of his distance from the BJP, the aide said. Bishnoi himself has given no indication of breaking away from the BJP and has reiterated that he remains with the party. Addressing his supporters in Dadri on Friday, Bishnoi said, Struggle has taught me not to bow down, but to keep moving forward. With your faith and support by my side, my courage is high, and my resolve is strong. Dadri has given this journey new energy today now the caravan will move forward. Expressing gratitude to his supporters for the gathering, Bishnoi said he viewed the honour as a reflection of the peoples continued support and blessings throughout his long political journey, including during difficult times. He said, In politics, I have seen both good times and difficult times. Circumstances changed, paths changed, but I never stopped trying to remain honest to my principles, my colleagues and my relationship with the people. I never let go of the hands of my people, and you too never withdrew your hand of affection from my shoulder. Nothing anti-party about Bishnois programmes BJP However, BJP leaders point out that Bishnoi currently holds no post in the party organisation, while his son and former MLA Bhavya Bishnoi is the partys state vice-president. Haryana BJP media head Bhupeshwar Dayal said, All political programmes being done by Bhavya are held under the banner of the BJP. Kuldeep Bishnoi is a very senior leader who is doing a lot of social activities. There is in no way anything anti-party about it, as social outreach is the right of any political leader. The ongoing outreach comes a few months after Kuldeep Bishnoi expressed anger over remarks made by BJP Rajya Sabha MP Rekha Sharma about Bhajan Lal on April 25. Her remarks drew a sharp reaction from Bishnoi, his supporters and members of the Bishnoi community, who sought an apology. Sharma expressed regret, saying she would withdraw her statement if it had caused pain to Bhajan Lals family and supporters. In an apparent effort to ease tensions, Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini visited Adampur in Hisar district in June to attend Bhajan Lals birth anniversary programme. Four-time MLA and two-time MP Bishnoi has also been a prominent Congress leader, a four-time MLA, and a two-time Lok Sabha MP. He eventually fell out with the Congress leadership after he was not considered for the post of the state party chief and joined the BJP in 2022 after resigning as an MLA. Later that year, his son Bhavya was elected MLA from Adampur on a BJP ticket but, contrary to expectations among their supporters, was not inducted into the Cabinet. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP chose Ranjit Singh Chautala over Kuldeep Bishnoi for the Hisar seat. Later that year, Bhavya lost the Adampur Assembly election.

articleTitle: Tata Trusts, Tata Sons board unaware of N Chandrasekaran family’s TVS link
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The tie-up has followed the September 17, 2026 board meeting of Tata Sons where Srinivasan supported the decision to reappoint Chandrasekaran for another five years
description: Chandra told son not to do any business with Tata Group companies, had updated companies about the venture… it's the son’s private venture, says Tata official.
body_raw: Tata Trusts and Tata Sons board were kept in the dark about the business arrangement between the family of Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran and TVS Motor Company where Venu Srinivasan - also a director of the Tata Sons - is Chairman Emeritus, and part of the promoter family, according to a Tata Trusts spokesperson. Tata Trusts has decided to act appropriately after evaluating the nature of their institutional response to this development. The tie-up has followed the September 17, 2026 board meeting of Tata Sons where Srinivasan supported the decision to reappoint Chandrasekaran for another five years despite opposition from Trusts Chairman Noel Tata. This has raised the issue of conflict of interest in some quarters. The Tata Trusts can confirm that no disclosures were made to the Trustees with regard to Hanno One WarehousingHanno Infra and TVS Motor by Srinivasan, said a Tata Trusts spokesperson. Tata Trusts indicated that Tata Sons board was also not informed about the decision. We are given to understand that no such disclosures were made to the board of Tata Sons either but since the Trusts do not have independent access to proceedings of the board, apart from their Nominee Directors having access to board papers, we cannot definitively comment on this, Tata Trusts said. If the allegations are proven to be true, the Trusts will evaluate the nature of their institutional response to these and act appropriately. We have nothing further to add at this stage, it said. However, a top-level source in the Tata Group, who is close to Chandrasekaran, said it was a private venture by his Chandrasekaran son who returned from the US. It has nothing to do with the Tata group. In fact, Chandrasekaran had told his son not to do any business with Tata group companies, he said. Trustees of Tata Trusts are not required to disclose their business arrangements to Tata Trusts. In fact, Chandrasekaran had disclosed this matter to various Tata Group companies, the Tata group source said, indicating that Srinivasan was not required to inform the Tata Trusts about his businesses. In March 2025, Hanno One Warehousing Pvt Ltd was incorporated with the Tata Sons Chairman Chandrasekarans wife Lalitha Chandrasekaran and his son, Pranav Chandrasekaran, as its directors. The company entered into a land-lease arrangement with TVS Motor within months of its incorporation. In June 2025, Hanno One took on lease approximately 17 acres of land belonging to TVS Motor at Uddanapalli village in Krishnagiri district of Tamil Nadu. The land was earmarked for the development of a large warehousing facility. The cost of construction and development stood at around Rs 106.3 crore.
