articleTitle: At centre of Delhi ‘slapgate’ row, who is minister Parvesh Verma
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Verma inspects a road at Tilak Nagar area, in New Delhi. Verma landed in a controversy on Sunday after a video showing him allegedly slapping a man recording a road inspection in Tilak Nagar circulated on social media.
description: BJP's Jat face in Delhi, Parvesh Sahib Singh Verma defeated Arvind Kejriwal in 2025 Assembly polls, and was then seen as a key CM contender.
body_raw: Delhi PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh Verma on Sunday grabbed headlines after a video clip circulated on social media, which showed him purportedly slapping a youth during his inspection of road repair work in Vikaspuri area in west Delhi. Sharing the video clip on X, AAP MLA from Tilak Nagar, Jarnail Singh, alleged He Parvesh had come to inspect the road, but upon seeing scam after scam being exposed, he lost his cool and ended up indulging in thuggery goondagardi with my colleague who was recording the video. Parvesh Sahib Singh Verma, too, shared a video on X later in which he alleged that AAP workers had abused his family. Listen to the full truth behind todays incident. but what happened should not have happened, he said in his post. Verma, who defeated AAP supremo and three-time Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal in his New Delhi seat in the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections, was inducted as a minister in the BJP Cabinet headed by CM Rekha Gupta. While Verma, a Jat leader, has been a front-runner in the chief ministerial race, the BJP leadership finally named Rekha Gupta, first-time MLA from Shalimar Bagh, for the top job. Throughout Vermas 2025 campaign, his supporters pitched him as a CM candidate. The party will decide. If they want to make me CM, I will heed their demands, he had then told The Indian Express. New Delhi is the seat from where Kejriwal had defeated late Congress stalwart and ex-CM Sheila Dikshit in 2013, ending her 15-year rule. The seat, which this time also saw Sheilas son Sandeep Dikshit in the fray as a Congress candidate he finished a distant third, has always been a barometer of the popularity of the incumbent government in Delhi. Delhi minister Pravesh Verma slaps man after altercation over road quality Read pic.twitter.comFRq7veQYJj - The Indian Express IndianExpress September 27, 2026 With 23 candidates including Kejriwal, Verma and Sandeep Dikshit, the contest in the New Delhi seat was intense. Verma finally pulled off the biggest upset of the Delhi polls, defeating Kejriwal by 4,089 votes, even as the BJP stormed to power in the national capital after 27 years, winning 48 out of 70 seats as against the AAPs 22. Verma, 47, made several promises during his poll campaign-making Yamuna a riverfront similar to the one at Sabarmati, giving houses to slum dwellers and providing them infrastructure, and ensuring 50,000 government jobs, flyovers, and a pollution-free Delhi. The two-time West Delhi MP and one-time Mehrauli MLA, who has been with the BJP for close to three decades, kickstarted his campaign in mid-January. While the AAP made allegations of voter list tampering, voter suppression and distribution of freebies by the BJP in violation of the Model Code of Conduct, Verma consistently targeted Kejriwal. A key part of his campaign was built around allegations of massive expenditure and irregularities in the construction and renovation of the bungalow at 6, Flagstaff Road at Civil Lines, the official residence of Kejriwal during his tenure as the CM, which was dubbed Sheesh Mahal by the BJP. A model of the Sheesh Mahal was kept outside Vermas house during his campaign. In his rallies, Verma targeted the AAP chief, saying Kejriwal has done nothing for Delhi in the last 11 years. While you all were dying of Covid, Kejriwal was busy building a Sheesh Mahal for himself. He also questioned the efficacy of the AAP governments welfare schemes, stating that they had not reached everyone in the city. He also called Kejriwal aaropi, referring to his alleged role in the excise policy scam case. The former Delhi CM has since been discharged from the case. From Rs 3.2 crore in 2019, Vermas assets jumped to Rs 96.5 crores in 2025, according to his election affidavit.

articleTitle: 5 ‘silent signs’ of high blood sugar: Doctor explains which symptoms really matter
articleFeaturedImageAlt: blood sugar
description: Excessive thirst and frequent urination can signal high blood sugar, but symptoms such as cravings and poor sleep have several possible causes.
body_raw: Health and wellness educator Glucosegurlrami recently shared five symptoms she described as silent signs of too much sugar in the body poor sleep, excessive thirst and urination, uncontrollable cravings, itching, and body aches or nerve pain. While some of these symptoms can occur when blood sugar is high, doctors caution that they are not all specific to hyperglycaemia and should not be used to diagnose diabetes. Dr Himika Chawla, Senior Consultant, Endocrinology and Diabetology, PSRI Hospital, explains which symptoms deserve attention and when it is worth getting your blood sugar checked. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. Excessive thirst and frequent urination Of the symptoms listed, excessive thirst is more closely associated with high blood sugar, particularly when it occurs alongside frequent urination, tiredness, blurred vision or unexplained weight loss. High blood glucose can cause your body to get rid of more water through your urine, which can leave you feeling thirstier, said Chawla. When blood glucose levels remain high, the kidneys try to remove the excess glucose through urine. This can increase fluid loss and, in turn, make a person feel unusually thirsty. Itchy or dry skin Itchy skin can also occur in people with diabetes, although it is not exclusive to the condition. High blood sugar can lead to dehydration, which causes skin changes. Recurrent fungal infections are also itchy, and more common when blood sugar is high, Chawla explained. However, itching can have several other causes, including dry skin, allergies and skin conditions. So persistent itching alone doesnt necessarily mean blood sugar is elevated. What about sugar cravings? Sugar cravings are commonly linked to high blood sugar on social media, but the relationship is not that straightforward. Cravings and body aches may be related to diet, physical activity, sleep problems or other health conditions, Chawla said. Similarly, experiencing a craving for sweets does not, by itself, indicate that a person has high blood glucose. Can poor sleep be a sign? Poor sleep is also not a specific symptom of high blood sugar. Stress, lifestyle, sleep habits and several health conditions can affect sleep quality. In fact, the relationship can work in the opposite direction too. Not sleeping enough can directly affect how efficiently your body uses insulin, Chawla said. This means that consistently poor sleep may influence blood sugar regulation, but waking up tired or sleeping poorly should not automatically be interpreted as a sign of diabetes. What about body aches and nerve pain? General body aches arent specific to high blood sugar. However, persistently elevated blood glucose over time can damage nerves and contribute to diabetic neuropathy, which may cause symptoms such as burning, tingling, numbness or pain, particularly in the feet and hands. Still, Chawla emphasised that symptoms alone cannot establish whether someones blood sugar is high. Symptoms by themselves are not enough to confirm that someone has too much sugar in the blood. You need a blood test to know whether blood glucose is really high or not, she said. When should you get your blood sugar checked? If excessive thirst, frequent urination, unusual tiredness, blurred vision, unexplained weight loss or recurrent infections occur together or persist over time, it is sensible to get blood sugar tested rather than waiting for symptoms to become severe, according to Chawla. Importantly, diabetes and prediabetes can sometimes occur with few or no symptoms. People with risk factors should therefore consider routine screening even if they feel well. Tests may include fasting blood glucose and HbA1c, as per the doctors discretion, Chawla said. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: Delhi is India’s No. 2 concert market. So why are global artists skipping it?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: cold play
description: Organisers say state incentives, venue readiness, pollution, permissions and differences in audience behaviour are making cities beyond Delhi more attractive.
body_raw: In the past year, Delhi-NCR has seen a spate of mega concerts, from hip hop star Travis Scott and English singer-songwriter Ed Sheeran, and is set to host upcoming shows by Fred Again and Khalid. It is currently Indias second-largest concert market, accounting for nearly 17 of concerts and live events in the country - about half the share of Mumbai. Yet some international artists planning India tours are skipping the national capital altogether, choosing Mumbai and Bengaluru - and, in some cases, smaller cities such as Guwahati and Ahmedabad - instead. For instance, English rock band Gorillaz is heading to Guwahati, Bengaluru and Mumbai in January next year. Post Malone performed at Guwahati last year while Coldplay only did shows in Ahmedabad and Mumbai. Many other artists like Enrique Iglesias and John Mayer only did concerts in Mumbai. Guns N Roses is headed to Guwahati in November after Bengaluru. For organisers and industry executives, the choice of city is increasingly about more than just audience size. They pointed to several factors behind the decision, from state subsidies and audience spending patterns to concerns around womens safety and air pollution in Delhi. To be sure, the Delhi government has been pushing to strengthen the Capitals concert economy, seeking to attract major international and homegrown artists and the wider economic activity that comes with them. After it emerged that high stadium rentals were an issue, in October last year, the Sports Authority of India SAI made it cheaper to host events at its venues by 40-50. Cities compete for global artists Deepak Choudhary, managing director of the event company Eva Live, said different states are increasingly seeking to attract concerts through subsidies. Speaking about the Guns N Roses tour, he said, Mumbai, theyve already done. Then they are going to Bengaluru, which is an automatic number two. Subsequently, instead of Delhi, they are headed to Guwahati because Assam subsidised the cost. The state government supported in a large way through sponsorship, Chaudhary explained. In 2024, Canadian artist Bryan Adams had performed in Meghalaya. Both Meghalaya and Assam have concert tourism policies, which subsidise part of the cost of organising the concert and simplify related processes, in return of expected gains to the states economy. Naman Pugalia, Chief Business Officer, Live Events, BookMyShow, disagreed. What we are seeing is a very robust and continuous decentralisation of demand. Delhi continues to be a strong and important market, while these other cities have also shown endeavor and initiative. He added that this is the story of India. We are growing in all directions and we are going fast. But that does not mean Delhi is any less important, he said. Why putting on a show is harder in Delhi An industry executive argued that the condition of venue infrastructure is not good in Delhi and a lot of money is spent on refurbishment. For instance, the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium is a great venue. All it needs is to be maintained, have clean toilets, well educated and well spoken, helpful staff who have answers. When we go and ask them about the rigging capacity, they dont know. They dont have basic layouts on digital files, so we have to make even the basic models ourselves, the executive said. He added that coordinating with government agencies is much easier in other states. Mohit Bijlani, Founder of events management company Team Innovation, agreed. In a massive metropolitan capital like Delhi, traffic, venue accessibility, permissions and crowd movement can make large-scale shows more complicated to execute. Because it is the seat of administration, the capital naturally requires meticulous coordination across multiple regulatory bodies, which can add layers of administrative planning for a promoter, he said. Upneet Bhatia, who has worked as a project director for Ed Sheeran, Post Malone and Backstreet Boys, among other artists, said people dont come to a concert just for the artist. They come for the whole experience, she said. If they are spending so much money and time, venues need to have proper hygiene, free drinking water, a medical professional on ground, and support for traffic and parking. The industry executive also said air pollution is a key factor which weighs on the minds of artists and their teams. It is very important for an international singer to justify the ticket price by giving his heart and soul, and building a great production, right? So, they have to sing live. But they also need to be protective of their voice. This is why the artist could be a little apprehensive, she believes. Different cities, different concert crowds Organisers also feel that different audiences have different tastes. For instance, a rock band will prefer going to Bengaluru rather than Delhi, since it has a South-Indian based audience which is well travelled. Shillong will also be a strong option, since it is known as the rock and music capital of India. On the other hand, a Punjabi artist will prefer Delhi and may not be able to sell out in Bengaluru, Chaudhary of Eva Live said. He also said paying capacity is another consideration. If a person from Mumbai is willing to pay Rs 10,000 for a ticket, the audience will be willing to pay Rs 9,000 in Bangalore, and the same will be Rs 8,000 in Delhi. Another industry executive said Delhi also has a larger market for complimentary tickets, which can affect advance sales. In Bengaluru and Mumbai, if people know an artist or festival is coming, they are excited and buy tickets. In Delhi, people tend to wait until the last minute, hoping they will get a complimentary ticket from someone, the executive said.

articleTitle: Nepal avalanche: 2 bodies recovered, 14 climbers and staff missing
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nepal floods, Nepal avalanche
description: At least 14 people are missing after an avalanche struck Himlung Himal in Nepal's Manang district amid heavy snowfall warnings. Rescue operations are underway.
body_raw: At least two bodies were recovered after an avalanche hit Himlung Himal, a 7,126-metre summit in the Nar Phu region of Nepals Manang district, leaving 14 people missing. The missing individuals comprised both mountain climbers and support personnel, reported Kathmandu Post. The incident was confirmed by Rishi Bhandari, general secretary of the Expedition Operators Association Nepal. According to Bhandari, two of the missing individuals were affiliated with Imagine Nepal Pvt Ltd, while the remaining eight were with Himalayan Holidays Nepal. Ram Krishna Lamichhane, director general of Nepals Department of Tourism, said authorities are actively monitoring the situation. Official efforts are currently underway to gather additional details and coordinate search and rescue operations for the missing group. Nepal authorities have been warning of the possibility of avalanche and flash floods since September 22 amid the heavy snowfall and persistent rain in the high-altitude mountain districts. The avalanche comes barely a few weeks after a devastating avalanche triggered a flash flood, killing nearly 1,400 people in Nepals Rasuwa.

articleTitle: Avengers Endgame Encore early reviews: Is the new footage worth watching in theatres?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Avengers: Endgame Encore
description: Avengers: Endgame Encore brings the 2019 Marvel blockbuster back to theatres with new footage linking it to Avengers: Doomsday. Here’s what critics and viewers are saying.
body_raw: Marvel Studios has brought Avengers Endgame back to theatres seven years after its original release, this time as Avengers Endgame Encore. The film releases in theatres on September 25, with the new scenes becoming the main reason for fans to return. While the 2019 film remains largely unchanged, the re-release adds new footage intended to establish a direct narrative bridge to Avengers Doomsday, releasing on December 18. Early reviews suggest that the added material is interesting, but it does not change the emotional impact of Endgame itself. What critics are saying The National finds the new material more effective than expected. Critic William Mullally says Endgame Encore provides a convincing foundation for Doomsday, connecting the upcoming film to characters and events audiences already know. The review particularly focuses on the new Loki sequence involving Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter, and suggests that the addition works better than expected. ComicBook.com is more critical of the new footage. The review questions how naturally the additional scenes fit into the original film and points out that some of the most enjoyable new material comes before the movie begins, rather than from the added story scenes. FilmiFeed takes a more measured view, noting that the additional footage is brief and mainly serves to connect Endgame with Doomsday. The review also considers whether changing or revisiting parts of the original ending was necessary. What are viewers saying on Rotten Tomatoes? Rotten Tomatoes does not currently have a separate audience score specifically for Endgame Encore the re-release is listed under the original Avengers Endgame page. Its audience reviews, however, include reactions from viewers who have seen the 2026 version. One viewer wrote that the added footage was less than I expected, although they still found it cool. Another said the new scenes were cool but werent anything groundbreaking, while praising the experience of watching Endgame in theatres again. A third viewer called the additions a nice value add and great set up for Doomsday. The extended ending brings Tom Hiddlestons Loki into Steve Rogers and Peggy Carters story. articleTitle: Yoga, exercise, sleep: Why old health practices are being rebranded as ‘neurowellness’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The neurowellness vocabulary may be different, but many of the practices behind it have been around for generations.
description: In a world where the modern brain is overworked and overstimulated, experts explain why people are paying for experiences designed to help them do less.
body_raw: W ellness, for all these years, has largely been about the body-eating better, exercising more, losing weight, building muscle and looking healthier. But that conversation is shifting. People are now asking different questions about their wellbeing Why cant I sleep properly? Why am I constantly overwhelmed? Why is my attention so fragmented? Why cant I switch off even when I am technically resting? The search for answers has given rise to a new wellness buzzword neurowellness. The term may be new, but much of what it includes is already familiar. Meditation, yoga, pranayama, breathwork, sound healing, spending time in nature, social connection, and simply allowing yourself to rest-all these have existed for years. So what exactly is new? Moreover, why are these familiar practices suddenly being presented as ways to care for the brain and nervous system? DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. A mind thats not allowed to clock out Dr Munia Bhattacharya, Senior Consultant, Clinical Psychology, Marengo Asia Hospitals, Gurgaon, describes neurowellness as an emerging umbrella term within the wellness industry rather than a formally established clinical concept. The term may be new, but the need is not, she says. Broadly speaking, it means caring for the brain as part of overall wellbeing-from sleep and concentration to emotional regulation, stress management, and recovery. The idea is especially relevant to how people live now. We are living in a world where the body gets a fitness routine, but the brain gets whatever time is left, says Dr Bhattacharya. The modern brain is being asked to process an extraordinary amount of information notifications, emails, social media, work demands, family responsibilities and an almost continuous stream of information. We have created a lifestyle where the body can stop, but the mind is rarely allowed to clock out, she says. And this may explain why someone can appear to be functioning perfectly well while still feeling mentally depleted. In my clinical practice, I increasingly meet people who are not necessarily presenting with a diagnosable psychological disorder. They are functioning. They are working, meeting deadlines, managing families and maintaining their responsibilities, says Dr Bhattacharya. Yet, she says, they may arrive saying, My mind doesnt switch off, I cannot concentrate like I used to, or I am exhausted even after sleeping. She hears another sentence increasingly often. Nothing is really wrong, but I dont feel like myself. We have become remarkably good at functioning while feeling unwell, she says, adding that a healthy brain is not one that is productive every minute of the day. It can focus when needed, rest when needed, experience emotions, adapt to change, and recover from stress. Old practices, new reasons This is perhaps the biggest distinction between the term neurowellness and all the wellness trends that preceded it. Tarun Gulati, Director, Ganga Kinare Resorts and Hotels, says meditation, yoga, pranayama, sound healing and time spent in nature have long been a part of peoples lives. What is new is not necessarily the practices, but what people are looking for from them, he says, mentioning that they want to sleep better, switch off from work, quieten the mind and come back feeling less overwhelmed. Shane Gunasekara, Director, Kurundu Wellness at Cinnamon Life in Colombo, Sri Lanka, observes a similar shift among guests. We are constantly connected to our phones, work pressure and deadlines, we travel more, sleep patterns are disturbed, and even when we are resting, our minds are still busy, he says. That changes the reason someone might seek out an old practice. People are no longer coming to a spa only because their back is tight or because they want a massage. They understand that beyond muscle relaxation, they also need to calm down, unwind and manage stress, he adds. To address this, Kurundu Wellness introduced Traditional Himalayan Sound Healing with Sakron Boonjing and developed its Sleep Enhancement Ritual. Making ancient practices relatable There is also a language shift. Dr Chandni Tugnait, MD A.M, Psychotherapist, Life Alchemist, Coach and Healer, Founder and Director, Gateway of Healing, says the growing scientific understanding of practices such as meditation and breathwork has given a vocabulary that appeals to a different generation of consumers. Theres now a much clearer picture of what meditation and breathwork are actually doing to the body, not just settling the mind in some vague way, but genuinely calming the nervous system, she says. That matters because the way something is framed and packaged can determine whether people are willing to try it. But I wouldnt call it pure repackaging. Sit through a breathing exercise and your body responds exactly the way it always has, long before anyone gave it a fancy name or a scientific framework to sit inside, says Dr Tugnait. What has changed is whos willing to try it. Someone who would never touch anything labelled spiritual will happily do the same breathwork if its framed as nervous system regulation, backed by a chart and a heart rate number, she says. She sees some of the trend as a rebranding exercise-but not entirely. So call it a rebrand if you want, honestly, in some ways it is exactly that, she says, adding, Underneath it, though, is something genuinely old, tested quietly for generations, just finally handed a name this particular audience trusts enough to actually sit down and try. Neurowellness and nervous-system regulation The two phrases appear together, but they describe different things. Dr Atampreet Singh, Senior Director and Head, Neurology, ShardaCare-Healthcity, says, Neurowellness is a broader approach to supporting brain and nervous-system health through habits such as adequate sleep, regular physical activity, balanced nutrition, social connection, stress management, cognitive stimulation and emotional wellbeing. However, nervous-system regulation refers to the bodys ability to appropriately respond to stress and then return towards a calmer baseline once the stressor has passed, he adds. Regulation does not mean being calm all the time it means being flexible in how you respond to different situations and recovering after stress. Dr Singh explains that several aspects of neurowellness can support this process. Regular exercise can help improve stress resilience and mood, while consistent, good-quality sleep is important for emotional and physiological recovery. Slow, controlled breathing, mindfulness, relaxation practices and activities that promote social connection may also help reduce physiological arousal. A healthy diet and limiting excessive alcohol, nicotine and stimulants can further support overall nervous-system health, he says. That distinction is important because wellness content can sometimes make regulation sound like a state in which a person should remain permanently calm. That is not what it means. Asking a more fundamental question The changing language of wellness reflects a broader change in what people want from it. Dr Bhattacharya says wellness was once commonly discussed in terms of diet, exercise, weight, and physical appearance. Now, people are asking about attention, sleep, stress and emotional exhaustion. These are not simply lifestyle questions, she says. They tell us something about how modern life is affecting the way we think, feel and function. This is also why the idea of a wellness experience is changing. Gulati says people are becoming less interested in wellness as a checklist. They dont necessarily want to attend a yoga class just because it is on the schedule. They want the experience to make a difference to how they feel. That is why multi-day programmes are becoming relevant, he says. At Ganga Kinare, programmes include combinations of yoga, meditation, kriya, pranayama, sound healing, therapies, wellness cuisine and nature experiences. I think people are looking at wellness less as an activity and more as a way of changing their pace for a few days, says Gulati. Gunasekara has noticed a similar change at Kurundu Wellness. Earlier, a guest might have booked a massage, attended a meditation session or experienced a sound bath as separate activities. Now, we are seeing guests looking for a more complete journey rather than one isolated treatment, he says. Its Sleep Enhancement Ritual, for instance, combines several elements The experience begins with a warm welcome ritual, followed by a light-pressure head massage and Thai stretching techniques to help the guest slow down, release tension and prepare the body and mind for deeper rest. This then flows into the sound-bathing experience. You can simply lie down, listen and allow yourself some time away from everything else. The experience doesnt finish there. Afterwards, guests can continue with hot and cold therapy through our steam, sauna and vitality pools with water jets, before finishing with a healthy cup of tea and a light snack. I think this kind of complete journey is becoming very important in modern wellness, says Gunasekara. It is no longer about experiencing one treatment in isolation, but about creating a journey that allows the guest to slow down, disconnect and leave feeling deeply relaxed. How priorities are changing Perhaps the most noticeable change is in the outcome people are seeking. People still want the traditional benefits of wellness-muscle relaxation, physical recovery, skincare and feeling physically better. But the desired endpoint is increasingly intangible. At Ganga Kinare, Gulati says programmes such as Nidra Samadhi centre on sleep, relaxation, stress and fatigue, while Dhyana Sadhana takes a more meditative approach involving yoga, meditation, kriya and pranayama. It tells us something about how peoples priorities are changing, he says. A wellness holiday doesnt necessarily have to result in a visible physical transformation. Sometimes, sleeping properly for a few nights, having a quieter mind and feeling like yourself again is the outcome people value most. Gunasekara says the same shift can be seen in conversations with guests, who increasingly talk about sleep, stress, mental tiredness and wanting to disconnect. Of course, guests still want traditional outcomes - releasing muscle tension, improving recovery, taking care of their skin and feeling physically better, but the conversation is becoming broader, he says. For Gunasekara, this is where wellness is heading-not choosing between physical and mental wellbeing but understanding that people increasingly want to experience them together and leave feeling satisfied and fulfilled. Why pay for doing nothing? An interesting contradiction lies at the heart of the neurowellness boom. People are paying for experiences designed to help them do less. According to hospitality experts, genuine downtime has become hard to find. Even when we go on holiday, we are often still checking our phones, answering messages or thinking about work, says Gulati. So simply being in a beautiful destination doesnt always mean that you have actually switched off. Gunasekara agrees. You can buy many things, but if you are constantly tired, mentally overloaded or unable to switch off, it affects your work, family time, holidays and physical wellbeing, he says. That may explain why structured wellness experiences are becoming more attractive. Someone else provides the setting, removes some decision-making, and creates protected time to step away. I think people are increasingly willing to pay for that because they recognise the value of having someone else take care of the setting and structure while they focus on themselves, says Gulati. He believes this may even be creating a different definition of luxury. It is not necessarily about having more things. It is about having the time, privacy and space to step away from everything for a while and genuinely feel rested. Neurowellness without the marketing Take away the apps, gadgets, retreats and optimisationneurowellness becomes all about basic mental wellbeing sleeping properly, moving regularly, taking breaks from constant stimulation, focusing on one thing at a time, allowing some boredom, staying socially connected and making space for emotions and activities you enjoy. As Dr Bhattacharya puts it, It does not have to involve expensive programmes, complicated routines or another gadget to track how well we are functioning. The basics are simple Treat sleep as a healthy behaviour rather than leftover time at the end of the day, she says. She also recommends periods of uninterrupted attention and regular movement, noting that physical activity is not only about physical fitness. And perhaps most importantly, the brain needs time without constant input. Five or ten minutes without a phone, podcast, television or constant input can be surprisingly restorative, says Dr Bhattacharya. We should not be afraid of a little boredom. The brain does not need stimulation every waking minute. The same goes for pleasure and connection. Reading, gardening, music, family time, meaningful conversation, or simply sitting quietly do not need to have a measurable benefit to be worthwhile. As Dr Bhattacharya says, Sometimes, the most powerful thing we can do for the brain is not ask it to perform better, but give it permission to rest. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: ‘Unease factor’ in Congress-Samajwadi Party ties ahead of UP polls: Who is Imran Masood
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress MP Imran Masood
description: Congress's move to name Saharanpur MP as UP working president has been seen by SP camp as its “pressure tactic” to bargain for more seats as Masood has been putting heat on Akhilesh over seat-sharing
body_raw: The Congresss decision to appoint Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president of its Uttar Pradesh unit ahead of the Assembly elections seems to have caused some unease in ally Samajwadi Party SP, which sees the move as a pressure tactic to bargain for more seats in the polls. While SP spokesperson Rajendra Chaudhary told The Indian Express that Masoods appointment would have no adverse impact on his partys seat-sharing talks with the Congress, some other SP leaders privately expressed discomfort over the development. I dont understand what is in the mind of the top Congress leadership. The new UP Congress president, Aradhana Misra Mona, and her father, Pramod Tiwari, have cordial relations with the SP. Her appointment will only help in smoothening dialogue between the two parties regarding the UP polls. But Masood, through his remarks on the SP, often creates uneasiness. Now, things will depend on how much authority senior Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra give Masood in seat-sharing talks, said an SP insider. He said the Congress wanted an early decision on seat-sharing, as any delay could leave it with little choice but to accept whatever seats the SP would offer. The UP elections are due in February 2027. A senior SP leader said Masoods appointment appeared to be both a Congress tactic to secure more seats and an attempt to compete for the Muslim vote, traditionally seen to be with the SP. Masood is influential in Saharanpur but not across western UP. He will not be able to disturb the SPs Muslim votes in this region. But his public remarks about the alliance and Muslim issues will build pressure on the SP to finalise seat-sharing early and share Muslim-dominated seats with the Congress. The Congress is eyeing anti-BJP votes of regional parties, the leader said. Another SP leader said the Congress should clarify whether Masood would have any role in alliance talks.He is continuously demanding early finalisation of the alliance. He should speak first with Gandhi before speaking about the SP in the media. All Opposition parties want Muslim votes but none is trying to make inroads into the 42 non-Muslim votes of the BJP, the leader said. An SP leader from western UP said Masoods attempts to put pressure on the party would not work. The SP will demand all Assembly seats falling under the Saharanpur Lok Sabha constituency. The SP is prepared to contest there, he said. Seat-sharing hurdles Seat-sharing in Saharanpur could be a point of contention between the SP and the Congress. Last month, Masood said the Congress would fight the five seats in Saharanpur that it had contested in 2017. Hamara majboot jila hai, apna majboot jila thode hi chhod denge The district is our stronghold. We will not leave it, he said. The Congress leaders declined to officially respond to the concerns expressed by SP leaders over Masoods appointment. SP leaders are irritated more with Masood because he had quit them after the 2022 Assembly polls, and later became a Congress MP with the SPs support in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. But we are hopeful that things will settle down between both camps soon because the Congress leadership has directed Masood to refrain from further attacks on the SP, said a senior Congress leader. Masoods journey A first-time MP, Masood, 56, has been a prominent face in western Uttar Pradesh politics for several years. Carrying forward his familys political legacy, he was earlier known for controversial remarks. Over the last few years, however, he has sought to shed the image of a Muslim hardliner and has reached out to Hindu voters. He has often been heard saying Ram milenge maryada se jeene mein, Ram milenge Hanuman ke seene mein Ram is found in living a life of dignity, Ram resides in Hanumans heart. Masood was first elected MLA as an Independent from the Muzaffarabad Assembly seat in 2007. In 2012, the Congress picked him as a youth face in Rahul Gandhis team. The same year, he contested the Nakur Assembly seat but lost to the BSPs Dharam Singh Saini. Just before the 2014 Lok Sabha polls, a video clip surfaced in which Masood was purportedly seen threatening then BJPs prime ministerial candidate Narendra Modi while blaming the BJP and RSS for the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots. A case was registered against him for hate speech. In the Lok Sabha polls, he lost to the BJPs Raghav Lakhan Pal in Saharanpur. Ahead of the 2022 UP Assembly polls, Masood ended his association with the Congress and joined the SP. He quit the SP in October that year after SP chief Akhilesh Yadav did not give a ticket to him or any of his associates for the Assembly polls. He then joined the BSP, where Mayawati immediately appointed him coordinator for western UP, with additional responsibility for working among Muslims in Uttarakhand. In August 2023, however, Mayawati expelled Masood from the party, accusing him of indiscipline and anti-party activities. He returned to the Congress later that year. Recent row On September 21, speaking to ANI, Masood said Akhileshs political activity was meaningless unless the alliance was finalised. Finalise the alliance if you have to have an alliance. If it the alliance is not to be done, we Congress are going ahead with our preparations. Akhilesh ji should finish this work alliance finalisation immediately. If you have to lead, the responsibility is on you. Dil bhi aapko bada karna padega You will have to have a large heart, Masood said. He said the SP should not think of moving ahead without the Congress. Because if you are going ahead without the Congress, defeating the BJP is not in your mind. Only the Congress can fight the BJP, he said. In June 2025, Masood had also stirred the alliance debate by saying the 62-17 formula would not work in the 2027 Assembly polls, referring to the seat-sharing arrangement between the two allies for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

articleTitle: FSSAI orders recall of Everest cumin powder: What to do if you have used affected batch
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Experts explain what consumers should do after consuming a recalled batch of cumin powder and how to check packaged spices.
description: A recalled batch of Everest cumin powder was found to contain pesticide residues above prescribed limits. Experts explain what this means, what consumers should do if they consumed it and how to check packaged spices.
body_raw: FSSAI continues to enforce strict regulatory compliance to safeguard consumer health across the country. On October 4, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India recalled a batch of Everest cumin powder. On X, it wrote, MS Everest Food Products Private Limited has been directed to immediately recall Pre-packed Cumin Powder after tests declared the sample unsafe. 2 Product Recall Order Ms Everest Food Products Private Limited has been directed to immediately recall Pre-packed Cumin Powder after tests declared the sample UNSAFE.22 FoodSafety FSSAINotice FSSAIAction - FSSAI fssaiindia October 4, 2026 The action follows laboratory testing that found pesticide residues above the prescribed limits. FSSAI has declared the affected batch of Everest cumin powder, Batch No. E080668761, unsafe after residues of Azoxystrobin and Thiamethoxam were found above permissible limits. This is afood-safety concern related to a specific recalled batch and should not be interpreted as meaning all packaged cumin powders are unsafe. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. What if you have accidentally consumed the product Dr Chirag Tandon, Director, Internal Medicine, ShardaCare - Healthcity says, Finding residues above the permitted limit does not automatically mean that someone who accidentally consumed the product containing residues of pesticides such as Azoxystrobin or Thiamethoxam will develop poisoning or immediate illness. So, it is important not to panic. The actual risk, he says, depends on the concentration, quantity consumed, frequency of exposure, and the persons age and body weight. EFSA assesses pesticide exposure using both acute and chronic dietary exposure models. However, if a product contains pesticide residues above the prescribed limit, you should stop using that batch. Repeated or higher exposure is more concerning. Thiamethoxam belongs to the neonicotinoid group of insecticides, while Azoxystrobin is a fungicide. Their presence above the permitted residue level does not by itself establish that a person will experience symptoms, and consumers should not assume that headaches, nausea or other nonspecific symptoms are necessarily caused by the spice, Dr Tandon explains. If a person has consumed a recalled product once, the sensible approach is to discontinue its use and avoid further exposure rather than attempting to induce vomiting or undertake a detox. However, Dr Tandon says that if anyone develops significant or persistent symptoms after suspected pesticide exposure, or has consumed a large quantity of the affected product, they should seek medical advice and provide the product packaging or batch details if available. Children and people with other vulnerabilities warrant particular caution because dietary exposure is assessed by body weight. What should consumers check? From a consumer perspective, checking the label is one of the simplest precautions. Before using a packaged spice, check the brand, batch or lot number, manufacturing and best-before dates, FSSAI licence details, and the integrity of the packaging. Avoid damaged, tampered, or poorly sealed packets. Consumers should also check official FSSAI recall information when a particular product or batch has been flagged. When it comes to powdered spices, adulteration is another major concern. Dr Tandon says, This is because grinding makes it difficult to identify what has been mixed into the product. FSSAI guidance notes that cumin may be adulterated with substances such as coloured grass seeds, while powdered spices can contain fillers such as starch, flour, sawdust or other cheaper materials. articleTitle: Hours after rescue, lioness that attacked 5 persons in Gujarat dies; rabies suspected
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hours after rescue, lioness that attacked 5 persons in Gujarat dies; rabies suspected
description: Tissue samples sent to agricultural university for tests, forest dept says 'no cause for worry'.
body_raw: A LIONESS has died of suspected rabies in Amreli district after it was rescued last week following separate attacks on five persons. Samples of its brain tissues have been sent to Anand Agriculture University for confirmation, a senior forest department officer said on Monday. Meanwhile, all the five persons injured after being attacked by the lioness earlier have been administered anti-rabies vaccine as per standard medical protocol, officers said. The lioness - aged 2-3 years - was rescued on October 2 from Arjunsukh village in Amreli after it injured five persons in separate incidents Four villagers and a forest department officer. The lioness was later shifted to Krankach Animal Care Centre, where it showed unusual behaviour, such as biting and unusual vocalisations. Within around 20 hours of its rescue, the lioness died at the centre on October 3, forest officers said. Deputy Conservator of Forests, Shetrunji Wildlife Division, Chirag Amin said that primary symptoms indicated that the cause of death may have been rabies, but added that this could be confirmed only after scientific tests. Amin added that the samples of the lionesss brain tissues have been sent to Anand Agricultural University. Amin said there was no cause for worry so far, as the lioness was solitary and there were no other instances of any other lion showing similar symptoms. Forest department officers also checked the surrounding areas near the spot from which the lioness was rescued. Another senior forest officer said a lion can get infected with rabies if it consumes or bites an animal infected by the virus. Similarly, if an infected animal drinks water from a waterbody and then the lion also drinks water from the same waterbody that has rabies infection through the saliva of the infected animal, it can cause transmission of the virus to the big cat. It can also happen that a lion has made a kill and temporarily abandoned the carcass after partially consuming it. It then comes back after some time and again consumes the meat. During this gap period, if some other infected animals such as dogs, hyena etc consume meat from the same carcass, it can lead to transmission of rabies to the lion. The chances of transmission of rabies is more in revenue areas which are not in so much of control and which have the presence of dogs and cattle. and they share the habitat with lions, the officer said.

articleTitle: Maharashtra poll chief wants ECINet discretion for staff — a demand ECs had flagged
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer S Chockalingam (centre); Election Commissioners SS Sandhu (left) and Vivek Joshi (right).
description: Sent a day after The Indian Express investigation, the CEO's letter seeks four ECINet changes. The Commission has since granted one, letting officers waive hearings.
body_raw: The Chief Electoral Officer of Maharashtra, the largest state now in the notice phase of the Special Intensive Revision SIR, wrote to the Election Commission EC in New Delhi last week, seeking four changes to the ECINet software, each, in effect, a request that the software let Electoral Registration Officers EROs exercise a discretion the law already gives them, The Indian Express has learnt. Maharashtra CEO S Chockalingams requests that EROs be allowed to decide which logical discrepancy cases need a hearing, what documents to accept and which discrepancies they can dispose of themselves, echo concerns already recorded by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. The CEOs communication, addressed to Senior Deputy Election Commissioner Maneesh Garg, Director General of IT Seema Khanna and two secretariat officers, went out on September 24, a day after an investigation by The Indian Express revealed that the two Election Commissioners had flagged, on record, that the software was curtailing the powers of the EROs. CEO Chockalingam could not be reached for comment Monday. The Indian Express sent a questionnaire to the ECI spokesperson who acknowledged receipt. A response is awaited. The Maharashtra draft roll, published August 31, cut 21.1 per cent of the states electors. Its final roll is due on November 16. A logical discrepancy is not a finding that someone is not a voter. It is a mismatch the Commissions ECINET software throws up when it tries to link an elector to a parent or grandparent on the roll from the last SIR, such as a parents name that doesnt match, an age gap between parent and child of under 15 or over 50 years, an age that doesnt progress correctly between the old roll and the new, or a case where the elector submitted no document, or only Aadhaar. As reported by The Indian Express, Sandhu wrote on August 14 that CEOs, DEOs and EROs, the statutory authorities for the voters list, were reporting they could not perform their duties, their powers curtailed by centralised control of ERONet at DGIT level. It is strange, he said, that all the responsibilities regarding Electoral Roll lie on EROS, DEOs and CEOs as per law, but the access control has been centralised by DGIT. The Maharashtra CEOs communication of September 24, in effect, asked for the same freedom the two commissioners said ECINet had curtailed four places where the law gives the ERO a decision to make and the software gives him no way to make it. Hearings The rules give the ERO the discretion to require a person to appear personally before him, the CEO wrote. ECINets Take Action menu has two options, and neither lets the ERO waive a hearing. He asked for a third, Exempted from Hearing, for electors who submit valid and satisfactory documents, so that senior citizens, the disabled and other vulnerable groups are spared unnecessary inconvenience and apprehension. Documents The 13 documents listed on the back of the notice are indicative and not exhaustive, the CEO wrote, and asked for a 14th option, OtherOther Equivalent Document, because electors from tribal, homeless and sex-worker communities may not able to provide any document from the indicative list. Who decides In some cases, an ERO cannot resolve a logical discrepancy on the basis of a Booth Level Officers statement alone. Supporting documents have to be sent to the District Election Officer DEO for verification. The CEO wants EROs to be able to decide these cases themselves when they are satisfied with the evidence. The request cites the law, which puts responsibility for the electoral roll on the ERO and says that, if satisfied that a person is eligible, the ERO should direct that the name be included. A mandatory upload The ECINet currently requires an Extract of Last SIR to be uploaded in every discrepancy case. The CEO said this should be optional because the discrepancy is already identified using the last SIR roll. Written instructions The EROs have number of queries about the process, the CEO said, and oral instructions from ECI or CEO are insufficient. He asked for FAQs explaining the notice, document submission, hearing and disposal process. Four of the five are the same request in different clothes the law gives the ERO a judgement to make, and the software does not give the ERO the button to make it. The Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 assign responsibility for the electoral roll to the Electoral Registration Officer, one for each Assembly seat. An ERO is usually the sub-divisional magistrate or an officer of equivalent rank in the district administration. The ERO prepares the voters list, hears claims and objections and decides which names will stay and which get deleted. This is a deliberately decentralised system. For decades, the ECI has leaned on that design to answer political allegations of mass manipulation of electoral rolls. No single person is supposed to control the voters list. On paper, the ERO still decides every name on the list. In practice, the ERO has been able to do only what the software allows add a name, delete one, reverse a decision or process an appeal. What the software allows is controlled centrally by Khannas division in New Delhi. On September 23, in its first response to The Indian Express investigation, the Commission had said its digital platforms operate under strict data security protocols to prevent unauthorized tampering, and that EROs and DEOs function as per statutory powers for registration and deletion under law. The Maharashtra CEOs communication went out a day later. On September 26, after a meeting of the full Commission, the Commission issued a statement that partially addressed the Maharashtra requests, giving EROs the discretion to exempt people flagged for logical discrepancies from personal hearings. It also said various upgradations of the portal have already been made based on the inputs from State CEOs in the past few months, and that in case any further flexibility is required by the field officers, that will be made operational. The four-page note announced eight other decisions that addressed, point by point, several of the concerns recorded by the two Commissioners. Agendas will now be circulated before every Commission meeting and minutes issued afterwards. Officers foreign trips will need Commission approval. New IT modules and portals will go through a committee of officers before being placed before the Commission. The ECINet will be reviewed by a committee headed by a senior Deputy Election Commissioner and will include an independent expert from an IIT or IIIT. If field officers need more flexibility in the system, it will be provided. And directions issued by Commissioners to officers will be meticulously complied with. These decisions map, almost item for item, onto the concerns the two Commissioners had put on file over 10 months that agendas were not circulated and minutes not issued, that officers went abroad without the Commissions approval, that new IT modules were built without its knowledge, that the electoral-roll database needed an audit by an independent expert, that field officers lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, and that an administrative order had altered the allocation of work around the IT division without them.

articleTitle: No Plan B, Just NEET: How an auto-driver’s son got MBBS seat at King George’s Medical University
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Prabhat Kumar Yadav
description: Talking about his plans, Prabhat said bringing his father back to his hometown is high on his priority list. But beyond that, he wants to support other aspiring students who come from families facing financial constraints similar to his own.
body_raw: No backup plans or alternate choices - just three subjects and one exam in vision thats how Prabhat Kumar Yadav, a 19-year-old native of Devkipur village in Uttar Pradeshs Jaunpur district, cleared the NEET UG 2026 with an All India Rank AIR 3864 and grabbed an MBBS seat at King Georges Medical University KGMU in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. But Prabhats journey to medical college was not a battle he fought alone in Kota. Hundreds of kilometres away, in a small chawl in Mumbai, his father was quietly making it possible for his son to chase that dream. He could not offer academic guidance, but he offered something just as crucial - financial support. Instalment by instalment, he shouldered the cost of his sons education, giving Prabhat the support he needed to keep going. A fathers support for his son Prabhats father, Mahendra Kumar Yadav, has been driving an auto-rickshaw in Mumbai for the past 20 years to support his family. After long days navigating the citys busy roads, he would often video-call Prabhat at night. I used to see him tired and drenched in sweat as he prepared his dinner, Prabhat recalled. Looking at the struggles his father is facing, the 19-year-old said that he never allowed the adversities of his family to drag him down but rather took them as a source of motivation.At least I dont have to find passengers all day at least I dont have to cook for myself after a whole day of toil the only thing I have to do is study, said Prabhat. Also Read After court reprimand over paper leaks, Nilekani-led panel consults ex-ISRO chairman on NTA overhaul A transition from UPSC to NEET Becoming a doctor was never my plan, but in the last two years it became the only choice I had, said Prabhat, explaining that in Class 9 he wanted to pursue UPSC and never aspired to join the medical field. After his Class 10 boards, which he passed with 89.44, his family persuaded him to choose medicine. Coming from a joint family, decisions cannot be taken unanimously it has to have everyones input and support, Prabhat said. He passed his Class 12 exams with 83.44. Prabhat completed his Class 12 in Jaunpur, while most of his friends had already left the town after Class 10 to begin their NEET preparation in Kota. After finishing school, he was determined to follow the same path. His family, trusting his decision, agreed to send him to Kota. But paying the coaching fees was a challenge. Prabhat wrote to the senior authorities at his coaching institute, requesting a concession as his family could not afford the full amount. His request was accepted, and he received a 10 to 20 per cent fee concession, with the remaining amount financed. For his father, who earns between Rs 25,000 and Rs 30,000 a month, meeting the cost of his sons education was not easy. Prabhats maternal uncle also stepped in, helping the family manage his living and other expenses in Kota. Two years of hard work before getting AIR 3864 In his first attempt at NEET UG 2025, Prabhat scored 504 marks. I was a bit relaxed, acclimatising to the competitiveness around me. Though I was getting admission to courses like BDS, BUMS, etc., I knew the mistakes I made and the weak points that were to be worked upon, said Prabhat. Many of his teachers, considering his familys financial situation, asked him to choose the allied courses he was getting, but he was rigid in his decision to pursue MBBS. Unlike most 19-year-olds today, Prabhat had zero screen time. No Instagram or YouTube, just his books and that one exam that he laid his eyes on. He sometimes sang film songs during the fun days at his coaching institute, but that was all. He did not allow any distractions to lead him astray from the main goal. He would sometimes go to the temple near his hostel or sit with his fellow hostellers to feel a bit light, but the rest of the day it was just classes, mock tests, and a long stretch of self-study. He was disheartened when he heard about the NEET paper leak. I did feel a bit burdened to reappear for the exam, but I know it would only allow me to improve my marks, said Prabhat. NEET result and celebration across Devkipur When the NEET UG 2026 result was announced on July 16, a wave of happiness swept through Prabhats village. Neighbours and relatives congratulated him, while hundreds of kilometres away in Mumbai, his father felt a deep sense of relief. Headlines describing him as an auto-drivers son who cleared NEET drew attention to his achievement. But for Prabhat and his family, the financial struggle did not end with his NEET success. In many ways, a new challenge was about to begin. Arranging Rs 50,000 for the admission fee of KGMU was also a task for us, but somehow my father and uncles managed it and got me enrolled, said Prabhat, adding that acquiring an MBBS seat does not end all the problems alone, but it is the prologue for the brighter days coming their way. Talking about his plans, Prabhat said bringing his father back to his hometown is high on his priority list. But beyond that, he wants to support other aspiring students who come from families facing financial constraints similar to his own. Whatever I have achieved would not have been possible without the support and trust of my family and the people in my village. I believe good deeds should not be one-way they should be reciprocated, in equal measure or, better still, in a much greater way, he said. After two years of hard work, sacrifices, and a single-minded focus on NEET, Prabhat is now preparing for the next chapter. He has also begun sharing his journey on social media and YouTube as he waits to take his first steps into medical college.

articleTitle: Launched by Amitabh Bachchan, Chandrachur Singh’s career ended amid a Shah Rukh film shoot
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chandrachur Singh
description: Chandrachur Singh was born into royalty and trained for the UPSC, Tere Mere Sapne and Maachis brought him stardom in the 90s, only for a horrific sea accident cutting it short during shoot schedule of Shah Rukh Khan's Josh.
body_raw: While destiny may seem like a myth to many, some lives make you wonder if it truly exists. How else do you explain the journey of a young man born into royalty, who dreamt of cracking the UPSC and becoming an Indian Foreign Service IFS officer, only to end up as one of Bollywoods most promising stars of the late 1990s? This is the story of Chandrachur Singh. With Tere Mere Sapne and Maachis in 1996, Chandrachur became an overnight sensation. Critics hailed his performances, audiences embraced him, and the media even began comparing him to Amitabh Bachchan-partly because they shared the same birthday. But as quickly as stardom arrived, it slipped away. A devastating accident in 2000, coupled with a series of professional setbacks, altered the course of his career forever. Chandrachur was set to become an IFS officer Born to Army officer and former MLA Baldev Singh and Princess Krishna Kumari Devi of the erstwhile princely state of Patna now in Odisha, Chandrachur excelled in academics from an early age. He was equally gifted outside the classroom, training in Hindustani classical music, setting district records in high jump, playing cricket, and serving as the art editor of his school magazine. Despite his creative interests, acting was never part of his plan. His dream was to join the civil services, particularly the Indian Foreign Service. Speaking in an interview with Samar Sarila, Chandrachur recalled that a teacher who became a father figure encouraged him to pursue humanities at St Stephens College to strengthen his UPSC preparation. Being in the IFS was actually my primary objective, and if not that, then the IAS. I was meeting a lot of civil servants to understand how to prepare for the UPSC. Everything changed during college While studying at St. Stephens College, Chandrachur actively participated in theatre and won the Best Actor award at the Rajpal Memorial in his very first year. The recognition soon began attracting film offers-even before he had considered moving to Mumbai. Creativity was inherently a part of my personality. Music played an important role in my school life, and so did drama. While I was playing lead roles in college plays, I started getting offers without even going to Bombay. Theatre eventually opened Bollywoods doors During his summer break in 1988, Chandrachur assisted filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt. A year later, he signed his first film, Jab Pyaar Kiya Toh Darna Kya, opposite Suchitra Krishnamurthy. The film was nearly 60 percent complete before it was shelved. I was pulled into films more by circumstances than by choice. It was a subconscious desire to express myself through art, but never a conscious career decision. The setbacks continued Several films either failed to take off or were shelved midway, forcing Chandrachur to return to Delhi. He spent the next few years teaching schoolchildren while waiting for another opportunity. Those years of uncertainty left a lasting impact. At that age, it was disappointing like hell. You begin questioning yourself-Am I not good enough? Is it because Im an outsider? All those doubts creep in during years of struggle. ALSO READ If my parents cant watch it, I wont do it Fans remind Yash of old vow amid Toxic row His fortunes changed dramatically in 1996 I struggled for a few years and taught children in schools in Delhi. Just when I had secured a permanent job, I got the call for Tere Mere Sapne. Around the same time, Maachis also happened, so I quit my job. This is where destiny seemed to work its magic once again. Tere Mere Sapne was directed by Joy Augustine-the very filmmaker who had earlier helmed Jab Pyaar Kiya Toh Darna Kya, the shelved film that was meant to launch Chandrachur Singhs career. Backed by Amitabh Bachchans production house, Tere Mere Sapne announced his arrival, while Gulzars Maachis established him as one of the industrys most promising newcomers, earning him the Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut in 1997. Yet Chandrachur admits he never enjoyed the pace of commercial stardom. I was doing three shifts a day. Sometimes I would simply change costumes and go from one set to another, touching the feet of two different mothers in two different films. I didnt enjoy that process. I wanted to do one film at a time. Despite the acclaim, Chandrachur believes being an outsider limited his opportunities. I never received solo hero roles, perhaps because I wasnt from the industry. It is very difficult for an outsider to establish themselves, he told WildFilmsIndia. The injury that changed the course of his career Then came the turning point. While shooting Josh in Goa, Chandrachur suffered a near career-ending accident during an off day at the sea. I had a water accident about two kilometres into the sea. My shoulder was so badly dislocated that my arm was almost detached from my body. The injury required surgery, repeated physiotherapy and years of rehabilitation. This became a recurring problem on sets. Shooting of films stopped for a while. I gained weight because I couldnt exercise. Even after surgery, it never fully healed. I had to work with that disability. Although the injury significantly affected his career, Chandrachur insists it wasnt the only reason behind his disappearance. It was a combination of factors. Success, setbacks, wrong decisions-everything contributed. When Chandrachur spoke about his mistakes and industry pressure Over time, he became increasingly selective with scripts and admits that he also made mistakes. Speaking to Dayandnightnews Chd, he said I took some incorrect decisions. Success can insulate you from reality just as much as failure can. He also addressed the immense pressure of being compared with Amitabh Bachchan. Amitabh Bachchan is an institution. He gave me my first break. To be compared with him after just one film put tremendous pressure on me. I dont consider myself anywhere close to Amit ji. Away from films, Chandrachur discovered a passion for cooking and even hosted the television show Royal Rasoi in 2012. He returned to acting with his digital debut in Aarya in 2020, followed by Cuttputlli and Bayaan. Looking back, Chandrachur says he has no regrets. Even today, he considers himself someone who never chased stardom aggressively. If I hadnt become an actor, he says, I would have become a teacher.

articleTitle: The Paradise box office collection day 4: Nani film earns Rs 139 cr worldwide, his highest grosser ever
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Paradise box office collection day 4: Nani film earns Rs 139 crore worldwide
description: The Paradise box office collection day 4: Despite largely negative reviews, Nani's film has earned Rs 138.2 crore worldwide gross in its first weekend.
body_raw: The Paradise box office collection day 4 Nanis latest release The Paradise is heading towards rs 150 crore mark despite receiving largely negative reviews from the audience and critics. The film crossed Rs 100 crore at the worldwide box office within three days of its release. After opening at Rs 34.65 crore, the film witnessed a massive 60 drop on day 2. The Paradise minted Rs 14.9 crore on Friday, Rs 15.25 crore on Saturday, and Rs 15.07 crore on Sunday from across 6764 shows. According to the industry tracker Sacnilk, The Paradise has reached at total India gross collection of Rs 109 crore and total net collections of Rs 92.1 crore. Its overseas gross collection stands at Rs 29.25 crore, and the worldwide gross collection is Rs 138.25 crore. The period action drama thriller has also managed to surpass the lifetime collection of Telugu actor Nanis previous film, HIT The Third Case. It had grossed around Rs 120 crore at the global box office during its entire theatrical run, making The Paradise the highest grossing film of Nanis career. The Paradise is also facing stiff competition from other current theatrical releases like Sidharth Malhotras The Vvaan - Force of the Forrest, Vishal Chaturvedis sleeper hit Hanuman Ansh, and Mirzapur The Movie. On Day 4, The Paradise had an overall 45.12 occupancy at the theatres in Telugu language - with morning shows at 35.08, afternoon shows at 55.38, evening shows recorded at 52.54, and evening shows at 37.46. The highest theatre occupancy was in Hyderabad region, registering 61.8 across 706 shows. On the other hand, the overall Hindi language occupancy was 25.09 and Tamil had 28.35 theatre occupancy. An excerpt of SCREENs review of The Paradise, read, The Paradise is what happens when that bankability meets a budget thats five times bigger, multi-fold expectations, and a screenplay that has nothing new to say. The problem of the film, rather, the problem of Srikanth Odela is that he cannot write good female characters around the story. Meanwhile, amid the films box-office run and the negative reviews, Nani spoke about the praise and criticism towards his film The Paradise. I have seen all your reactions and responses. Ive received all your love and equally enjoyed your hilarious trolls. Im heartwarmed by the way audience have owned the film, and also learnt from the flaws that critics and reviewers have pointed out. Thank you for everything is all I can say. We have made TheParadise with a lot of blood and sweat to give you a unique experience, and its all yours to celebrate or judge. With the excitement you had for the film and the affection you showed on me, I am filled with gratitude, he wrote on X. I have seen all your reactions and responses. Ive received all your love and equally enjoyed your hilarious trolls. Im heartwarmed by the way audience have owned the film, and also learnt from the flaws that critics and reviewers have pointed out. Thank you for everything is. - Nani NameisNani September 25, 2026 Helmed by Srikanth Odela, The Paradise features Nani, Raghav Juyal, Sonali Kulkarni and Kayadu Lohar.
