articleTitle: Nearly 1.9 lakh cancer cases in India linked to viral, bacterial infections, says Lancet study
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Cancer
description: HPV, H.pylori and hepatitis viruses are among the key preventable causes. Vaccination, screening and timely treatment could reduce the burden, say experts
body_raw: An estimated 1,90,000 cancer cases in India were linked to infections caused by viruses and bacteria, according to a 2024 study, which was published in The Lancet Oncology journal. An estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases globally - 12 of all cancers diagnosed that year - were linked to infections. In India, a majority of these infection-attributable cases, a little over a lakh, are driven by the Human Papillomavirus HPV, which causes cervical cancer, and can be prevented by HPV vaccination. Chronic hepatitis B and hepatitis C infections primarily cause liver cancer, specifically hepatocellular carcinoma HCC. H. Pylori Helicobacter pylori, a stomach bacterium accounts for an additional 47,000 cancer cases, mainly gastric cancer, followed by Epstein-Barr virus 22,000 cancer cases, Hepatitis B virus 10,000 cancer cases and Hepatitis C virus 5,300 cancer cases. According to data with the Global Cancer Observatory GLOBOCAN, this accounts for about 12 per cent of the total annual cancer burden. The authors of the report make a strong case about why these findings underline the importance of infection control in reducing rates of cancer. They highlight effective but underused measures HPV and hepatitis B vaccination testing and treatment for HIV Human Immunodeficiency Virus, H pylori, HBV hepatitis B virus and HCV hepatitis C virus safe injection practices access to condoms and pre-exposure prophylaxis to prevent HIV transmission and screening for precancerous lesions in HPV-driven cervical and anal cancer. Status of HPV vaccination in India India, which recently launched the national HPV vaccination programme, has already surpassed 80 lakh 8 million doses. The vaccine is transitioning into the routine immunization schedule. It uses Gardasil-4, a quadrivalent vaccine protecting against high-risk HPV types 16 and 18 responsible for over 80 of cervical cancer cases in India as well as types 6 and 11. Dr Smita Joshi, senior scientist at Prayas health group not attached with the study, says that some states in the country have done well on the uptake of the HPV vaccination target. What is also important is screening of adult women with an HPV test and appropriate management if positive for prevention of cervical cancer, she adds. Dr I S Gilada, Secretary General of Peoples Health Organisation-India, emphasises how both HPV and Hepatitis B infections are fully preventable through vaccination. The Hepatitis B vaccine is available at low cost but often there are supply shortages, he says. He notes that Hepatitis B testing was conducted in several settings as part of the Triple H screening programme HCV, HIV and HBV, including antenatal care clinics, blood banks and pre-surgical evaluations. However, linkage to Hepatitis B vaccination remains very poor among individuals who test negative for HBV. Of 12 pathogens assessed in the study, five accounted for almost all cases of cancers linked to infections. What the study reveals Lead author Dr Harriet Rumgay, Cancer Surveillance Branch, International Agency for Research on Cancer, Lyon, and other researchers combined the estimated number of new cancer cases in 2024 with estimates of what share of each cancer type is caused by different infections. Of the 12 pathogens assessed in the study, five accounted for almost all cases of cancers linked to infections. H pylori was linked to 760,000 cases in 2024 4 of all cancers diagnosed that year. HPV was linked to 750,000 cases 4, Hepatitis B virus was linked to 360,000 cases 2 EpsteinBarr virus EBV to 260,000 cases 1 and Hepatitis C virus to 160,000 cases under 1. Eastern Asia had largest number of infection-linked cancer cases Low-income and middle-income countries accounted for 77 of all infection-linked cancer cases. Eastern Asia had the largest number with 990,000 cancer cases linked to infections, 42 of the global total, driven mainly by H pylori and hepatitis B. Sub-Saharan Africa had the highest proportion of any region, with a quarter of all cancers there linked to infection, largely because of high HPV-linked cancer rates. The global burden of cancer is predicted to grow from 20 million new cases in 2024 to 35 million in 2050, due to population ageing alone. Infectious agents are a major preventable cause of cancer globally and are estimated to be the leading modifiable risk factor for cancer among women in 141 countries and men in 58 countries.

articleTitle: How ‘Hanuman Ansh’ turned Neem Karoli Baba’s ‘quiet’ Kainchi Dham into a crowded, littered hotspot
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hanuman Ansh Kainchi Dham
description: The surge has prompted concern among locals, with influencer Aishwarya Kandpal speaking out about the growing crowds, traffic, litter, and social media activity around the ashram.
body_raw: Kainchi Dham, the Uttarakhand ashram associated with Neem Karoli Baba, has seen a sharp rise in attention in recent months, with the site drawing larger crowds following the success of the film Hanuman Ansh, which has reportedly crossed Rs 400 crore worldwide. The surge has prompted concern among locals, with influencer Aishwarya Kandpal speaking out about the growing crowds, traffic, litter, and social media activity around the ashram. Kandpal, who identifies herself as a local and has a personal connection with Kainchi Dham, shared a lengthy note on Instagram urging visitors to be more mindful of the sites religious significance and its fragile mountain environment. Idk why Im posting this at almost midnight by maybe I just couldnt hold it back? As a local Im so enraged, so angry, so upset. If youre visiting - which I know A FEW HUNDREDS OF YOU ARE- read this before you go, she wrote in the caption. Explaining why she chose to speak about the issue, Kandpal began by acknowledging that the post was unlike the content she normally shares. She then described how dramatically Kainchi has changed from the place she remembers growing up around. I was at Kainchi two days ago. Most of you probably know it as Kainchi Dham - a name that the media and the internet latched onto post-2020, and then ran into overdrive after a recent feature film, she wrote. For us locals though, its always been the quiet, nondescript Kainchi. And the ashram of my Gurus, Maharajji and Siddhi Maa, she added. According to Kandpal, the site was once a relatively quiet place where locals would visit for prayer and religious activities. She also spoke about her familys longstanding association with the ashram. She said she has been fortunate enough to stay there and deliberately chose not to turn those personal experiences into social media content. My retreats, my experiences are personal, and I would like to keep it like that. Same goes for my parents and brother. Read the post View this post on Instagram A post shared by aishwarya kandpal skincare haircare indianskinblog Both my parents have been serving at the ashram for years, and post-retirement, been spending a considerable part of the year staying within the sanctum sanctorum, helping with the ashrams day-to-day activities and being a part of the management. Their visits, however, much like those of scores of other locals, have become increasingly difficult, Kandpal said. Sacred place not meant to hold so many people Kandpal described roads packed with vehicles and constant honking, saying that her father, who is over 65, gets migraines from the noise. However, she stressed that her concern goes beyond the inconvenience caused to her family. Its about the ecology of a sacred place that wasnt exactly meant to hold so many people. According to her, the change is visible across the area, from roadside waste to the rapid growth of shops and traffic. The constant honking leaves birds and animals disturbed. The sides of the roads are lined with plastic bottles, wrappers, cigarette butts-you name it The whole area suddenly has a sea of new shops selling religious artifacts and the flood of people doesnt seem to end. Everyones scrambling, everyones in a rush. Theres pollution, extreme congestion, endless selfies and endless litter. Inside the ashram, Kandpal said she has also noticed visitors ignoring restrictions on photography and filming. I dont remember it being like this at all. And then you enter the ashram and see people doing exactly what theyve been asked to not do Phones out, cameras rolling, people filming themselves inside the premises and vlogging loudly on mics You cannot do that. Kandpal pointed out that photography, filming, and excessive noise are prohibited on the premises. Youre disturbing the sanctity of a hill thats been the tapobhumi of several revered saints since pre-independence times. Theres a strict no-photography, no noise, no film rule. For a reason. Kandpal also recalled what she described as the understated nature of the ashram and the teachings associated with Maharajji and Maa. Maharajji and Maa were always against any kind of lavish show of wealth Cellphones didnt exist for a long time so naturally they werent part of the ruckus. But photography, loud noise, donations, camps, flashy visits from VIPs or ministers were all STRCITLY prohibited in the ashram and still are, she said. The simplicity was a CHOICE. Precisely why the whole culture of coming here, filming everything, putting it online, turning every visit into content feels so completely at odds with the place. Concerns extend to surrounding hills Kandpals concerns also extend to the surrounding hills, where she said the increase in vehicles and visitors is putting additional pressure on the local environment. And then there are the mountains. There are cars and taxis backed up for miles, people honking constantly, bikes revving, trying to squeeze through whatever little space is left. Our fragile hills arent meant to handle so many people and so much litter left in their wake. No points for guessing how this leaves the birds and animals in the area completely, irrevocably disturbed. And I know this probably sounds like Im asking people to not come. Im not, she added. Kandpal clarified that she was not against people visiting Kainchi Dham. Instead, she said she wanted visitors to experience the place with the same sense of quiet and simplicity that she remembers from her childhood. Because firstly, I dont think I have any right to do that. Secondly, God belongs to everyone. And thirdly, its heartening that so many people have discovered the grace of this tiny ashram. So you shouldnt have to NOT come here. I ever so SIMPLY want you to experience the Kainchi I grew up around - quiet, nondescript, no frills and miles away from the prying eyes of the media and the internet, she said. Kandpal ended her post with a request for visitors to make small changes to their behaviour while travelling to and visiting the ashram. So maybe, just maybe Leave the phone on silent for a few, leave it in your bag, come in a group instead of taking five cars, keep the honking to a minimum, take your plastic back with you, and once you enter the ashram, remember why you came here, she said. The post has gained significant attention, with several users sharing similar experiences visiting Kainchi Dham and other spiritual destinations. One more thing to add. People must not visit a pilgrimage or ashram just because their a buzz around it - a famous person endorsed it or their is a superhit movie related to that place .people must visit ashrams or temples or sacred places only when they have an inner calling to visit . And people who are actually spiritual know the fact that God and his grace are present everywhere and every being , they just need to be a good person not to show off . Visiting such places brings peace and calm but finding God and receiving his grace is a totally different thing, an Instagram user wrote. Another user compared the situation with Kasar Devi, saying, You said it so well. I recently went to kasar Devi and can understand what you are saying. The only solution to this problem is banning phones and cameras completely and you will see the rush dropping by 80. I pray for nature. A third user wrote, I am from Rudrapur and i have to think 10 times when i want to go there now.. its so much crowded now.. I miss the old Kainchi dham.. It was so peaceful few years back.

articleTitle: Drishyam 3 Box Office Day 6: Ajay Devgn film becomes 4th highest grosser, earns Rs 366.50 cr

description: Drishyam 3 Worldwide Box Office Collection Day 6: The Ajay Devgn-starrer's worldwide gross now stands at Rs 366.50 crore, making it the fourth-highest-grossing Hindi film of 2026.
body_raw: Drishyam 3 Box Office Collection Day 6 Despite a gradual and steady dip in daily earnings, director Abhishek Pathaks Drishyam 3 officially titled Drishyam The Conclusion is holding firm at the box office, with hopes of registering significantly bigger and better numbers over the weekend, particularly since it has been receiving favourable reviews from all quarters. The movies worldwide gross now stands at Rs 366.50 crore, making it the fourth-highest-grossing Hindi film of 2026, trailing Hanuman Ansh Rs 425.52 crore, Border 2 Rs 450.19 crore and Dhurandhar The Revenge Rs 1,813.39 crore. Drishyam 3 witnessed a minor dip in collections from the previous day as it earned Rs 19.50 crore on Day 5. Starring Ajay Devgn, Tabu, Shriya Saran, Jaideep Ahlawat, Rajat Kapoor, and Prakash Raj in key roles, the latest crime drama is the third and final instalment in the blockbuster franchise that commenced its journey with late director Nishikant Kamats Drishyam 2015, a remake of director Jeethu Josephs Mohanlal-starrer of the same name. However, when pressed about the possibility of another instalment in the blockbuster franchise, Devgn didnt deny it outrightly. The decision was, this is the conclusion. The decision right now is that this is the conclusion. Right now, he added.

articleTitle: Shreyas Iyer finds perfect timing for his first T20I century
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shreyas Iyer couldn't have timed his maiden T20I ton better. (Express photo by Vishal Srivastav)
description: India were in trouble at 35/2 when the skipper came to bat, but with an unbeaten 102 from 43 balls, he ensured they would be only one winner
body_raw: The last time Shreyas Iyer scored a T20I half-century before Tuesday was nearly three months ago - an unbeaten 80 against England at Bristol. Since then, he had not crossed 30 in 10 matches, with Indias top three often taking the pressure off him. The script changed dramatically at the Ekana Stadium in Lucknow. Chasing 172, Iyer walked in with India 35 India had lost both openers inside the first 21 balls. Roston Chase and Akeal Hosein had found early rhythm with the ball. Iyer absorbed the early pressure before turning the game decisively in Indias favour. The opening came in the sixth over. Shamar Joseph needed to build on the spinners start. Instead, he gave Iyer and India a release. He conceded 12 runs as Iyer went aerial over cover before repeating the treatment against Romario Shepherd. The West Indies kept bowling outside off, but on a pitch offering little movement, Iyer was able to free his arms and find the gaps. AS IT HAPPENED INDIA VS WEST INDIES 1ST T20I HIGHLIGHTS It forced the bowlers to go short. That had been regarded as a weakness in Iyers game. On Tuesday, he repeatedly brought out the pull against the rising delivery and found success. He reached his fifty in 28 balls, but the acceleration was only beginning. After seeing off the pacers, Iyer turned his attention to spin. Hosein was brought back in the 13th over and Iyer gave himself room before launching him over extra cover. The next over brought an assault on Forde, as Iyer struck two sixes before pulling another delivery over the boundary. He was given a reprieve when Joseph could not hold on to a miscued shot towards long-on. He reached his maiden T20I hundred with a six before India completed the chase in just 14.4 overs. Kishans role At the other end, Ishan Kishan found himself playing a different role. Walking in at No.3, he did not try to match Iyers aggression. Instead, he played the perfect supporting act, rotating the strike and waiting for opportunities to attack. His first boundary came when he went back to a slightly short delivery from Chase and whipped it through the leg side. Against Joseph, he then found the boundary through cover before taking advantage of another hit-me delivery from the pacer. He pulled Shepherd for a boundary and later cut Hosein through the off side, while his running kept the chase moving. There was one moment of drama when Kishan miscued a full toss towards deep cover. Forde appeared to have taken the catch, but the TV umpire ruled that the ball had touched the ground. By then, however, the partnership had taken complete control. Kishan stayed unbeaten as he and Iyer added 137 for the third wicket, allowing India to race home with 32 balls to spare. Earlier, Indias spin trio did the heavy lifting after the West Indies threatened to set a daunting score in good batting conditions. After Arshdeep Singh and Mayank Yadav failed to hit their straps early, Axar Patel, Kuldeep Yadav and Naman Dhir combined to take seven wickets for 90 runs, recovering from a middle-overs assault by Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford to keep the total manageable. After Shimron Hetmyer was run out, Axar dismissed Rovman Powell for nought to leave the West Indies 443 after six overs. But Hope and Rutherford then shifted the momentum, taking on Kuldeep and forcing Iyer to look elsewhere. Kuldeep, playing his first T20I since February, conceded 24 in his first two overs as Rutherford lofted him over cover and Hope swept him over wide long-on. Iyer brought him back after Hopes dismissal at 107 Then came the turnaround. Kuldeep found his lengths and Roston Chase fell lbw, going back to a delivery he should have played forward to. His final two overs cost only nine runs and brought two wickets, including Matthew Forde. Dhir, meanwhile, made an immediate impact on debut. After being handed the ball, he dismissed Hope for 52 before returning to remove Romario Shepherd and Shamar Springer. His three wickets gave India the control they needed. Axars miserly spell, Kuldeeps comeback and Dhirs three wickets ensured India recovered despite the pacers indiscipline. The late 36-run stand between Rutherford and Akeal Hosein gave the West Indies something to defend, but the spinners had already done enough to keep the target within reach. Brief Scores West Indies 171 all out in 19.1 overs Sherfane Rutherford 56, Shai Hope 52 Naman Dhir 331, Axar Patel 226, Kuldeep Yadav 233 lost to India 1722 in 14.4 overs Shreyas Iyer 102 not out, Ishan Kishan 37 by 8 wickets.

articleTitle: 1980s AI photo trend: 5 ChatGPT prompts to turn your photos into authentic 80s images
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ChatGPT 1980s AI photo trend
description: Depending on the prompt, your picture can resemble anything from an old family-album photograph to a college snapshot, wedding picture or film-camera portrait.
body_raw: There has always been something appealing about revisiting the past. From old-school hairstyles and clothes to music and photography, different decades keep finding their way back into the present. But until recently, recreating that feeling meant relying on costumes, filters, or carefully planned photo shoots. AI has changed that. With a simple photograph and the right prompt, you can now reimagine yourself as though you belonged to another era. The latest trend doing the rounds on social media involves turning ordinary photographs into convincing 1980s-style pictures. Rather than simply placing a retro filter over an image, AI can alter almost every visual element - from your clothes and hairstyle to the setting, lighting, colours and photography style - while keeping you recognisable. Depending on the prompt, your picture can resemble anything from an old family-album photograph to a college snapshot, wedding picture or film-camera portrait. Some styles can even recreate the look of VHS footage or a colourful 1980s Bollywood poster. If you want to try the trend yourself, upload a clear photograph to ChatGPT and experiment with these prompts 1980s classic studio portrait Transform my uploaded photo into a classic 1980s studio portrait. Keep my facial features, identity, and natural expression recognisable. Give me an authentic 1980s hairstyle and outfit, with a simple studio backdrop and soft portrait lighting. Make the image look like it was photographed on an analogue film camera in the 1980s, with subtle film grain, slightly muted colours, and natural imperfections. Avoid making it look like a modern digital photograph. 1980s family album For something that feels less posed, try recreating the warmth and imperfections of an old family photograph. Turn my uploaded photo into a warm 1980s family album photograph. Keep my face and identity unchanged while giving me period-appropriate clothing, hairstyle, and styling. Place me in a simple home setting with the feel of an ordinary family photograph from the decade. Use analogue film texture, slightly faded colours, natural lighting, mild grain and the imperfect quality of an old printed photograph. 1980s college student Want to imagine what you might have looked like on a college campus four decades ago? This prompt adds the setting and styling associated with the era. Transform my uploaded photo into an authentic 1980s college photograph. Keep my identity and facial features intact. Give me a hairstyle, outfit, and accessories inspired by college fashion of the 1980s. Place me in a vintage college campus setting with period-appropriate architecture and details. Make the photograph feel candid and nostalgic, with analogue film grain, natural lighting and the slightly soft appearance of an old printed photograph. 1980s wedding photograph This one recreates the look of a traditional wedding picture, complete with period styling and the slightly faded quality of photographs kept in old family albums. Transform my uploaded photo into a nostalgic 1980s wedding photograph. Keep my facial features and identity recognisable. Dress me in authentic wedding clothing and styling inspired by the 1980s, with period-appropriate hair and accessories. Create a traditional wedding setting with vintage decorations and analogue photography. Make it look like a real photograph from an old family album, with natural film grain, soft lighting and slightly faded colours. 1980s Bollywood poster For an unmistakably Indian take on the trend, you can go beyond photography and recreate the visual language of an old Bollywood poster. Transform this photo into a colourful 1980s Bollywood film poster. Use hand-painted poster aesthetics, dramatic lighting, saturated reds, yellows, and blues, bold typography-inspired graphic elements, and an exaggerated cinematic composition. Keep the persons identity and facial features recognisable.

body_raw: Radhika Apte is in the news again, because apparently a sex scene starring her from an upcoming film called Parched has leaked online and gone viral. Now Ive never actually watch a Radhika Apte film in the theatre yes, yes you can gasp about that later, but Ive come to know her name thanks to the alleged leaks of sex scenes and nude photos. Last year, it was a nude video of the actress from a short film directed by Anurag Kashyap, and now this year its a leaked sex scene. Cue the outrage, the gasp, the sensational headlines with words bold, sex, and nude all being present. And there we were, thinking this is the 21st century, an age where perhaps weve finally made our peace with sex in cinema. But as Aptes co-star in the film Adil Hussain rightly asks, why call it a Radhika Apte sex scene? Because when it comes to sex, India and Bollywood remain as hypocritical as ever, and the gaze remains firmly on the female body. Lets admit theres a certain hypocrisy when leaked sex scenes go viral as only the female star becomes the sole focus. ReadRadhika Apte-Adil Hussains sex scene from Parched leaked online While sex might be an act between two persons, the consequences it seems are reserved only for the females. And this is not just a Bollywood problem. In Hollywood too, women have been made infamous and slut-shamed, because of a sex tape leaks. And it is their name that remains firmly attached to the scandal, while the man is conveniently forgotten. Remember Paris Hiltons sex tape? Pretty sure youll have to Google the name of the man who was in it. Then in India, theres the larger problem of how we view sex, especially when it comes on screen. We might no longer be relying on two flowers or shots of feet touching to show sex on the big screen, but as these leaks show, were still in the Neanderthal age on this subject. We want to see every bit of sex that leaks, and yet dont want to talk about sex education in our schools. You leak only the sex scene and no other beautiful scenes from the film. It only shows that we are extremely obsessed with sex and yet we dont want to talk about it, Hussain told IndianExpress.com. And he nails the point. For a society thats all about preserving traditional Indian values with modernity, we are strangely obsessed with news around bold scenes, or of an actress in a bikini. When our politicians claim bikinis are ruining society, we are quick to condemn them. And yet when an actress dons a bikini for a film scene, it becomes big news. An actress wearing a bikini in 2016 in India surely cant be a surprise anymore, but Bollywood and yes, we the media, insists it is one. The reason Bikinis and sex scenes might have finally come to India, but Bollywoods approach on womens bodies and their sexuality remains centred around titillation. And it is an approach that continues to make money, so why bother changing it?

articleTitle: Surfeit of silver paints a picture of ‘what could have been’ for India at Asiad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: (Clockwise) India's Tajinderpal Singh Toor, Esha Singh, Elavenil Valarivan, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Ancy Sojan with their silver medals at 2026 Asian Games. (PTI & AP)
description: Aichi-Nagoya showed that competition has got tougher in the continent, and even personal best performances may not always be enough to challenge the cream
body_raw: Day 1 A 10.4 and 10.1 from Elavenil Valarivan on her last two shots of the 10m air rifle erased the Indians handy 1.5 lead, to see the first gold missed by India at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. What gets lost in the lament over the 27 silvers is acknowledgement that Japans Hinata Taichi shot 10.6 and 10.2 to snatch that gold - coming out of the blue, given Japan didnt have a single medal in this event since 1994. India finished tied on gold with Uzbekistan at 21, and only a last-day scramble helped push it up, with two extra silvers giving it fourth place. But all those silvers were gold medals lost. Accepting that even Indias best-ever showing in womens air rifle, Elavenils silver, might not be good enough for gold is central to understanding why the country was stuck at just four the first week, reaching double digits 10 only on the 11th day of the Games. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage The ultimate tally of 21 was seven off the 2023 Asiad with 28 gold, while total medal haul was 21 less than the 106 at Hangzhou. The drop has come in several sports Shooting 22 to 15 4 golds less, Athletics 29 to 24 5 gold less, Tennis 2 to 0 1 gold less, Badminton 3 to 1 1 gold less Rowing 6 to 1 Equestrian 2 to 0 1 gold less. While archery made fantastic gains in recurve, its total count stayed constant at nine from 2023, with five gold medals, the same as last time. Squash retained its five medals, but with a significant drop of two gold. Wrestling has maintained its count of six. While men added two gold to the nil last time, and won five of the six Indian medals, womens wrestling dropped from three last time to the one silver upgrade of Antim Panghal. Sujeet Kalkal and Aman Sehrawat will be expected to carry the momentum to Los Angeles. ALSO READ As the Asian Games close, with a last-minute gold rush, India finish fourth Boxing made real gains, going up from five to six medals-and significantly three gold from none last time. The golf gold for Pranavi Urs is an uptick, as is the womens team silver. However, a few medal drops are worrying. In badminton, Lakshya Sen could not defend HS Prannoy bronze while Ayush Shetty had a poor Games. Asiad medals are toughest in badminton, and Satwik-Chirag gold was missing in the 2026 tally. Shooting sent a star-studded womens air pistol troika, but a medal was nowhere in sight after poor qualifications. While Suruchi Phogat salvaged matters with a strong comeback for the Mixed Team gold and Esha Singh fought four shoot-offs to take sports pistol silver, individual golds were out of reach till Neeru Dhanda won in trap. India had regressed in 50m 3 position since the Paris Olympics, with two silvers in the event, while they had won two gold in Hangzhou, among other medals. Hits and misses Parul Chaudhary recorded her Personal Best PB in 5,000m to take a second bronze. Steeplechaser Avinash Sable, defending a gold medal, did his seasons best but missed a medal by four seconds to finish fourth. The next rung in steeplechase isnt on the horizon. Other freakish circumstances struck. Murali Sreesankar, looking to upgrade his silver, slipped on the takeoff on his fourth attempt and was in no position to contend for gold. Two Chinese did their best in their fifth attempt to leapfrog Ancy Sojan in the long jump. The Indian could not summon a 6.60 jump, though her best this season is a national record. Hurdler Jyothi Yarraji, triple jumper Praveen Chitravel and decathlete Thowfeeq Noushad couldnt register a mark to be in contention in their events. While AFI president Adille Sumariwala had stressed that the athletes would peak at the Asiad, the periodisation seemed to have gone awry as the push for the Commonwealth Games disrupted fitness for Asiad, including taking Neeraj Chopra out of contention. The two big events within two months of each other also saw some athletes bomb at both places. The rowing federation switched up combinations two days before the race, after crews had trained together for four years. They got an Australian expert to convey the news, and he didnt explain why his plan for gold didnt come through, or why the rowers were not kept in the loop. No gold fetched up either it was chaos injected into an erstwhile well-oiled unit. Equestrian was blighted by contested selections. A gold and bronze from Hangzhou got casually tossed out, finishing at zero. Some losses are nuanced - could Gulveer Singh have focused on one event and gone all out for gold, instead of four races in five days, finishing with two silver and one bronze? Are double-starters in shooting those who are fielded in two events costing India gold? Track and field athletes scored 11 personal bests, nine silvers and three seasons bests. But the net result was one gold. It proves both that the competition has levelled up and Indians, even at their best, are only playing catch-up.

articleTitle: Is Trump’s ‘forever war’ a liability in the US midterm elections?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: us midterm elections
description: Contrary to Trump’s expectations, the prolonged war in Iran has gradually crept into domestic prices
body_raw: President Donald Trump seems anxious about the upcoming US midterm elections-voting is on November 3. So much so that he confused Brazil with India in a recent social media post when comparing the vote-counting process, an issue that has seen intense debate in the current American political zeitgeist. Since Trumps loss to Joe Biden in the 2020 election, which the former has called rigged, he has repeated the claim more than 100 times publicly and has taken the fight to the US Supreme Court. At the heart of the issue is the vote-by-mail provision that Trump has railed against. At least four developments have riled up Trump Early and mail voting are already underway in more than 40 states almost one-third of American voters vote by mail Trump is reeling under one of the lowest approval ratings on the back of rising energy prices and a new forever war in Iran there is a sense that the Democrats may just edge out the Republicans in both the House and the Senate, and finally, the Supreme Court has just begun a new term with the anticipation that it may take up new cases on election issues like gun control, immigration and religious issues. In March 2026, Trump issued an Executive Order that sought to limit how Americans could vote, particularly through mail, and vowed to do away with voting machines. Consequently, the Supreme Court struck down Trumps attempts to restrict mail ballots. More than 23 states came together to appeal against Trumps Executive Order, which now remains blocked by a nationwide injunction and will almost certainly not apply this November. Then, there is the question of nationwide popularity. Trumps average approval rating fell to 38 per cent in late September, the lowest in his second term. A little over 35 per cent of Americans believe the country is headed in the right direction. On the generic congressional ballot, Democrats average 52 per cent against 43 per cent for Republicans, the widest margin since Trump returned to office. If the numbers and the sentiment do translate into votes, Democrats may likely win. To Trumps advantage, however, the actual voting may vary state-wise, altering some of these expectations. For the Democrats, the historical record may be more favourable. Since the 1950s, the presidents party has lost an average of more than 25 House seats in midterm elections, with losses plummeting further when the presidential approval rating is below 50 per cent. In his first term, Trump himself lost 40 House seats in 2018 Barack Obama lost 63 in 2010 and Bill Clinton 54 in 1994. Perhaps the exceptions are 1998 and 2002, which are attributed to the popularity of a president or an era-defining post-911 rallying of sentiments. Trump, on the contrary, has been sucked into a war abroad and is struggling to keep price rises at home under control. The economy, along with the cost of living, lies at the heart of the political contestations. Contrary to Trumps expectations, the prolonged war in Iran has gradually crept into domestic prices. While rising petrol prices gas and electricity bills are affecting households, a spike in diesel prices is impacting the truckers supply chain and farming, adding pressure on Republicans. Republicans hold a narrow House majority, and Democrats need a net gain of only three seats to win it-making the House win a stronger possibility than the Senate. What has complicated the picture is a gerrymandering war between the two parties. The process, which can happen once every decade, could give the Republicans an edge with new maps in Texas, Florida, Ohio, North Carolina, Missouri, among others, which could yield Republicans around 16 seats on paper, against roughly six for Democrats, mostly from California. What may prove decisive in the end is how many Republican-held seats turn Democrat, if any. In the Senate, the current Republican lead may prove to be a steeper climb for the Democrats. Republicans hold 53 seats, so Democrats need a net gain of four for an outright majority, along with the two independents who caucus with the latter. Although international issues tend to weigh less in midterms, given the prolonged nature and continued US commitments to the Middle East, this November could be different. On October 1, Trump ordered a third carrier strike group, led by the USS Theodore Roosevelt, and another 10,000 troops to the region. The carrier is not expected to arrive until late November, after the polls have closed, but the political signalling has been dire. The deployment follows the virtual collapse of efforts to secure a workable ceasefire or any modus vivendi with Tehran. The war has also spread beyond Iran with the Houthis renewing missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, drawing Riyadhs ongoing response. China adds a layer of contradiction in US politics. As Trump has sought constructive strategic stability with China, extending their trade truce to January 2027, many see the stability as structurally incongruent. For the soyabean farm-state Republicans in Iowa and Nebraska, the truce with China is a lifeline, but for China hawks, it looks like accommodation. For Americas partners, including India, the more consequential question is not who wins in November but what follows. The writer is Deputy Director of the Strategic Studies Programme at ORF

articleTitle: Jackie Shroff reveals why actors rejected the role of Chunnilal in Shah Rukh Khan’s Devdas

description: In a recent interview, Jackie Shroff revealed that he was offered the role of Chunnilal in Sanjay Leela Bhansali’s Devdas only after several other actors had turned it down.
body_raw: Jackie Shroff recently opened up about playing the iconic Chunnilal in Sanjay Leela Bhansalis Devdas, revealing that the role came to him only after several other actors had turned it down. During an interview with Republic Bharat, Jackie recalled his Devdas days after a woman in the audience told him that she had watched the film five times. Reacting to her response, the actor said, Nobody was taking that role because Shah Rukh Khan saab was essaying Devdas character. To those whom the film had been offered, they said, My characters name isnt even there.Devdas is his name. So, when nobody accepts the role, it comes to me, and I said, Yes, Ill do this role. Madhuri Dixit ji is there, and I am the king of her characters Chandramukhi brothel. Why shouldnt I sit there? I said, Very good and asked whats the second thing that I have. They filmmaker said There is one song for you and these are the dialogues. I read the dialogues, and I said, Even if my role comes during the interval, it wont matter to me because I am seen merely by standing. And, I was seen in Devdas. He asked the female fan, You also saw it. I was visible, right? Continuing further, Jackie said, When nobody accepts the role, they come to me, and I dont mind. Also Read Everyone was thrashing me Salman Khan recalls how Dus Ka Dum saved him from career downfall During the conversation, Jackie Shroff credited actor-filmmaker Dev Anand with spotting him and offering him a junior artistes role in Swami Dada 1982, in which he played one of Shakti Kapoors henchmen. Mithun Chakraborty played the lead. Shroff also expressed gratitude to filmmaker Subhash Ghai for giving him his breakthrough as a leading man with Hero 1983. articleTitle: Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat train: Check route, stops, timings and frequency
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat train has been approved. (Image: Ministry of Railways)
description: Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express has been approved by the Ministry of Railways. Check train numbers, route, major stoppages, timings, distance and weekly frequency here.
body_raw: Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express The Ministry of Railways has approved the introduction of a new Amrit Bharat Express between Bhuj in Gujarat and Barauni in Bihar. The new train is expected to improve rail connectivity between Gujarat and Bihar, while also connecting several important cities in Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. The Amrit Bharat trains offer a travel experience comparable to the Vande Bharat Express, but are specifically designed to provide affordable service for passengers from lower and lower-middle income category. Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express Train number, distance and travel time The Bhuj-Barauni-Bhuj Amrit Bharat Express will operate as train number 19427 The train will cover a distance of around 2,532 km and will operate via Gorakhpur in around 10 hours and 30 minutes. It will operate at speeds ranging from 110 kmph to 130 kmph. Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express Stoppages During its journey between Bhuj and Barauni, the Amrit Bharat Express will stop at several important stations. The major stoppages include Samakhiali, Ahmedabad, Ratlam, Kota, Sawai Madhopur, Gangapur City, Bharatpur, Mathura, Hathras, Bareilly, Izzatnagar, Pilibhit, Lakhimpur, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Siwan, Chhapra, Hajipur, Muzaffarpur and Samastipur, among others. The route will provide connectivity to passengers travelling between Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express Timings Train number 19427 Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express will depart from Bhuj at 530 PM and arrive at Barauni at 405 AM. In the return direction, train number 19428 Barauni-Bhuj Amrit Bharat Express will depart from Barauni at 1155 PM and reach Bhuj at 115 PM. Bhuj-Barauni Amrit Bharat Express Frequency The Bhuj-Barauni service will operate three days a week Monday, Wednesday and Saturday. The Barauni-Bhuj service will operate on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday. Launched in 2023, the Amrit Bharat Express train is equipped with advanced features such as semi-automatic couplers, fire detection systems, sealed gangways and talk-back units. This modern train comprise of 11 General Class coaches, 8 Sleeper Class coaches, 01 Pantry car and 02 Luggage cum Divyangjan coaches.

articleTitle: Shanthi, Sivasangari, Thinaah: Malaysia, Singapore’s best tracing Indian roots
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sivasangari Subramaniam (L), Thinaah Muralitharan and Shanti Pereira have been among the Indian-origin stars at the Asian Games. (Reuters/Badminton Photo/X)
description: Born and raised in South-East Asia, the three sporting stars shine for their countries winning two gold and ensuring another medal.
body_raw: This silk route actually ferried Kanjivaram and Katan silk sarees from India to the Kedahan province in Malaysia where Sivasangari Subramaniam adorned the most gorgeous Indian weaves. Peacock blues and fuschias and royal purples for temple visits every Diwali has been a tradition, accompanying her parents Subramaniam Kaniappan and Valli Nagappan in Sungai Petani. The town has one of Mahatma Gandhis tallest statues and a thriving Tamil community. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage The city answered an unlikely question to the most desperate search for the next Malaysian squash star after the legendary Nicol David. Sivasangari pr shivashankari was a petite and super-motivated prodigious youngster, and when she returned from the U15 British Juniors in 2012, her entire class at SMK Sultanah Asmah landed to receive her at the airport. Having sealed the first-ever Olympic singles spot for squash after beating Anahat Singh in the final, the Cornell University graduate will be greeted similarly on her return to Malaysia. 6TH GOLD MEDAL FOR MALAYSIA ANOTHER LA28 TICKET 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Squash Final Womens Singles Sivasangari Subramaniam 3-0 Anahat Singh 11-4 11-4 11-7sangari99 successfully defends her womens singles Asian Games title Back-to-back. pic.twitter.comXUaIJFd2c9 - Giarc Nibisna craigansibin September 27, 2026 Sivasangari is one of three Asiad champions with Indian roots, born and raised in the South-East Asian sporting system. Badminton star Thinaah Muralitharan, who ensured a medal after defeating Treesa Jolly-Gayatri Gopichand alongside partner Pearly Tan, and Singapores 200m sprint champion Shanthi Pereira are the others. The talent of Sivasangari, now World No.5, was evident at 9, and she only got better developing skills and smarts in the super-competitive Malaysian clubs. While she was making quick strides in sport winning NCAA titles for Cornell University, a road accident when her car rear-ended into a lorry, shook Malaysia. It was on the same stretch that had witnessed Kento Momotas accident a few years ago, and the country prayed as she was taken into emergency surgery with injuries to her head and C1 vertebrae. Sivasangari proceeded to return to the PSA Tour, win Asiad titles and was also the bearer of the Malur Gemilang national flag at Hangzhou. Malaysian Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim would call her proof of the determination, discipline, and fighting spirit of our athletes in bringing honour to Malaysia internationally. The high-achieving and hard-working Tamil community of Malaysia found a new hero after Nicol David, the eight-time Malaysian world champion and five-time Asiad gold winner, whose father Desmond David is an engineer of Tamil descent. 200m champ with Indian roots Shanthis favourite satins are ribbons in white and red, so when she sprints over the curve to hit the home stretch of the 200m, Singapores colours trail her like a comets tail. Then the gold gets added on the podium. Veronica Shanti Pereira equalled her seasons best of 22.78 seconds -0.2 to defend her 200m title at the Asian Games in Nagoya AsianGames2026 pic.twitter.comF1zPajP63O - Owen OwenM September 27, 2026 Her father Clarence Pereira moved to Singapore from Thiruvananthapuram. Her mother, Bridget Jeet Pereira, came from Amritsar. Her siblings are Shobana, Anand and Seema, and when shes not sprinting at the Asian Games, clocking 22.78s on Sunday, she dons a Kasavu visiting Kerala often. It was her grandfather who migrated from Vettukad. But Singapore went crazy when she ended their 49-year-wait for an Asiad track field medal at Hangzhou, taking silver in 100m. Singapore happily asked their Sprint Queen to lead the contingent at the Paris Olympics opening ceremony. Thinaah, the daughter of Indian-origin doctor and engineer, has a successful partnership with Tan, and thanks her for brushing up her Mandarin so communicating became easier. Her father S Muralitharan had been an engineer, and mother Parimala Devi Kalingam a doctor. The pressure of academics weighed on her as she grew up in Selangor. But badminton is a religion in Malaysia, and her siblings all trained at a club. Its like a family thing, she would once tell lifestyleasia.com. My sister stopped because shes more of the studious type. And my brother is an engineer now. So, Im the only one in the badminton field laughs. My family background is quite studious, Im the odd one in the family. I wanted to prove a point, that sports could bring me somewhere as well. The World Championships silver medallist and twice Commonwealth Games champ, now 28, finally ensured a long coveted Asian Games medal after beating Treesa-Gayatri in an attacking barrage to make the semis. The partnership had made badminton sense, both tall, powerful hitters. But communication had been an issue, so Thinaah added Mandarin to English, Malay and Tamil that she speaks fluently. When Im angry I dont know what language I speak. But she Tan understands, she would chuckle. They didnt forget their Indian roots, but with a World Top 5 in squash, doubles badminton star and a 200m gold medallist sprinter, they bust myths of restrictive genetics, even as Malaysia and Singapore flaunt their champions.

articleTitle: SBI credit card fee jumps from Rs 499 to Rs 2,999, woman wins Rs 50,000 compensation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Consumer Commission SBI Cards Woman Consumer News Credit Card Fee SBI
description: The commission was hearing a consumer complaint alleging deficiency in SBI credit card services and unfair trade practice over the issuance of the card with higher annual fees than the complainant said she had opted for.
body_raw: A Delhi Consumer Commission has held SBI Cards guilty of deficiency in service and ordered to pay Rs 50,000 to a woman who alleged that she had opted for a credit card with an annual fee of Rs 499 but was issued one carrying a Rs 2,999 fee in 2023. She repeatedly asked the company to change the card, but her request was not resolved. Nearly three years after she filed the complaint, the commission ordered the card to be closed. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, South-II, Delhi president Monika Aggarwal Srivastava and members Dr Rajender Dhar and Ritu Garodia, were hearing a complaint filed by one Neha Chaudhary against SBI Cards Payment Services Limited. It is difficult to comprehend as to the reason why the card was not closed if it could not be downgraded, the commission observed on September 18, finding SBI Cards guilty of deficiency in service. According to Chaudharys complaint, she had opted for a Simply Click credit card carrying an annual fee of Rs 499 plus GST. She alleged that the companys agent instead obtained her biometric KYC for a Club Vistara card. A card was issued with a credit limit of Rs 73,000, but she found that it carried an annual fee of Rs 2,999 along with GST. Woman repeatedly asks for card change A bill dated August 3, 2023 showed annual fees of Rs 2,999 and GST of Rs 592.32. On August 4, she emailed SBI Cards stating that she had not used the card and requested that it be changed to a Simply Save card, with the applicable charges. SBI Cards replied on August 10, 2023 that its representatives had been unable to contact her on her registered mobile number. It said upgrading or downgrading a credit card required OTP validation and asked her to receive a representatives call or contact its helpline. Chaudhary then informed the company that she had contacted the helpline but the requested change had not been made. On August 11, she said she had called multiple times and was told that the card could not be changed and the fees could not be waived. She also informed the company that she had approached the RBI Ombudsman. On August 18, SBI Cards informed her that it was unable to process the downgrade request. She sent a legal notice through email the same day. The commission noted that Chaudhary had contacted the company through email and its helpline multiple times, but was eventually told that the downgrade could not be processed without any reason being assigned. Commission questions why card was not closed The commission recorded that SBI Cards neither appeared nor rebutted the complainants allegations. Its written statement was not taken on record because it was time-barred under an order dated October 24, 2024. The commission took note of an earlier February 2026 decision of the Karnataka State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, which referred to RBI directions dated April 21, 2022 on credit card closure. Those directions provide that a closure request should be honoured within seven working days, subject to payment of dues, and that issuers must provide multiple channels for such requests. Failure to complete closure within seven working days attracts a penalty of Rs 500 per calendar day where there is no outstanding amount. The commission said it was difficult to comprehend why the card was not closed if it could not be downgraded. The commission held SBI Cards guilty of deficiency in service and directed it to close the credit card. It also directed the company to generate the bill as on August 4, 2023, the date of Chaudharys request for the change, provided the bill had not already been paid. The commission ordered SBI Cards to pay Rs 50,000 compensation. Takeaway If a credit card comes with a fee or charges different from what you agreed to, raise the issue immediately in writing and keep copies of all emails, bills and complaint records. If the issuer cannot make the requested change, ask for closure of the card and seek appropriate consumer redress rather than continuing to accept charges you dispute. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Delhi1800-11-4000 or call the National Consumer Helpline at1915for assistance. articleTitle: Vijay Deverakonda says Rashmika Mandanna tells him ‘I love you’ 10-15 times a day: ‘More mature’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna have opened up about the importance of expressing love in a relationship.
description: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna opened up about love, marriage and the importance of expressing feelings in their relationship during a podcast with Prakhar Gupta.
body_raw: Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna recently opened up about their bond, their marriage and how their understanding of love has evolved over the years. The couple also shared how little efforts keep a relationship going. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. In a podcast with Prakhar Gupta, calling Rashmika the more mature one, Vijay says, Rashmika is more mature when it comes to relationships. Look at how shes talking. She makes sure she tells me I love you at least 10-15 times a day, and she tells me that its important for me to express it too. I constantly feel it, but I shouldnt think, Okay, she knows it, so I dont need to say it. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Rashmika Mandanna rashmikamandanna Why is it important to express love Most people assume the person they love already knows it. They have shown up, stayed, and handled the practical things, so surely the feeling is obvious. That assumption is where a lot of quiet distance begins, because as Dr Chandni Tugnait, MD A.M Psychotherapist, Life Alchemist, Coach Healer, Founder Director, Gateway of Healing says, love that is felt but never said often goes unnoticed by the very person it is meant for. She also explains why it is necessary to express feelings instead of assuming the other person already knows. Unsaid love gets misread A partner cannot see whats inside your head, and everyday acts of care are easy to read as habit or duty. Saying it plainly removes the guesswork and turns a feeling the other person had into something they can actually hold onto. It calms the background worry Many people carry a faint, constant question about whether they are still wanted. Hearing love expressed regularly answers that question before it grows, which tends to lower stress and make both people feel safer, including the one saying it, since voicing a feeling also strengthens it. It stops the relationship coasting In long relationships, affection is usually the first thing to be said less often, simply because life gets busy and the words start to feel unnecessary. Small, regular expressions work like maintenance, keeping two people connected instead of running on autopilot. It fills a quiet gap In many Indian households, love is shown through food, favours, and quiet sacrifice rather than words, and that language is real. Saying it aloud does not replace those acts, it simply makes sure the feeling behind them is actually heard. None of this means that the number of times matters most. Words work only when actions back them, and honesty counts more than frequency. But a feeling spoken at the right moment often does what months of silent effort cannot, which is to leave no room for doubt, she adds. The importance of physical touch As conversation flowed, Rashmika and Vijay kept brushing their feet against each other. That is when Vijay asks Rashmika what the most romantic thing that he has done for her is. Immediately, Prakhar Gupta replies, First of all, what youre doing right now. However, that was normal for the duo. This goes on 24x7, they say. Vijay later says, Some physical touch should always be there. That is one part of it. Rashmika also agrees with him. She says, I feel like we just live in a very romantic world, so. To this, Vijay adds, Maybe what is romantic for you is normal for us. Their upcoming movie Vijay Deverakonda and Rashmika Mandanna aregearing up for the release of their period dramaRanabaali, markinganother on-screen reunion for the actors. Directed by Rahul Sankrityan and produced by Naveen Yerneni and Y Ravi Shankar under the banner of Mythri Movie Makers, the period action drama is scheduled to release in theatres worldwide on October 16. articleTitle: Railways to pay Rs 47,000 fine 8 years after family ‘robbed’ in Mewar Express AC coach
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Uttarakhand Consumer Commission Indian Railways Robbery AC Coach Passenger Railway Police Consumer News
description: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Commission was hearing the Railways’ appeal against the district commission awarding compensation for the theft of belongings of a family during the Mewar Express journey.
body_raw: The Uttarakhand State Consumer Commission held Indian Railways liable for negligence after a family travelling in a reserved AC coach of the Mewar Express reported that thieves forcibly took away their valuables near Mathura in the early hours of July 2, 2018. The commission also upheld Rs 47,222 payout ordered by the District Consumer Commission, Dehradun. The Uttarakhand State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president, Kumkum Rani, and member B S Manral heard an appeal filed by the Union of India and railway authorities against the May 11, 2022 order of the district commission, which had directed the Railways to pay Rs 37,222 towards the loss suffered by the complainants, Rs 25,000 towards mental agony and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. The negligence on the part of the railway administration and its servants is clearly proved, the state commission said on October 5, referring to the circumstances of the incident. It found that the reserved coach doors had been left open during the night and that there was no coach attendant, police personnel or TTE inside the coach when the theft occurred. The dispute arose from the familys return journey from Udaipur to New Delhi on July 1, 2018. They were travelling in the reserved AC coach of the Mewar Express and reached Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station on July 2. During the journey, when the train reached Mathura at around 4 am, the complainants said unauthorised persons entered the coach and forcibly took away the belongings of two passengers. Theft reported during early-morning journey According to the complaint, one of the persons forcibly took away a large bag belonging to Veena Dobhal, who was sleeping at her berth. The bag had been kept under her head, below the pillow. She woke up when the bag was taken and raised an alarm. Other members of the family and passengers also woke up and tried to catch the person, but he jumped from the moving train with the bag. The passengers then searched for the coach attendant, RPF personnel, and the TTE but did not find any of them available in the coach. The TTE was subsequently contacted and informed about the theft. An FIR form was filled in and later handed over to the Government Railway Police at Hazrat Nizamuddin. A Zero FIR was lodged at the railway police station at 750 am on July 2, 2018. The complainants told the commission that they had not been able to ascertain the outcome of the investigation despite their efforts. Railways blamed passengers The Railways denied negligence and argued that passengers were responsible for safeguarding luggage carried by them. It relied on the provisions of the Railways Act concerning liability for loss or damage to luggage and pointed out that the family had neither booked the luggage with the Railways nor declared that they were carrying valuables. The Railways also argued that passengers were advised inside the coach to secure their luggage with a chain and that the complainants had not followed the instruction. It maintained that reserved coaches were meant only for authorised passengers and that coach attendants and TTEs were responsible for keeping the doors closed during the night. The state commission rejected this defence in the circumstances of the case. It noted that the complainants had specifically alleged that the coach doors and the end doors of the vestibule had not been kept locked. The commission also noted that the Railways had not specifically denied this allegation and had not produced evidence from the coach attendant or TTE to establish that the doors had been kept closed. If the doors of the coach were locked closed, there was no occasion for the unauthorised persons miscreants to have enter into the coach and commit theft robbery, the commission observed. It further rejected the argument that the availability of remedies under railway laws barred the consumer complaint, noting that the Consumer Protection Act provides remedies in addition to those available under other laws. The commission awarded Rs 47,222 in total, comprising Rs 37,222 compensation and Rs 10,000 litigation expenses, with 7 per cent annual interest on Rs 37,222 from July 31, 2020, until payment. Takeaway Passengers may seek compensation for valuables stolen from a reserved railway coach when they can establish that the loss resulted from negligence or misconduct by railway staff, such as failure to secure the coach or prevent unauthorised entry. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories Uttarakhand 1800-180-4188 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: Amrinder Singh Raja Warring out, why Congress chose Pargat Singh to lead Punjab unit
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pargat Singh to lead Punjab Congress, Punjab Congress, Pargat Singh, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, Punjab Congress chief replacement, Sachin Pilot Punjab Congress report, Charanjit Singh Channi, Vijay Inder Singla, Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, Punjab Assembly Elections 2027, Rahul Gandhi Punjab PCC appointment, Malwa Doaba caste arithmetic Punjab, Punjab Congress factionalism
description: Sources say feedback Sachin Pilot received from leaders, including those considered close to Warring, was that he would not be able to inspire confidence among a large section of leaders.
body_raw: Months before the Assembly elections, the Congress on Friday appointed a new state unit president in Punjab, hoping to finally put a debilitating factional feud behind it. The party appointed former Indian hockey captain Pargat Singh the president of the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee, hours after Amrinder Singh Raja Warring resigned from the post. After handing over his resignation to Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi in Delhi, Warring blamed All India Congress Committees AICC Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot for the change. I think that the new general secretary thought it best to remove me chhutti kar deni chahiye, he said. This marks the culmination of a months-long battle for control of Punjab Congress between Warring, the Ludhiana MP, and former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi, the Jalandhar MP. Channi was angling for the post but ultimately had to reach a compromise and agree to the high commands decision to promote Pargat Singh, who has been the MLA from Jalandhar Cantonment since 2012. The sense in the high command was that almost the entire top state leadership was at odds with Warring. That is why it did not act on the Ajay Maken committees recommendations for a leadership change. A large section of the party, both in Delhi and Punjab, felt that Warring continued to hold on to the post because of support from Bhupesh Baghel, who was Pilots predecessor as AICC state in-charge. However, once Baghel - who faced pushback from the Channi camp - was replaced last month, it became apparent that Warrings time at the helm of the state Congress was nearing its end, sources said. Sources said the feedback Pilot received from leaders, including those considered close to Warring, was that he would not be able to inspire confidence among a large section of leaders and that keeping him in charge would complicate efforts to win back Punjab. Pilot is learnt to have conveyed this to party president Mallikarjun Kharge and Gandhi and left it to them to take the call. Earlier this week, the party finally decided to replace Warring, but Pilot, sources said, did not want the change of guard to be announced through a statement. He requested the leadership to meet Warring and ensure the change of guard is smooth and dignified. However, Warring sensed the mood and tried to mount pressure by making his unhappiness public. He changed his account bio on X, but the leadership had made up its mind by then, sources said. The high command, they said, was clear that appointing Channi or former Deputy CM Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, the current MP from Gurdaspur, the PCC president could upset the apple cart, as both of them are CM aspirants along with state LoP Partap Singh Bajwa. While the names of some Hindu leaders - including Vijay Inder Singla, Rana K P Singh and Bharat Bhushan Ashu - were discussed, the leadership was clear that a Sikh should be at the helm of the state Congress. And that too a figure known across Punjab, but who would not be in the race for the CM post if the party wins power next year. That is how the leadership zeroed in on Pargat Singh. The 62-year-old Singh is from Mithapur in Jalandhar, a village known for producing hockey players. Singh played as a full-back and is widely regarded as one of the best defenders of his generation. He represented India at the Olympics in Seoul 1988, Barcelona 1992, and Atlanta 1996, captaining the team in the last two editions. At Atlanta 1996, he was also the countrys flag-bearer in the opening ceremony. Singhs storied sports career includes winning a bronze medal at the 1986 Asian Games in Seoul and a silver at the 1990 Asian Games in Beijing. He received the Arjuna Award in 1989 and the Padma Shri in 1998. After retiring, he coached the mens national team and later held roles in hockey administration in Punjab, including as general secretary of Hockey Punjab 2017. He started his political career with the Shiromani Akali Dal SAD in 2012, when he won Jalandhar Cantonment for the first time. However, he broke from the Akalis in 2016 before moving to the Congress the following year.

description: The Delhi state consumer commission directed a holiday provider to refund Rs 1.75 lakh and pay Rs 1.5 lakh for mental agony and litigation costs.
body_raw: The Delhi State Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission recently ordered a hospitality and holiday provider chain to pay Rs 3.25 lakh to a man, as it was held guilty of deficiency in service for not issuing a membership card and allotting the promised plot after collecting the payment for a holiday membership scheme. President Sangita Dhingra Sehgal and Member Bimla Kumari were hearing a plea filed by a man who had paid Rs 1.75 lakh to a holiday provider chain for obtaining membership of a scheme which claimed to provide holiday offers, benefits and a complimentary plot on Bombay-Goa Highway. The opposite party holiday provider was deficient in providing its services to the complainant the man, as it failed to render the services and facilities assured under the Mr Cool Global Parivar Life Membership, including issuance of the membership card and allotment of the complimentary plot measuring 2000 sq. ft. at Kolad, Maharashtra, the September 28 order read. The commission further said that the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, came into being in order to protect the interests of consumers who are affected by the acts of the service providers, who in order to attract the consumers, tend to make lucrative offers but when it comes to actually providing the offered services, they take a step back. The man claimed that in April, 2008, he met the business promotion executives of the hospitality and holiday provider chain who were carrying out word-of-mouth business promotion of the scheme at Connaught Place, New Delhi. According to the man, the hospitality chain was providing various services and facilities in the scheme, including Lifetime membership for the member, spouse, and parents for life, and children up to the age of 18 years. Annual subscription of Rs 4,000. Lifelong, transferable, and global membership. 2000 square feet plot at Golf Village, Kolad, Mumbai, situated on the Bombay-Goa Highway, to be registered in the name of the man. Free holiday for 7 days and 6 nights at any of the properties of the chain for 30 years under Resort Condominiums International RCI membership. 3 days and 3 nights holiday for 5 years by paying Rs. 350 per day Food and Beverages charges extra. Five years free membership to RCI-affiliated clubs. Holiday in Goa for 3 nights and 2 days for a couple with one-way air ticket. The man alleged that, lured by the genuineness of the offer and services, he opted for Mr Cool Global Parivar Life Membership at the rate of Rs 2 lakh and paid Rs 1.75 lakh after a discount of Rs 25,000 was given to him. The man was also allotted a membership number. The man contended that he was assured by the holiday provider that he would receive his membership card and other information, brochures, etc., within two weeks so that he could enjoy the benefits of his membership during the summer vacation. However, no membership card was received, and the entire vacation plan made by the man with his family members was ruined. The man stated that he had to face a very awkward situation as he had also included one of his married relatives and their children. The man was forced to file a consumer complaint because even after calling various officials of the holiday provider and furnishing different documents that the provider asked for, he did not receive any satisfactory response, which caused considerable mental anguish to the man and his father. No proof of payment Advocate Ankur Saini, appearing for the holiday provider, argued that the man never applied for or availed any holiday package services under the agreement and that he had failed to place any proof that he had made a payment of Rs 1.75 lakh towards the membership of the holiday provider. The counsel urged that the man had himself opted for the membership after understanding the terms and conditions of the agreement and had paid the non-refundable membership fee. The counsel stated that the complimentary plot was subject to certain terms and conditions, like payment of Rs 20,000 towards registration and other expenses, which were not fulfilled by the man. Not sustainable The state commission noted that the holiday provider failed to issue the membership card to the complainant the man for availing the services and benefits under the said membership. According to the commission, the contention of the opposite party holiday provider that the complainant man was required to pay Rs 20,000 towards registration and other expenses for the complimentary plot and annual maintenance charges for availing the membership benefits, is also not sustainable, as the holiday provider had failed to establish that it had fulfilled its primary obligations under the membership scheme, including issuance of the membership card and allotment of the complimentary plot. The state commission directed the holiday provider to refund Rs 1.75 lakh paid by the man and further pay Rs 1 lakh as cost for mental agony. The holiday provider was also ordered to pay an additional sum of Rs 50,000 to the man as litigation costs. Takeaway The ruling establishes the obligation of holiday provider companies to follow up on their holiday schemes and that the concerns of the consumers must not be ignored, causing them unnecessary inconvenience. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: The Love Hypothesis movie review: Lili Reinhart brings the spark to a formulaic romance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Love Hypothesis review
description: The Love Hypothesis moview review: Tom Bateman is tall and handsome, but like all good love stories, he must also be cussed and stuck-up, and it seems too contrived.
body_raw: The Love Hypothesis review Writer Ali Hazelwood is a romantic novelist and a neuroscientist, a kind of bond that is hardly organic. The Love Hypothesis, the film based on her bestselling novel by the same name, mixes together the same chemicals. The couple in question, and the people in their lives, walk the rarefied corridors of Stanford. She is a PhD student, he is a professor, and they do top-of-the-line work such as detecting pancreatic cancer. However, barring the lab coats, some mice, a few beakers and mentions of molecules, chemicals and controlled experiments, this could be a love story from anywhere, any time - though, because Hazelwood knows this territory, the science part looks and sounds genuine. Plus, this love has a very weak hypothesis, actually two of them. Olive Lili Reinhart wants her best friend Anh Rachel Marsh to date without qualms a boy a bland Nicholas Duvernay she herself had a crush on. Adam Tom Bateman wants Stanford University to keep funding his research, and a girlfriend is apparently just what would convince his boss that he is serious about staying on. So, Olive and Adam fake date. And we know how that experiment will end, after taking the usual course of a stand-in gay friend Jaboukie Young-White providing the drama, a personal tragedy providing the backdrop, a hot hotel encounter providing the impetus, and a misunderstanding providing the brief tension. Reinhart is winning, which means there is some spark in this story. Bateman is tall and handsome, but like all good love stories, he must also be cussed and stuck-up, and it seems too contrived. articleTitle: Man reveals the most dramatic change after losing 30 kg: ‘Face fat’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: face fat
description: A 30-kg weight loss brought a noticeable change that had people talking. But what happens to the face as the body changes?
body_raw: Management consultant Aayush Joshi took to Instagram to share before-and-after photos of his drastic face-fat loss after losing 30 kg. Face fat was probably the most talked-about change after I lost 30 kg. Of course, the transformation happened across my whole body, but people noticed my face first. The features became more defined, and honestly, thats what I heard the most about. But the visible changes are only half the story. There are changes you cant really see. more confidence, better mental health, and a deeper sense of self-love. Things only you can truly feel, Joshi captioned the post. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. So if youre waiting for motivation to start, dont. Start with whatever you have, wherever you are. Take the first step, he added. Dr Shweta Nakhawa, consultant dermatologist, KIMS Hospitals Thane, concurred that the face is one of the areas where changes in body composition can become quite visible. As overall body fat decreases, there is also a reduction in the fat compartments that contribute to the fullness and contours of the face. This can make the cheekbones, jawline and other facial features appear more defined. How noticeable the change is varies from person to person and depends on factors such as genetics, age, the amount of weight lost and where an individual naturally stores fat, said Dr Nakhawa. Dr Nakhawa noted that a substantial reduction in body weight can alter facial volume and, in some people, the skin may not immediately adapt to the change in underlying tissue volume. Someone who loses a considerable amount of weight may therefore notice a sharper facial contour, but also some hollowness or mild skin laxity. The extent of these changes varies widely. Younger skin may have better elasticity, while factors such as age, genetics, sun exposure and the speed of weight loss can also influence how the skin responds, said Dr Nakhawa. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Aayush Joshi aayushjoshiiii Is it possible to specifically target face fat while losing weight? Not through exercise or diet alone, Dr Nakhawa clarified. The body decides where it loses fat based largely on genetics, hormones and individual fat distribution, so it is not possible to selectively reduce fat only from the face. As overall body fat comes down, facial changes may occur naturally. Trying to accelerate weight loss simply to achieve a sharper face is not advisable, because very rapid weight reduction can sometimes leave the face looking tired or less full, Dr Nakhawa told indianexpress.com. What can people do to maintain healthy-looking skin after major weight loss? A gradual and sustainable approach is preferable. Dr Nakhawa stressed that adequate protein and a balanced diet provide the nutrients required for healthy skin, while hydration, regular sleep and consistent sun protection are also important. Skincare can support the quality of the skin, but it cannot completely prevent changes in facial volume following substantial weight loss. Most importantly, view weight loss in terms of overall health rather than only changes in appearance. A sharper jawline or slimmer face may be visible outcomes, but healthy skin and a well-nourished body remain equally important, said Dr Nakhawa.
