articleTitle: Fake Number Fraud: Don’t Let Scammers Steal Your Money
articleFeaturedImageAlt: icici
description: Understand how fraudsters use fake contact numbers to trick you into revealing sensitive banking details and learn how to protect yourself.
body_raw: What is Fake Number Fraud? Fake Number Fraud is a scam where fraudsters pose as official representatives by creating fake websites, listings or online posts containing fraudulent customer care numbers. These numbers may appear in search results when people look online for helpline or customer support numbers. How does Fake Number Fraud work? When you search online for the customer care number of a bank, e-commerce platform, courier company or other service provider, fraudsters may use fake websites or listings to make their fraudulent numbers appear in the search results. They may also share these numbers on social media platforms, online forums and other websites. Believing the number to be genuine, you call the number and connect with someone posing as an official representative. They may then ask you to share sensitive information, reveal an OTP, approve a transaction or download a remote-access application under the pretext of resolving your issue. What begins as a simple search for customer support can quickly turn into a financial loss. And the most dangerous part? You initiated the call, believing you were reaching out to the official institution. Watch this video to see the scam in action. Common Tactics and Warning Signs Fraudsters use a range of methods, but certain red flags remain consistent. Recognising them can help prevent losses Fake customer care numbers appearing in online search results. Fake contact numbers shared through social media, online forums or other websites. Links or requests to download an app to resolve an issue or provide assistance. Requests for confidential details such as your ATM PIN, CVV, OTP, UPI PIN or net banking credentials. Pressure to act immediately, with warnings about account suspension, blocked cards or failed transactions. How to Protect Yourself Staying safe requires simple but consistent habits. Verify contact details from official sources Always find customer care numbers from the companys official website or verified mobile app. Do not rely solely on numbers found through search engines, social media, online forums or forwarded messages. Never share sensitive banking detailsDo not reveal your ATM PIN, CVV, OTP, UPI PIN or net banking password to anyone, no matter how convincing the caller sounds. Pause before you act Scammers thrive on urgency. If someone pressures you to act immediately, disconnect the call and verify the information independently through an official source. Report suspicious activity Online financial fraud can be reported via the Cyber Crime Portal www.cybercrime.gov.in or the Cyber Crime Helpline 1930. Suspicious calls, SMS or emails can also be reported through the Sanchar Saathi portal sancharsaathi.gov.in. By verifying contact details, protecting your banking information and reporting suspicious activity promptly, you can help protect yourself and others from Fake Number Fraud. articleTitle: Tata Sons listing: ‘Trusts not adequately briefed on RBI talks’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Natarajan Chandrasekaran, chairman of Tata Sons.
description: Tata Trusts have opposed the listing of Tata Sons and have urged the company to examine alternatives.
body_raw: Tata Sons extended engagement with the Reserve Bank of India RBI over its regulatory status has raised concerns within the Tata group over whether the Tata Trusts - the companys controlling shareholder - were adequately kept informed of the discussions with the regulator and options considered during the process. Sources familiar with the developments say the Tata Trusts were not given adequate updates on the submissions made to the RBI, hearings held with the regulator or the course that the regulatory process was taking. The question being raised is whether the Trusts, which hold about 66 per cent of Tata Sons, were kept informed of the representations being made on the companys behalf and of the alternatives being discussed with the regulator. Tata Sons and Tata Trusts did not respond to a mail from The Indian Express. Tata Sons had sought to surrender its registration as a Core Investment Company CIC, a move that would have allowed the groups principal holding company to remain unlisted. The RBI had classified Tata Sons as an upper-layer non-banking financial company NBFC-UL in September 2022, a classification that carries a requirement to list within the prescribed timeframe. Tata Sons subsequently pursued deregistration as a CIC as a route to avoiding a public listing. In August this year, the RBI said the deregistration application was still under examination. That effort, however, ended on September 12 when the RBI rejected Tata Sons application to surrender its registration and directed the company to take the necessary steps to ensure full compliance with the applicable regulatory requirements. The decision effectively put the company back on the path towards a stock market listing. The issue now is not merely what decision the RBI ultimately took, but what transpired during the several years that Tata Sons was engaged with the regulator. It appears the Trusts did not have a clue about the talks with the RBI, said a source. The concern, according to people aware of the matter, is fundamentally one of process. The Trusts apparently wanted Tata Sons to explore all possible regulatory and legal avenues that could reconcile compliance with the RBIs requirements while preserving the companys existing ownership and structure. That position did not necessarily amount to a refusal to engage with the regulator. Tata Trusts have opposed the listing of Tata Sons and have urged the company to examine alternatives. The Trusts had not agreed to a stock-market listing and wanted other options to be explored following the RBI communication. The RBIs decision has nevertheless changed the immediate regulatory landscape. Following the rejection of the deregistration request, the Tata Sons board on September 17 decided to proceed with a listing of the holding company in line with the RBIs directive. The boards decision was taken alongside a separate resolution extending N Chandrasekarans tenure as executive chairman for another five years. The September 17 board meeting also brought the differences between Tata Sons and the Tata Trusts into the open. Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata opposed Chandrasekarans reappointment, while Tata Trusts nominee Venu Srinivasan supported it. The Trusts have subsequently challenged the validity of the boards decision and questioned the use of a casting vote to establish a majority. The listing decision has similarly become a point of disagreement. The Trusts have said they did not agree to the listing and wanted the board to explore alternatives following the RBIs communication. Tata Sons, on the other hand, has decided to proceed with the listing process to comply with the regulators directive. Against this backdrop, the central question concerning the earlier RBI engagement is one of disclosure and shareholder consultation Were the Tata Trusts, as the majority shareholder, kept fully informed about what was being submitted to the RBI, the hearings and discussions with the regulator, and the alternatives being considered? If the engagement with the regulator lasted five or six years, the question now being raised within the group is not simply why the RBI ultimately rejected Tata Sons request. It is also what options were explored during those years, what representations were made to the regulator, when those representations were made, and whether the controlling shareholder was adequately informed of the process. The September 17 board decision has now moved the question into a new phase. Tata Sons has chosen to proceed with the listing, while the Trusts have maintained that alternatives should be examined. The companys next steps will therefore have to be viewed against both the RBIs regulatory direction and the continuing differences between Tata Sons and its controlling shareholder over the future structure of the group. Venu Srinivasan was not prevented from voting on listing-related matters. Concerns were raised over his public support for listing while Tata Sons application for deregistration as a CIC was still pending with the RBI. The issue should have been formally discussed by the Tata Sons and Trust boards. The Articles of Association require the affirmative votes of both Trust-nominated directors, since there are two such directors, and that a casting vote cannot substitute for a specifically required affirmative vote, said the source. The trusts say the Articles form the constitutional basis of Tata Sons and must be followed, particularly when decisions could fundamentally alter the companys ownership and governance structure.

articleTitle: Ajay Devgn shuts down Kapil Sharma’s Goa feni joke with sharp personal jab
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kapil Sharma, Ajay Devgn
description: On The Great Indian Kapil Show Seaspn 5, Kapil Sharma joked with Ajay Devgn about his love for Goa, and asked if there were some other reasons for him to return to the state.
body_raw: Ajay Devgn, Shriya Saran, Jaideep Ahlawat, Ishita Dutta and Mrunal Jadhav recently graced Netflixs The Great Indian Kapil Show Season 5 to promote Drishyam The Conclusion. Since the Drishyam films, as well as several of Ajays popular movies, have been set against the backdrop of Goa, Kapil Sharma couldnt resist taking a dig at the actors apparent love for the state. However, his joke quickly backfired when Ajay brought up Kapils own history with alcohol. Kapil pointed out that several of Ajays films, including Golmaal, Singham and Drishyam, have been shot in Goa. He also noted that the trailer of Drishyam The Conclusion was launched there. Most of Ajay Devgns films, Golmaal, Singham, Drishyam, they all have been shot in Goa. In fact, the trailer of Drishyam The Conclusion, was released in Goa. So, a few people have this question, its not my question, Do you really find Goa beautiful or you believe that you dont get better feni anywhere else or the pomfret is cheaper there? What is the reason? Kapil said. Ajay Devgn simply replied, Goa is very relaxing, and I dont drink feni. When Kapil Sharma joked that Ajay could at least get feni for someone else, the actor turned the joke around on him. Referring to Kapils past association with alcohol, Ajay said, Teri life mein feni ne bahut gadbad ki hai pehli hi, yaad rakhna. She added to the joke, Free mein tujhe kuch bhi mil jaaye tu pi legaYoull drink anything that you get for free. Kapil then continued his Goa-themed act, joking that Ajay was lucky because he gets paid to visit a place that ends up burning a hole in the pockets of common tourists. He also pointed out that while Goa is known for its beaches and forts, Drishyam made its pav bhaji famous. For the unversed, Ajay Devgns comment was a reference to a controversial phase in Kapil Sharmas life when the latter had openly spoken about his excessive drinking habits, and how it led him to make a series of impulsive tweets, including one directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi. In his 2022 stand-up special Im Not Done Yet, Kapil recalled getting drunk before tweeting, ARE THESE YOUR GOOD DAYS? NARENDRAMODI, and joked about the backlash that followed. articleTitle: Army man’s income ‘not assessed’, Calcutta High Court rejects wife’s maintenance hike
articleFeaturedImageAlt: domestic violence maintenance wife son husband army man calcutta high court (1)
description: The court said the magistrate had passed the order without giving reasons for the enhancement and stated that there was no proper basis to enhance the maintenance from Rs 7,000 to Rs 14,000 per month
body_raw: The Calcutta High Court has set aside an order enhancing the monthly maintenance to an Army mans wife from Rs 7,000 to Rs 14,000, holding that the magistrate had passed it without recording evidence or assessing the husbands actual income and financial capacity before determining the appropriate amount. Justice Chaitali Chatterjee Das was dealing with the plea of a woman seeking maintenance for herself and her son under the Domestic Violence DV Act. It is undisputed that the opposite party is in service.but he did not disclose his present income, which he is bound to produce before the court by filing an affidavit of assets and liabilities in consonance with the mandate of the apex court, the September 28 order read. It also noted that the son had already attained the age of 18 before the maintenance application was filed, and therefore he was not entitled to maintenance under the provisions of the Criminal Procedure Code CrPC. Wife alleges cruelty, desertion The couple got married according to Muslim rites in December 1989. The marriage was later registered before a Muslim registrar and kazi appointed by the West Bengal government. The couple then had two children-a daughter and a son. The husband later joined the Indian Army in 1991 and began serving as a havildar. The petitioner-wife alleged that marital discord developed and that she was subjected to physical and mental cruelty. She further alleged that the husband deserted her in 2012 after being posted in North India, leaving her and their son without financial support. The daughter died sometime during the period of litigation. Appearing for the wife, advocates Sobhendu Sekhar Roy, Debabriya Samanta and Samrat Ghosh submitted that she had no independent source of income and approached the Army authorities, following which deductions were ordered from the husbands salary towards maintenance for her and her son. Thereafter, she filed proceedings under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, seeking maintenance. A magistrate initially granted Rs 7,000 per month, which was later enhanced to Rs 14,000 per month. The husband challenged the enhancement before the appellate court, which reduced the maintenance to Rs 7,000 per month. The wife then approached the high court challenging the reduction. No proper basis for hike Order The court agreed with the appellate court that there was no proper basis for enhancing the maintenance from Rs 7,000 to Rs 14,000 per month. The magistrate had passed the final order without recording evidence or giving reasons for the enhancement. Referring to the Supreme Court judgment, the court noted that under the principles laid down, both parties must file affidavits of their assets and liabilities so that the court can assess their actual income and determine the appropriate maintenance. It observed that at the stage of final determination, both sides must get an opportunity to produce evidence and cross-examine, and the court must ascertain the actual income and financial capacity of the parties. The court stressed that reasons are essential for a judicial decision, noting that the magistrate had failed to explain why the maintenance was increased to Rs 14,000. From the facts and circumstances, it is evident that the magistrate passed the final order without calling for any evidence and further failed to ascertain the actual income of the husband and also to assign any reason regarding the quantum so arrived at or even the entitlement of the applicant, the order highlighted. The high court ultimately upheld the reduction, observing that the Rs 14,000 final maintenance order had been passed without evidence, without assessing the husbands actual income and without providing reasons for the enhancement. It directed both parties to file affidavits of assets and liabilities so that the magistrate could determine the appropriate maintenance afresh.

articleTitle: Thane gangrape: 7 farmhouses, 17 properties — Absconding constable’s assets under scanner
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ex MLA pawar and constable patil thane gangrape
description: Thane gangrape case: Police are now verifying addresses of 10 more farmhouses that are owned by constable Patil and his wife, bringing the total number of properties being examined to 17
body_raw: The Thane rural police, investigating the alleged gangrape of a 22-year-old woman, have found that absconding former police constable Shailesh Patil owns sevenfarmhouses in his and his wifes names. The farmhousewhere the alleged assault took place is also registered in Patils name. The police are now verifying the addresses of 10 morefarmhouses that, according to a close aide of Patil, are owned by him and his wife, bringing the total number of properties being examined to 17. Patil and former BJP MLA Narendra Pawar are both absconding in connection with the Thane gangrape case. An officer investigating the case said, We were informed by his close aide that there were 17 farmhouses in the couples names in the MMR region. We have found evidence linking him to seven. Given his background, it seems unlikely that he purchased thefarmhouseson his own, and we suspect somebody may be using his name as a front. The immediate priority is to trace Patil and Pawar in the Thane gangrape case. Patils mother alleges assault Soon after their names were mentioned in the FIR, Patils mother, Sulochana, held a press conference in which she alleged that her son had assaulted her as well and demanded the death penalty for him. She alleged that Patil was trying to protect an IPS officer. According to police sources, Patil was jailed and suspended after his arrest in 2013 for allegedly accepting a bribe on behalf of others. He was reinstated in 2019. Two days later, he applied for voluntary retirement and quit the force, an officer said. An FIR was registered against Pawar and Patil on September 17 based on the statement of a 22-year-old woman, who alleged that the two had gang-raped her at Patils farmhousein Padhga. Pawar and Patil have been absconding since the allegations surfaced. A few days later, CCTV cameras and the digital video recorder DVR at thefarmhousewere found missing. Thefarmhouseis located in a secluded area along National Highway 3 between Bhiwandi and Kalyan. Pawar has resigned from all party positions after the FIR was registered. In his resignation letter, he denied the allegations and called the FIR a conspiracy to defame him. He said he was resigning as the case could adversely affect the partys image.

articleTitle: ‘Seen him shouting at stars’: Raza Murad compares ‘perfectionists’ Bhansali, Raj Kapoor
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Raj Kapoor, Sanjay Leela Bhansali
description: Raza Murad recalled working with Raj Kapoor and Sanjay Leela Bhansali, saying both filmmakers are perfectionists who know how to get the best out of sensitive actors.
body_raw: Veteran actor Raza Murad, known for speaking his mind, recently took a sharp dig at the big stars of the film industry for skipping the last rites of Welcome actor Mushtaq Khan. And now, in a recent interview with Vickey Lalwani, the seasoned actor also opened up about the similarities between filmmakers Raj Kapoor and Sanjay Leela Bhansali, and why he considers both of them perfectionists. Raza Murad says Sanjay Leela Bhansali is a perfectionist Sanjay Leela Bhansali is a perfectionist, said Raza Murad. The host then asked him about reports of the filmmaker being moody and losing his temper. Responding to this, the actor said, See, about the anger, when you are consistently unable to understand what hes trying to say, then he loses his cool. Its not like he is angry right from the start. And, of course, every person has their own temperament, and that anger isnt personal, its related to work because it isnt happening properly. So, its fine, if hes getting angry. And, its not like he only loses his temper at his assistants. I have seen him shouting at bigger stars as well. When asked if he had seen Bhansali shout at Ranveer Singh, Deepika Padukone or Priyanka Chopra, Raza said, Yes, he wants what he wants, and of course, I have seen him getting angry at stars as well. Both of them are perfectionists Drawing a parallel between Bhansali and Raj Kapoor, Raza said both filmmakers wouldnt compromise when it came to their work. Speaking about how he would rate the two filmmakers, the Padmaavat actor stated, Both of them are perfectionists. They want what they want. Time, shift, money, set, dates were of least importance to them. Its okay, if it takes eight days instead of four days. And, when they are on set, they mean business. Hum kaam karne ke liye aaye hain We have come here to work. And, this has happened twice with me. Raza then recalled his first experience of working with Raj Kapoor in Prem Rog 1982. When I was working for the first time with Raj saab in Prem Rog. It was my first day, and meri kya aukaat thi unke saamne What was my status in front of him?. Despite stiff opposition from his sons stating that I wouldnt suit the role. and I was a small time actor, Raj saab said, Ye role karenge toh Raza saahab hi karenge If theres someone, who can do this role, its only Raza sir. He made me meet everyone on the set like I was some head of the state. Also Read Staff touched Bollywood stars feet Sabeer Bhatia says celeb worship shocked American guests Raza recalls similar experience with Sanjay Leela Bhansali Raza said he experienced a similar gesture from the Devdas filmmaker when he first worked with him. And the same thing happened with Sanjay Leela Bhansali, the first day when I went on his set, he also called his entire unit and introduced me to them saying, Raza saab is working with us. So, this was common in both filmmakers Raj Kapoor and Sanjay Leela Bhansali. They gave me a lot of respect and importance. He would get angry at heroines The host then asked Raza if Raj Kapoor would get angry at stars in the same way Sanjay Leela Bhansali does. The Prem Rog actor recalled, Actors are extremely sensitive but they directors know how to get work done from them. He would get angry at heroines, Kya kar rahi hai tu? Ye kya kar rahi hai? Aise mat kar What are you doing? What is this that you are doing? Dont do it. Youre not listening to me. Leave, Ill do and show it to you. He would shout the way elderly people do. And, I have never seen any heroine take offence at his anger. They used to listen to those harsh words and deliver, this was his working style. Raza also revealed that he had seen Raj Kapoor lose his temper with Padmini Kolhapure on the sets of Prem Rog and with Mandakini while shooting Ram Teri Ganga Maili 1985. Raj Kapoor would fall ill before film releases Raza further recalled how Raj Kapoor would become unwell before the release of his films. I saw Raj Kapoor saab fall ill twice, I have seen those pink lips and cheeks turn pale before any of his films release, and the moment the film would be declared a hit, he would recover. He was very concerned about RK Banner, Raj Kapoor ki film hai. Aise hi Raj Kapoor, Raj Kapoor nahi hue hai, Its a Raj Kapoor film. He didnt become Raj Kapoor by fluke, he had many qualities, shared the actor. On the debacle of Mera Naam Joker He was very upset about it. He couldnt come to terms with the reality that the film had flopped at the box office, because Sangam was also a very lengthy film, there were two intervals. But, because the times had changes, peoples mindsets had also changed, and he felt that maybe he made his autobiography. That film is a masterpiece but it happens, said Raza Murad on Raj Kapoors condition post the release of Mera Naam Joker.

articleTitle: Karnataka Asian Games gold medalists to get Rs 1 crore, 2% sports quota
articleFeaturedImageAlt: karnataka asian games
description: The hike in prize money comes amid sprinter M R Poovamma, a gold medallist in the 4x400 relay and silver medallist in the mixed relay at the Asian Games, expressing disappointment over the negligence from her home state.
body_raw: Karnataka has raised cash rewards for Asian Games 2026 medalists and announced a 2 per cent reservation for sportspersons in state government recruitment. While declaring rewards worth Rs 8 crore to Asian Games medalists, Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Tuesday said that gold medalists would now receive Rs 1 crore instead of Rs 35 lakh, silver medalists Rs 75 lakh instead of Rs 25 lakh, and bronze medalists Rs 50 lakh earlier Rs 15 lakh. The announcement came during a felicitation ceremony held at Vidhana Soudha to honour the Karnataka athletes who brought laurels at the Asian Games 2026. The hike in prize money comes amid sprinter M R Poovamma, a gold medal winner in the 4x400 relay and silver medallist in the mixed relay at the Asian Games, expressing disappointment over the negligence from her home state. While other states had congratulated their Asian Games athletes for bringing glory to the country, Poovamma had stated that there was not even a single congratulatory message or call from the Karnataka government. She had also said while other states were paying medal winners in crores, Karnataka continued to pay Rs 35 lakh, which could hardly support the sportspersons to focus. Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara, who was also present at the function, said, In addition to cash rewards, each of the eight medallists will receive Rs 5 lakh as a participation incentive for competing at the Asia Games 2026. There were 20 Karnataka athletes who qualified for the Asian Games. They will be rewarded with Rs 5 lakh each. Qualifying to compete at the international level is itself a major achievement. The decision has therefore been taken to encourage not only medal winners but every Karnataka athlete who represented the state at the Games. Direct recruitment for medallists The government also announced direct recruitment to Group B posts for Asian Games and Commonwealth Games medallists. Parameshwara, who is also the Minister for Youth Empowerment and Sports, said the objective is to provide career security to athletes who bring honour to the state and the country through sporting excellence. While a 2 per cent reservation has been introduced in direct recruitment, a notification in this regard was issued on October 3, providing direct recruitment to Group-A, Group-B, Group-C and Group-D posts across all levels of the state government. Parameshwara said sportspersons should not have to worry about employment after achieving success in sports. The measure is intended not only to honour their sporting achievements but also to provide security for their future.

articleTitle: Delhi CM Rekha Gupta lays foundation of waste processing, biogas plant; inspects Okhla landfill
articleFeaturedImageAlt: waste plant
description: Delhi generates around 13,500 tonnes of municipal waste every day, while MCD currently processes around 60 per cent of the waste generated in the city.
body_raw: In a move aimed at increasing Delhis capacity to process fresh waste, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi MCD is setting up three new waste-processing plants at Okhla, Singhola and Ghazipur, along with a 300-TPD tonnes per day biogas plant at Ghazipur. Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday laid the foundation stones for the three plants and the biogas facility, virtually from the Okhla landfill site and carried out a site inspection as well. Delhi generates around 13,500 tonnes of municipal waste every day, while MCD currently processes around 60 per cent of the waste generated in the city. The three new plants will add 2,900 TPD of fresh-waste processing capacity, helping bridge the gap between the waste generated and the quantity being scientifically processed. The Okhla plant will have a capacity of 1,400 TPD, while the Singhola and Ghazipur plants will process 800 TPD and 700 TPD, respectively. The civic bodys survey identified approximately 125,000 cattle across Delhi, which generate roughly 1,500 tons of dung daily. MCD was directed by central and state authorities to intercept this waste and prevent it from entering city drains and polluting the Yamuna. A 300-TPD biogas plant for biodegradable waste is being set up at Ghazipur to prevent this waste from entering and polluting Yamuna. The projects are aimed at strengthening Delhis fresh-waste processing infrastructure and preventing waste generated each day from adding to the burden of the existing landfills. The civic body is also constructing two more decentralised fresh-waste processing plants with a combined capacity of nearly 3,000 TPD, which will be operational in the coming year, officials said. Biogas plants at Goyla and Ghoga are set to be operational in the next two months, they added. Meanwhile, Gupta, during her inspection of Okhla landfill site on Saturday, reviewed the status of waste disposal, land reclaimed and the capacity of the new processing facilities. She directed officials to make the new units operational at the earliest and at their full capacity. The expansion of fresh-waste processing capacity comes alongside efforts to clear legacy waste from Delhis three landfill sites. According to government figures, 217.17 lakh metric tonnes of waste have been disposed of from Okhla, Bhalswa and Ghazipur over the past 18 months, freeing nearly 100 acres of land.MCD officials said the Okhla and Bhalswa landfill sites are expected to be cleared within three months, while the target for clearing Ghazipur is December 2027. Gupta said clearing the existing landfills would not be sufficient and that the system for processing fresh waste generated every day needed to be strengthened to prevent new garbage mountains from forming.

articleTitle: Don’t interfere with ‘right to azaan’ at mosque if noise norms followed: Allahabad HC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Saharanpur
description: Petitioners claim authorities were not allowing them to use loudspeakers for azaan despite court orders allowed it
body_raw: The Allahabad High Court has directed the authorities concerned to not interfere with the right to five-time azaan Islamic call for a prayer at a mosque in Saharanpur district, provided the noise pollution rules are complied with strictly. A writ petition was filed in the court in July requesting to direct the district administration and police to permit the mosque management to perform azaan five times at Ayesha Masjid in Pathed village of Gagalhedi area and permit the use of loudspeakers for the purpose. According to the petitioners, despite there being court judgments permitting the use of loudspeakers for azaan, the authorities were not allowing them to do so. The state governments counsel, however, submitted before the bench that the petitioners were not restrained from performing azaan as such but were only asked to use loudspeaker according to the Noise Pollution Regulation and Control Rules, 2000, which provide for certain level of sound in terms of decibel units. Citing a May 2020 Allahabad High Court judgment, the counsel maintained that certain timings have also been prescribed for the use of loudspeakers for the purpose of azaan. The 2020 judgment stated that azaan may be an integral part of Islam but the call through loudspeakers or other sound amplifying devices cannot be an essential part of the religion, warranting protection of the fundamental right under Article 25 of the Constitution. Therefore, under no circumstances sound amplifying devices can be permitted to be used between 10 pm and 6 am by the district administrations, it was stated. The 2020 order also maintained that in case any such application is filed before the authorities concerned, it may be dealt with in accordance with law, including noise pollution norms. The petitioners submitted that there was no question of violating any rule or the court order on the use of loudspeakers and their use during azaan will be followed strictly. After hearing the submissions, the division bench of Justices Ajit Kumar and Garima Prashad in its October 1 order directed the petitioners to file an affidavit to comply with the Noise Pollution Regulation and Control Rules, 2000, as well as the HCs 2020 order. It will however, be the duty of the police as well as district administration to ensure that the petitioners do abide by their own undertaking given in the affidavit, failing which it will remain open for them to take appropriate action in accordance with law, the bench stated.

articleTitle: Don’t export tomorrow’s wheat surplus today
articleFeaturedImageAlt: wheat supply, wheat production, Wheat procurement, wheat exports, wheat production, wheat surplus, editorial, Indian express, opinion news, current affairs
description: The crop that must replenish these stocks will be sown over the next two months, and there are reasons for caution
body_raw: Also by Vansh Oberoi India is not short of wheat. The question is whether it knows enough about the crop it will harvest six months from now to export freely today. On August 24, wheat exports moved from prohibited to free, following calibrated permissions of 2.5 MMT each in February and April. The balance sheet looks comfortable. Production is officially estimated at 120.7 MMT, though trade estimates are closer to 110 MMT. Procurement reached 35.76 MMT, against about 30 MMT last year. Central Pool wheat stocks stood at nearly 48 MMT on September 1, more than twice the October 1 buffer norm of 20.5 MMT. But a buffer surplus is not an export surplus. Todays abundance comes from a crop already harvested. The crop that must replenish these stocks will be sown over the next two months, and there are reasons for caution. The monsoon is about 15 per cent below normal, and the risk is uneven. Punjab and Haryana face large rainfall deficits, but their heavily irrigated wheat can lean on groundwater, at a cost to aquifers and state power subsidies. Rajasthan is more exposed Rainfall is about 25 per cent below normal and reservoir storage about 31 per cent below. Bihar has received around 35 per cent less rain, raising concerns over pre-sowing moisture and groundwater recharge. Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh are better placed for now. The outlook adds to the risk. NOAAs September 14 update keeps El Nino in place through January-March 2027. The International Research Institute for Climate and Society sees higher chances of below-normal rain and above-normal temperatures over parts of India through March. A warmer winter is effectively a shorter one, and March matters most - an early temperature rise during grain filling cuts yields.This is not a forecast of crop failure. But parts of the wheat belt enter rabi with a thinner water cushion, and the heat risk is very much alive. Nor can wheat be viewed apart from rice. Rice prices are already 7-8 per cent above a year ago, and kharif acreage is nearly 17 lakh hectares lower. Rabi and summer rice may recover some of this, but weak reservoirs and an unfavourable weather outlook could limit that. Indias cereal basket therefore has less room to absorb a wheat shock than headline stocks suggest. The incentive to export is real. Black Sea wheat lands at Chittagong for about 380mt, against roughly 330mt for Indian wheat based on Rs 27kg in Madhya Pradesh. Forward markets point firmer too. May 2027 Chicago wheat is around 275mt and Kansas HRW near 300mt, both about 15 per cent above May 2026 levels. With Black Sea disruptions persisting, futures are not signalling cheap wheat by the time Indias next crop arrives. India has seen how quickly such calculations change. In February 2022, Indian wheat production was estimated at a record 111.3 MMT. With the Russia-Ukraine war disrupting global supplies, India stepped up exports and targeted 10 MMT for 2022-23. Then came the unusually hot March. As late as May 12, the government was announcing trade delegations to promote wheat exports. A day later, exports were prohibited. On May 19, the production estimate was cut to 106.4 MMT. Sugar offered a reminder just last month. On expectations of comfortable availability, the government expanded sugar exports in February. Production subsequently disappointed. By August, policy had moved from permitting additional exports to allowing duty-free raw sugar imports. Such swings carry another cost. Opening exports fully and then shutting them abruptly erodes Indias reliability as a supplier. The answer is not to halt agricultural exports whenever forecasts are uncertain, but to retain room to respond. India can keep a calibrated wheat export window and revisit it as information improves. If the crop is excellent, India can always export more. Wheat shipped today cannot be recalled if the harvest disappoints. India has enough wheat now. What it lacks is enough information about its next crop. That is a reason to preserve optionality, not surrender it. The writers are with Arcus Policy Research

When we asked Swara how she looked at being pitted against Shehzad even before the show, she said, I have just discovered him, actually. And he has been pitching himself like that. articleTitle: Denied pension over schizophrenia, Orissa High Court restores it for retired CRPF man
articleFeaturedImageAlt: crpf man disability pension rules orissa high court (1)
description: The petitioner was a CRPF employee who retired on medical invalidation grounds in 1999 after he was found to have schizophrenia. The authorities later rejected his disability pension saying that it was a 'non-classified' disease.
body_raw: Holding that the petitioners claim could not be rejected merely because schizophrenia was not a classified disease, the Orissa High Court has quashed a 2011 order rejecting a former CRPF personnels claim for disability pension, directing the authorities to allow the pension and release the arrears. Justice Biraja Prasanna Satapathy was dealing with a plea of a former personnel with the Central Reserve Police Force CRPF, who retired on medical grounds in 1999 due to schizophrenia with an approved 50 per cent disability pension. However, the authorities later revoked the benefit, claiming schizophrenia was non-classified and he lacked 10 years of service. Taking into account the nature of the order passed and the grounds of rejection issued, this court is of the view that since the petitioner was allowed to take retirement on the ground of invalidation because of his.schizophrenia, on the ground that such a disease is not a classified disease, the petitioners claim could not have been rejected, the court said on October 1. The ruling held that since it was clearly indicated in the order that the petitioner is entitled to get the disability pension of 50 per cent and the said order since was never modified or recalled, this court is of the view that the ground on which the petitioners claim was rejected is not sustainable in the eyes of the law. Retired due to schizophrenia The petitioner was a CRPF employee who was allowed to retire on medical invalidation in 1999 after he was found to have schizophrenia. The medical board had found him completely and permanently incapacitated for future service and recommended disability pension of 50 per cent. The CRPFs order allowing his invalidation retirement also specifically stated that he would be entitled to the pension from the date of invalidation. However, his claim for disability pension was later rejected in 2011. The authorities said schizophrenia was not a classified disease for the purpose of Extraordinary Disability Pension EOP under the CCS Pension Rules, 1972, and that he had not completed the required 10 years of qualifying service. He was told he was only entitled to service gratuity, which had already been paid. The petitioner challenged the rejection before the high court, seeking quashing of the 2011 order and release of his disability pension. Original order never recalled Order The court noted that the petitioner was allowed to retire on medical invalidation because of schizophrenia, based on the medical boards assessment that he was permanently incapacitated for further service. The 1999 retirement order specifically stated that he was entitled to 50 per cent disability pension from the date of invalidation. The high court observed that the pension claim was later rejected on the grounds that schizophrenia was not a classified disease and that the petitioner had not completed 10 years of qualifying service. It further noted that the original retirement order had never been modified or recalled. Therefore, the subsequent rejection of the pension claim was not sustainable in law and was also hit by the principle of promissory estoppel, a legal principle that allows a court to enforce a promise even when there is no formal, written contract.

articleTitle: Hanging from moving car, daredevil Gujarat cop recovers Rs 3.75 cr looted gold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Gujarat Police Ahmedabad
description: Robbers snatch gold from train passenger at Nadiad station; after dramatic chase and fake messages trap the robbers, Inspector S A Gadhvi finishes the job with Bollywood-style action
body_raw: A car full of alleged criminals rams into a police vehicle, bashing in a door. As they reverse in an attempt to get away, an officer emerges from his damaged vehicle and lunges at the criminals car. He gets a grip, but they keep going, dragging him along. A few hundred metres on, the officer opens a door, grabs the steering wheel and pulls the handbrake, bringing the car to a halt. This couldve been an action sequence from a film about a hero cop. Except it isnt. The chase was real, and at the end of it, Police Inspector S A Gadhvi of the Ahmedabad Rural Police emerged as a real-life hero. The incident took place outside Viramgam town on October 3. A Tata Tiago driven by an alleged gold robber, rammed into a car being driven by Inspector Gadhvi, jamming the door. Police personnel accompanying Gadhvi managed to prise open the door, but the accused had enough time to reverse their vehicle to attempt a getaway. As police swarmed the car, Gadhvi grabbed the door on the drivers side. The accused dragged the officer along with the moving vehicle for nearly 500 metres. Displaying extraordinary courage and determination, P I S A Gadhvi managed to open the door, gain control of the steering wheel, and pulled the handbrake, bringing an end to the chase, Om Prakash Jat, Superintendent of Ahmedabad Rural Police, said on Monday. The actions of Gadhvi and his team, taken in collaboration with Government Railway Police GRP, stopped four men who had snatched gold valued at Rs 3.75 crore a few hours earlier. The sequence of events had begun almost 110 km away-around 5 pm that evening. As the 12834 Howrah-Ahmedabad Superfast Express pulled into Nadiad station in Anand, Bharat Karsan Chaudhary alighted on the platform, clutching a green bag that contained 2.9 kg of gold jewellery worth Rs 3.75 crore. Suddenly, he felt the bag being snatched from his hand. He tried to pursue the snatcher, but the man was too fast for him. Chaudhary saw him jump into a car that seemed to have been waiting for him. As the car, a Tiago, sped away, Chaudhary managed to take a picture of its registration plate GJ-08-DJ-0311. He then went to the GRP. By 7.30 pm, the GRP had shared the information with the Gujarat Police State Control Room. From there it reached Ahmedabad Rural Police, who tracked the registration of the Tiago and its owner to Banaskantha district. Informants told police the vehicle was travelling through Rural Ahmedabad, and that it was being followed by another vehicle, a Suzuki Baleno without a registration number. Based on the intelligence inputs, we identified the possible movement routes, particularly towards Sachana and Viramgam. The Local Crime Branch LCB and Viramgam Town Police immediately activated naka points and deployed teams strategically on these roads, police said in a statement. Police officers Himanshu of the LCB and Siddhraj of Viramgam Town Police then displayed exceptional alertness and presence of mind and strategically blocked the road using trucks and other vehicles, police said. The Baleno was intercepted just before it entered Viramgam Town. Inside was one of the four accused. But the Tiago seemed to have got away. After the man in the Baleno was interrogated on the spot, it was revealed that the other accused, along with the stolen gold, had already crossed Viramgam Town in the Tiago, police said. Police then used the phone of the accused in the Baleno to send a text to the men in the Tiago, pretending that he was lost. They managed to persuade the men to share the live location of their car, and to meet the Baleno at a specific point. They then reached the spot and blocked the road. Soon, the Tiago arrived. Police flagged it down, but the driver rammed the car into a police vehicle, and Gadhvis heroics followed. Once Gadhvi had managed to stop the car, other police personnel rushed to assist him and successfully overpowered the three accused inside the vehicle, Ahmedabad Rural Police said in a statement. .One of the accused managed to escape from the scene into the adjoining fields, but a systematic search and cordon operation led to his apprehension as well, police said. The gold was found under the seat covers of the Tiago and both vehicles were seized. The four accused were handed over to the Nadiad GRP, who arrested them for robbery, police said.

articleTitle: In Maharashtra, everybody is protesting – From ‘cockroaches’ to tribals to women
articleFeaturedImageAlt: abhijeet dipke, cjp, mumbai protests
description: The triggers are many – farm loan waiver, student hostel facilities, better roads, noise pollution, irregularities in government recruitment exams, functioning of the Election Commission, among others.
body_raw: Protests in Maharashtra have reached a crescendo. In the past few weeks, different parts of Maharashtra have witnessed a string of agitations-from Gen-Z to tribal students to women, though only a few made the headlines. On Friday, October 2, the Cockroach Janata Party CJP held a protest in Mumbai, demanding the ouster of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, followed by a similar protest by the Thackeray cousins. As this was happening, another one walked into Mumbai from Nashik over the weekend-the tribal students. The triggers are many-farm loan waiver, student hostel facilities, better roads, noise pollution, irregularities in government recruitment exams, functioning of the Election Commission, among others. The Indian Express has listed what has kept the state government and the Maharashtra Police on their toes over the past few months. Farmers Farmers protested in June and July 2026, demanding eligibility relaxations in the Punyashlok Ahilyadevi Holkar farm loan waiver scheme. In September 2026, the All India Kisan Sabha launched protests, demanding regular crop loan payees be given a Rs 2 lakh incentive In June 2026, onion farmers staged Rasta Roko on the Pune-Nashik national highway, demanding MSP for their produce. For the past year, farmers from western Maharashtra and Marathwada have protested against the Shaktipeeth road project, refusing to part ways with their lands. Students For over 2 years, students preparing for Maharashtra Public Service Commission MPSC examinations have protested against exam fees, online exams, delayed results and irregularities. The protests intensified after Vivek Bhimanwar was appointed the MPSC chairman. Students in Pune protested over hostel rules. What worked as a catalyst was the deaths of tribal students in Gadchiroli due to snake bites. In September 2026, resident doctors and interns across Maharashtras government medical colleges protested against allowing homoeopathy practitioners to be registered with the Maharashtra Medical Council MMC. Students have been protesting at IIT Bombay since the death of Sahil Wakode on September 18. CJP protests in Mumbai and surrounding areas in support of the Jantar Mantar agitation. Women Women excluded from Majhi Ladki Bahin scheme are protesting, alleging bias. Pune, Nagpur, and Mumbai witnessed citizens protesting in solidarity with the survivors of sexual assault across India. Social activist Manoj Jarange-Patil held a 20-day hunger strike, demanding Maratha quota To counter Jarange, OBC organisations held protests, alleging the government was diluting OBC reservation. Maharashtra is witnessing protests from Dhangar and Banjara communities, demanding Scheduled Tribe ST status. Mischellaneous A road blockade was held in August 2026 across Pune, Nashik and Ahilyanagar districts to demand restoration of the original direct railway alignment between Pune and Nashik. Citizens and environmentalists from across the state are protesting against the felling of trees in Nashik to make arrangements for the upcoming Sinhastha Kumbh Mela. Days before the Ganesh festival, Pune residents took to the streets, demanding a blanket ban on the use of DJs during festivals and religious events. Thanes Balkum, Majiwada and Dhokali saw protests against a hyperscale data centre, expected to consume 422 MW of power, 125 kilolitres of treated water daily and have 193 diesel generators on standby.
