articleTitle: Delhi’s September AQI was lowest in 5 years. So why did PM2.5 and PM10 rise?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi-pollution
description: The concentrations of PM2.5 and PM10, two of the pollutants most closely associated with harmful air pollution, slightly increased this September compared with last year, according to an analysis of data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB).
body_raw: Delhis air appeared to improve this September. The citys average Air Quality Index, or AQI-a numerical index that translates concentrations of multiple air pollutants into a single measure of air quality-fell to 102, its lowest September average in five years, according to official data from the Commission for Air Quality Management. But measurements of two specific key pollutants-PM2.5 and PM10-tell a different story. The concentrations of PM2.5 and PM10, two of the pollutants most closely associated with harmful air pollution, slightly increased this September compared with last year, according to an analysis of data from the Central Pollution Control Board CPCB. At first glance, the two sets of numbers appear contradictory. But they measure different aspects of air quality, and the difference largely lies in how the AQI is calculated and how the data is being compared. AQI is not an average of pollutants The National Air Quality Index classifies air quality into six categories Good 050, Satisfactory 51100, Moderately polluted 101200, Poor 201300, Very Poor 301400 and Severe 401500. With an average AQI of 102, Delhis air in September fell into the Moderately polluted category. The Air Quality Index is a composite measure based on concentrations of individual pollutants, including PM2.5, PM10, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, sulphur dioxide, carbon monoxide, ammonia and others. For each pollutant, a sub-index is calculated based on its concentration. The overall AQI is determined by the pollutant with the highest sub-index on a given day. This means the AQI is not obtained by simply adding or averaging the concentrations of PM2.5, PM10 and gaseous pollutants. As a result, a rise in PM2.5 does not necessarily mean the AQI will rise by a corresponding amount. If PM2.5 increases but its sub-index remains below that of another pollutant, the overall AQI can remain unchanged or even fall if the dominant pollutant is at a lower level. The same applies to PM10. What happened in September? The analysis of the CPCB data for September shows that the average PM10 concentration rose from 104 micrograms per cubic metre in September 2025 to 106 gm this year. PM2.5 increased from 35 gm to 39 g At the same time, the monthly averages of NO2 and ozone were lower than they were in September 2025. CAQM, meanwhile, reported that Delhis September average AQI was 102, compared with 105 in both 2025 and 2024, 108 in 2023 and 104 in 2022. So, the decline in the monthly AQI does not mean that concentrations of every pollutant declined. It means the composite AQI outcome was lower. Why does the AQI not move with PM2.5 alone? A rise in PM2.5 does not always mean the overall AQI will rise. That is because the AQI is based on several pollutants, and the pollutant with the highest sub-index determines the final AQI. So, even if PM2.5 or PM10 goes up, the overall AQI can still fall if another pollutant that was driving the index drops significantly. If PM2.5 rises from one concentration to another, its sub-index also rises. But if ozone or another pollutant still has the higher sub-index, the overall AQI is controlled by that pollutant. Conversely, if the pollutant that was previously driving the AQI falls substantially, the overall AQI can decline even if PM2.5 or PM10 rises, explained Sunil Dahiya, lead analyst and founder at Delhi-based think tank Envirocatalysts. He also pointed out that month-to-month variations in average AQI can affect the cumulative average when a longer period, such as January to September, is compared with previous years. Even relatively small differences in individual months can result in a slight change in the overall average when aggregated over nine months. On the scientific rationale behind such comparison, a CAQM spokesperson said the commissions evaluation uses a comprehensive approach, looking at cumulative trends from January through the month under review, including monthly averages and the number of days in different AQI categories as a standard practice in its analysis reports. For January 1 to September 28, Delhi recorded 194 days with an average AQI below 200, the highest count in the corresponding period of the last five years. The figure was 187 in 2025, 188 in 2024, 193 in 2023 and 146 in 2022, the Commission noted in a statement Wednesday. The number of days in the Poor to Severe categories also fell to 79, compared with 86 each in 2025 and 2024, 80 in 2023 and 127 in 2022. The cumulative PM2.5 average for January 1 to September 28 was 69 gm, the same as in 2025 and below 81 gm in 2024, 73 gm in 2023 and 80 gm in 2022. September is also a transition period as the city enters its post-monsoon phase. Pollution concentrations in Delhi can change sharply with weather conditions including high wind speed, rainfall and humidity.

articleTitle: Squawk 7500 and a stabbed Indian pilot: Inside cockpit of flydubai FZ1073
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ai generated image flydubai flight fz1073 hijacking bid squawk 7500 transponder cockpit
description: Israel's defence minister, Israel Katz, called it an 'attempted jihadist terrorist attack', and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilot tried to crash the plane with everyone aboard.
body_raw: It started as a routine morning flight. At 3.05 am UTC 8.35 am IST Smit Machchhar, the pilot in command of a Boeing 737 MAX 8 registered to flydubai, departed DXB, Dubai International Airport. The destination was Tel Aviv. The next three-four hours, though, were anything but routine. The pilot and co-pilot would have a violent and bloody fight, the plane would go through a terrifying loss of altitude, and speculation of a hijack would trigger an Israeli military response. Eventually flydubai FZ1073 landed safely in Saudi Arabias Tabuk, and the 170-odd passengers were flown home in another plane. Machchhar and his Omani co-pilot - the man who reports claim was trying to seize control of the plane to crash it - have been hospitalized in Tabuk. And Machchhar has been hailed as a hero. And Israeli leaders have denounced an apparent terror attack, though the airline has understandably been more restrained. What is confirmed At 5.21 UTC the plane lost altitude Al Jazeera says flydubai FZ1073 fell over 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds, while CNN says over 17,400 feet in under two minutes. Al Jazeera says the plane squawked 7700 - general emergency - at 5.31 UTC. Seven minutes later it was squawking 7500 - hijack. Squawk 7500 is a red flag. What happens when a plane squawks 7500 First, ATCs establish contact. They let the pilot know their distress call has been heard and that help is on the way. Communication is switched to a secure frequency. Second, airspace around the hijacked aircraft is isolated, i.e., it gets complete and absolute priority over all other aircraft. This involves multiple ATCs working together to keep other planes out of the flight path and the plane away from populated areas. And third, military interception. In this case, for example, Israeli fighter jets were reportedly scrambled to fly alongside. Crucially, in a post 911-world, most militaries are authorised to use deadly force if a hijacked aircraft ignores comms andor commands and moves towards a city or populated area. That said, there is no recorded instance in which lethal force has been employed. Once phases 1, 2, and 3 are active, ground control tries to negotiate a peaceful end to the situation, which could involve the plane landing at a designated airport, where the plane will isolated. But an unspecified number of minutes later the squawk changed back to 7700. What happened in those minutes? flydubai says there was an altercation in the cockpit. That lines up with passengers accounts and available mobile phone footage - alarm and chaos, and passengers rushing to the cockpit, followed by images of Machchhar lying, bloodied, on the floor. Visuals of another passenger with a wound on his head. Three labels, three different claims A stabbing - This is the best-supported description. Israeli officials, passengers, and the footage point to this and reporting, including Al Jazeeras, describes the attack on the captain, Smit Machchhar. A hijack bid - The 7500 squawk shows that someone signalled unlawful interference. Was it Machchhar? That has not been established yet. But a transponder code is a signal, not a finding. A terror attack - Israels defence minister, Israel Katz, called it an attempted jihadist terrorist attack, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the pilot tried to crash the plane with everyone aboard. The Israeli leader also said it is too early to comment on Iran links. flydubai has not confirmed this. The airline says motives remain unknown at this time. The cockpit? One confusing element of the reportage focuses on the cockpit doors - that a passenger kicked the door in and saved the plane. That is unlikely. Modern cockpit doors are built to keep threats in the cabin away from the pilots, and cannot be easily broken down. So any theory that suggests that is suspect, at best. An Israeli government spokesperson told Reuters the injured pilot Machchhar - lying bloodied on the floor, hit the cockpit door release - and that this was how pax and a crew member entered. Footage from the Flydubai flight shortly after the sharp drop in altitude, while the passengers were still unaware of the drama unfolding on board. Credit Itay Blumental,Kan11 News pic.twitter.comrTRrbxu5Js - Iris streetwize September 30, 2026 One of the passengers - Yaniv Hayoun, whom Netanyahu later met and called a lion - told the Israeli leader he put the co-pilot in a chokehold and dragged him out of the cockpit, and then grabbed the planes controls to help bring it back under control. Another passenger, a Dr Shota Musaev, a dentist, told CNN he tied the attacker up using headphone cords and plastic zip ties. He then started tending to the wounded pilot. Multiple media outlets have picked up on this event. Relief pilots? Israeli officials say a second set of pilots were on the flight that they were scheduled to replace the original crew. After the co-pilot was subdued, they reportedly took control and landed the plane in Tabuk. Now this is consistent with flydubais wording about on-duty crew travelling on the flight. But David Soucie, a CNN aviation safety analyst, told the US news website it is fairly uncommon for additional on-duty pilots to be on flights, unless they are being repositioned for other flights. What happens next On Thursday it was confirmed the UAE, where the airline is based, will lead the probe, ending uncertainty over whether Saudi Arabia where the plane landed or Israel its destination would take charge. Israel is meanwhile weighing its own response. The transport minister has asked security services to review whether flydubai should be allowed to keep flying to Israel. And a Netanyahu spokesman also told Reuters that Israel will tighten identity and security checks on every pilot flying into the country, including those working for foreign airlines. For now, the confirmed picture is a violent fight in the cockpit, a steep dive, and a safe landing, with an Indian captain at the centre of the rescue. Why it happened is still an open question, and one the UAE-led probe will now have to answer.

articleTitle: ‘Drowning political career’: Swara Bhasker, Shehzad Poonawalla clash on Rise and Fall 2
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Swara Bhasker Shehzad Poonwalla Rise and Fall 2
description: Swara Bhasker and Shehzad Poonawalla get into a heated argument in the latest episode of Virender Sehwag-hosted reality show Rise and Fall Season 2.
body_raw: Virender Sehwag-hosted Rise and Fall Season 2 premiered on Saturday, and the fireworks have already begun. The much-anticipated rivalry between Swara Bhasker and Shehzad Poonawalla erupted in the second episode, with the two getting into a heated war of words. The tension had been brewing since the premiere episode, when Shehzad ignored Swara after she entered the penthouse. He later made body-shaming remarks about her behind her back and brought up an old incident in which Swara was allegedly ignored by Salman Khan while dancing at his Ganpati Visarjan a few years ago. On Saturday, after Swara entered the show, Shehzad ignored Swara and spoke behind her back. He said, Once during a visarjan, one bhai was dancing, Swaraji, to get mileage and footage, danced at somebody elses Visarjan, and he also ignored her. I am in the same ignore mode. We dont have a personal issue our opinions clash, and for that, I can go to any extent. Later, Shehzad, Manish Kashyap, and Siwet Tomar made body-shaming remarks about Swara and said that she had only been eating ever since she entered the show. Also Read Hes a troll Swara Bhasker hits back at Rise And Fall 2 co-contestant Shehzad Poonawalla View this post on Instagram A post shared by RiseAndFall Season 02 riseandfall02 On Sunday, after all contestants joined the show, Virender Sehwag confronted Shehzad Poonawalla for ignoring Swara Bhasker. He said, Shehzad, you spoke a lot about Swara Bhasker on social media you tried to provoke her. Now, when she came inside the tower, you didnt even speak to her. Awaaz baith gayi hai kya? Reacting to this comment, Shehzad said, Mera swar dabane wala abhi tak koi maai ka laal paida nahi hua. But yes, I dont sit with negativity. If you poke me, I wont spare you. Its my lifes motto opinions are paramount, and I cannot budge from them. Nobodys father feeds me, so if anyone thinks that they can flaunt their elitism, ideas, or identity, they can leave it at home. If you come on to me, I will answer back. I am not scared of fighting you must have seen my debates. Sehwag, in response, said that he had not seen a single debate of Shehzad. His answer left Swara laughing. When Sehwag pointed out Swaras reaction, Shehzad added, I ignore such people. She is used to being ignored. Havent you seen her video? laughs Swara also hit back at Shehzads comment. She told Virender Sehwag, Ignoring someone means you wont acknowledge someone, but he has made 36 tweets, 3-4 videos, and over 50000 messages. Rather than asking for votes for him, his team is appealing to people to send me to the basement. Thats not what ignoring means. Soon after, a heated argument broke out between Swara Bhasker and Shehzad Poonawalla. Shehzad said, Whoever speaks against the country, we will speak against them. Swara hit back, This is a game, not an election, and this game wont save his drowning political career. Shehzad responded, Dont worry about my career try to make your husband win first. Swara then said, My husband got a party ticket at 32, not like you, who has to knock on several doors hoping to get a ticket. In this show, you are also trying to whitewash that image. Replying to Swara, Shehzad said, Dont worry about me. If I wanted to win elections, I would have stayed in the party. I walked out of it and stood up on my own. Swara tried to end the argument and told Sehwag, I know a lot about him. If I say that here, his standard will drop miserably, even though he is used to such low standards I dont want to do it. I am not interested in kichad-matti. Swara Bhaskar calls Shehzad Poonawalla a troll Before entering Rise and Fall Season 2, Swara Bhasker exclusively spoke to SCREEN and called Shehzad Poonawalla a troll. She said, I have just discovered him, actually. And he has been pitching himself like that. For me, hes a troll. And maybe now an elevated troll. I dont really see what his other credentials are. And it seems to me that once I agreed to do the show, they needed a rivalry. Thats how they found him. So he should say thank you to me. Sounds like hes in this show because of me. And hes milking it hes only doing interviews, talking about me like hes obsessed. Hes made three or four videos and shared tweets. I have many trolls, and he is one of them.

articleTitle: Why does a university in Gujarat celebrate Gandhi Jayanti on Oct 7?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mahatma Gandhi spinning the charkha, a symbol of Swadeshi, self-reliance and resistance to British rule (Wikimedia Commons)
description: Gujarat Vidyapith, which the Mahatma established in Ahmedabad in 1920, celebrates ‘Rentiya Baras’ every year – Gandhi’s birthday in accordance with the Vikram Samvat. This Oct 7, it took the charkha to 350-odd schools across Ahmedabad.
body_raw: Five days after the people and government of India observed Gandhi Jayanti, the university the Mahatma founded in Ahmedabad celebrated his birthday on Wednesday October 7. Gujarat Vidyapith traditionally observes Gandhijis birthday in accordance with the Hindu Vikram calendar. As part of this years celebration, it took the charkha to around 350 municipal schools across Ahmedabad to spread Gandhijis message of swadeshi. When was Gandhiji born according to the Hindu calendar? Gandhi was born on Bhadarva Vad Baras, that is, the 12th day dwadashi of the sixth month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar, known as Bhadrapada, in the year 1925 of the Vikram Samvat, which corresponds to October 2, 1869 of the Gregorian calendar-the date universally recognised as his birthday. The Vikram Samvat, which is used by many Hindus to determine the dates of religious rituals and festivals and for making astrological calculations, started in 57 BCE-that is, 57 years before the Gregorian calendar, which is the standard international civil dating system in use around the world. 2026 corresponds primarily to Vikram Samvat 2083, which began on March 19-20 of this year. The official Indian national calendar follows the Shaka Samvat, which began in 78CE. The Gujarat Vidyapith has been celebrating Gandhis birthday by the Hindu Vikram Samvat calendar as Rentiya Baras for the past 90 years. Why is the Mahatmas birthday called Rentiya Baras? Rentiya means spinning wheel in Gujarati, which Gandhi used to spin khadi. He had wanted to dedicate his birthday to the charkha, and desired that the day should be celebrated as Rentiya Baras. Ravindra Pancholi, associate professor of Social Work at Gujarat Vidyapith, told The Indian Express When a demand was raised by his Gandhis followers to celebrate his birthday, Gandhiji said that he did not like it, and that this day his birthday according to the Vikram Samvat could instead be observed as Rentiya Baras. So, from around 1929-30 began this tradition of celebrating Gandhis birthday as per the Vikram Samvat calendar as Rentiya Baras, and not as Mohan Jayanti or Gandhi Jayanti, Pancholi 55, who is grandson of the late Gujarati writer and educationist Manubhai Pancholi Darshak, said. Why did Gandhi want to use the imagery of the charkha? For Gandhi, the charkha or spinning wheel was the most potent symbol of Indian self-reliance. He saw the charkha as an instrument of economic, political, and moral resistance against the British. Gandhi first wrote about the symbolism of the charkha in Hind Swaraj in 1909. After he started living in the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad in 1917, he started to experiment with spinning and weaving by hand, and promoted khadi hand-spun, hand-woven cloth as an alternative to cloth made in the mills of Lancashire in Britain. Gandhi saw khadi and the charkha as a path to Indian self-sufficiency and non-violent resistance to colonialism. Besides the political and economic imperative of Swadeshi, he also encouraged the act of spinning to promote the dignity of labour and to identify with the poor. How has the Gujarat Vidyapith taken this message forward on Gandhis birthday? As part of the Non-Cooperation Movement that he launched in August 1920, Gandhi called for a boycott of schools and colleges under the control of the British government. In opposition to Lord Macaulays colonial education system that worked to sustain the interests of Empire, Indian nationalists established five Vidyapiths to provide anti-colonial education to Indian youth. Gujarat Vidyapith, which was founded on October 18, 1920 by the Mahatma himself, was one of these five Vidyapiths. Today, it is one of the national universities with a charter from the Government of India and seeks to promote Gandhijis ideals of service-oriented education, the Gujarat Vidyapith says on its website. To this end, the university has been celebrating Rentiya Baras in different ways every year, Advaita Dave, Public Relations Officer of the Vidyapith, said. Last year, our staff and students spun charkha at the Sabarmati Riverfront for around an hour and a half. Apart from Swadeshi, the idea was to spread the message that spinning the charkha is a kind of yoga as well, which helps one to improve concentration, Dave said. Pancholi said that in earlier years, students of the Vidyapith have taken part in Akhand Kantan or non-stop spinning on the occasion of Rentiya Baras, taking turns to spin the charkha continuously for 12 hours in batches of 20-25, with each batch spinning for two hours. What happened on Rentiya Baras this year? The Gujarat Vidyapith organised a special program on October 7 to take Gandhis ideals of Swadeshi, self-reliance and khadi to students of schools run by Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation. Around 200 volunteers and more than 1,800 students of Gujarat Vidyapith will visit 351 schools across 48 wards of Ahmedabad city. They will demonstrate the spinning wheel before school students and explain its significance, along with Mahatma Gandhis ideas of Swadeshi and self-reliance. Through this program, the message of the spinning wheel will reach more than 1,35,000 students, the Vidyapith said in a statement issued ahead of Rentiya Baras.

articleTitle: As nuclear power moves into space, how can it be made safe and responsible?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: nuclear power in space, India, NASA, ISRO
description: As countries explore nuclear power options for deep-space missions, an important question arises: how can nuclear power be used safely and responsibly, and are existing international space laws adequate to govern its use? See infographics.
body_raw: - Renuka As space exploration moves from short-term missions towards sustained activities on the Moon, Mars and beyond, reliable energy is becoming increasingly important. Solar power remains the main source of energy for most spacecraft, but its effectiveness falls with increasing distance from the Sun and is limited in permanently shadowed regions and during long lunar nights. Extreme temperatures and radiation also pose challenges for solar panels. Nuclear energy offers an alternative because it can provide compact and continuous power without depending on sunlight. Radioisotope power systems have supported space missions since 1961, while fission reactors are now being developed for higher-power applications and propulsion. As the US, China, Russia, and India expand their ambitions in lunar and deep-space exploration, nuclear power raises an important question how can it be deployed safely and responsibly, and what international rules should govern its use? Nuclear energy in space Nuclear energy is used in space in two broad ways through radioisotope systems and through fission systems. Radioisotope power systems Radioisotope thermoelectric generators RTGs convert the heat released by the natural decay of radioactive material, usually plutonium-238, into electricity. They have no moving parts and can supply useful power and heat for decades. A related device is the Radioisotope Heater Unit RHU, which produces no electricity but only supplies heat, which keeps instruments and batteries from freezing in extreme cold. Different types of RTGs have powered various space missions of NASA, including Voyager space probes, and Curiosity and Perseverance rovers. Voyager 1 and 2 were launched in 1977 on missions originally expected to last only five years, but have continued operating for nearly half a century. India has also begun exploring the use of nuclear power in its space missions. In 2021, ISRO invited proposals to develop a 100-watt RTG, which could provide a reliable source of power for future deep-space missions. India also has ambitious plans for human spaceflight missions, setting up a space station, and even landing humans on the Moon. Fission systems Fission reactors work differently from RTGs. Instead of producing energy from the natural decay of radioactive material, they generate heat through a controlled nuclear chain reaction. This heat can then be converted into electricity. Their main advantage is a relatively much higher power output. This makes fission reactors suitable for missions that require large amounts of electricity, such as future bases or long-duration missions on the Moon and Mars, where power would be needed for habitats, life support, communications, etc. Nuclear energy can also move spacecraft. Nuclear thermal propulsion NTP uses a reactor to heat a propellant such as liquid hydrogen and expels it through a nozzle, giving roughly twice the propellant efficiency of the best chemical rockets. Nuclear electric propulsion NEP converts reactor heat into electricity, which is then used to accelerate an ionised propellant. Its thrust is low, but its very high efficiency makes it attractive for long deep-space journeys. From deep-space missions to lunar bases These technologies provide reliable energy for spacecraft operating deep in space, enabling them to continue sending unique scientific data back to Earth. Some of the most established use of nuclear power is in deep-space missions, lunar exploration, and long-duration missions. Deep-space missions The most established uses of nuclear power are in deep space. Beyond Mars, sunlight becomes too weak for high-energy missions. Nuclear systems work continuously and do not need to be pointed at the Sun, which makes them especially useful in dark or cold environments. The Voyager spacecraft, now more than 20 billion km from Earth, has run on radioisotope power for nearly five decades. NASAs Dragonfly rotorcraft, scheduled to launch to Saturns Moon Titan in July 2028, will also be powered by a radioisotope generator. Lunar exploration The permanently shadowed regions at the lunar south pole may hold water ice, but they receive little or no sunlight. In August 2025, NASA announced plans to fast-track the development of a fission surface power system of at least 100 kilowatts, with the goal of placing a nuclear reactor on the Moon by the first quarter of fiscal year 2030. In April 2026, a White House memorandum targeted 20-kilowatt reactors in orbit by 2028 and on the Moon by 2030, with higher-power systems in the 2030s. NASA has also invited the Indian Space Research Organisation ISRO to join its Moon Base programme. Meanwhile, China and Russia have announced a joint plan to place a reactor on the Moon by the mid-2030s for their International Lunar Research Station. Long-duration missions Nuclear propulsion could transform how far and how fast we travel. Shorter transits to Mars would reduce astronauts exposure to space radiation and allow spacecraft to carry more cargo. Future space infrastructure Reactors could power lunar habitats, life-support systems and communications, and help extract water and oxygen from lunar soil. Over time, reliable nuclear power could anchor permanent bases on the Moon and Mars, and the wider infrastructure a sustained space economy requires. Governing nuclear power in space The deployment of nuclear technology in outer space gives rise to distinct safety concerns. The foremost is the risk of safe launch and re-entry. A nuclear source on a rocket must be designed to survive a launch failure or an accidental fall back to Earth. In 1978, the Soviet satellite Cosmos 954 re-entered over northern Canada and scattered radioactive debris from its onboard reactor. Canada claimed compensation, and the matter was settled in 1981 for C3 million. Notably, deep-space missions already expose astronauts and spacecraft to cosmic rays and solar particles. And the reactor itself needs careful shielding and operational controls. International space law provides a foundation, but not a complete regime. The Outer Space Treaty, 1967 It requires states to carry out space activities in line with international law and bans placing nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction in orbit or on celestial bodies. The Treaty makes states internationally responsible for national space activities, including those of private companies. It also requires states to avoid harmful contamination of outer space and celestial bodies. The Convention on International Liability for Damage Caused by Space Objects, 1972, makes a launching state absolutely liable for damage its space object causes on Earth or to aircraft in flight. Principles relevant to the Use of Nuclear Power Sources in Outer Space Adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 1992, it set rules on safety assessment, radiation protection and notification when a nuclear-powered object is about to re-enter the atmosphere. However, they apply only to nuclear sources that generate electricity for non-propulsive purposes. Safety Framework for Nuclear Power Source Applications in Outer Space The 2009 safety framework was developed jointly by the UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space COPUOS and the International Atomic Energy Agency IAEA. It provides guidance on safety during launch, operation and the end of a mission. Technical and safety challenges Several challenges need to be addressed before nuclear technology can be used more widely in space. Nuclear propulsion is still at an early stage of development and requires further testing before it can be used regularly. Another challenge is the limited availability of plutonium-238, which is used in radioisotope power systems. The US restarted its production in 2015 after a gap of nearly 3 decades, showing the difficulty of maintaining a reliable supply. Yet another key concern is safety. The nuclear systems used in space have to be designed so that they can endure launch accidents and other kinds of failure. They also require specialised materials, extensive testing, and careful safety procedures. Since an increasing number of countries are planning to use nuclear power for missions to the Moon and for deep-space missions, common safety standards and more international cooperation will become ever more important. Need to strengthen international regulations The way forward should, therefore, involve combining technological development with stronger international regulation. Countries should work towards common safety standards covering the design, launch, operation and disposal of nuclear systems in space. The United Nations could consider whether the existing principles on nuclear power sources in space need to be updated to address newer technologies such as high-power reactors and nuclear propulsion. While pursuing its ambitious space missions, India can contribute to international discussions on the safe and responsible use of nuclear technology. As the use of nuclear power in space expands, its success will depend not only on technological development but also on strong safety standards, international cooperation and responsible regulation. Post read questions 1. The growing use of nuclear technology in space reflects the transition from short-duration exploration to sustained space activities. Discuss. 2. Examine the technological and operational challenges involved in radioisotope power systems and fission reactors in deep-space exploration. 3. What are the principal safety, technological, environmental and geopolitical concerns associated with the deployment of nuclear systems in outer space? Suggest measures to address them. 4. With multiple countries planning lunar bases and deep-space missions, common international safety standards for space nuclear systems are becoming increasingly important. Discuss. 5. How adequate are existing international mechanisms for ensuring the safe and responsible use of nuclear power sources in outer space? How can India contribute to the international governance of nuclear technology in space? Dr. Renuka holds a PhD in environmental law from Himachal Pradesh National Law University, Shimla. articleTitle: 7 remarkable species found in Himachal Pradesh
articleFeaturedImageAlt: animals
description: From snow leopards and Himalayan ibex to the colourful monal and elusive musk deer, here are rare and distinctive animals you can spot in Himachal Pradesh.
body_raw: If your idea of wildlife in India begins and ends with tigers, elephants and leopards, Himachal Pradesh has a very different list waiting for you. Head higher into the mountains and the landscape changes, along with the animals that call it home. From the elusive snow leopard of Spiti to the brilliantly coloured Himalayan monal, Himachal is home to several rare and distinctive Himalayan species. Some are notoriously difficult to spot, but that is part of what makes seeing them in the wild so special. Here are some of the animals to look out for in Himachal Pradesh. Snow leopard The snow leopard is Himachal Pradeshs state animal and is strongly associated with the states high-altitude wilderness. Its important landscapes include Spiti, Pin Valley, Kinnaur, Lahaul and Pangi, as well as parts of the Greater Himalayan National Park region. Dont expect an easy sighting, though. Its grey, spotted coat blends remarkably well into rocky mountain terrain, which is why it is popularly known as the ghost of the mountains. Even in areas where snow leopards are known to occur, sightings remain rare. Himalayan monal Think of a pheasant, but make it spectacular. The Himalayan monal has iridescent plumage that can flash shades of green, blue, purple and copper when the light catches it. The bird occurs in Himachals temperate and subalpine forests, forest edges and higher meadows. The Great Himalayan National Park is among the protected landscapes where it is found. And while it is one of Himachals most distinctive birds, it is not the states official bird. The western tragopan holds that title. Himalayan ibex In Himachals high, rocky and trans-Himalayan terrain, the Himalayan ibex is another species to look for. This wild mountain goat has large, curved horns and is built for steep slopes. It is also an important prey species for snow leopards. Ibex populations have been studied in landscapes such as Pin Valley, but the animal is locally distributed, so it is far more likely to be encountered in suitable high-altitude terrain than across Himachal generally. Western tragopan The western tragopan, locally known as jujurana, is a rare pheasant and Himachal Pradeshs state bird. It occurs across parts of the western Himalayas, so it is not exclusive to Himachal, but the state provides important habitat for the species. The bird favours dense temperate and subalpine forests with thick undergrowth. Its secretive behaviour makes it difficult to spot even where it is known to occur. The Great Himalayan National Park landscape is among the areas that provide important habitat for it. Blue sheep or bharal Despite its name, the bharal, or blue sheep, is a wild mountain ungulate rather than a true sheep. Its greyish-blue coat helps it blend into rocky slopes, while its sure-footedness allows it to navigate steep terrain. Bharal are among the principal prey species of snow leopards and occur in the high-altitude ecosystems of Himachal. They occur in protected landscapes, including the Great Himalayan National Park and Rupi Bhaba Wildlife Sanctuary. Himalayan tahr The Himalayan tahr is a large, stocky wild goat found in parts of Himachals alpine and subalpine terrain. Its thick coat helps it withstand cold conditions, while its strong limbs allow it to navigate steep mountain slopes. The species is recorded in protected landscapes including Rupi Bhaba Wildlife Sanctuary and the Great Himalayan National Park region. Like the other mountain ungulates on this list, it is not an animal you are equally likely to see everywhere in the state. Himalayan musk deer View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dhritiman Mukherjee dhritimanmukherjee Small, secretive and very different from the deer you might picture in Indias forests, the Himalayan musk deer is found in Himachals temperate, subalpine and high-altitude forests. It is recorded in the Great Himalayan National Park landscape, but spotting one is another matter altogether. The species is highly elusive and prefers dense cover, making it much harder to see than larger mountain animals. articleTitle: Fake will, death certificate and a bid to inherit Kamal Nath’s land: Plot unravels in Bijnor
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nath also claimed that "this gang has prepared forged documents relating to several other properties as well".
description: Two arrested after former Madhya Pradesh CM found that attempts were underway to take over land belonging to his late father
body_raw: Former Madhya Pradesh chief minister Kamal Nath was in for a rude shock when he found that his ancestral land in Uttar Pradeshs Bijnor district was allegedly being acquired by people not associated with his family. When the former CM looked closer, he found that his late fathers land was allegedly being acquired based on an unregistered will, a forged death certificate and other documents. The Bijnor police have registered an FIR at Najibabad police station and, according to Superintendent of Police K K Bishnoi, two people have been arrested, while a third is absconding. Police are examining whether the group was involved in similar attempts involving other properties. The case came to light in an unusual way. On May 18, 2026, Nath approached the Najibabad tehsildars court to have his inheritance over 2 hectares of agricultural land in Amikhanpur village recorded. The land belonged to his late father, Mahendra Nath. But the local lekhpal informed the revenue authorities that another case concerning the land was already pending and the property was therefore being treated as disputed. It was while pursuing his inheritance claim, the FIR says, that Nath learnt that someone else was already staking a claim to the land. According to the FIR, Dharampal Singh, son of Ratan Singh, had produced a fake, forged and fabricated unregistered will in a case now pending before the Najibabad tehsildar. The alleged forgery did not stop at the will. The FIR says a purported death certificate of Mahendra Nath, dated April 10, 2003 and allegedly issued from Najibabad, had also been placed on the case record. Kamal Nath told police that the document was false his father, according to the complaint, died on September 7, 2004, at Escorts Hospital in New Delhi. The complaint also pointed to the name of Mahendra Naths wife being recorded as Premlata, which Kamal Nath said was incorrect. Nath alleged that the documents were being used to establish a false chain of ownership over his fathers property. According to the FIR, Dharampal Singh, Jasbinder Singh Dhillon, Vijay Shankar Pandey and David Kumar, the area lekhpal, along with other conspirators, had allegedly acted in collusion with each other and conspired with the intention of grabbing the applicants land. The complaint alleges that the group prepared a fake and forged unregistered will, death certificate and other documents with the intention of getting Naths agricultural land registered in their own names by fraudulent means and then selling it. Nath also claimed that this gang has prepared forged documents relating to several other properties as well. Bishnoi said the case may involve a larger portion of Naths family property. According to him, Kamal Naths father had around 90 bighas of land, of which approximately 36 bighas were allegedly targeted for misappropriation through forged documents. The accused allegedly produced a forged will purportedly executed in 2003 and, on the basis of that document, created a fake decree in 2004 in Bijnor. They subsequently filed a civil suit in 2020 and attempted to get the land transferred in their names, Bishnoi said.

articleTitle: Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam 3 reminds us that more than family, the franchise is about movies
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn's Vijay Salgaonkar tells a story throughout the Drishyam trilogy.
description: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 concludes on a high, unlike the far more family-oriented Malayalam version, because it ties in neatly with what's always been the franchise's spiritual fulcrum -- the movies.
body_raw: More than a standalone movie, Abhishek Pathaks Drishyam 3 works best as the third act of Drishyam, if it were a consolidated crime thriller instead of a trilogy. The conflict gets set in Nishikant Kamats first part 2020 when Sam dies at the hands of Vijay Salganonkars Ajay Devgn family. The plot thickens in Pathaks Drishyam 2 2022 before the resolution comes in at a cinematic high in Drishyam The Conclusion, which released this past Friday on the befitting date of October 2. Like for the Goa police, pav bhaji, Maharaj ji ka satsang, and film watching in Panjim which film did they watch? Drishyam 3? were all distractions even for the audience. All this while, unreliable narrator Salgaonkar was doing what he does best - telling us a story through drishyam visuals. The movie-watching underdog In the first Drishyam, were introduced to Vijay Salgaonkar, a fourth class dropout whose only means to securing an education has been watching movies. Hes particularly on a steady diet of thrillers. Theyve edited it with fast cuts and taking the audience for a ride. On top of that is the pounding music So that it seems a lot is going on. But nothing is really happening. You need to feel the tension, he tells his subordinate, probably also referring to the Drishyam trilogy that takes its own sweet time to lure the audience in. At one point, Salgaonkar is also seen watching and weeping to Vipul Shahs 2005 family drama Waqt The Race Against Time. Though thats far from being a crime thriller, it does sound like a tagline to the Drishyam franchise itself. Because as the films unfold, we realize that every step of the way, Salgaonkar was far ahead of anyone else in the race against time. After his family panics following the murder of Sam, the only son of Goa Police Inspector General Meera Deshmukh Tabu, Salgaonkar devises a foolproof plan. He takes his family for an outing in Panjim the next day in order to crystallize the same chronology in granular detail when the police eventually interrogates them. Not just that, he even lives out that delayed reality for all the other eyewitnesses involved - the restaurant owner and the cinema projector operator among others - so that their testimonies sync with those of his family. Since Indians all across have grown up on movies, he uses that very device of visual memory as his weapon of choice. So, when the first part ends, Salgaonkar has an upper hand. But like most sequels, the conflict is brought back with a new lens. Enter Akshaye Khanna, who takes over the case from Tabu, capitalizing on his objective gaze sans personal prejudice. But to Salgaonkar, hes not the chief antagonist, but yet another actor just playing his part ironic, since thats what it turned out to be, given Khannas sudden exit from the franchise before Drishyam 3. To make the stakes more implausible yet interesting, he brings in Saurabh Shuklas character, an author who churns out a book out of the chain of events Salgaonkar has preempted. When the court dismisses the states case against Salgaonkar on the argument that the police is trying to frame a common man and his family by recreating events of a book, that twist seems far too convenient and far-fetched. But Shuklas author character is brought back again in Drishyam 3 to explain the rationale communicated to him by Salgaonkar - Films need not to be real. They just need to seem and feel real. That then becomes the spiritual fulcrum of not only the threequel, but also the trilogy. Suddenly, as Drishyam 3 draws to a close, the audience realize that Salgaonkar had been pulling the puppet strings all along. He uses the fame he gains from the events in the first part to rise the ranks and become a theatre owner from a DVD store owner. The events of the sequel allow him to further gain traction in his career, and become a film producer. But little do we know hes been producing a film all along - the film that weve been watching for the past 11 years. Through whats described as Salgaonkars three-part chakravyuh, the audience gradually uncovers that the sequel wasnt actually the second act, but the beginning of the second half of the film thats Drishyam. The climax of the first part boats of the cinematic high and narrative clencher of the interval block, and Drishyam 2 is merely a stepping stone to the rousing conclusion in Drishyam 3. Like every time, Salgaonkar was way ahead in the game, planning his course of action in Drishyam 2 itself, instead of saving it for the epic conclusion. A step above Mohanlals Drishyam 3 Spoiler alert Till the first two parts, Devgns Drishyam remained mostly faithful to its original source material, Jeetu Josephs films Drishyam and Drishyam 2 respectively, starring Mohanlal as Georgekutty, the Malayalam counterpart of Vijay Salgaonkar. But after the Malayalam Drishyam 3 didnt live up to the hype, Pathak and Devgn changed the course of their franchise, taking a completely new direction. However, this new direction neatly ties in with the spirit of the first part. It also weaves in the polarizing reaction towards Malayalam Drishyam 3 to tell a slightly deceptive story about family. Pathaks Drishyam 3 begins with Rajat Kapoors character Mahesh Deshmukh vowing to reopen the case and put Salgaonkar behind the bars, after his wife Meera tries to end her life out of depression. When Jaideep Ahlawats DCP hits back at Mahesh, asking him if hes a servant who reopens the case at his beck and call, its also a dig at the Malayalam Drishyam 3 which takes too many swings to take the story forward. In that version, Siddique who plays the Malayalam counterpart of Mahesh turns evil, a far cry from the fairly balanced sympathizer he is in the first two parts. Since SalgaonkarGeorgekuttys purported narrative throughout the franchise has been about protecting the family, it makes narrative sense to have another father determined to protect his family by avenging the death of his son. So, when Siddiques character steps up, it shouldve made for a riveting clash of the patriarchs. But what follows is a long-drawn, unwarranted climactic twist in which Georgekutty beats up his daughter in order to frame a troublesome cop. His argument was simple - beating up his daughter was in the larger interest of protecting his family from conviction. But it was not only problematic to watch, but also felt like a melodramatic copout. Surely, when the audience enter a theatre, they want to immerse themselves in the emotion and the drama. But not at the cost of the films own voice. So, when Pathaks Drishyam 3 avoids going down that path and instead pays a tribute to the movies, it all makes complete sense. When Salgaonkar pulls out his final trick from the hat, and the skeletons in his closet come tumbling out pun intended, he underlines what the Drishyam franchise has always been about - movies. Yes, family is at its heart too, but when his wife Nandini Shriya Saran breaks out of the character of the hapless wife, the film exposes family as just a visual decoy to make the police - and the audience - forget that Salgaonkars superhero power is watching movies. As the Malayalam Drishyam 3 revealed, family in fact turns out to be Georgekuttys Kryptonite. While he manages to get his family to dodge conviction yet again - paving the path ahead for another part - it comes at the cost of not only his daughters injuries, but also the audiences dissatisfaction. By making his Drishyam 3 all about the movies, Pathak underscores that while a family man may often have to sacrifice a part of his conscience for the sake of his family, a cinephiles win is written in the movie stars. Whether its a thriller like Drishyam or a family drama like Waqt, its always the sacrificial patriarch who pays a heavy price, while the underdog movie buff wins the race against time.

articleTitle: Barapullah-III that cuts Noida-Delhi travel time to 15 minutes opens September 29
articleFeaturedImageAlt: barapullah flyover
description: Amit Shah to inaugurate the project that saw multiple delays over a decade
body_raw: In what is set to be the culmination to a decade-long project, the much awaited Barapullah Phase-III flyover, which will provide a signal-free commute between East Delhis Mayur Vihar to South East Delhis Sarai Kale Khan, will finally be thrown open to the public on September 29. The flyover will be inaugurated by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in the presence of Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and others, Public Works Department PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh told The Indian Express on Saturday. The opening of the flyover will ease the commute for people travelling from Noida and East Delhi to South Delhi. It is expected to reduce the average travel time from East Delhi and Noida to AIIMS in South Delhi from 35 to 40 minutes to 15 minutes. Project marred by delays For more than a decade, the Barapullah Phase-III project became synonymous with delays, and multiple missed deadlines. The project, which was approved in 2014 and was kicked off in 2015, was originally expected to be completed in 2017. However, it became one of Delhis most delayed infrastructure projects, with setbacks ranging from a seven-year land acquisition dispute and environmental approvals to technical challenges associated with constructing a bridge structure across the Yamuna floodplain. After BJP came to power last year in Delhi, the government got clearance from Centre to transplant trees from the site, to overcome one of the key environmental hurdles. For years, Delhiites saw deadlines come and go. Since last year, I have personally visited the site multiple times, reviewed progress regularly, and worked with officials to remove bottlenecks and get the project completed for the convenience of the public, said the PWD Minister. He added, The project witnessed accelerated progress over the past year and a half through continuous monitoring, regular inspections and coordinated action by multiple agencies, the Minister said. The delays also led to significant cost escalation, with the revised project cost now standing at approximately Rs 1,635 crore from the initial sanctioned cost of Rs 1,260 crore. Singh on Saturday visited the project site to review the final preparations. Speaking during the inspection, he said, For more than a decade, Delhi has been waiting for this project to become a reality. The project had remained delayed under the previous government. After the formation of our government, the long-pending work has now been completed and the corridor is ready to be opened for the people of Delhi. Singh said, The project has been designed keeping different kinds of road users in mind. Along with vehicular connectivity, the dedicated cycle track and pedestrian-friendly infrastructure will provide additional mobility options for Delhi residents. PWD officials said an extradosed bridge -- a cross between a girder bridge and a cable-stayed bridge -- across the Yamuna has also been completed and forms part of the connecting structure for the elevated corridor. Significance The 3.5 km long three-laned flyover will provide eight loops-four each at Sarai Kale Khan and Mayur Vihar. The corridor is expected to decongest traffic along National Highway-24, the DND Flyway, and Ring Road while enhancing access to a multi-modal transit hub that includes National Capital Region Transport Corporation, Indian Railways, ISBT, Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, and the DelhiMumbai Expressway. The project is also set to become a landmark in urban infrastructure development. Besides being a first-of-its-kind elevated corridor with a dedicated cycle track, another major engineering highlight is the special bridge structure over the Yamuna floodplain, said officials. It is estimated to cut carbon dioxide emissions by 2 tonnes per day, equivalent to absorption by nearly 30,000 trees, said officials.

articleTitle: Why President Murmu returned Bengal’s ‘Anti-Goonda’ Bill
articleFeaturedImageAlt: President Droupadi Murmu
description: President returns Bill for reconsideration after Centre raises conflict with NDPS Act, 1985
body_raw: In a setback to the BJP dispensation in West Bengal, the President of India has registered a sustainable objection to Suvendu Adhikari governments anti-Goonda Bill and returned it for reconsideration after the Centre raised the issue of a conflict between the proposed legislation and the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances NDPS Act, 1985. In its note before returning the Bill, the Central government said, Section B of the proposed Bill, insofar as it includes within the definition of goonda a person who commits, attempts to commit, abets, promotes, finances or facilitates any offence punishable under the NDPS Act, 1985, may overlap with the preventive-detention framework provided under the PITNDPS Act, 1988, which is a specific Central legislation dealing with preventive detention of persons engaged in illicit traffic in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances. The proposed provision may, therefore, create an overlapping or parallel preventive-detention mechanism in respect of drug-related activities and may give rise to an issue of repugnancy under Article 254 of the Constitution of India. Accordingly, the reference to offences under NDPS Act, 1985 in Section 2diiiB may be deleted to avoid duplication and overlap with the existing Central statutory framework, it added. A senior official of the state administration said, It is indeed a setback for the government as it wants to implement this Act as soon as possible. However, there is a provision to table this Bill again in the Assembly after making the necessary changes in the proposed Act where it is conflicting or overlapping with Central law. After that, it will be sent again for the assent of the President of India. To curb anti-social activities, the BJP government introduced the West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-Social Activities Bill, 2026 in June. However, after facing criticism from the Opposition, Adhikari assured the Opposition that the legislation would not be used for political vendetta. Those who are expressing concern about the provisions of preventive arrest have no reason to be afraid. The administration will act in accordance with the law, and there will be no misuse of the law in any way, the chief minister had said. The Bill, apart from defining what constitutes an anti-social activity and who is a goonda, also has provisions to bar such people from entering a specified area, district, or districts for a period not exceeding one year. The Bill states that if a district magistrate, a Commissioner of Police, or a police officer not below the rank of DIG authorised by the state government is apprehensive that a goonda is engaging in or will engage in anti-social activities, they may, to prevent it, direct such person to remove himself outside such area, district or districts, or part thereof, as may be specified in the order, within such time as may be specified therein, and prohibit him from entering or returning to such area for a period not exceeding one year and require such person to report his movements, or to report himself, in such manner, at such times, and to such authority as may be specified in the order. On August 6, a division bench of the Calcutta High Court comprising Justice Tapabrata Chakraborty and Justice Partha Sarathi Chatterjee dismissed three Public Interest Litigations challenging the Bill on the grounds that the petitions were premature because the Bill had not yet received the Presidents assent to become a law. However, the high courts observations and the states own submissions effectively contradict repeated public assertions made by Adhikari. On multiple occasions, Adhikari claimed that the Goonda Daman Bill had already received the Governors assent and became law. He also told the Assembly that the Goonda Daman Act had been invoked against all those accused of orchestrating violence during the July 24 protest march at Esplanade. However, the state has now informed the high court that the Bill is still awaiting the Presidents assent and has, therefore, not yet become law, rendering the chief ministers claims incorrect. Recording the states submission, the high court observed on Thursday, As the Act is yet to receive Presidential assent, the writ petition is premature. Thereafter, the bench further clarified that once the Bill received the required assent and was promulgated, the petitioners would be at liberty to challenge its validity. However, we made an observation once it receives the assent, you would be at liberty to come, the Bench observed.

articleTitle: Vijay’s wife Sangeetha makes rare public appearance to support son Jason’s Sigma
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vijay
description: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay’s wife Sangeetha Sornalingam made a rare public appearance at Kamala Cinemas with daughter Divya to watch son Jason Sanjay's directorial debut Sigma. This was her first public appearance after withdrawing the divorce case.
body_raw: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijays wife Sangeetha Sornalingam made a rare public appearance on Friday as she arrived at Chennais Kamala Cinemas with daughter Divya Saasha to watch her son Jason Sanjays directorial debut Sigma. The appearance comes nearly two months after Sangeetha withdrew the divorce petition she had filed against Vijay. Videos from outside the theatre show Sangeetha and Divya arriving for the early show of Sigma, which released in theatres on October 2. Sangeetha was seen smiling at photographers as she made her way inside, while Divya accompanied her. Sangeetha wore a cream-coloured suit with a golden border, while Divya opted for a black T-shirt and jeans. Sangeetha and Divya Sasha came to watch Sigma movie at Kamala pic.twitter.comfFIexqtyMU - Ayyappan Ayyappan1504 October 2, 2026 Jason was also seen accompanying his mother and sister at the theatre as his first film as a director hit the big screen. The outing marks Sangeethas first widely reported public appearance following the developments surrounding her marriage to Vijay. Vijay, however, was not seen at the screening and has also stayed away from the films promotional campaign. Jason Sanjay on why Vijay is not promoting Sigma Jason had earlier made it clear that Vijay would not be involved in the promotions of Sigma. He said he wanted the focus to remain on the film and its cast and crew rather than on his fathers celebrity status. My father is waiting for the release of Sigma. He wont be promoting my film. I want the promotions to be about the film and not him. I dont want it to overlap. And hes become CM now, so he has so many responsibilities. Hes waiting to see what Ive done and is very excited. Jason has also spoken about how he expects his father to react when he eventually watches Sigma. Speaking to Pearle Maaney on her YouTube show ahead of the release, he described Vijay as someone who takes time before giving his opinion. My dad is usually a quiet person. He takes his time. If I ask a question, hell take 10 seconds to respond. If hes quiet all the while, Ill ask, Did you cut the call, Appa? Think, come to your conclusion, and then call me, email me, or something. Jason said he understands that a film requires more time to process than a phone conversation and expects Vijay to take his time before sharing his thoughts on Sigma. I think you need more time to analyse the film. But hell like the film. Hell be proud, Jason said. ALSO READ Drishyam 3 movie review Terrific Ajay Devgn-Tabu give Drishyam the conclusion it deserved Sangeetha and Vijays divorce case Sangeetha and Vijays marriage came under public scrutiny earlier this year after she filed for divorce before the Family Court in Chengalpattu. Sangeetha filed the divorce petition in February 2026, seeking dissolution of her marriage to Vijay. In her petition, she alleged that Vijay was involved in an extramarital relationship with a female actor. She claimed that the alleged relationship had caused her deep emotional pain and mental suffering, amounting to betrayal and violation of marital trust. She cited alleged emotional neglect, public humiliation, mental cruelty and constructive desertion among the grounds for seeking divorce. She also sought permanent alimony and residential rights. Sangeetha withdrew the divorce petition on August 7, 2026. She appeared before the Chengalpattu Family Court through video conference and informed the court that she did not wish to pursue the proceedings. She also filed a withdrawal petition. The couple, who married in 1999, have two children - Jason Sanjay and Divya Saasha. About Sigma Directed by Jason Sanjay, Sigma stars Sundeep Kishan as Guru, a treasure hunter and radio host whose life falls apart after a betrayal leaves him with nothing. The film also stars Faria Abdullah, Sampath Raj, Raju Sundaram, Shiv Panditt, Anbu Thasan and Yog Japee. The film is produced by Subaskaran under Lyca Productions and has released across Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, Kannada and Malayalam.

I am very excited and happy for Bhuvneshwar Kumar because he is a very unassuming guy. Yes, when he played a couple of games in Australia, he was also finding it a little difficult, but he had some fitness issues. With the bat, he could contribute really well. If he swings the ball and shows decent fitness, nobody can stop Jasprit Bumrah and Bhuvneshwar Kumar from sitting together on that flight to the World Cup, with Bhuvneshwar bowling the first ball of the World Cup, hoped Ashwin.

articleTitle: Express Investigation: The unprecedented rift within the Election Commission
articleFeaturedImageAlt: express investigation election commission of india
description: An investigation about Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi's objections to decisions that according to them were taken without their knowledge.
body_raw: The Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, which began in Bihar last year, has resulted in more than 13 crore names being removed from draft rolls across 30 States and Union Territories, putting the Election Commission at the centre of an intense public debate. articleTitle: Rate hike: Behind the RBI’s pivot, a need to safeguard price stability
articleFeaturedImageAlt: rbi rate hike
description: The interaction between persistent supply shocks and strong demand warrants particular attention. Economic history suggests that when supply-driven price pressures coincide with robust growth, inflation often broadens beyond a narrow set of categories
body_raw: The shift in stance by the RBIs Monetary Policy Committee MPC, accompanied by a rate hike in its October review, was hardly unexpected. Monetary policy is shaped principally by domestic growth and inflation dynamics, with global developments playing a secondary role. Recent developments on both fronts increasingly pointed towards a recalibration of policy. This year was marked by an unusual combination of shocks and uncertainties. Yet, despite the conflict in West Asia and unresolved tariff-related turbulence, Indias economy has remained remarkably resilient. Growth has stayed robust, while inflation, particularly core inflation, has thus far been relatively contained. However, the balance of risks has begun to shift. Since the MPCs August review, upside risks to inflation have become more pronounced. Three factors stand out. First, the conflict in West Asia, marked by repeated cycles of escalation and de-escalation, has kept commodity markets volatile. Recent developments have pushed up crude prices again, with the Indian crude basket, as estimated by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell, returning to its April peak. Reflecting this, we now expect crude prices to average 88-93 per barrel this fiscal, compared with our earlier forecast of 82-87 per barrel. Even if geopolitical tensions ease, crude prices may remain elevated as damaged infrastructure is repaired and depleted inventories rebuilt. In such a scenario, another round of pass-through to domestic petrol and diesel prices appears likely. While higher pump prices could temper demand and ease pressure on oil marketing companies, they would also raise inflation through both direct and indirect channels. Food inflation represents a second major source of vulnerability. Food prices are the most volatile component of Indias inflation basket, and recent increases reflect both base effects and emerging supply concerns. To be sure, the relationship between monsoons and food inflation is not linear. Not every rainfall-deficient year has led to higher food inflation, and the governments free food programme for nearly 800 million people, alongside healthy rice buffer stocks, provides an important cushion. Nevertheless, the 2026 monsoon has ended with rainfall 13 per cent below the long-period average and over 42 per cent of districts in India classified as deficient. More importantly, the problem extends beyond the aggregate shortfall. The spatial distribution and timing of rainfall have been particularly unfavourable, making this one of the most disrupted monsoon seasons of the past decade. The implications extend beyond the current kharif season. Weak monsoons can impair rabi production by reducing soil moisture and reservoir levels. As of October 1, reservoir storage was 12.2 per cent below normal and 20.4 per cent lower than a year earlier. Crisils Deficient Rainfall Impact Parameter DRIP points to broad-based stress, with cotton, tur and bajra among the most vulnerable crops. Intensifying El Nino conditions, combined with supply disruptions linked to the West Asia conflict, are exerting upward pressure on food prices worldwide. Particularly notable is edible oil inflation, driven by weather-related disruptions in Southeast Asia and rising biofuel demand. According to the World Meteorological Organisation, the probability of a strong El Nino extending into early 2027 is close to certainty, raising the risk of extreme weather events and supply disruptions. Given that India imports over 55 per cent of its edible oil requirements, elevated global prices and currency weakness continue to keep domestic edible oil inflation elevated at around 20 per cent. The impact of the monsoon on agricultural output and food prices, then, will remain one of the most important variables for policymakers to monitor this year. Inflation risks, however, are no longer confined to supply-side shocks. Demand-side pressures also appear stronger than previously anticipated. GDP growth in the first quarter was not only above trend but also exceeded previous expectations, and the second quarter is also doing well. Reflecting this momentum, the RBI has raised its growth forecast for this fiscal to 7.1 per cent from 6.7 per cent earlier. Crisil likewise expects growth of 7.0 per cent. The interaction between persistent supply shocks and strong demand warrants particular attention. Economic history suggests that when supply-driven price pressures coincide with robust growth, inflation often broadens beyond a narrow set of categories. Early signs of such generalisation are becoming visible in core inflation, with price pressures gradually spreading beyond food and fuel. Global developments reinforce the need for caution. Bond yields in advanced economies have risen much more sharply than in India, reflecting persistent inflation and growing concerns over fiscal sustainability. Consequently, the spread between US and Indian 10-year government bond yields has narrowed to roughly 200 basis points, compared with over 400 basis points a few years ago, reducing the relative attractiveness of Indian government securities for foreign investors. At the same time, major central banks remain in tightening mode. The US Federal Reserve raised rates by 25 basis points in September, and markets continue to price in further tightening. The European Central Bank and the Bank of Japan have also maintained a tightening bias in response to persistent inflation pressures. Indias liquidity situation adds another layer of complexity. The RBIs efforts to mobilise foreign currency non-resident deposits have been highly successful, strengthening foreign exchange reserves and improving balance-of-payments resilience. However, these inflows have also injected substantial liquidity into the financial system. Consequently, financial conditions eased through August, and liquidity remains abundant. This creates a degree of tension, albeit transitory, between prevailing monetary conditions and the tightening bias increasingly warranted by growth and inflation dynamics. Taken together, these developments explain the RBIs policy shift. Inflation risks are becoming more broad-based, growth remains resilient, global monetary conditions continue to tighten, and domestic liquidity remains ample. Policymakers will need to remain highly vigilant on price developments. While future actions will remain data-dependent, the possibility of another rate hike this year can no longer be ruled out. The writer is chief economist, Crisil

articleTitle: How Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is challenged by Morne Morkel when he is left out of playing XI
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sooryavanshi is yet to play a senior international match in India. (BCCI Photo)
description: Morne Morkel said that being with the team is good for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's development, regardless of whether he is in the playing eleven or not.
body_raw: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may have captured the imagination of the cricket world with his big-hitting prowess at the age of 15 in last years IPL but the Indian team management is being cautious with the teenager. There have been moments in his fledgling international career when it has looked clear that he remains in early stages of his development despite his immense talent and India bowling coach Morne Morkel has said that he likes to challenge Sooryavanshi regardless of whether he is playing or not. Morkel said that being with the team is good for Sooryavanshis development, regardless of whether he is in the playing eleven or not. If he is not getting that game time, he is still on a bus, in the dugout, in the hotel with guys with a lot of experience, Morkel told reporters ahead of Indias first T20I against the West Indies. I think, with him, sharing that dressing room and talking to guys, just actually watching how the guys go through their processes and how they set up will be key. So I always challenge him. I say, watch what this guy is doing in training. How does he face his first 15 balls when the wicket is tough? What sort of game plan has he come up with? For any young player, if he gets game time or if that game time is a little bit limited, it is still our job to make sure that these guys learn, they grow and they ask questions. I always ask him on the bus, What is the one thing you have learned today? Tell me what you think about that guys batting. That makes him think, and I think next time he comes to the nets, the sort of things he will observe, he will adapt to his game. Morkel said that he cant say for sure if Sooryavanshi will open for India in all five of their upcoming T20Is against the West Indies. Head coach Gautam Gambhir had said that the teenager will have to wait for his chances. Sooryavanshi has played eight T20Is thus far and has a strike rate of 186.16 but an average of only 30.75 in the 246 runs he has scored. He is yet to play an international match in India, having been left on the bench during the T20I series against Afghanistan earlier this year while Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma opened. I am pretty sure Gautam will look to rotate them, Morkel said about Indias openers. The guys just came back from the Asian Games, so we want to see how everybody is feeling after jet lag, after travelling, and then from there make the plan.

articleTitle: Amid Rahul & Priyanka’s ‘Sting’ moment, PepsiCo gets court relief
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rahul, Priyanka Sting
description: Granting temporary relief, the Delhi High Court stayed the FSSAI’s order against PepsiCo over use of the “Energy Drink” label for its products
body_raw: During Tuesdays INDIA bloc protest, Rahul Gandhi offered his sister Priyanka a red drink. She looked at it with suspicion, sniffed it, and took a small sip. The video of the exchange went viral, prompting speculation that the drink was PepsiCos Sting. The viral moment came on the same day the Delhi High Court gave the beverage firm temporary relief in a case concerning Sting. On Tuesday, PepsiCo India Holdings Private Ltd and Monster Energy India Private Limited were before the court to seek an interim stay on the Food Safety and Standards Authority of Indias order to the two companies to discontinue using the energy drink description for its products. The products included PepsiCos Adrenaline Rush Energy Drink-Ultimate Performance and Sting Energy, and Monster Indias Monster Energy and Predator Energy. The food regulator had issued the order on the ground that using energy drink as a label for the product constitutes misbranding and misleading. Justice Amit Mahajan, on October 6, stayed the FSSAIs June 30 order against the two companies covering the four products, along with any consequential action taken by the regulator. The court noted that the order had been passed without issuing a show-cause notice to the beverage makers or giving them an opportunity to be heard. It also sought responses from the Health Ministry and the regulator and listed the matter for November 5. Last month, Red Bull India Pvt Ltd had approached the court with a similar grievance. It, too, was directed by the FSSAI to discontinue using the energy drink description for its caffeinated products. The HC had stayed the FSSAI action on similar grounds. The three companies argued that their products fall under the relevant food category and that the regulator had previously clarified that they could use the term Energy Drink. They contended that the regulator could not take a somersault and subsequently state that use of the term could amount to misbranding.

articleTitle: TV damaged ‘during shifting’, Delhi man wins Rs 50,000 payout from packers and movers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Delhi Consumer Commission TV Packers and Movers Delhi TV Gurgaon Consumer News
description: A Delhi consumer commission was hearing the complaint alleging deficiency in service after household goods, including a TV and shoe rack, were damaged during shifting.
body_raw: A Delhi consumer commission has ordered a packers and movers company to pay Rs 50,000 after a customers TV was allegedly damaged when its box fell during packing, and a shoe rack was also found damaged on delivery. It held that the companys own records and the consumers documents supported the claim. President Suresh Kumar Gupta and member Harshali Kaur of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, South-West Delhi were hearing a complaint filed by one Rajnish Kumar Ahuja, who had paid Rs 18,050 to the company for packing and transporting his household goods from Naraina Vihar to Gurgaon. We have no reason to disbelieve the complainants averments, the commission said in the September 16 order, considering the documentary evidence produced by him, and added that the evidence had remained unrebutted and uncontroverted. The dispute began on October 16, 2023, when four employees of the company arrived at Ahujas residence to pack his household goods. The company prepared a list of 50 items, including their values, as informed by the consumer. The goods were delivered the next day. TV box fell during packing According to Ahuja, the Sony LED TV was checked and found to be working before it was packed. He said the box containing the TV fell while the employees were making space to place it with the other goods. The delivery acknowledgement carried his handwritten note, stating that the TV box had fallen during packing and the screen was damaged, while the TV had been found in working condition before packing. The note also recorded that the shoe rack was damaged during unpacking. Photographs of the damaged items were placed before the commission. Ahuja then approached the companys customer care and shared photographs of the damaged TV. The authorised Sony service centre initially estimated the repair cost at Rs 29,618. It later informed him that it could not arrange the display panel and offered an exchange model for Rs 44,788. Ahuja forwarded the communication to the company. The company initially closed the claim as No Claim, stating that its scrutiny showed the TV had not been damaged by its employees. It later offered Rs 10,000. After Ahuja wrote to the companys chairman, its legal department offered Rs 15,000 through a letter dated February 6, 2024. He rejected the offer and pursued the consumer complaint, seeking Rs 90,000. Commission rejects valuation argument Before the commission, the company described the complaint as false and baseless. It argued that the TV had not been declared or valued and that its liability was restricted under the Carriage by Road Act. The commission rejected the valuation argument, pointing out that the companys own document listed the value of the LED TV as Rs 30,000. It also found that the consumers documentary evidence supporting his allegations had remained unrebutted and uncontroverted. The commission also noted that the companys defence had been struck off after it failed to file its reply within the legal period despite appearing before it. The commission did not accept Ahujas separate allegation that the company delayed delivery. He claimed that delivery had been promised on October 16 and that the delay caused inconvenience. However, the commission found no mention of the alleged delay in his handwritten delivery acknowledgement, the emails exchanged with the company or his National Consumer Helpline complaint dated December 2, 2023. It therefore declined to rely on the allegation. The commission allowed the complaint and held the company deficient in service. It directed the company to pay Rs 50,000 towards the damaged TV and shoe rack, inclusive of litigation costs. Takeaway Document the condition and value of your belongings before shifting, and record any damage on the delivery receipt itself. Keep photographs, emails, repair estimates and other supporting documents, as these can be crucial when seeking compensation for damage during transportation. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Delhi1800-11-4000 or call the National Consumer Helpline at1915for assistance.
