articleTitle: 4 killed, 10 injured as boiler explodes in Andhra Pradesh pharma factory
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rescue teams launched relief and rescue operations at the site and were working to locate and evacuate people who may still be trapped. (Representative Image)
description: The explosion at a pharmaceutical factory in Sri City caused a part of the building’s roof to collapse, trapping workers.
body_raw: At least four workers were killed and 10 others were injured when a boiler exploded at a pharmaceutical factory in Sri City in Andhra Pradeshs Tirupati district on Saturday morning. The massive blast caused a part of the buildings roof to collapse, trapping workers who were later rescued, officials said. Sri City, located along National Highway 16, is one of Indias largest multi-product Special Economic Zones and houses over 250 companies, including several pharmaceutical units. The explosion occurred as several night-shift workers were preparing to leave the facility. Fire, police and rescue teams rushed to the spot. The blaze that broke out following the explosion was later brought under control, while the injured were shifted to nearby hospitals for treatment. At least 3 similar incidents in 12 months The incident is the latest in a series of industrial accidents in Andhra Pradesh. In June, eight workers were killed after a ladle carrying molten steel broke and sparked a major fire at the Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd RINL plant, also known as the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant. In February, 21 people were killed in an explosion at a firecracker factory in Vetlapalem village in Kakinada district, while six people were killed in a blast at a firecracker manufacturing unit in Rayavaram in the Dr B R Ambedkar Konaseema district in October last year.

articleTitle: India to acclimatise for CWC 2027, with six ODIs at SA venues ahead of event
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India
description: The 2023 runners-up are bunched in Group A alongside Australia, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and Qualifier A; Super 7 new feature introduced
body_raw: India will open their 2027 ICC World Cup campaign against defending champions Australia on October 7 in Cape Town, which would be the first game of the group stages. Before the group stages begin with 12 teams, there would be a Super Series-which will be the preliminary round for the three lowest-ranked qualified teams-that will begin on October 2 inAWindhoek Namibia. The Indian Express understands that as part of the preparations, India will head to South Africa way in advance where they will play the Proteas in a 6-match ODI series at key venues including Johannesburg, Cape Town and Centurion. India, which finished runners-up in the 2023 edition which it hosted, is placed in Group A alongside Australia, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and Qualifier A. After playing their opening fixture against Australia at the picturesque Cape Town on October 7, they will head to the Bull Ring Wanderers for the high-octane fixture against Pakistan on October 10. Shubman Gill Co then will take on Afghanistan on October 14 at Centurion. They will then face Qualifier A at Bloemfontein before ending the group stages against Zimbabwe at the Mosi-oa-Tunya Stadium, which is currently under construction near Victoria Falls. The Group B consists of South Africa, England, Sri Lanka, New Zealand, Bangladesh and Qualifier B. dhdhdhdh dhdhSdhdh dhdhdhdhEdhdhdhdhdhZ dhY-i The ICC Mens CWC27 fixtures have been unveiled dhY Access the ticket ballot dhYZ pic.twitter.comY8CLgDcaYU - ICC Cricket World Cup cricketworldcup October 1, 2026 With one year to go for next years 50-over World Cup, the International Cricket Council on Thursday released the schedule in Cape Town. The tournament to be co-hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia sees the World Cup returning to Africa after the continent hosted it for the first time in 2003. While Kenya had been one of the co-hosts and made the semi-finals, this time it is Namibia which gets to host the event. Apart from the opening round it will also host three group matches. In Zimbabwe-Harare, Bulawayo and Victoria Falls will be the host cities while South Africa will remain the major host. The semi-finals will be played at Cape Town and Centurion before the Wanderers in Johannesburg hosts the final on November 21. In all 8 venues in the Rainbow nation will be used for crickets showpiece event. South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia will provide an unforgettable stage for the worlds best teams, combining a deep passion for cricket, extraordinary destinations and a renowned warmth of welcome. We look forward to welcoming fans from across the world and creating memories that will last long beyond the final, ICC chair Jay Shah said. Super 7 stage introduced The top three teams from each group and the best fourth-placed team with more points from both the groups will be the seventh team to make it to the Super 7 phase that has been introduced for the first time in the tournament. Unlike the Super 6 stage which existed in the World Cup till the 2003 edition, teams that make the Super 7 stages wont be carrying forward their points they collect in the group stage. For the Super 7 stage, which will see each team play six matches between October 25 to November 14, the ICC has also released the seedings. Being the top-ranked team in ODI rankings, India will be A1. The others are A2 Australia, A3 Pakistan, AB4 England, B1 New Zealand, B2 South Africa, B3 Sri Lanka. Should India make it past the Group Stages, they will face Australia again in Victoria Falls. Their next likely opponents will be South Africa at Wanderers, followed by New Zealand at Paarl, Pakistan again at Cape Town on November 7. Then they will face 2015 champions England at Gqeberha Port Elizabeth before finishing the phase against Sri Lanka at Durban on November 14. The top four teams from the Super 7 will advance to the semifinals. Group A India, Australia, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe, Qualifier A. Group B South Africa, New Zealand, England, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Qualifier B. Indias group matches Oct 7 vs Australia at Cape Town, Oct 10 Pakistan at Johannesburg, Oct 14 vs Afghanistan at Centurion, Oct 17 vs Qualifier A at Bloemfontein, Oct 24 vs Zimbabwe at Victoria Falls.

articleTitle: Centre approves Rs 65 crore for geo-spacial based survey of unauthorised colonies
articleFeaturedImageAlt: geo-spacial based survey of unauthorised colonies, unauthorised colonies, Delhi Revenue and Imaging Survey, Spatial Technology Initiative, DRISHTI, GIS-based survey, Rekha Gupta, Manohar Lal, Indian express news, current affairs
description: Delhi government is implementing the PM-UDAY (Pradhan Mantri-Unauthorized Colonies in Delhi Awas Adhikar Yojana), aimed at granting property rights to residents of the city's over 1,500 unauthorised colonies.
body_raw: Nearly three months after Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta wrote to Union Housing and Urban Affairs Minister Manohar Lal requesting an assistance to regularise unauthorised colonies, the Centre has approved Rs 65 crore under Delhi Revenue and Imaging Survey, Spatial Technology Initiative DRISHTI for GIS-based survey and mapping of such colonies. Delhi government is implementing the PM-UDAY Pradhan Mantri-Unauthorized Colonies in Delhi Awas Adhikar Yojana, aimed at granting property rights to residents of the citys over 1,500 unauthorised colonies. Moreover,PM-UDAY cells in 13 districts, and a headquarter, will be set up to expedite registration of properties in unauthorised colonies. The geographic information system GIS survey is required under PM-UDAY scheme to verify, map and authenticate property boundaries and geo-coordinates within Delhis notified unauthorised colonies. The technology-driven survey will make mapping of properties more transparent, systematic and time-bound. The project has an estimated total cost of Rs 65 crore, of which Rs 52 crore, or 80 per cent, will be provided as a grant from the Urban Development Fund UDF of the Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, the CMO said. The remaining Rs 13 crore, will be contributed by Delhi governments revenue department that will be responsible for implementing the project, it said. The initiative will help make the mapping and documentation process related to properties under PM-UDAY scheme more systematic and time-bound. The chief minister said the PM-UDAY scheme is not merely a process of issuing property-related documents but also an important means of providing legal security over homes and property rights to lakhs of families living in Delhis unauthorised colonies.

articleTitle: AIIMS BSc Nursing draws 1.91 lakh applications, records over 1000% jump in 5 years
articleFeaturedImageAlt: nursing allied healthcare option beyond mbbs
description: Allied healthcare includes a range of specialised undergraduate programmes, including medical laboratory technology, ophthalmic sciences, radiotherapy and perfusion technology.
body_raw: Nearly 1.91 lakh candidates applied for the BSc Hons Nursing entrance examination conducted by the All India Institute of Medical Sciences AIIMS for the August 2026 session, while more than 1.17 lakh applications were received for BSc Allied Healthcare Courses, according to information obtained under the Right to Information RTI Act. The data was sought by 30-year-old Vipul Sharma, an allied healthcare professional working in laboratory healthcare at Lady Hardinge Medical College. According to the AIIMS RTI response, 1,90,740 applications were received for BSc Hons Nursing for the August 2026 session, compared with 1,17,033 applications for BSc Allied Healthcare Courses. BSc Hons Nursing Entrance Exam Applications Category 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 OBC NCL 6,754 8,708 32,526 65,637 78,319 UR Unreserved 5,542 6,487 19,180 34,772 48,988 SC 2,292 2,755 9,883 22,109 28,543 EWS 1,334 1,700 5,405 11,865 15,218 ST 563 817 2,520 6,470 9,049 Total 16,485 20,467 69,514 140,853 180,117 BSc Allied Healthcare Courses Entrance ExamApplications Category 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 OBC NCL 3,326 3,483 12,400 29,242 54,489 UR Unreserved 1,737 2,011 5,894 16,849 35,137 SC 859 967 3,380 9,593 20,150 EWS 759 809 2,321 6,692 11,586 ST 197 209 694 2,291 5,606 Total 6,878 7,479 24,689 64,667 1,26,968 Sharma said the figures point to the need for greater awareness about undergraduate healthcare careers beyond medicine and nursing. Not everyone knows about the multiple professions that cost less to study and can offer good career opportunities. These professions were earlier broadly referred to as paramedical professions, but are now recognised as allied healthcare, Sharma said. Allied healthcare includes a range of specialised undergraduate programmes, including medical laboratory technology, ophthalmic sciences, radiotherapy and perfusion technology. These professionals work across diagnostic, therapeutic and other specialised healthcare services. Such programmes can also offer an alternative career pathway to students who aspire to become doctors but do not secure an MBBS seat. Around 22 lakh candidates appear for NEET-UG each year, while the number of MBBS seats is slightly above one lakh, leaving many students to explore other healthcare professions. AIIMS offers nursing and allied healthcare programmes across its network, while institutions such as PGIMER Chandigarh also offer specialised allied healthcare courses. Cost is another factor differentiating these programmes from conventional medical education. Government medical colleges and Institutes of National Importance such as AIIMS, PGIMER and JIPMER offer some allied healthcare programmes at relatively low fees. The fees at central institutions can range from around Rs 1,500 to Rs 15,000 for the programme, while courses in state-run medical colleges may cost around Rs 20,000 to Rs 60,000 a year. Private universities and deemed institutions, however, can charge substantially more. Bachelors programmes such as physiotherapy, medical imaging technology and cardiac technology can cost between Rs 80,000 and Rs 3 lakh a year, depending on the institution and programme. Shorter, skill-focused vocational and state paramedical board diploma courses typically cost around Rs 20,000 to Rs 70,000 a year. Sharma said nursing continues to have greater visibility among students, partly because of the clearer government recruitment pathway. The Nursing Officer Recruitment Common Eligibility Test NORCET and the government pay structure are among the factors that make nursing a more familiar option for students. He also pointed to differences in work patterns. Allied healthcare professionals may work in specialised departments such as biochemistry and other laboratory services, where hospitals may operate services in shifts. For students considering these programmes, Sharma said allied healthcare should not be viewed merely as a Plan B after NEET, but as a group of specialised healthcare professions in their own right.

articleTitle: 5 bedrooms, mountain views and a cricket room: Inside Ajinkya Rahane’s Igatpuri retreat
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajinkya Rahane family villa tour video
description: Ajinkya Rahane’s Igatpuri holiday home is a five-bedroom retreat with an infinity pool, lake views, open spaces and a room dedicated to cricket memorabilia.
body_raw: Indian cricketer Ajinkya Rahane and his wife Radhika Dhopavkar recently shared a rare glimpse inside their holiday home in Igatpuri, Maharashtra. Nestled amid the Sahyadri mountains and overlooking Vaitarna Lake, the five-bedroom villa is designed as a private family retreat, complete with an infinity pool, sprawling gardens, balconies and a dedicated room filled with Ajinkyas cricket memorabilia. The couple offered a tour of their property, Raaya Estate, informing that the villa was built after the Covid-19 pandemic. The cricketer chose open spaces and elevated living areas to let his family spend more time outdoors. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Ajinkya Rahanes childhood memories In the video, Ajinkya shared that he wanted the holiday home to link to his childhood. He drew inspiration from the summer holidays he spent at his grandmothers house, where he would spend much of his time playing outdoors. The cricketer wanted to recreate a similar environment for his children, giving them plenty of space to run around and enjoy the outdoors. The villa features five king-size bedrooms, an infinity pool, a gazebo, lush gardens, an in-house bar and a dedicated childrens play area. Several balconies around the property offer uninterrupted views of the mountains and Vaitarna Lake. The central entryway features double muted-blue doors with lion-head knockers. A slate-blue wooden console table with drawers and a lower shelf rests against the wall, topped with floral arrangements in white vases, and immediately grabs attention. Expansive bedrooms The main living room is situated on an elevated first floor and is divided into two sections. One part is a morning space where the family enjoys tea or coffee while taking in views of the lake and mountains. The other section is a more relaxed sitting area, with a large, comfortable sofa where the family can spend evenings or unwind during the day. The interiors follow a neutral and earthy colour palette. Natural shades dominate the rooms, giving the villa a warm and understated aesthetic while keeping the focus on the surrounding landscape. Each bedroom opens onto a spacious balcony. The couple said they often spend hours there, enjoying the views. Cricket memorabilia room The villas most personal space is arguably Ajinkyas cricket memorabilia room. The room houses items collected throughout his cricket career, including bats, balls, caps and team jerseys. The room, as seen on StayVistas YouTube, also displays photographs of the cricketers with his teammates. Each piece holds a different memory from his journey as a cricketer. Speaking about the room, he said revisiting the memorabilia is emotional. He revealed that he gets goosebumps whenever he enters the space, as the items remind him of different moments from his career. Rubeena Singh, Founder of The Verve Collective, interior stylist, and home decorator, shared subtle ways to make a home look luxurious without relying on expensive furniture or luxury brands. She stressed that luxury has very little to do with price. Its really about knowing where to spend, where to save, and how to elevate what you already own. You dont need to replace a perfectly good sofa beautiful cushions in rich fabrics can instantly make it feel more elevated. An old lamp can be given a completely new look with a patterned lampshade, Rubeena explained. Similarly, an existing console can be reimagined with a fresh coat of paint in an unexpected colour.the possibilities are endless. A luxurious home isnt about the label or the price tag its about having an eye for beautiful things and bringing them together in an interesting way, the expert added. articleTitle: Ahmedabad bridge meant to ease traffic ends up worsening it
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, Railway Overbridge project at Makarba, Makarba, Makarba Railway Overbridge, Makarba Railway Overbridge project, Ahmedabad news, Gujarat news, Indian express, current affairs
description: The Makarba railway overbridge that CM Bhupendra Patel inaugurated on Sept 24 lands smack at a junction on Corporate Road. The civic body has demanded an explanation from the design consultant and is scrambling to find immediate solutions to the traffic chaos that has ensued.
body_raw: The Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation AMC has issued a show-cause notice to a design consultant firm involved in a railway overbridge project at Makarba that has caused traffic chaos, within two weeks of its inauguration. This traffic congestion in the rapidly growing commercial and residential area in southwestern Ahmedabad has forced the civic body to widen the connecting road to resolve the problem, and to implement immediate traffic solutions. The firm, Ahmedabad-based DELF Consulting Engineers India Pvt Ltd., is an extension of DELF-South Africa, according to its website. The company was the design consultant for the railway overbridge that Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel inaugurated on September 24 under the Phatak-mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, a campaign to free roads from railway level crossings. However, the four-lane bridge, which was meant to ease traffic snarls caused by the closure of the gates of Level Crossing 24 on the Ahmedabad-Botad broad gauge section of Western Railway, lands at a junction on Corporate Road-which has resulted in congestion and traffic chaos on the roads that connect to the Sarkhej-Gandhinagar Highway. AMC has instructed the projects design consultant, DELF Consulting Engineers India Pvt Ltd, to conduct a technical study of the current traffic situation and submit a detailed report, Dinesh Gaurav, Deputy Municipal Commissioner, Roads and Building Department, said. He said the design consultant had been instructed to analyse the root causes of the current traffic congestion and traffic flow patterns, and to submit a detailed report outlining both immediate corrective measures for the current situation and long-term solutions to permanently resolve the traffic issues. Gaurav said the design firm has been asked to explain the technical reasons behind the situation, and to compare the traffic flow now with the time when the study was conducted. Work on the bridge began in 2023. The show-cause notice says, The bridge lands in close proximity to the Corporate Road junction, leaving inadequate length for merging, weaving and dispersal of traffic. Based on the findings of the technical study and the clarifications provided by the design consultant, an appropriate technical evaluation will be carried out, and necessary further action would be taken, Gaurav said. Meanwhile, the AMC has implemented a capsule design layout to streamline traffic flow and reduce congestion at this point. Also,.AMC has undertaken the widening of the existing road from Corporate Crossroads to SG Highway to its full width. Efforts are underway to ensure that traffic flow on this route improves significantly upon the completion of this work, Gaurav said.

articleTitle: Kainchi Dham drowns in tourists after Hanuman Ansh release, district may act to ease pressure
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kainchi Dham is located in the Kumaon hills (Express)
description: ‘We usually expect about 25,000 people visiting the shrine every day, but the long weekend saw a crowd of more than 35,000 every day,’ the DM told Express.
body_raw: For kilometres, cars crawled through the Kumaon hills towards Kainchi Dham over the long weekend, bumper-to-bumper on the mountain road. Pilgrims got out and walked along the roadside and families waited for hours, while vehicles heading towards Mukteshwar were caught in the same gridlock as those arriving for darshan. Videos circulating online over the weekend showed long lines of cars, buses and two-wheelers around Bhimtal, Bhowali and Kainchi, with reports of journeys that ordinarily take a few hours stretching much longer. The congestion has prompted the Nainital administration to consider opening an alternative route to ease pressure on Kainchi Dham. Speaking to The Indian Express, Nainital District Magistrate Lalit Mohan said that the administration is considering a new standard operating procedure under which an existing bypass connecting the Kainchi area towards Almora and Ranikhet could be opened to divert traffic as a solution to the crowd. The district administration will meet temple authorities, police and other stakeholders on Tuesday to finalise crowd-control measures, he said. We usually expect about 25,000 people visiting the shrine every day, but this weekend, since October 2, we have seen a crowd of more than 35,000 every day. Both the pilgrims and the locals use the same road to Kainchi, which also goes up to Mukteshwar, causing a traffic jam for hours, Lalit Mohan said. He said traffic had been cleared from the Mukteshwar side on Sunday. What explains the surge? Mohan attributed the latest surge to two factors the end of the monsoon, when travellers who had avoided the hills because of rain and landslides return, and the release of Hanuman Ansh, the film based on the life and teachings of Neem Karoli Baba. When The Indian Express reported on Kainchi Dham last month, Hanuman Ansh, made on a reported budget of Rs 2 crore, had grossed around Rs 300 crore worldwide. Its success has introduced Neem Karoli Baba, who died in 1973, to a younger audience far removed from the generation that knew him during his lifetime. It is learnt that 24.34 lakh people visited Kainchi Dham in the first six months of 2026, compared with around eight lakh visitors in the entire previous year. The surge has even prompted Hanuman Ansh director Vishal Chaturvedi to urge devotees to check the situation before travelling to Kainchi Dham. There is a huge crowd at Kainchi Dham at the moment. we should all check the situation there before going, he said, adding that visitors should avoid a situation where children and women in your family are suffocating in the crowd or are stuck in a traffic jam. He also suggested that devotees consider other sites associated with Neem Karoli Baba if Kainchi remains overcrowded. The hills are choked The proposed diversion comes as Uttarakhand is already building an 18.15-km Kainchi Dham bypass from Sanatorium to Ranighat. Eight kilometres were completed and hot-mixed earlier this year, and hill-cutting on another 10.15 km is done too. A motor bridge is also being built to connect the bypass with the Bhowali-Almora highway. The state has separately built the Bhowali bypass and a 30-metre double-lane bridge over the Shipra River to ease congestion in the area. The states Public Works Department has also identified the Talla Ramgarh-Ratighat road as an alternative route connecting Kainchi with Ramgarh, Mukteshwar, Lohaghat and Champawat, saying its strengthening could significantly reduce traffic pressure. A state planning document notes that Uttarakhand receives tourists equivalent to roughly 300 per cent of its resident population, compared with 185 per cent in Himachal Pradesh, and warns that hill destinations once known for walking and trekking are increasingly being choked by vehicles. The National Green Tribunal has recently taken on record a scientific carrying-capacity study covering major pilgrimage sites including Kedarnath, Hemkund Sahib, Gangotri and Yamunotri, reflecting a wider debate over the limits of tourism and pilgrimage in the fragile Himalayas. Kainchi has already had its own carrying-capacity study. A Tourism Department study conducted in 2025 found that 64 per cent of devotees came only for darshan and returned the same day, while 82.4 per cent were from outside Uttarakhand. Nearly two-thirds were aged between 15 and 30. Parking was the biggest infrastructure complaint, with 74 per cent of respondents dissatisfied with parking facilities. At the temple, authorities said the situation remained manageable. Pradeep Bhatt, who works in Kainchi Dhams accounts section, said authorities have deployed additional police personnel inside and outside the temple. The crowd has swelled due to the long weekend. Police are taking extra precautions. The police force is now being placed inside and outside the temple too. So far it has been managed all right, he said. By Monday, the immediate crisis had eased. Dheeraj Tiwari, 27, who runs his familys business beside the temple entrance, said the worst congestion lasted a day or two. The administration has now cleared everything out. Today everything looks normal. It was the long weekend that created a lot of flow of pilgrims, he said. For residents, however, the problem is measured differently. Mani Bharadwaj, who formerly worked at Hotel Monal, about 500 metres from the shrine, and lives in Bhowali, said the disruption extended beyond tourists. Today things seem to have gone back to normal, but over the weekend the locals faced a lot of problems. When thousands of vehicles are stuck on the same road, it affects everyone-people going to work, bringing supplies, travelling for medical needs or simply trying to get home. Locals have no separate road. The same infrastructure has to serve pilgrims and local residents. Every time there is a huge rush, locals bear the disruption. There needs to be a permanent solution rather than waiting for every long weekend and then putting more police on the roads, he said.

articleTitle: Flare-up at SRFTI as Hindu outfit protesters hurl bricks, bottles at students
articleFeaturedImageAlt: srfti
description: Students had earlier expressed concerns to I&B Ministry over protest march, and asked Kolkata Police not to give permission for rally
body_raw: A week after clashes at Kolkatas SRFTI over an RSS-linked outfits event on the campus, tension flared up at the film institute again on Sunday evening as members of a Hindu outfit hurled bricks and bottles at the students from outside. Members of the Bangiyo Hindu Jagaran Manch BHJM, who held a protest march, alleging insults to Swami Vivekananda and Bharat Mata by SRFTI students, also scuffled with the police as they tried to enter the SRFTI campus, leaving some of the policemen injured. According to students, they wrote to Kolkata Police and the West Bengal government on Saturday, asking them not to allow Bangiyo Hindu Jagaran Manch to hold the march, and to deploy adequate police personnel for their safety and security. A similar letter was sent to Union Minister for Information and Broadcasting Ashwini Vaishnaw by students of FTII Pune, SRFTI Kolkata, and FTII Itanagar, expressing serious concerns over the security of students at the institutes Kolkata campus in the aftermath of the September 27 clash on the campus. On Sunday, members of the Bangiyo Hindu Jagaran Manch reached the gates of the SRTFI on the EM Bypass and tried to enter the campus. They shouted slogans against the institute, calling the students of SRTFI Naxalites. They must be thrown out. They have insulted Bharat Maa. We will not tolerate this. They either have to love India or have to leave India, shouted a protester. Inside the campus, the students and teachers were seen deflecting the bottles and bricks thrown at them by protesters and chanting slogans like Go Back, No entry to fascists. A student of the SRFTI alleged that the protesters tore down the pictures of Dr BR Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi and instead put pictures of Bharat Maa on the gates of the institute. In a letter to the Minister of Information and Broadcasting, the students wrote, We have been informed that a rally organised by the Hindu Jagran Manch is proposed to take place on October 4 at 4 pm, approximately 800 metres from the main gate of the SRFTI. This comes barely a week after the violent confrontation on the SRFTI campus, in which several students and members of the institute community were injured. In the present circumstances, the proposed rally in such close proximity to the institute has understandably caused serious concern among the students. The SRFTI students are presently engaging with the concerned authorities to seek that the rally not be permitted within the periphery of the institute. Last Sunday, a group of students objected to an event of Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat, an RSS-linked outfit, on the campus, leading to clashes. The students union of the SRFTI said that members of ABGP assaulted students and teachers and called them anti-nationals, urban naxals and terrorists. A day later, three FIRs were registered on Monday-two against unknown students and one against unknown persons. Taking suo motu cognizance of the incident, the Kolkata Police filed an FIR against unknown students. Another FIR, registered on a complaint filed by Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat ABGP, the RSS-linked outfit, also named unknown students. Only the FIR, based on a complaint lodged by SRFTI Dean Film Sukanta Majumder, was filed against unknown persons. All three FIRs more or less include BNS sections of wrongful restraint, assault on public servants, voluntarily causing harm, and criminal intimidation. It was alleged that ABGP members wrongfully restrained students and two faculty members of the institute, voluntarily caused hurt, insulted women students modesty, and also threatened them. Two days later, the BJP government in the state formed a six-member Special Investigation Team to probe the September 27 violence on the campus.

articleTitle: Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao dies at 94
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao dead
description: Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao died in Chennai on Saturday night due to age-related health complications.
body_raw: Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, who directed some of the most innovative and genre-defining films in Indian cinema including the dialogue-free Pushpaka Vimanam, and the time-travel epic Aditya 369, died at Kauvery Hospital in Chennai on Saturday night. He was 94. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao was admitted to the hospital after his health deteriorated recently. He had been receiving treatment for age-related ailments. Born on September 21, 1931, in Gudur, Andhra Pradesh, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao began his career as an assistant to director L.V. Prasad before making his directorial debut with Neeti Nijayiti 1972. Also Read From Indias first time-travel epic to SSR61 How the 94-year-old filmmaker is set to disrupt cinema again Across a career spanning six decades and five languages, he directed some of the most innovative films in Indian cinema. Even at 94, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao refused to stop. His final film, Sing Geetham, a musical fantasy produced by Nag Ashwin, was completed earlier this year, making him among the oldest active filmmakers in the world. Actors, filmmakers and industry veterans across South Indian cinema have begun sharing tributes and condolences on social media. Actor Jr NTR called him a visionary who thought ahead of his time, delivering films that feel fresh even across generations. Composer Devi Sri Prasad wrote on X, Dearest SINGEETAM SIR..We wil MISS YOU Sir.. You will always live in our Hearts. You are an Unparalleled LEGEND..An Everest of Positivity filled with Evergreen Youth..The Movies You made with such Fururistic Ideas and Techniques are lessons to all of us and the Future Generations of Film Makers too. Thankyou Love You for Everything Sir..Iam blessed to have known You worked with You Sir. Singeetham Srinivasa Raos most notable films include Mayur, a biographical drama on amputee classical dancer Sudha Chandran that won several awards. Pushpaka Vimanam, a dialogue-free black comedy starring Kamal Haasan, won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Aditya 369, starring Nandamuri Balakrishna and featuring music by Ilaiyaraaja, was the first Telugu science fiction film to depict time travel. Bhairava Dweepam, also starring Balakrishna, was a high-fantasy adventure that completed a 100-day run in 28 centres. He also worked extensively in Kannada and Hindi cinema.

articleTitle: Woman tracked husband, his companion through hotel QR payment. Then, a crime
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Thrissur assault case, Thrissur sexual assault case, Thrissur Police arrests, hotel QR code tracking,
description: Assistant Police Commissioner T R Rajesh said the wife, whom police have identified as the chief suspect in the case, had known about her taxi-driver husband’s affair for eight years and had him followed.
body_raw: It was a payment made to the hotels QR code that allegedly exposed their whereabouts. This week, Thrissur Police arrested six people in connection with the alleged sexual assault of a woman from Malappuram in Keralam and the assault of her male friend from Tamil Nadu, after investigators said the latters wife allegedly tracked them down through a payment made to a hotel and allegedly sent a gang to pursue them. The six people arrested include the mans wife, who is from Tiruppur in Tamil Nadu. Others arrested are Thomas Priyadarsan Dev, a 27-year-old native of Nilgiris Regupathi Raja, a 20-year-old from Dindugal Sankar, a 20-year-old from Karur and Balraj, a 31-year-old from Kadavur. A magistrate court in Thrissur remanded them to judicial custody for two weeks. Assistant Police Commissioner T R Rajesh said the wife, whom police have identified as the chief suspect in the case, had known about her taxi-driver husbands affair for eight years and had him followed. The gang members were all taxi drivers. On the morning of September 22, the victims checked into a hotel while reportedly returning from a trip to Wayanad. Since he needed money, he contacted his wife and shared the hotels merchant payment QR code. She paid money to the hotels account from her UPI app, which enabled her to locate her husband, said the assistant commissioner. Police said the woman then alerted one of the gang. Four others joined him, and they rushed to Thrissur, some 170 km away, and introduced themselves to the hotel as a police team looking for a man from Tamil Nadu who they claimed had stolen 65 sovereigns of gold. Having gained entry, they allegedly stormed into the victims room, abducted them and took them back to Tiruppur, where police said the woman was sexually assaulted. The next day, the woman managed to escape while the group was relocating her. En route, when the car was stopped somewhere, two passersby grew suspicious when they saw a woman with torn clothes sitting in the car. As the gang fled, the locals helped her reach the nearest railway station and return to Keralam, the officer said. Upon reaching Keralam, the woman lodged a complaint with her home district Malappuram police, who in turn transferred the case to Thrissur. The duo the victims met in Ernakulam during the taxi drivers trip to Keralam. The Tamil Nadu mans wife had been having them for some time. We are checking whether the arrested gang has any recorded criminal antecedents, one officer.

articleTitle: IIM Lucknow, TeamLease launch 11-month executive programme in Brand Management
articleFeaturedImageAlt: iim lucknow medusa campus image
description: The curriculum covers consumer insights, brand strategy and integrated communications, along with digital marketing, e-commerce, performance marketing and customer lifecycle management.
body_raw: The Indian Institute of Management IIM Lucknow has launched an 11-month Executive Programme in Brand Management in partnership with TeamLease EdTech, for working professionals seeking to build skills in brand strategy, consumer understanding, digital marketing and business decision-making. The programme comprises 132 learning hours, including 114 hours of live online learning and 18 hours through a three-day campus immersion at IIM Lucknow. The course uses case studies, business simulations, projects, assignments, faculty-led live sessions, practitioner-led masterclasses and peer learning to connect classroom concepts with business situations. Read JEE scores can get you into these IIMs undergraduate programmes after Class 12 The curriculum covers consumer insights, brand strategy and integrated communications, along with digital marketing, e-commerce, performance marketing and customer lifecycle management. Participants will also study digital consumer psychology, brand storytelling, social media and influencer branding, marketplace and quick-commerce strategy, and omnichannel growth. A key component of the programme is the use of emerging technologies in marketing. The curriculum covers AI-driven marketing and advertising and examines how AI can be used to understand consumers and support engagement with them. The programme also looks at how changing digital consumer journeys affect brand building and customer experience. The programme links marketing decisions with the financial and commercial aspects of running a brand. Participants will learn about unit economics, profitability, financial planning, valuation and governance, along with cross-functional leadership. This is intended to help professionals assess brand decisions not only from a consumer or marketing perspective but also in terms of their wider business impact. Also Read From buckets to hangers Why No-Bag Day is becoming a campus trend at IITs, IIMs The programme is designed for brand and marketing professionals, digital and growth professionals, product and business leaders, entrepreneurs, sales professionals and those aspiring to marketing leadership roles. The curriculum is structured around the changing role of brand managers, where consumer insight, digital execution, data, technology and business economics increasingly overlap. Learning is primarily delivered online, with the campus component providing an opportunity for in-person learning at IIM Lucknow. The application-oriented format includes business simulations and projects alongside academic sessions, allowing participants to apply concepts such as positioning, customer experience, digital growth and marketing economics to business situations. The programme is open to graduates, diploma holders and postgraduates. Selection will be based on the candidates academic and professional background and experience. Participants who meet the prescribed academic and attendance requirements will receive a Certificate of Successful Completion from IIM Lucknow. Admissions for the upcoming cohort are open. Details on the programme curriculum, eligibility, fee and application process are available on the programme website.

articleTitle: Nimrat Kaur recalls father’s killing by terrorists: ‘Next time I saw him was in coffin’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Nimrat Kaur
description: Nimrat Kaur has opened up about losing her father, Major Bhupender Singh, who was kidnapped and killed by terrorists in Kashmir in 1994, when she was just 11 years old.
body_raw: Actor Nimrat Kaur has opened up about the trauma of losing her father, Major Bhupender Singh, in Kashmir when she was only 11 years old. Nimrat recalled how her mother, who was in her early to mid-30s at the time, was left to raise her and her sister after the tragedy. Major Bhupender Singh, an Indian Army officer, was posted in Kashmir when he was abducted and killed by terrorists in January 1994. He was later posthumously awarded the Shaurya Chakra. Nimrat Kaur recalls losing father at 11 In a recent conversation with ANI, Nimrat Kaur said her mother was very young when their world changed overnight. She said, My mom was very young when we lost my father in Kashmir. She was literally in her early to mid-30s. So, the world she knew collapsed. We were just two young girls she was bringing up. We had family around us to support us at the time, especially from my maternal side. But, having said that, the life we knew was over. Nimrat said it was the two daughters who gave her mother the courage to rebuild their lives. It was really, really traumatic for her. I think the reason she went on and found the courage to bring herself together was because she recognised that these two kids had an entire life ahead of them. I think thats what gave her the courage, she said. ALSO READ Amitabh Bachchan on bond with Abhishek Bachchan Views may differ, destination remains same Nimrat Kaur says father was kidnapped by men posing as soldiers Recalling the circumstances surrounding her fathers death, Nimrat Kaur said Major Bhupender Singh was kidnapped while returning from an official duty. He was actually kidnapped on a normal day of work. He was going somewhere for a duty that he had been assigned and then, on his way back, he was kidnapped by people who posed as soldiers. They were wearing army fatigues and he was taken away, she said. Nimrat said the terrorists made several demands over the following seven days, including the release of people held captive in India. There were some ridiculous demands. They demanded the release of other people who were in captivity in India, and other ridiculous demands that came up over a period of seven days, she said. The family was visiting Major Bhupender Singh in Kashmir at the time. Nimrat recalled that she, her mother and sister were initially in Verinag but were later moved to Srinagar after the situation became unsafe. On the seventh day, they received news that he had been killed. Recalling what she had learned about the conversations before he was killed, she said, He told them that, I have a family, I have two girls. I know that he was thinking of us in his last thoughts. That was all that I think he would have wanted to come back to. I saw my father leave for work, then saw him in a coffin Nimrat Kaur said the circumstances of her fathers death left the family without any sense of closure. I saw my father leave for work that morning. I just remember him leaving and then, after that, the next time I saw him was in a coffin. So, there is no closure there, she said. The actor added that the passage of decades has not erased the pain of the loss. Its a strange feeling even after all these years because, technically, you feel like its been so long. Its been a few decades, but nothing quite repairs that. Not for my mom, not for my sister, not for me, and not for the rest of the family. Nimrat Kaur credits her mother for rebuilding their lives The Lunchbox actor also spoke at length about her mothers resilience and the way she raised two daughters after losing her husband. I really feel like the way my mother has brought us up and the way she has rebuilt her life and rebuilt our lives after that, I dont know of many women who would be able to do that single-handedly and so respectfully and in such a dignified way, she said. After Major Bhupender Singhs death, Nimrat Kaur, her mother and sister moved to Noida, where her maternal grandparents lived.

articleTitle: Army officer died of illness. On way home with body, family loses 3 more
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Army officer family killed Purvanchal expressway
description: The body of Subedar Major Satyawan Singh was being taken from Chandigarh to Deoria when the ambulance hit a parked truck on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur.
body_raw: An Army officers three family members were killed when an ambulance carrying his body met with an accident on the Purvanchal Expressway in Sultanpur district early on Sunday. The ambulance driver also died in the accident. The police suspect that the ambulance hit a parked truck on the expressway. The police said the ambulance was carrying the body of Subedar Major Satyawan Singh, 50, a resident of Rudrapur in Deoria who was posted in Meerut. He had been receiving treatment for kidney disease at the Command Hospital in Chandigarh. The police identified the victims as the Army officers brother Ram Samujh, son Gaurav Singh, nephew Rajan Singh, and the ambulance driver, Jaspal. The impact of the accident was so severe that the front portion of the ambulance was mangled. Two people seated in the front, including the driver, died on the spot. Their bodies were trapped inside the wreckage and had to be extricated by cutting open the vehicle. The others died during treatment at a government hospital in Ayodhya. The bodies have been sent for postmortem examination. District Magistrate Indrajeet Singh said the bodies would be sent to Deoria after the completion of formalities. We are coordinating with officials in Deoria and the Army to facilitate the process, he added. According to the Sultanpur police, they received information from the police control room on Sunday morning about an ambulance accident involving an unidentified vehicle on the Purvanchal Expressway. A police team reached the spot and rushed the injured occupants to a hospital, where doctors declared them dead. Other family members of the officer were travelling in a separate vehicle that was following the ambulance.

articleTitle: Baby orangutans face longer quarantine at Odisha zoo
articleFeaturedImageAlt: According to zoo officials, the priority is to ensure the infants receive the best possible healthcare and management during their stay at Nandankanan.
description: Rescued from a Balasore forest last month, the five animals will remain under close watch at Nandankanan as officials monitor their health, behaviour and development
body_raw: The five baby orangutans rescued from a forest in Odishas Balasore district are set for a longer stay in Odishas Nandankanan Zoological Park. The animals, rescued from the forests of Balasore in September amid smuggling concerns, will remain in quarantine for 90 days at the zoo, where officials said their health and well-being will be closely monitored. Nandankanan officials said the Central Zoo Authority CZA has advised a 90-day quarantine for the orangutans as part of biosecurity protocols - measures used to prevent, control and stop the spread of diseases among animal populations. The CZA has also advised that only caregivers and doctors be allowed to enter the quarantine facility where the infant orangutans are being kept. The orangutans will be quarantined in the hand-rearing centre HRC area only, where they are currently kept. We have open enclosures at the side of HRC, having a larger area and open skies, where the apes will be moved during the day to acclimatise with the environment after the advice of the technical committee, Deputy Zoo Director Pradeep Mirase told The Indian Express. The five baby orangutans rescued from a forest in Odishas Balasore district are set for a longer stay in Odishas Nandankanan Zoological Park. The animals, rescued from the forests of Balasore in September amid smuggling concerns, will remain in quarantine for 90 days at the. pic.twitter.comtMvONCEkRK - The Indian Express IndianExpress October 3, 2026 While a mandatory quarantine period of 30 days is standard for animals imported into Indian zoos, it is generally extended to 90 days in multiple phases for highly protected or high-risk species. Orangutans are listed under Appendix I of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species CITES, which imposes the highest level of protection on species threatened with extinction and restricts their international trade. Orangutans are native to the rainforests of Indonesia and Malaysia, across Borneo and Sumatra, and are critically endangered according to the International Union for Conservation of Nature IUCN Red List. The decision to quarantine the orangutans comes as authorities continue to investigate where the apes, first spotted in the forests of Odisha on September 8, came from. The rescued orangutans are infants their place of origin remains unknown, and their health history is also unclear. We dont know if they have any underlying diseases. In view of the CZA advisory, it was decided to quarantine the apes for 90 days, said the zoo deputy director. Even after completion of the quarantine period, there will be no public viewing of the rescued orangutans at Nandankanan until a final decision is taken by the state government and other statutory bodies. According to zoo officials, the priority is to ensure the infants receive the best possible healthcare and management during their stay at Nandankanan. While the state government has formed a five-member technical committee comprising experts to oversee the health, welfare and management of the baby orangutans, zoo authorities monitor their health conditions daily. There is a gradual increase in the weight of each baby. The orangutan babies are apparently healthy and have a normal appetite, while their behaviour and activity levels are gradually improving. Their faecal consistency is also normal, said a statement issued by the zoo on September 26. While three of the five baby orangutans were found to be anaemic - one severely - officials said the haemoglobin levels in two of the three apes are gradually improving. No decision has been taken yet on conducting their DNA tests to determine their species and geographical origin. The five baby orangutans were rescued from a forest in the states Balasore district on September 8, raising concerns of smuggling. Meanwhile, the high-level probe into how the apes reached Odishas forests has remained slow, with sources saying there is still no breakthrough. The Wildlife Crime Control Bureau WCCB was also roped in to investigate potential smuggling in the case.

articleTitle: From calling for peace in Russia-Ukraine and beyond, Delhi is now working for it
articleFeaturedImageAlt: From calling for peace, Delhi is now working for it
description: Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has said that, among the proposals Kyiv has received, India’s is the “most comprehensive”; President Putin has said PM Modi “constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict” and has “very good ideas”.
body_raw: By all accounts, India has stepped into a more proactive role vis-a-vis the Russia-Ukraine war. Since the conflict began in February 2022, New Delhi has consistently urged restraint, with PM Narendra Modi saying to Russian President Vladimir Putin in September that year that this is not an era of war. Now, Ukraines Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has said that, among the proposals Kyiv has received, Indias is the most comprehensive President Putin has said PM Modi constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict and has very good ideas and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has acknowledged that India has gone beyond advocacy and is talking to both sides. The shift from calling for peace to working for it is welcome. Delhi must build on it. On this front, Indias interests align with those of the world. Strikes on ports and vessels by both Russia and Ukraine, two major grain exporters, have left farmers in both countries vulnerable and increased the risk of a global food shock. Minister Jaishankar referred to this a few days ago when he warned of a major food crisis in the coming months, in addition to the already significant fertiliser shortages caused by conflicts in Eastern Europe and West Asia. The Ukraine war has also disrupted European energy markets, while Indias purchases of Russian oil have strained ties with the US. An end to the war, or even a de-escalation, would ease such pressures. Going forward, Delhi would do well to focus on specific issues such as grain and energy, rather than sweeping questions involving territory or security guarantees. Both sides have immediate and shared interests in these areas, which means something can be agreed upon without first resolving the harder questions. Even if it does not exert as much leverage over Ukraine or Russia as the US and China, respectively, India can demonstrate that it is actively working towards getting the warring parties to talk. A record of even-handed diplomacy would also answer critics who see India as too close to Russia, a relationship that has drawn scrutiny, not least over oil purchases, for nearly five years.

articleTitle: CISF jawan kills colleagues: Inside the high-stress life of paramilitary and armed forces
articleFeaturedImageAlt: CISF
description: In 2022, the Union Home Ministry had constituted a task force to study suicides and fratricides in the CAPFs. The findings point to a mix of service-related pressures, difficult working conditions, and personal issues.
body_raw: On Tuesday evening September 29, an Assistant Commandant of the Central Industrial Security Force CISF and three other personnel were killed after a head constable of the force allegedly opened fire at them with his AK-47 following an altercation in Jammu and Kashmirs Kathua district. The incident has been termed as an instance of fratricide. The dictionary meaning of fratricide refers to the act of killing ones own brother or sister, or a person who has a very close bond like a brother. In a military context, however, it refers to a service member killing someone on their own side, be it a case of accidental friendly fire or otherwise. Tuesdays incident has once again brought the spotlight back on suicides and fratricides in the Central Armed Police Forces CAPFs as well as the armed forces. We explain why such incidents occur in the forces, what a government-constituted task force found, and what steps have been taken to help mitigate these incidents. Fratricide in the CAPFs The CAPFs, which fall under the administrative control of the Union Ministry of Home Affairs MHA, comprise the CISF, the Assam Rifles, the Border Security Force, the Central Reserve Police Force, the Indo Tibetan Border Police, the National Security Guard, and the Sashastra Seema Bal. In the nine years between 2017 and 2025, 64 CAPF personnel were killed in fratricidal incidents and 1,126 personnel died by suicide, according to official data and government records. A key concern repeatedly flagged in official and internal reviews is that many personnel work for long periods in difficult conditions. These include prolonged deployment in high-risk areas, separation from families, harsh terrain and climate, long duty hours, and limited opportunities for rest and recreation. Fratricide in the Army Cases of fratricide are not very common in the Indian Armed Forces, although not unheard of. Consolidated Parliamentary data between 2019 and 2022 shows that there were seven cases of fratricide in the Indian Army during this period - with two cases each in 2019, 2020 and 2021 and one case in 2022. The IAF reported one case in 2019, and the Indian Navy reported no cases during this period, as per the data. A separate set of Parliamentary data stated that between 2014 and 2021, there were 18 incidents of fratricide in the Army and two in the IAF. In 2023, there was a major fratricide case in the Indian Army in which four soldiers of the 80 Medium Regiment were killed inside the Bathinda military station, with a soldier killing his colleagues due to personal animosity. In October of the same year, a Major of 48 Rashtriya Rifles reportedly opened fire and threw a grenade at fellow personnel, injuring several officers. The Armys White Knight Corps described the incident as a likely grenade accident. There was another suspected case of fratricide in the Army when a junior commissioned officer was killed in Samba in Jammu division in 2025. Officials said that one of the major reasons for such cases, and even for suicides in the Armed Forces, is combat stress and also stresses in a soldiers personal life, which are also fueled by prolonged deployments and isolation due to posting in difficult locations. What did the task force find? A task force constituted by the MHA in 2022 to study suicides and fratricides in the forces found that personnel may turn violent when they feel their problems are not being addressed. The task force identified three broad factors behind suicides and fratricides service conditions, working conditions, and personal or individual issues. Under service conditions, it found that leave-related problems were a major trigger across the CAPFs. It also flagged discrimination among sub-groups, workplace bullying, abuse, fear of disciplinary or legal action, and poor communication between company commanders and jawans. Under working conditions, it pointed to extended working hours, inadequate rest and recreation, lack of job satisfaction, isolation, weak social and family support, and the absence of a robust grievance redressal mechanism. Why is leave such a sensitive issue? Leave is among the most frequently cited stress points, because CAPF personnel often serve far from home for long stretches. The task force found that denial or delay of leave, especially during family emergencies, can aggravate stress. In fratricide cases, the task force found that personnel may turn violent when they believe their grievances are not being resolved. It also noted that not getting leave when a family member is critically ill, or in the event of a death in the family, can become a serious provocation. What were the personal factors cited? The task force also listed several personal and social factors. These included mental health issues, feelings of hopelessness or depression, stigma around certain diseases, substance abuse, financial problems, marital or family-related problems, groupism, casteism, instigation by others over petty disputes, and the impact of frequent transfers on childrens education. The report also flagged broader morale-related issues such as slow promotions, dissatisfaction over the New Pension Scheme, continuous posting in conflict theatres, limited growth opportunities, and the absence of adequately trained professionals to deal with trauma among personnel. What has Parliament said on the issue? The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs had noted that CAPF personnel function under considerable duress because of the nature of their duties and postings in harsh climatic conditions. It observed that leave at appropriate intervals is necessary to help personnel spend time with their families and reduce stress. This aligns with the task forces finding that leave-related stress is one of the major triggers in suicide and fratricide cases. What steps have been taken for welfare and mental-health support? The CISF has taken force-specific steps. Earlier this month, it signed a three-year memorandum of understanding with the Institute of Human Behaviour and Allied Sciences IHBAS, adding a clinical and psychiatric layer to its mental-health support system. The agreement brings a specialist mental-health institution into the CISFs welfare framework. IHBAS will provide specialised psychometric assessments for CISF personnel posted in highly sensitive units, including those proposed for deployment at the Parliament House Complex. Praveer Ranjan, Director General - CISF, said CISF personnel work in exceptionally demanding and high-responsibility environments. This partnership with IHBAS will significantly strengthen our efforts toward early identification, professional counselling, and timely clinical treatment of mental health concerns. Our absolute focus is to create an organisational culture where seeking professional support is actively encouraged and entirely free from stigma, he told The Indian Express. In the case of the armed forces, the government has taken several steps towards stress amelioration amongst troops. This includes deployment of trained psychological counsellors, improvement in the quality of food and clothing, training in stress management, provision of recreational facilities, buddy system, leave concessions, approachability of seniors, facilities for movement of troops from border areas and establishing a grievance redressal mechanism at various levels. What are the challenges going forward? The findings show that suicides and fratricides in the CAPFs cannot be explained by a single trigger. They occur owing to multiple factors such as stressful deployment, leave pressures, weak communication, workplace grievances, family separation, mental-health concerns and career-related dissatisfaction. For both the government and the forces, the challenge is to move beyond reactive responses. Going forward, the task is to build systems that identify distress early, improve access to leave and counselling, strengthen grievance redressal, reduce avoidable humiliation or isolation within units, and make professional help easier to seek without stigma.

articleTitle: AAP sees 68% fall in donations, BJD declares zero contributions
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Former Odisha Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik and Former Odisha Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik (ANI and File Photo)
description: EC is yet to make public contribution reports of the BJP, Congress and other national parties.
body_raw: The Aam Aadmi Party declared donations of Rs 12.09 crore in 2025-26, showing a 68 decrease from the previous year, the partys contribution report to the Election Commission reveals. The contributions to the Biju Janata Dal fell 100 in the same year, which was its first year out of power in Odisha after over two decades. Of the AAPs total declared contributions in 2025-26, two donors - the Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Limited - accounted for nearly all of it, with Rs 5 crore each. Prudent Electoral Trust is one of the key donors to parties, which in past years received contributions from leading corporations, including Bharti, Tata Group, Jindal, etc. The report of donations to Prudent for 2025-26 was not yet available. Trident Ltd was founded by Rajinder Gupta, the Punjab-based billionaire who was an AAP MP until switching to the BJP earlier this year. AAP also received Rs 5 lakh from Jain Siddiqui and Associates and Rs 20,010 from Brilliant Study Centre, with the remaining donors being individuals. Ashutosh Ranka, now a co-convener of the Cockroach Janta Party CJP, who had earlier served as an AAP spokesperson, made a donation of Rs 21,100 to the party. In 2024-25, the AAP had declared Rs 38.10 crore in donations. The total amount of donations to the party may be higher as parties are only required to submit details of all donations above Rs 20,000 each in their annual contribution reports to the EC. The Biju Janata Dal, which was in power in Odisha for 24 continuous years until 2024, declared nil donations over Rs 20,000. Last year, it declared contributions of Rs 60 crore, with Vedanta Ltd the biggest donor with Rs 25 crore. Meanwhile, BJP ally Asom Gana Parishad, which received total contributions of Rs 7.64 crore, got a substantial chunk of this, that is Rs 5.18 crore, from the BJPs state unit in Assam. Apart from this, the party received contributions worth Rs 35 lakh from two companies in separate tranches of Rs 25 lakh and Rs 10 lakh, respectively. On the other hand, key NDA ally Telugu Desam Party received Rs 58.25 crore in contributions. Of that, Rs 45 crore were received from the Prudent Electoral Trust based out of Delhi. Companies were the next largest donors to the TDP having contributed Rs 1.76 crore. Chirag Paswans Lok Janshakti Party Ram Vilas, which received Rs 3.23 crore in donations, got Rs 1 crore from the Prudent Electoral Trust. On the other hand, companies such as Agventure Enterprises Private Ltd, Magnum Management and Services, Ganesh Infraworld Ltd, JPJ Infratech Pvt Ltd, and Bhawani Homes Projects Pvt Ltd, among others, accounted for over Rs 80 lakh of the contributions received. The YSRCP declared donations of Rs 24.30 crore, with the largest contribution of Rs 10 crore from Chennai-based Goodwood Sanctuary Pvt Ltd and Rs 5 crore from NA Divine Habitat Pvt Ltd, also from Chennai. The EC is yet to make public the contribution reports of the BJP, Congress and other national parties.

articleTitle: Trump’s Brazil blooper: ‘125 million voted in India’s Presidential Election’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Brazil-India
description: Trump's post came a day after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, 4 October.
body_raw: US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that 125 million people voted in the first round of Indias Presidential Election. The vote he described appears to be Brazils election, which was held on Sunday, 4 October. Trump used the post to say that US results take too long to count. He wrote that in Detroit, Philadelphia, California and other cities and states, results with far smaller numbers often take weeks. He ended with Voting in America is CORRUPT. In the post he first wrote the word Rig and then corrected it to calculate. Photo realDonaldTrump About 124.5 million Brazilians cast votes on Sunday, which is close to the figure Trump used, according to figures cited by Courthouse News. The post came a day after Brazils first round, which sent President Luiz Incio Lula da Silva and Senator Flvio Bolsonaro to a runoff. In the post, Trump said the results of the vote he described came out soon after polls closed, on the same day. He compared this with the US, where he said counts in some cities and states take weeks even though the numbers are much smaller. He signed off as President DJT. The post gave no evidence for his claims about US vote counting. Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, 4 October. With nearly all votes counted, Flvio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, came first with about 47 of valid votes, Reuters said. Lula came second with about 45. Neither man won more than half of the valid votes, so the two will face each other in a second round on 25 October. Brazil has nearly 159 million registered voters. About 124.5 million of them voted, and about 21 did not, according to figures cited by Courthouse News. The result gave a lift to the Bolsonaro family. Flvio was picked by his father to carry on the familys political work. Other family members and allies also won seats in Congress or state governor races. Meanwhile, India does not choose its president by a nationwide vote. The president is elected by an Electoral College. It is made up of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the state legislative assemblies, including Delhi and Puducherry. The vote uses proportional representation with a single transferable vote, and the ballot is secret.

articleTitle: Sharat Saxena starts work 27 days post spine surgery; expert explains recovery in the 70s
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sharat Saxena
description: The actor’s quick return to work after a major spine procedure has experts weighing in on what recovery really involves
body_raw: Veteran actor Sharat Saxena, 76, recently underwent a six-hour lumbar spine surgery and is back to work. What a wonderful feeling to be able to work again. Started working again, 27 days after spine surgery, he wrote in a post on Instagram. Dr Amogh Zawar, consultant, spine surgery, KIMS Hospitals Thane, told indianexpress.com that resuming work just over 25 days is possible in a few cases. Yes, in select cases, patients can return to work within a few weeks of spine surgery, particularly when the procedure is minimally invasive, and recovery is progressing well. However, there is no universal timeline for returning to work. It depends on the type of surgery, the spinal condition being treated, the patients age and health, and the physical demands of their work, said Dr Zawar. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. What factors determine how quickly someone can return to normal activities after spine surgery? According to Dr Zawar, pain control, mobility, muscle strength, neurological recovery, and the nature of the surgery are key factors. A patient with a less extensive procedure may regain mobility relatively quickly, while someone undergoing a more complex surgery may need several weeks or months. Rehabilitation and following post-operative precautions also play an important role, emphasised Dr Zawar. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Sharat Saxena sharatsaxena Does returning to work within 27 days mean the spine has completely healed? Not necessarily. Being fit to resume selected activities is different from complete healing. Patients may feel considerably better and become independent in their daily activities while the operated tissues continue to heal. Even after returning to work, they may need to avoid heavy lifting, prolonged sitting, excessive bending or other strenuous movements for some time, said Dr Zawar. The expert noted that the return must be assessed based on the specific demands of the job. An actor may need to deal with long hours, travel, prolonged standing or physical movements, depending on the role. A gradual return, with modifications wherever required, is generally safer than immediately resuming the full workload, asserted Dr Zawar. What to note? The focus should be on recovery rather than simply meeting a deadline. Patients should follow their surgeons advice, continue prescribed rehabilitation and increase activity gradually. New or worsening pain, weakness, numbness or difficulty walking should not be ignored. An early return can be possible for some patients, but 27 days should not be considered a standard recovery period for everyone, said Dr Zawar.
