articleTitle: Disquiet within, all three Election Commissioners meet, take first steps
articleFeaturedImageAlt: ECINET review, ECINET review committee, Election Commission ECINET, SIR row,
description: Unmapped voters need not attend hearings, ECINet to get a review
body_raw: IN ITS first meeting since The Indian Express reported on the deep divide within the Election Commission over the past 10 months, the poll panel on Saturday sought to address several concerns raised by its two commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. Electors who were issued notices for logical discrepancies and for being unmapped in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls will not be required to attend hearings to establish their eligibility, a statement issued by the ECI said. This exemption from in-person hearings will be a relief to lakhs of electors who were issued notices in the ongoing SIR. The decision comes as hearings are being held across states on the basis of system-generated notices. Unmapped voters are those whose names did not figure in the rolls of the previous intensive revision, and who were unable to provide the names of their parents or grandparents too during that revision. Logical discrepancies refers to certain discrepancies flagged by the ECIs centralised software based on which voters are issued notices following which they need to submit additional documentary proof to stay in the rolls. WATCH Election Commission Investigation Ritika Chopra Answers All Your Questions On ECI Investigation In case of any person to whom notice has been issued during the ongoing SIR, for being unmapped and logical discrepancies, BLOs will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them on the ECINet, for decision by the ERO. Such persons need not be called for hearing to EROAERO office. Only in exceptional circumstances, as decided by the ERO, the hearing will be held preferably online. Any adult member of the family can be authorised by the elector to attend the hearing on their behalf, if required, the EC announced. The Commission, comprising Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and ECs Sandhu and Joshi, held a meeting at 3pm on Saturday, the EC statement said. It underlined that the press note had the approval of the full Commission and released a photo of the three-member EC at the meeting. In its statement, the Commission also said that a declaration that was added without amendment to the voter enrolment form or Form 6, would go back to the original after the SIR. The Indian Express had reported that the two ECs had said this addition was illegal, unauthorised and called for its removal so that young, first-time voters are not harassed. Responding to some specific concerns, the EC said agendas would be circulated in advance for all commission meetings and minutes issued. The Annual Performance Appraisal Reports of officers would be completed within the stipulated time frame, which is by December 31 each year, and that the commissions approval will be taken for foreign trips of the officers. Further, in its statement, the EC said, All directions issued by the Commissioners to the officers of the Commission shall be meticulously complied with. The EC also clarified that the Form 6, which is the statutory form for new voter enrolment, would revert to the original one as per the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. Earlier this year, the EC had added a declaration to the online Form 6 that requires applicants to answer if they or their parentsgrandparents were on the rolls of the previous intensive revision of electoral rolls. While a separate declaration form was created by the EC for the SIR, the declaration was inserted within the online version of the Form 6, which can only be amended by the Law Ministry. The two Election Commissioners had raised concerns with the same. The declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Honble Supreme Court. For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used, the EC said in its statement. The two ECs, Sandhu and Joshi, had also flagged concerns with the centralisation of the ECINet portal. The EC on Saturday announced the setting up of a committee to review ECINet and double-check if it complies with the law. Field officers have role-based access to the ECINet system as per their statutory powers. A Committee headed by Sr. Deputy Election Commissioner DEC and including an independent expert from IITIIIT will review the ECINet to double-check that it complies with the provisions of the Acts and Rules and submit report to the Commission, it said. According to the statement, various upgradations of the portal have already been made based on the inputs from State CEOs in the past few months. In case, any further flexibility is required by the field officers, that will be made operational. Henceforth, all the new initiatives about IT modules and portals will be discussed in the Committee of Officers COO before approval by the Commission, it said. WATCH Sukhbir Singh Sandhu Vivek Joshi Who Are The 2 ECs Who Objected To SIR? The EC said that the letters written by the two ECs to Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan were in relation to the conduct of an officer. The letter to Cabinet Secretary was not related to any policy matter of the Commission or IT division but related to the working of an officer on deputation to ECI. The work re- distribution orders issued by the concerned officer were not actually implemented after the orders of the two Commissioners and the oversight over the IT division by the DEC was never actually withdrawn, the EC statement read. With regard to the ongoing SIR, which has been completed in 20 statesUTs so far, the EC said Any person whose name has got left out during SIR or thereafter, and any person including youngfirst-time voter, may apply to the concerned ERO, for inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls under the process of continuous updation. CEOs have been directed to facilitate the same. The CEOs, DEOs, EROs will immediately launch a special drive for enrolment of these electors. Regarding the issue of 97 Goa electors who had been deleted from the final roll despite the statutory officials recommending their inclusion during the SIR earlier this year, the EC said the Chief Electoral Officer of Goa had directed the Booth Level Officers concerned to collect enrolment forms from them, and 81 of those electors had already filled the Form 6.

articleTitle: Boxing to wrestling, archery to hockey: 6 gold medals power India to table top 5
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India's Kumkum Anil Mohod, Ankita Bhakat and Kirti celebrate on the podium during the medal ceremony after winning gold. (Reuters Photo)
description: Archers, women's hockey team, boxers and a wrestler make it count as India move to 5th place on the medal tally
body_raw: For nine days, India had waited for the gold rush. On Friday, it arrived - six in all - for the countrys best day at the Asian Games. With it India moved into the top-5 in the medal tally. It started with the archers making history and finished with the womens hockey team winning a rare gold. Each gold was won against the odds. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage The emcee introduced South Korea as a 10-time Olympic champion. Kumkum Mohod, the 17-year-old prodigy, heard it and thought But today, the Asian Games title will be ours. Minutes later, she, Kirti Sharma and Ankita Bhakat had brought the Korean archery dynasty crashing down. Three years ago in Hangzhou, boxer Parveen Hooda stood on the Asian Games podium. Then her bronze was taken away after an anti-doping rule violation, leaving her to rebuild her career. On Friday, she returned to the Asian Games to win gold. Wrestler Sujeet Kalkal had missed the last Asian Games after Bajrang Punia was handed a direct entry. He was stranded at a flooded Dubai airport, missed a crucial Olympic qualifier, and watched another door slam shut. In his maiden Asiad, he finally kicked one open, conquering wrestlings punishing 65 kg class. The womens hockey team missed the Paris Games, the dressing room had fractured and two coaches had come and gone. Then, coach Sjoerd Marijne returned. China was defeated in the final on Friday, the gold hung around the necks of Indian players for only the second time in Asian Games history, and the ticket to the LA Olympics was punched. From the wrestling mats in Noseki to the archery field in Okazaki, the boxing ring in Nishio and the hockey turf in Gifu, gold kept landing in different corners of Aichi in a matter of hours on Friday. The haul accounted for more than half of Indias gold tally at the start of the day. The gold rush propelled India into the top five on the table, with 76 medals - 16 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze. In Okazaki, the Indian archers had barely finished celebrating when the scale of what they had done began to sink in. Kumkum, Kirti and Ankita had beaten South Korea 5-3 to win the womens recurve team gold - Indias first in the event since recurve entered the Asian Games in 1994. The other statistic was even bigger. South Korea had held the throne like an heirloom since 1998, passing it from one generation to another. On a windy morning, an Indian team unburdened by that history ended the reign, leaving the Koreans with moist eyes. Lovlina shows the way Half an hour away, the boxers were warming up for an unprecedented haul. Lovlina Borgohain, celebrating her 29th birthday, added another layer to Japans hold on her career. Five years ago, Tokyo gave her an Olympic bronze. Since then, the journey has been uneven. Back in Japan, she found another major title, adding Asian Games gold to the Olympic medal she had won here. Until Friday, only Mary Kom had won an Asian Games boxing gold for India, in 2014. Lovlina pushed open the door, and Parveen Hooda stormed through it hours later. Parveen stepped into the ring carrying the memory of a medal she had already won. Her Hangzhou bronze was stripped after an anti-doping whereabouts violation, leaving her to wonder if she would have to rebuild her career from the beginning. When the whereabouts issue happened, I was mentally very down. Felt like everything was over and I would have to start from scratch, she said. She felt sorry for herself, but only briefly. So she returned. And in one of the closest bouts of the evening, she defeated Nien-chin Chen of Chinese Taipei to upgrade the lost bronze to gold. The Nishio ring then produced another kind of breakthrough. Ankush Panghal, one of the brightest young faces in Indian boxing, had no old wound to heal and no lost medal to reclaim. He had something else to prove that he belonged at this level. By the end of the day, he had the gold to prove it. Panghal wasnt the only one announcing himself. Sujeet Kalkal was trying to rescue a final that appeared to be slipping out of his grasp. He was down 9-2 against Abdulmazid Kudiev of Tajikistan in the 65kg final, a weight class he had spent years trying to conquer. Kalkal, whose father Dayanand was also a wrestler, had already defeated Paris Olympic champion and home favourite Kotaro Kiyooka in the semifinals. But halfway through the gold-medal bout, he looked down and out. Then came four quick takedowns in the final two minutes. Kalkal turned a 9-2 deficit into a 10-9 victory, capping a day in which he had finally made up for lost time - and announced himself as a contender with the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics on the horizon. By evening, the womens hockey team beat China 1-0 in Gifu, and the gold rush had come from the four corners of Aichi. Saturday is the penultimate day, but for India it could be another enormous one. The mens cricket team faces Pakistan in the final the hockey team meets Malaysia for gold the golfers head into the final round with leads to protect and the wrestlers have more medals to chase. And then there are the archers. After helping India end South Koreas long reign in the womens recurve team event, Kumkum returns for the individual rounds. The 17-year-old heard 10-time Olympic champion before Fridays final and thought today, the title will be ours. Now she gets another chance to shoot for a medal of her own.

articleTitle: Fahadh Faasil on Don’t Trouble the Trouble: ‘It is a kids’ film for grown-ups’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Fahadh Faasil, who plays the street magician Suri in Don't Trouble the Trouble
description: Fahadh Faasil speaks about the three-step mental process he used for every line of dialogue in Don't Trouble the Trouble, why he insisted on sync-sound discipline on a Telugu set and why writers matter more than actors.
body_raw: Fahadh Faasil thought in Malayalam, converted the thought to English, and then performed the line in Telugu. He did this for every single dialogue across 79 real locations in Hyderabad over a year and a half of production. He refused to use prompting on set, insisted on dubbing his own lines and brought the sync-sound discipline of Malayalam cinema to a Telugu production that was not built for it. The result is Dont Trouble the Trouble, his first Telugu film as a solo lead. In an interview with SCREEN, Fahadh shared the challenges he faced while shooting for Dont Trouble the Trouble. Having performed exclusively in Malayalam throughout his career, Dont Trouble the Trouble required him to carry an entire film in Telugu as the solo lead. The biggest challenge was thinking in Telugu. I think in Malayalam. Then convert to English. Then perform in Telugu. This is all not very smooth. So primarily the challenge was to start thinking in the language. Discovering words. Discovering the language itself. I was very particular that I wanted to dub, I wanted to do the lines myself. Back home we do sync sound. So we have to learn our lines. I made sure we function that way here also. There was no prompting on sets. We shot in Telugu, Fahadh Faasil said. Malayalam cinema operates almost exclusively on sync sound, where dialogue is recorded live on set, requiring complete silence from the crew. Telugu cinema traditionally dubs dialogue in post-production, which allows for more noise on set during shooting. Hence, Fahadh brought his Malayalam discipline to a Telugu set. While we didnt do sync sound specifically, I made sure we brought something of that sort here. The only thing I told them is I function with a small group. Lets try and do that, he said. Recalling his first impression of Dont Trouble the Troubles script, Fahad said, Honestly, I felt like I was hearing a story like this in my life for the first time. I have never heard anything like this before. He explained that his Malayalam films tend to operate in a very different register. My movies back home are very subtle. The drama is less. So I wanted to try out something in another space. And this just fell in place. There are so many talented actors here and they came to me. I didnt want to lose that opportunity. Fahadh Faasil was careful to clarify that Dont Trouble the Troubles appeal goes beyond its fantasy elements. The film is all about love. The film is all about concern. The film is all about care. Magic or being invisible, these are all elements. But the film is much deeper and more rooted than all these, he said. When asked to define the genre, he introduced a term he said he had coined himself A kids film for grown-ups. It brings out the kid in the adult. What Telugu cinema taught him Fahadh Faasil pointed to Telugu cinemas approach to taking films to a wider audience. I think Telugu cinema takes a lot of effort. At least in the last five, six years, it made great efforts to take the film outside the country to various other countries. It has to do with planning. It has nothing to do with the creative scope or the quality of your film or the stars. It just needs proper planning. Also Read How Fahadh Faasil delivered an acting masterclass across three distinct characters in 2019 He said he hopes to apply the same distribution thinking to his Malayalam productions. Hopefully, I will explore that for my Malayalam films also, the actor-producer said. Fahadh Faasil said he did not face any difficulty shooting in crowded real locations across Hyderabad, including areas like Secunderabad and near the Industrial Exhibition grounds, because he has never worked any other way. I am trained to performing in real locations. Back home, there are no studios or anything. So we shoot in real locations. I always prefer shooting in real locations. Pushpa is the first film that I have shot in a controlled environment. So thats one more thing Telugu cinema has taught me to do, he said. Writer or director? When asked about the ongoing conversation around Malayalam cinema giving more credit to its writers than other industries, Fahadh Faasil replied, I believe writers are perhaps more important than the actor. And I have functioned like that in my films. I rely on my director and writer a lot. Describing his working dynamic, he said, I hold my right hand to the director and my left hand to the writer. I go in tandem with them. For Dont Trouble the Trouble, writer-director Shashank Yeleti and co-writer Hamza Ali filled both roles. For me, it was like doing a film back home. It was with my family and friends. I was as comfortable as that, Fahadh said. On working across industries Throughout Fahadh Fassils career, he has been navigating between Malayalam, Tamil and Telugu cinema, and he thinks each collaboration is a discovery. When I worked with Kamal Hasaan, it was a discovery itself. The way he processes, the way he performs, the way he deals with his actors. There is so much to learn from any talent that you collaborate with. Everyone has their own technique. Its like cooking. You may not cook the way she cooks, but your food will taste good. Every artiste will have a technique. Its very interesting to watch it closely and discover it. On his character Suri In Dont Trouble the Trouble, Fahadh Faasil plays Suri, a street magician and con artist living in Hyderabad whose life changes when he encounters a young girl named Divya, played by Ssara Palekar. He said what attracted him to the character was the moral journey. The character has a very interesting journey from grey to white. That journey is very interesting. In that journey, you see the magic, the fantasy, the love, everything, he said. Also Read Fahadh Faasil mediocre in Patriot? Even Mammootty, Mohanlal couldnt save it On his production track record As a producer under his Fahadh Faasil and Friends banner, he has backed several of Malayalam cinemas biggest recent hits, including Bethlehem Kudumba Unit, Premalu and Aavesham. Asked whether he anticipated the scale of their success, he was candid. I knew Bethlehem Kudumba Unit would be a hit. But not this big. I didnt think Aavesham would be this big. I do not have a type while selecting a script. The only thing I can judge is whether people like it or not. The rest of it is bonus, he said. The actor-producer added, I wont start a film without a beginning, midpoint and end. These three aspects need to be in place for me to start shooting. Once you have that structuring, then you play around. Fahadh Fassil then offered an analogy that captures his entire philosophy of filmmaking. Making a film is just like playing a cricket match. You dont know if you are going to win or lose. The idea is to have fun. On his career journey Fahadh Faasil, who debuted in 2002 with the Malayalam film Kaiyethum Doorath, also reflected on the path that brought him here. His first film flopped, and he left India for America, where he had a philosphy scholarship. I did my engineering here. I was about to leave to America to pursue philosphy. I had a scholarship. I went there. The pain of losing kept bothering me. Maybe at that point I thought I was going to be in America for the rest of my life, he said. Fahad did not return for six years. In that time, he discovered world cinema, read widely and met people who changed his perspective. Those six years triggered the want to come back and do one film and maybe go back. One film became 66 films, he said. Fahadh Faasil confirmed he has signed one more Telugu film with Arka Media Works which will be his next project, starting next year. Dont Trouble the Trouble is produced by Shobu Yarlagadda, Prasad Devineni and SS Karthikeya under Arka Media Works and Showing Business, with music by Kaala Bhairava, cinematography by Brad Francis and editing by Praveen Anthony. It releases on October 2 in Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam.

articleTitle: For new energy, remove old bottlenecks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: For new energy, remove old bottlenecks
description: Renewables, especially solar and wind power, have transformed the country's energy basket, but their variability places new demands on transmission planning and storage
body_raw: With more than 300 GW of installed capacity, India ranks third globally in renewable-energy RE deployment. But this impressive growth has not always translated into green energy being available when demand is highest, particularly during the evening peak. As this newspaper reported on July 31, transmission constraints and the need to maintain grid security forced operators to curtail a significant amount of solar power-generated electricity during April to June. The Centres Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme tries to address this constraint by strengthening systems in states to evacuate up to 135 GW of renewable energy. The project will also add 50 GWh of battery energy storage. Renewables, especially solar and wind power, have transformed the countrys energy basket, but their variability places new demands on transmission planning and storage. The new scheme is expected to address intermittency during peak hours and meet demand when the Sun is not shining. The emphasis on intra-state networks is particularly significant. Renewable projects are often concentrated in specific regions while demand is spread across cities, industries and rural areas within states. Strengthening the networks last leg is crucial to ensuring that green power actually reaches consumers. The scheme has earmarked Rs 1,36,378 crore for transmission infrastructure. Its implementation will require learning from past experiences, which suggest that challenges are not restricted to drawing investment. A report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Energy tabled in Parliament in December last year, for instance, pointed out that issues related to right-of-way compensation - payment to landowners when high-voltage power transmission lines pass near their property - land acquisition and delays in environmental clearances are major hurdles in laying transmission lines. The other major challenge will be to ensure that the 50 GWh storage component becomes a functioning part of the grid rather than a procurement target. Battery projects need viable business models and incentives - especially because the sector relies on overseas suppliers for critical raw materials - recycling arrangements and clear rules on who can use and pay for storage. The Centre and states will have to work together on planning and implementation. Renewable resources, transmission corridors and electricity demand do not follow administrative boundaries, and - as the parliamentary committee pointed out - fragmented decision-making often delays projects. Going forward, the government needs to give serious thought to the panels proposal for a portal that brings all approving authorities together for real-time monitoring and faster decision-making. The new corridor could be the backbone of the next phase of Indias green energy transition. It will do well to overcome the bottlenecks of the past.

articleTitle: Plunged 14,000 feet in 2 minutes: Debris from missing jet found off US coast
articleFeaturedImageAlt: BERMUDA plane missing, boston plane crash
description: In a statement, the Coast Guard revealed the nationalities of those on board and said four Canadians and two Bermudian nationals were aboard, and their next of kin were notified.
body_raw: Crews searching for a Boston-bound medical transport plane that went missing over the Atlantic after leaving Bermuda with six people onboard have found a debris field off the coast of Nantucket, Massachusetts, the US Coast Guard said on Sunday. According to the Federal Aviation Administration FAA, the Coast Guard was notified about the plane around 2 am local time on Saturday that the Gulfstream G100 jet, tail number CGRJP, had lost contact with air traffic controllers, reports stated. Gulfstream jet lost contact after leaving Bermuda The plane was being used as an air ambulance and had two passengers and four crew members on board when it left for an overnight flight to Massachusetts. I am aware of reports of a Canadian-registered air ambulance aircraft that went missing while travelling from Bermuda to Boston. Four Canadians are among the six people on board. My thoughts are with everyone on board, as well as their families, loved ones and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time. We are closely monitoring the situation and are working with the relevant authorities as search and rescue efforts continue. I want to thank all first responders involved for their ongoing efforts. - Steven MacKinnon stevenmackinnon October 3, 2026 Four Canadians, two Bermudians were on board In a statement, the Coast Guard revealed the nationalities of those on board and said four Canadians and two Bermudians were aboard, and their next of kin were notified as the search continued. Following the discovery of a debris field that belongs to the missing plane, the armed forces added that the search operation for the six people aboard along the coast of Nantucket continues. Coast Guard search crews located a debris field that has been confirmed to be associated with the missing aircraft. Crews are continuing to search for the six people who were aboard the aircraft, and the Coast Guard cutter William Sparling will continue search efforts throughout the night, the US Coast Guard added. Pilot reported electrical issues before plane vanished Audio from the air traffic control suggests that the medical transport jet may have been coming in blind when a storm hit the area shortly before it vanished. The air traffic control audio, posted by LiveATC.net, stated that the pilot had reported electrical issues and declared an emergency. A controller can be heard asking the pilot, Roger, you said youre coming in blind. Is that what you said? AP reported. Plane plunged 14,000 feet in two minutes Data from the flight-tracking site FlightRadar24 revealed that the Gulfstream G100 jet nosedived from an altitude of around 24,000 feet to around 10,000 feet in about two minutes. Bermuda Premier David Burt, in a statement, said, We are praying that all six people will be found safe. Canada, Transport Minister, Steven MacKinnon, in a post on X said, My thoughts are with everyone on board, as well as their families, loved ones and colleagues during this incredibly difficult time. MacKinnon further wrote, We are closely monitoring the situation, and are working with the relevant authorities as search and rescue efforts continue. I want to thank all first responders involved for their ongoing efforts.

articleTitle: Supreme Court seeks Election Commission response to plea against chief Gyanesh Kumar after Express investigation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court Gyanesh Kumar
description: The petitioner has urged the court to declare SIR, and all actions, decisions, directions, and measures taken under it, invalid from the very beginning and without legal authority.
body_raw: Supreme Court Hears Plea on CEC Gyanesh Kumar Highlights The Supreme Court on Monday issued notice on petitions questioning the functioning of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, calling for an SIT probe against him and seeking to declare the nationwide SIR of electoral rolls illegal. A bench headed by CJI Surya Kant and also comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana heard the matter today. The petitions were filed days after The Indian Express reported that ECs Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders concerning the SIR of electoral rolls. The two commissioners said some of the decisions were issued without their knowledge or recommendation. The two ECs separately wrote to the countrys top bureaucrat, Cabinet Secretary T V Somanathan, flagging concerns over the integrity of voter software. The ECI said the letters sent by Sandhu and Joshi to the Cabinet Secretary concerned an officer on deputation and were not related to policy or IT division matters. Arguments before Court Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate Vikas Singh argued that amendments made to the law governing the Election Commission in 2023 had significantly enlarged the powers and protections available to the Chief Election Commissioner. Singh particularly referred to Section 16, a new provision introduced in the 2023 Act that grants protection from civil and criminal proceedings for acts done in the discharge of official duties. Singh argued that the new immunity provision was not present in the earlier law and said that it made the Election Commission even more powerful than any other constitutional functionary in the country. He sought interim measures, including the immediate suspension of CEC Gyanesh Kumar or, alternatively, divesting him of the authority to act as CEC. Let us first have an authenticated information, the CJI said. Justice Bagchi questioned whether the court could, without hearing the respondents, assume that all the decisions in question had been taken unilaterally. Can we ex-parte come to a decision that all the decisions were unilateral?, Justice Bagchi asked. The court thus issued notice to the Election Commission, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the other two Election Commissioners. Pleas before court One of the petitions by Patna resident Rakesh Kumar Singh referred to the alleged differences between CEC Kumar and Sandhu and Joshi and the objections raised by them. Article 3241 of the Constitution does not vest the superintendence, direction and control of elections in an individual Chief Election Commissioner. It vests those powers in a Commission, said the plea. The petitioner urged the court to declare SIR, and all actions, decisions, directions, and measures taken under it, invalid from the very beginning and without legal authority. The petitioner argued that the SIR was undertaken without the necessary statutory or constitutional authority and without following the procedure required by law. The other petition by Delhi-based lawyer Shailendra Mani Tripathi has sought a probe by an independent, high-powered judicial inquiry commission or an SIT headed by a retired judge of the top court. The petition refers to unprecedented constitutional fractures and illegalities committed within the ECI under the CEC as exposed by documentary records published on September 23, 2026. The plea said the alleged act of. CEC Kumar. falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability. The petition seeks directions to declare all decisions, guidelines, directives, and software modifications initiated, approved, or implemented under Gyanesh Kumar without full Commission concurrence or contrary to the majority opinion of the Election Commissioners under Section 18 of the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023 as unconstitutional. It further seeks quashing of the unauthorised modifications made to Form 6 on the ECINetERONet portal requiring ancestrylast-SIR declarations, and directing the immediate restoration of statutory Form 6 as prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960 and permit all eligible adults to register as voters on the basis of original statutory requirements.

articleTitle: Rewilding great Indian bustards: The project and the challenges ahead
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Two male great Indian bustards (GIB) are released in Rajasthan’s Desert National Park on Sunday. (X: Bhupender Yadav)
description: For the first time, two captive-bred great Indian bustards have been released into the wild. While this experiment is indeed important, the recovery of their population still remains a long-term challenge.
body_raw: October 4 marked a significant milestone in the efforts to conserve the critically endangered great Indian bustard GIB. Two captive-bred male GIBs were released into the wild for the first time in Rajasthans Desert National Park near Jaisalmer town. The pilot release marks the first step in rewilding bustards that have been bred and raised in captivity. This is part of Project GIB which the Centre is running along with the Wildlife Institute of India and the governments of Rajasthan and Gujarat. What is the great Indian bustard and why is its population being revived? The great Indian bustard is a large, ground-dwelling bird found in savannahs, grasslands and deserts in India. Till the late 19th and early 20th century, it was spread across 11 states - from Haryana in the north to Tamil Nadu in the south, and from Rajasthan in the west to Odisha in the east. But a range of issues resulted in its decline - hunting, poaching of eggs, gradual conversion of open habitats into croplands and mining areas and, more recently, deaths due to collisions with renewable energy power lines. GIBs poor frontal vision, combined with their heavy body, makes it difficult for them to detect or avoid such infrastructure. From an estimated 1,260-1,400 in the early 1970s, the wild GIB population has now plummeted to only around 150, of which around 130 -20 are in Rajasthan. The rest are in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh - facing the risk of local extinction. To counter their decline, the Centre and the Rajasthan government launched a long-term bustard and lesser florican project in 2012-13. This project was expanded from 2014 with funding support to start a conservation breeding program. Beginning 2019, wild GIB eggs were collected from Desert National Park and surrounding areas, incubated artificially at two centres in Rajasthans Sam and Ramdevra and hand-reared. These hand-reared birds mated at these centres, giving birth to 98 birds as of now. Of these, two were released Sunday and 11 more have been earmarked for wild release. The others remain at the centres for captive reproduction. What does rewilding entail? Before initiating the rewilding process, a rewilding aviary was set up at the Ramdevra Center while a soft release facility was developed by the Wildlife Institute of India inside Desert National Park. Unlike the hand-reared birds that were used to humans, chicks aged between three and four months were released in these facilities so that they could move freely and adapt to the natural environment without human imprinting. Scientists associated with the project said the birds have been fitted with transmitters. These devices will send alerts thrice a day on their coordinates and movement pattern. Teams will also monitor them from afar. Challenges in long-term recovery The beginning of the rewilding phase, while crucial, is a challenging experiment. The released birds will face a challenge to their survival. Enclosures within Desert National Park were picked because they comprised grasslands as well as stretches free of either human or technological interruptions. While this is an experiment in Rajasthan, similar experiments would have to be carried out in range states such as Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, albeit only after habitat improvements. We can learn from the Rajasthan experience, and if this is successful, then Gujarat may do a similar pilot. However, restoration and protection of grasslands is crucial for the revival of bustards outside Rajasthan, said Gobind Sagar Bhardwaj, Director, Wildlife Institute of India. Unlike forested areas across Indias states, grassland protection has always been challenging as they are not traditionally considered protected areas in public perception. Bharadwaj said this makes them vulnerable to land-use conversion and degradation, which consequently affects the livelihoods of pastoralists and those who rear livestock. The afforestation of grasslands was red-flagged by Asad Rahmani, one of Indias foremost bustard experts and former director of Bombay Natural History Society, in the NGOs famous Hornbill magazine back in 2008. Rahmani wrote Ironically, one of the biggest threats to grasslands is not from the graziers, but from the forest department. To live up to their name, officials of the forest department consider their solemn duty to convert every grassland and even wetlands into a forest. He noted that from Gujarat to Andhra Pradesh, it was seen that forest officers decided to improve habitats by planting trees or creating waterholes in bustard habitats. Threats to GIB revival At the conclusion of a landmark case seeking protection of GIBs, the Supreme Court had, accepting the recommendations of an expert panel, ordered some broad protection measures for GIBs and their habitats in Rajasthan and Gujarat. It demarcated priority areas for the bird 14,013 sq km in Rajasthan and 740 sq km in Gujarat and ordered that 80 km of power lines in Rajasthan should be buried underground. This has to be completed between 2027 and 2028. It also ordered the creation of powerline corridors that will accommodate re-routed overhead lines. Experts have warned that rewilding will not be sustainable if these power lines cannot be buried underground soon. Limestone mining is yet another issue that threatens to affect the open and flat areas that Bustards need. The Supreme Court did not order specific measures against mining, and mine operations are proposed in the northern side of DNP, where the birds were released.

articleTitle: Pneumonic plague in Russia? What we know about Siberian lab tech’s death
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sterile laboratory bench showing biohazard containment protocols (AI generated image). Russian health authority Rospotrebnadzor initiated plague quarantine procedures in Shelekhov near Irkutsk following the fatal laboratory-acquired infection of technician Daria Shipilova.
description: Plague outbreak in Russia: A lab technician at an Irkutsk anti-plague institute in Siberia died, and 197 contacts have been isolated amid reports of a pneumonic plague exposure but Rospotrebnadzor has not confirmed either a plague or a laboratory accident.
body_raw: It always begins with a broken test tube and a pathogen released, in every good or bad movie about plagues and epidemics. And one version of recent events in Russia sounds uncomfortably familiar. At least 197 people who may have had contact with a lab technician in Russias Irkutsk region have been placed under medical isolation. This was after reports the technician - Daria Shipilova - broke a test tube containing pneumonic plague bacteria while working at the anti-plague institute in Shelekhov, a small town roughly 20km from Irkutsk city. Shipilova was admitted to hospital with severe pneumonia on September 29. She died on October 2. Rospotrebnadzor, Russias federal public health body, diagnosed a pneumonia of unknown etiology but said it found no microorganisms associated with her work. It also said the sanitary and epidemiological situation in the region remains stable. But Alexei Tsydenov - the leader of Buryatia, a neighbouring republic Shipilova reportedly visited on work - first said she died of the plague. Hethen altered his post to add possibly. So is there really a plague in Russia? Not confirmed. Rospotrebnadzor has not confirmed a plague or that a laboratory accident occurred. Russian media has said 197 contacts have been identified and 189 are under observation. On October 2 Irkutsk Governor Igor Kobzev said none of them are showing symptoms and their laboratory tests are negative. However, since then two have tested positive for COVID-19 and two others for rhinovirus, a viral infection behind the common cold. Gennady Onishchenko, a former head of Rospotrebnadzor, told state news agency TASS the onset of cold weather would likely prevent transmission. But that is one officials view and not a guarantee. How did Daria Shipilova fall ill? That is unclear, and there are two competing accounts. The first is the broken test tube. According to The New York Post, after that incident she was at places on Russias eastern border - near Mongolia - and fell ill on September 25. But Rospotrebnadzor contradicts this story. Its biosafety commission found no emergency involving pathogenic microorganisms at the institute. The second is that she fell ill after the work trip to Buryatia. But Tsydenov says she never visited the republic and that there is no outbreak there. What is pneumonic plague? It is a disease caused by the Yersinia pestis bacterium, the same one behind bubonic plague that ravaged Europe from 1346 to 1353 and was one of the most fatal pandemics in human history as much as 60 per cent of the European population of the time were killed. According to the US Centers for Disease Control, the pneumonic form spreads through infectious droplets when an infected person or animal coughs or sneezes. It can also develop when bubonic or septicaemic plague spreads to the lungs. Health officials consider it the most serious form. Symptoms usually appear between one and four days after exposure and can include fever, headache, weakness and a bloody or watery cough. The pneumonia rapidly worsens without treatment and can be fatal. But common antibiotics work, and recovery rates are high when treatment starts within 24 hours of the first symptoms. That is why close contacts are monitored. So what now? Three things to watch a laboratory report confirming the cause of Shipilovas death, a clearer account of how she was exposed, and the health of those under observation.

articleTitle: The Paradise box office: Nani’s biggest opener can’t surpass Prabhas’ Raja Saab, earns Rs 77 cr
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Paradise box office collection day 1
description: The Paradise box office collection Day 1: For Nani, this is the biggest opener of his career, but it isn't as impressive when compared to other Telugu stars' records.
body_raw: The Paradise Box Office collection Day 1 Nani-starrer The Paradise has become the biggest opener of the stars career as the film has earned Rs 76.90 crore worldwide, as per trade tracker Sacnilk. The Srikanth Odela-directed action drama collected Rs 34.65 crore net in India on Day 1 across 9,732 shows, with total India gross collections reaching Rs 54.90 crore, which includes preview shows. The overseas market added Rs 22 crore in gross collections, pushing the worldwide gross collection to Rs 76.90 crore on its opening day. The Paradise is nearly 2x of Nanis previous biggest opener HIT The Third Case 2025 was Nanis previous biggest opener, collecting Rs 21 crore net across 4,171 shows with a worldwide gross of Rs 37.81 crore on Day 1. Saripodhaa Sanivaaram 2024, which went on to collect Rs 98 crore worldwide, had a comparatively modest opening of Rs 9 crore net across 3,365 shows with a worldwide gross of Rs 19.34 crore. Dasara 2023, Nanis previous collaboration with Srikanth Odela opened to Rs 23.20 crore net across 5,705 shows, with a worldwide gross of Rs 36.28 crore on Day 1. The Paradise has nearly doubled that figure in India and more than doubled it worldwide. However, outside of Nanis filmography, the Telugu box office space paints a different picture.Prabhas The Raja Saab opened to Rs 53.75 crore net across 16,470 shows, with a worldwide gross of Rs 100.20 crore on Day 1. However, Prabhas had nearly 7,000 more shows, as compared to The Paradise. Ram Charans Peddi opened to Rs 51 crore net across 12,412 shows, with a worldwide gross of Rs 110.49 crore. On the other hand, Chiranjeevis Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu opened to approximately Rs 28.5 crore in India with a worldwide Day 1 of Rs 37.1 crore. The Paradise has outperformed Chiranjeevis opening both domestically and worldwide, collecting Rs 6.15 crore more in India net and nearly double the worldwide gross. Set in 1980s Secunderabad, the film follows a marginalised communitys fight for recognition against feudal oppression. articleTitle: Multiple groups, moving crowds: Why CEC protest became a challenge for Delhi Police
articleFeaturedImageAlt: delhi cec protest
description: The agitation has seen student activists, politicians and civil society members making repeated attempts to march towards ‘restricted areas’ in Central Delhi over the past four days.
body_raw: What began as a protest planned at Delhis Jantar Mantar on October 2 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has, over the past four days, spread across central Delhi, with multiple groups attempting to march amid prohibitory orders and the Delhi Police registering more than nine FIRs. The police response has included denying permission for the march and deploying paramilitary personnel, local police from eight police stations in the New Delhi district and personnel from the Delhi Police Reserve Battalion. All roads leading to Jantar Mantar in the New Delhi district were also fortified with barricades and police personnel. According to a police officer, the agitation has not been confined to a single conventional demonstration but has involved political parties, student organisations, activists, lawyers and other groups attempting to march towards restricted areas in central Delhi. The challenge is not merely about preventing a crowd from entering Jantar Mantar, which is already heavily fortified. It is about controlling multiple moving groups, preventing attempts to breach barricades, managing detentions and, simultaneously, dealing with a large number of people recording events on mobile phones and cameras, the officer said. httpswww.youtube.comwatch?v-Hjn02Ty0kfeatureyoutu.be Advisory for media persons The protests have also brought journalists into closer contact with police operations, prompting the police to issue an advisory on Monday. This came after three women journalists alleged that they were harassed by police personnel while covering the protests. Their complaints have been transferred to the Crime Branch for investigation. The police advisory asked journalists to carry either an identity card issued by their organisation or valid PIBDIP accreditation and, importantly, to keep it visibly displayed. Journalists were to ensure that their presence does not obstruct police operations or the movement of law-enforcement personnel. They were also asked to maintain a reasonable and safe distance during tense situations and to position themselves so that they are clearly distinguishable from protesters. Another police officer said the advisory was an attempt to create a clearer operational distinction between those covering the protest and those participating in it. Because many of those protesting also sometimes start making videos, with a mic and mobile phone camera, it becomes extremely difficult for us to distinguish between an actual journalist and activists, the officer said. Lessons from CJPs July protest The Cockroach Janta Party CJP, which staged a massive protest in July demanding the resignation of then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak, was given permission to hold a one-day protest at Jantar Mantar. A Delhi Police officer of DCP rank handed over the permission letter to CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke at the Delhi Airport. The protesters, however, did not leave Jantar Mantar after the first day and returned for a second round of demonstrations. Delhi Police officers have acknowledged that they had underestimated the number of people who might turn up in support of the CJP. This time, the police have taken measures to prevent protesters from reaching Jantar Mantar. After the July protest ended following the resignation of Pradhan, Delhi Police officials underwent anti-protest counselling and were advised to remain calm, composed and patient while dealing with protesters and crowds. During the current protests, very few Delhi Police personnel have been seen carrying batons. Paramilitary personnel have mostly been seen carrying tear-gas shells. Many Delhi Police personnel have also been seen without name-plate badges while dealing with protesters. Sources claimed some personnel avoid wearing them because they do not want to be identified and subsequently trolled on social media.

articleTitle: Domestic capacity, reforms key amid global uncertainty: Shaktikanta Das
articleFeaturedImageAlt: On the external front, Das said India's financial sector and prudent management had also emerged as strong pillars of economic growth. (Image: Ministry of Finance)
description: India is within striking distance of 8% growth, said Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister at the Kautilya Economic Conclave
body_raw: Amid sustained shocks and global uncertainties, India seeks to emphasise on sustained structural reforms, building domestic capacity and competence in areas where there is large import dependence, and continuously focusing on fiscal, monetary, macroeconomic and macrofinancial stability, Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, said on Sunday. Das further said that the country stands at a pivotal moment in its development journey and a leap to Viksit Bharat 2047 is in the realm of realisation, adding that India is within a striking distance of 8 growth. There can never be a moment where you can say that, whatever I have done is sufficient. There is always something more to do but in the current context. The emphasis has been to build our domestic capacity, competence in areas where we are largely import dependent. So, whether it is energy or fertiliser and so many other areas, the government is now focusing on such areas. the focus of the government is also to take measures and to develop long-term capacity in areas where again we are dependent on imports, Das said while answering a question on day two of the three-day Kautilya Economic Conclave organised by the Ministry of Finance and the Institute of Economic Growth. Calling for strategic self-reliance, Das said self-reliance or Atmanirbharta should not mean isolation. Rather, it stands for building stronger domestic capabilities while remaining integrated with global markets and concluding more free trade agreements, he said. Das underlined that Indias real GDP grew by an impressive 7.8 in Q1 of 2026-27, adding that if the period from July-September 2025-26 to April-June 2026-27 is taken into account, real GDP growth in India just exceeds 8. This resonates with my statement to Financial Times London a few months ago that India is within a striking distance of 8 growth, he said. Reforms undertaken over the past decade were not one-off measures but were designed to build buffers that would help the economy absorb disruptions and recover rapidly, he said. Indias resilience is not accidental. It is the outcome of broad and mutually reinforcing reforms, he said. The former Reserve Bank of India governor cited flexible inflation targeting, the introduction of the goods and services tax, fiscal prudence, the push for digital payments and banking sector reforms among such measures. On the external front, Das said Indias financial sector and prudent management had also emerged as strong pillars of economic growth. External sector indicators have remained broadly resilient, supported by export diversification, free trade agreements, a sustained surplus in services trade and steady inward remittances, he said. Going ahead, Das said India must harness the artificial intelligence AI revolution to sustain high growth. Indias AI strategy rests on two complementary pillars. First, sovereign AI capability through investments in indigenous foundation models, high-performance computing infrastructure, semiconductor developments and robust innovation ecosystem, he said. He also called for deepening the financial sector to support Indias expanding economic weight. While Indias financial sector has evolved significantly, the next phase of growth will require strengthening of long-term finance and patient capital, Das said. This would require further deepening of the corporate bond market, pension and insurance funds, municipal finance and innovative infrastructure financing, he added.

articleTitle: JSA, working group seek cap on hospital charges, medicine margins
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Jan Swasthya Abhiyan and health rights groups urge government intervention to regulate private hospital rates amid soaring treatment and medicine costs
description: While the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 (CEA) provides a legal framework for regulating clinical establishments and envisages government-determined ranges of charges, it has not been implemented, they said.
body_raw: The Jan Swasthya Abhiyan JSA and the Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatment Working Group have called for urgent government intervention to regulate healthcare by private hospitals, warning that patients continue to face excessive and arbitrary charges for treatment, medicines and medical consumables with little effective protection or recourse. The demand comes amid renewed scrutiny of private hospital pricing. The Supreme Court recently questioned steep mark-ups on medicines sold through hospital pharmacies, including a case in which a cancer medicine supplied at around Rs 2,700 carried an MRP of around Rs 27,000. The SC also questioned practices that require patients to purchase medicines from hospital-linked pharmacies and has asked the government to examine regulation of trade margins. At a virtual media conference, Dr Abhay Shukla, co-convener, JSA, said private healthcare has expanded enormously in India, but regulation has simply not kept pace, adding there is no regulation of rates and the patient has virtually no bargaining power over what they are charged. Leading corporate hospital chains have been earning huge surpluses estimated in the range of Rs 22 lakh to Rs 55 lakh per year from each bed in the last few years, Dr Shukla observed. Experts said there is a need for an effective nationwide system to regulate what private hospitals can charge patients for procedures, services, medicines and consumables. Leading corporate hospital chains charge on average Rs 60,000 to Rs 78,000 per day of treatment. This is an unacceptably high level of profiteering that is paid for by ordinary patients through exorbitant hospital bills, Dr Shukla said. While the Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 CEA provides a legal framework for regulating clinical establishments and envisages government-determined ranges of charges, it has not been implemented, they said. Regarding fixing margins on medicines and medical consumables, concerns have also been raised with Maharashtra FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe. Dr Shukla said at the state level, the FDA Commissioners office can issue orders requiring hospitals that supply medical consumables above a specified unit price to disclose their procurement price alongside the selling price. This will lead to a huge amount of transparency, so that patients are aware of the actual cost of what they are buying and the cost incurred by the hospital, Dr Shukla said. Maharashtra is in the process of drafting a Clinical Establishments Act CEA. Since pricing is a subject in the Concurrent List, there is a possibility that the state could introduce a provision in the CEA requiring hospitals to limit the markup on medicines and consumables they supply to no more than 30 per cent over the procurement price. Such a provision could potentially be introduced and implemented at the state level itself, the experts said. The CEA was passed more than a decade ago, but its non-implementation has produced zero results on the ground. It is high time the government starts to regulate the procedures in private hospitals. A patient should know how much they will they be charged before agreeing to a treatment, according to K M Gopakumar, co-convener, Working Group. The MRP cannot become a licence to charge patients many times the procurement price. The government must urgently fix the trade margins on all medical products and ensure that patients are free to purchase medicines and consumables from outside wherever clinically possible, said Jyotsna Singh, Co-Convenor, Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatments.

articleTitle: ‘Am I dead?: Ambika breaks down over sister Radha’s Rs 46 cr cheque fraud allegations
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ambika broke down after dismissing Radha's cheque-fraud allegations against her as fake, revealing ongoing disputes over gold and ARS Garden.
description: Veteran actor Ambika broke down after dismissing her sister Radha's cheque-fraud allegations against her as fake, revealing ongoing disputes over gold and ARS Garden Studio.
body_raw: Days after veteran actor Radha levelled cheque fraud allegations against her sister, actor Ambika, and their brother, Mallikarjuna Kunjan Nair, Ambika has stepped forward to explain her side. Rubbishing Radhas claims as fake and fabricated, Ambika broke down in tears before the media, expressing disbelief that her dear sister portrayed her as a thief in front of the world. For those unfamiliar, Radha had recently filed a police complaint against Ambika and Mallikarjuna, alleging that blank cheques belonging to her were taken from her home and misused in an attempt to claim around Rs 46 crore. Must Read Radha accuses sister Ambika of stealing cheques to claim Rs 46 cr, files complaint Ambika refutes cheque fraud allegations While addressing the media, Ambika pointed out that it is hard to believe Radha, who is extremely cautious in all matters, would carelessly leave signed blank cheques at home. Radha is a person who uses a special number lock even for her handbag. Then, when she goes to sleep, she keeps that bag in a cupboard and locks it again. It is unbelievable when such a vigilant person says she left signed cheques elsewhere, she maintained. Ambika further expressed her heartbreak over ARS Garden Studio, which she said they built together, being renamed without informing her. She shared, When I saw the ARS Garden board being removed and another board being put up, I could not bear it. Everyone in Tamil cinema knows what ARS Garden means to me. The A for Ambika in ARS Garden is gone. Why? Am I dead? No, Im alive. Shouldnt I have been told? She doesnt even have that basic courtesy, the veteran actor alleged, tearing up. Ambika further revealed there had been earlier disputes over family property. She stated that a large share of gold ornaments entitled to her are in Radhas possession now. When I ask about the gold I deserve, she doesnt give a proper reply. Radha has a special weakness for gold. Its okay to take ones mothers or sisters gold once in a while. But a large amount of my gold is still with her. If I try to speak directly about it, she wont even pick up the phone, Ambika alleged. Their brother added to her statements, saying, It was decided to divide the properties equally when our mother was alive. Radhas method is to say nothing when spoken to directly and then change her statement later. ICYMI Bigg Boss Malayalam alumna Renu Sudhi in ICU after 5th chemo Cant withstand another round Ambika reportedly noted, When we were struggling, I was the first stepping stone for the family. At one point, we believed that if there was family and a bond, we should do anything for the family. But things are not like that now. Everyone is living separately. I dont know why Radha has filed a complaint against me. Looking at this, I find it strange because I am actually the one who was cheated. I should have been the one to give the complaint. It is okay. Someone may have advised Radha, and that is why she has given the complaint, Ambika added. About Ambika, Radha Ambika and Radha were two of the most celebrated South Indian female actors of the 1980s. Originally from Kerala, they worked in various languages and shared the screen with some of the biggest names in Indian show business. Meanwhile, Radha played notable roles in films such as Alaigal Oivathillai, Ilanjodigal, Pakkathu Veetu Roja, Valibamey Vaa Vaa, Nalla Thambi, Tik Tik Tik, Oru Kaidhiyin Diary, Muthal Mariyathai, Irakal, Revathikkoru Pavakkutty, and Kadhal Parisu.
