description: At a time when CEC Gyanesh Kumar is under fire over the SIR process, the Keralam government has reopened an earlier graft case that was followed by his resignation as PWD Secretary.
body_raw: Keralams Congress-led government on Sunday October 4 directed the states Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to re-open a 2006 probe into an alleged claim of bribery against Chief Election Commissioner of India Gyanesh Kumar. It comes as Congress leaders, including Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, have demanded the CECs resignation over allegations of irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision SIR process. At the time, Kumar, a 1988-batch IAS officer of the Keralam cadre, served as Secretary of the state Public Works Department PWD. The bribery claim stemmed from the suicide note of a Malaysian engineer, who was part of a World Bank-aided road work project executed by a Malaysian and Indian joint venture called PATI-BEL. What was the project? The Kerala State Transport Project KSTP has been a flagship project of the state PWD. Costing Rs 1,600 crore, it was envisaged to modernise and renovate select major roads of 1,600 km under the PWD with a World Bank loan. Initial discussions were completed during the last lap of the CPIM-led government from 1996 to 2001. P J Joseph, the leader of the breakaway faction Kerala Congress Joseph, was then the PWD minister. Joseph, then part of the Left Democratic Front LDF alliance, is now with the ruling United Democratic Front UDF alliance. What went wrong? KSTP was the first project in the state to be associated with an overseas contractor firm, with the Keralam-based Bhageeratha Engineering and Malaysian firm PATI joining hands for the bidding. The joint venture took up works worth Rs 216 crore, mainly involving the modernisation of the main central road from the state capital of Thiruvananthapuram in the south to Angamaly in Central Keralam. The project would build the states first road designed with novel surfacing techniques. PATI-BEL began their work in December 2002 after entering into a final agreement with the then Congress-led government. IUML leader M K Muneer was the PWD minister. However, the government had handed over the project to the contractor without acquiring the land for road development. The notification for land acquisition was issued only in 2004. In October 2006, the contractor informed the government that they could not complete the work within the original deadline, citing the delay in land acquisition. As construction costs escalated, PATI-BEL demanded a 30 increase in the contract amount. The finance department, led by Thomas Isaac under the CPIM government, refused the demand and sought the World Banks permission to re-tender the work. What was the suicide case? Lee See Been, 54, was the chief project manager of the works executed by PATI-BEL. In 2006, the company submitted bills worth Rs 18 crore for payment. According to Legislative Assembly documents from 2007, PATI-BEL officials visited the ministers several times to seek payment. As the chief project manager, Lee was reportedly under pressure from subcontractors and construction material vendors who sought their dues. As the work got delayed, the Congress-led Opposition also put pressure on the CPIM government. It was the former alliance that had awarded the work to the venture. Assembly documents show Congress had demanded the company be blacklisted, following the CPIM government conceding to PATI-BELs demand for a 30 increase in project cost. It also alleged that the CPIM government had an understanding with PATI-BEL. As pressure mounted from various quarters in Keralam, Lee, who had by then returned to Malaysia, died by suicide on November 11, 2006, in Kuala Lumpur. It was reported that he had left a suicide note addressed to the company director and his wife, alleging that PWD officials had sought bribes for clearing the bills. It was also reported that the suicide note had included the name of then PWD secretary Gyanesh Kumar. The note was never made public. What did the vigilance probe find? The death spotlighted issues including bureaucratic hurdles, corruption and delays in executing public works. A month after Lees death, the CPIM government removed Kumar from his post. The government also ordered a probe by the Vigilance Bureau to examine the allegations. In a related development, the government decided to cancel the contract with PATI-BEL, as the work could not be completed within the deadline. Subsequently, the government re-tendered the work. In March 2010, then Home Minister Kodiyeri Balakrishnan, a CPIM leader, informed the Legislative Assembly that two Vigilance probes concerning the KSTP were ongoing. One was about hiring foreign consultants during 2003-04 when Congress was in power, and another probe was ordered in December 2006 a month after Beens death about lapses in KSTP work. However, the probe did not proceed. According to Congress leader Malayinkeezhu Venugopal, on whose petition Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala ordered reopening the probe last week, the earlier investigation was torpedoed midway. Kumar, who was removed as the PWD secretary in December 2006, was not given any fresh posting in the state. He then went on central deputation to New Delhi, when the Congress-led UPA was in power. CPIM had also supported the UPA-I. What happened to the road work? In early 2007, the CPIM government cancelled the contract with PATI-BEL on the grounds that the delay in completion would invite action from the World Bank, which had funded the KSTP. Despite re-tendering, no entity came forward to bid for it. A year later, the government agreed to renew the contract with PATI-BEL itself. PATI-BEL took over the project again after the government allotted an additional Rs 72 crore apart from the original Rs 216 crore. Congress, then in Opposition, had asked the CPIM government to explain why the work was awarded to PATI-BEL when a probe was ongoing. Opposition leader Oommen Chandy had then demanded Finance Minister Thomas Isaac clarify the circumstances of the renewal, given that Isaac had demanded blacklisting of PATI-BEL when the work was delayed.

articleTitle: Bus rides to breakfast to gold rings: How Vijay weaves a welfare net for daily life
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Vettri Payanam
description: Bus rides to breakfast to gold rings: How Vijay weaves a welfare net for daily life.
body_raw: On Friday morning, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay stepped inside some government buses at Chennais Koyambedu bus terminus, and handed women something that ordinarily costs only a few rupees a ticket. Except these bus tickets required no payment. The launch of Vettri Payanam, an expansion of the states free bus travel programme for women and transgender persons, was the latest in a succession of welfare measures rolled out by the five-month-old Vijay government. Together, they are beginning to reveal the contours of its welfare politics, which retain popular schemes inherited from the previous DMK-led government, enlarge their reach, and place alongside them new benefits drawn from the Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagams TVK election promises. Individually, they are schemes. Taken together, they suggest an attempt to mark the states presence at several points in the life of a household-from birth and school to college, work, marriage and everyday commute. Until now, women travelled free on Ordinary buses in metropolitan and urban areas and on Ghat Ordinary services for journeys up to 40 km. From Friday, this facility has been expanded to Express, Limited Stop Service and Deluxe government buses operating in metropolitan and urban areas, Mofussil Ordinary buses, and Ghat Ordinary services beyond 40 km. According to a governments statement, 12,695 buses belonging to the seven State Transport Corporations have been brought under Vettri Payanam, operating 1,68,500 single trips. The government expects around 84.32 lakh women to benefit every day. The expansion had been announced by Vijay in the state Assembly on August 24 under Rule 110. At the time, as per the governments statement, the CM framed it explicitly as a question of social justice. The governments principle was that women, irrespective of where they lived in Tamil Nadu, should not lose opportunities because of transport costs. The government said the expansion would make public transport more accessible across the state, enabling girl students to travel to colleges farther from home and women and transgender persons to reach workplaces, medical facilities and other essential services without paying bus fares. The scheme will not, for now, be implemented in Chengalpattu and Tiruppur districts because the Model Code of Conduct is in force for the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly bypolls scheduled for October 6. Vijays roadmap The political significance of Vijays welfare push lies partly in what his government has chosen to continue. Ten days before the bus expansion, Vijay sat with schoolchildren in Chennai and ate breakfast as his government extended the free breakfast programme, introduced under the DMK government in 2022, from Classes I-V to Classes VI-VIII in government and government-aided schools. The expansion added around 15 lakh children to that programme, which provides one strand of Vijays approach. The other is the rollout of schemes carrying the imprint of TVKs own campaign. Six days after the breakfast expansion came one of its most striking instances. At Madurais Government Rajaji Hospital on September 28, Vijay launched the Thaimaaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam, under which eligible newborns delivered in the government health facilities will receive a one-gram, 22-carat gold ring. The symbolism is distinctly Tamil. Thaimaaman means maternal uncle, a relationship that carries a ceremonial role in many Tamil families, particularly around childbirth and their other milestones. The scheme converts that familial vocabulary into welfare-at birth, the government assumes the symbolic role of the maternal uncle arriving with a gift of gold. The Vijay governments first Budget in August had already signalled how broad this welfare architecture could become. It allocated Rs 560 crore for the newborn gold-ring programme. Under Annan Seer Thittam, eligible brides are to receive an eight-gram gold coin and a silk saree, backed by an allocation of Rs 812 crore. Another Rs 2,000 crore was allocated for the Vetri Laptop Scheme for college students. The Budget also proposed modernising more than 3,700 government schools, a school sanitation programme, residential schools for disadvantaged students and expanded welfare schemes covering senior citizens, transgender persons and women. Then came another large household intervention. On August 24, Vijay announced Annapoorani Super Six, under which eligible women-headed households would receive three free cooking-gas cylinders a year. The government estimated that about 1.30 crore families would benefit and put the annual cost at about Rs 4,000 crore, with implementation scheduled from Pongal in January 2027. The scope of these programmes inevitably bring Vijays welfare project up against a key question how will Tamil Nadu pay for it? The TVK governments Budget itself acknowledged the difficulty. Tamil Nadus debt burden was approaching Rs 11 lakh crore, even as Finance Minister N Marie Wilson argued that tighter administration, technology-driven governance and improved revenue collection would eventually provide the fiscal space for expanded welfare, education and healthcare expenditure. This tension is evident because the TVK came to power with promises extending considerably beyond what has so far been implemented. Before the election, it was estimated that implementing its larger welfare commitments could push the states annual welfare spending close to Rs 1 lakh crore, compared with roughly Rs 65,000 crore in welfare schemes and subsidies under the previous government in 2025-26. For the Vijay government, therefore, the emerging model is not simply one of replacing the welfare politics that preceded it during the Stalin-led DMK government. In several important areas, it is building on it.

articleTitle: AC short circuit sparks Surat factory fire, firefighters recover diamonds worth lakhs
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Within minutes, the flames intensified and the office was engulfed in dense black smoke, making it difficult to see or move inside the unit. (Express Photo)
description: According to officials of the Surat Municipal Corporation's Fire and Emergency Services Department, the fire broke out after a short circuit in the air conditioner in one of the polishing units of a diamond manufacturing factory.
body_raw: A fire that could have caused a loss running into lakhs was contained in time after Surat firefighters entered a smoke-filled diamond factory in Katargam and recovered diamonds worth more than Rs 50 lakh. The blaze, triggered by a short circuit in an air-conditioner, rapidly filled the unit with thick black smoke, forcing firefighters to enter wearing breathing apparatus to bring the flames under control and locate the valuables. According to officials of the Surat Municipal Corporations Fire and Emergency Services Department, the fire broke out after a short circuit in the air conditioner in one of the polishing units of a diamond manufacturing factory at Gangotri Tower near Kesar Ba Market in the Gotalawadi area of Katargam, one of Surats major diamond hubs. The sudden blaze sent panic through the premises as smoke quickly spread through the office. Within minutes, the flames intensified and the office was engulfed in dense black smoke, making it difficult to see or move inside the unit. Hitesh Thakur, Regional Fire Officer, Surat, told The Indian Express that the fire team reached the building soon after receiving the emergency call around 7.45 am on Monday. Five fire tenders from three fire stations were deployed for the operation. Thakur said that the smoke inside the office was so dense that the fire personnel equipped themselves with breathing apparatus sets before going inside. There had been a short circuit in the air conditioner and almost the entire room was charred. The workers vacated in a timely manner so no casualties occurred. Once the fire had been doused, the owner of the factory and the police accompanied fire personnel in order to recover the diamonds, Thakur said. He added that although an official value of the diamonds had not been calculated, with the help of the owner, the fire officials were able to retrieve gemstones from some of the work stations. The unit has partitions and since this fire was contained in one room, we were able to minimise the damage. There may have been gemstones misplaced while we were dousing the flames with water but we managed to retrieve several pieces from the work tables, Thakur said. The intensive firefighting and rescue operation, Thakur said, lasted around 45 minutes. The Katargam-Gotalawadi belt is densely populated with diamond-cutting, polishing and manufacturing units, making fire safety a recurring concern in the area. For the unit involved in Mondays incident, however, the rapid intervention of fire officials meant some of the assets inside were safely secured.

articleTitle: Knowledge Nugget | How secure are India’s freshwater resources?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Knowledge Nugget | How secure are India’s freshwater resources? (UPSC,UPSC IAS, UPSC CSE 2027)
description: Central Water Commission (CWC)’s latest assessment presents a worrying picture, with live storage in major reservoirs at a 10-year low. How much freshwater resources does India have, and how serious is its water stress? Go beyond the nugget to know key data from the UN’s Water Bankruptcy report.
body_raw: Take a look at the essential events, concepts, terms, quotes, or phenomena every day and brush up your knowledge. Heres your UPSC Current Affairs knowledge nugget for today on Indias freshwater resources. Knowledge Nugget Indias Freshwater Resources Subject Human Geography Why in the news? Even as the southwest monsoon season for this year is set to come to an end on September 30, water storage in 178 reservoirs across the country stands at 70 of the total capacity, according to a live reservoir storage report compiled by the Central Water Commission CWC. Key takeaways 1. This is below the decadal average 10-year average stock during this period every year of 76.62. The 2026 stocks are also below that of 2025 stocks for the same period 79. 2. The findings of the report, dated September 24, coincide with drought declarations in Maharashtra and Karnataka. 3. The CWC report has particularly painted a grim picture of water storage in 92 reservoirs located in the south, east and northern India regions. South India Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu has the lowest water reserves this year. 4. Except for Odisha and some parts of West Bengal, east and northeast regions have seen a seasonal deficit of 25 in water reserves. 5. In northern India, water reserves in 11 dams spanning Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Rajasthan have plummeted from 92.3 last year to 62 12.431 BCM of the total storage capacity this year. Why are Indias reservoirs at a low capacity? 6. One of the factors shrouding the monsoon season is the El Nino-a naturally occurring global ocean-atmospheric phenomenon in the Pacific Ocean which results in erratic rainfall and above normal temperatures. 7. Since late August, rainfall deficit and prolonged dry spells have been linked to the strengthening of the El Nino. As of September 28, India received rainfall 12 short of the normal. 8. Deficit in rainfall was recorded during June -35.4 and August -16.3 with July recording just about 1 above normal and September 01-28 -5. 9. With the monsoon about to exit, there is little to no hope for any significant improvement in the reservoir stocks this season. For your information Water security is an important theme for the UPSC CSE exam. In this article we will look at important freshwater sources for India and the world. We will also understand if India is water secure, water stressed or water scarce. You are encouraged to ponder upon initiatives and measures taken by the government to ensure water security in India. Where does Indias freshwater come from? 1. India, home to 18 per cent of the worlds population and 15 per cent of its livestock, depends on just 4 per cent of global freshwater resources. 2. Southwest monsoon brings over 70 per cent of Indias annual rainfall. Lasting from June through September, this helps replenish the water reservoirs and other surface water bodies that make the primary sources of drinking water, for hydel power generation, irrigation, and other purposes. 3. The Indian Himalayan Region IHR known as Water Tower of Asia stretching approximately 2,500 km is the source of major river systems, including the Indus, Ganges, and Brahmaputra, fed by glaciers and numerous springs. 4. The Godavari, Krishna, Mahanadi, Narmada, Tapi, Cauvery and Pennar are major peninsular river systems. Unlike Himalayan rivers, they are predominantly rain-fed, with much greater dependence on the monsoon. 5. Other sources are lakes, ponds, tanks and reservoirs which also largely depend on rainwater. Moreover, India heavily relies on freshwater stored in ground for irrigation, domestic supply and industrial use. 6. The Central Ground Water Board CGWBs 2024 assessment says Indias annual groundwater recharge stands at 446.90 BCM, and extraction stands at 60.47 of its annual extractable resource. 7. The World Bank states that India abstracts about 245 BCM of groundwater annually, which represents approximately 25 of global groundwater abstraction. It describes India as the worlds largest groundwater user. How much water does the world hold? - Though 70 per cent of Earths surface is covered by water. 96.5 of Earths water is saline, primarily in oceans and seas. - Only 2.5 per cent is freshwater, out of which nearly 69 is locked in glaciers and ice caps. Around 30 is groundwater, while only a tiny fraction exists as accessible surface less than 0.3 per cent water in lakes and rivers. - Importantly, the UN World Water Development Report 2022 notes that estimates of global freshwater volumes vary considerably because of methodological uncertainty. - It also emphasises that freshwater is very unevenly distributed geographically and that freshwater renewal rates vary substantially between continents. - This makes water security less about the absolute quantity of water on Earth and more about the availability, accessibility, quality, location and rate of renewal of freshwater. How severe is Indias water stress? 8. The World Bank defines water scarcity as a situation when annual per capita water availability drops below 1000 cubic metres m and when safe and usable water falls short of the total demand. 9. According to the Falkenmark Index, a region with per capita annual renewable water below 1700 mis considered under water stress, and if it further falls below 1000 m, it will be chronic water scarcity. 10. CWC in its study titled Assessment of Water Resources of India 2024 estimated that Indias average annual water availability, between 1985 and 2023, stood at 2,115.95 billion cubic meters BCM. 11. According to the Central Water Commission, Indias per capita water availability has significantly decreased from 5,177 m in 1951 to 1,486 in 2021 and is projected to decline further to 1,367 m by 2031. 12. As per a report by NITI Aayog, Indias per capita water is projected to be at 1140m by 2050.About 820 million people have close to or lower than 1000m per capita water availability, putting pressure particularly on Indian cities. 13. CWCs latest assessment shows that live storage in 178 major reservoirs stood at 70 of their total capacity - a 10-year low. 14. According to CGWBs 2024 assessment, 11.13 of Indias groundwater assessment units are already over-exploited, while another 13.59 are critical or semi-critical. 15. A NITI Aayod report in 2018 said that nearly 50 of springs in the IHR are either drying up or have already dried up. 16. Rapid unplanned urbanisation, encroachment of existing water bodies, extreme heat, and water shortages have become a recurring annual crisis. Shimla 2018, Chennai 2019 and recently Bengaluru 2024, all have faced Day Zero like situations. BEYOND THE NUGGET UNs Water Bankruptcy Report 2026 1. The United Nations University Institute for Water, Environment and Health UNU-INWEH released a new report titled Global Water Bankruptcy Living Beyond Our Hydrological Means in the Post-Crisis Era. 2. As per the report, nearly 75 of the worlds population lives in countries classified as water-insecure or critically water-insecure. 3. Around 70 of the worlds major aquifers show long-term declining trends. 4. Around 3 billion people and more than half of the worlds food production are located in areas where total water storage is already declining or unstable. 5. More than 170 million hectares of irrigated cropland are under high or very high water stress. Post Read Question Consider the following statements 1. Globally, the quantity of freshwater stored in ice caps, glaciers and permanent snow is greater than fresh groundwater. 2. Globally, freshwater stored as groundwater is much greater than that stored in rivers and lakes. 3. India accounts for about 50 of global groundwater abstraction. Which of the statements given above are correct? a There are two correct statements, that include statement 2. b There are two correct statements, that are statements 1 and 3. c There is only one correct statement. d All three statements are correct. Answer a Sources At 70, Indias water reserves at 10-year low, Water crisis in India stories of distress, gender disparities, and complex societal responses, Himalayan springs are drying. articleTitle: Flydubai FZ1073 attack: Co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami hit Smit Machchhar with crash axe, UAE says ‘terror act’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC key Captain Smit Machchaar, who allegedly foiled an attempt by his co-pilot to crash an Israel-bound flydubai flight and is currently undergoing treatment at a hospital in the UAE
description: An Omani co-pilot used a cockpit crash axe to attack Indian Captain Smit Machchhar on a flydubai flight, forcing an emergency landing as terror probes unfold.
body_raw: The weapon used in the flydubai plane cockpit attack on Wednesday has been identified now. After an investigation, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday that Omani co-pilot of flight FZ1073 Hamam al-Hammami allegedly used an axe to attack Indian pilot Smit Machchhar in an attempt to take control of the plane bound for Israel. The UAE and Israel are calling the incident a terror attack, while flydubai has termed it an altercation. As per a UAE statement, the passengers and crew members intervened after the co-pilot caused the plane to suddenly plunge, helping bring the aircraft under control. The flight eventually made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. The captain was seriously injured in the incident, and both pilots were later taken to the UAE, which is leading the investigation. What is a crash axe? A crash axe is a mandatory safety and emergency tool kept inside the cockpit of commercial aircraft. It is designed to allow flight crew to punch through the aircrafts bodywork or interior panels to free trapped passengers or crew after a crash. Pilots can also use it to shatter reinforced cockpit or cabin windows if emergency exits are blocked. The handle of the crash axe is typically insulated so crew members can cut through live electrical wires during an onboard fire. Most air safety authorities, such as the European Union Aviation Safety Agency EASA, the International Civil Aviation Organisation ICAO, and the Federal Aviation Administration FAA, require all large commercial passenger and cargo aircraft operated by air carriers to be equipped with an accessible crash axe. What happens to the co-pilot now? The investigation has raised questions about how the co-pilot came to be in the cockpit despite having previously been removed from flying duties in Oman over concerns about extremist views. According to The Guardian report, a person familiar with the matter said the co-pilot had worked for Omans national airline but was barred from flying after questions were raised about his views. He was later moved to an administrative position at Oman Air before eventually being hired by UAE-based flydubai. The person spoke on condition of anonymity because of the ongoing investigation. It was not immediately clear what background and security checks were carried out when he was hired by flydubai. As per the Wall Street Journal, a senior official confirmed that the co-pilot had been removed from flying duties and later assigned administrative work at Oman Air. The indian captain, who was badly wounded during the attack, has said he used his remaining strength to unlock the cockpit door after being stabbed. People who heard loud noises inside the cockpit then entered, dealt with the co-pilot and helped regain control of the aircraft. The UAE prosecutor general said the co-pilots actions had put the aircraft at risk of crashing. Investigators probing possible extremist motive Security agencies from four countries in the region are investigating the incident, with assistance from the US and other Western governments, an official familiar with the investigation said, The Guardian reported. UAE senior diplomatic adviser Anwar Gargash on Friday said that the incident was a dangerous terrorist act. According to The Guardian, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also said the co-pilot had undergone Islamist radicalisation, but did not provide evidence for the claim. The co-pilots Instagram account was active until Wednesday before it was deleted.

articleTitle: Inside Mithun Chakraborty’s 1.5-acre Madh Island estate: 22 pets, separate cottages and a Yellow Beetle
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Mithun Chakraborty's home tour
description: Son Namashi Chakraborty revealed that the estate holds Mithun’s very first Mumbai shelter, a vintage yellow Volkswagen Beetle where he slept for 15 days during early career struggles.
body_raw: Of the many properties Bollywood actor Mithun Chakraborty owns, the sprawling Madh Island bungalow stands out. Home to 22 pets, with separate cottages for different family members and a full-fledged in-house studio, the bungalow is named Mimoh Cottage after his eldest son, Mimoh Chakraborty. His younger son, Namashi Chakraborty, shared the story behind the 1.5-acre property, spread across approximately 65,000 square feet, during a recent video interview My parents bought this house in 1985, a few months after my elder brother Mimoh was born.Mithun is a fan of gardening, and the lush greenery surrounding the estate attests to that fact. Dad loves gardening. He often keeps himself busy doing that, Namashi added. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Mithuns first home in Mumbai As he walked around the space and gave a tour, Namashi pointed towards a yellow Volkswagen Beetle and called it his dads first home in Mumbai. When dad came to Mumbai, he didnt have a house to live. He spent 15 days of his life in this yellow Beetle. This was his first house. Now, it is not in a condition to be driven, yet dad spends a lot of money on its maintenance, he revealed. Separate cottages Whats interesting about the Madh Island property is that it is divided into different cottages for each family member. There are different cottages for different family members. Both my father and grandfather believed that every kid should have their own space, Namashi explained to Pinkvilla, adding that one cottage has been converted into a fully equipped gym, one into an office, another is reserved for guests, and the last one, opposite the guest accommodation, is where Mithun and his wife stay when they are in Mumbai. Gurleen Baruah, existential psychotherapist at That Culture Thing, says that if the choice to stay separately is made consciously - out of care for each others rhythms, rest needs, or simply a preference for solitude - it can actually strengthen the bond. The rooms then become a place to retreat, not to escape. It respects that people in a family are still individuals, with their histories, bodies, and ways of being in the world, she tells indianexpress.com. Wall of fame A walk through the office takes us down memory lane through Mithuns long and expansive career across the Tollywood and Bollywood film industries. A wall of fame is dedicated to Mithuns photographs with prominent public figures, guests, and celebrities, such as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and politician Bal Thackeray. Theres also a snapshot capturing the moment he received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award. Another wall is dedicated to his achievements, awards, fan sketches and gifts from the audience. Finally, a section of the house has been converted into a professional studio-called Myrnd Bungalow-available for wedding bookings and film shoots. Over the years, the estate has hosted several Diwali parties with star-studded guest lists, including veteran legends like Dharmendra and Jeetendra. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to.

articleTitle: Mere presence at protest no proof of crime: Rajasthan High Court shields 23 agitators
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Protest Rajasthan High Court Unlawful Assembly Crime dissent Constitution Legal News
description: The high court was hearing a petition by 23 residents of Hanumangarh district seeking protection from coercive action in a criminal case arising from their alleged involvement in a large public demonstration.
body_raw: Being part of a protest does not make a person criminally liable for everything that happens in the crowd, the Rajasthan High Court has said, noting that mere presence at a large demonstration cannot by itself establish individual criminality. The court said investigators must distinguish between a persons presence at a gathering and specific acts attributed to them, while balancing the right to dissent with the states duty to maintain public order. Justice Farjand Ali was hearing a petition filed by 23 people from Hanumangarh district in connection with a criminal case arising from a public protest and issued notice to the state and police directing that no coercive steps be taken against the petitioners in the meantime. The right to voice dissent, to assemble peacefully and to espouse a cause, subject of course to the reasonable restrictions permissible in law, constitutes an essential facet of the constitutional scheme governing a democratic polity. A protest, by itself, cannot be equated with criminality merely because the expression of dissent causes inconvenience or displeasure to the authorities, the court said on September 28. It added that at the same time, the constitutional protection available to peaceful expression cannot be permitted to become a shield for acts which are, independently and specifically, alleged to constitute cognisable offences. The distinction between the two assumes significance while considering the entitlement of an individual to protection during the pendency of investigation, it said. Mere presence not participation The case arose from allegations linked to a public protest in which a large number of people had assembled. Against this backdrop, the court considered whether every person present at such a gathering could be subjected to the same degree of criminal culpability without specific attribution of individual acts. The petition was filed by 23 residents of Hanumangarh district. The petitioners were represented by Senior Advocate Vineet Jain and advocate Kunal Upadhyay, with Additional Advocate General Deepak Choudhary and public prosecutor Narendra Gehlot appearing for the state. Making it clear that it was not deciding whether the allegations in the criminal case were true or whether any of the petitioners were ultimately guilty, the high court examined whether the material placed before it, at this stage, justified subjecting the petitioners to coercive action just because of their alleged association with or presence in the larger protest assembly. The court acknowledged that the allegations included acts allegedly committed by certain members of the gathering. If those allegations were ultimately established against the persons responsible, the court said, they could attract legal consequences. But those allegations could not automatically be extended to everyone who was present at the protest. Mere presence at the place of demonstration, without more, cannot ipso facto be treated as proof of participation in each and every overt act allegedly committed during the course of such assembly, Justice Ali said. The court said this distinction assumes considerable significance where a protest involves a very large number of people. Simply being part of a gathering and actually participating in a particular alleged act are not necessarily the same thing. Criminal liability must be linked The court said that in cases concerning public protests, particularly large gatherings, the investigating agency would have to undertake the exercise of separating individual culpability from general allegations relating to the assembly. Criminal liability is individual in character, the court observed. Ordinarily, it said, criminal liability cannot be fastened on a person merely by association with a gathering unless the ingredients of the particular offence are otherwise attracted against that person. The observation does not mean that people participating in protests are immune from criminal proceedings. Justice Ali recognised the states legitimate authority to regulate public protest and assemblies in the interest of public order. The court also noted that the right to voice dissent, assemble peacefully and espouse a cause is subject to reasonable restrictions permissible in law. It said it was not required at this stage to return a finding either with regard to their culpability or the truthfulness of the allegations. The court also said the issue was not merely a dispute between private parties. It concerned the manner in which citizens right to participate in democratic expression and the power of the state to maintain public order operate within their respective constitutional fields. Finding that the matter warranted examination before any precipitative or coercive action was permitted against the petitioners, the high court decided to intervene without expressing any opinion on the merits of the allegations or the defence of the petitioners. It issued notice and directed that the matter be listed after four weeks. In the meantime, the court ordered that no coercive steps shall be taken against the petitioners.

articleTitle: Delhi Minister Parvesh Singh faces non-cognizable report, court nod needed for probe
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The incident took place on Sunday afternoon when the minister visited the Outer Ring Road in Vikaspuri to inspect the construction of a stretch of road. (PTI and ANI Photos)
description: Police registered an non-cognisable report for voluntarily causing hurt against the Delhi minister after the 22-year-old man complained that he was slapped, threatened and abused during Sunday’s inspection.
body_raw: A day after Public Works Department PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh allegedly slapped an Aam Aadmi Party AAP worker during an inspection of a newly constructed road in West Delhis Tilak Nagar, police have registered an non-cognisable report NCR for voluntarily causing hurt against the minister. An NCR is registered for minor offences and police require permission from the court to conduct an investigation. It is different from an FIR, registered for offences where the police can directly conduct a probe. Police have registered an FIR against AAP MLA Jarnail Singh for obstructing government work, based on a complaint filed by a PWD Public Works Department assistant engineer. Five complaints lodged According to police sources, two local BJP workers Monday filed separate complaints against the AAP MLA and his supporters for allegedly misbehaving with the minister during the inspection. On Sunday, two complaints were filed against the AAP MLA by the PWD and the contractor entrusted with constructing the road. In both complaints, Jarnail Singh was accused of allegedly obstructing officials from discharging their duties and allegedly threatening, coercing and demanding money from contractors at the work site. Sahib Singh, the 22-year-old man who was allegedly slapped by the minister, also filed a complaint against the BJP minister, alleging that he was slapped, threatened and abused. All five complaints were filed at Vikaspuri police station. The incident took place on Sunday afternoon when the minister visited the Outer Ring Road in Vikaspuri to inspect the construction of a stretch of road. Jarnail Singh had reportedly been posting videos showing the roads poor quality for the past four days. In a video that went viral, Jarnail Singh was seen peeling off a layer of the road with his hands and showing it to the minister before Parvesh allegedly slapped the youth live-streaming the interaction. Delhi minister Pravesh Verma slaps man after altercation over road quality Read pic.twitter.comFRq7veQYJj - The Indian Express IndianExpress September 27, 2026 Jarnail Singh told The Indian Express that at 1.15 pm on Sunday, he received a call from Parvesh who said that he was visiting the road site. He Parvesh came without any prior intimation, but his team members were all prepared. They wanted to put on some sort of show and planned to leave immediately, as I had been challenging the government for the past few days to come and inspect the poor-quality road. But when I removed a layer of the road with my own hands, he got agitated and slapped the man who was recording the video, the MLA claimed. Regarding the complaint filed against him by PWD engineers, Jarnail Singh said the allegations were false. The minister is doing this to save himself from the law, he claimed.

articleTitle: Congestion ahead: Accurate Google Maps update on Barapullah traffic expected soon
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Google Maps, Google maps app, Google Maps accurate traffic update on Barahpullah, Google maps app accurate traffic update on Barahpullah, Google Maps accurate traffic update, Google maps app accurate traffic update, Delhi Traffic Police, delhi news, India news, Indian express, current affairs
description: Police also examining the possibility of regulating or diverting traffic towards NH-24, wherever feasible
body_raw: The Delhi Traffic Police is coordinating with Google Maps to ensure that the traffic situation on the newly opened Barapullah Phase-III corridor is accurately reflected on the app, officers said on Tuesday. This comes a day after the Delhi Traffic Police on Monday said in a post on X that with the app showing the route as relatively clear, commuters are being directed towards the already congested stretch.A drone survey had identified a major bottleneck at the Sundial Park merger near Sarai Kale Khan where lanes merge into the existing Barapullah corridor. Traffic Police officers said this is adding to the traffic load as vehicles that would otherwise use DND or NH-24 turns towards the new corridor, choking it further. The newly opened corridor is attracting substantial traffic that would otherwise use NH-24 and DND, thereby increasing the traffic load, an official said. The Traffic Police said the issue on the navigation app will be sorted out in a few days. PWD flags misinformation Public Works Department PWD officials have also blamed Google Maps for feeding misinformation to commuters, exacerbating the lockjam. There is some misinformation on Google Maps apparently, it is not updating real-time traffic information for commuters to properly navigate, causing more congestion on the stretch, PTI quoted an official as having said. Officials also said that despite a recent meeting with the Traffic Police and the National Highways Authority of India NHAI, no solution has been reached so far. Appropriate traffic-control measures and signals at suitable merging points may also be considered to regulate the inflow of vehicles and prevent excessive accumulation, Traffic Police officers said. The Traffic Police is also examining the possibility of regulating or diverting traffic towards NH-24, wherever feasible. Officers, meanwhile, also pointed to a traffic signal on the corridor that has no electricity connection yet, stating that once functional, it is expected to help regulate traffic entering the corridor. A request for an electricity connection has been sent to the BSES, the official said. Barapullah Phase-III flyover was inaugurated on September 29 and opened to commuters on September 30. The corridor has since witnessed heavy traffic and congestion. Senior Traffic Police personnel and PWD officials had on October 1 conducted a joint aerial inspection using drones. It was attended by Joint Commissioner of Police Traffic Sanjay Tyagi, Additional Commissioner of Police Traffic Dinesh Kumar Gupta and Deputy Commissioner of Police Southern Range Sandeep Gupta. The survey identified a sharp, almost rectangular geometry at the merger, resulting in an abrupt convergence of traffic and a bottleneck. There is a significant mismatch in lane capacity at the merging point. Multiple streams of traffic are converging towards the existing Barapullah corridor, which has comparatively limited lane capacity, an official had said. A senior traffic police officer said that they had asked the PWD to work on the curvature near Sundial park patch of the Barapullah flyover. The Traffic Police said it was closely monitoring the corridor and coordinating with PWD and other agencies to address the ongoing issues. Commuters have been advised to follow traffic advisories and directions of traffic police personnel and use alternate routes wherever advised. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: 7-month pregnant sarpanch faces no-trust motion, Chhattisgarh High Court steps in
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chhattisgarh High Court sarpanch pregnant no-confidence motion
description: Referring to Supreme Court observations recognising the right to health as part of the right to life and emphasising maternity protection, the court noted that removal of elected women representatives should not be treated casually.
body_raw: A seven-month pregnant village sarpanch has received temporary relief in a no-confidence motion after the Chhattisgarh High Court deferred the proceedings, saying elected panchas ward members have a statutory and democratic right to seek her removal, but authorities must also ensure she gets a fair opportunity to respond without compromising her health or that of her unborn child. Justice Amitendra Kishore Prasad was hearing a petition filed by one Manisha Raj Chouhan, the elected sarpanch of Siriyagarh gram panchayat in Sakti district, challenging a September 21 notice issued for a meeting to consider a no-confidence motion against her. The meeting was scheduled for noon on October 1 at the panchayat building. The right to health has been recognised as an integral facet of the right to life guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. The authorities are required to balance both aspects, namely, the statutory right of the Panchas to seek consideration of a no-confidence motion and the right of the petitioner to receive a fair and reasonable opportunity to participate in the proceedings without compromising her health or the health of her unborn child, the court said on October 1. The proceedings began after nine panchas submitted an application on September 17, saying they had lost confidence in Chouhan and seeking her removal. She received the notice on September 24 and challenged the process, saying supporting material had not been supplied to her and that she had not received seven clear days to prepare for the meeting. Financial allegations According to the states submissions recorded in the order, the panchas had filed affidavits alleging that Chouhan had misappropriated Rs 10 lakh, Rs 75,564, Rs 25,750 and Rs 1,91,600, and that the related works had not been completed. The state said the prescribed authority had considered the allegations and, after verification, found sufficient grounds to initiate the no-confidence proceedings. Chouhan argued that the prescribed authority had called for records from the chief executive officer of the panchayat body but issued the notice without waiting for the report. She also said documents relating to the allegations had not been provided to her. The high court said simply calling for records and issuing the notice before receiving them would not automatically invalidate the proceedings. The question was whether any mandatory legal requirement had been violated or whether the procedure had caused substantial prejudice to Chouhan. However, the court found significance in her complaint that the material relied upon for the no-confidence motion had not been supplied. The principles of fairness and natural justice require that the affected elected representative should have reasonable knowledge of the material relied upon against her, the court said, adding that this was necessary for her to effectively participate in the proceedings. Notice period also questioned The court also considered Chouhans objection to the notice period. The notice was dated September 21 but received by her on September 24. The meeting was fixed for October 1 at noon. The court noted that she, therefore, had seven calendar days from actual receipt of the notice to the scheduled meeting. It said the question of whether the legal requirement of seven days notice had been complied with had to be examined with reference to the date of service or receipt, particularly since Chouhan claimed that she had not received seven clear days to prepare for the proceedings. The court did not hold that the notice was legally defective. It directed the prescribed authority to consider Chouhans objection. Pregnancy a key consideration The high court then considered Chouhans medical condition. She had stated that she was around seven months pregnant and placed her Matru Avam Bal Suraksha Card on record. The court noted that the respondents had not specifically disputed her pregnancy. Referring to Supreme Court observations recognising the right to health as part of the right to life and emphasising maternity protection, maternal health and dignity, the court also noted observations that removal of elected women representatives, particularly in rural areas, should not be treated casually and that fairness, natural justice and democratic functioning must be respected. At the same time, the court made it clear that pregnancy did not automatically stop the no-confidence process. The right of the elected Panchas to move a no-confidence motion is also a statutory and democratic right, it said, adding that the court could not bar such proceedings just because the elected sarpanch was facing inconvenience. Chouhan was directed to submit a fresh detailed application before the prescribed authority, Dabhara, raising her objections regarding the notice period, non-supply of supporting material and her medical condition, along with relevant documents. The authority was directed to consider the application objectively and in accordance with law, while taking into account her medical condition and the legal rights of the panchas. If necessary, it could defer the proceedings and fix an appropriate future date. It was also directed to provide Chouhan the material on which the proposed motion was based, subject to the material being part of the record and legally disclosable.

articleTitle: IIT experts, JEE Board to discuss proposed entrance test reforms in meeting
articleFeaturedImageAlt: JEE Advanced syllabus
description: An expert committee has also been constituted to evaluate the adaptive testing proposal and its potential to reduce coaching dependency and exam vulnerabilities.
body_raw: Experts from IIT Kanpur and JEE Apex Board JAB members will meet on Monday to discuss proposed reforms to the JEE Advanced examination, including how to make the test more student-friendly and the impact of an aptitude test in the entrance, said an official. According to a senior IIT official, an aptitude test for the first-year students across 10-12 IITs has already been conducted to collect data and assess whether a similar test can eventually be incorporated in the entrance examination. In the last council meeting with the IITs held in August last year, IIT Kanpur Director Manindra Agrawal had flagged concerns over the existing structure of the JEE Advanced, the prevalence of a huge coaching industry, and the significant emotional and financial stress on families. To address these challenges, he proposed shifting to adaptive testing of quantitative and reasoning skills, which dynamically generates questions based on a students performance. An expert committee has also been constituted to evaluate the adaptive testing proposal and its potential to reduce coaching dependency and exam vulnerabilities. When asked about the status of the proposal, Agrawal said the aptitude-test proposal is still at an exploring stage and no decision has been taken on introducing it in JEE Advanced. We are exploring an improved aptitude test .this is not decided yet.It will take at least two to three years., Agrawal said. As per officials, the broader objective is to examine whether an aptitude test can reduce the influence of coaching on a students performance. Agrawal also said that studies have been done in the US to understand the impact of coaching on performance in aptitude tests. They found that after some 20-30 hours of coaching material, going beyond doesnt substantially improve performance. Based on that, they have switched many of their exams to aptitude tests. The SAT is an aptitude test, Agrawal said. So, we are going to use this information. We want to convince ourselves that in the Indian context this could be the case, because if we can establish that the aptitude test has a strong correlation with intelligence, that would imply that coaching will not impact much, the official added. A coaching institute cannot increase the innate intelligence of a student. The ability to do well in an aptitude test is more about practising different types of questions, Agrawal said. The proposed changes are also linked to the IITs broader discussions on making JEE Advanced more student-friendly. However, the official clarified that any major change in the examination structure would not be implemented overnight. It will take at least one or two years to implement the roadmap. Whenever we want to bring about a major change, it takes time. These students need time to prepare for the examination, the official said.

articleTitle: 109-year-old Dankuni railway station in Bengal to get Rs 18.66 crore upgrade
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The 109-year-old Dankuni railway station in West Bengal is set to receive an Rs 18.66-crore upgrade. (Image generated using AI)
description: Dankuni railway station redevelopment: The 109-year-old Dankuni railway station in Bengal is set for an Rs 18.66 crore upgrade under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme, with several passenger and station infrastructure works already completed.
body_raw: Redevelopment of Dankuni railway station The Ministry of Railways is upgrading the 109-year-old Dankuni railway station in West Bengal under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme ABSS. Located on the Howrah-Bardhaman Chord line, the station falls under the administrative jurisdiction of the Eastern Railways Howrah Division. Launched in 2022, the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme ABSS aims at development and upgradation of stations over the Indian Railways IR network. The ABSS has a long-term vision that involves creating master plans, promoting multimodal connectivity, better station accessibility for passengers, etc. Dankuni is an important intercity railway station serving the Kolkata metropolitan region. Built in 1917, the SG-3 Suburban Grade category station handles an average daily footfall of more than 30,000 passengers, including both incoming and outgoing passengers. Well connected to Howrah and Sealdah, Dankuni serves as a key rail hub for the region and an important intermediate stoppage for mail and express trains travelling to and from southern and northeastern states of the country. Now, with passenger numbers expected to rise in the coming years, the station is also set to play an important role in regional rail connectivity. According to Eastern Railway, the strategic location of Dankuni railway station has also contributed to the development of Dankuni as an important industrial hub. Its proximity to industrial areas and strong rail connectivity have helped attract businesses and industries to the region, supporting economic activity and creating employment opportunities. Modernisation of Dankuni railway station The redevelopment of Dankuni Railway Station is being carried out at an estimated cost of Rs 18.66 crore. According to the zonal railway, several works have already been completed, including the ground floor of the main station building, renovation of the building facade and construction of the porch. Development of the circulating and parking areas, platform surfaces and sheds has also been completed. The station has also received improved lighting and new train information and GPS clock systems. The importance of Dankuni is also expected to grow with the proposed freight connectivity projects. In the Union Budget 2026, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman proposed a new Dedicated Freight Corridor DFC linking Dankuni with Surat in Gujarat. The proposed corridor could further strengthen Dankunis role as an important freight and logistics hub, adding to the significance of the station and its surrounding industrial region.

articleTitle: Nearly 2 lakh fewer voters: Meet Chandigarh residents missing after SIR
articleFeaturedImageAlt: martyr mother
description: Chandigarh’s final electoral roll has 4,60,209 electors, against 6,59,805 in the 2024 General Election roll — a net reduction of 1,99,596 electors, or 30.25 per cent.
body_raw: A mother lost her only son following an encounter in Jammu and Kashmir. Another family has spent three decades serving chai and paranthas to generations of Chandigarh students and voted for decades here. Yet, after the Special Intensive Revision SIR, all of these and more have found their names absent in the electoral roles of a city they have called home for decades. Chandigarhs final electoral roll has 4,60,209 electors, against 6,59,805 in the 2024 General Election roll - a net reduction of 1,99,596 electors, or 30.25 per cent. Notices have been sent to people with a call for personal hearing. Veena Sharma, 86, lost her only son, Captain Rohit Kaushal, who was killed while fighting militants in an encounter in Doda district of Jammu and Kashmir on November 11, 1995. Captain Kaushal was awarded the Shaurya Chakra for gallantry. The 86-year-old was flagged for deletion during the SIR after a discrepancy was found in her surname in older electoral records. A notice was served by the jurisdictional Booth Level Officer BLO, asking her to appear for a personal hearing. Sharma has been staying in Vrindavan for the past several months following the death of her husband and was not in Chandigarh when the notice was issued. Her son-in-law, Vinod Vashisht, then stepped in. In the 2002 electoral rolls, she had Sharma as her surname. At that time, they were staying in Sector 22 and after having moved to Sector 43, her vote showed the surname Kaushal. But the change had not been made in her older electoral record. And she was served a notice with calls that she has to personally attend the hearing, Vashisht told The Indian Express. What troubled the family was that Sharma was being asked to travel to Chandigarh despite being 86 and having several government documents establishing her identity. She is 86 years old and has been a voter in Chandigarh for more than 40 years. She is currently staying in Vrindavan and could not simply be asked to travel to Chandigarh again and again just to establish something that is already supported by her documents, Vashisht, who is also patron of the Shaheed Capt Rohit Kaushal Charitable Trust, said. He said Sharmas Aadhaar, PAN, pensioner card and passport all carry her present surname and are linked to her registered mobile number. I had to repeatedly approach the election authorities and explain that this was an elderly woman and the issue was only a surname mismatch. She was being asked to appear in person in Chandigarh, but why should an 86-year-old woman have to undertake such a journey when her Aadhaar, PAN, pensioner card and passport were already there, he said. Vashisht eventually appeared before the BLO and local election officials are now examining the case. But the episode, he said, raises a larger question about elderly voters who may not have family members to pursue such cases. She had already given her only son to the nation. It was painful to see that today she was being made to struggle to establish her right to vote. The process makes us wonder about elderly voters who may not have someone to take up their case, he said. 30 years of serving chai, paranthas, now an entire family missing from the rolls For more than three decades, the chai-parantha stall in Sector 35-D has been part of Chandigarhs student life. Generations of students, PG residents and college-goers have spent time there over steaming cups of tea and plates of parathas. But for the family that has run the stall since 1997, that three-decade connection with Chandigarh has not translated into their names remaining on the electoral rolls. Manoj, 35, who lives with his family in Sector 42-B, Attawa, said his wife, brothers Anil and Krishna, and mother have all been left out of the rolls. His father, too, had been a Chandigarh voter. We came here for work and the BLO told us that our house was locked and they could not find us. They have struck off the names of our entire family - my wife, my brothers Anil and Krishna and my mother. My father also voted here only. This stall was started by him in 1997, Manoj said. For him, the deletion is difficult to understand because voting in Chandigarh has been part of the familys life for decades. I am born here. my brothers are born here.. we have been voting since we were 18. My father also voted here, he said. Manoj, who currently lives on rent, questioned why being a tenant should become a reason for exclusion from the electoral rolls. Just because we stay on rent does not mean we should be excluded from the rolls. We have been living and working here for years. I have asked the BLO to come and verify us at our home, but he does not come, he said. He said he also has documents to establish his address. My government license that is given to me for this stall, my Aadhaar Card and all my documents have my address. Still, our name has been struck off. Why were all the names removed? They should come and verify us, he said. How can they ask us for the 2002 roll? I was just six For Karanbir Singh - a lawyer - the demand to establish an electoral link to a 2002 roll when he was just six, has turned into a family ordeal. Karanbir, 30, his wife Rupal Trivedi, sister Harkriti Singh, domestic help Neema Rawat and her son Pankaj Rawat were all asked to undergo verification. He said all five members had submitted the required documents before the BLO and filed their SIR forms within the stipulated time. He said he submitted his own form on June 24. Yet, he later received a notice stating that his vote had been cancelled and was called for a hearing on August 4, where he had to submit documents again to get his name restored. What particularly puzzled him was the demand to establish the familys electoral link with the 2002 roll. I was six. My sister wasnt even born. How can they ask us for the 2002 roll, he asked. The family was later called to Sector 17 for cross-verification of their documents. For Karanbir, the process meant taking time off work, travelling to the designated centre and waiting in long queues - despite having already submitted the required paperwork. There was hardly any clear information about where to go or what exactly had to be done. The place was severely understaffed and people were standing in queues for hours, he said. Describing the scene at Sector 17, Karanbir said, It honestly looked like a complete fish market.

articleTitle: 54 years, five languages, zero repetitions: Singeetham Srinivasa Rao was one of a kind
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao
description: In a career spanning 54 years and five languages, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao attempted things no other Indian filmmaker dared to try: A dialogue-free comedy, a time-travel science fiction, a high-fantasy adventure rooted in folklore. And at 94, a musical fantasy.
body_raw: The easiest way to understand what Singeetham Srinivasa Rao meant to Indian cinema is to list what he did and then try to find another filmmaker who did the same. He made a film without dialogue. He made a film with a time machine. He made a film set on a mythical island ruled by a sorcerer. He made a film about a classical dancer who lost her leg and returned to the stage. He made a film where the comedy was entirely physical, entirely visual, entirely dependent on the audiences ability to follow a story through images alone. And then, at 94, he made one more film because he was not done. Find another Indian filmmaker who did all of this. Not one of these. All of these. Across five languages. Across six decades. Without a single repetition. You will not find one. Because there is no one else. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao, who died at Kauvery Hospital in Chennai on Saturday night at the age of 94, was not merely an experimental filmmaker. He was the filmmaker against whom every other attempt at innovation in Indian cinema must be measured, and one who, measured against anyone else, invariably comes out ahead. Also Read Legendary filmmaker Singeetham Srinivasa Rao dies at 94 The experiment nobody believed in The story of Pushpaka Vimanam is the story of Singeetham Srinivasa Rao in miniature. A filmmaker walks into a room and says I want to make a film with no dialogue. Not a silent film. A film with sound, music, ambient noise, everything except spoken words. The story will be told entirely through images. In 1987, this was not a pitch that anyone wanted to hear. Indian cinema, in every language, was built on dialogue. Take away dialogue, and you take away the scaffolding that the entire commercial film industry stood on. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao could not find a producer. Nobody wanted to fund a film that could not be marketed with a single quotable line. So he produced it himself, partnering with Shringar Nagaraj, a Kannada producer who was willing to take the risk. The idea for the film came to Singeetham while he was in the shower. He wrote the screenplay in two weeks. Also Read Made for Rs 15 lakh, Kamal Haasan, Singeethams pathbreaking film earned 6.6x its budget The result was a black comedy starring Kamal Haasan, Amala and Tinnu Anand that told a complex, funny and emotionally engaging story without a single word being spoken on screen. Because there was no dialogue, the film did not need dubbing. It was released simultaneously across all Indian languages under different titles Pushpaka Vimana in Kannada, Pushpaka Vimanam in Telugu, Pushpak in Hindi. Same film. Same audio track. Every audience understood it. The film won the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. The time machine nobody expected Four years later, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao did it again. This time, the experiment was science fiction. Aditya 369, starring Nandamuri Balakrishna and Mohini, was the first Telugu film to feature a time machine. The concept was inspired by H.G. Wells The Time Machine, which Singeetham had read during his college years at the University of Madras. The film sent its characters back in time to the court of Sri Krishnadevaraya in the Vijayanagara Empire, mixing historical drama with futuristic technology in a way that nobody in Telugu cinema had attempted before. The film was presented by S.P. Balasubrahmanyam, the legendary playback singer who was also Singeetham Srinivasa Raos frequent collaborator. The combination of talents was extraordinary, but the concept was the real risk. In 1991, Telugu cinema was defined by family dramas, action films and romantic comedies. Science fiction was not a genre anyone believed the audience would accept. However, they accepted it. The film that proved the audience was willing to go wherever the filmmaker took them, as long as the maker knew where he was going. Singeetham always knew. Thirty-five years later, time travel is a common device in Telugu cinema. The lineage traces back to Aditya 369 and, by extension, to a filmmaker who read HG Wells in a Madras university library and decided that Telugu cinema deserved a time machine. The fantasy world nobody had built Bhairava Dweepam was the third experiment in three consecutive decades, each in a different genre, each doing something Indian cinema had not done before. Also Read Sing Geetham movie review At 94, Singeetam Srinivasa Rao delivers a musical fable The film, starring Balakrishna, was a high-fantasy adventure set on a mystical island ruled by a malevolent sorcerer seeking immortality. It drew from Indian folklore, mythology and adventure storytelling to create a world that was entirely self-contained its own geography, its own rules, its own visual language. The screenplay was co-written with Raavi Kondala Rao, one of Telugu literatures most respected writers, and produced under the Chandamama Vijaya Pictures banner. In 1994, Indian cinema did not make high-fantasy films. The genre was considered too expensive, too risky and too unfamiliar for audiences raised on realism-adjacent commercial cinema. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao ignored all of that. He built the island. He populated it with wizards, warriors and magical creatures. He created set pieces that were elaborate by any standard, let alone the standards of a mid-budget Telugu film in the early 1990s. Bhairava Dweepam completed a 100-day theatrical run in 28 centres. It proved a full two decades, before Baahubali made high fantasy commercially viable on a massive scale, that Telugu audiences were ready for mythology, magic and world-building. They just needed a filmmaker who was willing to try. The biography that changed lives Before the dialogue-free comedy, before the time machine, before the fantasy island, there was Mayuri. The film that made Singeetham Srinivasa Raos name and, in the process, changed a young womans life. Mayuri was inspired by the true story of Mumbai-based Bharatanatyam dancer Sudha Chandran, whose right leg had to be amputated after she was injured in a road accident in Tamil Nadu in 1981. Doctors fitted her with a Jaipur foot prosthetic, and Chandran returned to the stage, performing classical dance with an artificial limb. Singeetham saw the story and knew it was a film. Sudha, who had never acted, played herself. The film was a critical and commercial triumph. It was remade in Hindi as Naache Mayuri with the same cast. It launched Sudha Chandrans career as a film and television actress, a career that continues to this day. And it demonstrated that Singeetham could take a real-life story, handle it with sensitivity and turn it into a mainstream film without compromising either the storys truth or the audiences entertainment. The Tamil connection Singeetham Srinivasa Raos versatility extended beyond genres to languages. While Telugu was his primary language, his Tamil filmography includes some of the most significant films in that industrys history. Also Read Why Singeetham Srinivasa Rao banned Sing Geetham crew from referencing his masterpieces Anand, a romantic comedy starring Kamal Haasan and Revathi, was a commercial hit that was later remade in multiple languages. His collaboration with Kamal on Pushpaka Vimanam remains one of the most critically acclaimed actor-director partnerships in South Indian cinema. Magalir Mattum was a Tamil film that addressed womens issues. He also worked in Kannada, Malayalam and Hindi, making him one of the very few Indian filmmakers to direct films in five languages. The question that lingers after reviewing Singeetham Srinivasa Raos filmography is why did nobody else attempt what he did? The answer is not that other filmmakers lacked talent. It is that they lacked the specific combination of traits that Singeetham Srinivasa Rao possessed technical knowledge deep enough to execute his ideas, creative ambition wild enough to conceive them, and a stubborn indifference to whether the market was ready for them. Most filmmakers work within genres. They find what works and refine it. They make action films, or comedies, or romances, and they get better at making those specific things over time. Singeetham never did this. Each one of his films was a fresh start. Each one required learning a new visual language, a new set of production challenges and a new way of engaging with the audience. The commercial film industry does not reward this behaviour. It rewards consistency, predictability and brand identity. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao offered none of these. He offered surprise. And surprise, while thrilling for the audience, is terrifying for the people who invest money in films. The fact that he continued to find producers willing to back his experiments, decade after decade, is itself a testament to the power of his track record. The last experiment In February 2026, at the age of 94, Singeetham Srinivasa Rao announced his return to directing with Sing Geetham, a musical fantasy that marked his first film in over a decade. The project was produced by Nag Ashwin, the director of Kalki 2898 AD. Sing Geetham was completed. It was released. And it was the work of a man who, at an age when most people have forgotten what ambition feels like, walked onto a set and made one more film. Because he had one more story to tell. Because cinema was not something he did, it was something he was. Also Read Singeetham Srinivasa Rao 1931-2026 Kamal Haasan pays last respects to filmmaker Chiranjeevi, Jr NTR mourn demise The measure of the man Singeetham Srinivasa Raos career cannot be reduced to awards, it can only be understood as a body of work that is unlike any other in Indian cinema. Not because every film was a masterpiece, but every film was an attempt to do something that had not been done before. Indian cinema has produced filmmakers who are more commercially successful. It has produced filmmakers who are more critically acclaimed. It has produced filmmakers who are more consistently brilliant. But it has not produced another filmmaker who spent 54 years refusing to make the same film twice, who treated every project as a first film, who looked at the boundaries of what Indian cinema could do and, every single time, decided to step past them. Singeetham Srinivasa Rao did not push boundaries. He made the films he wanted to make, in the way he wanted to make them, for 54 years. And then, at 94, he made one more. Because one more was still not enough. That is not experimentation, that is devotion. And Indian cinema will not see its like again.

articleTitle: Accomplices, a military armoury, a plan to sell guns: Inside Secunderabad arms heist
articleFeaturedImageAlt: According to the police, the suspect first broke open the armoury lock and took out 12 weapons, hiding them in the thick foliage outside. (Image: DGP Telanagana Police/X/Express Photo)
description: On August 31, 12 military-grade weapons were stolen from the armoury of the 20 Madras Regiment at Bolarum in Secunderabad Cantonment. A subsequent police investigation has alleged an elaborate plan involving seven people -- one ex-havildar, three serving army personnel and four civilians
body_raw: The retired army man arrested in the Secunderabad arms heist case allegedly had seven accomplices, including three serving army personnel, police have said. Investigators have alleged that the theft was part of a larger plan to rob banks, jewellers and wealthy people. At a press conference Saturday, Malkajgiri Police Commissioner B Sumathi ruled out a terror angle in the case, alleging instead that 37-year-old retired Havildar Upputholla Mallesh alias Raju had plotted and executed the heist at the armoury of the 20 Madras Regiment at Bolarum in Secunderabad Cantonment with seven others for financial reasons. According to police, he also planned to sell some of the weapons on the black market. The revelations come a month after the theft of 12 military-grade weapons and over 1,900 rounds of ammunition, all of which the Telangana Police later said they had recovered. The stolen weapons included four AK-203 assault rifles, seven pistols and an INSAS rifle. Mallesh was arrested on September 11. At the time, police had said they suspected he had acted alone. At Saturdays press conference, police announced the arrest of seven people in connection with the case. They will be produced before the magistrate soon, Sumathi said. The eight-member team also intended to sell some of the weapons in the black market, for prices ranging from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh. Police said the others arrested are 36-year-old Konduri Sheshulu, a Sepoy 34-year-old Vinod Kumar, a Naik and 37-year-old Kucharakanthi Praveen, a Havildar - all serving army personnel. Sheshulu and Vinod Kumar are from Markapuram in Andhra Pradesh, while Praveen is fromGundlapotlapally in Mahabubnagar district, Telangana. The four civilians arrested in the case, according to police, are 32-year-old Avi Dey alias Obi of Barrackpore, West Bengal 27-year-old Birbal Shaw, who ran a sugarcane juice shop near Barrackpore Cantonment Malleshs 39-year-old cousin Upputholla Mallikarjun, a mason from Padara in Nagarkurnool district and 39-year-old Chemmakar Niranjan, a kirana shop owner from Nagarkurnool. According to police, Mallesh was facing financial difficulties and allegedly involved his cousin Mallikarjun and friend Niranjan, who police said had similar financial problems. He had received Rs 22 lakh as retirement benefits, which he partly used to build a house and buy a car. He faced financial difficulties and felt that robbery and extortion could be the way out, Sumathi said. Police said Mallesh had met Dey and Shaw when he was posted in Barrackpore in 2022 and had allegedly purchased a country-made firearm and one live round of ammunition from the former. In the recent past,he reached out to his friends Sheshulu, Vinod Kumar and Praveen, and they extended support for the theft. Once the deal was brokered, Mallesh contacted Dey and Shaw, who informed him that some of the weapons could also be sold in the black market - for Rs 3 lakh for pistols and Rs 5 lakh for rifles, Sumathi said. Police alleged that Mallesh broke the armoury lock and magazine with the help of the three other army personnel. Police also claimed that Mallesh had a previous criminal record, citing a history of extortion and house burglary in Nagarkurnool district. The proceeds of these burglaries were also kept at his fathers residence in Achampet. We have also recovered the country-made weapon he purchased from Dey, Sumathi said. The police will soon take custody of the other accused. Our investigation into the heist will continue once we get custody of the other accused for interrogation, Sumathi said. The police, however, said they had found no terrorist or extremist links in the case. No such links have been established. The motive of the crime was to amass wealth, Sumathi said.
