articleTitle: In US, Jaishankar warns of ‘major food crisis’ in coming months amid Ukraine, Iran conflicts
articleFeaturedImageAlt: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar speaks at Asia Society after the United Nations General Assemblys high-level week, in New York on Monday. (ANI)
description: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar warned that disruptions to grain shipments and fertiliser supplies could trigger a major food crisis in the coming months.
body_raw: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has warned of a major food crisis in the coming months amid fertiliser shortages and disruptions to grain shipments caused by the Ukraine and Iran-Gulf conflicts. He also said the combined impact of energy, food, fertiliser and financial pressures is proving very very stressful for Global South economies. Speaking at a conversation hosted by the Asia Society in New York Monday, Jaishankar said the Ukraine war and the Iran-Gulf conflict had had a devastating impact on Global South economies, news agency PTI reported. . this is a big concern for us, which is, if you look at these two conflicts, the Ukraine and now the Iran-Gulf conflict, theyve actually had a devastating impact on Global South economies, he said. Jaishankar said there was particular concern over the energy situation as the market is very tight. He also warned that political decisions affecting oil supplies could further complicate the situation and drive up prices at a time when countries should be trying to stabilise them. So part of it is actually the security of oil supplies, and part of it is the politics of oil supplies, and they are feeding into each other, and they are creating a double crisis or an aggravated crisis, he said. Jaishankar warns of food, fertiliser shortages Speaking on the global food situation, Jaishankar said some major grain exporters may not be able to send out shipments, particularly through the Black Sea. We are today looking at a situation where some of the major grain exporters will not be able to send out their shipments, particularly out to the Black Sea, he said. He also said the world was facing significant fertiliser shortages because key producers were in West Asia and Russia and their production had been affected. Jaishankar said the situation could worsen when combined with climate patterns such as a super El Nino. There is going to be a major food crisis probably in the coming months, he said. He said the pressures were not limited to food and fertiliser supplies, with energy and finance also adding to the strain. So if you have energy as a big crunch, and then food and fertilisers on top of it, and finance because every time theres a conflict, money moves towards safe harbours and away from the Global South, the net result of it has been really very very stressful, he said. Countries should not be so self-centred Jaishankar said policymakers could not dismiss the wider consequences of their decisions by arguing that economic hardship elsewhere was unintended. Countries should not be so self-centred that youre in your own world and take your decision and say, Well, it was not my intention to make your life difficult. He said sound common sense should ensure that the basic needs of countries were not neglected to the point of putting them in distress. And that is a concern that we have, he said. Jaishankar warns of instability Jaishankar also warned that the energy crisis could contribute to political instability. We have already seen it after the Ukraine war. We saw in our neighbourhood the direct result of that in political instability, and my fear is what is happening in Iran and the Gulf is going to feed, is going to aggravate, he said. He said some countries would continue to maintain their independence and autonomy despite the pressure created by global conflicts, while others could find it more difficult. Some others would find it harder to do so. So those of us who are autonomous, wed like to see more of us who are autonomous. But its not a black and white scenario. It would depend on the issue and the stakes involved. Therell be cases where countries would make adjustments. Therell be cases where they would fight back, he said. With inputs from PTI

articleTitle: Pneumonic plague case in Russia raises questions: How it spreads and what Indians should know
articleFeaturedImageAlt: cough
description: A rare respiratory infection is drawing attention, but experts say the real differences may be more important to consider
body_raw: Hundreds have been quarantined after a 28-year-old laboratory technician reportedly died of pneumonic plague in the Siberian region of Irkutsk in Russia, according to Moscow Times report. Alexei Tsydenov, head of the neighboring republic of Buryatia, told the independent news outlet that the woman had died from an unspecified form of plague. Unverified X accounts also claim that pneumonic plague is about 100x deadlier than Covid-19. Given the threat, we spoke with experts to better understand the infectious disease and how it differs from Covid-19. Dr Amit Saraf, director, internal medicine, Jupiter Hospital, Thane, said that a pneumonic plague is a serious lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. It is one of the three major forms of plague and is the one that can spread directly from person to person through respiratory droplets, particularly during close contact. The illness can develop rapidly, causing high fever, chills, weakness, cough, chest pain and difficulty breathing. In some cases, the patient may cough up blood-stained sputum. Unlike the plague of history books, this disease is not untreatable today. The important factor is recognising it early and starting the appropriate antibiotics without delay, said Dr Saraf. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. How is pneumonic plague different from Covid-19? The biggest difference is the organism responsible. Covid-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, whereas pneumonic plague is caused by bacteria. Their routes of transmission also differ. Covid-19 can spread quite efficiently through respiratory particles, including from people who may have mild or no symptoms. Pneumonic plague generally requires close exposure to respiratory droplets from an infected person, and person-to-person spread is much less common, said Dr Saraf. Both illnesses can cause fever, cough, weakness and breathing difficulty, so symptoms alone may not always distinguish them, mentioned Dr Samir Garde, director, Dept of Pulmonology and Lung Transplant, Gleneagles Hospital, Parel. However, pneumonic plague can progress rapidly and may cause severe pneumonia, chest pain and sometimes bloody or watery sputum. Covid-19 has a much broader range of presentations, from no symptoms to severe respiratory illness. For Indians, the key message is not to panic or assume every respiratory illness outbreak is plague. Plague is uncommon in India, and its occurrence is generally linked to specific epidemiological circumstances, said Dr Garde. Another important distinction is treatment. Antibiotics are effective against plague bacteria when given promptly they do not work against viruses such as SARS-CoV-2. Both illnesses can affect the lungs and cause pneumonia, so symptoms alone cannot establish the diagnosis. A proper clinical assessment and laboratory testing are essential, said Dr Saraf. Should Indians be worried about pneumonic plague? The general public has no reason to panic just because pneumonic plague is being discussed. Plague is rare today, although it has not disappeared completely. India has experienced plague outbreaks in the past, but that does not mean every respiratory infection or fever should be viewed as plague, Dr Sarf told indianexpress.com. Awareness rather than alarm helps. Those who have a relevant history of exposure to rodents, fleas, sick or dead animals, or a confirmed case of pneumonic plague should seek medical attention if they develop sudden fever and rapidly worsening respiratory symptoms, said Dr Saraf. The Pneumonic Plague that just escaped a lab in Russia is about 100x deadlier than COVID - Todd Hagopian Stagnation Assassin ToddHagopian October 5, 2026 What precautions should people take? Basic precautions remain important. Avoid handling sick or dead animals, particularly rodents, and maintain good hygiene. If someone has a suspected or confirmed pneumonic infection,minimise close contact and follow appropriaterespiratory precautions. Most importantly, do not self-medicate with antibiotics. If sudden fever is accompanied by breathlessness or a rapidly worsening cough, do not delay medical evaluation. Early diagnosis and appropriate treatment can make a significant difference in the outcome, said Dr Saraf. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

articleTitle: The universe whispers through ghost particles
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The universe whispers through ghost particles
description: His work has used neutrinos to probe some of the universe’s hitherto most inaccessible environments, helping open a new window on the cosmos.
body_raw: For centuries, astronomy has essentially been the science of observing light. However, some of the universes most consequential events take place in environments so dense or violent that photons cannot escape. Could the universe be observed through something other than light? In 1930, when Austrian physicist Wolfgang Pauli proposed the existence of an elusive particle to explain a mystery in radioactive decay, he was laying the foundations for a new way of exploring the cosmos. The ghost particle called the neutrino was detected two decades later, and the quest to understand it has since been rewarded with a string of Nobel Prizes. On Tuesday, the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, which awards the Nobel Prize in Physics, recognised another pioneer in the field - Belgian-American astrophysicist Francis Halzen. His work has used neutrinos to probe some of the universes hitherto most inaccessible environments, helping open a new window on the cosmos. Neutrinos have tiny masses, carry no electric charge and interact so weakly with matter that billions pass through the Earth - and our bodies - without leaving a trace. These particles can escape from the dense interiors of exploding stars and other extreme cosmic environments, carrying information about places that conventional telescopes cannot see. Halzen recognised this potential. His pioneering work led to the IceCube Observatory, an enormous neutrino detector buried deep beneath the Antarctic ice. Rather than building a conventional telescope, scientists effectively turned a cubic kilometre of natural ice at the South Pole into a detector, embedding more than 5,000 optical sensors in it. Almost every neutrino passes straight through the ice. But on the rare occasion when one sheds its shyness, the resulting flash of light can give information on the particles travel path. In 2013, IceCube provided evidence for a flux of high-energy neutrinos originating beyond the solar system. Halzens work demonstrated that sometimes the way to see farther is not to build a more powerful eye, but to learn to detect what the universe is whispering through particles that pass silently through it. The next frontier is multi-messenger astronomy, in which neutrinos can be studied alongside light, gravitational waves and cosmic rays. Together, these cosmic messengers could reveal the workings of black holes, exploding stars and other extreme objects that remain invisible to any single form of observation.

articleTitle: Why did actors Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder protest Netanyahu outside UN?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Susan Sarandon, center, and other demonstrators are arrested ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahus address at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, Thursday, September 24, 2026, in New York. (AP Photo)
description: Sarandon and Einbinder were among more than 100 people detained after protesters blocked a street outside the UN during Netanyahu’s visit.
body_raw: Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon and Hacks star Hannah Einbinder were among more than 100 people detained by New York police during a protest against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu outside the United Nations on Thursday. The protesters were objecting primarily to Israels military campaign in Gaza and continued US military support for Israel, as Netanyahu prepared to address the UN General Assembly. The demonstration was organised by Jewish Voice for Peace, which said its demands included ending US arms supplies to Israel and stopping the war in Gaza. Einbinder, who is Jewish, said she took part because she viewed speaking out against Israels actions in Gaza as a moral responsibility. Sarandon, meanwhile, joined demonstrators wearing a T-shirt reading Fund people, not bombs as protesters chanted Let Gaza live, stop arming Israel. Why were the actors protesting Netanyahu? The immediate trigger was Netanyahus appearance at the UN, but the protest was broader than opposition to the Israeli prime minister personally. Jewish Voice for Peace said the demonstration was intended to demand that the US stop arming Israel and end what the group describes as genocide in Gaza. The organisation said about 400 Jewish, Palestinian, Iranian and Lebanese New Yorkers took part in the sit-in. Dozens of protesters, including actor Susan Sarandon, were detained by police in New York after staging a sit-in in the roadway to demand an end to US arms supplies to Israel pic.twitter.comPM7fpJdaLv - Reuters Reuters September 25, 2026 Protesters carried signs reading Stop Arming Israel and End the Genocide, while many wore white T-shirts with the message Fund People Not Bombs. They blocked First Avenue near the UN headquarters and remained in the street after police ordered them to disperse. Manijeh Moradian, a university professor who participated in the protest, told news agency Reuters that the destruction in Gaza was being carried out in our name, with our tax dollars and argued that Netanyahu should not use the UN platform to justify Israels actions. What did Hannah Einbinder say? Einbinder has previously spoken publicly about Palestinians and Israel. During her Emmy acceptance speech in 2025, she voiced support for Palestine. She also spoke about the issue at the Cannes Film Festival in 2026, saying the personal or professional cost of speaking out could not be weighed against a human life. At Thursdays protest, Einbinder said she was participating as a Jew, as an American, and as a human, describing opposition to the Israeli governments actions in Gaza as a moral responsibility. After her detention, she said in an Instagram statement that she wanted attention to remain on the war and its consequences rather than on the celebrities who had been arrested. She referred to the destruction in Gaza, settler attacks, home demolitions and airstrikes. Why was Susan Sarandon arrested? Sarandon, 79, joined the sit-in outside the UN ahead of Netanyahus speech. Reuters footage showed her among demonstrators wearing the Fund people, not bombs shirt and chanting against US support for Israel. Reuters reported that police arrested at least 30 protesters in its initial account. New York police later told CNN that 103 people were taken into custody as officers cleared protesters blocking First Avenue. Jewish Voice for Peace said more than 104 people were arrested. What were protesters objecting to? The protest centred on three connected issues - Israels military campaign in Gaza, which protesters accused Israel of conducting at the expense of Palestinian civilians, US military and financial support for Israel, with demonstrators calling for Washington to stop supplying weapons and Netanyahus appearance at the UN, which organisers argued gave him an international platform despite the allegations and controversy surrounding Israels conduct in Gaza. What happened inside the UN? The protest outside coincided with Netanyahus address to the General Assembly. During his speech, Netanyahu defended Israels actions in Gaza and rejected allegations that Israel was committing genocide. He also defended the US-Israeli military action against Iran and criticised his opponents. Dozens of delegates walked out as he began speaking. Netanyahu also criticised the protesters outside the UN, questioning why they had not protested against Irans crackdown on demonstrators earlier in the year. Why the actors involvement drew attention Alongside Sarandon and Einbinder, celebrities including Elliot Page, Cynthia Nixon, Chelsea Manning, Glennon Doyle, Sarah Sherman, Lucy Dacus and Julien Baker participated, according to Jewish Voice for Peace. With inputs from agencies

articleTitle: Stalker attacks Pune corporate employee, smashes her phone for refusing marriage
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pimpri-Chinchwad police initiate deportation of 26-year-old Afghan national Danyar Hussain for overstaying after visa expiry in Pune
description: The accused allegedly stalked the woman both physically and over phone calls to pressure her into marriage.
body_raw: A 29-year-old man allegedly intercepted a 24-year-old woman, assaulted her and destroyed her mobile phone in Punes Chinchwad area Saturday after she refused to marry him. The woman, who works at a corporate firm, lodged an FIR at the Chinchwad police station following the assault. The police identified the accused as Rohan Rajendra Kamble, also a resident of Chinchwad. According to a press release issued by the police on Sunday, the accused allegedly stalked the victim both physically and over phone calls to pressure her into marriage. When the woman rejected his advances, the accused allegedly grew upset and attacked her. The incident occurred around 3 pm in Bijli Nagar, Chinchwad. The police said that Kamble intercepted the woman, thrashed her, and smashed her cell phone against a hard surface to destroy it. Following the attack, the victim approached the police to file a complaint. Sub Inspector Mohini Dongre, the investigating officer, confirmed that the police have launched a search to locate the accused. The complainant works with a corporate company. The accused and complainant are residents of the same area hence, they know each other. Prima facie probe revealed that the complainant was not willing to marry the accused, so he committed the offence. Further investigation is on, Sub Inspector Dongre said. Kamble has been charged with stalking, voluntarily causing hurt, and mischief causing property damage.

articleTitle: ‘Gyanesh Kumar must turn approver’: Rahul Gandhi on Express investigation
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rahul Gandhi during a press conference in New Delhi on Thursday.
description: Addressing a press conference on Thursday, he started by showing video clips of speeches by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, in which they are seen saying how the BJP will remain in power for a long time.
body_raw: As the Opposition stepped up its demand for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and planned to move a motion in Parliament for his removal in the wake of The Indian Express report on multiple objections by the two Election Commissioners to SIR-related decisions taken without their knowledge, Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi claimed Thursday that all elections were being rigged in the country. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Gandhi said, Our elections are fundamentally broken. The sacred belief in elections, he said, was dying. If tomorrow, the BJP sweeps elections, no one will believe it, he said. He made these remarks even as Congress sources said the Opposition will soon move a motion in both houses of Parliament to remove Kumar as the CEC. The motion is being drafted with legal experts and we will soon submit notices in both Houses on behalf of the joint Opposition, the sources said. Referring to The Indian Express report, Gandhi showed video clips of speeches by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah in which they say the BJP will remain in power for a long time. I come from a political family. No political leader can say or make such statements. In India, there is a force called anti-incumbency. It doesnt spare anybody. Indira Gandhiji won the Bangladesh war. And within a year or two, massive anti-incumbency. The same happens to leader after leader. For some reason, it doesnt happen to Narendra Modi, Mr Shah, BJP, he said. States swing. We can understand the popularity of a person, the performance of a government. But we cant understand how anti-incumbency disappears. It doesnt exist in North Korea. There is no democracy where anti-incumbency doesnt work. We are looking for answers to where it went here. And we have found answers, he said. He said the laws are made by people chosen through votes. If the vote has been destroyed, then our Constitution has been destroyed. It no longer has power. If our Constitution is destroyed, our laws are illegal, and our institutions are attacked. The sacred belief in elections is dying. If tomorrow, the BJP sweeps elections, no one will believe it, he said. We have been saying it again and again that there is a problem with the vote. The Election Commission is the institutional protector of this vote. It is their responsibility to protect the vote, he said, adding, all elections are being rigged. Gandhi recalled how the Prime Minister and the Home Minister bypassed his opinion to elevate Gyanesh Kumar as the CEC. Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi were appointed under a 2023 Act by a selection panel comprising the Prime Minister, the Home Minister and the Leader of the Opposition. In March 2024, the Opposition member, Congresss Adhir Chowdhury, recorded a dissent over the appointment process when Sandhu and Kumar were named Election Commissioners. In February 2025, Gandhi recorded his dissent when Kumar was elevated as CEC. We are sitting in a place where we have never been. Our elections are fundamentally broken. And this is the first time in independent India that we are here, he said. Demanding Kumars resignation, Gandhi said, This thing you have done is against the Indian nation. This is an attack against the Constitution. There are going to be consequences to this. We are not going to let democracy be destroyed. The two Election Commissioners have done a wise thing. I appreciate it. Mr Kumar should turn approver. That would be an act of nationalism. We know what has happened, and we will reveal it, he said. The Prime Minister and Home Minister, he said, should be investigated. They are at the top of the conspiracy. This is an act against the Indian state and its people. We cant sit silently, he said. Calling a person who attacks the vote a deshdrohi traitor, he said, I am not saying this lightly. For three years, I have been saying this. I have used facts. The fact is that the Prime Minister and the Home Minister have attacked the democratic architecture of this country. He described Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi as patriots, and said remaining silent will be anti-national.

articleFeaturedImageAlt: UPSC Mains Answer Practice — GS 2
description: UPSC Civil Services Mains Exam 2027: This week’s GS 2 answer practice explores the role of community participation in water governance and Legislative privileges. Check out our thought process.
body_raw: UPSC Essentialsbrings to you its initiative for the practice ofMains answer writing.It covers essential topics of static and dynamic parts of the UPSC Civil Services syllabus covered under various GS papers. This answer-writing practice is designed to help you as a value addition to your UPSC CSE Mains. Attempt todays answer writing on questions related to topics ofGS-2to check your progress. As we mark the 3rd anniversary of the UPSC Essentials magazine, we thank our readers for being part of this journey. Your trust, feedback and continued support have shaped the magazine and encouraged us to keep improving with every edition. Click Here to read the UPSC Essentials magazine for September 2026. QUESTION 1 How can decentralisation and community participation improve the effectiveness and sustainability of water governance in India? QUESTION 2 Legislative privileges are intended to secure the effective functioning of legislatures, not to insulate them from public scrutiny. Discuss. QUESTION 1 How can decentralisation and community participation improve the effectiveness and sustainability of water governance in India? Relevance The question links with GS Paper 2 Governance, decentralisation, local self-government and participatory governance. It also provides scope to discuss cooperative federalism and multi-level governance in addressing water challenges. NoteThis is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. Introduction - Indias water challenge is multifaceted, encompassing not only infrastructure development but also governance, institutional capacity, and sustainable service delivery. - The Gujarat example demonstrates that water security improves when governance, infrastructure, and community ownership are pursued simultaneously. Body You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer Role of decentralisation and community participation - Water-related decisions can be decentralised to reflect local variables such as availability, quality, location, and household requirements. The notion of subsidiarity states that functions should be carried out at the lowest appropriate level. This strategy is used by Gujarats WASMO and other similar initiatives. - Institutions like Pani Samitis can help communities become active participants rather than passive beneficiaries. The Gujarat model demonstrates how local water governance institutions, with suitable infrastructure and external aid, may improve water conservation, harvesting, and recharge. - Decentralisation can improve operation and maintenance since local institutions are directly involved in water system management. This is especially critical as the task switches from simply providing tap connections to guaranteeing consistent, adequate, and dependable water service. - Community participation can assist ensure that taps are accompanied by steps to protect the underlying water source. Groundwater recharging, rainwater collection, and water supply must all be addressed simultaneously, rather than considering water provision as a standalone engineering project. - When local communities participate in planning and implementation, they can check service quality and continuity, as well as file grievances. This can help close the gap between administrative claims of infrastructure coverage and real service delivery on the ground. - Water availability and infrastructure requirements vary greatly by region. Local institutions can tailor responses to local hydrological and socioeconomic conditions rather than depending solely on centrally designed techniques. Conclusion - Effective water administration necessitates a shift from a centralized, infrastructure-centric strategy to participatory and decentralized service governance. Indias experience, particularly the Gujarat model and the developing Jal Jeevan Mission strategy, illustrates that infrastructure becomes more sustainable when people play an active role in planning, managing, and monitoring water systems. - Thus, decentralization can transform water governance from a government-provided function to a shared institutional and community duty. Sources From India to Global South, a Gujarat water-governance model, Many challenges of Jal Jeevan Mission Decentralisation is the only way ahead, Centre asks district collectors to regularly review Jal Jeevan Mission works, address gaps Points to Ponder What institutional mechanisms can facilitate effective participation in water management? What are the major challenges to decentralised water governance in India? Related Previous Year Question What are environmental pressure groups? Discuss their role in raising awareness, influencing policies and advocating for environmental protection in India. 2025 QUESTION 2 Legislative privileges are intended to secure the effective functioning of legislatures, not to insulate them from public scrutiny. Discuss. Relevance The question directly relates to GS Paper 2 Parliament and State Legislatures, constitutional provisions and legislative privileges. It helps to analyse the role of legislative privileges in preserving parliamentary functioning while protecting democratic scrutiny. NoteThis is not a model UPSC answer. It only provides you with a thought process which you may incorporate into the answers. Introduction - Legislative privileges are constitutional provisions designed to ensure that Parliament and state legislatures may carry out their tasks independently and effectively. - Articles 105 and 194 provide privileges and immunities to Parliament and State Legislatures respectively. However, these privileges are meant to facilitate legislative functioning, not create an unrestricted sphere of immunity from constitutional scrutiny or legitimate public criticism. Body You may incorporate some of the following points in your answer Why are legislative privileges necessary? - Privileges protect legislators from external interference and enable them to participate freely in legislative proceedings. Article 1051 provides freedom of speech in Parliament, subject to the Constitution and parliamentary rules corresponding protection exists under Article 194 for State Legislatures. - Collective privileges allow Houses to govern their proceedings and deal with conduct that disrupts their operation. - Immunities enable lawmakers to carry out their constitutional duties without fear of legal ramifications from valid legislative speech or voting. Why cant privileges be used as a barrier against scrutiny? - The Supreme Court must decide whether privileges under Articles 105 and 194 can supersede fundamental rights like free speech and expression under Article 191a. The position made before the Court is that privileges exist to defend the Houses operation rather than the reputations of MPs, governments, or ruling parties. - India adheres to constitutional supremacy rather than the model of unrestrained parliamentary authority. As a result, legislative privileges function within the constitutional framework and cannot automatically take precedence over fundamental rights. - The Supreme Courts jurisprudence has gradually acknowledged limits to legislative privilege. In Raja Ram Pal 2007, the Court determined that the exercise of parliamentary privilege is subject to judicial review. In Amarinder Singh 2010, it was determined that privilege could not be utilised to punish conduct unrelated to the operation of the House. - When privilege proceedings culminate in the arrest or imprisonment of citizens or journalists, Articles 14 and 21 are invoked alongside Article 19. The exercise of legislative power over personal liberty creates issues of fairness, due process, and arbitrariness. - A free press allows individuals to monitor legislative activity. The 2003 Tamil Nadu Assembly privilege event, which involved actions against journalists from The Hindu and Murasoli, exemplifies the conflict between legislative privilege and press freedom. The Supreme Court suspended the arrest warrants and referred serious constitutional matters related to Articles 1943 and 191a for review. Conclusion - Legislative privilege is a tool for protecting legislative democracy, not an end in itself. Its credibility is ultimately tied to the legislatures ability to function effectively. - A constitutional balance must consequently protect legislative authority while ensuring that privilege is not used to repress valid criticism, journalistic freedom, or fundamental rights. Such a balance strengthens, not diminishes, the authority of democratic institutions. Sources Legislative privileges vs free speech The question before Supreme Court, JMM bribes for votes ruling How Supreme Court interpreted privilege for lawmakers, Article 105 of Constitution The limits to free speech in Parliament, and what Supreme Court has ruled Points to Ponder How do Articles 105 and 194 protect the functioning of Parliament and State Legislatures? Related Previous Year Question The Powers, Privileges and Immunities of Parliament and its Members as envisaged in Article 105 of the Constitution leave room for a large number of un-codified and un-enumerated privileges to continue. Assess the reasons for the absence of legal codification of the parliamentary privileges. articleTitle: Rajinikanth sent Rs 45 lakhs, worked for free in Pedarayudu to save Mohan Babu’s career
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajinikanth and Mohan Babu in Pedarayudu
description: In 1994, Mohan Babu was at the lowest point of his career. Rajinikanth found him a story, secured the remake rights, sent money when funds ran out and appeared in the film without charging a rupee. Three decades later, Mohan Babu is still going strong.
body_raw: The story of how Pedarayudu got made is, in many ways, more dramatic than the film itself. It involves a veteran Telugu actor at rock bottom, a Tamil superstar at the peak of his powers, Rs 45 lakhs sent without a contract, a cameo performed without a fee and a friendship that turned a career-ending crisis into the biggest hit of a lifetime. In 1994, Mohan Babu had nothing. By June 1995, he had Pedarayudu, a blockbuster and a career that would last another three decades. The man who made all of it possible was Rajinikanth. By the early 1990s, Mohan Babu had been in the Telugu film industry for nearly two decades. He had debuted with Swargam Narakam under the guidance of his mentor Dasari Narayana Rao, who had rechristened him from Manchu Bhakthavatsalam Naidu to Mohan Babu. Over the following years, he had built a career spanning over 200 films, earning a reputation as a dependable, versatile performer who could carry action entertainers, family dramas and comedy films with equal ease. But by 1993-94, the career had hit a wall. A string of action entertainers had flopped consecutively, leading to collapse of the box office returns. Mohan Babu needed a film that would not just perform at the box office but fundamentally reset his career. Also Read Meet the Original Gangsters Rajinikanth and Mohan Babu Rajinikanth finds the film In 1994, a Tamil film called Nattamai, directed by KS Ravikumar and starring Sarathkumar in a dual role, became a runaway hit in Tamil Nadu. The rural family drama, written by Erode Sounder, was a tightly constructed emotional entertainer about a village patriarch navigating family disputes, land conflicts and generational tensions. It was the kind of story that travelled across languages because its emotional core was universal family, duty, honour and the weight of being the person everyone turns to. Rajinikanth watched Nattamai and immediately thought of Mohan Babu. He called his friend and told him to watch the film, believing it would work as a Telugu remake and, more importantly, believing the role of the patriarch would suit Mohan Babus strengths as a performer. And Mohan Babu agreed. But wanting to remake a hit Tamil film and being able to acquire the rights were two different things, especially for an actor whose recent track record gave him no bargaining power. The remake rights to Nattamai were held by producer RB Choudary. According to multiple telugu reports, Sr NTR himself was in the running to remake the film, which meant Mohan Babu was competing for rights against one of the most powerful names in Telugu cinema history. Before I went to meet Choudary, Rajinikanth already passed the message, Mohan Babu recalled in a 2020 interview marking the films 25th anniversary. So, the producer didnt utter a word and offered remake rights. I could get the rights only because of my friend Rajinikanth. Also Read Rajinikanth, Nani, Jackie Shroff, Brahmanandam attend event celebrating 50 years of Mohan Babu. See photos, videos Mohan Babu started production on Pedarayudu under his own banner, Sree Lakshmi Prasanna Pictures. He hired director Ravi Raja Pinisetty, known as a remake specialist who could adapt Tamil films for Telugu audiences with precision. Music director Koti was brought on board. The cast included Bhanupriya and Soundarya in prominent roles. A young Manchu Manoj, Mohan Babus son, played a role as a child artist. As money ran out during the shoot, Mohan Babu, who was already at the lowest point of his career, had no provisions to arrange the money.What happened next has become one of the most frequently told stories about Rajinikanth in the Telugu film industry. Rajinikanth sent Mohan Babu Rs 45 lakhs. The instruction that came with it was equally direct finish the film. Return the money once the film starts earning. Rajinikanth did not stop at the money. He agreed to appear in Pedarayudu in a special role as Paparayudu, and he did it without charging any remuneration. In 1995, Rajinikanth was the highest-paid actor in South Indian cinema. He showed up on Mohan Babus set and worked for free. The commercial value of Rajinikanths name on the poster was enormous. For distributors and exhibitors who were being asked to buy rights to a Mohan Babu film after a string of flops, the guarantee that Rajinikanth appeared in the film changed the risk calculation entirely. It was not just a Mohan Babu film anymore. It was a Mohan Babu film with Rajinikanth in it. That distinction, in 1995, was worth crores. Also Read Rajinikanth, Mohan Babu share adorable moment on Hyderabad-bound flight, see photo Pedarayudu released in 1995, and became one of the biggest Telugu hits of the year. It was classified as an industry hit, a term the trade reserves for films that perform at the highest commercial level across all territories. Mohan Babus career was saved. The financial crisis was resolved. The bag of money was returned. And the friendship that made it all possible continued for another three decades.

articleTitle: ‘Your money is Ata Pata Laapata’: Supreme Court to Rajpal Yadav in cheque bounce case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Supreme Court Rajpal Yadav
description: The Supreme Court directed actor Rajpal Yadav to deposit Rs 2 crore by October 13 in a long-running series of cheque bounce cases.
body_raw: The Supreme Court on Wednesday took note of actor Rajpal Yadav arranging Rs 1.15 crore in a long-running cheque bounce case and told him to make some good movies to entertain people that will rebuild his image. A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing the actors plea in connection with cheque bounce cases in which the Delhi High Court sentenced him to three months imprisonment. The court directed the actor to deposit Rs 2 crore by October 13. During the hearing, the actor produced demand drafts of Rs 1.15 crore, and the court was told that the remaining Rs 85 lakh would be paid by a prospective buyer of his property. The petitioner has finally brought demand drafts in the sum of Rs 1.15 crore, which is directed to be deposited with the Registry during the course of the day. As regards Rs 85 lakh, the petitioner claims that the prospective buyer of his property is present in Court. Mr Anant Prakash Yadav is present in Court and he is willing to pay a sum of Rs 85 lakh. He is willing to deposit the sum of Rs 85 lakh by way of demand draft with the registry on October 13, the CJI said while dictating the order. The CJI also made a light-hearted remark, Your money is Ata Pata Laapata, gayab. During the hearing, actor Yadav, who personally appeared before the court, said that he had suffered losses of around Rs 250 crore over the past 13 years, including Rs 17 crore in the dispute arising from his film Ata Pata Laapata. He said that although the total amount involved was around Rs 22 crore, the dispute over a cheque of about Rs 5 crore had resulted in his losing Rs 17 crore and had also caused substantial damage to his branding and career. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant struck a lighter note and advised Yadav to rebuild his image by making a good film and entertaining audiences again. Koi achi si movie banake logo ko dobara entertain karo. Aapki image dobara ban jaegi. Humare yahan kuch advocate bhi ache actor hain, unko bhi role de dijye, the CJI said. Make a good movie and entertain people again. Your image will be rebuilt. We also have some lawyers here who are good actors give them roles as well What happened in the previous hearings? The Supreme Court had earlier allowed Yadavs request for a last opportunity to deposit Rs 2 crore with its registry as part payment toward clearing dues owed to a production house. A three-judge bench, presided over by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, had also extended Yadavs interim protection from surrendering until October 5 in connection with cheque bounce cases in which the Delhi High Court sentenced him to three months imprisonment. Before that the Supreme Court had granted Yadav exemption from surrendering on the condition that he deposit Rs 5 crore with its registry. The senior counsel had stated that Yadav plans to dispose of some immovable properties belonging to his mother to raise the money. He promised the actor would deposit at least Rs 2 crore of the outstanding dues in court by then and present a concrete proposal to settle the remaining amount. Cheque-bounce case against Rajpal Yadav Recalling what led to the ongoing dispute, the complainant alleged that in 2013, Yadav tendered seven cheques of Rs 1.05 crore each to settle financial assistance of Rs 5 crore for a film in 2010. The cheques were, however, dishonoured. Subsequently, an agreement was reached between the parties in 2012, stating that the actor, his wife, and their company would repay around Rs 11 crore, including interest. However, that repayment has also yet to occur.

articleTitle: Richer than Shah Rukh, maker of Rs 4,000 cr Ramayana is worth Rs 16,000 cr: Hurun list
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Naresh Malhotra and family of Prime Focus, the banner behind the Rs 4,000 crore Ramayana, saw their wealth rise 279 per cent to Rs 16,000 crore.
description: Namit Malhotra has previously claimed that the budget of Ramayana is Rs 4,000 crore. His family's net worth currently stands at Rs 16,000 crore.
body_raw: Namit Malhotra, who is producing Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana, comes from one of the wealthiest families in India and as per the recent Hurun India Rich List 2026, the family has witnessed a 279 percent spike in their wealth. His father, Naresh Malhotra, who owns the visual effects company Prime Focus, and the family are now worth Rs 16,000 crore. This takes the Malhotra family to the 232nd spot on the list. It may be recalled that the Hurun Global Rich List 2026, released earlier this year, had positioned Namit Malhotra at the 3,306th spot, with an estimated net worth exceeding Rs 9,204 crore. Must Read Hanuman Ansh director did film for free, will now make over Rs 50 cr film earns Rs 366 cr Who are Namit Malhotra and Naresh Malhotra? A film producer and visual effects entrepreneur, Namit is the eldest son of film producer Naresh Malhotra, renowned for bankrolling movies like Shashi Kapoors Duniya Meri Jeb Mein 1979, Amitabh Bachchans Shahenshah 1988, and Debu Boses Sahari Bagha 1985. According to ET Now, Namit commenced his entrepreneurial journey in 1995 with a video workshop set up in his fathers garage. He subsequently merged his company with Nareshs production banner, Video Works, and their combined venture was named Prime Focus. The firm later expanded to London, New York City, Los Angeles, and Vancouver. Prime Focus subsequently merged with Double Negative DNEG, a UK-based visual effects studio. For the uninitiated, DNEG did the visual effects for Oscar-winning films such as Inception, Interstellar, Dune and Dune Part Two. Namit Malhotra currently serves as DNEGs chairman and CEO. Ramayanas Rs 4,000 crore budget Mounted on a total budget of Rs 4,000 crore, the Ramayana franchises first instalment will hit screens worldwide on the occasion of this years Diwali. In an earlier chat with Prakhar Gupta on his YouTueb channel, Namit had shared, So, when we set out to make it 6-7 years ago, just after the pandemic, when we started to really get serious about mounting it and producing it, and budget-wise, it was like everybody thought Im a lunatic. Because no Indian film, by a long distance, comes close to it. So, to put it simply, itll be about 500 million by the time were done, on both films put together, part one and part two, which is over Rs 4,000 crore. Starring Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Yash as Ravana, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, and Sunny Deol as Hanuman, Ramayan features music by Hans Zimmer and AR Rahman.

articleTitle: ‘Constructed controversy’: Swara Bhasker addresses backlash over Padmaavat jauhar remarks
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Swara Bhasker Padmaavat Controversy
description: In an exclusive interview, actress Swara Bhasker weighed in on the recent Padmaavat controversy and said it was consciously 'constructed'.
body_raw: Swara Bhasker has never shied away from expressing her views on contentious issues. While her opinions have often landed her in controversies, the actor has always stood by what she has said. Before entering Rise and Fall 2, Swara spoke exclusively to SCREEN about the recent Padmaavat controversy, which she described as constructed. She also claimed that several trolls make money by targeting her online. Swara Bhasker reacts to the Padmaavat controversy Recently, Swara Bhasker faced severe backlash over comments about the jauhar scene in Padmaavat. Sharing her side of the story, she said, I dont understand. This is a 9- or 10-year-old controversy. I have already got the same gaalis for it in 2018 when that open letter came out. Now Im only answering a question about what the open letter was for, which I have already been abused for, and the controversy is done and dusted. Now, again, youre angry about the same thing that you were angry about 10 years ago. I dont get it. And youre not just misconstruing. You are lying about what I said. She further added, Earlier, I thought they didnt understand English, so I said it in Hindi. I said that if I had been a rape survivor and I watched that glorification, I would feel like a coward. Im saying I would feel like a coward. Even major media channels, for Gods sake, are reporting that Swara Bhaskar calls jauhar an act of cowardice or the jauhar women are cowards. Honestly, I felt that was a constructed controversy. There was an organized, very self-conscious sort of decision to keep that controversy alive. Also Read Swara Bhasker I already act for a living, I cannot act in my political views View this post on Instagram A post shared by Swara Bhasker reallyswara Swara said the episode was not an isolated one, claiming that several controversies involving her in recent years have been deliberately manufactured and amplified. I have said the same thing many times in many interviews. There are other clips of me also on the internet saying the same thing. Nothing happened at that time. So how did people get angry all of a sudden? It felt very shady. And in general, Ive noticed this trend. We all know now that there are IT cells of various political parties. I really feel that all these kinds of controversies of mine, especially in recent years and the last few weeks, are all constructed and being pushed because other agendas are being conducted on the shoulders of my controversies. She added, Some people are getting jobs in my name. They spent the whole day training the army, doing the same thing that is to troll Swara Bhasker. I always say to people, if your job is coming out of having my name in the headlines and lying about me, misquoting me, constantly naming me and harassing me, targeting me, then kindly send a Diwali hamper this year with a thank you note. Sharing who she feels is behind these constructed attacks, the actress said, Its very obvious, right? We know which IT cell is the strongest, has the most money, and is the most powerful. Its obviously them. It takes away from all the criticism thats happening on their side right now. Swara Bhaskers Padmaavat controversy Recently, a clip from her appearance at the Woman, Life, Freedom talk in Delhi went viral. In the video, Swara Bhaskert was seen answering a question about the open letter she wrote to Sanjay Leela Bhansali, slamming the jauhar scene in Padmaavat. However, Swaras remarks were construed as her calling the practice of jauhar cowardly or referring to Queen Padmavati as a coward. At the event, Swara had said, Im watching this, these 800 women committing jauhar, and I was like, yaar, if I had been, God forbid, if I was a rape survivor, what is this film telling me? I would feel like a coward, that I didnt kill myself to save my honour. Is that what you want to tell in a society like ours, where I feel like theres a rape epidemic? Is this what we want to tell our survivors, that you didnt deserve to live? That if you actually had been honourable and brave women, you would have killed yourself. Are we saying that rape is the end of a womans life? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Swara Bhasker reallyswara She further explained, And then there was that one shot it made me so mad, I was like, chiii, in the audience loudly. There is a close-up of a pregnant womans belly. And she is going, so youre saying that a foetus that might be female doesnt deserve to be born, because she might be raped by a Muslim ruler? Clarifying her remarks, Swara posted a video on social media and said, This morning, a clip of mine has been going viral on social media. It was from an event yesterday, where I was asked why I had sent an open letter to Sanjay Leela Bhansali after watching Padmaavat. While explaining what my issue was, I said something that is now being completely mistranslated and spread falsely, claiming that I had said that Rani Padmavati and the other women who committed Jauhar were cowards. I want to make it absolutely clear that I did not say that Rani Padmavati was a coward or that the other women in the palace were cowards. Those who want to abuse me, go ahead, but at least abuse me for the right thing. What I had said was that while watching the climax, I thought, God forbid, if I were a rape survivor, I would feel like a coward for not having taken my own life - that if I had survived after being raped, I would feel like a coward, Swara concluded. Disclaimer This story contains commentary and personal views expressed by a public figure regarding past controversies. The comments are presented for informational purposes only.

articleTitle: Punjab Kings teammate decodes change in Iyer’s hitting technique: ‘When Shreyas came at the start…’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Iyer
description: Recalling his own bowling experience against Iyer, the bowler said: "When I bowled to him in the nets, I had to bowl wider, or else he used to easily hit me over cover for a six
body_raw: One standout aspect of Shreyas Iyers century on Tuesday was his ability to accelerate after reaching his half-century, which he reached in 26 deliveries, and scoring the next 50 runs in just 16 deliveries. His power-hitting and technique seemed quite flawless against the spinners. His Punjab Kings teammate, Yuzvendra Chahal, decoded what has changed in Iyers approach to his innings. Definitely, attacking the mind. When Shreyas came at the start, he used to go back and play the cut. Now he comes across, and if the midwicket fielder is up, he has that option as well. If you bowl outside the off-stump, his reach is so good that he plays over cover and mid-off. So, the bowler gets slightly stuck there as to what he should do when he is not getting any help from the wicket, the Punjab Kings PBKS bowler said on Star Sports. Recalling his own bowling experience against Iyer, Chahal said When I bowled to him in the nets, I had to bowl wider, or else he used to easily hit me over cover for a six. One or one-and-a-half years ago, he used to hit hard, but nowadays he times the ball, and thats the specialty because of which his batting has improved so much, he added. Batters go back and across toward the off-stump, but he was going outside the off-stump because he knew Shepherd would try to bowl only outside the off-stump. Thats why he played the lofted extra cover drive and lofted off-drive. He read the bowlers mind, and thats why he was able to get into those positions. Brilliant batting, sensational batting, former batting legend Sunil Gavaskar elaborated on the same show. Iyers century helped India beat West Indies by eight wickets, chasing a target of 172 runs in 14.4 overs. If its your day, make sure that you win the match for the team. And today it was me. Previous couple of games, it was the batsmen who finished off the game. So yeah, overall I feel it was a comprehensive performance, and I think if we continue with the same mindset, we will be one of the destructive teams in T20s, Iyer said.

articleTitle: AISA chief Neha Bora among 120 detained on Day 3 of protest against CEC
articleFeaturedImageAlt: neha bora
description: The protest came a day after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment while covering the stir near Jantar Mantar.
body_raw: Around 120 protesters, including All India Students Association AISA president Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav, were detained for several hours on Sunday as the protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision SIR of voter rolls entered its third consecutive day. The protest came a day after three women journalists accused Delhi Police officers of sexual harassment while covering the stir near Jantar Mantar. On Sunday, while some protested against CEC Kumar, others attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar to demand accountability and a probe into the journalists allegations of sexual assault. Bora was detained while leading a march from Andhra Bhavan Canteen towards Jantar Mantar. The march saw participation from civil society activists such as Yadav, student protesters and political parties like the Indian Youth Congress IYC and the AAP. This has just started and many organisations are now joining this, we wont stop. Even though the Jantar Mantar is closed, were on the streets, even women are here to reclaim them. This is the power of common people. Jab tak Gyanesh Kumar ki chhutti nahi hoti, hum chhutti nahi karnege Until Gyanesh Kumar takes a leave, we will not take a leave, Yadav said while marching towards Jantar Mantar. Flags waved and slogans of Gyanesh has to go pierced the air as the crowd split into groups and moved towards Ashoka Road. With the protest entering its third day, Lutyens Delhi was heavily fortified, with elaborate security arrangements in place since morning. A large fleet of buses and riot action vehicles had been deployed on multiple lanes, and movement on several roads leading to Jantar Mantar and the Parliament Street police station was restricted. The Delhi Police also closed the stretch between Ashoka Road and Parliament Street near Jantar Mantar, while prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita BNSS were already put across the New Delhi district. At around 4 pm, as the march progressed towards Jantar Mantar, barricades were put up. When a few protesters tried to cross them, the police began detaining them. Bora was detained in a car by officers, but the vehicle remained stuck for over 20 minutes as protesters stood around it to prevent it from moving. Ashoka Road remained shut and traffic was halted until 6.30 pm as the protests continued. Amid the chaos, police kept detaining protesters, including AISA activists and members of other left-wing parties. As one police bus filled with detainees pulled away, the next quickly took its place in line. Teams of four to five officers lifted and carried protesters to the buses, while some tried to break the bus windows to get out. Even as detentions continued, people kept protesting. Traffic resumed briefly on the roundabout, but police carried on detaining protesters as their numbers grew. According to police sources, around 120 people, including AISA, AAP and IYC workers and Yadav, were detained. Bora was taken to Narela police station, police said, adding that all of the protesters were later released. According to police, around half a dozen of their personnel including women staff were also injured while handling the protesters. The injured officers were given first aid at a hospital as well, police said.

articleTitle: Ketan Agarwal death: Probe reveals 2 more who knew of murder plot
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Siya Goyal Ketan Agarwal
description: One was approached for assistance; both later became witnesses
body_raw: TWO PEOPLE, besides Siya Goyal, Chetan Chaudhary and Chetans friend Ritesh Hange, knew about the trios alleged plan to murder Ketan Agarwal and tried to dissuade them from carrying it out, the Pune Rural police probe has revealed. The two - one known to Ritesh and another linked to Siya - have been made witnesses in the case, sources said. The Pune Rural police, probing the June 18 murder of Ketan Agarwal at Lohagad Fort in Punes Maval taluka, arrested his fiance Siya Goyal 20 and Chetan Chaudhary 22 on June 23. Police arrested Chetans friend Ritesh Hange 22 on September 5 for his alleged role in the conspiracy. Last week, the Pune Rural police filed a 5,053-page chargesheet against the trio on charges including murder and criminal conspiracy. Police have also invoked provisions of the Information Technology Act after the probe revealed that the accused allegedly used a fake Instagram account in the name and identity of a fictitious friend of Siya, Mahi, to chat with Ketan and convince him to visit Lohagad Fort on June 18 to celebrate Siyas birthday the following day. Investigation has revealed that two people besides Siya, Chetan and Ritesh knew about the trios plan to murder Ketan Agarwal. One of the two persons is a man known to Ritesh Hange and currently resides outside Maharashtra. He was contacted for his help to harm Ketan. But this person tried to dissuade them from acting on their plan. The second is a person linked to Siya. This person too made attempts to persuade the accused not to execute their plan. Both these persons have been made witnesses in the case and their statements have been recorded and are part of the chargesheet, said an officer from Pune Rural police. What initially appeared to be a tragic accident at Lohagad Fort later emerged as a planned murder, according to the Pune Rural police probe. Investigators have alleged that Ketan, 26, who belonged to a prominent realtor family in Pune, was pushed off a cliff at Lohagad Fort on June 18 as part of a conspiracy allegedly orchestrated by his fiance Siya and Chetan. The two were arrested on June 23. Police said Siya and Ketan got engaged on February 19 and were to marry later this year. However, investigators claim Siya had been in a relationship with Chetan since October last year and was unwilling to go ahead with the marriage. Siya, Chetan and Hange are currently in judicial custody. Pune Rural Superintendent of Police Sandeep Singh Gill had earlier said Hange was arrested after his role in the conspiracy was established. He said investigators found incriminating evidence against him after retrieving deleted data from phone communications between the accused. The probe had earlier revealed that the accused deleted several chats and other communications after the incident. Their seized phones were sent for cyber-forensic analysis. According to officers investigating the case, Siya had earlier derailed a planned pre-wedding shoot with Ketan in Bali by stealing his passport and later discarding it in the washroom of a food mall on the Pune-Mumbai Expressway. Police have also said that days before they allegedly pushed Ketan off the Lohagad Fort cliff on June 18, Siya and Chetan rehearsed how they would execute their alleged plan to murder him. According to police, the rehearsal took place in an open space next to a club lounge in Punes Lulla Nagar area.

articleTitle: How OpenAI’s runaway agents covered their tracks while targeting govt websites
articleFeaturedImageAlt: OpenAI agents
description: Key findings from a new report on the novel tactics used by OpenAI’s agents to erase records or make them inaccessible in order to obscure their activity.
body_raw: OpenAI agents that targeted Australian and US government websites earlier this year, were part of a much broader pattern of rogue agent activity, which included probing dozens of other organisations websites, using sophisticated tactics to try to exfiltrate data, and conceal their traces, according to a new security report. In a report published on Thursday, October 1, Asymmetric Security claimed to have found evidence that 55 additional US government and other websites were probed by OpenAIs agents, including the CDC, International Energy Agency, and Mayo Clinic. These websites were accessed in ways that bypass OpenAIs restrictions between March and September 2026, using only publicly available data, as per the report. Based on a 48-hour investigation, the report highlights the novel tactics used by the agents to erase records or make them inaccessible in order to obscure their hacking attempts. Additionally, the researchers uncovered how the AI agents gained access to private test versions of live government websites and the use of attacker-style reconnaissance tactics. The Asymmetric Security reports findings add another piece to the unsettling picture emerging of what happened in July 2026, when OpenAIs under-testing agents broke out of containment, gained unauthorised access to the internet, and went on a hacking spree. Similar incidents have since been reported by Anthropic, Meta, and Google, with each new case or type of behaviour raising fresh questions about how far AI agents can go once they escape from their sandboxes. Their use of tactics for deliberate subterfuge also makes it harder to rule out that the agents accessed sensitive data, as per the report. Heres a look at new details uncovered by Asymmetric Security researchers about OpenAI agents rogue activity. Key findings from the report Primary motivations The report suggests that limiting web access and imposing other constraints on the agents may have prompted them to devise increasingly elaborate ways to circumvent these restrictions. On a similar note, OpenAI and Google researchers have found evidence that constraints could lead to misalignment and reward hacking type of behaviour by the agents. Tasks assigned to agents Based on their analysis, the researchers said that the rogue AI agents were originally tasked with researching public health and other data, possibly as part of an evaluation. As a result, the agents searched for health and prescription statistics from the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare AIHW trade figures from the UNs Trade and Development Body UNCTAD and university statistics from Data USA, as per the report. Tools used by agents The report found that the AI agents used a host of tools to exfiltrate data from targeted websites and support other activity, including remote browsers such as Wayback Machine, payload hosts, reader services like Common Crawl index, and link shorteners such as tinyurl.com. How it played out As per the evidence seen by the researchers, the agents went beyond searching for official information sources to complete their assigned tasks. They attempted to find exposed configuration files, create accounts, route requests through third-party services, and retrieve results through unintended channels. Mimicking a web browser One of the ways in which agents worked around sandbox restrictions is by using public web tools such as httpbin and urlquery to access websites on their behalf. Httpbin lets developers test how their software communicates with websites while Urlquery opens submitted links in a browser and records what happens. The agents relied on a combination of these services to emulate a full web browser to try and fetch data from the target website. Retrieving data through notifications The AI agents used a push-notification service called ntfy and other web archives in order to exfiltrate data from targeted websites. The agents may have used ntfy because they could not download the data directly from the targeted websites with their available tools, as per the report. Notably, ntfy messages expire after 12 hours by default which means that there is some evidence of data exfiltration, no one knows what that data actually was. Creating multiple accounts to obscure activity From June 14, 2026, onwards, the agents created a number of private accounts to hide their activity on the urlquery platform. They used disposable email services, browser platforms, and scanning services that could further support such activity. Temporary mailboxes could receive registration and verification emails, while scanning-service accounts could unlock additional features. Over time the agents began creating private accounts which limited visibility into their browser activity, as per the report. Differences between agents and threat actors One of the key differences between a swarm of rogue AI agents and traditional threat actor groups is the rapid evolution of tactics. There was a spike in activity targeting Australian entities between June 16 and 21. During this period, the agents rapidly cycled through tools and tactics. For traditional threat actors this type of technique evolution happens over months or years the evolution of agent techniques was compressed into just days, the report said. Harder to detect agent activity The bursts of activity resembled the surges that can follow disclosure of a major vulnerability. However, because the agents varied approaches produced a more varied set of indicators, activity was harder to recognise and cluster, it added. What next The researchers said that getting access to OpenAI agents chains of thoughts or reasoning traces could help determine whether the agents were deliberately using these mechanisms to cover their tracks. The report also calls for further investigation to help establish what the agents did and why, including analysing model transcripts, tool calls, internal logs from targeted websites, and additional records held by third-party services used by the agents.

articleTitle: Pakistan appoint Sahibzada Farhan as new T20I captain, drop Salman Ali Agha from squad
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Pakistan appointed Sahibzada Farhan as the new T20I captain in place of Salman Ali Agha. (AP)
description: Farhan, the top run-scorer at the 2026 T20 World Cup, takes over for the Sri Lanka series; Shaheen Shah Afridi retains ODI captaincy
body_raw: Pakistan have named top-order batter Sahibzada Farhan as their new T20I captain, with the 30-year-old taking over from Salman Ali Agha starting with the upcoming series against Sri Lanka. Agha, who led the side at the 2026 T20 World Cup, has been dropped from the 15-member squad for the shortest format. Agha is set to remain part of the ODI setup, where Shaheen Shah Afridi retains the captaincy for the tri-nation series against England and Sri Lanka. Former captain Babar Azam has also been included in the ODI squad. Pakistans three-match T20 series against Sri Lanka begins on Friday, October 9 in Rawalpindi, while the ODI tri-series will begin on October 18 and feature a double round-robin format, with the top two teams facing off in the final on October 31 at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore. Farhan, who top-scored at the T20 World Cup earlier this year, led Pakistan to a silver medal at the recently concluded 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. He scored 383 runs at a strike rate of 160 to become the player with the most runs in a single edition of a T20 World Cup. The right-handed opener is among several players from that squad retained for the senior side, with Abdul Samad, Saim Ayub, Hasan Nawaz, Arafat Minhas, Maaz Sadaqat, Abrar Ahmed, Sufiyan Moqim and Mohammad Salman Mirza also included. While Farhan has been named captain the shortest format, he is not part of a 16-member ODI squad. From the squad that last played the format and beat Australia 2-1 in January this year, Abdul Samad, Rohail Nazir, Shamyl Hussain, Maaz Sadaqat and Ahmed Daniyal have also been left out. Fakhar Zaman, Faheem Ashraf, Razaullah, Saad Baig and Saim Ayub have been called up alongside Hasan Nawaz, who scored a fine 96 in the Asian Games final against India. Pakistans T20I squad Sahibzada Farhan c, Abdul Samad, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Fakhar Zaman, Hasan Nawaz, Khawaja Nafay wk, Maaz Sadaqat, Mohammad Salman Mirza, Muhammad Imran Randhawa, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saim Ayub, Shadab Khan, Sufiyan Moqim. Pakistans ODI squad for tri-series Shaheen Shah Afridi c, Abrar Ahmed, Arafat Minhas, Babar Azam, Faheem Ashraf, Fakhar Zaman, Haris Rauf, Hasan Nawaz, Muhammad Ghazi Ghori wk, Naseem Shah, Razaullah, Saad Baig wk, Saim Ayub, Salman Ali Agha, Shadab Khan, Sufiyan Moqim.

articleTitle: By-Elections 2026 Highlights: TN’s Madurantakam tops bypoll turnout at 83.86%, Bengal’s Nandigram records 79.39% until 5 PM
articleFeaturedImageAlt: By Election 2026
description: Tamil Nadu's Madurantakam Assembly byelection recorded the highest turnout of 83.86% by 5 pm.
body_raw: By Elections 2026 Voting Live Updates Polling in the Madurantakam Assembly byelection in Tamil Nadu recorded the highest voter turnout among the constituencies reporting figures by 5 pm, with 83.86 of voters casting their ballots, according to the Election Commission. In West Bengal, the Nandigram Assembly constituency saw 79.39 voter turnout till 5 PM.In Puducherry, the Thattanchavady Assembly bypoll recorded 78.83 turnout, while the Nagaon Lok Sabha byelection in Assam saw nearly 76 of voters exercise their franchise. In Tamil Nadus Dharapuram, the figure stood at 78.53. Both Dharapuram and Madurantakam are reserved for Scheduled Caste candidates. Polling in Bengal will continue till 6 pm, while voting in Assam will end at 5 pm. Counting of votes in all the constituencies will take place on October 9. Tamil Nadu The bypolls in Madurantakam and Dharapuram were necessitated by the resignation of then AIADMK MLAs K Maragatham Kumaravel and P Satyabama, who later joined the ruling TVK. Both have been re-nominated from their respective seats. The DMK and AIADMK are also contesting both constituencies. In West Bengal Nandigram is the more closely watched contest, with BJP candidate Hasirani Rath facing Congress nominee Milan Pradhan, rival TMC faction candidate Mohammad Eteshamul Haque and CPIs Santigopal Giri. Rath is the mother of Chandranath Rath, a former aide of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari who was killed in May. In Rejinagar, the candidates include Golam Nabi Azad of the Aam Janata Unnayan Party, BJPs Sakharav Sarkar, TMCs Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, rival TMC candidate Safiuzzaman Sheikh, Congress Mohammad Abdullahil Kafi and CPIMs Syed Asad Ali. In Assam The Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll is an important contest for the BJP, Congress and AIUDF. The BJP is trying to increase its support in the Muslim-majority seat, while the Congress is working to hold on to its minority voters. AIUDF chief Badruddin Ajmal is also trying to regain the partys influence after it won only two Assembly seats in April, down from 16 earlier. Fifteen candidates are contesting, but the main fight is expected to be between BJPs Devashish Sharma, former Congress MLA Sibamoni Bora and Ajmal In Puducherry Bypoll is being seen as a test of the four-month-old NDA government led by Chief Minister N Rangasamy. The election was necessitated by Rangasamys resignation from the seat. While 11 candidates are in the fray, the main contest is expected to be between the ruling AINRC-led NDA, the Congress and former ally DMK.

articleTitle: 83-year-old Lonavala man held for ‘shooting dead’ grandson over property dispute
articleFeaturedImageAlt: grandfather kills grandson
description: Officers from Lonavala City Police Station reached the spot and initially registered the case as an accidental death.
body_raw: Lonavala city police have arrested an 83-year-old man for allegedly shooting dead his 33-year-old grandson, a lawyer, following a property dispute in Bhushi village, and then trying to pass off the killing as an accident. A case has been registered against five members of the family. The deceased has been identified as Advocate Abhay Manik Marathe. The accused, his grandfather Motiram Marathe, was arrested after police found inconsistencies in the familys version of events. Abhays father, Manik Marathe, is a former Lonavala municipal council corporator. The family owns Hotel Motiram in Bhushi village. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Superintendent of Police Sandeep Singh Gill said, Motiram Marathe holds a valid arms licence for a 12-bore gun, which he used for hunting. According to the family, the incident took place on Monday. They told police that Abhay was cleaning his grandfathers gun when the trigger was accidentally pulled and a bullet hit him in the chest. Officers from Lonavala City Police Station reached the spot and initially registered the case as an accidental death. However, police grew suspicious on inspecting the scene. The injury on Abhays chest, the bloodstains and the firearm itself did not appear to match the familys account. The body was sent to Sassoon Hospital for a post-mortem examination, and police consulted medical experts. Officers also questioned the Marathe family members, along with the manager and staff of the hotel. The inquiry revealed that Abhay and his grandfather had been involved in a property dispute. Motiram wanted to sell their land and distribute money among family members, however, Abhay had different plans for the land development, which led to the dispute, Gill said. Police said that the two had a heated argument and that the grandfather allegedly shot Abhay when the latter charged at him. Abhay was reportedly inside the hotel premises. Based on these findings, police registered a case against five people, including Motilal Marathe, and arrested him. Attempt to destroy evidence According to police, the family tried to cover up the crime after the shooting. CCTV cameras near the spot were allegedly removed, along with the DVR unit that stored the footage. Hotel staff were also allegedly threatened against speaking about the incident. Officials are now probing the property dispute within the Marathe family, the sequence of events after the shooting, and the attempts to destroy evidence, inspector Pramod Kshirsagar of the local crime branch said.
