articleTitle: To Trinath Mishra, with respect and wistfulness
articleFeaturedImageAlt: To Trinath Mishra, with respect and wistfulness
description: Mishra's career is proof that one can pay the price, keep one's dignity, and go on serving the institution that failed to protect you for doing the right thing.
body_raw: A life in khaki is not for everyone. Even amongst those given the privilege to wear the uniform, a few stand out as the embodiment of virtues that make an ideal police officer. Trinath Mishra, a member of the 1965 batch of the Indian Police Service, who passed away on October 1, belonged to that rare category. For a generation of policemen, his name was spoken with a mixture of respect and wistfulness Respect for what he did, wistfulness because the system he served with impeccable integrity and dedication seldom makes room for officers of his calibre. I first met him not as an officer but as a young school boy. The introduction came through Kanhaiya Lal Gupta, his batchmate in the UP cadre, and my uncle by marriage, who passed away last year. In the company of these two men, I encountered, for the first time, policing as an idea rather than a job. They disagreed about almost everything except the one thing that mattered Khaki is a trust, not a privilege. Mishras story began, in a sense, at Netarhat. He was among the first batch of a remarkable residential school there, an institution founded on the conviction that a holistic education need not be the monopoly of metropolitan elites. It instilled in him his love for austerity and a quiet sense of self-belief. As a young SP, he served in some of the most challenging districts of UP and was an integral part of the team of officers who wiped out the scourge of dacoity in the state. In the early 1990s, he served as the director of the Special Protection Group. He was then selected to officiate as director of the CBI, and subsequently headed the Central Reserve Police Force CRPF, holding concurrent charge of the CISF as well. Few officers of any generation have commanded so many of the institutions that hold the Indian state together. But what matters is what a man does when the coveted seat he occupies is on the line. That test came in October 1998. As CBI director, he authorised searches on the premises of the countrys most powerful corporate house. Within weeks, he was out. Not for any impropriety, but, by every account of the time, for not having kept the political executive in the loop. There was then no fixed tenure for the CBI chief. He took this transfer as a badge of honour and moved on. What struck me then, and strikes me more now, is that he did not nurse a grievance in public. He went on to lead the CRPF, and did that job with the same unfussy competence. Years later, as courts and governments argued over tenure protection for the CBI director, his removal was cited as Exhibit A for why it was needed. He had become, without ever seeking it, a case study in the vulnerability of honest institutions. What did I learn from men like Trinath Mishra and Kanhaiya Lal Gupta? From Mishra, I learnt that the hardest decisions in policing are between the right thing and the safe thing, and the safe thing almost always comes with the better posting. From Gupta, I learnt that such choices must be made without self-righteousness, and their consequences borne without bitterness. Together, they taught me that institutional loyalty and personal integrity are not opposites, though many well-wishers will often try to persuade you otherwise. The Indian police has not always been generous to its best and brightest. It rewards compliance and penalises professional integrity more often than it cares to admit. Mishras career is proof that one can pay the price, keep ones dignity, and go on serving the institution that failed to protect you for doing the right thing. He belonged to a generation who built many of the institutions we inherited, and always warned us how easily they could be hollowed out from within. Arguably, we have honoured the first half of their legacy far more faithfully than the second. To his family, my deepest condolences. To the young officers who never knew him, I offer a small assignment Read about the events of October 1998, and then, ask yourself honestly what you would have done in his place. That question is his parting gift to all of us who attempt to wear the uniform with pride and honour. The writer is a serving IPS officer. Views are personal

articleTitle: Digger: Tom Cruise leans into one of his career’s most remarkable performances with glee
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Digger movie review
description: Alejandro G Iñárritu digs even deeper into dark comedy and satire, and retreads his Birdman’s theatre-cum-real life territory, to give us a caricaturish and cartoonish view of the rich and the powerful.
body_raw: Satire, farce, comedy, irony, entertainment, or tragedy? What is Digger, is a question Kenny Jesse Plemmons asks at a crucial moment in Alejandro G Inrritus latest film. Does it matter, when an ice shelf five times the size of Washington DC is headed towards Europe to wreak death and destruction? Yeah, does it, when we are currently at the mercy of the worlds most powerful leader who may be equally unhinged, and not averse to destruction? Inrritu digs even deeper into dark comedy and satire, and retreads his Birdmans theatre-cum-real life territory, to give us a caricaturish and cartoonish view of the rich and the powerful, which would be absurd, but for the fact that it isnt. The US seeing Europe as a needy, whiny friend? Tick. A President who has tycoons sit in on his Cabinet meetings? Tick. A post-truth audience that doesnt need facts, but a well-told story? Tick. A President who sees the world through the prism of his a.hole? Tick. A tech-billionaire lurking in the shadows who can solve problems, just dont ask how? Tick. The progressives lofty liberalism vs the hard lives of ordinary people? Tick. Big tech professing to bring people together. Tick. Bomb first, questions later? Tick. Also Read - Riz Ahmed on beating Fahadh Faasil, Vir Das to Digger role Hope we get to work together One can argue that Digger doesnt actually have much that is new to say, from the avarice of oil billionaires to cowardice of politics. And that the effect of the one rousing scene where Tom Cruises Digger a.k.a Rockwell holds up the mirror to the world is frittered away by Inrritu simultaneously mocking his titular character. However, it is the absolute irreverence with which Inrritu, who also co-wrote the story and the screenplay, tells what we already know, that it forces us to re-think all that we do. About the world we live in, the world that is changing scarily, and the world we are leaving behind. In what has to be one of the most remarkable performances of his long career, Tom Cruise leans gleefully into prosthetics and the role of an ageing, balding, paunchy, greedy businessman, whose only love is a cat that may or may not be dead. He lives in a grand, empty mansion with sister Emma a wasted Sandra Huller, whom he barely tolerates, as he unloads on underlings. One particular recipient of his wrath is his in-house climate scientist Ganesh from Kerala Riz Ahmed, deserved more, whose warnings are used by Rockwell only to serve his purpose. John Goodman turns up the buffoonery, his jowly cheeks doing most of the work, as the US President who is about to die and doesnt have the time for too many details. He also has as a constant companion a Reverend, who conducts impromptu prayers and blessings for the President and his men. The play-within-the-film format allows Inrritu to switch between worlds, and hint at real life where things may not be all that great either, even as the climate disaster unfolds on the stage in unbroken bleak greys and browns. It is a marvel in staging, sets, and sound. Sometimes it is too much and often it is distracting, as Rockwells mansion leaks and creaks. The conflict that Cruises Curtis feels as the actor playing the over-the-top Rockwell is not fully explored either. Also Read - Digger movie review After 30 years of defying gravity, Tom Cruise takes his biggest leap And, that ending. does it give Rockwell a sort-of redemption the film is telling us he does not deserve? My oil gives you freedom, Rockwell says during his address to the assembly of European nations. The freedom to bask in the comfort of your unsustainable lives. Thats the kind of discomfort Digger needed to raise more.

articleTitle: Shreyas Iyer slams maiden T20I ton, leads India to 8-wicket win over West Indies in 1st T20I
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shreyas Iyer slammed maiden T20I ton during first India vs West Indies T20I. (CREIMAS)
description: Iyer scored the fastest ton by an Indian in T20Is against West Indies as India chased down 172 in just 14.4 overs with 8 wickets in hand.
body_raw: Playing a captains innings, Shreyas Iyer led from the front by slamming his maiden T20I century to lead India to a comfortable 8-wicket victory over West Indies in the first T20I at Ekana International Cricket Stadium in Lucknow on Tuesday. Iyer scored the fastest ton by an Indian in T20Is against West Indies as India chased down 172 in just 14.4 overs with 8 wickets in hand. Chasing the total, India didnt have the best of starts as they lost both openers Abhishek Sharma 21 and Sanju Samson 11 inside four overs with the scoreboard reading 35. Roston Chase picked up Abhishek in the third over, with Shimron Hetmyer taking a brilliant diving catch while running in from long-off. An over later, Sanju Samson departed, extending his lean patch since the Asian Games, as he sliced a short delivery back to Akeal Hosein, who took the catch off his own bowling. AS IT HAPPENED INDIA VS WEST INDIES 1ST T20I HIGHLIGHTS Thereafter, skipper Shreyas Iyer and Ishan Kishan stabilised the innings with a 137-run partnership. Earlier, all-rounder Naman Dhir had a dream T20I debut, picking up three wickets with his off-spin to help India bowl out West Indies for 171. Dhir finished with impressive figures of 331, while Kuldeep Yadav also scalped 2 for 33 to help India restrict West Indies to a manageable total. Sent into bat, West Indies skipper Shai Hope started the innings in a flurry, smacking Mayank Yadav for four boundaries in the second over to set the tone. The four boundaries forced skipper Shreyas Iyer to replace Mayank with Axar Patel in third over. Arshdeep got the first breakthrough for India, cleaning up Kamil Pooran with a pitch-up delivery. West Indies were dealt another blow in the sixth over when Shimron Hetmyer was run out while going for an unnecessary single. It turned out to be double blow for the West Indies as Axar cleaned up Rovman Powell in the sixth over with a pitch-up delivery after the right-hander went for a huge heave over square-leg. Sherfane Rutherford 56 off 34 gave the much needed impetus to West Indies innings with the left-hander hitting Kuldeep Yadav for two sixes in the ninth over and then smashing Axar for two boundaries and a six in the 11th over. With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Gujarat Hardlook: How do you remake Gandhi’s ashram for Rs 1,200 crore — and keep it simple?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A good part of that pathway is already complete. It is lined with baobabs from Madagascar, black neem from Thailand and exotic flora such as Mayan spinach from Mexico and bird-of-paradise.
description: Visitors can walk through the house where Gandhi and his wife Kasturba once lived — a house that, every year without fail, marks Gandhi Jayanti with an all-faith prayer meeting open to the public.
body_raw: Under the Gandhi Ashram Redevelopment Project, most of the original ashrams buildings have been restored. The project is now deciding how these buildings will tell the Mahatmas story through museums, activities and experiences for visitors within the 55-acre space, write Parimal A Dabhi and Leena Misra. IMAGINE A granite-paved pathway lit by Victorian-style lampposts, with ornate wooden benches along the way, taking visitors on a journey through the life of a barrister who became a Mahatma while fighting to free India from British rule. A good part of that pathway is already complete. It is lined with baobabs from Madagascar, black neem from Thailand and exotic flora such as Mayan spinach from Mexico and bird-of-paradise. The walk through a series of repurposed buildings is designed to culminate in an arboretum called Mohan-to-Mahatma - the plants are colour-coded to mark each phase of Gandhis life. That, though, is all in the extended part of the project. At its heart is a five-acre space that feels frozen in time. The Five Acres Frozen in Time Here, visitors can walk through the house where Gandhi and his wife Kasturba once lived - a house that, every year without fail, marks Gandhi Jayanti with an all-faith prayer meeting open to the public. This year, on October 2, Vijaybhai Joshi arrived at the ceremony dressed in khadi, with a cotton hank around his neck and a walking stick slung over his shoulder. After the prayer meeting at Hriday Kunj - marking Gandhis 157th birth anniversary - he climbed onto the back of a scooter to head home. This country has not seen anyone like Gandhiji. Weve been shaped by his ideology, and because we followed it, here I am before you at 104 years, Joshi says, chuckling. Hard of hearing, Joshi pulls a small contraption from his bag - a funnel attached to a transparent pipe. To speak with him, one must talk into the funnel he listens through the other end, pressed to his ear. Born in Bihar in 1922, Joshi worked for a British firm and was posted in Pakistan. During the partition in 1947, his employer asked if he wanted to stay on. No, he told them, and asked instead to be transferred to his home state of Gujarat. He has lived in Ahmedabad since, where his family sings Gandhis favourite bhajan, Vaishnava Jana To, every evening. Driving the scooter was 84-year-old Jesingbhai Parmar, a former Reserve Bank of India employee who reaches the ashram every Friday - because that is the day Gandhiji died, he says. On his visits, he spins 250 metres of yarn on the charkha at Hriday Kunj for over three hours. This October 2, he sat in the front row of the prayer meeting, spinning alongside children from the ashrams school, which has since relocated outside the complex. One Ashram, Six Trusts Hriday Kunj - the house Gandhi built in 1917 on land he bought along the Sabarmati River a year earlier - was just one structure among several that made up the 120-acre ashram until 1930. Todays redevelopment covers the 55-acre ashram itself, within a wider precinct of roughly 322 acres. After Gandhis death in 1948, the land was divided among six trusts tasked with carrying forward Gandhian thoughts and practices the Harijan Ashram Trust 1939, Gujarat Khadi Gramodyog Mandal 1940, Sabarmati Ashram Preservation and Memorial Trust or SAPMT 1950, Gujarat Harijan Sevak Sangh 1952, Sabarmati Ashram Gaushala Trust 1952 and Khadi Gramodyog Prayog Samiti 1958. The Core Hriday Kunj sits within the five acres known simply as Sabarmati Ashram. On an average day, this stretch alone draws 4,000 visitors, says Kartikeya Sarabhai, chairman of SAPMT - whose first chairman, in 1949, was Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Several luminaries succeeded him, such as Ganesh Mavlankar, the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha, and Kartikeyas late father Dr Vikram Sarabhai known as the father of Indias space mission, to name a few. SAPMT manages this core area, which includes Gandhis and Kasturbas residence, Vinoba Bhave and Mira Kutir, Nandini Guest House, Magan Nivas, and Sanghralaya - a museum designed by late architect Charles Correa that houses the ashrams exhibition and library. A Vision, Delivered Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched the Rs 1,200-crore redevelopment project in 2024. It envisions the ashram as one contiguous space across 55 acres its buildings restored to how they stood when Gandhi was alive. The project is being executed by the Union Ministry of Culture and the Gujarat government through the Mahatma Gandhi Sabarmati Ashram Memorial Trust MGSAMT, headed by Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. Retired Gujarat IAS officer I P Gautam is leading the projects execution as Chairman of the Executive Council. Another retired IAS officer, I K Patel, is also playing a key role in the project as officer on special duty and member secretary of the Governing Council. It was the Prime Ministers wish that we restore the ashram to how Gandhi left it in 1930, with modern facilities, says a source associated with the project. A public road that once split the land in two has now been closed and a large brick-and-concrete gateway has come up to serve as the new main entrance. Beyond the SAPMT-managed core lies the part of the ashram now under restoration - buildings that once housed schools, hostels, teachers quarters, and units producing cloth, paper, leather and dairy products. This stretch, the source says, will take visitors through Gandhis life, from the Champaran Satyagraha, where he became Mahatma, through the freedom movement, and till the British left India. Restoring 28 Buildings, Developing 24 Museums Inside what used to be the ashrams gaushala cowshed, an artisan, Hirenbhai, dips bunches of coir fibre into a paste of Fullers earth, popularly called Multani mitti, and smooths it over a plinth. We will finish it with lippan, he says, referring to traditional mud plaster. A marble plaque at the entrance notes that the structure was built in 1938 for Rs 7,200, funded by a donation from the Ahmedabad American Cotton Exchange Association Ltd, a private company founded in 1932. It is among the first of 28 buildings to be fully restored. In one room, thatched roofs for a set of representational cowsheds - part of an upcoming museum - are in place. It is the only one of 24 planned museums being developed by the National Dairy Development Board NDDB. The rest have been contracted to Paris-based Museum Studio, which is working in consortium with Ecofirst Private Ltd, a subsidiary of Tata Consulting Engineers. Ahmedabad-based urban planner Bimal Patels firm HCP Design Planning Management Pvt Ltd created the master plan for the project and executed the civil works using traditional methods. Sources say no cement concrete was used in any of the restorations. Of the 28 restored buildings, 24 will house museums. Activities once central to ashram life - papermaking and spinning among them - have been assigned to buildings within the wider precinct. It was Gandhijis idea that these activities should not just survive but also prosper. We will produce more khadi and more paper, so visitors to the ashram can buy them, says a source involved in the project. At the entrance, an interpretation centre will lay out what each space in the new ashram offers, helping visitors plan their visit around the time they have. Keeping the Tranquility SAPMT prepared a concept note meant to guide the MGSAMTs work closely. Kartikeya Sarabhai recalls that Modi, as Gujarats Chief Minister then, had a clear vision for the revamped ashram even back in 2009, when the Trust first approached him. The PM, from the beginning, felt that whatever changes we make should be done in the context of the overall ashram, not as individual ones. He had that vision even then - it got articulated later, Sarabhai says. When Modi became Prime Minister and approached the ashrams trustees about redeveloping the full complex, Our only request was that the ashrams core values - tranquility among them - stay at its heart, Sarabhai says, adding that the government held to that promise. He notes that Hriday Kunj, the Gandhis home from 1917 to 1930, originally stood amid an open maidan. We will keep it in the maidan, he says. The concept note, Sarabhai explains, outlines the need to communicate what the ashram stood for in Gandhis time. It was a site for experiments in truth, non-violence, dignity of labour, respect for all religions and the removal of untouchability. It was to be one of modern Indias most audacious experiments. The uniqueness of this experiment makes this site of immense significance to India and to the world, he says. The new trust has left SAPMTs management of the core area undisturbed. SAPMT has engaged Ahmedabad-based conservation architect Dr Rabindra Vasavda to restore its portion of the buildings. Making Room The Ashramvasis According to sources, 307 claims were made by ashramvasis - long-time residents occupying 256 buildings- who had to vacate the premises. The MGSAMT offered three options compensation by cheque, flats purchased by the trust, or homes in cooperative housing financed by the trust. The trust has spent Rs 190 crore on rehabilitation so far. Of those relocated, 223 families - the largest group - opted for compensation, with payouts of up to Rs 90 lakh per family. We have treated them with respect. They were not encroachers, said a source. Only Krunal Rathod and his family, who occupy a cottage, are yet to evacuate. Their case is under litigation in the Small Causes Court. The Rathods fight concerns three properties which they claim were handed over to their predecessor by the trustee of the relevant Ashram trust around 1930. The PMs Stamp Several personal interventions by Modi shaped the redevelopments final look The pathways colour was changed from red to grey cobblestone Victorian-style wrought-iron lamp posts will be installed throughout red stone benches were replaced with ornate wooden ones. What Visitors Can Expect Original artefacts from SAPMTs collection - a sari Gandhi wove for Kasturba, his cycle, his charkha - may be part of the exhibits, with security details still being worked out parking for 250 cars and 25 buses to serve the higher number of visitors. At present, the Sabarmati Ashram sees nearly 4,000 visitors daily. A food court near the entry gate that will serve sattvik cuisine. A souvenir shop featuring Gandhis three monkeys, carved from wood sourced from the original ashram. A walkthrough rainforest of medicinal plants and trees. The ashrams original trees - peepal, jamun, asopalav, piludi, neem, gundo, mango, moringa - still stand in many places. Retired Deputy Conservator of Forest Jayant Solanki is overseeing this effort, assigned to the Heartfulness Institute, a spiritual organisation. Ticketing still undecided - though Kartikeya Sarabhai suggests non-priced tickets to regulate visitor flow. Residential facilities for visiting Gandhian scholars, an idea still under consideration. An artificial lake connected to stormwater drains to harvest rainwater. The lake was naturally tested in July when the city saw excessive rain, and water drained into it, filling it. The Ashram is my best and only creation. And the world will judge me by its results, reads a quote by the Father of the Nation at the entrance of the MGSAMT office, as if summarising the projects objective. By the time the pathway reaches its end, visitors will have walked through more than a restored ashram - they will have retraced, tree by tree and room by room, the journey of a barrister who became one of historys most enduring symbols of non-violent resistance. Iconic Buildings Being Restored Anand Bhavan Constructed around 1920 as the ashrams needs grew. Gandhis secretary and confidant, Mahadev Desai, lived here for a time. Imam Manzil Built in 1919 for Imam Saheb Abdul Kader Bawazeer, a close companion of Gandhis in both South Africa and India. He gave up his business to join the Satyagraha movement and stayed with Gandhi until he died in 1931. Bal Mandir Inaugurated in 1940 by Madame Montessori, this building trained the children of Dalit craftsmen and workers in the crafts practised in their own homes. Junu Rasodu Built in 1918 as a kitchen and dining hall with a storeroom cellar. Meals followed a strict ritual a bell rang thrice, the kitchen doors closed after the second ring, and prayers began at the third, according to an account by the late Narayan Desai, Mahadev Desais son. Somnath Chhatralaya Built in 1922 to house the growing number of ashram residents, this 100-room facility later served as a hostel for female PTC students after 1955. Jamna Kutir Built in 1924 by industrialist Jamnalal Bajaj as a residence for his family during visits to the Satyagraha Ashram, which Gandhi later renamed Harijan Ashram. It later housed two ashram workers. Restoration of this building is pending due to litigation.

articleTitle: Scheduled call with Putin to discuss possible case of pneumonic plague in Russia: Trump
articleFeaturedImageAlt: United States President Donald Trump. (Photo: AP)
description: Asked what the U.S. intelligence community was saying about the case, Trump said the U.S. is in “very deep discussions” on the topic. “We’ll be able to report about it, probably tomorrow,” Trump said.
body_raw: President Donald Trump on Tuesday said he has a call scheduled with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible case of plague at a Siberian research institute. Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said he would be talking with Putin about the case very soon. Health authorities are investigating after the death of an employee at an anti-plague institute, which authorities attributed to pneumonia with an unknown cause. Asked what the U.S. intelligence community was saying about the case, Trump said the U.S. is in very deep discussions on the topic. Well be able to report about it, probably tomorrow, Trump said. The World Health Organization on Tuesday said the case presents a very low risk outside Russia. The United Nations agency said it was in contact with Russian authorities following reports of the death last week of a woman who worked at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East. On Monday, Trump said the U.S. would be willing to help Russia with the situation. Its a rough disease. You know, thats a disease we used to be able to control, but somehow those microbes have gotten stronger and smarter. Theyre like an army, Trump told reporters at the White House. The call also comes as the Trump administration faces an Oct. 18 deadline to decide which Russian entities, if any, it will sanction under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which Trump signed into law on Sept. 18. Ukraine has given the administration and Congress a wish list of Russian companies, vessels and individuals it would like to see hit with U.S. sanctions under that law.

articleTitle: This actor became Trinamool MP in April. Now she is BJP Rajya Sabha pick
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Koel Mallick Rajya Sabha
description: Asked why she cut ties with the Trinamool, Koel Mallick avoided a direct response. “I have no anger towards them. Perhaps being a student of psychology has made me empathetic."
body_raw: On April 6 this year, popular Bengali actor Koel Mallick took the oath as a Rajya Sabha MP from the Trinamool Congress. In an Instagram post sharing photographs of her in Parliament, Mallick wrote that she is honoured to get the opportunity to serve the people of Bengal and called it the beginning of a new journey. The journey proved to be short. Less than a month later, the Trinamool Congress lost the Assembly polls in Bengal, and the BJP came to power. The poll setback triggered an implosion in the Trinamool Congress ranks, with leader after leader deserting the partys firebrand chief Mamata Banerjee. Amid the Trinamool meltdown, Mallick resigned as a Rajya Sabha MP on July 16. Shortly after, she met Union Minister Bhupender Yadav at his Delhi residence. And in less than three months, she is on the list of BJP candidates for the Rajya Sabha. Earlier, the BJP sent former Trinamool MPs Sukhendu Sekhar Ray, Sushmita Dev and Prakash Chik Baraik to the Rajya Sabha, shortly after they quit as Trinamool MPs. Who is Koel Mallick A popular actor in Bengali films, Mallick has received multiple awards, including the Bengal governments Mahanayak Samman in 2023. An alumna of Modern High School and Gokhale Memorial Girls College, she holds a degree in psychology. She is the daughter of veteran Bengali actor Ranjit Mallick and is married to film producer Nispal Singh. aaaoeaa aaaoeaaaa aaaaaa aaaaaaaaa, a aaaaaaa aaa aaaa aaaoeaa aaaoeaaaa aaaaaa aaaaaaaaa aaaaEaaa shashikisoch aaaaaaaa aaa aaa aaaoeaaa aaaaaaa aaa- aaaaa aaaaaaaY aaaaaaaaaE aaaaaa aaaaaaaY aaaoeaaa aaaaaaa aaaaa aaaaa-a - BJP West Bengal BJP4Bengal October 5, 2026 Koel Mallicks BJP entry Mallick joined the BJP on Monday, a day after the party announced that it has chosen her for a Rajya Sabha seat. She filed the nomination in the presence of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and the partys state president Samik Bhattacharya. Speaking to the media, Mallick said, I am honoured. I have been given a great responsibility. Serving people is a duty, and that is what I will do happily. I am overwhelmed to see the development work that has begun in Bengal over the past few months. This is what Bengal needs the most. she said. I have always heard my father at home saying, Why is this happening? Why is that not happening in the state? As an ordinary person, there are so many things we want and so many thoughts we keep to ourselves. This time, I will speak about those issues. It is easy to read a newspaper and say, Oh, this was not done, but the real thing is to come to the field and work on those issues, she said. Asked why she cut ties with the Trinamool, she avoided a direct response. I have no anger towards them. Perhaps being a student of psychology has made me empathetic. Those who derive satisfaction from putting others down may themselves be facing problems. I wish them mental well-being, she said. The ideologies of the two parties are different. Every party tries to do good in its own way. I am proud to have joined this party. They are working for the development of the people. I will also try to do the same, she said. A tale of 2 meetings On January 15, a month before Trinamool chose Koel Mallick for the Rajya Sabha seat, the partys national general secretary, Lok Sabha MP and Mamata Banerjees nephew Abhishek Banerjee met Ranjit Mallick at his Kolkata home and presented him with Unnayaner Panchali, a report card of 15 years of the Trinamool governments achievements. Both spoke highly of each other. Cut to September 4, Bengal Chief Minister Adhikari greeted Ranjit Mallick by touching his feet and holding his hand to lead him onto the stage during the centenary celebrations of legendary actor Uttam Kumar in Tollygunge. And a month later, his daughter is BJPs Rajya Sabha choice.

articleTitle: Dozen Bengal tribunal judges flag EC portal: ‘Can’t restore deleted voters’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Dozen Bengal Tribunal judges flag their EC portal: ‘Can’t serve notices, hold hearings or restore deleted voters’
description: 3 months after polls, on Aug 11, Tribunals put on record challenges in SIR appeal process; sent to EC, Calcutta High Court Chief Justice.
body_raw: Judges of more than a dozen Tribunals appointed in West Bengal on the orders of the Supreme Court to process SIR appeals, including of 27 lakh deleted electors, have highlighted glaring gaps in a digital portal set up for them by the Election Commission of Indias IT division. Official records show they complained that the portal did not allow them to serve notices to parties, slowing down the disposal of appeals. It did not allow the Tribunals to upload additional documents from voters who filed appeals, or hold virtual hearings, or restore a deleted voter. It didnt even let the appellants download Tribunal orders, the judges said. These concerns form the minutes of a meeting of over a dozen Tribunal judges on August 11 - there are 19 in all - and were conveyed to the Election Commission of India and the Chief Justice of the High Court of Calcutta, The Indian Express has learnt. An investigation by The Indian Express last month had revealed that two Election Commissioners had put on record 14 objections in 10 months to a string of decisions taken that pertain to who gets to vote and who doesnt. One of the key concerns they raised was that ECINET, the ECs principal digital system for citizens and officials, restricted access for the officers on the ground responsible for finalising the electoral rolls. Subsequently, the EC announced it would set up a committee with an independent expert to review ECINET and double-check its compliance with the law. Similarly, the hurdles highlighted by the Tribunal judges, they said, were, in effect, getting in the way of ensuring due process for deleted voters. On October 1, The Indian Express sent emails to the Election Commission of India and the Registrar General of the High Court of Calcutta for their response to the judges concerns and whether these were addressed. There was no response. The key challenges judges put on record The August 11 minutes put on record the challenges the judges face. The excerpts from the minutes are telling Cant serve notices There is no mechanism.till date in spite of several requests and reminders to develop a common and proper mechanism on the portal to serve notice to the parties directly or through proper channel. Sometime in the month of May 2026 some of us even approved a format of notice to be issued to the parties but it has not seen the light of the day till date. Cant store documents .when the Tribunal finds uploaded documents are not in terms of enumeration form or whenever the Tribunal needs additional documents, there is no mechanism how the same are to be secured. In the absence of such a mechanism on the portal, each Tribunal is trying to serve the notices through e-emails, that is, through DMDEO concerned but the response is very poor. Cant hold virtual hearings There is no mechanism to hold virtual hearings in case the Tribunal intends to hear the parties.Once the appeal is disposed of either by way of deletion or inclusion of the voter, it cannot be restored on the portal if the restoration is needed on account of direction of the judicial order or otherwise. Cant give an order copy to appellant There is no procedure for the parties to get certified copy or download copy of the order of the Tribunal from the designated portal to know the reasons why their name is deleted or included. This is significant because the Supreme Court, in its order on April 1, had asked the tribunals to communicate the reasons and to revisit the records before they decide on the appeals. Cant digitise physical records The judges flagged the uncertainty over the appeals filed physically with the District MagistrateDistrict Election Officers. .there is no proper mechanism for maintenance of record of these appeals since they are not digitized. If their appeals are not brought to the proper channel, injustice will be done to such citizens, they said. Incidentally, as early as April 6, the Supreme Court had acknowledged this same issue which had then been raised during the hearing in the petition of Mostari Banu, a West Bengal voter. The ECI has already notified on 20.03.2026 that appeals can be filed either online through the ECI NET platform or physically at the office of the DMSDMSDO, who shall ensure digitisation and uploading of the appeal on the ECI NET platform at the earliest, the SC had said in its April 6 order. Another judge complained in May There was an earlier alert, too. On May 22, one of the tribunal judges, wrote to the Calcutta High Court Chief highlighting how the issue of setting up a mechanism to send a notice was raised but went unheeded. Absence of such a mechanism to notify the parties to the appeal is adversely affecting the pace of disposal of appeals, said the judge in the letter to the CJ. The judge also underlined the lack of accurate data on the number of appeals disposed of being shared by the EC. Unfortunately through EC source incorrect data is being catered to the press regarding number of disposal, suppressing the fact ECI has not been able to set up proper mechanism for issuance of notice to the parties for hearing of the appeal, the judge said in the letter. Shadow over appeal process All these concerns raised by Tribunal judges cast a shadow on the Supreme Court-ordered unique appellate process meant to give the 27 lakh deleted voters a chance to appeal their exclusion from the rolls. The Tribunals are a unique aspect of the contested West Bengal SIR process. As many as 27 lakh voters deleted had been identified by the Election Commission using algorithms for logical discrepancies and unmapped as per the documents they submitted during the SIR. After invoking its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution while hearing a challenge to the SIR in West Bengal, the Supreme Court had on February 20 ordered appointment of judicial officers to decide on the eligibility of electors in the state. The Commission, using its centralised software, had drawn up a list of 60.06 lakh such electors, based on logical discrepancies flagged in their documents. Hundreds of judicial officers from Bengal, Odisha and Jharkhand, appointed by the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, following the Supreme Court directions, went through these cases, finally deleting 27.16 lakh electors just weeks ahead of polling in the Assembly elections in the state in April. To give those affected a chance to appeal, the Supreme Court had on March 10 ordered appellate Tribunals of retired High Court judges to be established, which the EC did on March 20 by notifying 19 single-member tribunals. Since then, two judges have resigned citing personal reasons. They have been replaced with other former judges, it is learnt. TMC, BJP evenly shared gains in seats with heavy deletions The two-phase elections in West Bengal last April led to a landslide win for the BJP. The incumbent Trinamool Congress claimed voter deletions played a role in its defeat but thats an allegation more political than empirical. SIR deletions exceeded the victory margin in 49 seats of the 293 that went to polls. In these, the spoils were almost evenly shared - 26 were won by the BJP and 21 by the TMC. The EC had not released any data of the appellate process until a submission in the Supreme Court in another related matter on September 18, when it said 38.31 lakh appeals had been filed, of which only 1.26 lakh had been disposed of till September 10. Of the total appeals, it said, 22.21 lakh were filed by voters who had been deleted and 16.10 lakh were filed against inclusions i.e., seeking deletion. Before the elections, problems with another portal used by judicial officers to adjudicate 60 lakh names were also raised during Supreme Court hearings. In fact, the court noted this in its order on March 10. The judicial officers, through the Honble Chief Justice, have expressed an urgent concern, which seems to have been created due to some mistake at the level of the Election Commission of India. Learned senior counsel for the Election Commission of India assures that the same shall be rectified immediately without any delay. We strongly recommend that the Election Commission of India provide full logistic support to the High Court at Calcutta and all the judicial officers in the completion of the responsibilities which we have assigned to them through our order dated 24.02.2026, the March 10 order said.

articleTitle: Delhi park gangrape survivor identifies all 3 accused in jail lineup
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Police personnel stand at a sealed area, at a park located between Kalkaji Mandir and ISKCON Temple after a 17 year old was allegedly sexually assaulted, in New Delhi.
description: The three men were arrested for raping the girl last month at a park in Southeast Delhi. They are lodged at Tihar Jail
body_raw: The 17-year-old girl who was allegedly gangraped at a park in Southeast Delhi last month has identified all three accused during a Test Identification Parade TIP at Tihar Jail on Wednesday, official sources said. The three accused - Asif, Hemant Singh and his brother Mukesh - are lodged at the jail. A TIP is a procedure in criminal investigations in which a victim or witness is asked to identify an accused before a magistrate. The process is conducted in the presence of the investigating officer to ensure there is no mistaken identity, which could lead to a wrongful conviction. Police said they are trying to build a watertight case. Weapons like the firearm and knife used in the crime have been recovered forensic report of the evidence is awaited. Posed as cops, assaulted girl on 17th birthday The incident took place September 21 when the girl and her male friend were walking through Aastha Kunj Park after offering prayers at a nearby temple on her birthday. According to police, the accused allegedly posed as police officers and threatened the teenagers with a gun and a knife. The accused allegedly demanded phone numbers of their families. When the teenagers refused, the men allegedly slapped the boy and forcibly separated him from the girl. Police said the three men then raped the girl one after another while one of them restrained her friend. The boy made a PCR call at 8.45 pm, informing the police that he and the girl had been assaulted by three policemen inside the park. A police team reached the spot, after which the girl was taken for a medical examination. A case was registered under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences POCSO Act and relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita BNS, including those dealing with gang rape of a person under 18, criminal conspiracy, voluntarily causing grievous hurt and criminal intimidation. Asif, a school dropout who worked at a vegetable shop, allegedly used to loiter in the park. According to the police, he had previously been involved in theft and snatching cases, including incidents in which firearms were allegedly used. He was arrested hours after the incident near the spot while travelling on a motorcycle, following a brief exchange of fire. Hemant and Mukesh were arrested from their house near the park, where they had been living for several months. Hemant is a law graduate, while Mukesh is pursuing a Bachelor of Science degree in mathematics.

articleTitle: Sujeet’s 27 minutes of Slaying: Takes down Oly champ, flips 2-9 score for Asian Games gold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Sujeet Kalkal poses with his Asian Games gold medal. (PTI Photo)
description: Four take-downs in the last one minute helped the 65 kg wrestler beat back Abdulmazhid Kudiev of Tajikistan, for gold
body_raw: When Sujeet Kalkal left for Aichi Nagoya for the 2026 Asian Games, all eyes were on him he was labelled as the brightest medal prospect with his medal chances being higher than Olympic bronze medallist Aman Sehrawat. There were reasons behind the expectations. He is World no 2 in mens 65 kg wrestling, unbeaten this season, and was fighting for a medal that had belonged to India in 2014 and 2018 before going to Mongolia in 2022. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage As he effected a last minute takedown on his opponent Abdulmazhid Kudiev of Tajikistan to win the final bout 10-9, not only did he deliver on all the expectations but also ended Indias wait of an Asian Games gold after eight years bringing back the 65 kg gold to India continuing the legacy of Yogeshwar Dutt 2014 Gold and Bajrang Punia 2018 Gold. I didnt expect anything less than a gold. I had told him when he left for Japan and I told him today also, you are here to win a gold. He delivered on all the promise he has displayed over the last two years, his coach Kuldeep Singh Sehrawat told The Indian Express. Such pressure in a major event can do funny things to athletes but Sujeet remained ice cold in his wrestling and overturned a 2-9 deficit in the first half of the final to claim the gold medal. Staring at 2-9, two men sitting miles apart were tense looking at the scoreline, as the Tajik used his superior ground wrestling and leg attacks to pick quick points. Coach Kuldeep was sitting behind him in the stands while his father Dayanand Kalkal was sitting in his home in Imlota, Haryana. Sujeet had time, but the Tajik was riding momentum - which the Indian flipped faster than a Phitle. However, their tense faces soon started smiling as Sujeet launched four take-downs. For a moment, I was worried but it is okay. Wrestling is a sport like that where you can have those moments. The important thing is that he didnt buckle under the pressure, said Dayanand, who was a wrestler himself and early coach of Sujeet. Defeating Oly champion, comeback drama It will be fair to say that the final and Sujeets comeback was no less than dramatic. He entered the mat to loud cheers from the Indian contingent. But the Indian fans and coaches were stunned alike as Kudiev countered Sujeet brilliantly, including scoring two points off a leg lace, to lead 9-2 after the first round. Sujeet made a few mistakes. Especially, once he lost the attacking position, the Tajik counter attacked him. The Tajik is a good ground wrestler and he executed his moves well, said Kuldeep. However, the second half was completely different. Sujeet came back determined and he effected four take downs to win the gold medal. It was a mix of speed and smarts that allowed Sujeet to catch Kudiev by surprise on two occasions. He moved behind quickly to take him down in the second half before executing a right leg attack successfully. As Kudiev tired out, Sujeet used his speed to get hold of his legs and make it 8-9. With less than 30 seconds on the clock, came the last move where Sujeet got hold of Kudievs left leg and continued the attack to take him down and make it 10-9. However, before even entering the final, Sujeet had made the headlines after defeating reigning Olympic champion Kotaro Kiyooka of Japan in front of the home fans in the semi-finals. It was a tactical bout fought between two of the best wrestlers in the business. The bout ended on 3-3 with Sujeet winning on technical criteria. We knew that Kiyooka was going to be the biggest challenge. Incidentally, he came in the same half of the draw. Kiyookas main attacking move is that he goes for the right leg while attacking and we had planned to counter it that way, explained Kuldeep. When Kiyooka tried it for the first time, Sujeet defended and conceded only one point. However, when Kiyooka did it a second time, Sujeet was ready and he countered it to take two points and eventually won the bout. It was a momentous result for the 23-year-old who has his eyes firmly set on the World Championships 2026 and reaction from his coach Kuldeep summed up his gold medal run. I had told everyone that he would defeat Iranian and Japanese wrestlers but had never thought that he would do that in a space of 27 minutes, Kuldeep laughed.

articleTitle: Too much screen time? Try the 20-20-20 rule to protect your eyes
articleFeaturedImageAlt: eyes
description: Prolonged screen exposure is increasingly becoming a lifestyle challenge for eye health, with digital eye strain, dry eyes and rising concerns around myopia, especially among children
body_raw: Written by By Dr Mahipal Singh Sachdev A 12-year-old boy was recently brought to our hospital by his parents after he began complaining that he could no longer see the writing clearly on his classroom board. At home, he was spending several hours on a tablet for online classes, gaming and videos, often without taking breaks. His parents initially assumed that the frequent eye rubbing and headaches were simply because he was using the screen too much. An eye examination, however, revealed myopia or short-sightedness that required correction. The case is a reminder that what may appear to be ordinary screen fatigue can sometimes signal an underlying vision problem-particularly in children. His prolonged close-up work on devices, combined with very low outdoor activity and exposure to natural light had affected vision. This may cause the eyeball to grow longer than normal, causing light to focus in front of the retina instead of directly on it. As a result, distant objects appear blurry. From the moment we wake up to check our phones to hours spent on laptops at work and evenings scrolling through social media, screens have become an inseparable part of modern life. While digital devices have transformed the way we work, learn and communicate, prolonged and uninterrupted screen use is also putting increasing demands on our eyes. One of the most common consequences of prolonged screen use is digital eye strain. People may experience dryness, burning or irritation in the eyes, blurred vision, headaches, tired eyes and difficulty focusing after spending long periods looking at a screen. A major reason is that we tend to blink less while concentrating on digital content, allowing the surface of the eye to become dry. Simply looking at a screen does not mean that our eyes are being permanently damaged. However, prolonged, uninterrupted near work can cause significant discomfort and fatigue. The solution is not necessarily to abandon technology, but to use it more responsibly. The 20-20-20 rule can make a difference One of the simplest habits is the 20-20-20 rule after every 20 minutes of screen use, look at something around 20 feet away for at least 20 seconds. Regular breaks allow the eyes to relax and can reduce symptoms of digital eye strain. Blinking consciously and frequently is equally important. Screen users should also maintain an appropriate viewing distance, reduce glare and ensure that the screen is positioned slightly below eye level. If dryness persists, an eye specialist can advise whether lubricating eye drops are appropriate. Children need special attention The concern becomes particularly important in children. Increasing time spent on near-vision activities, combined with insufficient outdoor exposure, has been associated with the growing concern around myopia, or short-sightedness. WHO guidance recommends regular breaks during near work and encouraging children to spend adequate time outdoors in daylight. Parents should therefore avoid allowing children to spend long, uninterrupted periods on phones, tablets or gaming devices. Outdoor play should be made a regular part of a childs daily routine rather than treating it as an occasional activity. Dont blame everything on blue light There is also considerable confusion around blue light. While excessive exposure to bright screens in the evening can interfere with the bodys sleep-wake cycle, current evidence does not establish that the blue light emitted by ordinary digital screens causes retinal damage or age-related macular degeneration. Digital eye discomfort is more closely associated with prolonged or improper screen use. Therefore, rather than relying solely on blue-light-blocking glasses, people should focus on the fundamentals - regular breaks, adequate blinking, appropriate screen distance, good lighting and reduced screen use before bedtime. When should you see an eye specialist? Occasional tiredness after a long day on screens is usually not a cause for alarm. However, persistent blurred vision, frequent headaches, recurrent eye pain, redness, double vision, difficulty seeing distant objects or continuing dryness should not simply be attributed to screen use. A comprehensive eye examination can identify an underlying refractive error or other eye condition that may be contributing to the symptoms. Regular eye examinations are particularly important for children, as early detection of vision problems can help prevent them from affecting learning and daily activities. Screens are here to stay, but unhealthy screen habits dont have to be. Small behavioural changes - taking regular breaks, blinking more, spending time outdoors and getting periodic eye examinations - can go a long way towards keeping our eyes comfortable and our vision healthy in an increasingly digital world. The author is Chairman Managing Director, Centre for Sight Group of Eye Hospitals

articleTitle: Denied fee refund after daughter quit Indian school in 4 days, dad wins Rs 63,000 payout
articleFeaturedImageAlt: school fees USA Consumer court admission
description: The complainant’s daughter studied in the USA from Class 7 to 10 before joining a Hyderabad school for Class 11 in 2018, but allegedly struggled to keep up with the teaching method.
body_raw: A Hyderabad District Consumer Commission recently directed a school to pay Rs 63,000 to a father after his daughter left Class 11 after just four days of classes. The girl had studied in the US from classes 7 to 10 and allegedly struggled to adjust to the different teaching method. The commission held that a student cannot be charged for services that were not availed and that refusing to refund the unused fee amounted to an unfair trade practice. President Vakkanti Narasimha Rao, along with members P V T R Jawahar Babu and Suma Vala, also criticised the school, noting that it is well known that the number of candidates seeking admission far exceeds the available seats. The schools are doubly enriching themselves by admitting another candidate without refunding the fees of a student who has withdrawn their admission in mid-term. Such institutes have become commercial shops, and there cannot be any worse form of unscrupulous and unfair trade practice in the field of education, it added. The commission, while allowing the complaint filed by the 50-year-old man, noted that the parent allegedly paid Rs 48,000 in school fees besides a Rs 10,000 security deposit. A student may be at liberty to leave midstream if she finds the service deficient and non-yielding, and to tell her that fees once paid are not refundable was an unfair trade practice, as no service provider can take or charge the consideration of the service which it has either not given or has not been availed, the September 16 order read. Daughter struggled to adjust to US-to-India schooling The 50-year-old man said he approached the school to admit his daughter to Class 11 in the Science stream after she returned from the US. He said she was enrolled on August 20, 2018, and he paid Rs 10,000 as a security deposit and Rs 48,000 as school fees. The man said that at the schools request, he furnished a no-objection certificate relating to his daughters previous schooling in the US. She then attended the school for a few days but allegedly struggled to follow the lessons because of the difference in the method of teaching and presentation. He said he requested the school authorities to provide extra support and also sought a refund of the fee as his daughter had discontinued her studies. However, the request was denied by the school authority. Aggrieved, he moved the commission seeking refund and compensation. Schools defence The school, through advocate A Rajashekhar Reddy, emphasised that the Supreme Court held that education is not a commodity. It submitted that educational institutions do not provide a service and therefore there could be no question of deficiency in service in matters relating to admission or fees. The school also argued that the parent had agreed to its terms and conditions relating to the fee structure and had signed the declaration form required at the time of admission. Parent is consumer Commission The commission pointed out that fees are paid for services to be rendered by way of imparting education by the educational institutions. If there is no rendering of service, question of payment of fee would not arise, it added. It was also clarified that the complainant had hired the services of the school for a payment, so they are consumers as defined in the Consumer Protection Act. It added, imparting education by an educational institution for consideration falls within the ambit of service as defined under the Consumer Protection Act. The commission further added that if the student is not comfortable with the teaching methodsskills, they may leave the institution in between or mid-session or after attending for a few days.In our opinion, the educational institution or coaching centre for which such coaching centres or educational institutions should not be denied a refund of the fee for the remaining period, which heshe did not attend, the commission emphasised. It said no service provider can take or charge consideration of the service which neither it has provided nor has been availed. Pointing to the complainants daughters different educational background after studying in the USA, the commission said A student may leave midstream if she finds the service deficient and non-yielding, and to tell her that fees once paid are not refundable is gross unfair trade practice on the part of the opposite party school. Accordingly, the commission directed the school to refund the sum of Rs 58,000 from the date of payment along with costs of Rs 5,000 towards the litigation. Takeaway This ruling highlights that a no-refund policy cannot by itself allow a school to retain fees for a period during which a student did not avail the educational services. Aggrieved consumers may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states Telangana 0771-2582902 or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. articleTitle: NYC Council hearing on AI risks: What Jacob Coxon, others told policymakers
articleFeaturedImageAlt: NYC Council hearing
description: The hearing comes at a time when the New York City Council is examining legislative proposals to require companies to disclose information about AI tools.
body_raw: Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who quit his job last month over concerns that AI could lead to human extinction by the end of the decade, reiterated those warnings in a hearing by the New York City Council on Monday, October 5. The hearing was held to discuss the risks that AI poses to humanity. Officials from OpenAI, Google, Anthropic and Meta also appeared before the Council, but Elon Musks SpaceX was a no-show. In their testimonies, AI safety researchers who recently exited Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind, laid out a reckless culture at the firms. They said that the biggest tech companies are racing to create technology they do not understand how to control. Meanwhile, the tech industry representatives called for greater oversight by local governments in response to mounting concerns that advanced AI systems could endanger humanity. The hearing comes at a time when the Council is examining legislative proposals to require companies to disclose information about AI tools, require third-party approval for AI systems in the city, and allow whistleblowers to receive a portion of fines from AI companies that violate laws. New York Governor Kathy Hochul has also moved to impose reporting and transparency standards around AI. Policymakers elsewhere in the US and the rest of the world are also exploring measures to strengthen AI safety. These moves have been driven by the growing fear of AI systems causing catastrophic harm, coupled with a string of hacking incidents involving AI agents behaving unexpectedly. Last month, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for an intentional slowdown of frontier AI efforts across the world to let safety research catch up. The titans of the AI industry, including OpenAIs Sam Altman, SpaceXAIs Elon Musk, and Googles Demis Hassabis, were in rare agreement. But others like Nvidias Jensen Huang and US President Donald Trump dismissed these concerns as trivial and a hoax. What happened at the NYC Council hearing? The companies run on a startup mindset Move fast, break things, fix them later. That works for a photo sharing app. It does not work for building the most powerful technology ever built, Jacob Coxon, the Anthropic former engineer who has become a leading voice for regulation, was quoted as saying by Associated Press at the Council hearing. On the current path, I think it is more likely than not that humanity loses control to these AIs and it could end in human extinction, Coxon said. A panel of AI company staffers representing tech giants OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, also testified at the hearing. They told officials that their systems are already improving peoples daily lives and emphasised that safety was the top-most priority. Anthropic and OpenAI representatives said their advanced AI products need to be regulated. I share your commitment to ensuring that technology is developed safely and that its benefits are widely shared, said OpenAIs Morgan Dwyer. On whether the risk posed by AI could be quantified, Dwyer replied, I dont know - I also dont think it matters whether its 1 or 10 or 20 chance that something catastrophic will go wrong. None of these levels is remotely acceptable. We should not train models that we cannot make an extremely strong case that we can keep under human control. I would say that the percentage chance doesnt matter. What matters is the commitment to safety, and that is what OpenAI is committed to doing, he added. Anthropics Logan Graham told the Council that the company welcomes smart regulation and that state and local governments have a role to play in developing frameworks. AI is powerful enough that getting this wrong has real consequences, for individuals, institutions, public trust. We have to work relentlessly to do the science of mitigating the risks, he said.

articleTitle: Campaign dragged down by cross-voting and rebellion, Congress to probe Rajasthan local body poll performance
articleFeaturedImageAlt: According to party sources, Congress is preparing to take disciplinary action against councillors who won on the party symbol but voted for BJP candidates in the mayor and chairman elections held in 309 urban local bodies.
description: With over 400 councillors reportedly under scrutiny, CP Joshi-led panel asked to examine complaints and recommend action against those who cross-voted for BJP candidates in mayor and chairman polls
body_raw: The Rajasthan Pradesh Congress Committee PCC has constituted a nine-member committee to investigate complaints of cross-voting and other irregularities during the recently concluded municipal elections in the state. The committee, headed by former Assembly Speaker CP Joshi, has been asked to submit its report within seven days. According to party sources, Congress is preparing to take disciplinary action against councillors who won on the party symbol but voted for BJP candidates in the mayor and chairman elections held in 309 urban local bodies. Party leaders said reports identifying councillors suspected of cross-voting have been prepared from different districts. More than 400 Congress councillors are reportedly under scrutiny, though the exact number facing disciplinary action will be decided after the inquiry. PCC president Govind Singh Dotasra has formed the committee that includes Ram Singh Kaswan, Murari Lal Meena, Kuldeep Indora, Pramod Jain Bhaya, Shakuntala Rawat, Hakeem Ali, Ganesh Ghoghara and Raghuveer Singh Rathore as members. The panel will examine complaints received by the state Congress from several municipal bodies, including Bhilwara, Pali and Bharatpur, and submit its findings along with its comments to the PCC chief. The issue has also reached the AICC, with the party leadership expressing concern over cross-voting and rebellion in several municipal corporations, including Bikaner, Bharatpur, Ajmer, Kota and Pali. Dotasra was summoned to Delhi and asked to take action against those responsible, according to party sources. The party is also facing questions over the situation in Bhilwara, where 17 Congress candidates reportedly did not receive their symbols on time after they were issued from Jaipur. The incident followed differences between two Congress leaders, Dheeraj Gurjar and Ramlal Jat, who had opposed Dotasra. PCC officials said the Bhilwara matter could be dealt with by the AICC in Delhi rather than the state unit. Congress sources said the partys central leadership, including Rahul Gandhi and KC Venugopal, had taken note of the incident. The disciplinary action over cross-voting is likely to be taken after the CP Joshi-led committee submits its report. The inquiry will examine the complaints received by the PCC and establish the facts before the party decides on suspension or other action against councillors.

articleTitle: Two heads, one body: Rare turtle hatchling found on Cape Cod
articleFeaturedImageAlt: turtle
description: A rare two-headed diamondback terrapin hatchling has been discovered on Cape Cod, Massachusetts. Here’s what bicephaly means and why it occurs.
body_raw: A tiny turtle hatchling with two heads has been discovered on Cape Cod, Massachusetts, in a rare case that has caught the attention of wildlife experts. Researchers monitoring diamondback terrapins, a turtle species native to the salt marshes and coastal areas of the eastern United States, found the unusual terrapin. What made this hatchling different was immediately visible it had two distinct heads attached to a single body. The condition is known as bicephaly, a form of conjoined development in which an embryo develops two heads. It happens when an embryo doesnt fully separate during early development. While two-headed animals are exceptionally rare, this is not the first such turtle to turn up on Cape Cod. According to Live Science, the newly discovered hatchling is the third bicephalic terrapin found on Cape Cod in the past five years. The discovery is particularly unusual because researchers already closely monitor diamondback terrapins in the region. Finding multiple hatchlings with the same rare developmental abnormality has therefore raised questions about what might be happening during their development. A two-headed turtle does not necessarily have two completely separate bodies. Instead, the hatchling generally shares organs and other body structures, even though the two heads may function independently. That can make movement, feeding and other basic behaviours more difficult. The survival of such animals can also be uncertain. Depending on how extensively they share internal organs and other structures, some may struggle to survive long, while others can live considerably longer. For researchers, however, unusual hatchlings such as this one offer a rare glimpse into how development can sometimes take an unexpected turn. And while the sight of a tiny turtle with two heads may look almost otherworldly, the phenomenon itself is a developmental abnormality rather than evidence of a new or separate species. articleTitle: Before killing Ketan, Siya, Chetan searched law student’s Lohagad death, mushroom poisoning
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ketan Agarwal murder
description: The police, probing the June 18 murder of Agarwal (26) at Lohagad Fort, arrested his fiancée Siya (20) and Chaudhary (22) on June 23.
body_raw: The probe by Pune Rural police into the murder of Ketan Agarwal has revealed that his fiancee and accused Siya Goyal read online information about the death of a law student Manasi Govindpurkar in March 2025 and then she and her friend Chetan Chaudhary allegedly finalised Lohagad fort to murder Ketan. Police probe has also revealed that among various Internet and social media searches, Siya and Chetan had searched about Death Cap Mushroom, a deadly mushroom variety, and also about a woman who killed her family with mushroom in Australia a few years ago. The police, probing the June 18 murder of Agarwal 26 at Lohagad Fort, arrested his fiance Siya 20 and Chaudhary 22 on June 23. Police have also arrested Chetans friend Ritesh Hange 22 on September 5 for his alleged role in the conspiracy. In September the police filed a 5,053-page chargesheet against the trio charging them with murder and criminal conspiracy among others. Police have also invoked provisions of the Information Technology Act after probe revealed the accused used a fake Instagram handle carrying the name and identity of a fictitious friend of Siya named Mahi to chat with Ketan and to convince him to be at Lohagad Fort on June 18 to for the celebration of Siyas birthday the next day. The investigation has revealed Siya and Chetan were deliberating ways to stage the murder of Ketan as an accident. Around this time, Siya came across information about the death of Manasi Govindpurkar, a 21-year-old law student who had died after a fall from the cliff of Lohagad fort in March 2025. Subsequent to this Siya and Chetan allegedly finalised Lohagad Fort as the location to murder Ketan by pushing him down. Then they researched about the fort on the Internet and social media and also told Hange that the location had been finalised, said an officer who is part of the probe. Sources said this is part of the chargesheet filed by the police. The probe has also revealed details about various internet and social media searches by Siya and Chetan while allegedly hatching the murder conspiracy. An officer said, Analysis of deleted data of Siya and Chetans phones which was later retrieved has revealed their searches. Siya and Chetan searched for Death cap mushroom, a poisonous mushroom variety, and its availability in India. They also searched about the case in Australia. They also searched how to format Google history, how to format Google accounts and how to format iPhone. What initially appeared to be a tragic accident at Lohagad Fort later unravelled into a meticulously planned murder, as per the probe by police. Ketan, who was from a prominent realtor family of Pune, was allegedly pushed off a cliff at Lohagad fort on June 18 as part of a conspiracy allegedly orchestrated by Siya and Chetan. Siya and Ketan got engaged on February 19 and were to marry later this year. However, investigators claim Siya was in a relationship with Chetan since October last year and was unwilling to go ahead with the marriage.

articleTitle: Radhika Apte on men getting nervous during intimate scenes: ‘The vulnerability is real’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Radhika Apte talks about male vulnerability while filming intimacy
description: Vulnerability is the bridge between isolation and intimacy, between fear and real connection.
body_raw: Radhika Apte recently opened up about the awkwardness around filming intimate scenes, saying that its sweet to see men getting nervous. My generation of men and yours also, whenever they had to do intimate scenes, a lot of attention is given to women, obviously at the moment, because theres a change that needs to happen. That should be there. And I can literally hear their heart beating faster from nervousness. The vulnerability and nervousness in their bodies and minds is real, she shared with Filmfare while promoting her latest film Lust Stories 3. Many people think of vulnerability as a liability, a sign of emotional exposure or fragility. But in reality, vulnerability takes strength. Rutuja Walawalkar, Psychologist at Mpower, Aditya Birla Education Trust, says that it takes courage to admit when were unsure, afraid, or overwhelmed, especially in moments where were expected to be composed or in control. She shares that in therapy, relationships, or workspaces, vulnerability creates connection. It sends a silent message it gently says, You dont have to pretend here. Being human is enough. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Clinically, she says that vulnerability helps reduce emotional isolation. When we share our truth, we signal to others that we trust them and that trust invites empathy. Neuroscience backs this up our brains mirror neuron system lights up when we see someone express real emotion, triggering emotional resonance, Walawalkar tells indianexpress.com. Thats why honest moments build stronger connections between co-stars, friends, partners, or even coworkers. Research shows that people who are willing to show vulnerability are often seen as more relatable, emotionally intelligent, and trustworthy. According to Walawalkar, opening up can feel risky, especially if past experiences involved judgment or rejection. But being vulnerable doesnt mean spilling everything. It means sharing honestly and intentionally. What to keep in mind Walkwakar shares some easy ways to begin Start with safe people Open up with those whove shown empathy and care. Safety matters. Use small moments Vulnerability doesnt require big confessions. Saying, That was hard, or I feel unsure, can open the door to connection. Validate your emotions Before sharing, learn to honour your own feelings. Accepting them internally makes them easier to express. Let go of perfectionism You dont have to be flawless to be worthy. Your humanity is what draws others closer. Know your boundaries Vulnerability is thoughtful, not reckless. Share only what feels true to you and honours your emotional boundaries. Walawalkar says that in a society that idolises strength and composure, we often silence our real feelings. But Aptes story shows that its not flawless moments that connect us, but the honest ones. Her experience reminds us that true courage isnt about pretending were fearless its about choosing to share our fears with honesty and care.
