description: High Court Chief Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh elevated to Supreme Court
body_raw: President Droupadi Murmu has appointed three High Court chief justices - Justices Sunita Agarwal, Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Aparesh Kumar Singh as judges of the Supreme Court. The appointments were made in exercise of the powers conferred on the President by the Constitution of India, Union Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said in a post on X on Monday. In exercise of the powers conferred by the Constitution of India, the President of India is pleased to appoint the following Chief Justices of High Courts as Judges of the Supreme Court of India - Arjun Ram Meghwal arjunrammeghwal October 5, 2026 Justice Sunita Agarwal is the Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court, while Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya is the Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court. Both have the Allahabad High Court as their parent High Court. Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh is the Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court and has the Jharkhand High Court as his parent High Court. The Supreme Court Collegium had recommended the names on September 28. While the current working strength of the apex court is 34, once the three new judges formally take the oath, its effective strength will go up to 37. The top courts sanctioned strength is 38 judges, including the chief justice of India. It was recently increased from 34 following the Supreme Court Amendment Act, 2026. -With PTI inputs

articleTitle: Smart Cities Mission was a dream. That’s the problem with our urban vision
articleFeaturedImageAlt: smart cities mission, representative image
description: Dream projects privilege what can be seen over what is needed, what can be inaugurated over what is sustainable, and what can be advertised over what citizens experience
body_raw: Dream projects are common in Indian politics. Almost every politician has a dream project that often becomes an extension of their persona. The Smart Cities Mission was the biggest dream project in Indian history, and now that the Mission has ended, its record invites closer scrutiny. Can politicians just dream up urban development projects? A critical inquiry into the SCM reveals that political dreaming cannot be allowed to masquerade as urban planning. Dream projects tend to begin with advertisements of radical transformation that prove their feasibility through state narratives, rather than expert input or citizen experience - often even before the first brick is laid. The SCM was no different. The SCM was sold as a future-facing vision of urban India through narratives of integrated command centres, digitisation, and selected pockets of redevelopment. It promised to deliver urban development across the diverse landscape of India under the vague quality of smartness. This vagueness made SCM powerful as a political narrative. It allowed governments to package very different interventions under a single glamorous label and circulate them as proof of modern governance. It was an effective national public-relations machine. Like all other dream projects, the image of promised transformation was sustained through the device of the showcase. The Missions Area-Based Development model concentrated resources in bounded precincts where rapid visual change could be staged and photographed as transformation. For example, a 2025 study by Sarbeswar Praharaj found that, across the 100 cities, SCM interventions reached less than 10 per cent of the population, and in 41 cities, the ABD area covered less than 10 per cent of municipal territory and just 5 per cent of total population. In cities such as Ludhiana, Ahmedabad, and Jaipur, areas affecting only 0.5 per cent of the city received around 20 per cent of total investment. In other words, the mission produced enclaves of display and then promoted those enclaves as the city. Dream projects, therefore, privilege what can be seen over what is needed, what can be inaugurated over what is sustainable, and what can be advertised over what citizens experience. While a command-and-control centre, a smart road, or a digitally branded service platform travels well in photographs and speeches, cities are made habitable through good drainage, affordable housing, and ward-level repair. Sadly, they do not make good visual material. Dream projects tend to be top-down in their approach. They tend to fit the city to the politicians dream, rather than let local needs guide project formulation. And hence, they weaken local governance. The SCM worked similarly. Projects were routed through Special Purpose Vehicles that operated as parallel structures to local bodies. The SPVs were justified by the claim that municipalities lacked capacity. But instead of strengthening local bodies or building that capacity, the SCM worked around them. This reproduced a familiar constitutional weakness and simply recreated the greatest problem in Indian urbanism That the third tier remains the weakest, urban local bodies are fiscally dependent, and key decisions continue to be shaped by state and central actors. The people who best understood local conditions did not have decisive authority under the SCM, and the project did nothing to change that. This centralised nature of dream projects ignores an important reality, as dreams do. Indian cities do not suffer from one generic problem awaiting one generic solution. Chennais flood risk, Surats industrial expansion, Guwahatis uneven growth, Jaipurs heritage pressures, Bengalurus mobility crisis, and small-city deficits are contextually rooted issues. Predictably, then, SCM struggled to address local needs. It encouraged cities to retrofit themselves to a nationally legible template of smartness. It privileged roads, parking, digitised monitoring, and visible capital works over the everyday infrastructures on which most residents depend. For instance, a 2021 study by Bajpai and Biberman found that nearly 40 per cent of Smart Cities transport funding went to roads and parking, compared to only 2 per cent for buses. This brings us to a critical point. For their rhetorical work, dream projects implement a distinct visual politics. They are often represented from above-through drone footage, aerial panoramas, and before-and-after imagery that showcase mastery over landscape, showing urban development as an image of command. This perspective is not accidental. From the air, the project appears like a coherent success - the dream made true - while the experience of citizens on the ground or the displacement that the project might have caused never makes the cut. Citizens then enter the frame not as citizens with agency, or authors of planning or users of the city, but merely as dots in the drone shots or moving images - proof that the dream has been realised. This is probably the most corrosive feature of dream projects. They treat people as an audience, sometimes even as props, rather than as citizens with knowledge and claims. Participation becomes procedural or theatrical. Consultations are often held much after the direction has been dreamt of. Dashboards invite complaints, but in the face of weakened local bodies, those complaints cannot be equitably handled. And eventual inaugurations visually include the public in the success narrative while excluding them from the actual workings or visions of the project. Citizens merely validate the symbol of development. They dont shape its content, and can never narrate its failures. Fortunately, the Indian urban experience also offers a different tradition. Projects that have worked better are often those that were not announced as someones dream. Odishas Jaga Mission, initiatives by federations such as SPARC, NSDF, and Mahila Milan have succeeded because they worked from the ground upwards. They addressed daily use and social context. But these efforts are less photogenic, less centralised, and less suited to political mythmaking. They are, but, democratic and durable. Let me be clear. This is not an argument against aspiration. Cities need aspiration. They need vision. Aspiration makes us ask better questions about what collective life could become. But aspiration begins in inquiry and curiosity it is tested against evidence, revised through professional expertise, and made answerable to situated knowledge. A dream, by definition, is detached from reality. It begins with a finished image and then demands that reality be rearranged to validate it. Most post-mortems of SCM have shied away from this fundamental problem. Dreaming by a politician is not planning. It privileges charisma over diagnosis, visibility over equity, and legacy over expertise. Building castles in the air is not the problem. We must dream. But as the American essayist Henry Thoreau said, we must then put foundations beneath them. The Smart Cities Mission did the reverse. It spent a decade suspending a glamorous urban future in the air while too often leaving the boring foundations of city life unattended. The French poet Paul Valry gave more humbling advice The best way to make your dreams come true is to wake up, he said. Let go of dreams-not because cities should abandon ambition, but because they deserve something more demanding than fantasy. They deserve the discipline of waking up. Zuberi is a PhD Scholar at Massachusetts Institute of Technology. He writes on history, politics, architecture and cities

articleTitle: No outsiders at LPU, walkie-talkie carriers were Army men: Punjab Police
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lovely Professional University, Lovely Professional University news, LPU unrest, LPU protest, Lovely Professional University unrest, LPU student protest, LPU campus news, Army personnel at LPU, LPU walkie-talkie men, Punjab Police, LPU vandalism, LPU students unrest, Phagwara LPU news, LPU investigation, Indian Express news
description: The Punjab Police said the Army personnel were identified after questioning, amid claims by political leaders that outsiders had been brought onto the LPU campus.
body_raw: The people carrying walkie-talkie sets who were found on the Lovely Professional University LPU campus in Punjabs Phagwara during the students unrest have turned out to be Indian Army officers and personnel from a Special Forces battalion of the Parachute Regiment. Speaking to The Indian Express, Naveen Singla, Deputy Inspector General DIG, Jalandhar Range, said the police questioned the men after finding them carrying the walkie-talkie sets and established that they were Army personnel. They had come to collect the ward of an Army officer, and they were not intruders of any kind, Singla said. Several political leaders cited the discovery of the walkie-talkie-carrying personnel as evidence that outsiders had been brought onto the LPU campus to create trouble. Meanwhile, the police have formed a Special Investigation Team SIT to investigate the incident that triggered the unrest at LPU. The team comprises Jalandhar Rural Superintendent of Police Detective Vineet Ahlawat, Phagwara SP Major Singh, CIA Staff in-charge Balwinder Singh and Inspector Amanpreet Kaur, along with CCTV experts. Five student representatives have also been included to assist with the investigation. Singla said he held a meeting Monday with the LPU vice-chancellor, other university officials, and student representatives to discuss their grievances and work towards resolving them. There are certain demands of the students which they have conveyed to the LPU authorities and which will be addressed. Everything is peaceful now and around 14,000 students have left for their homes after the announcement of a ten-day break, he said. The DIG said he also met a girl staying in one of the hostels, from where complaints had emerged, and spoke to them in detail. He said the students had certain apprehensions, following which the police decided to register an FIR and conduct a detailed investigation into the matter. Conscious decision not to use force On Monday, Gaurav Yadav, Director General of Police DGP Punjab, visited the LPU campus and spoke to the media following the student unrest. Yadav said the trouble began on the night of September 26-27 after rumours of certain incidents on campus. A large number of students gathered, following which there was vandalism and part of a gate was set on fire. The police had made a conscious decision not to use force against students as they are like our children and instead acted as a bridge between students and the university administration, Yadav said. He added that they held discussions with students and the university administration to address their grievances, including the demand for only women staff in girls hostels. Yadav said those responsible for arson and vandalism would face strict action, irrespective of their position. The police are examining CCTV footage and investigating whether outsiders were involved, he added. He also appealed to people not to spread or believe unverified rumours.

articleTitle: Why Samajwadi Party fielded Reliance executive Dhanraj Nathwani in Rajya Sabha polls
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Why Samajwadi Party fielded Reliance executive Dhanraj Nathwani in Rajya Sabha polls
description: Opposition party's leaders cite Ram Manohar Lohia to claim that Nathwani's candidature not a departure from socialist ethos.
body_raw: The Samajwadi Partys SP decision to nominate corporate executive Dhanraj Nathwani for the Rajya Sabha election has raised questions about the political messaging behind the choice, particularly when the party is building its 2027 Uttar Pradesh campaign around the Pichhda, Dalit aur Alpasankhyak, or PDA, plank. Nathwani is the son of top Reliance Industries executive Parimal Nathwani, the Director of Corporate Affairs for Reliance Industries Ltd RIL, who was re-elected to the Rajya Sabha from Jharkhand as an NDA-backed Independent this June, securing his fourth consecutive term in the Upper House. The 40-year-old has been associated with Reliance Industries for about 16 years. He oversees the groups Jamnagar manufacturing division, one of the worlds largest integrated refining and petrochemical complexes, and also works with Reliance Jio in Gujarat. Nathwani also leads the engineering, procurement, and construction vertical and supervises all construction and infrastructure projects in the Reliance ecosystem. He also oversees Reliance Jio Defence System Ltd, which focuses on high-tech manufacturing of advanced military equipment and aerospace propulsion systems. The decision initially surprised sections within and outside the party. Senior SP leaders, however, maintain that the party will field a third candidate who will be from a PDA community, potentially a Dalit or a Muslim. The party, however, does not have the numbers on its own to get a third candidate elected. The SP and the Congress together effectively have 102 MLAs on their side, with the numbers enough to elect two MPs 37 first-preference votes are required. They are, however, nine first-preference votes short of getting a third candidate elected. As of now, the SP has announced the candidatures of veteran Ram Gopal Yadav and Nathwani. This is where a candidate such as Nathwani becomes important. The arithmetic of the contest has brought the possibility of attempts at cross-voting to the fore. SP leaders claimed that some BJP MLAs who feel they may not be considered for another term could be open to supporting the Opposition candidate. In tune with socialist politics Within the SP, the candidature is being defended not as a departure from its socialist ethos, but as an attempt to widen both its social and industry outreach. His selection is in tune with the socialist ideology. Ram Manohar Lohia talked of sampannata aur samta prosperity and equality going hand in hand. When there are people who are taxpayers, they help build the welfare state, a party leader said, explaining the rationale behind Nathwanis candidature. The SP argues that Nathwanis corporate background should not be viewed as an ideological departure, presenting the candidature as part of an existing, if limited, effort to establish a relationship with the business and corporate community and expand its political constituency. An SP leader cited the example of businessman Sanjay Seth who was elected to the Rajya Sabha on an SP ticket in 2016. Seth later joined the BJP in 2019 and was subsequently re-elected to the Rajya Sabha as a BJP member. Now it is our turn. There are many within the BJP who are unhappy and want to join. We are not sure how much and what kind of space we would be able to give them, but they are ready to support us. The upcoming Rajya Sabha election will make it clear when we field the third candidate, the leader said. We are fielding the third candidate and it would be from PDA. But what is important is the perception that Nathwanis inclusion will create. Imagine, in the current situation, if someone from the corporate sector is seeing an opportunity in the SP, it means they are seeing prospects in the SP. It is a good narrative for us before 2027 and also at the national front, said another SP leader. Internal reading in SP The internal reading in the SP is that the candidature can help counter the perception that the SPs political appeal is restricted to its traditional social constituencies. A corporate executive agreeing to contest for the party is being seen by party leaders as evidence that the party is seeking - and attracting - constituencies beyond its conventional political base. This, party leaders said, could be helpful in the run-up to the 2027 elections. The BJP is also closely watching the developments, with the Nathwani nomination taking many in the ruling party by surprise. For a party preparing for a 2027 contest in which it wants to present itself as a broad-based political alternative, the Nathwani nomination allows the SP to make a different argument that PDA politics and engagement with the corporate sector are not mutually exclusive and that economic prosperity and social equality can be presented as parallel components of its political narrative.

articleTitle: Chamoli officials, Army lock horns after row over Uttarakhand music festival
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Badrinath festival, Badrinath festival row, Indian army, Satpal Maharaj, Badrinath temple conch row, conch made of bone claim, Suryakant Dhasmana, Devbhoomi Cultural Festival 2026, Priyanka Meher Badrinath performance, Murli Manohar Joshi Badrinath row, Operation Sadbhavana Chamoli, Pushkar Singh Dhami, Sanatan tradition conch shell science, Uttarakhand politics news
description: Army sources tell Express that the programme at the shrine, which is now being criticised, was held with the knowledge of all stakeholders
body_raw: Days after the Chamoli administration wrote to the Indian Army seeking an explanation on the Devbhoomi Cultural Festival held at Badrinath, no communication has reached the official Army channel yet, The Indian Express has learnt. This comes as documents from the Chamoli administration, which has sought to distance itself from the cultural programme following criticism over music and dance performances, show that it was responsible for coordinating the event. Speaking to The Indian Express, Army sources said that the programme at the shrine was held with the knowledge of all stakeholders. Asked about their response to the District Magistrates communication, one source said, We have not received any communication as of yet. The two-day Devbhoomi Cultural Festival was held on September 19 and 20 at the Tourist Arrival Plaza in Badrinath under the Armys Operation Sadbhavana in collaboration with the district administration and Uttarakhand Tourism. The district administrations own documents show that a senior official was tasked with coordinating it. In an order dated September 8, District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar said the festival was proposed for September 19 and 20 and designated the Chief Development Officer, Chamoli, as the nodal officer. It is hereby ordered that the Devbhoomi Cultural Festival 2026, proposed to be organised on 19 and 20 September 2026 at the Tourist Arrival Plaza at Badrinath, be conducted successfully and that the necessary arrangements for the event be ensured, the order said, directing the nodal officer to ensure that all necessary arrangements are made for the successful conduct of the proposed Devbhoomi Cultural Festival 2026. A communication issued by the DMs office on September 9 also refers to correspondence from the Commanding Officer, Garhwal Scouts, Joshimath, dated August 11, regarding arrangements for the festival. It stated that a meeting had been convened under the chairmanship of the Chief Development Officer, Chamoli, at 1130 am on September 10 to discuss arrangements for the event, and asked officials to attend. You are requested to kindly ensure your presence at the meeting on the scheduled date and time and participate in the discussion regarding the arrangements for the festival, the order said. A second communication issued the same day similarly refers to the Army correspondence and lists officials from the police, health, tourism, transport, supplies, sports and other departments. The documents come against the backdrop of a subsequent letter from the District Magistrate to Colonel Shantanu, Commanding Officer, Garhwal Rifles, 56 APO, seeking clarification over the festival. In that letter, the DM said, It has come to our notice through various communicationssocial media platforms that a Cultural Festival programme was organised by you at Shri Badrinath Dham. The letter asks Colonel Shantanu to clarify whether you had obtained permission for organising such a programme at Shri Badrinath Dham and, if so, from which authority. It also asks whether permission was obtained and seeks reasons for using a high-volume sound system. Colonel Shantanu did not respond to requests for comment. The DMs letter says Badrinath is a sacred religious place and that using a high-volume sound system was contrary to the sanctity of the shrine and could affect regular worship and rituals. You are also requested to ensure that such an incident does not recur at Shri Badrinath Dham in future, it added. The DM was unavailable for comment. The event came under criticism after videos of performances circulated on social media, including a performance by Uttarakhand singer Priyanka Meher, which featured music and dancing and brought the first day of the festival to a close. Former BJP president Murli Manohar Joshi was among those who objected to the programme.

articleTitle: ‘Illegal, unauthorised’: Election Commissioners objected to Form 6 change
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Illegal, unauthorised...(it’s) harassment of young: ECs object to change in Form 6
description: The section itself was not marked mandatory, but applicants could not proceed to submit the form without answering it.
body_raw: The change is illegal, unauthorised, it needs to be sent to the Government.it must be removed immediately so that young, first-time voters are not harassed. The warning by the two Election Commissioners couldnt have been clearer - and yet it was ignored. The change brought questions related to SIR into Form 6, the form new voters have to fill. It asked applicants to choose one of three statements whether their name appeared in electoral roll during the last SIR held in the early 2000s, whether the name of a parent or grandparent appeared in that roll, or whether neither their name nor that of their parents appeared in it. The section itself was not marked mandatory, but applicants could not proceed to submit the form without answering it. Internal records investigated by The Indian Express show this declaration was added despite two of the Commissions three members recording in May that it could not be done without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, notified by the Centre after consultation with the Election Commission. 2 Commissioners, 1 warning On May 16, responding to the proposal to change Form 6 through the SIR framework, Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded his objections. The SIR, he noted, was being conducted under Section 213 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 - the provision that lets the Commission order a special revision of the roll - as one time measure and exception. The forms prescribed for the SIR were specific to that exercise and were non-statutory, or not part of law, he wrote. Form 6 and Form 8 for making changes and corrections they are prescribed statutorily and cannot be altered without making amendments in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. Joshi specifically rejected the idea that a sentence in an SIR order or guideline could change a form fixed by law. His conclusion was that the best and legally sustainable course of action would be to send the proposal to the Government for changes to the rules. He also proposed that a draft of the changes to Form 6 and Form 8 be put before the Commission immediately. On May 19, his colleague on the panel Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred with Joshi on file. On July 12, The Indian Express first reported on the new declaration in Form 6 on the Commissions ECINet portal. On August 13, referring to The Indian Express report, Sandhu wrote to the Deputy Election Commissioner and the Director General in charge of IT, with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and Joshi copied on the note. Sandhu recalled Joshis May 16 note, with which he had agreed, that Form 6 was a statutory form embedded in the rules and could not be changed without approval from the competent authority - meaning, the Government. In spite of these very clear views expressed by two Election Commissioners, Sandhu wrote, the unauthorised illegal changes in Form-6 on the portal had not been removed and the original form had not been restored. The changes must be removed immediately so that young and would-be first time voters, who are otherwise eligible, can register themselves as voters as per law, without any harassment, he wrote. What the addition means The right to vote belongs to the individual a person qualifies by age, citizenship and residence, not by whether their parents made it through the last revision. And, in a deeply contested SIR where over 13 crore people have already been dropped from the list, inserting such a question puts a shadow on their children as well. Indeed, the new question on Form 6 mattered most to new voters whose parents or grandparents did not figure in the rolls prepared after the last SIR. An 18-year-old in such a family could not truthfully choose either of the first two options, and the form did not explain what would happen if they chose the third. It also assumes significance because there is already a clear route for changing Form 6. In 2021, Parliament amended the Representation of the People Act, 1950 to allow the Commission to collect Aadhaar numbers from voters. That change to Form 6 was not made by the Commission itself on June 17, 2022, the Law Ministrys Legislative Department notified the corresponding changes to the Registration of Electors Rules and Form 6. It was against this legal framework that the proposed SIR-linked change to Form 6 came before the Commission this year.

articleTitle: CJI says Supreme Court did not approve Form 6 changes: What the form is, why it matters
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Form 6 mess: People served SIR (Special Intensive Revision) notices arrive at Appasaheb Kulkarni Primary School in Gokhalenagar on Monday with their documents. (Express Photo - Arul Horizon)
description: The voter enrolment form was changed to include questions linked to the special intensive revision, prompting objections over the legal process followed.
body_raw: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday October 5 said that the Supreme Court had not approved any of the modifications to Form 6 in response to an argument on the unlawful modifications made to Form 6. While hearing petitions against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, a three-judge bench headed by the CJI said the Supreme Court will examine who modified the form after receiving a report from the Election Commission. The latest development comes two weeks after The Indian Express investigation on September 23 that revealed that two Election Commissioners had flagged the illegal and unauthorised changes to Form 6. One petition accused the Chief Election Commissioner of deliberately manipulating the electoral roll bears no reasonable nexus or legal connection to his official duties. Such an act falls squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constitutes distinct, personal criminal liability, it added. What is Form 6? Form 6 is the statutory form for applicants who have newly become eligible voters after turning 18 years of age or acquiring Indian citizenship or deleted voters who want to apply afresh. The existing Form 6, which is published in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, asks the applicant to provide the name and EPIC number of those family members with whom they currently reside. The Indian Express reported on July 12 that the online version of the form on ECINET had a new declaration inserted between the above two sections. The change introduced questions related to the Special Intensive Revision SIR into Form 6. It asked applicants to choose one of three statements whether their name appeared in the electoral roll during the last SIR held in the early 2000s, whether a parents or grandparents name appeared in that roll, or whether neither their name nor that of their parents appeared in it. If their name appeared in the 2000s SIR, applicants were asked to provide the Assembly constituency number, the polling booth number known as part number and the serial number at which their father or mother was registered in the last SIR. Interestingly, the Form 6 available for download on the EC portal did not have this declaration. Why was the change disputed? The Indian Express investigation revealed that Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi had formally objected to decisions taken and orders issued without their knowledge at least 14 times over 10 months. The changes under scrutiny concerned the national rollout of the SIR. After The Indian Express reported on the updated Form 6 on ECINET in July, Sandhu put on record on August 13 that it was unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately. Since the move was without amendment, the two Election Commissioners had objected to the same. Under the Representation of the People Act, 1950, only the central government can amend the voter enrolment, deletion and correction forms. On September 26, the Election Commission announced it had removed the SIR declaration in Form 6 on the ECINET application portal in states where the SIR has concluded. However, the declaration was still there for those states where the SIR is still ongoing. The EC said, For non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used. Interestingly, the ECs press note did not mention the online form, or the question, or say whether it has been removed. However, it said that the Supreme Court upheld the declaration, which the courts May 27 order on the SIR does not appear to do in terms. And it does not say who put the question there in July, or why it stayed after Sandhu called it unauthorisedillegal on August 13. What does the law say? Article 326 of the Constitution guarantees the right to enrol as an elector to all adult citizens who are ordinarily resident in a particular Assembly constituency, unless otherwise disqualified by law. The Representation of the People Act, 1950 empowers the Union government to make rules for the conduct of elections and the registration of electors. Section 28 of the Act, titled Power to make rules, says The Central Government may, after consulting the Election Commission by notification in the Official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act. It also says that every rule made under the Act shall be laid, as soon as may be after it is made, before each House of Parliament. Form 6 is a part of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, which emerges from the Act. Therefore, any change to the form would require an amendment and gazette notification by the Law and Justice Ministry. However, the ministry did not notify any change to Form 6, as seen in the notifications available on the e-Gazette website from June 24, 2025 - when the EC first announced the SIR - to date.

articleTitle: Qazi Touqeer does 100 push-ups in one go on Bigg Boss 20: ‘My warm-up’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Qazi Touqeer’s 100 Pushups Challenge
description: Taking to Instagram, the 2005 Fame Gurukul winner shared: "100 push ups is my warm up! Abhi toh I am just gearing up! Stay tuned for more."
body_raw: Bigg Boss Season 20 contestant Qazi Touqeer has impressed viewers with his fitness prowess. In a recent episode of the reality show, the 2005 Fame Gurukul winner completed 100 push-ups in one go. Taking to Instagram, he shared 100 push-ups is my warm-up Abhi toh I am just gearing up Stay tuned for more. Dr Shreyas Kathrani, HOD, Department of Physiotherapy, Jaslok Hospital and Research Centre, Mumbai, says that push-ups are the most democratic exercise-for which you require no gym, no gear, just floor space. DISCLAIMER This article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your fitness practitioner before starting any routine. Done right, pushups build functional upper-body strength, bulletproof your core, and train shoulder stability that helps in daily life. High-rep sets also give you a cardio spike, though they dont replace walking, running, or cycling, he tells indianexpress.com. According to him, our focus should be less on the number and more about what it signals disciplined, high-frequency training over decades. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Qazi Touqeer qazitouqeerofficial For the average person, he says that crossing even 50 reps means youve moved from strength into endurance territory. It lights up the chest, shoulders, triceps, and core, and if your form slips mid-set, the shoulders and lower back take the hit instead, he tells indianexpress.com. For beginners, he suggests starting with wall or incline pushups and build from that. 10 clean reps are better than 30 sloppy ones, he says. If your goal is to build strength and muscle, he recommends aiming for 815 perfect reps where the last 2 feel hard. Add harder variations when it gets easy, he says. And for general fitness, 2030 solid pushups is a great benchmark in Indias fitness community. What to keep in mind When doing push ups, Dr Vajalla Shravani, MPT, fitness and pilates expert at Tone30 Pilates, says one of the biggest mistakes is prioritising quantity over quality. Many people rush to increase reps without building the proper foundational strength or focusing on form. This often leads to compensations like sagging hips, flared elbows, or incomplete range of motion, which not only reduces effectiveness but can lead to injury, she tells indianexpress.com. To improve safely, she suggests that its helpful to break push ups into progressions Start with wall or incline pushups, then move to knee pushups before graduating to full pushups. Strength training that targets the chest, shoulders, triceps, and core can also complement your pushup practice, adds Dr Shravani. According to her, another overlooked aspect is recovery. articleTitle: How Amitabh Bachchan & Amish Tripathi are taking Indian mythology global through gaming
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Age of Bhaarat - Visual (1)
description: The Age of Bhaarat is a dark fantasy action adventure game that draws on Indian epics and traditions.
body_raw: Ancient India is a land of noble heroes and glittering cities. But, where heroes rule, villains will attack. Where wealth is plentiful, plunderers will pillage, says Amitabh Bachchan in the trailer of the game, The Age of Bhaarat. Your time has come to declare war, he says as the screen crackles with images of fire bursting out of the ruins of grand sculptured pillars. Bachchan is the co-founder of Tara Gaming Ltd, gamemakers for PCs and consoles that features mythical landscapes and magical characters and stories drawn from the Indian epics. The other eminent founder is Amish Tripathi, author of Shiva Trilogy. Tara Gamings vision is a large franchise that is aimed at telling Indian stories in a way that resonates worldwide. The Age of Bhaarat, for instance, is a dark fantasy action-adventure game that draws on Indian epics and traditions to inspire an international audience to undertake a journey of an ordinary person who becomes a powerful Forest Warden armed with magical capabilities. This is possibly Indias first AAA action adventure game, which is the hallmark of a high profile, big-budget game of top production capability. The game is currently under development and is expected to hit the markets in a couple of years. The studio where the game is being developed is in Pune. There is an immense combination of the richness of mythology, their novelty to the West, their relevance in India and the talent in India and, particularly, in Pune. When we started, the first thing we did was hiring a head for a studio in Pune, Siddharth Singh. In about 18 months, we grew the studio to 85 people, says executive chairman Nicolas Granatino. Gaming has caught the interest of the Central government as well. In the Union Budget this year, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had spoken of the rapid growth of Indias animation, visual effects, gaming and comics AVGC sector, he added. Singh said, a lot of times, the Indian industry has worked as vendors or outsourcers for foreign companies. They come in and give us a part of the work. Not a lot of companies in India have done this kind of large-scale execution, from the initial ideation and concept phase all the way through to the final launch. So, not many people have actually seen or experienced the entire lifecycle of game development in India, and thats where Tara Gaming is different. We have also managed to bring together the right kind of talent, says Singh. While Tripathi is responsible for crafting the lore of the game, Bachchan is involved in the creative process and provides the voiceover for the games trailer. The rest of the team is equally rooted to the story. Success is not only bringing a successful game and these stories to the world. For us, success is that some of the people in the studio in Pune will leave a few years from now and create their own studio, because they will have seen the production of the game from scratch. Thats a very different way to train and upskill and work with talent in India, says Granatino.

articleTitle: 3 years after Umesh Pal murder, UP Police trace wanted accused to Bihar jail
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Umesh Pal murder case
description: The Uttar Pradesh Police are moving court for a warrant to bring Mohammad Arman from Bihar's Gaya jail to Prayagraj in connection with the February 2023 Umesh Pal murder case.
body_raw: Three years after advocate Umesh Pal and his two police security personnel were shot dead in Prayagrajs Dhoomanganj area, the Uttar Pradesh Police have traced a wanted accused carrying a reward of Rs 5 lakh to a jail in Bihar. The police said the accused, Mohammad Arman, was allegedly associated with the gang of slain Prayagraj mafia figure Atiq Ahmed. The Uttar Pradesh Police had been searching for Arman for the past three years after his alleged role in the murder of advocate Umesh Pal and his two security personnel emerged during the investigation. Arman was allegedly riding the motorcycle on which another wanted accused, Guddu Muslim, was travelling as a pillion rider. A senior police officer said they learnt about a week ago that Arman was lodged in a jail in Bihars Gaya district in connection with an old case. A police team subsequently verified the information with their counterparts in Gaya. We will approach the Prayagraj court on Monday seeking a B-warrant to bring him to Prayagraj in connection with the murder of Umesh Pal and his two security personnel, the senior police officer said. The police said that during the preliminary inquiry, they learnt that after the murder of Umesh Pal and his two security personnel, Arman went to Gaya and surrendered before a court in connection with an old firing case after getting his bail cancelled. He has remained lodged in Gaya jail since then. During the preliminary inquiry, police found that Arman, a native of Bihar, allegedly ran a food stall in Prayagrajs Civil Lines area, where he came into contact with associates of Atiq Ahmed who visited the stall. Police said he later began working with Atiq Ahmed and expanded his business with money he allegedly earned through criminal activities. Arman is among the six accused wanted in connection with the murder of advocate Umesh Pal and his two police security personnel on February 24, 2023, in Prayagrajs Dhoomanganj area. Umesh Pal was attacked as he got out of his car near the entrance to his house. The assailants opened fire and hurled bombs at him and his two police bodyguards before fleeing the spot in a vehicle. Four accused killed in encounters The police have so far gunned down four accused in the case in crossfire. Atiq Ahmed and his younger brother Ashraf, also accused in the case, were shot dead in April 2023 while they were in police custody, in an incident that was broadcast live on television. Among the six wanted persons are three members of gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmeds family - his wife Shaista Parveen, sister-in-law Zainab Fatima Ashrafs wife and elder sister Ayesha Noori. Shaista Parveen carries a reward of Rs 50,000, while a reward of Rs 25,000 has been announced for Ayesha Noori. Two other wanted accused in the case, Guddu Muslim and Sabir, carry a reward of Rs 5 lakh each for information leading to their arrest. Umesh Pal was a witness in the murder case of Bahujan Samaj Party BSP MLA Raju Pal, who was shot dead in Prayagraj in 2005, in which Atiq Ahmed and his brother Ashraf were accused.

articleTitle: Firing distance raised suspicion: How an ‘accidental’ shooting in Lonavala turned into a murder case
articleFeaturedImageAlt: accidental shooting in Lonavala, Lonavala accidental shooting, Lonavala police murder case, Motiram Marathe arrested, Advocate Abhay Manik Marathe, Lonavala lawyer shooting, Bhushi village property dispute, Hotel Motiram Lonavala, Sassoon Hospital post mortem, Sandeep Singh Gill SP, Lonavala city police station, family property dispute murder, 12 bore gun shooting Lonavala
description: Lonavala City police have arrested Motiram Marathe for allegedly shooting dead his 33-year-old grandson, advocate Abhay Manik Marathe, at Hotel Motiram in Bhushi village on Monday.
body_raw: A shooting initially reported as an accidental firing at a hotel in Lonavala turned into a murder investigation after the post-mortem examination found that the bullet had been fired from a distance of around 30 centimetres, police said. The investigation subsequently revealed a property dispute between the deceased and his 83-year-old grandfather, who later allegedly confessed to shooting him. Lonavala City police have arrested Motiram Marathe for allegedly shooting dead his 33-year-old grandson, advocate Abhay Manik Marathe, at Hotel Motiram in Bhushi village on Monday. Police have also booked four other family members for allegedly attempting to destroy evidence and conceal the crime. Family initially claimed accidental firing According to police, Motiram, who holds a valid licence for a 12-bore rifle that he used for hunting, was at the hotel when the incident took place. Motiram Marathe holds a valid arms licence for a 12-bore gun, which he used for hunting. The family said that the incident took place on Monday. They told police that Abhay was cleaning his grandfathers gun when the trigger was accidentally pulled and a bullet hit him in the chest, Superintendent of Police Sandeep Singh Gill said at a press conference on Tuesday. Lonavala City police initially registered the case as an accidental death after reaching the spot. However, officers began to suspect that the familys account did not match the circumstances at the scene. Police examined the firearm, the injury to Abhays chest and the bloodstains on the wall, and sent the body to Sassoon Hospital for a post-mortem examination. The post-mortem findings further raised suspicion. Police said doctors found that the bullet had been fired from a distance of around 30 centimetres, making the claim of an accidental firing while cleaning the rifle difficult to establish. Property dispute emerges during probe As part of the investigation, police questioned family members as well as the hotel manager and staff. They found that Abhay and his grandfather had been involved in a dispute over land and its development. Motiram wanted to sell their land and distribute the money among family members however, Abhay had different plans for the land development, which led to the dispute, Gill said. Gill said the nature of the firearm also added to the suspicion. Also, a 12-bore rifle, which is around 4 to 4.5 feet long, so using it to fire towards self is difficult. So the suspicion increased. Even when inquired with the hotel staff and manager, they also said that for quite some time there have been quarrels between the two regarding financial and land-related matters, he said. Police said the two were at the restaurant counter of Hotel Motiram around 11 am on Monday when they had a heated argument. During the argument, Motiram allegedly took his licensed 12-bore rifle and shot Abhay in the chest. The bullet proved fatal. Police said the two had a history of disagreements over land and financial matters. Police allege attempt to destroy evidence The investigation also led police to suspect an attempt to cover up the shooting. According to Gill, CCTV cameras near the spot were allegedly removed and the DVR containing the footage was taken away. Police also alleged that hotel staff were threatened against speaking about the incident. The body was displaced to a different location and even the weapons were taken away to a different location. So we have booked five of the family members, Gill said. Police said that while it was initially difficult to determine whether the shooting was accidental or deliberate because family members maintained that it was an accidental firing, the post-mortem findings and subsequent investigation strengthened the murder suspicion. Police said Motiram later confessed to the crime. Initially the family members denied but the accused Motiram confessed to the crime. The three family members-Motiram Marathe, Hiraman Motiram Marathe, and Manoj Hiraman Marathe-have been granted police custody till October 12, Sachin Patil, senior police inspector, Lonavala City police station, told The Indian Express. Police have also booked Kavita Hiraman Marathe and Rajashree Dashrath Pawar, sister of Hiraman Marathe. Marathe familys business political links Abhay was the son of Manik Marathe, a former councillor of the Lonavala municipal council. The Marathe family owns Hotel Motiram and Manik Moti in Bhushi village and is involved in the beer bar business. The family also runs a petrol pump in Lonavala, according to people familiar with the family. Macchindra Kharade, former Shiv Sena Pune district chief and a close associate of Manik Marathe, said the family had been living together for several years. The Marathe family has always been involved in business. Motiram Marathe has three sons and a daughter-Rajashree, Hiraman, Manik, and Ratan, the youngest son. All the family members, even Motirams brother, used to live together. It was rare to see such a huge joint family still living together, Kharade said. He said Manik had been active in local politics while also managing the family businesses. According to Kharade, Manik had contested the Lonavala municipal council election on an NCP ticket in 2011 and later won as a Shiv Sena candidate in 2016. He contested the 2025 election from Shiv Sena UBT but was defeated. Ratan is currently the Bhushi ward chief of Shiv Sena UBT, Kharade said. Though Manik had been in politics, he had limited presence as he also used to manage family businesses. Abhay was married and also used to help in their family business. And it was shocking for Lonavala residents that such an incident had happened, Kharade said. A tea stall owner in Lonavala said, The Marathe family had been prominent in the area for several decades and had also been associated with religious and community activities during the annual Kanifnath Maharaj yatra held in Lonavala during Rangpanchami.

articleTitle: Ukraine or West Asia, India backs all meaningful peace efforts: PM Modi
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ukraine or West Asia, India backs all meaningful peace efforts: PM
description: His statement came a day after External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said that India has got a “little more involved beyond advocacy” and is having conversations with both Russia and Ukraine.
body_raw: In his first remarks since India initiated a proposal to end the war between Russia and Ukraine, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Monday that India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace. In his statement after the bilateral meeting with visiting Swiss President Guy Parmelin, Modi said Both India and Switzerland believe in democratic values, the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy. We will continue to work together for global peace and stability. Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, India has consistently supported every meaningful effort towards peace. His statement came a day after External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar said that India has got a little more involved beyond advocacy and is having conversations with both Russia and Ukraine, trying to be helpful on the safety of shipping in the Black Sea, grain and energy exports and on non-attack possibilities. Last week, Ukraines Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha had said that India has put forward a comprehensive and broad proposal to end the war, for the first time since the war began in February 2022. Elaborating on the context and rationale behind Indias move, Jaishankar said on Monday that Delhi started the latest round of conversations with Russia and Ukraine in July this year, after commercial ships came under attack from both sides in the Black Sea. Speaking at an interactive session at the Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi, Jaishankar said In the month of July, there were attacks on civilian shipping by both Russia and Ukraine. And in the course of those attacks, some Indian sailors were killed, some were injured. We regard these attacks as completely unacceptable, whether it is in the Black Sea, the Red Sea, or the Gulf. So we protested very strongly to the Russians, to the Ukrainians. I myself took it up with the foreign ministers of both countries. And we started getting active initially to secure the maritime shipping and the mariners involved in that. Jaishankar said those conversations brought out the nature of the cargo being carried. And there was concern over grain exports which had come to a halt in the Black Sea. So the conversation developed into whether non-attack on shipping is good, but is there a possibility of facilitating the shipment of grain. So it got linked to energy. So it became a somewhat broader conversation, he said. He said those conversations are ongoing - including during Modis meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek on August 31, after which Jaishankar went to Kyiv to meet Ukrainian President Vlodymyr Zelenskyy in early September, followed by another discussion between Modi and Putin in New Delhi on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit on September 11-12. We still keep in touch with both sides. Its obviously not an easy situation. Its not something which anybody can say with a high degree of confidence that something is going to come out. But it seems definitely an effort worth making, Jaishankar said, adding that resolving concerns pertaining to grain, fertiliser and fuel are in the interest of India, as well as the Global South. We have the interests of the parties themselves, that if they can even agree on something of a limited nature, we feel that in the given circumstance thats a big positive, he said. From the very beginning, he said, India has held the view that this conflict is unlikely to be resolved on the battlefield. Therefore, it was important to have negotiations between the parties. there were actually negotiations in the early stages of the conflict. Though we have been maintaining for some time that both parties should come to the table, and there were a number of conferences where countries gathered to express their support for peace, but often they would gather in the absence of Russia, he said, in a reference to initiatives like the Swiss peace conference. However, he said, India has always believed that there wasnt any point of having a gathering dealing with the Ukraine conflict where Russia is not there. On October 1, Putin had said that Modi constantly raises the question about putting an end to the conflict and has very good ideas. Later that day, speaking to reporters in Kyiv, Ukraines Foreign Minister Sybiha had said, We have four proposals. The most comprehensive is Indias proposal. For the first time, India has signalled its willingness to play a role. He had said Ukraine was prepared to agree to an energy and agricultural truce in the Black Sea, and was also considering an unconditional ceasefire along the line of contact. Besides India, Ukraine has received proposals for a possible ceasefire from Turkey, Egypt and the United States. According to Sybiha, Ukraine will agree to a ceasefire on the condition that it covers not only combat operations, but also an end to attacks on energy and port infrastructure, as well as the situation in the Black Sea. Modi has been raising the issue with Putin since 2022, when he first said this is not the era of war. In a meeting with Putin in Moscow in July 2024, Modi said peace talks do not succeed amid bombs, guns and bullets, and a solution cannot be found on the battlefield. On August 31 this year, Modi had urged Putin to move from endless war to end of war, when they met in Bishkek on the sidelines of the summit of SCO leaders.

articleTitle: Drishyam 3 Collection Day 1: Ajay Devgn film crosses Rs 113 cr gross in India, eyes Rs 190 cr weekend

articleTitle: He saved us from a 9/11: PM Modi leads praise for Indian pilot Smit Machchhar

description: PM Narendra Modi speaks to Captain Smit Machchhar’s family; mission in UAE assures all help.
body_raw: A day after Indian pilot Smit Machchhar fought off a co-pilot who attacked him and allegedly attempted to crash a flydubai aircraft headed to Tel Aviv from Dubai, Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised the pilot Thursday and said he had prevented a 911 - a reference to the 2001 terror attack in the US when al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked and crashed passenger aircraft. We wish and pray for his speedy recovery. The nation proudly stands with him and his. - Randhir Jaiswal MEAIndia October 1, 2026 Addressing an event to mark 100 years of the UPSC, Modi said, Yesterday, an incident took place in which Indian Captain Smit displayed a remarkable presence of mind and courage. And as the Prime Minister of Israel said, an Indian has saved us from a 9 Smits bravery fills every Indian with pride. Today, I also spoke to his father Bhupendra Bhai, his mother Geeta Behen, and his wife Sonal Behen. He is currently undergoing treatment. The entire world is proud of him today. I appeal to all citizens to pray for Smits long life and good health, and to honour Smit who has made India proud, he said. Our Embassy in Riyadh and Consulate in Jeddah have been following the health condition of Mr Smit Machchhar, the brave Indian pilot of Flydubai flight that was diverted to Tabuk today. He is admitted in a hospital in Tabuk city in northwest Saudi Arabia and receiving necessary. - India in Saudi Arabia IndianEmbRiyadh September 30, 2026 In a post on X, President Droupadi Murmu noted Machchhars heroic courage and incredible presence of mind. Even after being seriously injured in a moment of grave peril, he remained determined to protect the lives of others. His bravery and quick response helped prevent a major tragedy and saved many precious lives. I salute his indomitable spirit. I pray for his speedy recovery and good health, she said. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, among a host of political leaders, also hailed the Indian pilot and wished him swift and full recovery. Reuven Azar, Israels Ambassador to India, said, Together with Israel, India and UAE, I pray for the life of Captain Smit Machchhar, the experienced and gifted hero Indian pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073. His courage the courage of other Israeli Emirati passengers crew members saved the lives of 180 souls. The Ministry of External Affairs said that although Machchhar was gravely injured, he was safe. We salute the bravery of Captain Smit Machchhar who, in spite of being gravely injured, showed remarkable courage that saved the lives of many. He is receiving medical attention and is safe. We wish and pray for his speedy recovery. The nation proudly stands with him and his family, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.

articleTitle: US-Iran War Live Updates: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards call US President Trump a ‘big liar’

description: Oil prices rose for a second successive session on Tuesday as lingering concern over Middle East supply disruption brought about by US-Iran conflict.

articleTitle: Rajya Sabha polls: BJP fields Dinesh Arya from Uttarakhand, Koel Mallick from Bengal
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Trinamool leader Koel Mallick has quit her Rajya Sabha MP's post.
description: Ahead of the October 16 Rajya Sabha elections, the BJP finalised candidate names for Uttarakhand and West Bengal.
body_raw: The BJP Sunday announced Dinesh Arya and former Trinamool Congress TMC leader and actor Rukmini alias Koel Mallick as its candidates for the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections from Uttarakhand and West Bengal, respectively. Biennial elections for 11 Rajya Sabha seats, 10 from Uttar Pradesh and one from Uttarakhand, are scheduled for October 16, alongside a bypoll in West Bengal. Mallick will contest the West Bengal bypoll to retain the seat after joining the BJP following the TMCs defeat in the Assembly elections. Arya, an organisational leader with ties to both the RSS and Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami, currently serves as vice chairperson of the states Water Resources Management and Regulatory Commission, a position equivalent to a state Cabinet minister. TMC split and Mallicks nomination Mallick, a prominent figure in Bengali cinema, was nominated to the Rajya Sabha by the TMC in April. She subsequently resigned and joined the BJP in July as part of a split within TMC ranks, during which 18 MPs separated, merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India NCPI, and extended support to the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance NDA government. With the October 6 deadline for filing nominations approaching, BJP leaders held discussions at the party headquarters in New Delhi to finalise candidates for the remaining seats, particularly in Uttar Pradesh. Party sources said the BJP is prioritising women candidates and experienced organisational workers as it seeks to expand its current tally of 116 seats in the 245-member House. In Uttar Pradesh, 10 seats are falling vacant, eight of which are currently held by the BJP, while the Samajwadi Party SP and the Bahujan Samaj Party BSP hold one each. The single seat falling vacant in Uttarakhand is held by BJP MP Naresh Bansal. While BJP leaders expressed confidence in retaining all eight seats in Uttar Pradesh, party insiders noted that one seat could be contested. With 256 MLAs in the 403-member UP Assembly, the party falls slightly short of the required first-preference votes 37 per seat to secure all eight seats outright without opposition. Currently, the BJP-led NDA holds 150 seats in the 245-member Rajya Sabha, while non-NDA parties account for just over 100 seats.

articleTitle: Inspired by father, guided by father-in-law: Kynan Chenai’s road to Asiad gold
articleFeaturedImageAlt: India's Kynan Chenai celebrates after winning gold medal in the trap mixed team shooting event during the 20th Asian Games, in Nagoya, Japan, Wednesday, Sept. 30, 2026. (PTI Photo)
description: Son of former national champion and Randhir Singh's son-in-law teamed up with individual champ Neeru Dhanda to clinch trap mixed team gold at Aichi-Nagoya
body_raw: Kynan Chenais father Darius was a close friend of 1978 Asian Games trap gold medallist Randhir Singh, and one of their favourite subjects of conversation used to be guns. Darius is a former national trap champion himself, and the bond of friendship solidified further recently when Kynan, who began shotgun shooting in 2003, married Randhir Singhs daughter Ria Rajeshwari Kumari, who also practises the sport. Randhir passed away earlier this year and Darius feels he would have been delighted when Kynan and womens individual winner Neeru Dhanda combined to clinch the trap mixed team gold medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Wednesday. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage I knew Randhir Singh ji through our common friends in shooting for the last two decades or more. The only advice he would give Kynan was to keep it simple and go back to the basics when things went wrong. Thats what Kynan did today, Darius told The Indian Express. Neeru was competing in her maiden Asian Games, while Kynan had tasted success at Hangzhou in 2023 when he won the team gold and individual bronze. Kynan had started after watching his father in Hyderabad, and had even competed against him at the 2007 Nationals in Jaipur. He was part of the Rio Olympics squad, where he finished 19th. I started shooting competitively in my 30s on the insistence of my friends Manavjit Singh Sandhu and Mansher Singh. While Kynan studied at a boarding school, he would accompany me to the shooting range during our vacations abroad. And when he showed an interest in shooting, I got him to train under Mansher, shares the father. On Wednesday, the Indian pair shot a total of 136 to qualify fourth for the four-team final. They were placed fourth with six points after the first 10 shots, but eventually set an Asian Games record of 34 to win the gold medal, edging out China. Out of his 20 shots, Kynan missed only his first. Neeru missed three of her first five shots before she recovered to shoot two perfect series. She would miss two shots in the last series but they had already done enough to win the gold. Kynan was a bit disappointed after he missed the individual final. And with Neeru struggling initially, he made sure that the team made a comeback. Neeru showed with her recovery why she is one of the best shooters. Training under 2008 Olympic champion David Kostelecky of the Czech Republic has made him a better shooter. Indias foreign coach Peter Wilson too has been working on Kynans technique and gun stock adjustments, says Darius. With the trap mixed team event part of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, the gold assumes added significance. Getting the Olympic quota is the next target but such performances do help, says Mansher, now Indias High-Performance Manager Shotgun.

articleTitle: Darshan kicked Renukaswamy, paid Rs 30 lakh for false confessions: Approver
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Renukaswamy murder case actor Darshan
description: Pradosh Subba Rao, the accused-turned-approver in the Renukaswamy murder case, recounted in a Bengaluru court what he said he had witnessed.
body_raw: Kannada actor Darshan Thoogudeepa kicked Renukaswamy in the neck and burnt his chest with a cigarette, an accused-turned-approver said in a court statement recorded over five days in the murder case. Pradosh Subba Rao recounted what he said he had witnessed at a shed where Darshan and his co-accused allegedly assaulted Renukaswamy, who had allegedly sent lewd comments to the actors friend Pavithra Gowda on Instagram. Bengalurus 59th City Civil and Sessions Court recorded Pradoshs statement starting September 28. Pradosh, who worked as a finance manager at Oracle and was an acquaintance of Darshan for about 20 years, was the 14th accused in the case. He has now become a prosecution witness after turning approver. Besides Darshan and Pavithra, the others named in the chargesheet are Pawan K, 29 Raghavendra, 43 Nandish, 28 Jagadish, 36 Anukumar, 25 Ravi Shankar, 32 Dhanraj D, 27 Vinay V, 38 Nagaraju, 41 Laxman, 54 Deepak, 39 Pradhosh, 40 Karthik, 27 Keshavamurthy, 27 and Nikhil Nayak, 21. Lunch at a pub and a video call to Pavithra Gowda In a 128-page statement, Pradosh stated that on June 8, 2024, he visited Darshans home to join him for lunch at the Stony Brook pub, owned by Vinay. At the pub, Pawan showed Darshan some photographs on his phone and whispered something. He asked Pawan to video-call Pavithra and assured her that he would handle the matter, according to Pradoshs statement. Pradosh said he later drove Darshan, Pavithra, and Vinay in his Scorpio, with Vinay giving directions to a shed at Pattanagere in Bengaluru South. There, he said, Renukaswamy was sitting on the ground, bleeding from the head, surrounded by members of Darshans Chitradurga fan club, including Raghavendra. According to Pradosh, Pavithra told him the man had been sending her obscene messages. He told the court, Darshan abused, slapped and kicked Renukaswamy, made him apologise, and hit him with a nylon rope, while Pawan and Nandish beat him with a baton and a stick. He said he warned Nagaraj that matters could go out of hand. He later tried to pull Darshan away when the actor allegedly pressed the mans neck with his foot and burnt his chest with a cigarette. Darshan panicks and threatens to kill himself Pradosh said he left the shed and received a call later around 7 pm from Laxman saying that Renukaswamy was dead. When he told Darshan about the death, he testified, the actor panicked and threatened to kill himself. Darshan told him that Pawan had got Renukaswamy brought from Chitradurga on his instructions. While his associates tried to console Darshan, they came up with the plan that they would ask others to surrender before the police claiming they were the killers. Pradosh said that Rs 30 lakh would be needed to meet expenses related to lawyers, family, and jail. He said Darshan handed Rs 10 lakh to Vinay and arranged Rs 5 lakh for Raghavendra, and gave him a bag with 60 bundles of Rs 500 notes totalling Rs 30 lakh. The police recovered Rs 30 lakh from his Girinagar home on June 11, 2024. A cover story that didnt hold up Pradosh further said in his statement that he knew a sub-inspector named Vinay who worked at the Kamakshipalya police station. On the same day, Pradosh called Vinay, who was in Kerala with his family then, and made up a story about a money dispute among three people in which one was beaten to death. Aware that Sattva Apartment on Magadi Road would fall under the Kamakshipalya police limits, Pradosh said that he helped to dispose of the body near it. Pradosh stated that the accused removed number plates and a D-Boss sticker from a white Scorpio and used the vehicle to transport Renukaswamys body, which was then left by a service road near a drain. He said he threw Renukaswamys and Raghavendras phones into the drain and lied to the police officer about what had happened. On June 9, SI Vinay sent Pradosh CCTV footage of a white Scorpio going to and from the spot with its rear door open and three people walking. Pradosh told Vinay that those three seen in the video were his people but did not divulge any more information. Vinay told him to surrender at the earliest. Raghavendra, Karthik, Nikhil Nayak, and Keshavamurthy surrendered at the Kamakshipalya police station on June 10. But SI Vinay got to know the Scorpio was traced to the Pattanagere shed. He also learnt that the four men were telling a different story, involving Darshan, Pavithra and Pawan. Pradosh and Vinay later met near NICE Road, where he revealed the part about Darshan. But when he learnt about Pradoshs involvement, Vinay told him to never call him again. On June 10, 2024, Vinay called Pradosh to check where he and Pawan were. On learning that they were returning from Mysuru, the police intercepted them near the Bidadi toll. The next day, Assistant Commissioner of Police Chandan took Pradosh around 3 am to Mysuru looking for Darshan. Around 5.30 am, they reached the Radisson Blue hotel. They took Darshan into custody and returned to Bengaluru, the witness said in the court. On the same day, the police arrested Darshan, Gowda, and 15 others in connection with Renukaswamys murder.

articleTitle: INX Media case: SC extends Chidambaram’s interim protection from ED arrest till tomorrow
articleFeaturedImageAlt: p chidambaram, p chidambaram in jail, p chidambaram inx media case, ed custody of p chidambaram
description: The top court has extended the interim protection from arrest by the Enforcement Directorate, granted to the former finance minister till tomorrow. The probe agency will now argue in the apex court on Wednesday.
body_raw: As the hearing in the INX Media money laundering case filed against former Union minister P Chidambaram resumed Tuesday, the Supreme Court extended till tomorrow protection from arrest granted to the senior Congress leader. The probe agency will now argue in the apex court on Wednesday, reported PTI. Follow LIVE Updates As the case was presented in the top court today, a bench of Justices R Banumathi and A S Bopanna said it would hear the arguments of the ED on Chidambarams two petitions, including the challenge to remand orders, on Wednesday. Meanwhile, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for the former Union minister, filed an application seeking direction to the ED to produce the transcripts of the questioning conducted on December 19 last year and January 1 and January 21 this year in the case. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for ED, said he would like to reply to the fresh application during the course of his arguments. Sibal said that the transcripts will show whether Chidambaram was evasive during his questioning, as alleged by the ED. The former finance ministers counsel in the case also told the bench that the ED cannot place documents in the court randomly and behind the back for seeking Chidambarams custody. They are just producing documents at random and saying this is part of the case diary, Sibal said, adding, They cannot place the documents behind the back and seek custody of accused. Also appearing for Chidambaram, senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi, referred to the constitutional and legal provisions and said that fundamental right of citizens under Article 21 right to life and personal liberty cannot be suspended. He argued that the Prevention of Money Laundering Act PMLA was amended in 2009 whereas the allegations in the case are of 2007-2008. You try and paint a person as a kingpin when these alleged offences did not exist at that time, he told the court during the arguments which continued in the post-lunch session. The apex court had on Monday extended till Tuesday the protection from arrest given to Chidambaram in the INX Media money laundering case lodged by the ED. Chidambaram was the Union minister for finance as also home during the UPA-I and UPA-II government from 2004 to 2014. The CBI had registered an FIR on May 15, 2017, alleging irregularities in the Foreign Investment Promotion Board FIPB clearance granted to the INX Media group for receiving overseas funds of Rs 305 crore in 2007 during Chidambarams tenure as the finance minister. Thereafter, the ED lodged a money laundering case against him in 2017. On Monday, a Delhi special court remanded Congress leader and former Union Minister P Chidambaram in CBI custody for an additional four days till August 30 in the case. Special Judge Ajay Kumar Kuhar said the CBI demand that Chidambaram has to be further interrogated in its custody was justified. With PTI inputs
