Looking ahead I want to work at the intersection of technology and business strategy, building products that use software development and predictive modelling to solve real logistical problems. The combination of a BSBE foundation with the technical skills I have been building on the side feels like the right toolkit for it. I have also recently found trading genuinely interesting, so that is something I am following carefully. One thing IIT has taught me - though I would never say this to a professors face - is that engineering is largely the art of learning an entire semesters worth of content the night before an exam. I say this with respect and firsthand experience. But what it has also taught me is that the version of yourself you plan to be when you arrive is seldom the person you actually become. I came to IIT Guwahati with a study plan. I left my first year with a coffin dance performance, an Events Head title I had never intended to hold, and a room that permanently smelled of guitar strings and late-night Maggi. I would not trade any of it.

articleTitle: Karthik Subbaraj dismisses ‘Boycott Dorothy’ calls: ‘There’s online hate, audience likes it’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Director Karthik Subbaraj addressed the transphobic criticism surrounding his latest film Dorothy
description: Director Karthik Subbaraj has responded to the transphobic backlash and boycott calls surrounding his TIFF-premiered film Dorothy, dismissing the online criticism as coming from "a small world" and saying audiences in theatres have responded positively.
body_raw: Director Karthik Subbaraj has publicly responded to the transphobic criticism and boycott calls his latest film Dorothy has received since its theatrical release on Friday. The film, which explores the life of a transgender person against the backdrop of a patriarchal, caste-driven household in 1990s Madurai, has divided audiences online, with a section of social media users accusing the filmmaker of promoting LGBTQ ideas and calling for a boycott under the hashtag BoycottDorothy. In a recent interaction with media, Subbaraj dismissed the online backlash as unrepresentative of the films actual audience. When an interviewer referenced the criticism by quoting the Tamil phrase Ipdi panritaare Why did he do this?, Subbaraj questioned the weight being given to these reactions. Who are these people? he asked. When told the comments were from users on X formerly Twitter, he was blunt. Twitter is a small world and those who think about my film like what you said belong to a smaller world. But audiences who are watching a movie are bigger. Why should we be talking about that? he said. Also Read Dorothy movie review Karthik Subbarajs film will make everyone uncomfortable He contrasted the online negativity with what he has witnessed in theatres. So many people came up to me and said that the film was good. Please ask about that as well, he said, adding that media coverage was disproportionately focused on a handful of negative voices. You are asking me about it based on four people who spoke against it. Theres online hatred. I couldnt see it among the audience who visited the theatre. But when I go on press tours, people are asking about that specifically. Subbaraj addressed the discomfort some viewers expressed about watching a transgender persons story on screen. Dorothy follows two close friends, Karthi and Subbu, who grow up in a testosterone-driven, patriarchal household in Madurai. One of them eventually comes out as a transgender person, and the film explores the discrimination, violence and social pressure they face in a community that views any deviation from rigid masculinity as a threat. If someone has a problem with seeing a transgenders life as just a movie, then thats their internal problem. They should also come and watch the film, Subbaraj said. Rather than shutting down the conversation, the director said he would welcome a genuine discussion about the films portrayal of gender identity. We can then have a conversation or debate. That will go towards a solution or discussion, he said. He acknowledged that the film has at least succeeded in generating a public conversation about its subject matter, even if parts of that conversation have been hostile. One good thing is that it has created a conversation, he said. He also made it clear he would not engage with online trolls. If I give a punch for their punch, itll go on forever, he said. About Dorothy Dorothy is written and directed by Karthik Subbaraj and stars Keerthy Suresh, Sananth and Rishikanth. The film features an original score by Ilaiyaraaja, his 1,540th film, with cinematography by Thiru. It is produced by Jio Studios and Guneet Monga Kapoors Sikhya Entertainment, in association with Subbarajs own Dhammam Films. The film had its world premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival in the Centrepiece category on September 12, where it received a standing ovation at the Scotiabank Theatre. It marks the first Tamil film to premiere at TIFF in over a decade.

articleTitle: Woman loses 43 kg in 8 months: What experts say about losing 10 kg in a month
articleFeaturedImageAlt: weight loss
description: A dramatic first-month drop may look impressive, but expert says the numbers need to be understood in context
body_raw: Dubai-based weight-loss coach Aymen AL Othmani revealed on Instagram that a woman lost 43 kg in 8 months. The transformation is particularly striking because she lost around 10 kg in the first month. While the numbers have understandably caught attention on social media, they also raise an important question Is losing 10 kg in one month really possible, and is it safe? The short answer is yes. A 10-kg drop on the weighing scale in the first month is possible for some people, particularly when they begin at a high body weight, but it does not necessarily mean that all 10 kg was body fat, said consultant dietitian Garima Goyal. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. During the initial weeks of a major dietary change, the body can lose a substantial amount of water weight and glycogen. Glycogen, the stored form of carbohydrate in the body, is stored along with water. When calorie intake and carbohydrate intake are significantly reduced, glycogen stores can decrease, leading to a rapid fall in body weight. Changes in salt intake and food volume can also contribute to a dramatic reduction on the scale during the first few weeks, said Goyal. The womans overall reported loss of 43 kg over eight months, however, highlights how weight-loss rates can vary significantly depending on the persons starting weight, body composition, medical condition, diet, physical activity and level of professional supervision. Someone beginning at a substantially higher weight may experience faster initial weight loss than someone who has only a small amount of weight to lose, said Goyal. From a clinical nutrition perspective, the concern with very rapid weight loss is not simply the number on the weighing scale. Losing weight too aggressively can increase the risk of muscle loss, nutritional inadequacy, fatigue and difficulty maintaining the results. This is why a good weight-loss programme should ideally focus on preserving muscle through adequate protein intake and appropriate resistance training, while ensuring that the calorie deficit is not unnecessarily extreme, said Goyal. Another important point is that weight loss is rarely linear. The first month may show a dramatic reduction, followed by slower progress or plateaus. This is completely normal. As body weight decreases, the bodys energy requirements also change, and continued weight loss may become slower, Goyal told indianexpress.com. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Aymen AL Othmani Weight Loss Coach aymen.alothmani The transformation shared by the coach can certainly be inspiring, but it should not become a benchmark for everyone. Trying to replicate someone elses 10-kg first-month result can lead people towards crash diets and unhealthy restriction. The safest and most sustainable pace depends on the individual, said Goyal. description: Drishyam 3 Worldwide Box Office Collection Updates: Within five days, the suspense thriller Drishyam The Conclusion has crossed the Rs 200 crore mark in India and Rs 300 crore worldwide.
body_raw: Drishyam 3 Box Office Collection Day 5 Live Updates Ajay Devgns latest film Drishyam The Conclusion has been shattering box-office records since its release. Within five days, the suspense thriller has crossed the Rs 200 crore mark in India and Rs 300 crore worldwide. According to Sacnilk, the film earned Rs 19 crore net on Tuesday from 16,075 shows, taking its total India net collection to Rs 216.50 crore and domestic gross to Rs 259.80 crore. Its worldwide gross currently stands at Rs 341.30 crore. On its fifth day, Drishyam 3s overall theatre occupancy was 23.42, with morning shows registering 12, afternoon shows recording 19.54, evening shows at 24.62, and night shows at 37.54. Ajay Devgns return as Vijay Salgaonkar for the third and final instalment of the Hindi Drishyam franchise has proved fruitful for the actor. Drishyam 3 has become the fastest Ajay film to cross the Rs 200 crore mark in India. In comparison, his previous release, Dhamaal 4, had earned Rs 9.5 crore on its fifth day and had a gross collection of Rs 167.88 crore by then. ALSO READ Ajay Devgns Drishyam 3 reminds us that more than family, the franchise is about movies Drishyam 3, which released in theatres on October 2, has been receiving positive reviews from audiences and critics. The film has continued to hold its ground despite competition from other theatrical releases, including Vishal Chaturvedis Hanuman Ansh Rs 326.4 crore net in India and the Sidharth Malhotra-starrer Force of the Forrest Rs 64.12 crore net. The film also comfortably surpassed the opening-day collections of the previous two instalments. Drishyam 2015 had earned Rs 5.85 crore on Day 1 and went on to collect Rs 110 crore worldwide, while Drishyam 2 2022 opened at Rs 15.38 crore and ended its theatrical run with a worldwide collection of Rs 342 crore. Drishyam The Conclusion is produced by Star Studio18 and Panorama Studios, with Abhishek Pathak serving as the director. Besides Ajay Devgn, the film stars Tabu as IG Meera Deshmukh and Shriya Saran as Nandini Salgaonkar. The cast also includes Ishita Dutta, Mrunal Jadhav, Rajat Kapoor, Kamlesh Sawant, Prakash Raj and Jaideep Ahlawat.

articleTitle: Two days to election: Can Maharashtra opposition alliance stop infighting?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A meeting of Maha Vikas Aghadi at Tilak Bhavan, to discuss the Legislative Council elections and other important issue, in the presence of Congress State President Harshvardhan Sapkal, NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule, NCP (SP) State president Shashikant Shinde, Shivsena (UBT) leader Anil Parab, Shivsena (UBT) leader Ambadas Danve, and Shivsena (UBT) leader Milind Narvekar, in Mumbai on Wednesday
description: With the October 9 deadline for withdrawals approaching in the Legislative Council elections, allies have little time to avert “friendly fights”
body_raw: Opposition parties may be trying to remain on the same page nationally when it comes to taking on the BJP, but a recurring problem has been resolving their differences at the regional level. In Maharashtra, the Opposition Maha Vikas Aghadis MVA plan to contest the October 23 Legislative Council elections together is under strain, with the Congress and the Shiv Sena UBT set to face each other in Amravati Teachers constituency, while the Sena UBT and the NCP SP are pitted against each other in the Marathwada Graduates constituency. The other seats where elections are being held are Pune Graduates, Nagpur Graduates, and Pune Teachers. The differences have cropped up within days of the three parties deciding to contest the five Council seats together. With Tuesday the last day to file nominations - candidates have till October 9 to withdraw their nominations - the parties have failed to reach an agreement in these two constituencies. In Amravati Teachers constituency, the Congress has fielded Aditi Pohare, while the Sena UBT has put up Dattatray Lahane. Lahane filed his nomination on October 6 in the presence of Sena leaders. The Congress had announced Pohare along with sitting MLCs Abhijit Wanjari from Nagpur Graduates and Jayant Asgaonkar from Pune Teachers on October 3. Pohare joined the Congress days before her candidature was announced. She is the daughter of Harshvardhan Deshmukh who heads the Shri Shivaji Education Society in Amravati. The society has a large number of teachers among its staff, giving Pohare a local base in a constituency where the candidates are elected by registered teachers. The Sena UBT, however, says it was Lahane for the Amravati seat. After announcing his candidature, Sena UBT MP Sanjay Raut made it clear that the party would not give up the seat simply to avoid a contest with the Congress. We are contesting two seats, Amravati and Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Marathwada. You call it a friendly fight or whatever you want. We are contesting them, he said. Raut argues that the Sena UBT was not seeking all the seats the Congress was claiming. He said his party was willing to leave the Nagpur Graduates and Pune Teachers seats to the Congress and was even prepared to give up Pune Graduates to the NCP SP, despite the work done by its leaders to register voters there. All three parties have worked separately to build their voter base in the Graduates and Teachers constituencies and each has its own claim to some of the seats, Raut has said. Congress leader Vijay Wadettiwar said voter registration was an important factor in these elections. These elections are not based on ordinary voting. The side that registers more membersvoters has greater weight, he said. He said the Congress had not claimed Pune Graduates when the Sena UBT had a sitting member there, while the Sena UBT had not claimed Pune Teachers as the Congress had a sitting member there. When there is a sitting member, it is not right for another party to demand that seat, he said. The position of the NCP SP in Amravati remains less clear. On Monday, one of its district presidents attended Lahanes nomination programme, while another local leader said the senior leadership had not taken a final decision. The contrasting positions suggested that the party was not comfortable with the situation. A direct contest The second dispute has become more direct. The Sena UBT has fielded Dilip Ghuge from the Marathwada Graduates constituency. Ghuge filed his nomination on October 5. The following day, Dr Pratapsinh Patil of the NCP SP announced that he was filing his nomination as the authorised candidate of the Sharad Pawar-led party and the MVA. Patils campaign also shows how the contest could play out. In a social media post on Tuesday, he said his candidature was not merely about filing a nomination but about starting a new fight for graduates, students, unemployed youth, and ordinary people in Marathwada. Taking aim at Satish Chavan, who has represented the seat since 2008 and is contesting this time as the candidate of the NCP and ruling Mahayuti alliance, Patil asked what had changed for graduates in the past 18 years, raising issues such as employment, education, examination paper leaks, and students future. However, the Sena UBTs decision to contest the seat has complicated the equations and upset the NCP SP, which has traditionally regarded Marathwada Graduates as an NCP seat. NCP SP leaders in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar have argued that the party won the constituency for three consecutive terms and should therefore continue to contest it. NCP SP MP Supriya Sule sought to play down the differences. Asked about the disagreement over the Council seats, she said there was no dissatisfaction within the MVA and that the issue will become clear after further discussions. Raut has rejected the argument that the NCP SP somehow has an automatic claim over the seat. He has pointed out that before joining the NCP following the split in the party, Chavan was a Congress member and the political situation has changed since then. Understanding fails to hold Earlier this month, the MVA decided to contest the five seats going to polls on October 23 together. The Opposition alliances strategy was discussed at a meeting attended by Congress leaders Naseem Khan and Harshwardhan Sapkal, NCP SP leaders Shashikant Shinde and Harshwardhan Patil, and Raut. The Congress at the time said the parties were looking at the constituencies held by the NCP, the NCP SP, and an Independent, and would take a call on the candidates after determining their chances of winning. That understanding now appears to have failed in two constituencies. In both cases, the parties have moved ahead with nominations rather than waiting for a final decision at the alliance level. However, the Opposition alliance still has time till October 9 to avoid friendly fights and give itself the best possible chance to defeat the Mahayuti. Otherwise, the folly of friendly fights might become apparent when the votes are counted on October 27.

articleTitle: Gyanesh Kumar should get Padma Bhushan, says Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya
articleFeaturedImageAlt: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya
description: The Opposition plans to move a motion in Parliament to remove the CEC after The Indian Express reported that the two ECs raised objections to SIR-related decisions made without their knowledge.
body_raw: Amid Oppositions demand for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, West Bengal BJP chief Samik Bhattacharya on Friday defended him, saying he deserves the Padma Bhushan for handling the Assembly polls in the state earlier this year. The Opposition plans to move a motion in Parliament to remove the CEC after The Indian Express reported that the two ECs raised objections to SIR-related decisions made without their knowledge. The people of West Bengal are delighted that, after so long, intimidation was kept at bay. There were no incidents of murder, and people were actually allowed to cast their votes. Furthermore, in a border state like this, Gyanesh Kumar took the initiative to remove the names of Bangladeshi infiltrators from the voter lists, the senior BJP leader said, adding, Gyanesh Kumar deserves to be awarded, at the very least, with the Padma Bhushan. He lauded the SIR of electoral rolls, claiming it successfully purged deceased, fictitious, and illegal Bangladeshi voters. The people of Bengal have rarely witnessed an election like this.

articleTitle: Rahane on Tendulkar’s 100 centuries: ‘Only Virat Kohli can achieve that’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Kohli
description: "Many times we think that if a player is thinking about milestones, that means he is selfish. But when Virat Kohli puts pressure on himself, that is when he does well," said Rahane
body_raw: On Sunday, Virat Kohli scored his 86th century for India against the West Indies in Thiruvananthapuram. Sachin Tendulkar is the only cricketer who has managed 100 international centuries, and former Indian cricketer Ajinkya Rahane said Kohli will also think about achieving that stat. Rahane was also confident that if Kohli is confident, he will achieve the elusive mark. I think when Virat Kohli puts pressure on himself, that is when he is at his best. In every innings, he has done that. He has those expectations of himself. That is why he has been able to do it consistently for so many years. Knowing Virat, if he thinks about 100 centuries, there is nothing wrong with it, because his role model has been Sachin Tendulkar. So, I am sure he must be thinking about it. If he thinks about it, only Virat Kohli can achieve that, Ajinkya Rahane said on Cricbuzz. Giving insights into Kohlis mind, Rahane revealed that fans, pundits and former players sometimes perceive that thinking about milestones might make a player selfish, but Rahane said that is what works best for Kohli to put pressure on himself. Many times we think that if a player is thinking about milestones, that means he is selfish. But when Virat Kohli puts pressure on himself, that is when he does well. So, I am sure he will have a number on his mind, but at the same time, he will also have the thought that he has to enjoy the game as long as he is playing, he added. However, after his blistering 88-ball 139, Kohli revealed that he has never really thought about milestones. My focus has never really been on these milestones, so to say. Its just understanding the situation along the course of just doing the job for the team, whatever. Achievements come along. Obviously, I feel very grateful and very blessed to be in this position, having played for so long, Virat Kohli said during the post-match presentation.

articleTitle: Ajay Devgn’s Drishyam 3 writer says wrote 100 versions of film: ‘Friends tried to bribe me for ending’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Ajay Devgn's Drishyam 3 writer says wrote 100 versions of film
description: Ajay Devgn starrer Drishyam 3's screenwriter recently recalled writing more than 100 versions of the blockbuster film, that he had almost lost count.
body_raw: Ajay Devgn returned as the iconic Vijay Salgaonkar in his latest release Drishyam 3 The Conclusion. After two successful parts, the third installment of the Drishyam franchise is also following the same footsteps. The film has emerged a winner, both critically and commercially, collecting over Rs 270 crore worldwide within three days. As the storytelling and climax of Drishyam 3 is being widely discussed, the films screenwriter Aamil Keeyan Khan, opened up about working on the final chapter. During a conversation with The Free Press Journal, he shared, I have folders inside folders, drafts with dates, numbers, dates after numbers, and files called things like FINAL, FINAL 2, FINAL FINAL and presumably FINAL PLEASE GOD. I have genuinely lost count, but well over a hundred drafts in different forms. Easily. The makers of Drishyam 3 also took strict steps to keep the films major twists under wraps. Aamil Khan revealed that the ending of the film was not shared with most of the cast and crew. Abhishek basically ran the production like Vijay Salgaonkar would. The climax wasnt given to a large part of the crew. People got information on a need-to-know basis, he said. He continued, Sometimes a department only knew what it needed to execute a scene, not necessarily why it was executing it. A lot of actors and crew from the film, and my own friends and relatives, tried to bribe me for the ending. But like Gaitonde, I remained honest and loyal to the producers. ALSO READ Tom Cruises Digger gets crushed by Ajay Devgns Drishyam 3, grosses Rs 1.30 crore in India The writer further explained how the screenplay was expected to maintain the identity of the franchise, while giving the audience something they had never experienced before. It was an enormous mountain to climb. You have a beloved franchise, a family that the audiences have lived with for years, and the legacy of two hugely loved films sitting on your shoulders. And most importantly, how do you surprise an audience for the third time? Khan added, In the first film, Vijay Salgaonkar is almost a blank slate. Now the audience knows him. They know how his mind works they know he has tricks up his sleeve, and frankly, theyre suspicious of everything the poor man does. Then there was the challenge of writing an original screenplay while retaining the DNA of Drishyam. It still had to have humour, family, emotion, drama and thrills without any one ingredient swallowing the others. It was a very, very thin tightrope. Thankfully, none of us looked down. About the film Drishyam 3 The Conclusion has been produced by Star Studio18 and Panorama Studios, and helmed by Abhishek Pathak, who also directed the previous instalment. He has also co-written the film with Aamil Keeyan Khan and Parveez Shaikh. Besides Ajay Devgn, the Hindi thriller will features Tabu, reprising her role as IG Meera Deshmukh and Shriya Saran as Nandini. Actors Prakash Raj and Jaideep Ahlawat have also joined the star cast. The Hindi Drishyam franchise started in 2015 with the remake of Mohanlals Malayalam hit of the same name. The first Drishyam starring Ajay Devgn in Hindi language was also a huge success and it minted around Rs 110 crore worldwide. Drishyam 2, which hit the theatres in 2022, also emerged as a massive blockbuster, collecting around Rs 345 crore worldwide. Now, the latest Drishyam 3 has crossed Rs 272.8 crore worldwide in its first three days.

articleTitle: Throat slit, caretaker missing: Ex-IAS officer found dead in Bhopal home
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rakesh agarwal
description: Agrawal's body was found inside his bedroom at his residence behind Panghat Colony in Suraj Nagar. According to ACP Ankita Khatarkar, the suspected time of the murder was between 2 am and 3 am.
body_raw: Retired IAS officer Rakesh Agrawal was found with his throat slit at his residence in Suraj Nagar under Ratibad police station limits early Wednesday morning, with police saying they were investigating the disappearance of a caretaker who had been hired through an agency only days before the murder. Agrawals body was found inside his bedroom at his residence behind Panghat Colony in Suraj Nagar. According to ACP Ankita Khatarkar, the suspected time of the murder was between 2 am and 3 am. A forensic team examined the house and collected evidence as police began reconstructing what happened during the intervening hours. Agrawals wife woke up at around 4 am and found the door of her room latched from the outside, police said. She allegedly called another caretaker, Amar, who helped open the door and found Agrawal lying dead inside with his throat allegedly slit. Police say they are now looking closely at Varun Kumar, a caretaker who had been hired through an agency three days earlier as a 24-hour caretaker-cum-male nurse. Kumar, who is reportedly from Punjab, has been missing since the incident. Police suspect he may have fled from the house and have begun efforts to trace him. Most of his belongings, save for a pair of clothes, were also found missing from the house, officials say. The caretaker had been hired through an agency three days ago as a 24-hour caretaker-cum-male nurse. He is currently untraceable, and we are trying to establish his movements, ACP Khatarkar told The Indian Express. Police, however, have not yet conclusively established Kumars role in the murder. Investigators are examining the physical evidence from the house, CCTV footage from the surrounding area and other leads to determine who was inside the premises at the time of the killing and how the person or persons involved left the house. The police have also not been able to establish a motive for the murder. So far, no valuables were missing from the house. Only after the suspect is arrested can we establish what transpired, the officer said. Agrawal belonged to the 1982 batch of the Madhya Pradesh cadre and spent more than three decades in the state administration, holding a succession of senior positions before his retirement. During his career, he served as district collector, deputy secretary, joint secretary, additional secretary, managing director, director, secretary and principal secretary. An employee who was present at the home said he was woken up by the wife of the deceased IAS officer. She said the gate was closed, so I went up to the house. Inside, the nozzle of the gas cylinder was left on. There was nothing suspicious in the last 2-3 days, he said. Rajesh Agrawal, a friend of the deceased IAS officer, said he was deeply shocked by the incident when he visited the family home in Bhopal. His wife is now admitted to the hospital, and the son is headed home from the US, he said. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav expressed condolences and said the guilty wont be spared. The Director General of Police has been instructed to monitor the case. The state government is fully sensitive to this matter. The culprits will be identified, and legal action will be taken. No culprit will be spared, he said. The Congress sought to corner the state government over the law and order situation in Bhopal. Leader of the Opposition Umang Singhar said Criminals are getting emboldened under the BJP government, and people are not safe even in the capital, Bhopal. Law and order has completely collapsed under Chief Minister Mohan Yadav. When a retired IAS officer is not safe in his own home in the capital, who will take responsibility for the safety of the general public?.

articleTitle: Diveagar beach accident: ‘I don’t like to swim in salt water, hence survived’: Student who witnessed death of 8
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Soham Gore, an eyewitness (L) and and police deployed outside Winners Academy. (Special Arrangement)
description: All eight deceased were students of Winners Academy, a private coaching centre in Alandi.
body_raw: Soham Gore, a student of class 11th science, from the temple town of Alandi in Pune, was devastated with grief at the funeral of his 17-year-old friend Pranav Ramdas Bansode, who died along with seven others, after drowning at Diveagar beach in Maharashtras Raigad district. All eight deceased were students of Winners Academy, a private coaching centre in Alandi. The Academy had organized a one-day trip to Raigad Fort and Diveagar beach for the students. Soham said the teachers at Winners Academy asked interested students to bring a consent form signed by their parents. Soham said, Pravnav and I have been friends since our school days. We were now studying together at the Winners Academy. Both of us went for the trip with other students.Those having the consent form were asked to gather at 3 am on Thursday. Accordingly, 42 students, including 25 boys and 17 girls came for the trip. We were accompanied by two male and three female teachers. We first went to Raigad Fort by bus. The Ropeway was closed, so we trekked up the fort. We came down around 2 pm, had lunch at a hotel and then proceeded towards Diveagar beach., said Soham. We reached the beach around 5 pm. Teachers said those who could swim could play in the sea. Others were asked to stay on the seashore. The teachers accompanied those who went into the seawater. The group of girl students was playing in shallow water along the seaside.I can swim. But I do not like swimming in salt water. So I did not enter the sea and hence survived, said Soham. He added, From the sea shore, I saw the boys had not gone very deep into the sea. They were into the seawater up to their waist along with our teachers. But, within a few minutes, I noticed movements of police and water sports personnel. When I went closer, I saw they were trying to rescue my friends who were drowning in the sea. Our teachers Amar Adak and Mrunal Narkhade and some students who were good swimmers were also making efforts to rescue those drowning. While some students were rescued safely, eight died in the incident. They included Pranav, my freind.I did not see any caution boards, life guards or life jacket facility at the beach. After the incident, Soham called his father Govind Gore. I was very worried. So I asked Soham to talk to me on a video call, his father said. Soham said he returned with other students and teachers in the same bus that reached Alandi around 6 am on Friday. Meanwhile, Raigad police handed over the bodies to family members after the postmortem was conducted at a local hospital, early on Friday. Alandi observed bandh for funeral Funerals of Pranav Bansode, Sumit Bharat Ahire, Pranav Ramdas Bansode, Kaivalya Satish Vasankar, and Tanmay Dattatray Wahile were performed at the crematorium in Alandi. All four were residents of Alandi. Last rites of Rahveer Yuvraj Wahile and Soham Tukaram Bhandwalkar were performed at Kelagaon village, located about three kilometers from Alandi. Yash Kiran Wankhede and Kaustubh Sandip Daundh were residents of Charholi Budruk. Wankhedes funeral was held at his native place in Amravati, while Daundh was cremated at his homeland in Ahilyanagar district, police said. Alandi, a well known religious place in Pune, observed a bandh on Friday to pay tribute to the eight youngsters who died by drowning. Hundreds of villagers, including President of Alandi Municipal Council Prashant Kurhade, local MLA Baba Kale and others from social, political and religious sectors, attended the students funeral. Police deployed outside Winners Academy According to police, Winners Academy is a coaching center that has about 100 students mainly preparing for 11th and 12th along with other courses. The Academy, located in a building in Alandi, was closed on Friday, with police officials deployed outside its premises. Alandi police said they have not received any complaints yet against the Winners Academy.

articleTitle: Delhi’s new liquor policy rollout likely, prices may surge before festive season
articleFeaturedImageAlt: A Liquor shop in New Delhi
description: On excise duty and liquor prices, Vinod Giri said that Delhi’s excise duties are not among the highest in the country.
body_raw: Liquor prices in the Capital may increase in the coming months as the Delhi government is planning to raise excise duty and retail margin to boost revenue under the new excise policy, which is ready and is likely to be notified in October, The Indian Express has learnt. The final draft of the new excise policy is ready, said a senior Delhi government official. Last week, however, Delhi Excise Commissioner Ravi Jha was transferred to Arunachal Pradesh. Once a new officer is appointed, the final draft proposal will be sent to the Delhi Cabinet and Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu for final nod. Once the approval comes, the government plans to notify it in October ahead of the peak festival season, the official added. The official said, Even as the entry of private players is unlikely, raising the fixed retail margin and excise duty are among the key objectives. This will be a major change as currently there are only government-run liquor shops in the city. The retailers do not get much revenue due to fixed margins. With this key change,the shops are expected to be upgraded and draw more customers. More premium liquor stores Delhi is also expected to see an increase in the number of premium liquor stores. Explaining further, another government official said, Currently, the retail margin cap is fixed at Rs 50 on Indian Made Foreign Liquor and Rs 100 on foreign liquor on a per bottle basis. The liquor shops in Delhi do not keep premium imported liquors that cost above Rs 1,000 due to a fixed margin, which eventually pushes the customers to neighbouring cities such as Gurugram, Faridabad where shops operate without a fixed margin. For instance, lets say the price of Black Label in Delhi is Rs 3,500 but you will get the same brand for a lesser price like Rs 2,400 in Gurgaon. This can be addressed once the fixed margins are removed. The government is also planning to increase excise duty to boost revenue, said officials. Currently, excise duty in Delhi is levied according to different Wholesale Price WSP slabs and varies depending on the type of liquor. For instance, the duty on Indian spirits ranges from 30 to 300. Any increase in these slabs is likely to raise the tax component of liquor prices.if excise duty is increased, the liquor prices will also increase, the official explained. Further, officials said that there might be changes in timings of serving liquor in hotels, clubs and restaurants. After the scrapping of the previous AAP governments liquor policy, following a probe by CBI and the Enforcement Directorate, Delhi government brought back the older policy and allowed only government shops to operate in Delhi. Last year, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced her plans to introduce a new excise policy for Delhi. She also constituted a ministerial committee headed by Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh to formulate a transparent and socially secure policy. Currently, there are over 700 liquor shops in the city, which are run by the four government corporations - Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation, Delhi State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation, Delhi Consumers Cooperative Wholesale Store, and Delhi State Civil Supplies Corporation. Reacting to the proposed changes, Vinod Giri, Director General of Brewers Association of India, which represents the countrys largest beer makers, said, Retail margins are currently fixed on a per-bottle basis, regardless of the price of the bottle. For Scotch whiskies, for instance, it is around Rs 100 per bottle and then comes down to Rs 50 and so on. The question is what margin they will allow under the new policy. Margins of 5, 10 or 15 are generally the norm. There should not be an objection if the margin is up to 10 anything substantially higher could raise questions. On excise duty and liquor prices, Giri said that Delhis excise duties are not among the highest in the country. If the government is looking at excise duty as a means of increasing revenue, there may be some headroom to raise it. Beer, for example, currently attracts 150 excise duty, while imported liquor attracts 85. There is also a 25 VAT. If excise duty is increased, liquor prices will rise. This could have a multiplier effect because an increase in excise duty raises the base price, which in turn affects the retail margin calculated on the baselanded price. Therefore, changes in both retail margins and excise duty could have a multiplier effect on retail prices, he added.

articleTitle: Dissent is not dysfunction, institutions need it
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Dissent is not dysfunction, institutions need it
description: India's constitutional institutions today. Institutional integrity is preserved not by manufactured consensus, but by faithful adherence to the Constitution, statutory mandates, and respect for collegiate outcomes.
body_raw: Deliberation, debate, and internal dissent form the lifeblood of any functional constitutional democracy. Yet, an elementary principle of constitutional jurisprudence governs all collegiate bodies While deliberation and dissent represent the intellectual process, it is the final outcome that constitutes the binding decision. To challenge the legitimacy of an institution simply because its internal deliberations reflect divergent viewpoints, or because a ruling does not produce absolute unanimity, is legally unlettered and a calculated assault on institutional integrity. A multi-member body is crafted to assemble diverse viewpoints. When the Constitution provided for an Election Commission ECI under Article 324, and Parliament subsequently framed statutory frameworks to govern its functioning, the law explicitly structured the mechanics of collegiate decision-making. Section 18 of the statutory enactment governing the ECI provides that while it should endeavour to act unanimously, in the event of any difference of opinion, matters must be decided according to the opinion of the majority. Consequently, an order delivered by even a 21 split does not suffer from any constitutional or legal infirmity. In the eyes of the law, the majority verdict is the sovereign verdict of the ECI. The legal fiction that collegiate bodies require absolute unanimity was put to rest three decades ago by the Supreme Court in its landmark five-judge Constitution Bench ruling in T N Seshan, Chief Election Commissioner of India v. Union of India Ors. 1995. The then-CEC challenged the conversion of the ECI from a single-member entity to a multi-member collegiate body, claiming absolute primacy and asserting that collegiate decision-making would impair institutional efficiency. The Court, speaking through Chief Justice A M Ahmadi, dismissed the challenge in its entirety. It held, The function of the Election Commission is to take decisions through the process of collective deliberation, and in the event of a difference of opinion among the members, by a majority. the view of the majority is the view of the body. The apex court operates under the identical constitutional premise. Landmark rulings, including the Kesavananda Bharati judgment, which established the Basic Structure doctrine via a razor-thin 76 majority, govern the Republic of India. Congresss claim to be a protector of institutional autonomy is discredited by its history of institutional subversion. During the UPA regime, reports widely highlighted that appointments were steered directly through party channels. Reputed news agencies documented that critical appointment files for the electoral watchdog were cleared directly at the behest of Sonia Gandhi, culminating in the appointment of Navin Chawla as Election Commissioner in 2005. Decades earlier, the Justice J C Shah Commission, established to investigate excesses committed during the 19751977 Emergency, explicitly found Chawla unfit to hold any public office due to documented abuse of administrative power. The institutional crisis peaked when sitting CEC N Gopalaswami invoked his constitutional prerogative under Article 3245, submitting a detailed note to the President seeking Chawlas removal on grounds of institutional bias and political partisanship. Instead of honouring the constitutional framework, the Congress government summarily rejected the recommendation and rewarded Chawla by elevating him to CEC. An equally damaging blow to the perception of electoral independence was dealt in the case of M S Gill. After being CEC, Gill was rewarded by Congress with a Rajya Sabha seat and inducted into the Union Cabinet as a minister of state. Those who spent decades superseding judges, abusing emergency powers, treating election commissioners appointments as party prerogatives, and awarding cabinet berths to referees after retirement possess zero moral or jurisprudential authority to question Indias constitutional institutions today. Institutional integrity is preserved not by manufactured consensus, but by faithful adherence to the Constitution, statutory mandates, and respect for collegiate outcomes. The writer is national spokesperson, BJP and a senior advocate

articleTitle: ‘Happy 5th, my love’: Hrithik Roshan marks anniversary with Saba Azad; Sussanne Khan reacts
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Hrithik Roshan Saba Azad 5th anniversary
description: Hrithik Roshan recently shared a sweet social media post for girlfriend Saba Azad as the couple completed five years together.
body_raw: Hrithik Roshan and his girlfriend Saba Azad often express their affection for each other on social media. articleTitle: ‘You are like a serpent’: Why SS Rajamouli sent this unusual message to Fahadh Faasil
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Rajamouli
description: SS Rajamouli recently opened up about Malayalam cinema, Mohanlal, and his wish to collaborate with Fahadh Faasil.
body_raw: Filmmakers SS Rajamouli has spoken about his admiration for Malayalam cinema and actors Fahadh Faasil and Mohanlal during a conversation with the team of Dont Trouble The Trouble. The filmmaker, who is presenting Fahadhs upcoming Telugu film, opened up about the Malayalam films he watches, his favourite performances by Fahadh and the acting philosophy he once heard from Mohanlal. SS Rajamouli on Fahadh Faasil, Trance and Aavesham While admitting that he does not watch Malayalam films extensively, SS Rajamouli said he has followed Fahadh Faasils work closely and has been impressed by the actors performances. I dont watch a lot of Malayalam films. Definitely, I have watched a lot of Fahadhs films. I love his films. Trance has been my all-time favourite and, of course, Aavesham. I always tell him that I love to hate him, Rajamouli said. Fahadh then recalled a message Rajamouli had sent him after watching Joji. I remember you texted me after watching Joji that, You are like a serpent. I want to turn it off, but I dont know how, Fahadh said. SS Rajamouli also praised the breadth of Malayalam cinema and singled out its writing and acting. One of my all-time favourites is Lal sirs Drishyam. Just two days back, I watched Bro Daddy. I am amazed with the kind of films Malayalam cinema makes. From small films to big films, to socially conscious films, to action, to thrillers. If you ask me one thing that is the highest quality in Malayalam cinema, I will say it is the acting and writing, he said. Rajamouli said he is curious to understand Fahadhs process and how he transforms himself for a character. I really want to work with Fahadh to learn how he brings the character into his acting. I want to see that. That is why I want to work with him, Rajamouli added. ALSO READ Amitabh Bachchan on bond with Abhishek Bachchan Views may differ, destination remains same SS Rajamouli recalls Mohanlals acting philosophy SS Rajamouli also shared an anecdote about meeting Mohanlal in Hyderabad. He said he once asked the veteran actor about his process of acting, to which Mohanlal gave him an answer centred on surrendering himself to the character and the universe. He said, I will tell you my secret. Just before shooting any film, I go and talk to the universe and say, I know nothing. And I mean it with every cell of my body - that I know nothing about acting and nothing about the character. I dont know anything. I am a part of you. You give it to me. I believe it and I do that, and the universe gives it to me, Rajamouli recalled. SS Rajamouli on realising Fahadh Faasils appeal Earlier, while speaking at the Dont Trouble The Trouble pre-release event in Kerala, SS Rajamouli recalled that he had initially assumed Fahadh Faasils films appealed mainly to an elite audience. Like many people in India, apart from Malayalis, I am a big fan of Fahadh Faasil. I watched many of his films on OTT I was discovering them one after another. What surprised me was that I always thought there would be some elite films, class films. That was my perception, Rajamouli said. He recalled that around five or six years ago, his wifes 55-year-old cousin, who lives in a small town, visited him in Hyderabad and asked, Have you seen FaFas films? Rajamouli said he did not even know who FaFa was at that point and realised she was referring to Fahadh. Then I realised Fahadh Faasils reach was not restricted to the elite. People across Telugu land had already known him, he recalled. About Dont Trouble The Trouble Dont Trouble The Trouble marks Fahadh Faasils first Telugu film as a solo lead. He plays Suri, a street magician and small-time con artist whose world changes after he encounters a young girl, Divya, played by child actor Ssara Palekar. Directed and written by Shashank Yeleti, the film is produced by Shobu Yarlagadda, Prasad Devineni and SS Karthikeya under Arka Mediaworks and Showing Business, with SS Rajamouli presenting the project. It also stars Saurabh Sachdeva. The film is set for a worldwide theatrical release on October 2 in Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam.

articleTitle: Indian-origin woman arrested in Canada after confrontation with pedestrian turns physical
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Indian origin woman arrested in Canada
description: In the video, the woman is seen getting out of the passenger side of the vehicle and confronting the pedestrian. She appears to tell him that recording her was illegal before reaching for his phone.
body_raw: An Indian-origin woman was arrested in Calgary, Canada, after a confrontation with a pedestrian, who filmed the act on his phone and later circulated it online. The incident reportedly started when the vehicle carrying the woman allegedly failed to give way to a pedestrian crossing the road. The man began filming the encounter on his phone, after which the situation appeared to escalate. In the video, the woman is seen getting out of the passenger side of the vehicle and confronting the pedestrian. She appears to tell him that recording her was illegal before reaching for his phone. Its not legal to make a video, she can be heard saying in the footage. The confrontation then turned physical, with the woman allegedly grabbing the mans backpack and dragging him across the pavement. The police arrived at the scene soon after and arrested her. In the video, the man at the receiving end of the assault claimed that the womans husband, who was behind the wheel, was driving without valid insurance. Authorities have not publicly provided further details about the viral video or the circumstances surrounding the arrest. Watch the video View this post on Instagram A post shared by BodyCamDDE bodycamdde The footage has since been viewed thousands of times on social media, prompting a debate over the confrontation and whether a person can legally record an incident taking place in a public space. Before you mess with people, make sure your papers are legit, one user commented. Why do they always think that theyre above the law? Probably because they usually get away with it, another wrote. You have no right to act superior in a country that isnt yours, a third user said, while another added, She forgot that shes not in India anymore. The Calgary incident comes weeks after another case involving an Indian-origin woman in Canada also drew attention online. Raj Tiwana was arrested following a confrontation with her tenant, who later posted a series of videos alleging that his landlady had repeatedly harassed him and interfered in his life. The dispute reportedly began after Tiwana objected to the tenant using a barbecue in the garden while a friend was visiting. She allegedly accused him of trying to burn down her property.

articleTitle: ‘First in my bloodline’ to ‘life not a leaderboard’: PM Modi’s moments from IIT Delhi convocation 2026
articleFeaturedImageAlt: PM Modi at IIT Delhi convocation 2026
description: At the IIT Delhi convocation, PM Modi urged students to carry forward the friendships, mentorship, lessons and values they gained at the institute, treating them as lasting assets.
body_raw: More than 3,000 graduating students, including undergraduates, postgraduates and 587 PhD scholars, walked up to receive their degrees at IIT Delhis 57th convocation on Saturday, August 8, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi presiding as chief guest. PM Modi opened not with policy but with feeling, telling the graduating class that they werent merely collecting a degree but carrying out a dream for the country. The speech then moved along familiar lines of Viksit Bharat, research funding, self-reliance across sectors, etc. But it was bloodline and leaderboard and the calling out of hostel blocks that the hall really responded to. The choice of words wasnt incidental since Gen Z-led protests broke out in the national capital and elsewhere in the country, MPs across the political aisle have visibly leaned on the same internet-native lingo in Parliament and beyond. The speechs centre of gravity was a phrase PM Modi repeated like a refrain, and its the one that will likely travel furthest beyond the halls of IIT Delhi First in my bloodline. He used it first for a hypothetical young engineer building a rocket, then for someone making a semiconductor chip in India, then for someone assembling a drone - each time invoking a young Indian saying it with pride, marking a personal, generational first inside sectors the government has been positioning as newly opened to entrepreneurial youth space, semiconductors, drones. Warning students against distraction He carried that same register into the speechs other big idea, warning students against what he called distraction - from the comparison trap that social media entrenches who got what package, who joined which company, who moved to which city or country, who started a startup first. His answer was blunt and, again, borrowed from a very online register life, he said, is not a leaderboard. Your real race isnt against anyone else its against yourself, trying each day to be a little better than the one before, while not losing sight of physical and mental health along the way. Campus life, he said, comes with a syllabus life outside does not. On campus, sab funda clear hai everything was sorted, what to study, what assignment was due, what exam was next. Outside, theres no fixed course, no question paper, and often nobody to even tell you what the real question is you have to identify it yourself, he said. He drew on IIT alumni journeys to argue that their success lay less in answering questions correctly than in noticing questions the world had stopped treating as questions at all - urging the students to keep their curiosity lit, question easy assumptions, and pair every question with the courage to chase a solution. This was also a batch of firsts the maiden graduating cohorts of the Bachelor of Design, the Executive MBA, the MSc in Biological Sciences and the MA in Culture, Society and Thought programmes received their degrees alongside the older, more familiar BTech and MTech contingents. Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi and NITI Aayog member Prof Abhay Karandikar attended as guests of honour, while Harish Salve, Chairperson of IIT Delhis Board of Governors, and Director Prof. Rangan Banerjee led proceedings from the institutes side. The ceremony also saw the inauguration of new AI-linked initiatives at the institute, even as the mood in Dogra Hall stayed determinedly informal, heavy on nostalgia, light on protocol, and, in the Prime Ministers own delivery, tuned to a discernable Gen-Z frequency. Nicer to see more daughters on winners list PM Modi congratulated the medal winners, then broke into an aside that got a laugh in the hall, that it would have been a little nicer to see one or two more daughters on that list, before correcting himself not one or two, but far more. From there, PM Modi turned confessional in a way rarely associated with his regular addresses. He is not Baba Vageshwar, he joked, saying that he cant read whats playing on everyones mind, but he was certain something was stirring in each students head, beyond the caps and gowns. Some, he said, were waiting for their first salary. Others were bracing for a fresh start in a new city. Some were nursing the dream of a first startup, and some had already fixed their sights on the next competitive exam. Every path was different, every dream distinct, but one feeling, he insisted, would be common to them all the ambush of memory, the sudden recall of that first day on campus, arriving at a moment that felt like only yesterday was orientation and today was already convocation. Parathas from Satpura mess He went on to name the hostels one by one, the way only someone whod clearly been briefed by people who lived there could Kumaon, Aravali called as Ara, Karakoram as Kara, Vindhyachal Vindhy, Nilgiri, Kailash, Himadri. He spoke of inter-hostel competition stories, of purani lokjok, the old in-jokes, and pushed the point that this wasnt only about academics. The reference landed with specific, almost on a logistical tone the parathas from Satpura mess were probably being served right about now, he noted, and if anyone made it to the local tea-spot for one last round, they should think of him too. He then turned that sentimentality into instruction. The friends, teachers, mentors and support staff whod become family, the professors whod taken on the job of shaping talent like theirs, the institute that had slowly become a second home, carry all of it out with you as an asset, he said Dont forget it. Dont leave it behind. Take it with you. PM Modi wrapped up thanking students and parents, wishing them nayi unchaiyan-new heights.

articleTitle: Mahesh Bhatt’s first wife lived in an orphanage, gave him ‘permission’ to marry woman he cheated on her with: ‘Wrote love letters in blood’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: mahesh bhatt pooja bhatt
description: Mahesh Bhatt recalled his love story with first wife Lorraine Bright, whom he met when she was just 14 and living in an orphanage.
body_raw: Filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt recalled his love story with first wife Lorraine Bright, aka Kiran Bhatt, whom he met when she was just 14. Bhatt himself was 16 at the time, and would slip love letters written in his own blood through a tailor. In a chat with their daughter, Pooja Bhatt, on her new podcast, Bhatt recalled that Lorraine lived in an orphanage as a child, and that he still takes care of her to this day despite having separated many years ago. In the interview, he also reflected on his infidelities, and her reaction to his second marriage, to Soni Razdan. Recalling their first meeting, he said, I was 16, she was 14. She was living in an orphanage, because her mother did not have the means to keep her as a day scholar. One day, I saw this gorgeous girl standing with her friends at the gate of Bombay Scottish. There was something about her that drew me to her. But, somehow, love was preceded by the feeling of unworthiness. So, it took me a couple of evenings. So, I went up to her and introduced myself. I remember I offered her Milan Supari. Bhatt said that he was struck by her after their first conversation, after which they devised a plan to communicate with each other through a tailor. He used to stitch school uniforms. Struck by her charm and beauty, I begged him to carry my letter to her. He expressed the hazards of doing that, because if he was caught, he would lose his job. But he was a generous man, so he took my letter and I waited for her reply. And then, she did I wrote to her in blood and she also replied in blood. Also read - When Mahesh Bhatt said that his kids from first wife resented Soni Razdan She was the evil seductress who took their papa away Bhatt said that they first met in an empty classroom at the school, after Lorraine had bribed the watchman to keep the doors unlocked for him. Bhatt snuck in through a back door, and found himself face to face with Lorraine. It was getting dark, and Lorraine asked to see his face, so he lit a matchstick until it went out. She was the most beautiful woman Id ever seen in my life, he said. But tragedy struck some time later, when Bhatt got caught. All hell broke loose, and the tailor lost his job, and Lorraine was thrown out of school, he said. Lorraines mother was angry, but Bhatt assured her that he would find her new lodging. He forged his fathers signature and found her a place to stay at the YWCA. Eventually, Lorraine learned skills through which she found a job as a receptionist and a telephone operator. I really believed in fairytale love, but then I fell into a relationship with Parveen Babi, he said. He recalled the moment he told Lorraine about the affair, and said that Pooja was asleep at the time. He looked at himself in the mirror and thought, All your life you hated your father for keeping your mother as the other woman. What have you done? His fairytale romance, he said, was reduced to ashes. Bhatt went on to separate from Lorraine, and married Soni Razdan after his relationship with Parveen Babi ended. Lorraine gave them her blessing. The first phone call that Bhatt made after his and Sonis daughter Shaheen was born was to Lorraine. Pooja recalled, When they questioned the legitimacy of your marriage, and they said, Who gave permission? And Ill never forget, my mother got up and said, Who gave permission? I gave permission. He has my blessing. Praising her father for continuing to look after her mother, she said, Ive met very few men who, once they hold a womans hand, they never let go. The nature of the love might change, but the love doesnt go away. Today, you are more like a parent. She knows that, no matter what, she can rely on you. You have never made her feel that you are stretching yourself by providing. People remind each other about how much theyre doing providing a home, sending money. But Ive watched you. When you said to my grandmother that you will look after her, you still look after her. In the same interview, Bhatt wept as he recalled Poojas reaction to when she found out that he had had an affair with Soni. She said, I saw you sitting at the edge of my bed and telling me about the woman that you have met, Soni, and the fact that youre going to be marrying her and move out. I was just privileged to be treated as an equal because you told me this before you even told my mother.

articleTitle: Kashmiri filmmaker Arfat Sheikh detained by ICE en route to ‘Art as Resistance’ panel
articleFeaturedImageAlt: arfat sheikh
description: The 42-year-old Sheikh has been kept at the Caroline Detention Facility in Virginia and was expected to appear before an immigration judge on Tuesday.
body_raw: An award-winning Kashmiri filmmaker has been detained by the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement ICE, the Independent reported, citing his friends and supporters. ICE detained Arfat Sheikh at the Washington Dulles airport on September 24 while he was on his way to attend an Art as Resistance panel, scheduled to take place at Busboys and Poets in Washington DC, the Independent reported. Sheikh had just stepped off his flight from California when the ICE agents surrounded him and took him into custody without a warrant despite him presenting his immigration paperwork, his friends alleged. The 42-year-old Sheikh has been kept at the Caroline Detention Facility in Virginia and was expected to appear before an immigration judge on Tuesday. He was travelling with author Tara Dorabji, who was one of the speakers at the September 26 panel, where she would address the experiences of the survivors of torture in Kashmir, Independent reported. ICE has not yet responded to the issue. On September 24th, 2026, our friend and filmmaker, Arfat Sheikh was unlawfully detained by ICE coming off a plane at Dulles Airport IAD. FreeArfatSheikh 15 - Free Arfat Sheikh freearfatsheikh October 6, 2026 His friends, colleagues, Americans, and family have launched a campaign to raise 50,000 to pay for his legal representation. About Arfat Sheikh Arfat Sheikh is a Kashmiri filmmaker, living in the US for the past few years. According to the Independent, his first feature film, Saffron Kingdom, which won him accolades, explores conflict, displacement, and identity in Kashmir. The film won him accolades at several independent film festivals. At the Teaneck International Film Festival, 2025, Sheikh was named an Emerging Filmmaker Activist.

articleTitle: 22-year-old victim of Chhattisgarh acid attack may lose vision
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Balod acid attack
description: The woman suffered severe burn injuries on her face and hand, including deep wounds on her right cheek and right eye, which is likely to lead to a complete loss of vision.
body_raw: A 22-year-old woman was the victim of an acid attack in Chhattisgarhs Balod district after she spurned the attackers requests to marry him. The incident occurred on Monday afternoon, when the victim, who was preparing for competitive exams, was returning home from the library. The attackers, Yash Kumar Sonkar and his friend Karan Kunjam, waylaid the woman and threw acid on her face before fleeing. The woman suffered severe burn injuries on her face and hand, including deep wounds on her right cheek and right eye, which is likely to lead to a complete loss of vision. The woman has suffered injuries on her face and both eyes. Her right eye is badly affected. She has a total of 8 per cent burn injuries on her body. She will recover, but the vision in her right eye will take time to restore. At present, she does not have vision in her right eye, said a doctor who wished to remain anonymous. The incident, purportedly the first acid attack in Balod, sparked outrage in the region, and in a swift response, police traced and arrested within just eight hours both the 20-year-old accused and his aide, also 20. Their heads were also tonsured before the duo was paraded to the court complex. There, a mob, mostly women, sat, gheraoing the complex and awaiting them. Some held placards and shouted slogans, demanding justice for the victim and capital punishment for the attackers. Harshita Sahu, a childhood friend of the victim, said, We want immediate hanging of the accused. Now, this has happened with someones daughter, and tomorrow, can happen to anyones daughter. Such an incident acid attack has occurred for the first time in the history of Balod. We will not rest till they get capital punishment. Another girl, Vidya Sahu, a BA student, told the media, She was our colleague. She was innocent and has done nothing wrong. Till now, no woman here has ever been attacked with acid. This has happened for the first time. During the investigation, Sonkar told the police that he knew the victim and had requested her to marry him. However, when she refused his many attempts, the man plotted to carry out an acid attack with the help of his school friend Kunjam. The two bought the acid on September 27 and had planned to carry out the attack during the Ganesh immersion procession. However, the tight security arrangements on the day dissuaded them from carrying it out. Later, on October 5, they waylaid the woman and attacked her. She was first rushed to a local hospital and subsequently shifted to DKS super-speciality hospital in Raipur.

articleTitle: Inside Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajput’s luxe home with a dramatic black staircase, majestic carpets and more
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Shahid Kapoor
description: Take a look inside Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajput’s 10,000-sq-ft Mumbai home, with a dramatic staircase, art, sculptural furniture and earthy interiors.
body_raw: alk into Shahid Kapoor and Mira Rajputs Mumbai home, and there is plenty to catch your eye. A dramatic black geometric staircase cuts through the interiors, large artworks fill the walls, sculptural furniture adds unexpected shapes, warm light adds drama, and plants bring greenery into almost every space. Yet, for a home spread across approximately 10,000 square feet, it doesnt feel like it is trying too hard to look luxurious. Instead, the four-bedroom duplex feels warm, personal and lived in - a mix of art, architecture and everyday comfort that reflects both Shahid and Miras personalities. While he likes to be a lot more experimental and creative, I only think about how practical things are and if it is easy to clean. So, it was about finding the right balance between form and function and allowing both our personalities to shine, Mira said while welcoming Architectural Digest India into their home. That balance becomes apparent as you move through the house. DISCLAIMERThis article is based on information from the public domain andor the experts we spoke to. The dramatic staircase that steals the show The first thing you may notice is the staircase, which is also the Kapoors favourite. Finished in black and made up of bold geometric forms, it is far from purely functional. It acts almost like a piece of sculpture, becoming a visual anchor around which the homes spaces are arranged. The geometric black staircases in this house are used as architectural statements rather than as vertical circulation infrastructure, Manoj Goyal, Director, Forteasia Realty Pvt. Ltd tells indianexpress.com. And this is part of a larger shift in luxury home design. According to Goyal, staircases in large Indian homes and duplexes are increasingly being treated as sculptural elements, with designers experimenting with geometry, materials, lighting and finishes. Raghunandan Saraf, founder and CEO, Saraf Furniture, agrees. Geometric Black Staircase is a striking example of how architecture can transform a merely functional element into a defining design element of an interior. In Shahid and Miras home, the staircase does exactly that it gives the otherwise soft interiors a strong architectural edge. A calm palette, with plenty happening The rest of the house takes a gentler approach. Whites, creams, warm wood, black and earthy neutrals form the base, while natural light and greenery keep the spaces from feeling stark. Textured upholstery, rugs and wooden elements add warmth without disrupting the clean lines. Goyal describes the palette as a warm contemporary one, created through a mix of blacks, whites, neutrals, wood and greenery. It is also a clever backdrop for the homes most expressive elements - particularly its art. The art gives the home personality Miras love for art is evident throughout the residence. Among the pieces are a striking Yuvan Bothysathuvar work, a sculpture by Radhakrishnan and a commissioned work by Subodh Kerkar. The formal dining area, for instance, gets a strong focal point from the Yuvan Bothysathuvar painting. But the artworks dont feel as though they have simply been added to fill empty walls. Art has the power to influence the mood of a space. It helps to create a unique sense of a space and makes the space feel complete and collected, rather than decorated, Goyal says. Saraf puts it more succinctly Art adds an emotional layer to a home. Furnishings define how you use a given space. Meanwhile, art defines how the space is felt. That distinction is important here. The house feels collected rather than coordinated, as though the objects belong to the family rather than having been selected from one catalogue. Even the furniture gets to be playful The couple has not played it entirely safe with furniture either. One particularly eye-catching sofa features a paw-like base, while other pieces bring in unusual silhouettes and sculptural forms. They add little moments of surprise to an otherwise restrained interior. When a chair or sofa has an unusual silhouette, sculptural base or unexpected detail, it can function almost like an art object, Saraf says. But there is a catch statement furniture works best when the rest of the room knows when to step back. Balance is good. If you have a relatively simple palette in your architecture, you can add a few playful, unusual, unexpected pieces of furniture without overwhelming a space, Goyal explains. A design rule seems to run through the house keep the larger picture calm and let a few pieces do the talking. Look down, and youll notice a different world altogether Another, quieter design layer lies underfoot. The rugs around the seating areas rely more on texture and tonal variation than loud patterns, helping define the spaces while adding softness to the homes stone, wood and glass surfaces. Anupriya Choudhary, Director, Saraswati Rugs, was particularly drawn to the rug near the sofa. I liked how the tonal variation and texture add depth and visual interest without becoming overpowering, she tells indianexpress.com. That restraint is particularly useful in a home already filled with artwork and sculptural elements. A hand-crafted rug can bring together furniture, art and architecture through colour, scale and texture, Choudhary says. In luxury homes, she adds, rugs are increasingly being viewed as more than floor coverings. It is no longer simply a floor covering it is an important design and collectable element within the home. But this isnt just a house to look at Beyond the carefully curated living spaces, the home has plenty of room for actual living. The upper level includes a glam room, guest suite, home theatre and lounge, Shahids DJ setup, an open-air gym, a small pantry and an office. The expansive balcony has also been treated as an extension of the living room, with seating and greenery rather than being left as a purely decorative outdoor space. The family designed the home entirely online over 14 months during the Covid pandemic, making it particularly meaningful to them. This house is where the four of us Mira, Shahid and their two kids have found ourselves all together our first one for all of us, Mira said. Her idea of home also has roots in her childhood. Growing up, my mom loved entertaining. She really is the perfect hostess, and there were always people at our house. Thats the kind of home I wanted to create, full of fresh flowers and enough food on the table. Thats something I wanted to recreate, that feeling of an inviting home. And that perhaps explains why the house doesnt feel overly precious. There is art, but also comfortable seating. There are statement pieces, but also greenery and open spaces. A dramatic staircase, but plenty of warmth around it. The new idea of luxury Perhaps the most interesting thing about Shahid and Miras home isnt its size or even its collection of expensive-looking pieces. It is how selectively those pieces have been used. Goyal believes luxury housing is moving toward what he calls the curated lifestyle house-a home that reflects the person living in it rather than simply signalling how much they spent. Saraf sees the same evolution. I dont see the future in the luxury of personal homes becoming centred in the overfill of rooms with expensive objects. Rather, I see those homes becoming selective in the quality of pieces and how those pieces become instrumental in developing the houses character. And perhaps that is what makes this home memorable. It doesnt just look luxurious. It looks like someone actually lives there - someone with an eye for art, a weakness for beautiful objects and, judging by Miras description, a very strong preference for a home where there is always something good to eat.
