articleTitle: WHO issues first ever guidelines on child & teen obesity: No weight loss drugs for under-10 kids
articleFeaturedImageAlt: WHO obesity guidelines for children
description: The development comes following the increasing cases of Type 2 diabetes and related complications in the younger age group.
body_raw: For the first time, the World Health Organisation WHO on Wednesday released guidelines on management of obesity in children and adolescents, strongly recommending against use of any weight loss drugs or surgery in children below the age of nine and only in very select cases in adolescents between the ages of 10 and 19. The guidelines allow the use of drugs and surgery for adolescents who are morbidly obese with lifestyle conditions such as type-2 diabetes, insulin resistance, or uncontrolled hypertension, and for those among whom lifestyle modifications such as diet and exercise have failed to achieve any results after six months. Children and adolescents living with obesity are likely to develop lifestyle diseases much earlier in life and have to live longer with complications arising from them. We now know that losing weight can help prolong their lives. This is the reason we need to intervene aggressively in the early years, says Dr Jothydev Kesavadev, chairperson, Jothydevs Diabetes and Research Centre. What do the guidelines recommend? What are they against? The guidelines have looked at existing evidence on diet, exercise, use of digital technologies, drugs, surgeries, as well as the use of a combined behaviour change programme for effective obesity management in children and made the following recommendations. Based on evidence, the guidelines have strongly recommended the use of structured diets, physical activity and behaviour change, or all of these together for managing obesity in both children and adolescents. They recommend against the use of surgeries such as gastric bypass and drugs such as GLP-1 in children up to the age of nine years. While the guideline on the use of drugs is not specifically meant for GLP-1 alone - with these drugs being an area of interest when it comes to obesity - Dr Luz Maria De Regil, Director of the Department of Nutrition and Food Safety at WHO, said that there was no long-term data on the efficacy and effects of these drugs in children yet. She said that while the research was ongoing, WHO will continue to monitor the emerging evidence and change the guidelines in the future if necessary. The guidelines conditionally recommend the use of surgeries and drugs in adolescents between the ages of 10 and 19 years. These interventions, as mentioned above, are recommended only in those with severe obesity, living with conditions linked to obesity, or in whom other interventions have failed after six months. Dr Luz says that there is a lack of consensus because of a lot of pending questions on how long the medicines should be taken, when they should be stopped and when the maintenance dose should be reduced. The guidelines conditionally recommend the use of digital interventions such as active video games, exergames, exercise activity applications, pedometers or accelerometers among others that may increase physical activity and promote behavioural changes. While the evidence is not too strong, the guidelines say that such activities may be desirable while sedentary use of screens may be limited. Why are the guidelines necessary? Effective ways of addressing obesity in children and adolescents have become essential given the data. There were 170 million children and adolescents aged 519 years living with obesity in 2024, which include 70 million children aged 59 years and 100 million adolescents aged 1019 years, according to WHO. More so for countries such as India. Dr Luz says, While obesity is on the rise globally, the trends show that it is still growing at a rapid pace in low and middle income countries and arresting in high income countries. It has not started going down in any of the WHO regions. In India, there was a three percentage point increase in obesity in girls and 3.7 in boys over a three decade period up to 2022, according to a Lancet study. While 0.2 million boys and 0.2 million girls were obese in 1990, 7.3 million boys and 5.2 million girls were obese in 2022. By 2020, India is expected to be home to over 27 million children and adolescents between the ages of 5 and 19 years living with obesity, accounting for 11 of the global burden, according to the Comprehensive National Nutrition Survey CNNS 2016-18. What do Indian physicians say? Dr Anurag Bajpai, president of the Indian Society for Paediatric and Adolescent Endocrinology, says that he has seen a three-fold increase in the number of children coming to his clinic with obesity. Most of them come in with other co-morbidities such as fatty liver, prediabetes, and high cholesterol levels. So far, there were very limited treatment options but now the use of semaglutide has been approved in children over the age of 12 years by CDSCO Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation. This should not be used by everybody and limited to children living with morbid obesity and complications, he says. In fact, his society is currently in the process of drafting guidelines for the use of GLP-1 drugs in children and adolescents to ensure that it is not over-used and yet is offered to those who require it. Diet, exercise, and other lifestyle changes - even the most rigorous ones - can reduce only 3 to 5 of the body weight in children. This can be effective in those who are borderline but will not be sufficient in many of the patients that we see today - teenagers weighing 140 to 150 kg with other co-morbidities, he explains. According to Dr Bajpai, surgeries are generally not recommended in children and adolescents because they can result in improper nutrition and hamper their growth.

articleTitle: 3 ex-Port Blair civic officers booked over Rs 2.08 crore property tax ‘loss’
articleFeaturedImageAlt: CBI PBMC property tax case, CBI Port Blair case, PBMC officials corruption case, Port Blair Municipal Council, CBI anti-corruption branch, PBMC revenue officials, property tax interest, Port Blair corruption case, CBI FIR Port Blair
description: CBI has alleged a criminal conspiracy between hotel and bar owners and Port Blair Municipal Council officials to avoid paying property tax interest.
body_raw: CBI has booked three officials of the Port Blair Municipal Council PBMC for alleged corruption in issuing around 252 no-dues certificates to hotels and bars without recovering interest on outstanding property tax, causing an estimated loss of Rs 2.08 crore to the public exchequer. According to a First Information Report FIR registered by the Central Bureau of Investigations Anti-Corruption Branch in Port Blair on September 29, a former revenue officer of PBMC, an ex-assistant revenue officer, and an ex-tax inspector have been booked. The central agency registered the FIR after a preliminary inquiry. The inquiry examined alleged irregularities in the issuance of no-objection certificates and no-dues certificates by PBMCs revenue section between 2020 and 2023. The revenue section of PBMC was responsible for collecting revenue, including property tax, market rent and water charges. After the abolition of octroi and the introduction of GST, property tax became one of the main sources of revenue for the municipal body, the FIR said. The FIR refers to a 2015 order of the Calcutta High Courts Circuit Bench at Port Blair, which permitted the council to adopt a new methodology for assessing annual rental value under municipal regulations. The PBMC later passed a resolution in December 2016 to implement the unit area method for property tax calculation, followed by a public notice in January 2017. However, the FIR alleges that the PBMC took no further effective action to interpret and implement the High Courts order. It further alleges that property tax files were maintained separately for each taxpayer and that calculation of outstanding principal and interest had been pending since 2011. Procedure not followed The agency alleges that hotel and bar owners entered into a criminal conspiracy with municipal officials to avoid paying the interest portion of outstanding property tax. According to the FIR, around 252 no objection certificates were issued to hotel and bar owners between 2020 and 2023. Such certificates were issued to 32 hotels and bars even though Rs 2,08,55,880 in interest was allegedly pending from them on the dates the certificates were issued, the FIR alleged. The CBI alleges that the tax inspector calculated the outstanding dues and, despite the interest remaining unpaid, recommended issuing no dues certificates. It further alleges that the assistant revenue officer also recommended such certificates, while files maintained by the revenue officer showed instances where the chief account officer had not approved them. According to the FIR, the chief account officer was the competent authority for approving no objection certificates and no dues certificates, while the revenue officer was delegated only to sign such certificates on behalf of PBMCs secretary. The FIR said the relevant files were not placed before the chief account officer and approvals were granted at the level of the revenue officer in violation of rules.

articleTitle: Asian Games gold best medal of my life, says Lovlina Borgohain
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Lovlina Borgohain poses for photographers during the medal ceremony for the women's 75kg boxing event at the 20th Asian Games, in Nishio, Aichi, Japan, Friday, Oct. 2, 2026. (PTI Photo)
description: After winning an Olympic bronze medal in Japan, Lovlina made a successful return to the country, winning an Asian Games gold half a decade later.
body_raw: Getting punched in the head hasnt worried Lovlina Borgohain for a while now rather, her headspace over the past few years has caused an odd sense of displacement. No Indian boxer barring Mary Kom has the kind of resume the Assamese boxer carried to the Asian Games. Lovlina added another notch to that comparison, becoming only the second Indian woman to win boxing gold at the Asian Games after Kom - a twelve-year wait between the two. The gold, though, came after mental battles that Lovlina has faced in the last two years. The backpack of medals she has won got heavier and heavier until 2024, when the weight, simply, was too much to handle. Losses started to follow and take their toll. The 2025 World Championship brought along with it the final gong of a round lost - for a boxer who had three medals and was the defending champion in her weight category, Liverpool brought her world crashing down. Two full years filled with disappointment left her scarred. Click here to read our Asian Games full coverage A lot of things have to be faced when we come back after losing, said Lovlina. Back in Delhi after her successful campaign in Nagoya, it was those difficult moments that she remembered with a gold medal around her neck. Accepting it yourself is very difficult. when we have expectations from ourselves, and the result doesnt come that way, it hurts a lot. Then somewhere that holds us back from moving forward, added Lovlina. Mindset shift The way back to being herself started with a rethink. How she approached the sport had to be restructured. She began framing injuries and losses positively. In a way, Lovlina chose not to care about the result - and just made an attempt to enjoy the process. It led to a therapeutic lack of pressure as she went into her second-ever Asian Games. ALSO READ Surfeit of silver paints a picture of what could have been for India at Asiad First of all, I didnt go into the Games with very high expectations. I had in mind that whatever the result is, I will accept it, but I have to give my best. So when gold came, maybe. I was not overly excited. Whatever happened, I accepted it. I felt it, I was enjoying it-throughout the game, I enjoyed it. Whether gold came or not, even then, this would have been the best Asian Games of my life, admitted Lovlina. But a silver at the Commonwealth Games, a first for her, and now gold at the Asian Games have once again put her back on track. Part of that realignment came from changes she made. Rather than working hard, Lovlina now tends to work smart. Gone are the days when she preferred staying in camp and grinding out sparring sessions. When we play a competition, its not a matter of one or two days of hard work its the whole year. I had faith that overworking myself shouldnt be done. And the biggest thing I feel when we reach this stage, rather than pushing oneself too much, polishing oneself is more important. If you keep rubbing a diamond too much, it will get ruined, says Lovlina. The changes she brought to her mindset were also reflected during her semi-final match. Lovlina has been part of many multi-sport events for India, but this was the first time she won a gold medal. Usually, her campaign would end in the semi-finals or finals. But things felt different this time. Going up against the 70kg world champion Natalya Bogdanova was no longer as daunting. The semi-final match is very important because - either we have to be satisfied with bronze or we can try to win gold. It stays in your mind because within us, we know whether we could have done better or not. I didnt want that feeling this time, said Lovlina. She won 3-2, arguably weathering the toughest bout of her Games. Till the end, everyone was scared, but I wasnt that scared. I didnt go onto the ring with much stress. The opponent was also very strong, but sometimes it feels good when we play against good opponents and win, said Lovlina. Now that the nonchalance of the end result and the juice of simply performing have come back, Lovlina has thought about all the medals she has won. All the previous World Championship medals, the solitary Olympic bronze and now a Commonwealth silver and Asian Games gold have been added to the collection. When I keep it alongside all my other medals, this one is the one that shines the brightest, admits Lovlina.

articleTitle: They gave up arms last year. Now, seven former Maoists clear SSC exam – 3 of them with first class
articleFeaturedImageAlt: They gave up arms last year. Now, seven former Maoists clear SSC exam – 3 of them with first class
description: All of them wrote the exam in August from Chhattisgarh Open School.
body_raw: While growing up in Maharashtras Gadchiroli district, Geeta Narote had a keen interest in academics. But due to circumstances, she had to drop out of school. Soon, she got influenced by the Maoist movement, left home, and became Dr Champa. When she returned to the mainstream after two decades, she knew exactly what to do Get back to academics. At the age of 35, she cleared her SSC exams this month. I want to become a nurse, she tells The Indian Express. Geeta is among a batch of 210 Maoists who gave up arms in October last year. Seven of the former Maoists wrote the SSC exams this year. Of these, three, including Geeta, secured the first class. All of them wrote the exam in August from Chhattisgarh Open School. The three former Maoists said they held fire-arms but never fired a bullet. Recalling her childhood, Geeta said she belonged to Gurekasa village in Dhanora tehsil where she lived with her parents and three sisters. She was a 10-year-old girl when Maoists killed her father. Geeta had to quit her studies in sixth standard. Despite her fathers death, Geeta got influenced by the Maoist movement, impressed by their claims of fighting against patriarchy and forced marriages and talks about womens rights. Geeta fled her village and joined the movement, which brought her to Abujhmaad in Chhattisgarh. She has not seen her home since. Talking about her life in the jungle, she said, The Maoists encouraged people to study but there were no means for it. No school, no proper teachers. But our suppliers used to bring us medical related books. I also have had a tablet since 2017 on which I would read, said Geeta. I was also trained in treating bullet wounds, stitching, administering injections as well as giving medicines for several health issues. I also helped many villagers who could not get medical aid, she added. Geeta was a divisional committee member in the CPI Maoist when, led by Takkalappalli Vasudeva Rao, alias Rupesh, known as the Maoists bombmaker, she surrendered in Jagdalpur. Geeta got Rs 50,000 from the government. She used some of the money to buy books. Geeta said she received some guidance from one Pathak sir. But most of it was self-study, without any coaching, she added. I am very happy. My father wanted me to become a teacher. I will complete my HSC and try to become a nurse. I wish to see my mother and sisters soon, said Geeta, who lives in a rehabilitation centre in Jagdalpur. Life has completely changed. Like Geeta, Arjun Oyam, 32, also wanted to study but as Maoism intensified in his village, the teachers stopped coming to school. Arjun comes from Todka village, which falls in Bijapur districts Gangaloor area, infamous for mass recruitment of Maoists. During Salwa Judum, my house was burnt and I lost my books too. I ended up joining the Maoists in 2010 and was sent to Abujhmaad, said Arjun, 32. With the Maoists, Arjun became an Area Committee Member ACM. However, he continued to study. He said the Maoists did not allow him to return. I studied in their political school and became a teacher there for a year, teaching basic Maths, Hindi, Environment etc. I also requested them to send me to a government school but they said I will get arrested. I did not agree with them when they murdered Anganwadi workers and teachers, said Arjun. With hundreds of Maoists being killed, Arjun thought he would die too. But our leaders chose to give up weapons. The Bijapur SP, among others, encouraged me to study. The policemen helped me get my birth certificate and caste certificate needed to apply for the exam, and Chaitu dada a former Maoist encouraged me to study. I bought my own books from the surrender amount, he said. Arjun also gave the credit to his friends in his village who guided him on WhatsApp. During the day, I received training in fish-farming and on working as an electrician while I spent my nights studying. I am very happy that I got the first class, he said. My friends and the SP congratulated me. Now I want to complete my studies and become a teacher in my village. I have not gone to my village in over a decade, added Arjun. Asked how his life has changed since his days in the jungle, Arjun said, There is a huge difference. First time in my life I got to see a lot in the outside world like social media and education. They authorities took us to Raipur and showed us the Vidhan Sabha, Tribal Museum, Jungle Safari and the Cricket stadium. Like Arjun, Santosh Achla, better known as Sannu, an ACM, was also a teacher in the Maoist party. My father was a suspected Maoist and died in judicial custody in 2023 after spending years in jail. My mother died this June and I was allowed to attend her final rites, said Sannu, 31. He dropped out of school in the second standard. I joined the Maoists in 2008 after getting inspired by Chetna Natya Manch the cultural troupe of the Maoist party as I also wanted to sing, dance and give speeches. We were told that the Raoghat mining project will take away our village in Gundur, Koyelibeda, in Kanker district in Chhattisgarh, he said. The Maoists taught Sannu to read and write and he became a teacher in 2023, teaching young cadres basic Maths and Hindi. I had a phone without a SIM card on which I used to read. I used a memory card and a pen drive to get online books, he added. Sannu said he wants to study further. I want to start my own business and also do farming on my land. But to do anything, you need to be educated.

articleTitle: BLOs shared details for ‘verification’. Hundreds of voters in Odisha nearly struck out of roll
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Odisha sir, Odisha voters electoral roll, Odisha voters nearly struck out of roll, odisha Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise, SIR of electoral roll, nationwide SIR, Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Assembly elections, Assembly polls, nationwide Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, nationwide SIR of of electoral rolls, Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, SIR of of electoral rolls, Election Commission, Election Commission of India, Indian express news, current affairs
description: After BLOs in Dhamnagar complain their credentials used to file Form 7s for deletion without their knowledge, officer suspended. Almost all names flagged were Muslim, almost all are in final Odisha roll
body_raw: When Nirupama Tripathy, a Booth Level Officer BLO in Odishas Dhamnagar Assembly seat, opened the app she was using for the Special Intensive Revision SIR exercise, she discovered at least 227 Form 7 applications seeking deletion of voters names uploaded using her credentials without, she says, her knowledge. Tripathy wasnt the only one. Several BLOs in Dhamnagars Notified Area Council-an Urban Local Body, alongside municipalities and municipal corporations-claimed multiple Form 7 applications similarly uploaded in their names. On September 4, 10 such BLOs registered a police complaint and approached the Bhadrak District Collector. On September 7, the BJD, the principal opposition party, submitted a memorandum to Odisha Chief Electoral Officer CEO R S Gopalan raising the issue. Now, after a preliminary inquiry, the Election Commission of India ECI has suspended Santosh Kumar Nayak, the Executive Officer of the Dhamnagar council and the areas Assistant Electoral Registration Officer AERO for the SIR exercise, who allegedly used the credentials of BLOs to submit the bulk deletion applications. The applications were also withdrawn, with most of the voters against whom Form 7s were allegedly filed fraudulently in Dhamnagar figuring in Odishas final electoral roll, released on September 21. As per officials, more than 90 of these applications concerned Muslim voters. Dhamnagar, located in northeast Odisha, is one of the few Assembly seats in the state with a sizeable Muslim population. The BLOs who spoke to The Indian Express said almost all voters flagged via Form 7s had been cleared by them in the enumeration round, and also mapped to the 2002 SIR. Apart from the large presence of Muslim names in the applications, what raised suspicion, sources said, was the high number of Form 7s-over 3,000-from one constituency of Dhamnagar. In contrast, across Odishas 147 Assembly constituencies, a total of 20,707 names were deleted on the basis of Form 7 applications, working out to an average of 141 voters per seat. After the BJDs memorandum, the CEO office sought a report from the Additional Sub-Collector, Bhadrak, who is the Electoral Registration Officer ERO for Dhamnagar. The allegations raised in the memorandum are of a sensitive nature and therefore require immediate examination, the September 8 letter said. A source said The ERO verified the issue internally and prima facie found that the forms had been processed in an unauthorized manner. On September 21, the CEO wrote to the Bhadrak District Collector saying the ECI had conveyed its approval for suspension and initiation of disciplinary proceeding against Nayak, in connection with. allegations of unauthorised use of BLO credentials OTPs and unauthorised submission uploading of Form-7 applications during the ongoing SIR exercise. On Monday, the Odisha Housing and Urban Development Department issued the official order suspending Nayak. CEO Gopalan refused to comment on the matter. Speaking to The Indian Express, BLO Tripathy said I shared OTPs with the AERO and his staff at least three times. I thought its for verification purposes. When I found out about processing of 227 Form 7s for deletion of voters on my behalf, I spoke to other BLOs, and they said they were seeing a similar situation. This prompted us to take action. An anganwadi worker, Tripathy was the BLO for Booth No. 153 in Dhamnagar Assembly constituency. In their police complaint, Tripathy and the other BLOs submitted Despite us knowing all the works on the BLO App, the AERO took OTP from us on the pretext of verification, and processed Form 7 using our credentials to remove names of genuine voters. The AERO has also been pressurizing us through our supervisor for completion of early field verification of the names. He threatened to issue a show cause if we dont follow the order. Tripathy said the people against whom Form 7 applications were filed using her credentials were all valid voters, who were also in the 2002 SIR, and that of the 227 such names, all were Muslim barring three-four. We approached police as we wanted to convey that we had no role in deleting any names. We would have been targeted otherwise by those who faced deletion, she said. Sk Ramjan Alli, an Urdu teacher and the BLO for Booth No. 154 in Dhamnagar, said 130 Form 7s were filed in his name. While he was not among the 10 BLOs who lodged a police complaint, Alli said he was part of a group who raised concerns with the AERO office. The AERO sought OTPs though our supervisor and I shared them twice. More than 90 of the names against whom Form 7s were uploaded using my credentials had been found to be genuine during the enumeration process. Their names were also in the 2002 SIR, Alli told The Indian Express. Another BLO, Binjulata Majhi, who handled Booth No. 155, said 190 Form 7 applications were filed against her name. An official of the CEO office said the Bhadrak District Collector has also been asked to forward a full-fledged draft charge against the AERO, and a detailed inquiry has been ordered against him. The SIR numbers There were 20,000 Muslim voters among Dhamnagar constituencys total of 2.49 lakh at the start of the SIR exercise. Around 7.19 17,956 voters were deleted during the enumeration phase. In the final roll, released on September 21, the constituencys count is 2.31 lakh voters. Dhamnagar has been won the past two times by the BJP, by narrow margins of over 4,000 and 8,000-plus votes, in 2019 and 2024, respectively. The BJD, which was the runner-up both times, says the prima facie findings regarding Form 7s need a thorough probe. BJD general secretary Bijay Nayak said If the allegations are proved to be true, it raises a serious question on the credibility of the electoral process. Given the situation in Dhamnagar, all deletions carried out through Form 7s in Odisha should be reviewed. Not a single eligible voter should be excluded from the voter list. Overall, the total number of voters in Odisha went down from 3.33 crore before the SIR began to 3.16 crore in the final roll.

articleTitle: What is Bengal’s controversial anti-Goonda Bill?
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari has claimed that the Bill had already received the Governor's assent. It has now been returned by the President. (ANI/Wikimedia Commons)
description: Passed by the West Bengal Assembly on June 29, the anti-Goonda Bill is a preventive detention statute aimed at 'goondas' and 'anti-social activities'.
body_raw: The West Bengal Public Safety and Control of Anti-Social Activities Bill, 2026 - also known as the anti-Goonda Bill - was among the first pieces of legislation introduced by the new BJP government in West Bengal. Passed by the Assembly on June 29, it is a preventive detention statute aimed at goondas and anti-social activities. Why is the Bill controversial? What is the Bengal anti-Goonda Bill? West Bengal already has a preventive detention law dating back to the 1970s. The present Bill is wider in its ambit. It allows authorities to detain a person for up to 12 months - without trial - and bar or extern them from entering a specified area, district or districts for up to the same period to prevent anti-social activity. The Bill has expansive definitions of the term goonda, as well as anti-social activity. A goonda is a person who is generally reputed to be desperate and dangerous to the community or is a Habitual Offender. An anti-social activity covers conduct that directly or indirectly causes alarm or insecurity among the public, danger to life or property, disturbance of public order, unlawful dispossession, or illegal mining, quarrying, sand or forest activity that drains the public exchequer. The Bill also allows for search and seizure, punishes the harbouring of a detained or externed person, grants officials good-faith immunity, and makes offences cognizable and non-bailable. Goonda laws exist in several states, most notably in Gujarat, as the Prevention of Anti-Social Activities Act, 1985. The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita also has provisions to deal with organised crime. Preventive detention is permitted under Article 22 of the Constitution with certain safeguards. Such issues are legislated under public order, which is a state subject. The controversies around the Bill The proposed legislation triggered multiple controversies ever since its introduction. Three Public Interest Litigations challenging the Bill were moved in the Calcutta High Court over its sweeping provisions, as detailed above. The High Court last month dismissed the three PILs mentioned above, saying the petitions were premature because the Bill had not yet received the Presidents assent to become a law When does a state Bill go to president? Normally, a Bill passed by a state Assembly and a Council, if the state has one requires only the Governors assent to become law. But Article 200 of the Constitution gives the Governor the power to decide whether any Bill needs to be referred to the President. Article 200 states When a Bill has been passed by the Legislative Assembly of a State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, has been passed by both Houses of the Legislature of the State, it shall be presented to the Governor and the Governor shall declare either that he assents to the Bill or that he withholds assent therefrom or that he reserves the Bill for the consideration of the President. While this is usually left to the Governors discretion, there is one condition in which it is mandatory for the Governor to refer a Bill to the President. This is also set out in Article 200 Provided further that the Governor shall not assent to, but shall reserve for the consideration of the President, any Bill which in the opinion of the Governor would, if it became law, so derogate from the powers of the High Court as to endanger the position which that Court is by this Constitution designed to fill. In simple terms, this means that if a state Bill weakens the High Courts powers, so much that it threatens its constitutional role, the Governor must refer it to the President. A Governor can also return a Bill - if its not a Money Bill - to the legislature for reconsideration or revision. If the legislature passes it again, even without change, the Governor cannot withhold assent, Article 200 says. What are the next steps? When a Bill is reserved by a Governor for the consideration of the President, the President can either assent to the Bill or withhold assent. 201 of the Constitution states Provided that, where the Bill is not a Money Bill, the President may direct the Governor to return the Bill to the House or, as the case may be, the Houses of the Legislature of the State together with such a message as is mentioned in the first proviso to article 200. According to Article 201, the state legislature has six months to reconsider the Bill from the date of receipt of such a message. ..if it is again passed by the House or Houses with or without amendment, it shall be presented again to the President for his consideration, the Article says.

articleTitle: KPSC chairman Sahukar, member Geetha took bribes to leak answer keys
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Karnataka Public Service Commission job racket, KPSC recruitment scam, Shivashankarappa Sahukar, Karnataka KPSC scam, KPSC chairman daughter recruitment, Suma Sahukar income certificate case, KPSC veterinary doctor paper leak .Karnataka veterinary recruitment scam. Shivashankarappa Sahukar CID probe, KPSC question paper leak, Karnataka High Court KPSC case, KPSC corruption allegations, Basavaraj Kannale KPSC scam, Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar arrest, 400 veterinary doctors recruitment scam, Karnataka government job scam, Express investigation, KPSC recruitment controversy
description: Sahukar reportedly leaked the keys to an aspirant for a Rs 10 lakh advance, who subsequently secured the third rank, while Geetha allegedly provided them to the first-rank winner for a Rs 20 lakh advance.
body_raw: An Enforcement Directorate ED probe has revealed that the now-suspended Karnataka Public Service Commission KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar and KPSC member B V Geetha allegedly leaked answer keys for the January 6 veterinary doctors recruitment exam in exchange for bribes. Sahukar reportedly leaked the keys to an aspirant for a Rs 10 lakh advance, who subsequently secured the third rank, while Geetha allegedly provided them to the first-rank winner for a Rs 20 lakh advance. They were arrested by the ED on Tuesday following a probe into allegations of money laundering by KPSC officials through job frauds in the Commission with a specific reference to the fraud in the recruitment of veterinary doctors for Karnataka. The EDs findings with respect to Sahukar and Geetha were presented in court on Wednesday, where the agency submitted that the two had obtained the answer keys for 80 questions prepared for the entrance exam from the now-arrested KPSC Controller of Exams and IAS officer, Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, and supplied it to as many as six candidates. Incidentally, Gangwar and a middleman Basavaraj Kannale were earlier arrested for allegedly leaking up to 80 questions to as many as 11 aspirants for bribes ranging from Rs 20 lakh to Rs 40 lakh. In the case of the previous arrests, it was the questions that were leaked. Here, in this case, it is the answer keys, the ED counsel Madhu N Rao told the court. This is a different modus operandi from the first cases, he added. The ED probe has found that four other candidates - the eight, ninth, 11th and 12th rank winners - were also given access to answer keys by Sahukar and Geetha. The probe found that Geetha gave the names of six aspirants to Exam Controller Gangwar and he, in turn, looked at the seating arrangement for them in the exam hall and then provided the answer keys for the specific set of question papers they would receive on the exam day, the ED counsel said. Only 80 answers For 100 questions were given, and the candidates were asked to memorise them. This is why these candidates have all got the same answers wrong in the exam, the counsel added. The ED has shown prima facie that the two accused were misusing their positions for leakage of answer keys to the two candidates for consideration of illegal gratification of Rs 20 lakh and Rs 10 lakh respectively, the special court said while remanding Sahukar and Geetha to EDs custody till October 19. The ED probe also prima facie discloses that Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar, VH the third rank candidate, her father, NB the first rank candidate and his father, and Shivashankarappa Sahukar and B V Geetha were connected with monetary transactions. the court observed. The ED has taken the two accused into custody until October 19 to probe transactions with other selected candidates and to find the money trail from the bribes.

articleTitle: Election Commission clarified stand on SIR… no one questioned 7 lakh deletions in Bihar: Samrat Choudhary
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary (File photo)
description: Targeting the Congress, the Bihar CM said that a party which made an Election Commissioner a Rajya Sabha MP and another a Governor, has no moral right to talk about the poll panel's functioning
body_raw: Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Sunday said that since the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners have issued a joint statement confirming consensus on the poll panels decisions on SIR, the matter should be put to rest now. Choudhary said that the EC has also clarified that the letter to the Cabinet Secretary was sent regarding a different issue, so there should be no doubts in peoples minds. He said NDA allies had every right to raise concerns, but they should present concrete facts so that any discrepancies could be corrected. Speaking to reporters on the specific issue of the Special Intensive Revision SIR and questions surrounding the ECs functioning, Choudhary said No one questioned the deletion of seven lakh voters during the SIR in Bihar, and all objections raised by Congress and other political parties were addressed. The SIR process revealed that 36 lakh voters had shifted, 22 lakh had died, and seven lakh were registered in more than one place. We ended up with a final list of 7.42 crore voters. No one challenged those seven lakh deletions. Regarding concerns raised by allies Chirag Paswan and Upendra Kushwaha seeking clarification from the EC on the SIR, Choudhary stated The EC has clarified everything. They confirmed that all decisions were taken by consensus. Any political party that still has complaints should present facts. after the EC completes its process, the courts are there to review it. Rahul, Tejashwi travel in Bihar like tourists He said that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had previously cited specific instances of discrepancies, which were addressed. The problem with Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, and Tejashwi Prasad Yadav, Leader of the Opposition in the Bihar Assembly, is that they rarely present facts. They travel around Bihar like tourists, he said. Further targeting the Congress, Choudhary said The party that sent former Election Commissioner M S Gill to Rajya Sabha and appointed another former Election Commissioner, R K Trivedi, as Gujarat Governor has been targeting the EC. This is the same party whose Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi, had her election set aside by the court. Choudhary said that the party, which produced three Prime Ministers from a single family - Jawaharlal Nehru, Indira Gandhi, and Rajiv Gandhi - along with a superpower in Sonia Gandhi, should not lecture others. Rahul Gandhi took the position of Leader of the Opposition only because it brings power and privilege, he said. On CPIM threatening protests in Bihar and INDIA bloc planning meetings over the SIR issue, he said, Political movements happen they have every right to protest, but they should bring facts. The CM questioned how Congress won consecutive elections from 1952 to 1967 and several others afterward if systems were flawed. We are now winning elections under PM Narendra Modi alongside our allies. Congress simply cannot digest a poor mans son as Prime Minister, Choudhary said.

articleTitle: Beijing doesn’t get it – Jane Eyre is no model for domesticity
articleFeaturedImageAlt: The Jane Eyre Beijing doesn’t get
description: Marriage at the end of Jane Eyre is undergirded by clarity. Eyre walks away from it when staying would have meant becoming lesser, unequal
body_raw: Charlotte Brontes Jane Eyre is an unlikely heroine for a state seeking to teach young women a moderate face of feminism and the value of domesticity. Plain, financially constrained, lacking in social capital she might be, but Brontes heroine wasnt short on self-awareness. She declares, I can live alone, if self-respect, and circumstances require me so to do. I need not sell my soul to buy bliss. It is probably this insistence on equality that has lent the novel such appeal in China since it was first introduced in translation in the early 1920s. Now, however, the Chinese state has made it mandatory reading for ninth-grade students, arguably for quite different reasons Beijing is waging an uphill campaign against plummeting birth and marriage rates. A 19th-century romance, with its promise of true love and a value system oriented towards home and hearth, could work as useful propaganda. In this modernist state re-reading, Eyre is rebellious, but not irredeemably so independent, but not averse to settling down outspoken, but unmistakably feminine. She is proof that a woman can have a mind of her own without turning her back on the domestic. And yet, there are postscripts to this reading. Marriage at the end of Jane Eyre is undergirded by clarity. Eyre walks away from it when staying would have meant becoming lesser, unequal. Only later, with an inheritance of her own and the independence it guarantees, does she return to Rochester. Love becomes, in Brontes telling, a choice, not a surrender. Perhaps that is the lesson young readers will take away from it.

articleTitle: Barapullah Phase III traffic mess: Delhi plans U-turn, road widening, Google Maps fix
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Barapullah Phase 3 traffic jam, Barapullah Phase 3 congestion, Barapullah flyover traffic,
description: The corridor opened last week but has already seen long traffic snarls, prompting the Delhi government to look at short-term measures.
body_raw: With congestion building up soon after Barapullah Phase III opened last week, the Delhi government is now relying on a series of quick measures-deployment of traffic police at merging points, a new U-turn, redesigning the point where traffic merges, widening the road and removing a footpath, while also working with Google Maps to ensure real-time route information is provided to the commuters. Citing an engineering flaw in the construction, which had not taken into account the traffic situation expected after 10 years, PWD Minister Parvesh Sahib Singh said on Wednesday, The government is currently working on immediate traffic-management measures, while discussions on a longer-term solution continue. see box Singh blamed the previous AAP-led Delhi government for the flaw in the construction. The Barapullah Phase III flyover project began in 2015. That means its design had already been approved in 2014-2015, when the AAP government had come to power in Delhi. The entire design was approved during their tenure. How many lanes the flyover would have, all of this was decided by them, he said. Asked whether there was any warning sign that such a situation could arise, Singh said, We had no such study. We had no estimate. The new corridor connects Mayur Vihar with Sarai Kale Khan and links to the existing Barapullah network, creating a continuous stretch of around 10 km towards the AIIMS roundabout. However, the promise of a 15-minute, signal-free ride has run into a bottleneck at Sarai Kale Khan, where vehicles arriving from Mayur Vihar, those joining from the Sundial loop, and traffic approaching from the DND side converge before entering the older and narrower Barapullah flyover. The project was originally scheduled for completion in 2017 but opened only in 2026 after construction delays. Over these nine years, while vehicle numbers rose significantly, East Delhi and the wider NCR also grew, changing vehicular movement between East Delhi, Noida, Ghaziabad, and South Delhi. Singh also said that the issue was not limited to the road itself. The interaction of Barapulla with DND Flyway, NH 24, Ring Road, RRTS connectivity, Sarai Kale Khan and the surrounding railway and Metro network has created a much larger integrated traffic movement. Traffic Police had earlier flagged another problem Google Maps was showing the new corridor as relatively clear, directing motorists towards a stretch that was already congested. This was adding to the load as some vehicles that could otherwise use DND or NH 24 were being routed towards Barapullah. Singh said the PWD was in touch with Google Maps and that its algorithm could take about 15 days to reflect the changed traffic situation. He also raised questions over the financial and contractual decisions taken during the previous AAP government. An additional payment of around Rs 640 crore was made to the contractor through arbitration. The projects prolonged delay, cost escalation, and arbitration-related payments need to be examined together, Singh said. The AAP called for a CBI investigation. The BJP government itself admits that Barapulla Phase nIII has serious issues of planning, design and traffic integration. It must answer why it sanctioned Rs. 1,635 crore without a proper technical assessment. The CBI must investigate the matter, an AAP spokesperson said. Instead of blaming the previous government, the BJP should explain the technical assessment and the basis on which Rs. 1,635 crore of public money was sanctioned, the spokesperson added. The quick fixes Traffic police deployment Personnel to be deployed at peak hours to regulate the three merging traffic streams. Sundial merge Traffic Police has suggested redesigning the merger point to improve vehicle flow. New U-turn A dedicated U-turn near Gurdwara Bala Sahib for Siddharth Extension residents, reducing dependence on the ramp to the old Barapullah. Footpath removal A footpath between Sarai Kale Khan and ITO is being removed to improve traffic movement. Road widening The government is working on widening the affected stretch to accommodate the increased flow. Google Maps changes PWD is coordinating with Google Maps to ensure routing reflects the current congestion and traffic patterns.

articleTitle: UWA Chennai campus gets final UGC approval, classes to begin by October-end
articleFeaturedImageAlt: university western australia chennai
description: UWA's first Indian campus officially opened on September 18, 2026, in Andheri East. It began teaching its first cohort in September, with programmes spanning computer science, data science, artificial intelligence and more.
body_raw: The University of Western Australia UWA has received final approval from the University Grants Commission UGC to operate its international branch campus in Chennai. The campus will begin orientation on October 5, with classes scheduled to start on October 19. The 70,000-square-foot campus is located on the seventh floor of One National Park on Velachery Main Road in Chennai. UWA Chennai will offer undergraduate programmes in business management, computer science, data science and advanced computer science with artificial intelligence. Its postgraduate offerings will include a Master of Information Technology and Master of Business Administration MBA. Read IIT Madras begins applications for online executive courses Course fee, schedule and more The Chennai campus is the second UWA campus to begin operations in India. The university opened its Mumbai campus in September 2026. UWA has said it plans to invest about AUD 80 million in its wholly owned campuses in India. The Chennai campus will initially focus on programmes in data science, artificial intelligence, information technology and business. Students will begin with an orientation programme before regular classes start later this month. The opening comes as more foreign universities begin operating branch campuses in India under the UGCs regulatory framework for foreign higher educational institutions. Several such campuses have started teaching or welcomed their first students since the beginning of 2026. Also Read IIT Guwahati taught me more than engineering Coffin dances, Maggi and an events head title Which other foreign universities in India have opened in 2026? Among the numerous that have announced a campus in India, over the past two years, several have begun their intake processes and operating their classrooms this year. The University of New South Wales UNSW opened its Bengaluru campus in August 2026 and welcomed its first students that month. The campus initially offers undergraduate degrees in business, computer science and data science, along with a postgraduate degree in cyber security. Birkbeck, University of London began operations at its Bengaluru campus in 2026. The university received UGC approval to begin teaching from its Whitefield campus and opened it to students for the 2026-27 academic year. Its initial programmes include undergraduate degrees in business management, business analytics and international business, and postgraduate programmes in international business management and business analytics. Also Read IIT Madras, BITS Pilani join hands to promote academic, research opportunities The University of Bristol opened its Mumbai Enterprise Campus on September 10, 2026, and welcomed its inaugural cohort. Located at Cignus Powai, the campus is the universitys first international campus and has an initial focus on areas including data science and finance. The expansion is part of a broader increase in foreign university campuses in India. In an August 2026 response to Parliament, the Education Ministry said UGC had issued 16 Letters of Intent to foreign higher education institutions from Australia, Italy, the UK and the US. At that point, the ministry said the University of Southampton and UNSW had already established campuses in Gurugram and Bengaluru respectively, while four institutions in Mumbai - York, Bristol, Aberdeen and Illinois Institute of Technology - had received approval to start operations. Additionally, the University of York welcomed its first students to its Mumbai campus in September 2026. The Powai-based campus began its inaugural academic year with undergraduate and postgraduate programmes covering computer science with artificial intelligence and cyber security, business and the creative industries. UWAs first Indian campus officially opened on September 18, 2026, in Andheri East. It began teaching its first cohort in September, with programmes spanning computer science, data science, artificial intelligence, cyber security, information technology, business management and an MBA. Chennai is the second UWA campus to follow.

articleTitle: India News Highlights, 6 October 2026 | Delhi Police release Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi from detention hours after Opposition’s anti-CEC protest
articleFeaturedImageAlt: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra are detained by police during a protest against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls at Akashvani Bhawan in Delhi on Tuesday. (Express Photo by Gajendra Yadav)
description: INDIA bloc MPs were demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid allegations of irregularities in the revision of electoral rolls.
body_raw: Delhi Police on Tuesday night released Opposition leaders, including Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, after a nearly nine-hour protest at Akashvani Bhavan in Delhi. The INDIA bloc leaders had been detained after staging a protest inside the All India Radio premises next to the Election Commission office. They were taken away in buses before being released later in the evening. The Opposition leaders, who had earlier climbed atop barricades during the protest, had vowed to continue their demonstration until they were allowed to meet Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and tell him that he had committed vote theft. The protest was held over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision SIR of electoral rolls. Earlier several opposition MPs were detained by Delhi police and taken away in buses to different police stations. These detainees included Akhilesh Yadav, Abhishek Banerjee, Kalyan Banerjee, Derek OBrien, Imran Masood, P Santosh and A Rahim. As the protest escalated, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, along with some supporters, entered the Akashvani Bhawan premises while attempting to reach the Election Commission headquarters. Congress leaders Pawan Khera and other party workers also remained at the premises. Rahul Gandhi, speaking to media persons from inside Akashvani Bhawan, said the opposition was fighting to save democracy. We are not only countering them. I have no interest in what the BJP is saying. Im standing here to save democracy. Other MPs are also trying the same, Gandhi said. He alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had finished democracy in the country. Youth of our country have understood this. Even the police officers were also telling me the same thing. They have done vote chori and hijacked the elections, Gandhi alleged.
